-Lobby
After a very long wait, the hallway doors open at {time=9.}
Naomi comes from the right door and takes the first group to the event room.
-Event room
As Naomi is unlocking the Sekimeiya cabinet, smoke appears, and I fall to the floor.
Before losing consciousness, an alarm plays.

-Event room
I reawaken in the event room. Its appearance has drastically changed.
Shiroya and Akaro are safe, but Naomi is missing.

-Right hallway
We're drawn to the right hallway by a yell.
We meet up with the second group and Katei.
Katei tells us that we'll be trapped for twelve hours in Ashiya Tower.
-Lobby
A shutter is covering the exit. No smoke was released in the lobby.

-Event room
We return to the event room to check if the Sekimeiya is in the cabinet.
We see a shining, white egg that seems to be the Sekimeiya.
-Left hallway
We go to the left hallway to access the security room.
Katei unlocks the security room, and we check the layout of the crystal floor.

-Security room
The {u}computer displays {time=9:41.}{/u} We talk to Suripo, a policeman outside the tower.
At the end of the conversation, the leftmost computer monitor powers off.
The computer and all the screens power off.
-Mechanical room
Sai and I go to the mechanical room to check the light breakers.
Sai guarantees that Katei has been lying to us.
-Event room
Sai and I go to the event room. The Sekimeiya is still inside the cabinet.

-Security room
Sai and I return to the security room.
Katei presses the power button on the computer, and it boots up.
-Hallway A
We leave Katei in the security room and go look for Naomi.

-Event room
Sai takes the Sekimeiya out of the cabinet.
Katei enters the room and puts the Sekimeiya back in the cabinet.
Katei explains what he knows about the Sekimeiya's discovery.
-Crystal room A1
We begin searching through all the rooms to find Naomi.
All the curtains are lowered, and behind them are gemstones displayed to the visitors.

-Hallway A
Isla finds a rusty key on the floor of hallway A, close to the event room.
-Crystal floor
We keep looking for Naomi in the crystal rooms.
-Crystal room A5
We enter room A5. The walls show that smoke was released in it.
All the cabinets are empty.

-Hallway C
We find an empty suitcase in hallway C.
-Staff room
After the cleaning room and B6, we enter the staff room.
Katei opens his locker. Only a coat is inside it.
-Crystal floor
We look through the remaining rooms in hallway B and are unable to find Naomi.

-Floor 6
Shiroya, Isla, Erina, and I take the elevator to the sixth floor.
We investigate it and don't find anyone.
-Floor 5
We go to the fifth floor, which shares a similar layout.
As we're about to leave, Erina and I hear a deep sound in the distance.
Isla tells us that a friend of hers told her that we'd get trapped in the tower.

-Floor 4
We go to the fourth floor. It looks like the previous two.
Akaro and Sai are next to the elevator. They tell us that Naomi appeared from below and asked to talk to Katei privately.
Katei comes from the stairs. He says that Naomi refused to come with him after she failed to clear her name.
Shiroya and I stay on the fourth floor after everyone goes to find Naomi.

-Floor 4
Shiroya and I hear the elevator passing through the fourth floor. We run up.
-Floor 5
We call the elevator on the fifth floor and determine it was on the sixth.
-Floor 6
I stay next to the elevator while Shiroya goes to find the person who took the elevator.
She comes back and hasn't found anyone, but she brings me to the door that we missed earlier, presumably leading to the attic.
Akaro comes and tells us to hurry to the crystal floor. We walk all the way down.

-Crystal floor
Everyone is by the crystal floor's staircase. Sai tells us that the Sekimeiya has been taken from the cabinet.
Shiroya and I confirm that the Sekimeiya is gone.
-Crystal room A5
Sai and I fail to find the Sekimeiya in room A5, but I realize that some cabinets have inner compartments.
-Crystal floor
We resume the crystal floor search.

-Crystal room B4
In room B4, Naomi's dead body is found.
Katei accuses me of having killed Naomi. I notice that one of the cabinets has a damaged wheel. Inside the cabinet is the Sekimeiya.

-Hallway A
After touching the Sekimeiya, I find myself in hallway A, next to the lobby.
-Crystal floor
I can't find anyone on the crystal floor.
-Floor 6
I take the elevator to the sixth floor.
Shiroya is there, but she doesn't pay me any mind and enters the partitions.
The attic door is still locked. I can't find Shiroya in the partitions.
-Crystal floor
After minutes of waiting on floor 5, I keep going down the floors without finding anyone.

-Crystal room B4
Everyone is in room B4 again. They say that I disappeared as soon as I leaned into the cabinet. The Sekimeiya has become gray.
I entertain the idea that I might've gone to the past.

-Event room
The moment that we put the Sekimeiya in a cold environment, it becomes white again. We lock the cabinet manually.
We hear a door closing outside of the room.
-Crystal floor
We search for the person who made the sound. Erina, Isla, Katei, and I look through the hallway A rooms while Shiroya, Akaro, and Sai look through hallway B's.
Nobody is found. Sai, doubting Katei's word, finds the Sekimeiya in the storeroom.
-Event room
Erina and Isla stay by the stairs. The rest of us put the Sekimeiya inside the cabinet.
-Crystal room B4
We check Naomi's corpse and are unable to find the key for the Sekimeiya cabinet.
Before leaving, I detach a curtain from a cabinet and lay it over Naomi.

-Ashiya Tower
To find the person who made the noise, all of us stay on a different floor. Erina and Isla stay on floor 2, Sai stays on floor 3, Akaro stays on floor 4, Shiroya and I stay on floor 5, and Katei stays on floor 6.
-Floor 5
Shiroya and I talk in front of the elevator. Minutes later, Katei returns, and we all go back to the crystal floor.
-Crystal floor
Sai calls the elevator and assures us that it came from floor 5.
Sai reveals that while we were all on different floors, he heard the elevator three times. Everyone else says they didn't hear anything.
-Event room
The Sekimeiya hasn't been taken from the cabinet.
{u}Sai's wristwatch displays {time=11:20.}{/u}

-Event room
We hear the sound of a door closing yet again, although quieter than the previous time.
-Crystal floor
We search through the crystal floor and are unable to find anyone. Realizing that we forgot the bathrooms, and that the men's is locked, Katei retrieves the bathroom key from the security room.
-Men's bathroom
Inside the bathroom, we find Naomi's corpse.
-Crystal room B4
Naomi's original corpse is still in room B4.
-Men's bathroom
We inspect Naomi's second body.
-Event room
Sai takes the Sekimeiya out of the cabinet, but nothing seems to happen when we touch it.

-Crystal room B4
I realize that one of Naomi's keys might unlock the attic. I take it from her keyring.
Shiroya reveals that Akaro is no longer with us.
-Crystal floor
Next to the stairs, Erina and Isla deny having seen Akaro.
The elevator's keyhole confirms that our key will unlock the entrance to the attic.
We search through the crystal floor again and are unable to find Akaro.
-Floor 6
We unlock the attic's door.

-Attic's living room
Footprints reveal someone was in the attic recently.
The footprints seem to start at the sofa, go to the staircase, and then to the hallway.
* Attic footprints?|bg attic2
* Attic footprints?|bg attic3
There's an empty suitcase on the sofa, which looks like the one on the crystal floor.
-Attic
We inspect the attic and can't find anyone. It has four bedrooms, a kitchen, an empty storeroom, and a bathroom.

-Ashiya Tower
After confirming that nobody else is in the attic, we disable the elevator and thoroughly inspect every floor on the way down to the crystal floor.
-Crystal floor
The men's bathroom door seems to have moved. Akaro is inside.
Akaro appears unresponsive and tells us that he touched the Sekimeiya and teleported.
Shiroya covers Naomi's second body with a curtain.
-Event room
I check that the Sekimeiya is inside the cabinet. I touch it and feel no response.

-Attic
We leave Akaro in the men's bathroom and return to the attic.
-Right bedroom
Shiroya, Erina, Isla, and I rest in the right bedroom.
I notice a voice recorder inside Isla's purse. 
We play a saved audio file that implies we'll be trapped in the tower for at least a month. We hear Akaro, Sai, and Isla's voices. Erina and I are mentioned to still be there.
Sai and Katei arrive. They found a note in the kitchen that reveals that Naomi's job was to maintain the attic and keep it tidy.
Shiroya finds the Sekimeiya cabinet key in her purse.

-Ashiya Tower
Shiroya and I leave the bedroom and walk to the crystal floor. On the fifth floor, we come across Akaro, who's going to the attic.
-Event room
The Sekimeiya is no longer in the cabinet.
-Crystal room B3
Shiroya finds the Sekimeiya under a cushion in a cabinet.

-Security room
I appear in the security room after touching the Sekimeiya and fall to the floor.
The {u}computer says it's {time=11:10}{/u}, letting me estimate that I traveled forty minutes to the past.
-Hallway A
I see the group coming from the upper floors.
-Cleaning room
I wait in the cleaning room, staring at the men's bathroom.
Naomi comes from hallway C and looks inside the men's bathroom. She is pulled in by someone.
I run to save Naomi, but the door is slammed and locked from the inside. Recognizing it as the sound we heard from the event room, I run to the second floor.

-Floor 2 
I wait in the floor 2 partitions until the group goes to the attic. I confirm that nobody walked up before that point.
-Crystal floor
I see that Naomi is dead in the bathroom. I look through every room and am unable to find Akaro.
-Cleaning room
I notice that I was the one who moved the bathroom's door. That's what causes the group to approach it and find Akaro inside when they come from the attic.
The group goes back to the attic and leaves Akaro in the bathroom.
Akaro walks to the attic.
-Men's bathroom
I'm unable to find anything of importance after Akaro leaves.
I hear a sound outside the bathroom.

-Hallway A
I find Sai in hallway A. We're both shocked to see each other.
-Lobby
Sai has the gray Sekimeiya in his hip pack. Soon after he takes it out, it suddenly turns white.
-Crystal room B3
Shiroya is not in the room where I traveled from.
-Event room
I prevent Sai from running away, and we put the Sekimeiya in its cabinet.

-Security room
I bring Sai to the security room and notice that the door wasn't shut. The computer monitors are on, and the {u}time displayed is {time=11:57.}{/u}
The computer monitors power off due to prolonged inactivity. According to Sai, that means the computer hasn't been used in fifty minutes.
The screen of Sai's wristwatch is blank.
-Attic's living room
We obtain a lithium battery for Sai's wristwatch.
-Floor 6
We swap the batteries, and the wristwatch powers on. The time and date show "--:--" and "9999-12-31" respectively.
-Crystal floor
Sai manages to run away.
-Security room
The {u}computer shows it's {time=12:18.}{/u}
I leave at {time=12:31} after failing to display the live footage of the cameras.

-Hallway A
I reunite with Shiroya. She tells me she also traveled forty minutes to the past at the moment that I touched the Sekimeiya. She appeared in the partitions on the second floor.
-Crystal floor
We can't find the Sekimeiya in the event room or in room B3.
-Right bedroom
We return to the attic's bedroom and meet up with everyone else. {u}Sai's wristwatch displays {time=12:37}{/u}, and people claim he didn't leave the attic.
-Crystal floor
We go to the crystal floor to find the Sekimeiya. In the event room, we realize that Sai isn't with us, but we're able to find him in front of the cleaning room. When he sees us, he walks to hallway C.
-Cleaning room
Shiroya and I enter the room Sai had been about to open while Katei chases after Sai.

-Attic's living room
I suddenly find myself in the living room.
Shiroya appears from the hallway, and we realize that both of us just traveled from the cleaning room.
-Left bedroom
We go to the upper level of the left bedroom.
We estimate that we traveled at {time=12:40} and went one hour to the past. Shiroya and I seemed to have appeared in the locations we'd been at {time=12:10.}
Both of us fall asleep.

-Left bedroom
Shiroya and I reawaken.
-Attic
The door to the staircase has been closed, telling us that the group already left the right bedroom. We walk to the crystal floor.
-Cleaning room
The cleaning cart has disappeared. Three cleaning buckets, which were under it, are still there. The white Sekimeiya is inside one.
Touching the Sekimeiya doesn't make us travel, and I notice that it's cold.
-Crystal room B4
I take a key from Naomi's keyring.
-Staff room
We're able to use the key to open a locker, and we lock the Sekimeiya inside it.
-Hallway B
We can't find anyone in any of the hallway B rooms.
-Lobby
Erina, Akaro, Katei, and Sai are next to the metallic shutter.

-Lobby
Sai tells us what happened while we were sleeping.
After Shiroya and I disappeared from the cleaning room, Sai, Erina, Isla, and Akaro were also unable to find Katei. After they searched the entire crystal floor, Isla was drawn to a cabinet in room A5. She let out a yell before falling in and disappearing.
Erina found the cabinet empty when she looked inside it. The group searched the building for Isla, but they couldn't find her. After waiting in the lobby, Katei appeared from hallway A, and he was told what had happened. They looked at the cabinet where Isla had disappeared and found her dead body. Then, they waited next to the shutter until the arrival of myself and Shiroya.

-Crystal room A5
I see Isla's body in the cabinet, and next to it is the white Sekimeiya.
-Cleaning room
Everyone verifies that the Sekimeiya is no longer in the cleaning room.
-Event room
I bring the Sekimeiya from room A5 to its cabinet.
-Crystal room A5
A quick glance reveals no blood or apparent wounds on Isla's corpse.

-Lobby
We all wait in the lobby.
Katei and Sai leave the lobby and don't immediately return. Before I go to find them, Katei comes back.
Shiroya and I go find Sai.

-Event room
The Sekimeiya is still in the cabinet.
-Crystal room B4
The temperature of one of the cabinets is set to 0ºC. We change it to "room temperature".
-Storeroom
Shiroya finds the mechanism that uncovers a secret corridor. At the end of it, there's a door without a handle.
The others come and see the secret corridor.
-Event room
Erina suggests locking ourselves up in one place until {time=21:00.}

-Right bedroom
The key to the Sekimeiya cabinet is still in the bedroom.
-Event room
We lock the Sekimeiya inside the cabinet.
-Right bedroom
We inspect the room and make sure none of us are hiding anything.
We lock ourselves inside the bedroom.
{u}Sai's wristwatch displays {time=15:08.}{/u}

-Right bedroom
Erina, Shiroya, and I go to the upper level of the bedroom, where Shiroya presents the possibility of Isla's friend being Isla herself.
Katei comes up from the hatch, accusing me of being behind all the deaths.
We realize that Akaro and Sai have escaped.
The inner chain isn't set, and the key to the Sekimeiya cabinet is gone.

-Right bedroom
Akaro knocks from the outside. He opens the door, which has the key inserted on his side.
Akaro claims not to know Katei, and many of his memories contradict ours. We close the door again and set the chain.
We leave Akaro on the bed while the rest of us go to the upper level of the bedroom.

-Right bedroom
I wonder whether Akaro and Sai escaped the bedroom by thinking up a causal loop.
I'm unable to execute a causal loop myself.
We realize that Akaro has escaped again. This time, the chain is still set.
Katei takes the bedroom key from Erina's pocket and unlocks the door. He and Erina leave.

-Right bedroom
Shiroya and I reattach the door handles.
-Kitchen
I try to have some tap water, but it's not drinkable.
-Ashiya Tower
We notice that the elevator was reenabled. As we're walking down the floors, we hear the elevator once on floors 4 and 3.

-Crystal floor
The elevator is on the crystal floor.
-Event room
The Sekimeiya is not inside the cabinet.
-Staff room
The Sekimeiya is not inside Naomi's locker.
-Women's bathroom
I flush the key to Naomi's locker away, but nothing seems to happen as a result.
-Crystal room B6
We find the white Sekimeiya on the floor of room B6.

-Right bedroom
Shiroya and I travel from room B6 to the right attic bedroom.
-Attic
We determine that we traveled a few minutes to the past. Shiroya calls the elevator, and we realize that the last two times we heard it were our doing. We take it to the crystal floor.
-Lobby
We conclude that we traveled five minutes to the past and appeared where we'd been ten minutes before traveling.
Shiroya notices a drop of blood near the hallway A door.
I see that the key to Naomi's locker is still in my pocket, which confirms that a past body of mine was replicated.
-Women's bathroom
I flush Naomi's locker key away again.
-Crystal room B6
The Sekimeiya is not in the room.
We find the Sekimeiya inside a drawer of a cabinet after noticing it wasn't properly shut.

-Ashiya Tower
In front of the event room, Atsuki touches the Sekimeiya and finds himself in the dark. Thanks to a faint light, he realizes he's in the lobby of Ashiya Tower.
While he's in hallway B, a robotic voice coming from the security room plays throughout the floor. Atsuki realizes it's not addressing him, and he rushes to the staff room, where he can't be recorded.
After a very long wait in the dark, the lights suddenly turn on.
Atsuki hears a sound in the hallway, and soon after, the door to the staff room is opened by a man carrying a black suitcase.
The man pushes Atsuki against the wall, making him rapidly lose consciousness. Before Atsuki's world fades, he sees four people in front of him, all of whom he recognizes—two men, a woman, and a girl.
Atsuki dies in a world devoid of sense—a frozen world that had defied a very important rule.
Ending: Ethereal Arc

-Event room
We decide not to activate the Sekimeiya and lock it inside its cabinet.
We see another drop of blood on the floor.
-Security room
Nobody is in any of the hallway A rooms, and in the security room, we find Katei's body lying in a pool of blood under the desk. His skull has a large crack.
We find a message on the computer's middle screen: "{time=10:04}: Camera(s) disabled and associated footage erased". {u}The time displayed is {time=17.}{/u}
-Hallway A
We can still see the green lights on the cameras.

-Crystal floor
Shiroya and I search together to find Erina. We don't find anyone in the mechanical room or in the first rooms in hallway B.
-Crystal room B4
Erina's body is on the floor next to Naomi's, soaked in blood. We cover it with a curtain.
-Event room
Shiroya and I wait in the event room after confirming that the Sekimeiya is still in the cabinet.

-Event room
I fall asleep and am woken up by footsteps. I see Shiroya in hallway B wearing different clothes, and the moment she sees me, she walks away.
I wake up the Shiroya who's still in the event room. I tell her what I saw and am unable to find the other Shiroya.
-Security room
The {u}computer displays {time=17:29.}{/u}
-Right bedroom
We walk to the attic. In the wardrobe of the right bedroom are the clothes the other Shiroya was wearing.
I draw a cross on the collar of the shirt I saw Shiroya wearing.
-Attic
We call the elevator and press the lowest button, but we stop on the third floor.

-Floor 3
A knife swings at me from the partitions.
-Attic
Shiroya and I are chased, but we're able to lock ourselves in the attic.
We confirm we're alone.
-Left bedroom
We hear someone walking in the hallway.
-Attic's storeroom
Unable to decide on an escaping method, we wait in the storeroom.
-Floor 6
We walk out of the attic. The exit door is unlocked, and Shiroya locks it with the key we'd left next to it.
-Floor 4
Sai swings a knife at me from behind.

-Ashiya Tower
Atsuki and Shiroya board the elevator on the third floor and bring it to the attic.
They find the right bedroom's key in the drawer, but before they can lock themselves inside, Sai knocks Shiroya away from the door.
Sai stabs Atsuki. Shiroya attempts to stop him, but Sai slices her across the chest without giving it much thought. Sai stabs Atsuki repeatedly until his senses fade.
Ending: Pendulum

-Ashiya Tower
Atsuki and Shiroya board the elevator on the third floor. As it's moving up, they press the stop button and remain stationary between two floors.
Once a long wait passes, Atsuki looks up and sees a hand stabbing a knife into his chest. He can't comprehend even a single piece of the ridiculous last image his brain perceives before his sight blackens.
Ending: Personal Paradox

-Floor 3
I decide not to take the elevator.
-Event room
We run to the event room. The Sekimeiya is still locked inside the cabinet.
I collide with Sai after dashing to hallway B.
Sai's will to kill me seems to fade away. After he asks me what time it is, he says the {u}time on his wristwatch is {time=17:41.}{/u}
Sai reveals he wants the Sekimeiya that's inside the cabinet. He leaves his knife on the floor and runs to hallway B.

-Hallway B
Before I can look at the hallway, I hear one of its doors closing.
I find a new key in the cleaning room, but I'm unable to find Sai inside any room in hallway B.
-Hallway A
After looking at the mechanical room, I return to the event room from hallway A. Shiroya looks at the bathrooms and meets back up with me.
-Event room
Sai unlocks the cabinet and takes out the Sekimeiya.
Approximately fifteen minutes later, Shiroya and I rush him. With a quick reaction, Sai touches the Sekimeiya and disappears, causing Shiroya to vanish with him.
*Event Room Positioning|bg sr1

-Event room
Approximately five minutes after Sai and Shiroya disappear, the Sekimeiya turns white. I put it inside the cabinet.
-Crystal floor
I circle around the floor, wondering if I'm alone in the building. When I return to the event room, I take the Sekimeiya out of the cabinet, debating whether or not to use it.
-Staff room
I realize that the key I found in the cleaning room resembles the one for Naomi's locker. I bring the Sekimeiya to the staff room and manage to open a new locker.
A winter coat and a pair of pants are inside it. In the coat, I find a set of keys and a spying bug.
I touch the Sekimeiya when I estimate it's been out of the cabinet for fifteen minutes.

-Event room
I appear in the event room, facing the covered cabinet.
-Hallway A
I find my past self walking in hallway A, which tells me I went about twenty minutes to the past.
-Ashiya Tower
I look through floors 2 to 6, but I realize the attic's door is locked and that Shiroya disappeared with its key.
The elevator is still on the third floor.
-Crystal floor
I'm unable to find anyone in any of the hallway A rooms.
-Security room
I'm in the {u}security room from {time=18:24} to {time=18:30.}{/u}
-Staff room
I return to the staff room and find the gray Sekimeiya on the floor, which I lock in the new locker. I sit on the floor to rest.
As I'm about to leave, I notice a note next to where I was sitting.

-Hallway B
After crying out Shiroya's name, I hear footsteps coming from the lobby. Shiroya is there, but she's wearing the clothes from the attic.
Erina appears from hallway C with bloodstained clothing.
Erina's body is no longer in room B4. I realize that we didn't confirm her death.
-Event room
We follow Erina to the event room and find the Sekimeiya in the cabinet. Erina rolls it into her purse.
Sai appears from hallway A.
I see the note in Erina's purse. She gives it to me, and I quickly stuff it in one of my pockets.
Erina claims to have seen Miiya.
After approximately fifteen minutes of charge time, Erina activates the Sekimeiya.

-Event room
Sai is the only person to disappear. The Sekimeiya vanishes from Erina's purse and appears in the cabinet.
*Event Room Positioning|bg sr5
-Staff room
I confirm that the Sekimeiya I hid in the new locker is not there.
-Hallway B
Sai appears from the lobby and Akaro from the event room. Both of them are taken aback by Shiroya's presence.
{u}Sai's wristwatch displays {time=18:43}{/u}, which is twenty minutes behind the real time I estimate.
Out of nowhere, Shiroya runs to the attic and tells us not to follow her.
-Hallway C
We wait next to the elevator.
When {u}Sai's wristwatch displays {time=19:08}{/u}, we go to the attic. Erina and I take the elevator while Sai and Akaro go up the stairs.

-Floor 3
The elevator suddenly stops on the third floor. That causes us to fall to the floor, and I injure my hand on the handrail.
-Event room
I take the elevator down by myself and run to the event room. The Sekimeiya isn't in the cabinet.
-Staff room
After failing to find the Sekimeiya in the cleaning room and B6, I find it in the unknown person's locker.

-Hallway B
I touch the Sekimeiya and appear at the front of hallway B, looking toward hallway C. My wound has stopped bleeding, but it's still there.
I hear voices in the event room, which lets me estimate that I appeared a couple minutes before the time only Sai traveled.
-Security room
The {u}computer displays {time=18:54.}{/u}
-Hallway A
I slam the door to the storeroom and produce a loud sound we didn't originally hear.
-Men's bathroom (Floor 2)
I stay in a bathroom on floor 2. Shiroya no longer seems to go to the attic.
-Floor 3

entries.new: 入夜之后

entries.text: I'd been mindlessly staring at the wall in front of me for a few minutes. When that finally registered, I slowly spun around.
entries.new: 我对着眼前的墙壁呆呆望了好几分钟。等终于回过神来，才慢慢转过身去。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd always thought I'd be quick at adapting to sudden changes, but I'd recently realized how mistaken that was. Still unable to process everything, my brain continually struggled to accept that the previous few days had really happened.
entries.new: 我一直以为自己面对突发变故总能很快适应，最近才发现根本不是这样。那几天的事，我至今还回不过神来，脑子里怎么也接受不了那是真的。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I wasn't familiar with the walls around me, but I'd always known of the place. Next to me was Shiroya, less willing to acknowledge her surroundings. Keeping her gaze on the floor, she suddenly spoke for the first time since we'd entered.
entries.new: ……四周的墙壁对我来说很陌生，但这地方我早有耳闻。身旁的 Shiroya 却更不愿意面对周围的一切。她始终盯着地面，忽然开口——这是进来之后她第一次说话。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I think it'll be time soon.
entries.new: ……我想，快到时候了。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yeah, probably less than twenty minutes.
entries.new: 嗯，大概不到二十分钟。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That was all I managed to muster. Even though I was still the same Atsuki as always, it felt like I'd been rewritten into an entirely different entity in only a few days.
entries.new: 我只挤得出这一句。我明明还是原来的我，却觉得短短几天里，自己已经被改写成另一个人了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't try to say anything else. During the previous two weeks, I'd grown accustomed to those brief interactions with Shiroya. After I spoke, the lost look in her eyes returned. We had both agreed to go together, but it seemed like neither of us knew what we were doing.
entries.new: 我没有再说别的。过去两周，我已经习惯了和 Shiroya 这样简短地说上几句。等我说完，她眼里那种茫然又回来了。我们明明说好一起过来，可到头来，两个人好像都不知道自己在做什么。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We awkwardly scanned the vast hall, moving forward tiny steps at a time and awaiting further instructions.
entries.new: 我们局促地打量着这座空旷的大厅，一小步一小步地往前挪，等着接下来的指示。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Neither of us had any strength; I'd known Shiroya for more than fifteen years, and not once had she looked so empty. On top of everything else, I hadn't even been able to make her feel any better.
entries.new: 我们俩都没什么力气了。我认识 Shiroya 超过十五年，从没见她这样空落过。更糟的是，我连让她好受一点都做不到。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Despite that, at almost {time=9}, we were inside Ashiya Tower.
entries.new: 尽管如此，快到 {time=9} 的时候，我们还是走进了芦屋塔。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The biggest building in Yushibana—the town where we'd always lived. It was situated on the outskirts, and we had never entered it before.
entries.new: 那是丰花镇上最大的一栋楼——我们一直生活在这个镇上。楼在镇子边上，我们却从没进去过。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: From the outside, the tower's contrast with its surroundings was immense. Beyond all the similar-looking houses, its size made it visible anywhere in the town. It was that contrast which had caused it to be called a "tower", but it was only as big as an urban building. The structure itself was more or less a cube, essentially as wide as it was tall, but it seemed towering to people who had spent their whole lives in a rural area.
entries.new: 从外面看，这座塔和周围的反差大得惊人。附近全是差不多的房子，可它体量太大，站在镇上哪儿都能望见。也正因为这份反差，它才被叫作「塔」，其实它也就是城里一栋楼的规模。整栋楼差不多是个立方体，宽和高几乎一样，但对一辈子住在乡下的人来说，已经显得很高耸了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was a place Shiroya and I had always avoided because of the stigma associated with it. A significant amount of the citizens opposed the tower's existence due to both the group who owned it and its unnatural size.
entries.new: Shiroya 和我一直避开这个地方，因为它名声不好。不少镇民都反对这座塔，既因为拥有它的那伙人，也因为它的体量大得不正常。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I wasn't very familiar with the topic. Apparently, decades in the past, when the building hadn't been anywhere near as large, it was the original Ashiya family's home. It was known that they were a shady family, but they never suffered any real consequences. At that time, they held a silent power over the town, and over the years, it gradually grew stronger.
entries.new: 这些事我知道得不多。据说几十年前，这栋楼还远没有今天这么大，是芦屋家最早的老宅。人人都知道这家人来路不正，可他们从没真正吃过亏。那时他们在镇上暗中掌权，多年下来，势力越来越大。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They became the image of Yushibana. Anyone visiting from the outside knew about that family before anything else in the town. Over the years, the old residence transformed into a focal point for business and tourism.
entries.new: 他们成了丰花的门面。外地来的人，最先听说的就是这家人，之后才轮到镇上的其他事。多年下来，那座老宅渐渐成了商贸和观光的中心。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had never immersed myself in the matter, but that was common information that I couldn't even recall where I'd heard first.
entries.new: 我从没去深究过这些，可这都是人人皆知的说法，我连最初是从哪儿听来的都想不起来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The place was some sort of museum, and behind it extended a mountain range that encircled Yushibana. It was known for housing numerous caves that held valuable gemstones, so enthusiasts tended to visit often. The Ashiya family had taken advantage of it and utilized their building as a gallery for the different gemstones that could be found in the nearby mountains.
entries.new: 这地方算是一座博物馆，它背后是一道环抱着丰花的山脉。那片山里有很多洞窟，出产宝石，所以好这口的人常来。芦屋家借着这份地利，把自家大楼当成展馆，陈列附近山里挖出来的各种宝石。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And when that happened, the part of the town in favor of the tower increased due to the incoming flow of people who specialized in those gemstones. That was what caused a split in the population; the younger residents generally didn't mind Ashiya, while the older maintained their private discontent.
entries.new: 随着专为宝石而来的人越来越多，镇上支持这座塔的人也多了起来。人们因此分成了两派：年轻的大多不介意芦屋家，年长的则暗暗不满。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That was why we had never entered it, and on top of our more recent circumstances, I thought Shiroya might've been experiencing a feeling of betrayal simply by being there. While I couldn't say I shared that strong of an emotion toward it, I wasn't very fond of the whole thing either.
entries.new: 我们一直没进去过，原因就在于此。再加上近来这些事，我想 Shiroya 单是待在这里，或许就有种被背叛的感觉。我虽说不上有她那么强烈的情绪，对整个地方也谈不上喜欢。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}The reason why we were inside wasn't one I could easily put into words.
entries.new: ……{w}我们为什么会在里面，我很难说清楚。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There had been constant publicity about the day's event for two weeks. According to Ashiya, they were going to showcase a major discovery, one found in the very same mountains around the town.
entries.new: 两周以来，关于今天这场活动的宣传铺天盖地。按芦屋家的说法，他们要展示一项重大发现，那东西正是在镇子周围的山里找到的。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But that wasn't something that particularly interested me, and I wasn't sure what to expect. Our motivation for coming to the tower wasn't anything as simple as curiosity.
entries.new: 可我对这个并不太感兴趣，也说不清自己到底在期待什么。我们来这座塔，并不是单纯出于好奇。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was December 15th. Outside, the environment was cold and coated in snow, and while the temperature inside was regulated, we'd been outside for so long that we still felt unpleasant.
entries.new: 那天是十二月十五日。外面天寒地冻，到处是雪。屋里虽然有温控，可我们在外头待得太久，身上还是不舒服。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I glanced at Shiroya, who didn't return my look. Feeling slightly agitated, I turned a little.
entries.new: 我瞥了 Shiroya 一眼，她没有看我。我有点烦躁，稍微转了转身。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I could see a line of people who had come thanks to Ashiya's ambitious advertisements. Shiroya and I had been at the front of it for a long time.
entries.new: 我能看见一队人，都是被芦屋家大张旗鼓的宣传引来的。Shiroya 和我已经在队伍最前面待了很久。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Next to us was a man I'd never seen before. He was tall and had dark hair, and like us, he seemed distant from everyone else. I hadn't seen him so much as look at me, so I hadn't paid attention to him.
entries.new: 我们旁边站着一个从没见过的男人。他个子很高，头发乌黑，和我们一样，似乎跟旁人都隔着一段距离。我从没见他看过我一眼，也就没去留意他。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We were next to him because we would go see the gemstone in groups of three. Since we'd been the initial three to show up, we formed the first group.
entries.new: 我们之所以挨着他，是因为参观宝石要三人一组。我们是头三个到场的，于是成了第一组。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The entrance fee had been expensive, but we'd paid it well in advance. From our perspective, it had been worth it.
entries.new: 门票很贵，不过我们早就付过了。我们觉得这钱花得值。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We remained by the door that would open at {time=9}, simply waiting for that to happen. At our left was another door that would open at the same time, and according to what we'd been told, both led to the main floor of the tower.{w} On that particular day, not many people seemed to care about that, as everyone who could be seen was in our same line.
entries.new: 我们待在 {time=9} 会打开的那扇门前，就等着门开。左边还有一扇门也会同时开，听说两扇门都通向塔的主层。{w} 不过今天好像没多少人在意这个，能看见的人全排在我们这条队里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: For a moment, I wondered what the big deal was. Yushibana wasn't a large town, so the amount of people waiting behind us was fairly impressive. All that for a gemstone didn't seem quite right to me.
entries.new: 有那么一瞬间，我在想这有什么大不了的。丰花不算大，身后排队的人却多得有点惊人。只为一块宝石就弄成这样，我总觉得不太对劲。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But perhaps it made sense, given that it was Ashiya's event. They cared about appearances, as anyone could attest. They had their hands in all types of business, but the most important one was looking good.
entries.new: 不过，既然是芦屋家办的活动，也许就说得通了。谁都知道他们极重门面。他们什么生意都插手，但最看重的还是让自己显得体面。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Apart from the line, the only other people in the lobby were guards talking with a policeman, a woman behind the reception desk checking everyone's tickets, and a janitor who had been scrubbing the same part of the floor for a while.
entries.new: 除了排队的人，大厅里就只有几个正和警察说话的门卫、接待台后核验门票的女子，以及一个在同一块地板上擦了半天的清洁工。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was all unsettling and alien. The event itself was an abstract thing to me, and my view on the people who ran it was far from positive. All I could do was look at things and wait for it all to start.
entries.new: 这一切都让人不安又陌生。这场活动对我来说很虚，我对主办方的印象也远谈不上好。我能做的只有四处看看，等着开场。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We'd been asked to leave our phones outside for the duration of our stay, as nothing of the sort was permitted in the building. That meant that I had no way of looking at the time; there weren't any clocks on the walls.
entries.new: 我们被告知，逗留期间要把手机留在外面，楼内一律不许携带这类东西。这就意味着我没法看时间——墙上也没有挂钟。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Adding the fact that the person I was with was clearly uncomfortable and trying to hide it, the long wait had been much more tedious than I'd hoped.
entries.new: 再加上身边那人明显不自在，还努力掩饰着，这段漫长的等待比我预想的要难熬得多。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I continued looking at her, not knowing how to deal with the situation better. Finally, after minutes of looking down, she suddenly lifted her head as if she'd just remembered that she was in a public environment.
entries.new: 我一直看着她，不知道该怎么办才好。她低头看了好几分钟，最后忽然抬起头，像是这才想起自己是在公共场合。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Following behind, she looked at me and seemed to try to smile.
entries.new: 接着，她看向我，似乎想挤出一点笑容。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But it was barely visible before vanishing again.
entries.new: 可那笑意还未成形，便又消失了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I kept falling back into negative thoughts. No matter how I tried, I couldn't help that.
entries.new: ……我又一次次陷回那些消沉的念头里。不管怎么努力，都拦不住自己。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I needed to be stronger and help lift Shiroya out of the pit she was in, but that was tricky, seeing as I first had to get out of the same one.
entries.new: 我得振作起来，把 Shiroya 从她掉进去的那个坑里拉出来；可我自己也陷在同一个坑里，得先爬出去才行，这就难办了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So I just struggled against my feelings, wishing all the while that I could go back to how things had been before.
entries.new: 于是我只能跟自己的情绪较劲，一边盼着一切能回到从前的样子。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Minutes later, a well-dressed man who'd been standing near the entrance told us that if we weren't waiting for the event, we could go through the left door.
entries.new: 几分钟后，一个衣着考究、一直站在入口附近的男人告诉我们：要是我们不打算等这场活动开始，可以从左边那扇门进去。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shortly after, a tall, blonde woman wearing a suit entered through the one on the right.
entries.new: 不久之后，一个穿西装的高个金发女人从右边那扇门走了进来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd seen her in a coat earlier, before she'd disappeared through one of the doors. She looked over everyone present and began to explain what the procedure would be.
entries.new: 我先前见过她穿大衣，后来她进了某扇门，不见了。她环视在场的所有人，开始说明流程。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sorry for the wait, everyone. We'll now begin the group entrances.{w} My name is Naomi. I'll be chaperoning today's guided visit.
entries.new: 各位，久等了。现在开始分组入场。{w}我是 Naomi，今天的参观由我来带。
entries.speaker: sa

entries.text: As you likely already know, groups of three will move forward in turns. Each viewing is estimated to take approximately fifteen minutes.{w} Once inside, I will personally explain what we have prepared, and I will also be available to answer questions within the specified time.
entries.new: 各位大概已经知道，三人一组，依次进场。每次参观预计十五分钟左右。{w}进去之后，我会亲自为大家讲解我们准备的展品，也会在规定时间内回答大家的问题。
entries.speaker: sa

entries.text: Naomi's explanation was directed at everyone present, but it was hard to believe anyone farther back could've heard her. She continued in a monotone voice.
entries.new: Naomi 这番话是冲着全场所有人说的，可站在后面的人多半听不见。她继续用毫无起伏的语调说着。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Keep in mind that phones and video cameras are strictly prohibited. I ask for all of you to please be patient and await your turn.
entries.new: 请记住，手机和摄像机一律不准带入。也请大家耐心等候，轮到了再进。
entries.speaker: sa

entries.text: When her scripted message was over, she relaxed her posture and directed her look at us.
entries.new: 那套照本宣科的话讲完，她整个人才松下来，目光转向我们。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You three are the first group, correct?
entries.new: 你们三位就是第一批，对吧？
entries.speaker: sa

entries.text: Seconds later, nobody had answered. The two people at my sides had barely paid attention to her, so I spoke before she would have to ask again.
entries.new: 几秒过去，没人应声。我身边那两个人也没怎么理会她，我只好赶在她再问一遍之前先开口。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yes.
entries.new: 是的。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...All right, then. Please follow me to the event room to be the first to see the Sekimeiya.
entries.new: ……好吧。那请随我去活动室，你们会是第一批见到 Sekimeiya 的人。
entries.speaker: sa

entries.text: I'd heard that word many times recently. As soon as she said it, she turned around and walked through the same door she'd entered from.
entries.new: 这个词我最近已听过无数遍。她刚说完，就转身从进来时的那扇门走了出去。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked to my right to check on Shiroya. Her demeanor hadn't changed, but she was aware of the situation.
entries.new: 我转头往右看 Shiroya 怎么样。她神色如常，却也知道眼下的局面。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: By the time I turned back, the man on my left had nearly reached the door. It seemed he was taking the initiative despite his unenthused appearance.
entries.new: 等我回过头，左边的男人已经快走到门口了。他看上去提不起兴致，倒先迈开了步子。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Rather, it was probably better to think of myself as lagging behind than him being proactive. I followed, motioning to Shiroya as I did. She approached me, still wearing her heavy-looking coat.
entries.new: 与其说他积极，不如说是我落后了。我跟上去，一边朝 Shiroya 示意。她朝我走来，身上还穿着那件看上去很厚重的外套。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We found ourselves in a long hallway. We could see many doors lining each wall, some opened and connected by a decorative handrail. However, there were no traces of Naomi or the man.
entries.new: 我们来到一条长长的走廊。两侧墙上排着许多门，有几扇敞开着，门与门之间由一道装饰扶手相连。可是，Naomi 和那个男人都不见踪影。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The floor seemed pointlessly wide. Up to the end of the hall, I could see a number of security cameras hanging from the ceiling. As we started walking, unclear about where to go, I found it appropriate to try talking with Shiroya again.
entries.new: 地面宽得有些莫名其妙。一直望到走廊尽头，天花板上悬着好几台监控摄像头。我们开始往前走，却不清楚该去哪里，我觉得正好可以再和 Shiroya 说说话。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Are you feeling better?
entries.new: 你好些了吗？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Oh... Yeah, I'm fine. Don't worry about it.
entries.new: 哦……嗯，我没事。别在意。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...She continued walking, assuming that was the end of our exchange.
entries.new: ……她大概觉得话已到此为止，继续往前走。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I tried to press it a bit further.
entries.new: 我想再多问一句。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Do you regret coming?
entries.new: ……你后悔来这儿吗？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...No, of course not.{w} I'm seriously glad we're here. I mean it.
entries.new: ……不，当然不后悔。{w}能来这里，我真的很高兴。我是认真的。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I know how you feel, okay? It's... the same for me. It doesn't help a lot to say it, but I don't want to see you sad.
entries.new: 你的心情我明白，好吗？我也……一样。说出来未必有什么用，但我不想看你难过。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I'm here because I want to be, Atsuki. I'm okay. This is where I need to be right now. Sorry, I must look terrible.
entries.new: Atsuki，我是因为想来才来的。我没事。现在我就该待在这里。抱歉，我这副样子一定很难看。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: She wasn't being very convincing.
entries.new: 这话听着并不怎么让人信服。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...You know this isn't something you need to apologize for. Nothing about this is your fault.
entries.new: ……你该知道，这没什么好道歉的。那件事没有一处是你的错。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I'm... not so sure. I wish I didn't have to be a drag for you now.
entries.new: 我……不太确定。真希望现在不是我拖累你。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: H-Hey, come on. If you want to leave, we still can. Don't feel like you have to push yourself for my sake.
entries.new: 喂、喂，别这样。你要是想走，我们现在也能走。别为了我勉强自己。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It's all right. Thank you.{w} Let's continue, though. I was the one who wanted to do this.
entries.new: 没事的。谢谢你。{w}不过，我们继续走吧。当初想这么做的人是我。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Okay.
entries.new: 好。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We'd hoped coming to the exhibition would be for the better. Once it was settled that we wouldn't back out, I looked around hesitantly until a voice calling for us came from the middle of the hallway, through an open door.
entries.new: 我们原本希望来这个展览会能让情况好转。既然已经说好了不会打退堂鼓，我便迟疑地四下张望，直到走廊中段一扇敞开的门后传来招呼我们的声音。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You two, hurry up! The clock is ticking.
entries.new: 你们两个，快一点！时间不等人。
entries.speaker: sa

entries.text: Her unprofessional shout broke the silence and drew us forward.
entries.new: 她这一嗓子谈不上专业，却打破了寂静，把我们的脚步引了过去。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I saw her figure in a seemingly empty room. Through the other doors, there were cabinets covered by red cloths.
entries.new: 我看见她站在一间看似空荡的屋里。透过另外几扇门，能看到盖着红布的展示柜。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Good, we're all finally here. Now we can start.
entries.new: 好，人总算齐了。那就开始吧。
entries.speaker: sa

entries.text: Once I went inside, I realized my initial impression had been wrong. The room would've been barren if it weren't for a single cabinet covered by a velvet curtain.
entries.new: 走进去我才发现，先前的印象错了。屋里除了一个罩着天鹅绒遮布的柜子，什么都没有。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The black-haired man was there, yet again looking entirely aloof and fixing his eyes on the plain opposite wall.
entries.new: 那个黑发男人也在，还是一副全然不关心的样子，眼睛盯着对面那面光秃秃的墙。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: All right. It would be helpful if you could tell me your names since you know mine.
entries.new: 好。既然你们知道我的名字，那也请告诉我你们叫什么。
entries.speaker: sa

entries.text: While she said that, she closed the door we'd come through, and I took notice of the security camera in one of the corners, which was fitting for the place we were in. There was another closed door on the opposite wall, so we had fifteen minutes ahead of us where we would be shut inside.
entries.new: 说着，她关上了我们进来的那扇门。我注意到角落里装着监控摄像头——这地方有这种东西倒也寻常。对面墙上还有一扇紧闭的门，也就是说，接下来的十五分钟，我们都要被关在这间屋里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Naomi looked at me expectantly, probably because I'd been the one to speak earlier.
entries.new: Naomi 期待地看着我，大概是因为刚才开口的人是我。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki Hakutoki.
entries.new: Atsuki Hakutoki。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Shiroya Mirana.
entries.new: Shiroya Mirana。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Without being cajoled, Shiroya spoke her name. To my relief, she was looking directly at Naomi, and her posture was significantly less stiff than before.
entries.new: 不用人催，Shiroya 便报上了名字。让我安心的是，她直视着 Naomi，姿态也比先前松弛了许多。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The black-haired man didn't respond immediately when we eyed him.
entries.new: 我们看向那个黑发男人，他却没有立刻回应。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And your name?
entries.new: 还有你的名字？
entries.speaker: sa

entries.text: ...{w}Akaro.{w} Akaro Esata.
entries.new: ……{w}Akaro。{w}Akaro Esata。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Perfect. Happy to meet the three of you.
entries.new: 很好。很高兴见到你们三位。
entries.speaker: sa

entries.text: It was hard to read him. He looked passive, but he must've been interested in the exhibition.
entries.new: 我看不透他。他看上去无动于衷，可他对这场展览想必是有兴趣的。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Naomi moved aside and placed herself before the velvet curtain.{w} Then, she took out a keyring from her pocket as she got ready to begin the introduction.
entries.new: Naomi 走到一旁，站到天鹅绒遮布前。{w}接着，她从口袋里掏出一串钥匙，准备开始讲解。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As you might already know, what's behind this curtain is not to be taken lightly, and being the first public viewers is a bigger privilege than you might think.
entries.new: 你们或许已经知道，这遮布后的东西不容小觑；能作为第一批公众观赏者，这份殊荣比你们想的更大。
entries.speaker: sa

entries.text: What's being kept here is among the rarest pieces that we've ever seen, and it's only been two weeks since the discovery.
entries.new: 放在这里的，是我们见过的最稀有的藏品之一，而从发现到现在才过了两周。
entries.speaker: sa

entries.text: We estimate that the value of this cabinet's contents is immense. A proper appraisal has already occurred, but more estimates will come forth as everyone realizes just what we have on our hands.
entries.new: 这柜子里的东西，价值难以估量。虽说已经做过正式鉴定，可等大家都看清它究竟是什么，只怕还得再估一次。
entries.speaker: sa

entries.text: Part of the experience is the touch, so I will open the cabinet and let you experience it yourselves. However, I must insist that you be gentle and keep your hands inside the cabinet at all times.
entries.new: 这次体验的一部分就是亲手触摸，所以我会打开柜子，让你们自己感受。不过有件事我必须强调：动作要轻，手自始至终别伸出柜外。
entries.speaker: sa

entries.text: We know, and don't need this introduction, so let's move along. You've been praising this find of yours in every advertisement. Let's see how your claims hold up.
entries.new: 这些我们都知道，用不着这番介绍，直接进入正题。你们在每一条广告里都把这次的发现吹上了天。让我们看看你们的说法能不能站得住脚。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Akaro's sudden input took us by surprise, but it made it clear that he did actually care about the event.
entries.new: Akaro 突然插话，让我们有些意外，不过这也说明他确实在意这次活动。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: M-My apologies. Let's start, then.
entries.new: 抱、抱歉。那我们开始吧。
entries.speaker: sa

entries.text: Naomi put a small key into a lock on the left side of the cabinet and turned it.
entries.new: Naomi 把一把小钥匙插进展示柜左侧的锁孔，转动了一下。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Admittedly, all the build-up was making me slightly curious, but for all I knew, we were talking about a slightly shining rock, nothing that would ever interest me very much.
entries.new: 平心而论，被这么一番铺垫，我也起了几分好奇。可说白了，那多半只是块会微微发亮的石头，引不起我多少兴趣。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Let's stop with the teasing. Here's what you've come here to see, named "The Sekimeiya".
entries.new: 别再卖关子了。这就是各位此行的目的，它名为『The Sekimeiya』。
entries.speaker: sa

entries.text: With one hand, she grabbed the bottom of the curtain and began to raise it.
entries.new: 她一只手抓住遮布下沿，缓缓将它掀起。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But even though my focus should've been on the cabinet, something else took priority.
entries.new: 可我的注意力本该落在展示柜上，却偏偏被别的东西抢先夺走了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When I was least expecting it, smoke rose instead of the curtain, accompanied by a familiar, putrid smell that invaded the room.
entries.new: 就在我毫无防备之际，升起的不是遮布，而是浓烟；一股熟悉的腐臭随之弥漫开来，迅速充满了整个房间。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wha... What is this!?
entries.new: 这……这是什么！？
entries.speaker: sa

entries.text: Without bothering to ask myself questions, I tried to find Shiroya. At my right, I saw her face morphing into shock.
entries.new: 我顾不上多想，立刻去找 Shiroya。她就在我右手边，我看见她脸上一点点浮出惊愕。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki... Wha...
entries.new: Atsuki……怎么……
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Her last word faded out quietly, and it was then when I realized that my consciousness was getting cloudy. All of a sudden, the only thing I could see was very dark smoke filling my field of vision. I couldn't believe it was happening again.
entries.new: 她最后那个字轻轻消散，我这才意识到自己的意识正一点点模糊。转眼间，视野里只剩下浓黑的烟雾。我不敢相信，这种事竟然又发生了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Naomi's hand had immediately released the curtain, and she was trying to steady herself while covering her nose. I couldn't find Akaro until I looked down and saw that he had already fallen to the floor.
entries.new: Naomi 的手当即松开遮布，她捂住鼻子，努力稳住身子。我一时找不到 Akaro，低头才看见他已经倒在地上。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The smoke filled up the entire room at once. In just a few seconds, my legs stopped responding, and every effort at getting my muscles to obey me met with failure.
entries.new: 浓烟一下子充满了整个房间。不过几秒，我的双腿便不听使唤，无论怎么使劲，肌肉都不肯服从。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: At last, my entire body gave up, and I plummeted down. Thanks to the view I had from the floor, I could see Shiroya's outcome had not been any different, and from the falling noise I heard, the same could be said for Naomi.
entries.new: 终于，我浑身一软，重重栽倒在地。躺在那儿，我看见 Shiroya 也一样倒下了；听那声响，Naomi 想必也没能撑住。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Behind Shiroya was the door we'd come through. The smoke had covered the ceiling, so everything was dark. Amid the confusion, I was able to notice the lack of light under the door, something which should've been easily noticeable from where I was.
entries.new: Shiroya 身后就是我们进来的那扇门。烟雾遮住了天花板，四下昏暗。混乱之中，我仍注意到门缝下没有一丝光——从我当时的位置，应该一眼就能注意到。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After I ultimately accepted there was nothing I could do to salvage the situation, I had a few seconds where I could only think about what was going on. Our room and its surroundings were fully silent: I couldn't hear a thing despite what had happened, and I wasn't able to produce any noise.
entries.new: 最终我认了命，知道局面已无可挽回，只能趁着那几秒钟想想究竟是怎么回事。房间内外一片死寂：出了这种事，我却什么都听不见，自己也发不出半点声音。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the fuck had just happened? I was able to recognize how strange it was. Both doors had been closed, so I had no idea where the smoke came from.
entries.new: 这他妈到底是怎么回事？我清楚这有多蹊跷。两扇门都关着，我根本想不到烟是从哪儿来的。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Knowing the smoke was blotting out our awareness, I realized it had been done deliberately, and there were many reasons I could come up with as to why, going off what we'd just been told.
entries.new: 既然这烟能夺走我们的意识，那显然是有人刻意为之；结合刚才听到的那些话，我能想到的理由有不少。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As my remaining consciousness faded away, I could only hope I would quickly wake up to see Shiroya again. I wanted to pretend that I knew nothing would happen, but the images came back to me. ...Seeing that hole in the floor.
entries.new: 残余的意识渐渐消散，我只盼着能快些醒来，再见到 Shiroya。我想装作自己笃定不会有事，可那些画面又浮现眼前。……地板上的那个洞。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My heartbeat slowed and became inaudible. I knew that resisting was completely futile, so I closed my eyes, hoping to fast-forward to being awake again. The thought of dying there was pathetic, but without a choice in the matter, I resigned myself to what was happening.
entries.new: 心跳慢了下来，渐渐听不见了。我知道反抗毫无意义，便闭上眼睛，只盼能快进到苏醒的那一刻。想到自己可能死在这里，实在窝囊，可事到如今别无选择，我只能听天由命。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Before all my senses faded, the silence was broken by a loud alarm, which had taken a while to be broadcast after the appearance of the smoke. Further in the background, I briefly perceived a much fainter and rougher sound that I couldn't identify.
entries.new: 就在所有感官彻底消退之前，一阵刺耳的警报划破了寂静——它从烟雾出现到响起，隔了好一会儿。更远的背景里，我隐约捕捉到另一种声音，微弱而粗粝，辨不出是什么。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I lay on the floor of that smoky room with three other people, completely powerless and clueless.
entries.new: 我躺在那间烟雾弥漫的房间里，身边还有另外三个人，全然无能为力，也毫无头绪。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Soon after the alarm played, the darkness became absolute, and all my thoughts vanished.
entries.new: 警报响过不久，四周彻底陷入黑暗，我的思绪也尽数消散。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Cave-in
entries.new: 坍塌

entries.text: An indeterminate amount of time had passed. I was a complete mess, and a constant pain pounded against the interior of my skull.
entries.new: 不知过了多久。我整个人狼狈不堪，颅骨内侧一阵接一阵地作痛。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Nothing had changed apart from the walls and ceiling, which had been tainted by the smoke.
entries.new: 除了被烟熏黑的墙壁和天花板，一切都没有变。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As I confirmed that I was still in the event room, I tried to battle the intense headache mercilessly hammering me from the inside, focusing my vision in an attempt to spot Shiroya.
entries.new: 确认自己还在活动室后，我强忍着从颅内狠狠敲打的剧痛，凝神寻找 Shiroya。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There she was, still on the floor. She hadn't moved since I'd blacked out.
entries.new: 她就在那儿，仍躺在地上。从我昏过去起，她就没动过。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I used all the energy I could muster to try to rise, and after a few attempts, I was able to sit up.
entries.new: 我拼尽全身力气想爬起来，试了几次，总算坐了起来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: While I crawled to Shiroya, I looked behind me. As expected, Akaro's body still lay on the floor, but he was far from my first priority.
entries.new: 我一边朝 Shiroya 爬去，一边回头看了一眼。果然，Akaro 仍躺在地上，可他远不是我最先要管的。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I reached Shiroya and turned her to face me. Her eyes were half-open, and she seemed conscious, which was exactly what I needed to see.
entries.new: 我爬到 Shiroya 身边，把她扳过来面向我。她双眼半睁，似乎还有意识——这正是我最想看到的。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Are y—*cough* *cough*
entries.new: 你没——*咳* *咳*
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: My sentence was cut off by dry coughing that took over my body. It seemed I had inhaled a bit of the smoke, but it might've meant that we hadn't been unconscious for a long time.
entries.new: 话还没说完，一阵干咳便攫住了我。看来我吸进了一些烟——不过这也说明，我们昏过去的时间或许并不长。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yes... I think so. *cough*
entries.new: 嗯……我想是吧。*咳*
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Her eyes opened fully, and she tried to steady herself with an arm.
entries.new: 她完全睁开眼，用一只手臂撑住身子。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That smoke... W-Was it...?
entries.new: 那阵烟……难、难道是……？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Maybe. Liste—*cough* {w}Listen. We'll find out what happened. Just stay there for a minute, okay? Do you feel okay?
entries.new: 也许吧。听我——*咳*{w}听我说。发生了什么，我们总会弄清楚的。你先在那儿待一会儿，好吗？你感觉还好吗？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Y-Yes...
entries.new: 嗯……还好。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I could tell that she was barely keeping it together. She must've been afraid of the worst, just like I was, but that time we'd woken up safely.
entries.new: 我看得出她几乎撑不住了。她一定和我一样，往最坏处想过，可这一次，我们好歹平安醒了过来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked around me. It was a bizarre sight, and the disgusting smell was still present after the smoke had faded.{w} The room had been painted black. The curtain's beautiful red, the walls, the ceiling... They'd all been corrupted by an ugly, dark color, almost purple.
entries.new: 我环顾四周。眼前的景象诡异至极，烟雾散去后，那股恶臭依然残留。{w}整个房间都被染成了黑色。遮布原本漂亮的红色，还有墙壁、天花板……全被一种难看的深色侵蚀，近乎发紫。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The floor, however, had not received the same treatment. It had become gray, but it was nowhere near the strong black that consumed the ceiling.
entries.new: 地板却不一样。它变成了灰色，远没有天花板那种浓重的黑。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And there was something much more important that I quickly noticed.
entries.new: 而更重要的，是我很快注意到的另一件事。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Naomi's gone... She's not here.
entries.new: Naomi 不见了……她不在这儿。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...What? Y-You're right. Wh-Where could she have gone?
entries.new: ……什么？你、你说得对。她、她能去哪儿？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: The door's open.
entries.new: 门开着。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The door opposite the one we'd entered was very slightly ajar. Naomi could've woken up and left through it, maybe to understand what had happened after seeing that we were still knocked out.
entries.new: 我们进来的那扇门正对面那扇，微微开着一条缝。Naomi 也许醒了过来，从那儿出去了——或许是见我们还昏着，想去弄清到底发生了什么。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even reaching that small conclusion took a lot out of me, but the headache was beginning to fade almost as quickly as it had come on.
entries.new: 光是理出这么一点头绪，就已耗尽了我的心力，好在头痛来得急，退得也快。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I noticed our voices had woken Akaro, who still hadn't moved at all.
entries.new: 我这才发觉，我们的说话声把 Akaro 吵醒了——他先前一直一动不动。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Ugh.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: What the... fuck is this?
entries.new: 这他妈是怎么回事？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: He felt his face with his hand as he grimaced. Then, he slowly stood up and attempted to balance himself while perplexedly looking around him.
entries.new: 他抬手摸了摸自己的脸，皱起眉头。随后慢慢站起身，一边努力稳住身体，一边困惑地环顾四周。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hey, what is all this? You said Naomi's gone? What the fuck just happened...? I think a lot of smoke suddenly appeared out of nowhere, right? Did it knock us out?
entries.new: 喂，这到底是怎么回事？你说 Naomi 不见了？刚才到底他妈发生了什么……？我记得好像忽然凭空冒出好多烟，对吧？我们是被那烟弄晕的？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: For the first time, he started a conversation with us. Before answering, I began to clean my face, as the smoke had created a sticky mask on it as well.
entries.new: 这是他头一次主动跟我们搭话。我没有立刻回答，先擦起脸来——那烟雾也在我的脸上凝成了一层黏腻的薄膜。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I have no idea. But yes, th-that smoke must've had something in it that made us fall unconscious.
entries.new: 我完全不知道。不过没错，那、那烟里肯定掺了什么，才让我们失去意识的。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: And a few seconds before I fainted, a very loud alarm went off.
entries.new: 而且在我昏过去前几秒，响起了很刺耳的警报声。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: An alarm? I must've fallen unconscious too fast. All I remember is getting dizzy as hell out of nowhere and falling over.
entries.new: 警报？那我大概是晕得太快了。我只记得不知怎的头晕得厉害，接着就栽倒了。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: ...I don't think I heard it either. Did it say anything?
entries.new: ……我好像也没听见。它有说什么吗？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: No, it was only a loud sound.
entries.new: 没有，只是很响的声音。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: While I was still attempting to stand up, Akaro walked to the open door and looked through it.
entries.new: 我还在地上试着站起来，Akaro 已经走到敞开的那扇门前，探头往外看。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh... What the hell happened here?{w} It's dark in this room, but the hallway is too. The walls and ceiling are black, and I can't see anyone. The whole hallway's covered. How much smoke was there?
entries.new: 噢……这里到底出了什么事？{w}房间里很暗，走廊也一样。墙壁和天花板都黑了，一个人也看不见。整条走廊都被熏遍了。这得有多少烟啊？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Everyone must've evacuated when they heard the alarm, even though it came a bit after the smoke appeared.
entries.new: 大家应该都是听到警报就疏散了吧，虽然警报比烟雾出现得晚了些。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Did you see where the smoke came from? I didn't see anything, and there's nothing here.
entries.new: ……你看到烟是从哪儿冒出来的吗？我什么都没看到，这里也没有任何东西。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: N-No, but you're right. It surrounded us in an instant, and it probably appeared in this room and in the hallways at the same time.
entries.new: 没、没有，不过你说得对。它一瞬间就把我们包围了，恐怕是同时出现在这个房间和几条走廊里的。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Both of these doors were closed, so the origin had to have been here. Something must've happened while we were unconscious.
entries.new: 两扇门当时都关着，所以源头只能在这里。我们昏迷的时候一定出了什么事。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Why are we alone, though? There were police officers outside. Why haven't they come?
entries.new: 可为什么只有我们在这儿？外面明明有警察。他们怎么没过来？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I had no idea.{w} Still a bit disoriented, I forced my neck to turn. The only thing in the room was the covered cabinet. However, I doubted the Sekimeiya would still be there. The easiest conclusion to reach was that the smoke had been part of an attack designed to steal it.
entries.new: 我也答不上来。{w}我还有些恍惚，硬是扭过头去。房间里只有那个盖着布的展示柜。可我不觉得 Sekimeiya 还会在里面。最容易想到的结论是：那阵烟雾是袭击的一部分，目的就是偷走它。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The smoke wasn't released in the other rooms in the hallway.
entries.new: 走廊上其他房间并没有冒出烟来。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Everything was giving me a surreal vibe. I had no idea what was going on, but at first glance, the danger seemed to have faded away.
entries.new: 眼前的一切都透着一种不真实感。我完全不知道发生了什么，但乍看之下，危险似乎已经退去了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My headache was nearly gone, thankfully. That meant that I could start thinking things through. {w}What had happened? Why had it happened? How was I going to find the person responsible?
entries.new: 所幸头痛几乎已经消失，这意味着我可以开始把事情理清楚了。{w}发生了什么？为什么会发生？我又要怎么找出该为此负责的人？
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Maybe I was just trying to distract myself from reality by thinking things like that, but I had a personal stake in it. I couldn't forgive whoever was responsible.
entries.new: 也许想这些只是我在逃避现实，但这件事与我切身相关。不管是谁做的，我都无法原谅。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya probably felt the same way. We couldn't just ignore it, and someone was missing.
entries.new: Shiroya 大概也是同样的想法。这件事不能就这么算了，而且还有一个人下落不明。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The room was empty, and it had been empty before we'd fallen unconscious. Only the cabinet had been with us, but if the smoke had come out of it, it wouldn't have surrounded us so fast.{w} We had been stained, but not as much on the lower parts of our bodies. The ceiling was significantly darkened, the floor not so much. The smoke's density was low.
entries.new: 房间里空无一物，我们昏迷之前也是这样。陪在这里的只有那个展示柜；可如果烟是从柜子里冒出来的，不可能这么快就把我们团团围住。{w}我们身上都沾上了烟渍，但下半身要少得多。天花板黑得很明显，地板却没有。说明烟的密度并不高。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Did that mean that the origin of the smoke had been the very center of the room? How did that make any sense?
entries.new: ……那是不是说，烟的源头就在房间正中央？可这根本说不通。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya staggered slightly. I reached out to try and hold her shoulder, but as my body was still recovering, both of us fell back to the floor.
entries.new: Shiroya 晃了一下。我伸手去扶她的肩，可我的身体还没恢复，结果两个人一起摔回了地上。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Without looking at us, Akaro walked to the door we'd entered through.
entries.new: Akaro 看都没看我们一眼，径自朝我们进来的那扇门走去。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It happened here too.
entries.new: 这边也一样。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: ...Yeah. When I fell to the floor, I noticed there was no light below that door. Given how dark the room had become, I thought the hallway must've been just as dark. ...The smoke was released at the same time, even though both places looked empty.
entries.new: ……嗯。我倒在地上的时候，注意到那扇门底下一点光都没有。房间里已经这么暗了，我就想走廊肯定也一样暗。……烟是同时冒出来的，可这两边看起来都是空的。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...What the fuck is this about? That woman disappeared, but she fell unconscious too, didn't she? And you're right. Why is no one else here?
entries.new: ……这他妈到底是怎么回事？那女人不见了，可她不也一样昏过去了吗？还有，你说得对，为什么这里没有别人？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Although those points were very strange, I was still relieved that none of us had been harmed. I lay on the floor for a bit, attempting to gather more strength.{w} When thoughts came to me, it was calming to realize that they were different from what had recently filled my head.
entries.new: 这些疑点虽然十分蹊跷，但至少我们谁都没有受伤，这让我松了口气。我在原地躺了一会儿，想多攒些力气。{w}等思绪重新浮起来，我竟觉得安心——它们与近来盘踞在我脑中的东西截然不同。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This room connects two parallel hallways, which were attacked alongside this room all at once. Was this done to isolate us?
entries.new: 这个房间连接着两条平行的走廊，那两条走廊和这个房间同时遭到了袭击。这样做是为了把我们孤立起来吗？
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Someone attacked the building to steal the Sekimeiya, right? That must've been the intention. The smoke formed an easy path for whoever had planned it to make their way here, obtain the Sekimeiya, and leave.
entries.new: 有人袭击了这栋楼，为的是偷走 Sekimeiya——大概就是这样。烟雾为策划者铺出一条通路，让他能一路来到这里，取走 Sekimeiya，再离开。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: It sounds like a messy, risky plan, but it's the obvious thing that comes to mind. The open door seems to back it up, even though Naomi must have left through one anyway.
entries.new: 听起来是个混乱又冒险的计划，却也是最容易想到的。敞开的那扇门似乎也印证了这一点，尽管 Naomi 反正是要从某扇门离开的。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Do I have to conclude that Naomi was part of this, and while we were out, she took the Sekimeiya and left? ...Making herself look suspicious immediately? Being a staff member, she'd know many things about the security system... and we were the first group to enter, meaning out of us four, she was the only one that wasn't part of the first visit coincidentally.
entries.new: 难道我只能断定 Naomi 也牵涉其中，趁我们昏迷时拿走 Sekimeiya 离开？……她这样一来，不就立刻让自己显得可疑了吗？身为工作人员，她对安保系统了解许多……而我们又是第一批进入的人，也就是说，四个人里只有她不是碰巧参加第一次参观的。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Or, I could say that if I knew Akaro at all. I did think he looked distant from everything else.
entries.new: 又或者，如果我真了解 Akaro 的话——我确实觉得他对周围的一切都漠不关心。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Maybe Akaro was aware of the fact the smoke would appear. He could have immediately faked his unconsciousness by throwing himself to the floor, knowing he would avoid breathing in anything from the upper half of the room. The fact the floor is barely stained proves the smoke never came down.
entries.new: 也许 Akaro 早就知道会有烟雾出现。他可以立刻扑倒在地，装作昏过去，因为他清楚这样就能避开房间上半部的烟。地板几乎没有被熏黑，正说明烟从未沉到下面来。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Once we're all out of it, he obtains the Sekimeiya.{w} I should also consider that the smoke first arose shortly after Naomi unlocked the cabinet. This doesn't mean much, given that she could have had her key taken after she was unconscious, but if whoever did this didn't know much about the cabinet's mechanism, it makes sense they waited until it was unlocked.
entries.new: 等我们都失去意识，他就能把 Sekimeiya 弄到手。{w}我还得考虑另一种可能：烟雾是在 Naomi 打开展示柜后不久才出现的。这一点说明不了太多——毕竟她的钥匙也可能是在昏迷后被人取走的；不过，如果下手的人对展示柜的构造不甚了解，那么等到柜子被打开再行动就说得通了。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: But how did they know exactly when that was? Doesn't this mean that they must've been inside the room? Or, again, doesn't this mean that only Akaro could've done it? Assuming this precise timing actually happened... how did he trigger the smoke? It could simply be that he gave some sort of signal to someone else outside, but phones aren't allowed here.
entries.new: 可他们怎么知道那是什么时候？这不就意味着，他们当时必定就在房间里？或者说，只有 Akaro 才做得到？倘若时机真的如此精准……那他又是怎么触发烟雾的？也可能只是他给外面的某个人发了什么信号，但这里不允许带手机。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: After we regained consciousness, he seemed to be perfectly fine physically. However, the mass difference between his body and our nineteen-year-old ones is significant. It makes sense that the substance had a somewhat weaker effect on him.
entries.new: 我们醒来之后，他身体看上去毫无异样。不过，他的体格与我们这些十九岁的人相差不少。那种药物对他的作用稍弱一些，倒也说得通。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Is Akaro in possession of the Sekimeiya right now, or did he leave it somewhere? If so, why did he come back? Only to avoid suspicion? But this doesn't explain Naomi's disappearance. And how did the smoke appear, or why did the alarm sound late? And what kind of risky plan is this?
entries.new: Sekimeiya 现在在 Akaro 手上吗，还是被他藏到了别处？如果是后者，他为什么还要回来？只为洗脱嫌疑？可这解释不了 Naomi 的失踪。还有，烟是怎么出现的，警报为什么迟了？这又算哪门子的冒险计划？
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I grimaced. I was getting carried away without realizing how far I was going. In the first place, it was ridiculous to suspect anyone until I had information.
entries.new: 我皱紧了眉。我想得越来越远，自己却浑然不觉。说到底，在掌握情报之前就去怀疑谁，实在荒唐。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But I knew. I could never let things remain as they were. Someone was responsible, and I wouldn't let them get away. I only had to bide my time.
entries.new: 但我心里清楚。事情不能就这样维持原状。总有人要为此负责，而我绝不会让他逃掉。我只需等待时机。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Before I could stand, I realized there was another avenue open to me. There was a security camera on the ceiling.
entries.new: 还没等我站起来，我就意识到自己还有另一条路可走。天花板上装着监控摄像头。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If someone was looking at the footage and the smoke came out of an automated system, this would make a lot more sense. However, Akaro could've simply been the one to wait for the automated smoke and then followed up with whatever plan they had. This must've happened during the first visit for a reason.
entries.new: 如果有人一直在看监控画面，而烟雾又是自动系统放出来的，那事情就合理多了。不过，也可能只是 Akaro 等自动烟雾发作，再顺势执行他们的计划。这件事偏偏发生在首次参观期间，一定有原因。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: It means that whoever was looking at the direct footage would've been the one to activate the smoke system.
entries.new: 也就是说，看着实时画面的人，就是启动烟雾系统的人。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: ...{w}I was doing it again, almost like a coping mechanism. I had to make sure Shiroya was really okay before anything else.
entries.new: ……{w}我又开始这样了，几乎像是一种自我安抚。无论如何，我得先确认 Shiroya 真的没事。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When I attempted to lift my head, my body thankfully obeyed. I stared at the curtain that concealed the so-called Sekimeiya. It was dark, and the substance the smoke was composed of had dried up on it.
entries.new: 我试着抬起头，身体总算还听使唤。我望着那块遮着所谓 Sekimeiya 的遮布。遮布已经发黑，烟雾凝结成的物质在上面干结成了块。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Can you stand up?
entries.new: ……你站得起来吗？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I think so.
entries.new: 应该可以。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Supporting each other, Shiroya and I slowly steadied ourselves. Then, I realized Akaro had gone to the hallway.
entries.new: 我和 Shiroya 互相搀扶着，慢慢站稳了身子。这时我才发现，Akaro 已经往走廊那边去了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Finally! Thank goodness!
entries.new: 总算醒了！谢天谢地！
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: A shout came from the same area. It was a feminine voice, which at least indicated we weren't alone.
entries.new: 同一个方向传来一声喊叫。那是个女人的声音，至少说明这里还有别人。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We walked to it slowly as I wiped more of the solidified substance off of myself. I was curious to see if the Sekimeiya was still in the cabinet, but we would find that out very soon regardless.
entries.new: 我一边擦掉身上更多凝固的污物，一边慢慢朝那边走去。我也想知道 Sekimeiya 是否还在展示柜里，不过答案很快就会揭晓。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The hallway was almost as dark as the room. The smoke had coated every light bulb, but since there were many of them, some light could make it past the barrier.
entries.new: 走廊几乎和房间一样昏暗。烟雾裹住了每一只灯泡，但灯泡为数众多，总有些光能透出那层遮蔽。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The smoke had created a thorough cover on the walls and ceilings, which must've been an intended result. It had set up a dark environment, but that couldn't be the sole purpose: something had been added to the smoke to create the same effect on every surface it touched.
entries.new: 烟雾在墙壁和天花板上留下了厚厚一层覆盖，这想必是刻意为之。它营造出一片昏暗，但这显然不是唯一的目的：烟雾里掺了东西，凡是它接触到的表面，都会产生同样的效果。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Close to the start of the hallway, near the door Naomi had first appeared through, I saw human figures. Our approaching footsteps were noticed by one, and it rose from its knees.
entries.new: 走廊入口附近，也就是 Naomi 最初出现的那扇门旁，我看见了人影。我们的脚步声被其中一人察觉，那人从跪姿站了起来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We got closer and saw two more people kneeling down. Akaro was with them, and after finally arriving where they were, I noticed a small body on the floor.
entries.new: 走近些，又看见两个人跪在那里。Akaro 也在其中。等我们终于走到他们身边，我才发现地上躺着一个小小的身影。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Isla's finally waking up. Thank God.
entries.new: Isla 终于醒了。谢天谢地。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: That woman was the person we'd heard. She had the little girl on her lap and was looking at her closed eyes with concern.
entries.new: 方才那声喊叫就是她发出的。她把小女孩抱在膝上，忧心地注视着她紧闭的双眼。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I see. So, you three were also unable to evacuate.
entries.new: 原来如此。这么说，你们三个也没能撤出去。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: The person who had stood up was a well-dressed old man. As he said that, the two kneeling people turned their heads to face us.
entries.new: 站起来的是位衣着考究的老人。他说这话时，跪着的两人转头看向我们。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But the words "unable to evacuate" were more ominous than I'd expected, especially due to his rough voice.
entries.new: 可「没能撤出去」这几个字，比我预想的更叫人不寒而栗——尤其是从他沙哑的嗓音里说出来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is she okay?
entries.new: 她没事吧？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I... I think so. She's finally breathing fine.
entries.new: 我……应该没事。她总算能好好喘气了。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Shiroya sat next to the others and worriedly looked at the girl who'd been called Isla. Next to them was a guy my age, who was staring at the girl in silence.
entries.new: Shiroya 在几人身边坐下，忧心忡忡地看着那个叫 Isla 的女孩。旁边还有个和我年纪相仿的男人，一言不发地盯着女孩。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Smoke appeared out of nowhere and knocked us out. Do you know what happened?
entries.new: 烟雾不知从哪儿冒出来，把我们全弄晕了。你知道这是怎么回事吗？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: ...I'm afraid I don't.{w} You were in the event room, right? Shouldn't another woman be with you?
entries.new: ……这我恐怕不清楚。{w}你们当时在活动室吧？不是还有一位女士和你们在一起吗？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Naomi, yes. She was gone when we woke up.
entries.new: Naomi，对。我们醒来时她已经不见了。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Despite the dim light, I was able to discern his frown.
entries.new: 光线虽暗，我还是看得出他皱起了眉。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'm pretty sure she passed out too, but the door to the other hallway was open when we woke up.
entries.new: 她肯定也昏过去了，可我们醒来时，另一侧走廊的门是开着的。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...She left while you were still unconscious? That's strange. I inspected this floor a bit and didn't find her.
entries.new: ……她趁你们昏迷时离开了？奇怪。我大致查过这一层，没找到她。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Is that strange? Maybe she exited the building entirely.
entries.new: 这有什么奇怪的？也许她直接出了大楼。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: When his look lowered again, I realized there was something very important that we were missing. Why was nobody else there? Why had the unconscious child not been taken outside, at the very least?
entries.new: 他再次垂下目光时，我意识到我们漏了一件至关重要的事。为什么这里没有别人？至少，为什么没人把昏迷的孩子带到外面去？
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She couldn't have left. If she fell unconscious like the rest of you, she still has to be here.
entries.new: 她不可能离开。如果她像你们一样昏了过去，那她一定还在这里。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: What?
entries.new: 什么？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: The man didn't answer immediately, so I took that time to look him over. Due to the lighting, I'd just gotten the impression that he was a simple well-dressed old man, but those weren't casual clothes.
entries.new: 男人没有立刻回答，我便趁这段时间打量他。因为光线昏暗，我先前只觉得他是个衣着得体的普通老人，可那身衣服并不是普通的便装。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did all of you hear the alarm that played throughout the building? After I heard it, I saw all the smoke.
entries.new: 楼里响过的警报，你们都听见了吧？我听到警报之后，就看见到处是烟。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Those words made me consider an important detail. His shirt was white and a lot less stained than ours, indicating that it hadn't been hit by the smoke during its release. In contrast, the woman and the other guy had the same smoke pattern we did, being more stained on their top halves.
entries.new: 这番话让我留意到一个重要细节。他的衬衫是白色的，污迹比我们少得多，说明烟雾喷出时并没有沾到他身上。相比之下，那女人和另一个男人身上的痕迹与我们一样，上半身沾得更多。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I am responsible for this building's security system. When the smoke appeared, I was in the security room, found in the other hallway.
entries.new: 这栋楼的安保系统由我负责。烟雾出现时，我在监控室——就在另一条走廊上。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Since today was a special day, most of the visitors were in the lobby awaiting their turn for the event, so they had no problem leaving safely when they saw the smoke. You might know that this tower has many floors, but only this one is open to the public, and no one was on the higher levels.
entries.new: 今天是个特殊的日子，多数来客都在大厅等候活动开始，所以一看到烟雾就顺利疏散了。你们或许知道，这座塔有很多层，但只有这一层对外开放，楼上并没有人。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: It was a big shock to see all that smoke, so I panicked and spent a while in the security room trying to figure out what had happened. When I realized I couldn't get anywhere, I exited and began searching through this floor. It seems you all were the first two groups of three for today's event.
entries.new: 看到那满楼的烟，我一时慌了神，在监控室里待了好一阵，想弄清究竟出了什么事。等发现毫无头绪，我才走出来，开始在这一层搜寻。看来你们就是今天活动的前两组，每组三个人。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Yes. We were told to wait here after the first group moved forward.
entries.new: 是的。第一组进去之后，我们就被告知在这里等候。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Oh, that's right. I remember seeing her earlier, now that I look at her closer.
entries.new: 哦，对了。凑近一看，我想起之前见过她。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I also recalled seeing the three of them behind us in the lobby. I was still trying to understand the older man's words, though, as he had said the security room was in the other hallway. At the same time, we cleaned the rest of the smoke off our bodies until only a few traces remained.
entries.new: 我也想起来了，在大厅时他们三个就排在我们后面。不过，我还在琢磨老人的话——他说监控室在另一条走廊上。与此同时，我们把身上剩下的烟渍也擦掉了，只留下浅浅几道痕迹。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You said you saw the smoke, but your clothes are much cleaner than ours. Did it not hit you?
entries.new: 你说你看见了烟雾，可你的衣服比我们干净多了。难道没沾到你身上？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That's right. I didn't leave the room while it was in the hallway. When I said I saw the smoke, I was talking about the security cameras.
entries.new: 没错。走廊里满是烟的时候，我并没有出房间。我说看见烟，是指从监控画面上看到的。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Oh, I see.
entries.new: 哦，原来如此。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...So, he was the person I'd just accused in my head.
entries.new: ……原来我刚才在心里冤枉的就是他。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I wasn't able to figure anything out through the cameras, unfortunately. When I left a few minutes later, I saw all the walls were black.
entries.new: 可惜，我从监控里什么也没看出来。几分钟后我出门时，只见到处墙壁都是黑的。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I knew he was slowly giving me information, so I didn't want to interrupt him. However, more questions were coming to my mind, such as why he hadn't come across our group first.
entries.new: 看得出他在一点点透露信息，我不想打断他。可心里冒出的疑问越来越多，比如他为什么没有先遇到我们这一组。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait, you saw what the hallway looked like after you left the security room? Don't you have enough security cameras to see it from there?
entries.new: 等等，你是出了监控室之后才看到走廊变成什么样？监控室里的摄像头不是足够看清楚吗？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I couldn't help myself from asking for details. The more I tried to coast through things, the more I resisted it. I needed to know as much as possible.
entries.new: 我忍不住追问细节。越是想着姑且听之，心里越是放不下——我必须尽可能多了解情况。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No. The thing is, they became useless after the smoke appeared. It instantly covered the lens of every camera that was hit by it.
entries.new: 不。问题在于，烟雾一出现，它们就派不上用场了。凡是沾到烟的摄像头，镜头转眼就被糊住了。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...That makes sense. It must be why the smoke created this film on every surface it touched. It worked to disable the cameras.
entries.new: ……这就说得通了。烟雾之所以在接触到的每样东西上留下一层膜，就是为了让摄像头失灵。
entries.speaker: a
