entries.text: Everything has pointed to Katei, and there are multiple ways to construct it. If he's really a security member, he probably would've had an easy time setting this up. If he's not, Sai's theory is valid too. He's definitely the most suspicious person here.
entries.new: 所有线索都指向 Katei，而且能拼出好几种解释。如果他真是保安，布置这一切大概轻而易举；如果他不是，Sai 的推理也同样成立。他无疑是这里最可疑的人。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Unless I choose to doubt Sai, it's almost a guarantee that Katei lied about being in the security room during the attack. There could be many reasons behind the lie, though. If Katei is actually innocent, a similar plan could be adapted around anyone who got trapped.
entries.new: 除非我连 Sai 也一并怀疑，否则几乎可以肯定，Katei 说袭击时自己待在监控室里是谎话。不过，他说谎的理由可以有很多。若 Katei 真是清白的，那么同样的计划，也可以套用在任何被困在这里的人身上。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Of course, I can rule myself and Shiroya out. We've come here innocently and never expected anything like this to happen. Shiroya and I have spent our entire lives together, and I know she'd never think of doing such a thing, not even with her being less than fond of Ashiya.
entries.new: 当然，我和 Shiroya 可以排除。我们来这里问心无愧，从没料到会发生这种事。Shiroya 和我从小到大都在一起，我知道她绝不会动这种念头——哪怕她对芦屋没什么好感。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I myself don't suffer from memory loss or split personalities, nor do I have a particular interest in ruining my life after failing a robbery attempt.
entries.new: 至于我自己，既没有失忆，也没有多重人格，更不至于在抢劫未遂之后，还一心想把人生彻底毁掉。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Akaro was the last person in our group. Out of us seven, I feel he's the easiest person to suspect after Katei. He claimed not to care much about today's event but was here from the very beginning. Earlier, his behavior was clearly off, but it's gotten better since we woke up.
entries.new: 我们这群人里，最后一个是 Akaro。七个人当中，我觉得除 Katei 之外就数他最值得怀疑。他嘴上说对今天的活动没什么兴趣，却从最开始就待在这里。先前他的举动明显不对劲，不过我们醒来之后，他倒是正常多了。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: It could be that he's letting the time pass so that his plan can conclude. But since he stands out from the rest of us, he's an easy target to blame for a plan Sai and I have concocted.
entries.new: 也许他是在拖时间，好让自己的计划走向终点。可他本就跟我们格格不入，也难怪会被我和 Sai 拿来当作这套推论的靶子。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The same could be said for Erina and Isla, even though it sounds less likely. It's too naïve to rule them out because of Isla's age. A well-constructed plan could take advantage of that to lower our guard.
entries.new: Erina 和 Isla 也一样，尽管听起来可能性小些。因为 Isla 年纪小就把她排除在外，未免太天真了——一个周全的计划，完全可以利用这一点让我们放松警惕。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Out of the six of us that were waiting for the event, only they have their early arrival justified... Isla's the only one who seemed to care about the event, but I can only truly rule out Shiroya and myself.
entries.new: 在等待活动开始的我们六个人里，只有她们有正当理由早到……真正在意这场活动的只有 Isla，而我能真正排除的，也只有 Shiroya 和我自己。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: And Sai... I don't believe he's the culprit, but if he's even crazier than he seems, he could've designed the whole thing and then messed with me for entertainment, maybe even to prevent my suspicion and interference. He could be trying to manipulate me into thinking whatever is convenient for him.
entries.new: 还有 Sai……我不认为他是犯人，可万一他比表面看上去还要疯狂，那整件事就可能是他一手设计，再拿我来消遣——甚至是为了让我不起疑、不来碍事。他也许正引导我往对他有利的方向去想。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I don't think that's likely, though. Similarly, he might've determined I'm not a likely suspect.
entries.new: 不过我觉得这不太可能。同样地，他或许也已经断定，我不像是会做出这种事的人。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: There are two more options: Naomi, and an unknown person.
entries.new: 还剩两种可能：Naomi，以及一个身份不明的人。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: If Naomi wants to wait until the exit opens to execute the last part of her plan, then hiding from us is probably a good idea. She's been hidden from the very beginning and will spend all the remaining time without being spotted, able to move by herself whenever she needs to. There's gotta be a good hiding spot somewhere in this huge building.
entries.new: 如果 Naomi 打算等到出口打开时再执行计划的最后一步，那么躲着我们大概就是上策。她从最开始就藏了起来，接下来的时间也只要一直不被发现，随时都能自行行动。这么一栋大楼里，总该有处藏身的好地方。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Using Naomi as the culprit helps explain the alarm triggering. Suripo said that the only way to activate it was by breaking open the Sekimeiya cabinet, and when I heard the alarm, Naomi was the one next to it.
entries.new: 把 Naomi 当作犯人，警报被触发也就说得通了。Suripo 说过，唯一能启动警报的方式就是强行撬开 Sekimeiya 的展示柜，而我听到警报时，守在柜子旁边的正是 Naomi。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: If she silently "broke" it in a way she knew would work and then faked being unconscious, she could've covertly trapped us. Then, when we looked at the cabinet, we failed to recognize what had triggered the mechanism.
entries.new: 如果她不声不响地用自己确信可行的方式「破坏」了柜子，然后假装昏迷，就能神不知鬼不觉地把我们困住。而后我们去看展示柜时，也没能看出究竟是什么触发了机关。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Why would she do that? Could she have wanted to make it look like it was a malfunction, so anything else could be a malfunction too? The fact that the alarm went off right after Naomi unlocked the cabinet with her key also leads me to think that the source of the alarm had to be something else.
entries.new: 她为什么要那样做？难道是想让一切看起来像是设备故障，好让别的异常也能一并归到故障上？而且，警报恰好是在 Naomi 用钥匙打开展示柜之后响起的，这也让我觉得触发警报的必定另有其物。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: However, this also could have been done purposely to make the three of us confirm that by the time the alarm was set off, there was no reason to force the cabinet open. After all, there's no way Naomi could've known I'd stay conscious for enough time to hear the alarm.
entries.new: 不过，这也可能是刻意安排的，好让我们三个人认定：警报响起时，根本没有必要去强行打开展示柜。毕竟，Naomi 不可能知道我还能保持清醒，清醒到听见警报。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: But if Naomi is innocent, is there more than one option behind her disappearance? Unless she woke up ahead of time and saw the culprit, the only person with a clear motive would've been Katei. She could still be trapped and walking around, but I'm not sure why she wouldn't have shown herself already if she has nothing to do with the attack...
entries.new: 可如果 Naomi 是清白的，她失踪的原因就不止一种了。除非她提前醒来，看见了犯人，否则唯一动机明确的人就是 Katei。她也可能只是被困住，还在某处走动——但如果她与这场袭击毫无关系，我想不出她为什么至今不肯露面……
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Is it actually possible Naomi is currently outside the tower? This would mean that the alarm had a delayed effect and Naomi's not innocent at all. I'm pretty sure what I heard in the event room was the shutter, but I can't be totally certain.
entries.new: Naomi 有可能此刻已经在塔外了吗？若真是这样，就说明警报有延迟，而 Naomi 也绝非清白。我相当确定自己在活动室听到的是卷帘门的声音，但没法完全肯定。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The only way she could be outside is if Naomi is a culprit. Otherwise, Suripo surely would've said that she was outside when we brought up her name. The only way this wouldn't have happened is if Naomi was the "individual" with the suitcase whose identity was kept a secret.
entries.new: 她若在塔外，唯一的可能就是 Naomi 本人就是犯人。否则，我们提到她的名字时，Suripo 一定会说她就在外面。而他没有这么说的唯一解释，就是 Naomi 正是那个被隐去身份、带着手提箱的「某人」。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The "unknown person" option is basically the same, but better. After all, with Naomi, we'd know the identity of the culprit by the end. If an unknown person has stayed with us and somehow plans to sneak out with the Sekimeiya when the time comes, we'll have no way to know who they were.
entries.new: 「身份不明的人」这一种本质上相同，却更站得住脚。毕竟若犯人是 Naomi，到最后我们至少还知道她是谁；可要是一个身份不明的人一直混在我们当中，还打算到时候带着 Sekimeiya 悄悄溜走，我们就根本无从知道他是谁。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The lobby doesn't have security cameras. When everyone evacuated, someone hid behind the reception desk or entered the staircase to the mechanical room. Once the smoke faded, they hid in a better place, maybe after moving Naomi's body. Maybe they were in one of the rooms in a hallway, and that's why they made sure we couldn't look at the recorded footage.
entries.new: 大厅里没有监控摄像头。所有人撤离时，某个人躲到了接待台后面，或者进了通往机械室的楼梯间。等烟雾散去，他又藏到了更稳妥的地方——也许在搬动 Naomi 的身体之后。他也许一直待在走廊旁的某个房间里——正因如此，他才确保我们看不到监控录像。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Once this is all listed out, there are a few extra options, like two people working together. If Naomi and Katei were in cahoots, one would cover what doesn't make sense if the other person is working alone.
entries.new: 这样一一列下来，还有几种额外的可能，比如两人合谋。若 Naomi 和 Katei 是一伙的，那么单独一人行动时说不通的地方，另一个人正好能补上。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The two staff members could have easily designed an internal attack thanks to the knowledge they possess. Katei made us think the Sekimeiya we saw was the real deal. Now, Naomi can do as she pleases since she'll be constantly covered by Katei, who will guide all of us as the most knowledgeable person here.{w} ...Perhaps that's unlikely since he had no problem staying behind in the security room while we went to investigate.
entries.new: 这两名员工凭着自己掌握的内情，要策划一场内部袭击并不难。Katei 让我们相信眼前的就是真正的 Sekimeiya；而 Naomi 则可以随心所欲，因为 Katei 会一直替她遮掩——作为这里最了解情况的人，他还在为我们所有人带路。{w} ……不过这也许不太可能，毕竟我们出去调查时，他留在监控室里毫无顾虑。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Surprisingly, the conclusion I drew was that if the plan was still being carried out, Sai's theory was close to what I believed to be likely.
entries.new: 出乎意料，我的结论是：如果计划还在继续，那么 Sai 的推理已经很接近我认为最有可能的情形。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We had to know what triggered the alarm. It would clear up multiple doubts and remove possibilities such as the person responsible already escaping.
entries.new: 我们必须弄清是什么触发了警报。这能解开好几处疑点，也能排除诸如犯人早已逃出去之类的可能。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Maybe what you said is the most likely possibility. A lot of things point to Katei being suspicious, and he knew about the alarm from the start. That could mean that he's the most likely person to be carrying out a plan that involves waiting for the alarm's timer.
entries.new: 也许你说的就是最有可能的情况。很多地方都让人觉得 Katei 可疑，而且他从一开始就知道警报的事。照这么说，最有可能实施这个「等警报计时」计划的人就是他。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Yes, I agree.{w} Either him or Naomi, but with the scenario I constructed, Naomi's already taken care of. Most things are, actually. I don't know how the smoke was released, what triggered the alarm, and how Katei plans to disappear with the Sekimeiya. It's also good to note that regardless of the method, a member of security staff like him could easily design a way to release the smoke.
entries.new: ……嗯，我同意。{w}不是他就是 Naomi，不过按我构建的情形来看，Naomi 那边已经处理妥当了。其实大部分环节都有着落了。烟雾是怎么放出来的、警报是什么触发的、Katei 又打算怎么带着 Sekimeiya 消失，这些我还不知道。另外还有一点值得记下：不管用什么方法，像他这样的安保人员都很容易设计出释放烟雾的手段。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It'd be wise to keep track of him at all times. He stayed alone earlier, and in the security room of all places. I'm very curious to know how he intends to make this plan work. He'll probably make sure that we don't come across Naomi or the body of the real Katei, if I'm also right about that.
entries.new: 最好一直盯着他。他刚才单独待过一阵，而且偏偏是在监控室。我很想知道他打算怎么让这个计划成立。如果我另一项推断也没错，他多半会设法不让我们碰上 Naomi，也不让我们看到真正 Katei 的尸体。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You seem pretty excited.
entries.new: 你看起来相当兴奋。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: A bit. Aren't you?{w} Aren't you looking forward to knowing which theory ends up being the correct one? Or maybe to find out that we were both incorrect. What if this is all bigger than we think, or just a coincidental accident?
entries.new: 有一点。你不兴奋吗？{w}你就不想知道最后哪一种推理才是对的？又或者，发现我们两个都猜错了。万一这件事比我们想的要大得多，或者只是一场偶然的事故呢？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I want to make a lot of theories and then have the best one turn out to be right. That would be great.
entries.new: 我想先提出一大堆推理，然后让其中最漂亮的那个成真。那就太棒了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: For example, think about this. Everything we've thought about has been in part based on the call with Suripo. However, our main assumption right now is that Katei is responsible for all this.
entries.new: 比如说，你想想这个。我们所有的思考，多少都建立在和 Suripo 的那通通话上。可我们眼下最主要的假设，是这一切都该由 Katei 负责。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You brought up a good point earlier when you asked why Katei said we could communicate with the outside. You're right. If he's a security member while also being the culprit, he'd look incredibly bad to the police if he never told us about it.
entries.new: 你刚才那个问题问得很好——Katei 为什么说我们能和外界联系。你说得对。如果他既是安保人员，又是始作俑者，却始终不告诉我们这件事，在警方眼里他就太难看了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: But if I'm right and he doesn't work here, it wasn't very smart of him to bring it up voluntarily.
entries.new: 可如果我猜得没错，他根本不在这里工作，那他主动提起这件事就实在算不上聪明。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You're saying that Suripo was an accomplice, and they planned what to tell us?
entries.new: 你是说 Suripo 是同伙，那些话是他们事先商量好的？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Exactly. ...He spoke very highly of Xyn.{w} What if he was speaking very highly of himself? The group he works for, alongside Katei?
entries.new: 正是。……他把 Xyn 夸得很高。{w}可要是他夸的其实是他自己呢？夸的是他和 Katei 同属的那个组织？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He had a police uniform and was in a car next to the tower, ignored by everyone around it. If it was a real video feed, he's an actual policeman. Wouldn't things make sense if Xyn was involved with the police?
entries.new: 他穿着警服，坐在塔旁的车里，周围的人却对他视而不见。如果那是真实的视频画面，他就是货真价实的警察。要是 Xyn 和警方有牵连，一切不就说得通了吗？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That program hidden deep within the computer's folders could've been another factor of this plan designed by Xyn. They knew Ashiya were working on a mechanism to defeat them, so they created this plan to keep their superiority. Assuming part of what he told us was the truth.
entries.new: 藏在电脑文件夹深处的那段程序，也许就是 Xyn 设计的这个计划里的另一环。他们知道芦屋正在研制对付他们的手段，于是布下这个计划来保住优势。前提是他告诉我们的话里有一部分是真的。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: As soon as he began to explain things, my suspicions about Katei immediately lessened. After all, what that policeman was saying matched up well with the information Katei gave us. Now, if they were working together, made-up details would appear like the absolute truth, and they'd make all of Katei's subsequent claims sound authentic.
entries.new: 他一开口解释，我对 Katei 的怀疑立刻就淡了。毕竟那个警察说的和 Katei 给我们的信息对得上。可要是他们本就是一伙的，编造的细节也会显得千真万确，还能让 Katei 之后说的每一句话都显得可信。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Suripo mainly spoke to Katei. If they were following a script, they could pretty easily deceive us. Suripo is the only reliable source we think we have.
entries.new: Suripo 主要是在跟 Katei 说话。如果他们是照着剧本演的，骗过我们并不难。而 Suripo 是我们自认为唯一可靠的消息来源。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: And after he was done, the power conveniently went out. Not only that, but Katei was unable to contact him again. How believable is that, really? Did the Ashiya family really revoke his authority, knowing they'd leave us incommunicado for twelve hours?
entries.new: 而且他说完话，电就恰好断了。不止如此，Katei 还再也联系不上他。这种事真有那么可信吗？芦屋家真的会在明知会让我们失联十二小时的情况下，撤掉他的权限？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Wouldn't it be exciting if we were in the middle of such a plan? Would you stop Xyn if you saw through everything?
entries.new: 如果我们正身处这样一个计划之中，难道不让人兴奋吗？要是你看穿了一切，你会去阻止 Xyn 吗？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...I'm not excited about being caught up in this, I can say that much. But if I get the chance to take these guys down, I absolutely would. I won't let them get away with this... this shit.
entries.new: ……被卷进这种事里，我可兴奋不起来，这点我可以肯定。但要是有机会把这些人扳倒，我绝对不会放过。我不会让他们就这么算了……干出这种混账事。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I see.{w} Me, I'm just curious. I can't wait to know how this plan ends. Sadly, there's still a while until that. Maybe they need these twelve hours for something... Suripo corroborated the amount of time Katei said, so it would be strange if it turned out to be wrong.
entries.new: 原来如此。{w}我嘛，只是好奇而已。我迫不及待想知道这个计划会怎么收场。可惜离那还有好一阵子。也许这十二小时他们另有用途……Suripo 也证实了 Katei 说的时间，要是这个数目出了错，反倒奇怪了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We'll have to see what happens.
entries.new: 只能看接下来的发展了。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I suppose so, but if this is an ongoing plan, they won't make it obvious. If they're trying to trick the Ashiya family, we might get tricked too. I'm just not going to get fooled so easily.
entries.new: 话是这么说，可如果这个计划还在继续，他们不会做得那么明显。他们要是想骗芦屋家，我们说不定也会被骗。只不过我没那么容易被糊弄。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Hm.
entries.new: 嗯。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I didn't feel like saying anything else. A part of me thought that everything Sai was saying entailed pointless danger. I related to the interest, but not so much to his approach.
entries.new: 我不太想再说什么。心里有一半觉得，Sai 说的那些都带着毫无必要的危险。那份兴趣我能理解，他的做法我却不敢苟同。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In our situation, there was no reason for us to be in danger. It was something between Ashiya and Xyn, and we'd just been caught up in the middle of it. Letting everything happen without giving our own input to strangers seemed like the smarter course of action.
entries.new: 以我们的处境，根本没有理由让自己陷入危险。这是芦屋和 Xyn 之间的事，我们只是被卷了进来。顺其自然，不主动跟陌生人说什么，似乎是更明智的做法。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, trying to piece things together on the side probably wouldn't do any harm.
entries.new: 不过，在一旁自己试着拼凑真相，大概也无伤大雅。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Although I hadn't reacted, what Sai said was intriguing. I'd let Suripo influence my thoughts with no opposition, but it was true that Katei had been the one who'd let us hear him.
entries.new: 我虽然没有表露出来，Sai 的话却勾起了我的兴趣。我毫无抵触地任由 Suripo 影响了我的想法，可确实，让我们听到他说话的是 Katei。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The first thing he'd said was that Ashiya instructed the police to talk to us, but he'd never proven that at all. It hadn't sounded all that strange, but instead of telling the police what to let us know, Ashiya could've said everything directly.
entries.new: 他开口第一句就说，是芦屋让警方来跟我们通话的，可这一点他从未证实过。这话听着倒也不算太奇怪，但芦屋与其让警方转告我们，本可以直接把一切告诉我们。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Suripo also said that Ashiya told them about the communication method. Initially, the other side should've been picked up by Ashiya, who'd supposedly passed it off to the police...
entries.new: Suripo 还说，通信方式也是芦屋告诉他们的。最初本该是芦屋接到另一头的信号，然后他又把它转交给了警方……
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: While there was room for suspicion, thinking that he was an actual corrupt policeman was probably incorrect. If he had fed us false information, he would be exposed after we got out.
entries.new: 虽然有值得怀疑的地方，但认定他就是个真正堕落的警察，恐怕并不正确。如果他真给了我们假情报，等我们出去之后，他就会被揭穿。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I could feel my head getting cloudy. The tiredness was coming back, so I tried to cool off.
entries.new: 我能感觉到脑子越来越混沌。倦意又涌了上来，我便试着让自己冷静一下。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The room's inspection finished without anything missing. Once again, we silently moved on to the next one.
entries.new: 这个房间检查完毕，什么也没少。我们又默默走向下一个房间。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After not talking for two weeks, my voice had easily come out in front of Sai. As I'd thought, it was only Shiroya who I had difficulty talking to.
entries.new: 两周没开口，我的声音却在 Sai 面前很自然地发了出来。果然，让我难以开口的只有 Shiroya。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: At the same time, the incident had given me something else to think about after so long. It was likely I was trying to fill up my mind with it, as I knew what would fill it otherwise.
entries.new: 同时，这起事件也让我在这么久之后，终于有了别的事情可想。多半是我在用这件事填满脑子，因为我知道否则填进去的会是什么。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Isla didn't look tired of repeating the same procedure. She ran to the door, eagerly awaiting Katei.
entries.new: ……Isla 一遍遍重复同样的流程，却看不出丝毫厌烦。她跑到门边，急切地等着 Katei。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd noticed that every room had a specific theme. Before leaving, I'd glanced at the cabinets and seen a bunch of unimpressive white gemstones, much smaller in size than the Sekimeiya.
entries.new: 我注意到每个房间都有各自的主题。离开前我瞥了一眼展示柜，里面是一堆并不起眼的白宝石，个头比 Sekimeiya 小得多。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Labeled A5, the last crystal room in the hallway was left before the storeroom. When Isla turned the knob, we expected to be met with the same scene as the other rooms.
entries.new: 标着 A5 的这间，是走廊里最后一间水晶展室，再往前就是储藏室。Isla 转动门把手时，我们都以为会看到和其他房间一样的景象。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh...
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The entire room was tinted black, and it was shaped differently. The ceiling and four walls had been deprived of their color, as a dry, dark coating had taken hold of them.
entries.new: 整个房间都染上了黑色，形状也不一样。天花板和四面墙壁失去了原本的颜色，被一层干涸的深色附着物盖住了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Every cabinet was covered by a curtain, but instead of bright red, they were gray, black, and purple, colors that removed all of their elegance.
entries.new: 每个展示柜都罩着遮布，可不再是鲜红色，而是灰、黑、紫，这些颜色把原本的雅致一扫而空。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was the same appearance the hallways bore. We immediately understood the smoke had also gotten into the last room.{w} We only found it a shocking sight because of what Katei previously told us.
entries.new: 走廊里也是同样的景象。我们立刻明白，烟雾也进了最后一间房。{w}只因 Katei 先前说过的话，这一幕才让我们如此震惊。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I see. This makes a lot of sense.
entries.new: 原来如此。这样就说得通了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What does? Didn't Katei say that the smoke hadn't been released in any other room?
entries.new: 说得通什么？Katei 不是说，烟雾没有进过别的房间吗？
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Instead of clarifying, Sai moved forward. He stained his hand black by grabbing the bottom of a curtain, and without any care, he raised it to show us the interior of the cabinet it was covering.
entries.new: Sai 没有解释，而是走上前去。他抓住遮布下摆，手被染成了黑色，却毫不在意地把遮布掀起，让我们看柜内的情形。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What...? There isn't anything...
entries.new: 什么……？里面什么都没有……
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: He did the same with every cabinet, and the result never differed.
entries.new: 他把每个展示柜都掀了一遍，结果毫无二致。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I see, this is the room that was robbed. The gems found in the suitcase came from these cabinets.
entries.new: 原来如此，失窃的就是这个房间。行李箱里找到的宝石，就是从这些展示柜里拿的。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes, that has to be it. But the smoke...
entries.new: 对，一定是这样。可那些烟雾……
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: You all remember what I said earlier, right?{w} That this part of the plan didn't make a ton of sense. The gems were stolen without releasing smoke in their room, which implied that the smoke had another purpose.
entries.new: 你们都记得我刚才说的吧？{w}我说这部分计划说不通。宝石被偷，却没有在它们的房间里放烟雾，这就说明烟雾另有用途。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: But it seems the smoke was released in this room too. Of course, that's required if they wanted to make it seem like those various gems were the target.
entries.new: 可看来这个房间里也放了烟雾。当然，如果想让人觉得那些各式各样的宝石才是目标，这一步是必须的。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The lens of the single camera was stained black, showing that we weren't being recorded. The green light had been buried under the same blackness, but it was still discernible.
entries.new: 唯一一台摄像头的镜头也被染黑了，说明我们没有被拍到。绿色指示灯被同一层黑色盖住，却仍能分辨出来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Katei told us the places where the smoke was released. Obviously, he wouldn't have said that if he hadn't been sure of it, so I believed him.
entries.new: Katei 告诉过我们烟雾是在哪几处放的。他若没有十足把握，显然不会那样说，所以我信了他。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'm sorry. I must've made a mistake.
entries.new: 抱歉。是我弄错了。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: No. I have no idea why you did that, but this settles it: this proves you were not in the security room when the alarm went off.
entries.new: 不。我不知道你为什么要那样做，但这一下就定论了——这证明警报响起时，你并不在监控室。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai glanced at me to let me know that he'd been correct. I was probably the only person aside from Katei who knew what he was talking about.
entries.new: Sai 朝我瞥了一眼，示意自己说对了。除了 Katei，大概只有我知道他在讲什么。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What do you mean...?
entries.new: 你这话是什么意思……？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Exactly! What are you talking about?
entries.new: 就是！你到底在说什么？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: You didn't even suspect it? This is about the fifth thing that confirms it, but this one lets me bring it up openly. After all, it also rules out a few things I talked about with Atsuki.
entries.new: 你连这都没怀疑过？算起来，这差不多是第五条佐证了，只不过这一条能让我当着大家的面提出来。毕竟，它也排除了几件我和 Atsuki 谈过的事。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I more or less understood why Sai said that. Without inspecting every room, Katei felt confident in saying that only three different places had been hit with the smoke, but he'd been incorrect.{w} That indicated he hadn't been behind the attack itself, since he wouldn't have made that mistake. It let Sai confront him since he no longer believed he was confronting Xyn, but a mere suspicious individual.
entries.new: 我大致明白 Sai 为什么这么说。Katei 并没有逐一检查每个房间，却敢断言只有三处被烟雾波及，而他错了。{w} 这说明他并非袭击的幕后主使——若真是他，就不会犯这种错。这也让 Sai 敢于当面质问他，因为他已不再觉得自己面对的是 Xyn，而只是一个形迹可疑的人。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't know what you mean... How does this indicate in any way that I wasn't in the security room?
entries.new: 我不明白你的意思……这怎么能说明我当时不在监控室？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: It's very simple, but let me ask first: why did you say that only the hallways and the event room had smoke released in them?
entries.new: 道理很简单，不过我先问你：你为什么说只有走廊和活动室里放了烟雾？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...I had a bit of time to inspect these rooms before I found Erina's group. Every room I entered was clean, so I simply assumed it was the case with all of them. I shouldn't have made such an assumption.
entries.new: ……在找到 Erina 他们之前，我还有点时间查看那些房间。我进过的每一间都是干净的，便想当然以为所有房间都如此。我不该这样臆断。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: All right. This proves it further. You were not in the security room.
entries.new: 好，这更能证明你不在监控室。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You all get it too, right?
entries.new: 你们也都明白了吧？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Katei has said multiple times that during the time the smoke was released, he was locked inside the security room. He also claimed that he tried to monitor what the situation was on this floor by looking through the available cameras.
entries.new: Katei 反复说过，释放烟雾的那段时间他被锁在监控室里，还声称通过能用的摄像头查看过这一层的情况。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Not only that, but he also said that he saw the smoke rising out of nowhere. I'm saying that if he really was looking through the cameras when the smoke appeared, he would've seen it being released here.
entries.new: 不止如此，他还说他看见烟雾凭空升起。我的意思是：烟雾出现时，他若真在看监控，就该看到这里也有烟雾放出来。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What? No. I was in a rush, so I never realized it.
entries.new: 什么？不。当时太急，我根本没注意到。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I don't understand it at all. You were never in the security room and you never inspected the first floor. So then, why did you say that only three places had been hit by the smoke? Why were you certain you could say that, despite being wrong?
entries.new: 这我就完全想不通了。你从没进过监控室，也从未查看过一楼。那么，你凭什么说只有三处被烟雾波及？你明明说错了，为什么还那么笃定？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That was the same question I'd been wondering. If Sai was right, Katei wouldn't have stated incorrect information he hadn't been able to verify, which meant that he felt certain about the room's appearance without personally seeing it.
entries.new: 这也正是我一直没想通的地方。若 Sai 说得对，Katei 就不会说出这种自己无法核实、又弄错的信息；也就是说，他根本没亲眼看到，却对那间房里的情形十分笃定。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Your assumption is mistaken. I can explain what led to that assertion.{w} When I was in the security room, most of the cameras from this floor were being displayed. It is true that I saw the smoke appearing out of nowhere, but at that time, this room's camera was not being shown. Usually, monitoring the interior of a room isn't needed if another camera shows its door.
entries.new: 你的假设不对。我可以解释我为什么会得出那个结论。{w} 我在监控室时，这一层大部分摄像头的画面都开着。我确实看到烟雾凭空冒出，但那时这间房的画面并没有显示出来。通常来说，只要另有摄像头对着房门，就不必再看房内的情况。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Then, I proceeded to look through all the other cameras while trying to determine what was happening. As you saw with your own eyes, some of them had been disabled; because of the smoke, a black screen was all that I could see through them.
entries.new: 接着，我一边查看其余所有摄像头，一边判断发生了什么。正如你们亲眼所见，其中有些已经失效；因为烟雾，那些画面只剩一片漆黑。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: So, all that this room's camera showed was a black screen. This means that I was unable to recognize that one of the disabled screens belonged to this room.{w} Since both hallways possess numerous cameras, I did not notice there were one too many black screens. Later, since I looked into most of the clean rooms, I wrongly assumed that they all were the same.
entries.new: 所以，这间房的摄像头画面也只是一片黑。也就是说，我没发现其中一块黑屏属于这间房。{w} 两条走廊都装了不少摄像头，我没察觉黑屏多了一块。后来，我查看过的房间大多是干净的，便错误地以为所有房间都一样。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Hm.
entries.new: 嗯。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We all thought about it. Did what Katei said make sense? If I'd been in their places, it's likely I would've believed it, but Sai and I had more reasons to think Katei had never been in the security room and that he was fabricating another lie out of nowhere.
entries.new: 我们都在想，Katei 的说法讲得通吗？如果我是他们，多半会信；但我和 Sai 有更多理由认为，Katei 根本没进过监控室，这番话不过是他临时编的又一个谎。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Are you really sure about this, Sai?
entries.new: Sai，你真有把握吗？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Absolutely.
entries.new: 当然。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Now answer me this. At first, you saw the smoke being released through some cameras. To assess the situation, you looked at all the remaining places on this floor, and this room wasn't initially being displayed.
entries.new: 那你回答我：一开始，你从几个监控画面里看到烟雾放出。为了判断情况，你把这一层其余的地方都看了一遍，而这间房起初并没有显示出来。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Correct. That is why I never saw the smoke appearing here.
entries.new: 没错。所以我一直没看到这里有烟雾冒出。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: All right. So then you switched the displayed cameras. This means that at some point, you switched one of the cameras for this room's. You're seriously saying that when you did that, you didn't realize the smoke had also been released here?
entries.new: 好。那么你切换了显示的摄像头。也就是说，在某个时间点，你把其中一个画面切到了这间房的摄像头。你是在说，你那么做的时候居然没发现这里也冒了烟？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Oh, I see what you mean. That eventually, I must've chosen to observe the live footage of this room by manually selecting its camera and I would've noticed the black screen.
entries.new: 哦，我明白你的意思了。你是说，我迟早会手动选中这间房的摄像头去看实时画面，然后就会发现那块黑屏。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...Yes.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It's understandable you'd think that, but no. That would've been slow and suboptimal given the situation. Do you remember earlier, when I looked through the cameras while talking to Suripo?
entries.new: 你会这么想，也情有可原，但并非如此。那样做在当时既慢又不合适。你还记得吗，刚才我和 Suripo 说话时，查看过监控？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: The program that manages them lets me replace the nine cameras being displayed at once for the ones that come next on the list. That's what I did.
entries.new: 管理这些摄像头的程序可以让我一次性把当前显示的九个画面换成列表中的下一组。我就是这么做的。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I was nervous and switched the cameras nine at a time. I never consciously acknowledged that one of the new cameras belonged to this room. As I already said, I simply failed to recognize that there was an extra black screen. The crystal rooms all look very similar, so I didn't really miss this one.
entries.new: 我当时很紧张，一次切换九个画面。我根本没留意新画面里有一块属于这间房。正如我所说，我只是没看出多出了一块黑屏。几个水晶展室看起来都很相似，所以我没特别注意到这一间。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: The shape of this one is completely different, though.
entries.new: 可这一间的形状完全不同。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: To tell you the truth, it all threw me off. The mere sight of the screens displaying nothing but black was disconcerting because they're equipped with night vision and I'd never seen them like that. I wasn't really thinking about the number of crystal rooms.
entries.new: 老实说，那情形把我弄懵了。光是看到屏幕上只剩一片黑，就足够叫人心慌——它们都装了夜视功能，我从没见过那样的画面。我根本没心思去数水晶展室的数目。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Katei's explanation was unconvincing, but there was nothing Sai could use to object to it. At least, not without the computer's sleep mode timer, which Sai didn't appear to be using for his argument.
entries.new: Katei 的解释难以服人，但 Sai 也拿不出什么来反驳。至少，不靠电脑的休眠计时器是驳不倒的——可 Sai 似乎并不打算拿它来当论据。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Katei hadn't addressed the event room either. If he'd seen the smoke appearing in the event room, it should've been a given that our group had been trapped in the tower, but that wasn't what he said when we met.
entries.new: Katei 也没提到活动室。他若真看到活动室冒出烟雾，按理说就该立刻想到我们这伙人被困在塔里了，可他见到我们时说的并不是这个。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was unbelievable that the event room wouldn't have been displayed on such a special day. If it really hadn't been, it meant that Katei hadn't failed to notice one extra black camera, but two. And it was still very questionable that he had stopped at Erina's group before ours.
entries.new: 在这么特殊的日子，活动室的画面居然没被调出来，实在令人难以置信。若果真如此，那就意味着 Katei 漏看的黑屏不是一块，而是两块。再说，他先找到 Erina 那一组、后找到我们，这本身也很可疑。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Everyone else looked dubious as well, but less so, as they hadn't yet entertained that possibility.
entries.new: 其他人也都面露疑虑，只是没那么深——他们还没往这个方向想过。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Not for a second do I believe anything that you're saying.
entries.new: 你说的这些，我一个字都不信。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I apologize for not being more convincing. I understand why you might find what I'm telling you strange, but I promise all of you that I'm telling the truth.
entries.new: 没能让你更信服，我很抱歉。我知道我说的这些话在你们听来很奇怪，但我向你们保证，我说的都是实话。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: So, you switched all the cameras at once and, for some reason, assumed only three places had been exposed to the smoke.
entries.new: 于是，你一次性切换了所有摄像头，又不知怎么的，认定只有三处被烟雾波及。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yes. I saw the smoke appearing in the hallways, which disabled multiple cameras. I mistakenly assumed all of them belonged to the hallways.
entries.new: 是的。我看见走廊里冒烟，有好几台摄像头因此失效。我误以为那些黑屏全都来自走廊。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: And after that, despite not having looked through every room, you claimed that the smoke hadn't been released anywhere else but in the three places we'd all personally observed.
entries.new: 然后，你明明没有逐间查看过所有房间，却宣称除了我们都亲眼看到的那三处，别处都没有释放过烟雾。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Correct. I apologize for my mistake. It seems it led you to suspect something about me, but I repeat that it was all a mistake I made in a rush.
entries.new: 没错。是我疏忽了，抱歉。看来这让你对我起了疑心，但我再说一遍，这全是我匆忙之中犯的错。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Let me be clear: I don't believe you nor intend to do so. You are full of shit. However, I don't know why you told us that only those three places had been hit, and it's pissing me off.{w} Do you remember when you said you'd left the lobby door open? Like Atsuki pointed out, it was opened after the smoke was released since almost none went through it. Still saying that's true?
entries.new: 我把话说清楚：我不信你，也不打算信你。你满嘴鬼话。可我还是想不通，你为什么要告诉我们只有那三处被烟雾波及——这让我很不痛快。{w} 你还记得你说过，大厅的门是你打开的吗？就像 Atsuki 指出的那样，那扇门是在烟雾放出之后才开的，因为几乎没有烟从那边透过去。你现在还坚持这个说法？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yes, of course.
entries.new: 是，当然。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Well, when you said that, I looked at the hallway A door. That one was properly closed.
entries.new: 你说那句话的时候，我看了一眼A走廊的门。那扇门关得好好的。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...And?
entries.new: ……然后呢？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: According to you, after you left the security room, you ended up where we were without going through the event room. If you'd done that, you would've gone through the lobby, so you should've opened both doors.
entries.new: 按你的说法，你离开监控室之后，没经过活动室就到了我们所在的地方。可如果真是那样，你就得穿过大厅，那两扇门你应该都打开过才对。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Which is what I did.
entries.new: 我确实都打开了。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: And why did you leave the hallway A door closed but not the other one?
entries.new: 那你为什么把A走廊的门关上了，另一扇却没有？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Because the three of you were unconscious in hallway B, and I hurried to kneel beside you.
entries.new: ……因为你们三个都昏倒在B走廊，我急忙蹲到你们身边。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Sure, I imagined you'd say that. However, if you really opened that door, what I find most likely is that you didn't come from the security room and that you never went through the other one. Maybe it was Naomi who opened it and you had to say you did it because of the movements you'd already claimed you made.
entries.new: 当然，我早就料到你会这么说。可如果你真打开过那扇门，我觉得最可能的情况是：你根本不是从监控室过来的，也没有穿过另一扇门。也许是 Naomi 打开的，而你先前已经交代过自己的行动路线，只好把这事也揽到自己头上。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You're ridiculous.
entries.new: 真是荒唐。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Okay, but if you'd never looked at the cameras or entered the rooms, why the hell did you say something that could easily be wrong...? Were you misinformed about the plan you took part in? That's what would be ridiculous.
entries.new: 好，可要是你根本没看过监控、也没进过那些房间，你为什么要说这种一戳就破的话……？难道你参与的那个计划，连你得到的消息都是错的？那才叫荒唐。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: *sigh* I already told you what happened. If you find it hard to believe, there's nothing else I can do.
entries.new: *叹气* 该说的我都说了。你要是不肯信，我也没有别的办法。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: There were a few seconds of silence during which nobody knew what to say. In the background, Isla ignored us and kept looking through the cabinets, hoping something had been left behind.
entries.new: 有几秒钟，谁都没有出声，也不知道该说什么。另一边，Isla 没理会我们，仍在翻看那些展示柜，盼着里面还留着什么。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Erina followed everything she did with her eyes, obviously unwilling to needlessly engage in the barrage Sai was firing off.
entries.new: Erina 的目光一直跟着她的动作，显然不愿无谓地卷进 Sai 那一连串炮火般的追问里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You know... It's possible you're right. It's possible that not noticing the extra black screen and the missing crystal room is too unlikely. Even under the stress of not knowing what was happening.
entries.new: 说起来……也许你说得对。没注意到多出来的那块黑屏，也没发现少了一间水晶展室，这确实不太可能。哪怕当时一头雾水、心里发慌，也不至于。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: What if this room was clean at that time? It has already been a long time since I looked through the cameras. The smoke could've been released here afterward.
entries.new: 如果那时这个房间还没有被动手脚呢？我看监控已经是很久以前的事了。这里的烟雾，也许是之后才放的。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: This wouldn't contradict anything, and it might make even more sense than what I first believed.
entries.new: 这不会和任何线索冲突，甚至比我先前那套说法更说得通。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Quick lie revision? Are we supposed to listen to that?
entries.new: 临时改口？这种话也要我们听？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Well, I don't know why that would've been done, but you can't deny it just because you find it unlikely.{w} It could very well be that it happened after I left the security room. The rooms all look very similar, so maybe I did see this one when I looked through the cameras. Now I'm not sure. I don't know which of the two possibilities I'm presenting is the correct one.
entries.new: 这个嘛，我也不知道为什么要那么做，但你不能只因为觉得不太可能就否定它。{w}完全有可能是在我离开监控室之后才发生的。这些房间看起来都差不多，说不定我看监控时确实看到了这一间。现在我也说不准了。我提出的两种可能性，到底哪一种是正确的，我自己也不知道。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: You know very well they're both incorrect. But yes, I can deny the second one.
entries.new: 你心里很清楚，两种都不对。不过，没错，第二种我确实可以否定。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: How would you do that?
entries.new: 你怎么否定？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: It has to do with something very important. Normally, I would've brought it up straight away.
entries.new: 这牵涉到一件很重要的事。按说，我一开始就该提出来。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It makes this whole situation much easier to understand. Remember the two questions from earlier? Why were the gemstones stolen, and how were they brought outside before the alarm went off?
entries.new: 有了它，整件事就好懂得多了。还记得之前那两个问题吗？宝石为什么被偷，又怎么在警报响起之前被带出去？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'm fairly sure the answers are, respectively, to make it seem like they were the goal of the attack, and because they were stolen before the time we thought.
entries.new: 我基本可以确定，答案分别是：为了让它们看起来像是袭击的目标；以及，它们在我们以为的时间之前就已经被偷走了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I mean, the curtains here were lowered when we entered. Most importantly, they were stained with the smoke.{w} This means that during the time the smoke was released, the cabinets were covered.
entries.new: 我是说，我们进来的时候，这里的遮布是放下来的。最关键的是，遮布上沾了烟雾的痕迹。{w}也就是说，放烟雾的时候，这些展示柜是遮着的。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: If someone stole the contents of these cabinets when the smoke was being released, as the Ashiya family thinks right now, why would they have lowered the curtains again? No way they would've all fallen down by themselves.
entries.new: 如果有人是在放烟雾的时候偷走这些柜子里的东西——就像芦屋家现在以为的那样——那他们为什么还要把遮布重新放下来？总不可能所有遮布都自己掉下来吧。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You all see what I'm saying, right? It would have been a pointless waste of time to lower them. After the smoke was released in this room, the curtains weren't moved.{w} To put it simply, the gemstones that were once here were stolen before the smoke was released. This is why someone was able to bring them outside before the exit closed.
entries.new: 你们都明白我的意思吧？再放下来纯属浪费时间。这个房间放出烟雾之后，遮布就没再被动过。{w}简单来说，原本放在这里的宝石，是在烟雾放出之前就被偷走的。所以才会有人能在出口关闭之前把它们带出去。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I suppose that makes sense, but how did they do that?
entries.new: 听上去有道理，可他们是怎么做到的？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: You tell me. What's important is that they could've been stolen during the night. Then, before the exit closed, they were brought out.
entries.new: 这得问你了。重要的是，它们有可能是在夜里被偷走的。然后在出口关闭之前被带了出去。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: By releasing the smoke here too, they tried to make it look like the gems were stolen at a later time and that they were the actual target of the theft.
entries.new: 他们在这里也放了烟雾，就是想让人以为宝石是在更晚的时候被偷的，而且它们才是这次盗窃真正的目标。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...What you're saying makes sense, but I still have a hard time visualizing how this plan works.
entries.new: ……你说的有道理，可我还是很难想象这个计划具体是怎么运作的。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Me too. A very important thing we don't know yet is whether the alarm was taken into consideration. You said it was a top-secret alarm, right?
entries.new: 我也是。还有一件很关键的事我们不知道：他们有没有把警报算进去。你说过那是绝密警报，对吧？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yes. I believe it's nearly impossible that Xyn designed a plan with it in mind.
entries.new: 对。我认为 Xyn 几乎不可能在制定计划时考虑到它。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: If so, that means the smoke here couldn't have been released after you left the security room. That would only have been done if they already knew the exit was getting locked down.
entries.new: 这样的话，这里的烟雾就不可能是你离开监控室之后才放的。只有已经知道出口即将封锁，才会那么做。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I believe you're right. If they didn't know about the alarm, they would not have staggered the smoke in this room. It would've been released everywhere at once.
entries.new: 你说得对。如果不知道警报的事，他们不会让这个房间的烟雾晚一步放出，而是会在各处同时释放。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...Exactly.
entries.new: ……正是。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Can I say something? We're only assuming the gems here were stolen before the time of the attack because the curtains were down. That makes sense, but wouldn't they have thought of it?
entries.new: ……我能说一句吗？我们之所以认为这里的宝石是在袭击之前就被偷走的，只是因为遮布放了下来。这确实说得通，可他们难道会想不到这一点吗？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That's true. If Xyn didn't know about the alarm, they must've expected Ashiya to rush in right away. They would only have seen these curtains, not that the gems were missing.
entries.new: 确实。如果 Xyn 不知道警报，他们一定以为芦屋会立刻冲进来。那样他们只会看到这些遮布，而不会发现宝石不见了。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah. After all, they only believe these random gems were the target because they don't have access to the tower. Isn't it as if the alarm is working positively for the culprit?
entries.new: 对。毕竟，他们之所以认定这些随便摆在这里的宝石就是目标，只是因为他们进不了塔。这么看，警报反倒像是在帮犯人的忙，不是吗？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yeah... There's no way Xyn would've ignored the curtains giving away the timing of the theft, right?
entries.new: 嗯……遮布会暴露盗窃的时间，Xyn 不可能忽略这一点吧？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Not if they didn't know about the alarm. If they did, and the intent was to simply let Ashiya think what they think until the tower unlocks, it doesn't matter that we've figured it out. After all, it's not like we can contact the outside to tell them, is it?
entries.new: 除非他们并不知道警报的事。要是他们知道，而且目的只是让芦屋一直抱着现在的想法，直到塔解锁，那就算我们看穿了也无所谓。毕竟，我们也没法联系外面告诉他们，对吧？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You're wrong. Then they would've had no reason to release the smoke here.
entries.new: 你错了。那样的话，他们就没有理由在这里放烟雾了。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Hm, I'm not sure. We did have the chance to talk to the police, but it happened before we came here.{w} I'm saying this was done to trick Ashiya into thinking the gems were the goal. However, I also think that the plan must somehow end by stealing the Sekimeiya, which will directly reveal that the gems were never the goal. It could definitely be that the smoke was released to trick us—the people who got trapped. It all depends on whether someone is trying to trick us.
entries.new: 嗯，我也说不准。我们确实有过联系警方的机会，但那是在我们来这里之前。{w}我的意思是，他们这么做是为了让芦屋以为宝石才是目标。不过我也认为，这个计划最后必定会以偷走 Sekimeiya 收场，而那样就直接表明宝石从来不是目标。那些烟雾说不定就是为了骗我们这些被困住的人。关键在于，到底有没有人在骗我们。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: There were a few seconds of silence. Would Xyn have put so much effort into deceiving us? It didn't sound likely, but it was true that we had a method to contact the outside and could've informed Ashiya of every suspicious detail we'd noticed. It was strange, because if the culprit had always been able to disable the communication method, there would have been no point in doing any of it.
entries.new: 几秒钟的沉默。Xyn 会花这么大力气来骗我们吗？听起来不太可能，但我们确实有办法联系外界，本来也可以把注意到的每一处可疑之处都告诉芦屋。奇怪的是，如果犯人一直有办法切断我们的联络，那做这些就毫无意义了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Do you actually believe the alarm was considered?
entries.new: ……你真觉得他们考虑过警报？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Who knows? If the gems were stolen during the night through some method Xyn are capable of, they'd leave the curtains lowered to prevent it from being noticed through the cameras and so that the visitors couldn't see them before {time=9:10.}
entries.new: 谁知道呢。如果宝石是在夜里被 Xyn 用某种他们办得到的手段偷走的，那他们就会让遮布一直保持放下，免得被监控看出来，也让参观者在 {time=9:10.} 之前看不到里面。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I wasn't the guard on duty last night, so I can't help you with that.
entries.new: 昨晚值班的守卫不是我，这个我帮不了你。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...{w}Well, they were forced to leave the cabinets covered, but doing so also indicates that the gems were stolen before the doors were open to the public...
entries.new: ……{w}总之，他们是不得已才让展示柜一直遮着，可这样一来，也说明宝石是在对公众开放之前就被偷走的……
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: *sigh*
entries.new: *叹气*
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I don't know why. I've approached it from different angles, but I can't come up with something that makes sense.{w} In some way, these gems must've only been a side part of the plan. Them getting stolen before the smoke was released is close to confirmation, but how everything pieces together is not as simple to figure out.
entries.new: 我不知道为什么。我换了好几个角度去想，还是想不出一个说得通的解释。{w}从某种意义上看，这些宝石一定只是计划中的次要部分。它们是在烟雾放出之前就被偷走的，这几乎可以确定；但整件事怎么拼在一起，就不是那么容易想明白的了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I apologize that I can't be of more help. I assume this is Xyn's doing, but I don't know what they intend to do. I am equally clueless when it comes to how these gems could've been stolen before this morning.
entries.new: 很抱歉，我帮不上更多忙。我猜这是 Xyn 所为，但不知道他们打算做什么。至于这些宝石怎么可能在今天早上之前就被偷走，我同样毫无头绪。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Sai, I know you don't believe much of what I say, but I have been honest from the beginning. I have just been trying to help and provide you with as much information as I can.
entries.new: Sai，我知道我说的话你多半不信，但我从一开始就没有撒谎。我只是想帮忙，把我能提供的信息尽量都告诉你。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Is that so?
entries.new: 是这样吗？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: While everyone stood still, Sai began to examine the room. Even though it looked drastically different from the others, only the illumination and shape varied. It was still a simple room that only contained cabinets.
entries.new: 众人还愣在原地，Sai 已经开始打量这间屋子。它看上去与其余几间大不相同，可变化的只有光线和形状，说到底仍是个只摆着展示柜的简单房间。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't think there's much to do here. Every cabinet is empty, and the same kind of smoke was released, most likely at the same time as in the other places. We should move on.
entries.new: 这里应该没什么可查的了。每个展示柜都是空的，释放的也是同一种烟雾，多半和其他几处同时发生。我们走吧。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Yeah. Let's get going.
entries.new: ……嗯。走吧。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Isla seemed happy with that proposition as well. We all agreed and left quietly to avoid any more conflict.
entries.new: Isla 似乎也赞成这个提议。大家一致同意，为了不再起争执，我们安静地离开了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Only the storeroom remained in hallway A. We tried to enter it together, but it was too narrow for all of us.
entries.new: A走廊只剩下储藏室还没查。我们本想一起进去，可门内太窄，容不下所有人。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was a stretched-out, dim room. While the name implied that its purpose was to store things, the amount of space didn't allow for much of that, and it only contained a few empty shelves and a dusty couch that looked dangerous to sit in. Even the door was lower quality than the rest.
entries.new: 房间狭长而昏暗。名字虽说是用来储物，可这点空间也存不了多少东西，里面只有几个空架子，还有一张落满灰尘、坐上去怕是会出事的沙发。连门都比别处劣质。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I exited the room as Akaro and Erina entered it. Sai seemed to be enjoying himself, considering different options in an attempt to "win".
entries.new: Akaro 和 Erina 进去时，我退了出来。Sai 似乎乐在其中，正盘算着各种可能，想借此「赢」下来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If we parted from the assumption that there was a plan more complex than met the eye, I had something to consider.
entries.new: 若抛开表象，假设背后另有更复杂的算计，那有一点值得我细想。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We had all assumed that the gems were stolen before the smoke was released since the curtains had been lowered. If anyone stole the gems after the attack, there was no reason to waste their time lowering the curtains again.{w} However, that was a very simple indicator of the time the gems had been stolen, and one that would not have been overlooked.
entries.new: 遮布被放了下来，所以我们才都认定宝石是在烟雾释放之前被偷走的。若有人是在袭击之后才行窃，就没必要多此一举再把遮布放下。{w} 可这个判断失窃时间的依据实在太过简单，谁都不会忽略。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So, what if the curtains had been lowered again precisely for that reason? To make us, or anyone who looked at it, think that they had been stolen before the time of the attack. After all, anything else would've been a huge mistake.
entries.new: 那么，如果遮布正是为此才被重新放下呢？为了让我们——或任何看到这一幕的人——以为宝石是在袭击之前失窃的。毕竟除此之外的任何情形，都等于犯下大错。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't think of an immediate benefit, but deliberately misleading us about the time or reason behind an action was a potent move. That effect wouldn't have been achieved if the tower had really been robbed at night and the curtains were left down. {w} ...And realistically, even though Xyn could've been involved, how could they have emptied so many cabinets during the night? Hadn't the police been nearby? Hadn't the cameras been monitoring everything?
entries.new: 我一时想不到这能带来什么好处，但刻意误导他人对某个举动的时间与缘由的判断，本身就是极有效的手段。若塔里真是在夜里失窃，遮布也一直垂着，就达不到这样的效果。{w} ……况且说实在的，就算 Xyn 牵涉其中，他们又怎能在夜里搬空那么多展示柜？警察难道不在附近？监控难道没有拍下一切？
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Before I could determine if there was a better conclusion to reach, everyone left the storeroom, Katei returning last.
entries.new: 我还没想清楚是否另有更合理的结论，众人已陆续走出储藏室，Katei 走在最后。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We didn't all have to enter. There isn't anywhere to hide in here.
entries.new: 不必全都挤进来。这里根本没有能藏人的地方。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: What's this room even for? It's called the storeroom, but there isn't much inside, and I doubt it'd be much use with how small it is.
entries.new: 这房间到底是干什么用的？叫储藏室，里面却没多少东西，还这么小，我看也派不上什么用场。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Things have been stored here before, but it's true that now it looks like a useless room. I heard that this room already existed before this building started to be used for business, and it was too small to give it any other purpose.
entries.new: 以前确实在这里存过东西，不过如今看来，它就是个派不上用场的房间。听说这栋楼改作商用之前，这间屋子就已经存在了，因为太小，也改不成别的用途。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I see...
entries.new: 原来如此……
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The door didn't look that different from the others. However, once you opened it, the room would detract from the aesthetic the place usually had. I figured that when the building was repurposed, they replaced the door but left the inside unchanged.
entries.new: 那扇门看上去和别处没什么两样。可一打开，屋里的景象就破坏了这里一贯的美感。我猜这栋楼改用途时，门换了新的，里面却原封未动。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...So we're halfway done with this floor. Maybe we'll find something in hallway B.
entries.new: ……这么说这层我们已经查了一半。说不定 B走廊能有所发现。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: To get there, we stepped into hallway C for the first time, which contained the stairs and elevator to move through the different floors.
entries.new: 为了过去，我们头一次踏进 C走廊——通往各层的楼梯和电梯都在那里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What's this...?
entries.new: 这是……？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Something immediately caught our attention.
entries.new: 有件东西立刻吸引了我们的注意。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's a suitcase, Katei.
entries.new: 一个行李箱，Katei。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Yes. What is it doing here?
entries.new: ……嗯。它怎么会在这儿？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: We all approached it. Just like he said, a small and conspicuous black suitcase was lying in the middle of the hallway, next to the wall.
entries.new: 我们一齐走上前。正如他所说，一只不大的黑色行李箱格外显眼地躺在走廊中央，紧挨着墙。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Let's see... There might be something inside.
entries.new: 看看再说……里面说不定有东西。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai went ahead and unclasped it. He opened it up on the floor and exposed its interior.
entries.new: Sai 径直上前打开卡扣，就着地面把箱子摊开，露出里面的东西。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Nothing...?
entries.new: 什么都没有……？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That's disappointing, but I suppose otherwise they wouldn't have left it here.
entries.new: 真让人失望。不过反过来说，若里头有东西，对方大概也不会把它留在这儿。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Did you see this when you looked through the security cameras?
entries.new: 你查看监控的时候，看到过这个吗？
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Erina looked at Katei. The cameras in hallway C hadn't been touched, so Katei should've been able to look through them.
entries.new: Erina 望向 Katei。C走廊的摄像头没有被动过，Katei 理应能看到那里的画面。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He didn't.
entries.new: 他没看到。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Right. I would've told you if I had.
entries.new: 对。要是看到了，我会告诉你们的。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I see. Does that mean that it was left after we woke up?
entries.new: 原来如此。那是否说明，它是在我们醒来之后才被放在这里的？
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: No, of course not. Did you not hear anything I said? He never looked through the cameras.
entries.new: 不，当然不是。我刚刚说的话你没听见吗？他根本没看过监控。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You're still going with that? I guess you'll never change your mind.
entries.new: 你还是坚持这套说法？看来你是不会改主意了。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I understand you can't say that you saw this suitcase since it'd be suspicious you hadn't told us, but you should give up on the lie. It's kind of pathetic.
entries.new: 我明白你没法承认自己见过这只箱子，毕竟一直瞒着我们反而更可疑。但这谎还是别撒了，实在有些难看。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: If you really didn't see this, it would mean that someone was here after or right before we woke up. It's not impossible, but I don't find it more likely than you lying.
entries.new: 如果你真没看到，那就说明有人在我们醒来之后、或者就在醒来前不久来过这里。这不是不可能，但我不觉得这比你在撒谎更有可能。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Katei looked at us. He was asking if we all thought the same, and no replies were heard.
entries.new: Katei 看向我们。他是在问，我们是不是都这么想。没有人应声。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Look at where the cameras are positioned. A bit of smoke covered them, but not enough to block the image completely.
entries.new: 看看摄像头架在什么位置。是有一些烟雾遮住了镜头，但还不至于把画面完全挡住。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: One encompasses the bathrooms, and the other records the staircase and elevator. This middle section isn't shown at all. Even if the suitcase was here, I wouldn't have seen it. That's why none of us saw it earlier when we briefly looked through the monitors.
entries.new: 一个拍的是洗手间，另一个拍的是楼梯和电梯。中间这一段根本不在画面里。就算当时箱子已经在这儿，我也看不到。所以刚才我们匆匆扫过监控时，谁都没发现它。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I figured you'd say that, but it's only an excuse. If you actually inspected this floor, there's no way you never came across it.
entries.new: 我猜你就会这么说，可这不过是借口。你若是真查过这一层，绝不可能没撞见它。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I inspected part of this floor and didn't see it. Not because I didn't come here, but because it wasn't here yet.
entries.new: 我查过这一层的部分区域，没有看到它。不是因为我没来过，而是那时它还不在这里。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I see. It's a shame the recorded footage just so happened to stop being accessible.
entries.new: 原来如此。可惜偏偏那么巧，录像正好看不了了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You're right, that's unfortunate. It'd be an easy way to prove myself.
entries.new: 你说得对，确实可惜。那本是证明我清白最省事的办法。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Sai and Isla continued examining the suitcase, but they didn't find anything. No smaller compartments appeared to exist, so it was actually empty.
entries.new: Sai 和 Isla 继续翻查箱子，却一无所获。箱内似乎没有更小的隔层，确实是空的。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Look. I can see traces of the smoke.
entries.new: 看，这里有烟雾留下的痕迹。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Oh, right. There's no way it was hit directly, though.
entries.new: 哦，对。不过它应该没有被直接喷到吧。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah. Perhaps it made contact with it before it had fully faded. I'm not sure.
entries.new: 嗯。也许是在烟雾散尽之前沾上的。我也不确定。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Why was it left here, then? If it happened after you looked around, it's a big red flag telling us that someone else is still here.
entries.new: 那它为什么会被留在这里？如果这是在你查看之后才发生的，那就等于明明白白地告诉我们，还有别人留在这里。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: But we already know that. It must've been Naomi.{w} After she did something, she must've wanted to get rid of this and didn't care about leaving it here. It makes sense that she would have disabled the security system before dropping it.
entries.new: 可这一点我们早就知道了。只可能是 Naomi。{w} 她做完那件事之后，想必就想处理掉这个，也不在乎把它丢在这里。她会在丢下它之前先关掉安保系统，这说得通。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: That's stupid. Footage is still being recorded, so I doubt she'd care whether we saw her or not. Especially given that leaving the suitcase after we woke up tells us she's here.
entries.new: 这说法未免太蠢了。录像还在继续拍，我不觉得她会在意我们有没有看到她。何况，她若是在我们醒来后才把行李箱放在那里，就等于告诉我们她还在这里。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...The culprit must've wanted to get rid of the suitcase as soon as possible since it's linked to the robbery attempt. Suripo did tell us an "individual" was found outside with a black suitcase, so being seen with one wouldn't be desirable.
entries.new: ……犯人想必想尽快处理掉那个行李箱，因为它和那起抢劫未遂事件有关。Suripo 确实说过，外面发现过一个带着黑色行李箱的「人」，所以被人看见自己拿着行李箱总归不妙。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: If Katei is telling the truth, it means that whoever left it here could've only been Naomi or an unknown culprit. ...There's technically another possibility, but it's too ridiculous to consider it seriously.
entries.new: 如果 Katei 说的是真话，那么把行李箱留在这里的人，只可能是 Naomi，或者某个我们不知道的犯人。……严格来说，还有一种可能，但实在荒谬，没必要当真。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: When we went to the mechanical room, you all stayed together, right?
entries.new: 我们去机械室的时候，你们一直待在一起吧？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: For better or worse, Sai had been thinking the same.
entries.new: 也不知是好是坏，Sai 显然也想到了同一个问题。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yes. Nobody left the security room.
entries.new: 是的。没人离开过监控室。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: You want to suspect us this openly? Did you two get separated at all when you left?
entries.new: 你就这么明目张胆地怀疑我们？你们离开的时候，有没有分开过？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: N-Now that you mention it, yes.{w} I went to the mechanical room while Atsuki said he would inspect the rest of this floor.
entries.new: 这、这么一说，确实有。{w} 我去了机械室，Atsuki 则说他要去查看这一层剩下的地方。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Wh-What?
entries.new: 什、什么？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: It was a strange sensation, seeing everyone turn to me while I silently waited for Sai to retract what he said.
entries.new: 大家一齐看向我，而我默默等着 Sai 收回刚才那句话——那种感觉说不出的古怪。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...He's messing with you.
entries.new: ……他在耍你们。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Probably. We didn't get separated.
entries.new: 多半是。我们并没有分开。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You aren't being funny.
entries.new: 这并不好笑。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Well, I'm just surprised you don't find us suspicious.
entries.new: 我只是有点意外，你们居然不觉得我们可疑。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Why would we? Even though you left, that's not enough of a reason.
entries.new: 为什么要怀疑？你们虽然离开过，但那不足以成为理由。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Ah, no. That's not what I meant. I think you have a good reason to suspect us.{w} Don't you remember when we got back? We said we'd gone to the bathroom, didn't we?
entries.new: 啊，不，我不是那个意思。我觉得你们有充分的理由怀疑我们。{w} 你还记得我们回来的时候吗？我们说过去洗手间了，对吧？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Did you? I didn't hear you from under the desk.
entries.new: 有吗？我躲在桌子底下，可没听见。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I bet you regret not accusing us first, then.
entries.new: 那你现在一定后悔没先指控我们了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Did we go to the bathroom and miss this suitcase? It could be Katei was right and it wasn't here yet.
entries.new: 难道我们去洗手间的时候，正好错过了这个行李箱？也许 Katei 说得对，那时候它还不在这里。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Don't take him seriously. We didn't go.
entries.new: ……别听他的。我们没去。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Of course. Katei wouldn't really tell the truth, would he? Admittedly, we were a bit late, so we agreed we'd say that so we weren't suspected of anything.
entries.new: 当然。Katei 怎么可能真说实话呢？不过我们确实来晚了一点，所以商量好那么说，免得被人怀疑。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We never came here, but I knew we should've. Didn't I tell you?
entries.new: 我们根本没来过这里，可我知道我们本该来一趟。我不是跟你说过吗？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: So you accuse me of lying and immediately admit to lying yourself. Your arguments keep falling apart.
entries.new: 你指控我说谎，转头又承认自己在撒谎。你的说法根本站不住脚。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...We don't really have a way to know when this was left here, but I'd say it's likely it wasn't one of us. It must've been left by the people behind the attack.
entries.new: ……我们确实没法知道这东西是什么时候留在这里的，不过我看多半不是我们当中的人。应该是袭击事件的幕后之人留下的。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Right, and most likely before we woke up. There could be a reason why they had to leave it here.
entries.new: 对，而且很可能是在我们醒来之前。他们不得已把它留在这里，或许有什么原因。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Like what?
entries.new: ……什么原因？
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: No clue. I'm only saying that because the smoke wasn't released here. Even though this exact spot isn't recorded, whoever left the suitcase must've been seen by one of these two cameras.
entries.new: 我之所以这么说，只是因为这里没有释放烟雾。虽然这个位置本身没被拍到，但放下行李箱的人一定被这两台摄像头中的某一台拍到过。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: If you wanted to dispose of something incriminating, I'd say you'd do it in a place without cameras, and there are many.
entries.new: 如果想处理掉什么见不得光的东西，总该挑没有摄像头的地方吧？而这里没摄像头的地方多得是。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That's true. If it was put here after Katei inspected this floor, whoever did it is back to hiding.
entries.new: 有道理。如果是在 Katei 检查完这一层之后才放下的，那动手的人现在又躲回去了。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Which is why we should keep investigating. Let's finish checking the crystal floor and move up.
entries.new: 所以我们才要继续查。先把水晶层检查完，再往上走。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: The bathrooms were empty, so we were ready to move on. Regarding the suitcase, we weren't sure what to think, but we didn't take it with us.{w} The location where it had been discarded was the only information we had to work with. I didn't want to think too deeply into every detail, but something came to mind.
entries.new: 洗手间里空无一人，我们便准备继续调查。至于那个行李箱，我们不知道该怎么判断，但也没有把它带走。{w} 唯一能供我们推敲的线索，就是它被丢弃的地点。我本不想对每个细节想得太深，可有个念头还是冒了出来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It could be that Katei was right this time. The location someone chose to leave the suitcase was one we hadn't yet been in.{w} If the culprit left it there before we woke up, I can't think of a reason why they wouldn't have left it in one of the two main hallways. After all, the plan only involved them and the event room at a glance. At no point was it necessary to enter hallway C, which has security cameras.
entries.new: 也许这一次 Katei 说对了。留下行李箱的人所选的地点，正是我们还没去过的地方。{w} 如果犯人在我们醒来之前就把它留在那里，我想不出他们为什么不干脆放在两条主走廊中的一条。毕竟表面上看，整个计划只涉及他们和活动室。根本没有必要进入装有监控摄像头的 C走廊。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I felt someone might've been nearby and had known we hadn't yet been in hallway C. They'd chosen it so that we couldn't be sure it hadn't been there the whole time. If they'd known we couldn't access the saved footage anymore, they could've tricked us. If they'd left it in one of the two parallel hallways instead, we would've immediately known it wasn't there before.
entries.new: 我觉得，也许有人就在附近，而且知道我们还没去过 C走廊。对方选在那里，就是为了让我们无法确定行李箱是不是从一开始就在。如果对方知道我们已经调不出保存的录像，就能借此误导我们。可要是把行李箱留在两条平行走廊中的任意一条，我们立刻就能知道它之前并不在那里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In addition, that spot wasn't in range of any of the cameras, so we couldn't have seen it while we'd been in the security room.{w} ...But the trick wouldn't work on Katei, who'd already inspected the area.
entries.new: 此外，那个位置不在任何摄像头的拍摄范围内，所以我们待在监控室时不可能看到它。{w} ……但这套把戏对已经检查过那片区域的 Katei 不起作用。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, there was a plethora of reasons to believe he was lying. The culprit could've known that Katei had never been in hallway C, and unaware he had lied about it, placed the suitcase to trick him as well.
entries.new: 然而，有太多理由让人相信他在说谎。犯人也可能知道 Katei 从未进过 C走廊，却不知道他在这件事上撒了谎，于是把行李箱放在那里，想连他一起骗过。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There weren't many better places to do that. It was true that upper floors existed, but according to Katei, they weren't open to the public. No matter the way I thought about it, it was baffling that it hadn't been left in a room without cameras like the storeroom.
entries.new: 比那更合适的地方并不多。楼上确实还有楼层，但据 Katei 说，那些地方并不对公众开放。可无论怎么想，我还是不明白，为什么它没有被留在储藏室那种没有摄像头的房间里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I thought about it as we entered hallway B, and an ominous feeling hit me. If I was right, someone else trapped there was still very close to us.
entries.new: 我们走进 B走廊时，我仍在想这件事，一股不祥的预感忽然袭来。如果我没猜错，还有另一个人被困在这里，而且离我们很近。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We walked to the first room, which had a sign stuck on its door. When we removed the smoke dust on it, we saw an image of a mop and a bucket.
entries.new: 我们走到第一个房间前，门上贴着一块标牌。擦掉上面的烟尘后，我们看到一幅拖把和水桶的图案。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As you see, the cleaning cart is left here when it's not in use, alongside cleaning products and items.
entries.new: 如你们所见，清洁推车不用的时候就放在这里，旁边还有清洁用品之类的东西。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Yeah, there's probably nothing of importance here. It's not a big room.
entries.new: 嗯，这里应该没什么重要的东西。房间也不大。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Akaro was the first to step inside and glance around. As he'd said, the room was small and only served the obvious purpose of storing cleaning materials. After stepping in and out, we all agreed and silently moved on to the crystal rooms in hallway B.
entries.new: Akaro 第一个走进去，环视了一圈。正如他所说，房间很小，显然只是用来存放清洁用品。我们进去看过后都表示同意，便默默前往 B走廊的水晶展室。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We had the first one in front—B6. Once Katei and Isla made sure nothing was off, we moved to the next door.
entries.new: 第一间就在我们面前——B6。Katei 和 Isla 确认没有异常后，我们走向下一扇门。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is the staff room, right?
entries.new: 这是员工室吧？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yes. Visitors are not supposed to go in, but it's not locked.
entries.new: 没错。访客按理不能进去，不过门没锁。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: So we can't go in?
entries.new: 那我们不能进去吗？
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Don't worry. It's fine under the circumstances.
entries.new: 别担心。这种情况下进去也没关系。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Katei opened the door. Behind it, we saw another small room, different than all the others we'd been in.
entries.new: Katei 推开门。门后又是一间小屋，和我们之前进过的所有房间都不一样。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Every staff member has their own space here. We use it to leave and pick up personal objects, and it's where we store our uniforms before heading off.
entries.new: 每位员工在这里都有自己的空间，用来存放和取用私人物品，下班前也会把制服放在这里。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I see. So the belongings of some employees are still in these lockers.
entries.new: 原来如此。所以有些员工的物品还留在这几个储物柜里。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Isla soon stopped looking interested, but for the rest of us, it was the most notable room yet.
entries.new: Isla 很快就不太感兴趣了，但对我们其余人来说，这却是目前为止最引人注意的房间。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yes, but everyone tends to lock them.
entries.new: 是啊，不过大家一般都会上锁。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Let's see if any are open.
entries.new: 去看看有没有哪个没上锁吧。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'm not sure we should. We might get in trouble.
entries.new: 我觉得还是别这么做。说不定会惹上麻烦。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: You kidding me? There could be a phone or something in here. I'd call that incredibly useful.
entries.new: 开什么玩笑？这里面说不定有电话之类的。那可太有用了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: As I said, they're not usually left open. You can check if you want.
entries.new: 我说过了，这些柜子平时都锁着。你要想查，尽管去看。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Sai went ahead and tried to open every locker.{w} Shortly, we confirmed that Katei was right: they were all locked tight.
entries.new: Sai 径直上前，试着逐个打开储物柜。{w} 没过多久我们就证实 Katei 说得没错：所有柜子都锁得严严实实。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You have your own locker, right? Do you keep anything that could be useful in it?
entries.new: 你也有自己的储物柜吧？里面有没有放什么能派上用场的东西？
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: No. They do allow us to bring phones in as long as we keep them here, but I never bring mine. Right now, the only thing in my locker should be my coat.
entries.new: 没有。他们确实允许我们带手机进来，只要把手机放在这里，不过我从来不带。现在我的柜子里应该只有一件外套。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Can we see it?
entries.new: 能让我们看看吗？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You want to see my coat?
entries.new: 你想看我的外套？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Partly yes, but I also want to see the lack of other things.
entries.new: 算是吧，不过我也想确认里面没有别的东西。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Do you still think I'm lying? Very well, it's good that this is something I can easily prove.
entries.new: 你还觉得我在说谎？也好，这件事我正好能轻易证明。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Katei took a few keys out of his pocket. One of them was the one he'd used to unlock the security room.
entries.new: Katei 从口袋里取出几把钥匙。其中一把正是他之前用来打开监控室的。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He inserted a small one into a locker and turned it. Without a problem, he opened the door and showed us what was inside.
entries.new: 他把其中一把小钥匙插进储物柜，转动了一下。柜门应声而开，他把里面的东西展示给我们看。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We could only see a coat, but Katei went ahead and brought it out to show that nothing else was hidden behind it. He went as far as to show us every empty pocket.
entries.new: 里面只能看到一件外套，但 Katei 还是把它取了出来，证明后面没有藏别的东西。他甚至把每个空口袋都翻给我们看。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You see? I understand it's easy to suspect me, but I've only been telling the truth.
entries.new: 看到了吧？我明白，怀疑我很容易，可我一直说的都是实话。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: One truth doesn't make up for all the previous lies. Certainly, if the contents of your locker were harmful to you, you would've claimed not to have any.
entries.new: 一次实话弥补不了之前所有的谎话。更何况，若柜里的东西会对你不利，你自然会一口咬定里面什么都没有。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I really can't make you happy. Do you have more requests that would prove my sincerity?
entries.new: 我实在没法让你满意。你还想让我做什么，来证明我的诚意？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: No, not really.
entries.new: 没有了，没什么要求。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Katei put the coat back inside and locked it up again.
entries.new: Katei 把外套放回去，又重新锁上了柜子。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: All the lockers were very tall and had an extra smaller compartment in their upper part. Three horizontal bars could be seen in the metallic doors, slits that allowed us to somewhat see the interior of those smaller compartments. However, I couldn't spot anything of importance, as the darkness concealed what was in them.
entries.new: 所有储物柜都很高，上半部另有一个较小的隔层。金属门上可见三道横向细缝，透过缝隙勉强能窥见小隔层内部。只是里面黑漆漆的，我什么要紧的东西都没看见。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Everyone was listening closely to the conversations between Katei and Sai. Sai had continually reiterated that Katei was openly lying to us, so it was no surprise that they wanted to form their own thoughts.
entries.new: 所有人都在仔细听着 Katei 和 Sai 的对话。Sai 一再重申 Katei 在当面撒谎，大家想自己判断也不足为奇。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai knew nothing would be found inside the locker, so I suspect he wanted to see that coat. If it was the same one he'd seen Katei wearing in the lobby, it could back up his identity.
entries.new: Sai 知道柜子里找不到什么，所以我猜他想看的是那件外套。如果那正是他在大厅里见过 Katei 穿的那件，就能佐证 Katei 的身份。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Since he didn't react to it, it's fair to assume it was the same one, but it doesn't settle anything. One extra step of his impersonation plan could've involved changing the locker's contents while we were unconscious.
entries.new: 既然他没什么反应，姑且可以认为就是同一件，但这说明不了什么。若他真要冒充，完全可能趁我们昏迷时把柜里的东西换掉。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Could there be a way to force open the lockers? One of them must be Naomi's, so it'd be interesting to look inside it.
entries.new: 有没有办法强行打开储物柜？其中一个肯定是 Naomi 的，看看里面应该会很有意思。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What? No, please don't think about that. There are no tools to do it with, the lockers are quite sturdy, and I'm sure Ashiya would not be happy about it.
entries.new: 什么？不行，请别打这个主意。这里没有能用的工具，柜子也很结实，而且我敢肯定芦屋不会乐意看到这种事。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Similarly, I'm not happy with spending twelve boring hours here without getting to conclusions. Right now, Naomi is very suspicious.
entries.new: 同样，我也不想在这里无聊地耗上十二个小时，最后却什么结论都没有。眼下 Naomi 的嫌疑很大。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: And what if she is? What do you think you'll find inside her locker? I'm letting you overstep a little. You shouldn't be allowed in this room, but I will not be giving you free reign. Please, get this idea out of your head.
entries.new: 就算她可疑又怎样？你觉得她柜子里能找到什么？我已经让你越界了一点。这间屋子本来不该让你进，但我不会让你为所欲为。请把这个念头打消吧。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I'll keep thinking whatever I want, but I agree. It'd probably be a worthless hassle. If Naomi is the culprit, she must know how suspicious she is, so she wouldn't have left anything relevant in her locker.
entries.new: 我想怎么想是我的事，不过这点我同意。那多半只是白费力气。如果 Naomi 真是犯人，她肯定知道自己有多可疑，不会把相关的东西留在柜子里。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...That's what I'm saying.
entries.new: ……我就是这个意思。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Isla tugged at Erina's clothes.
entries.new: Isla 拽了拽 Erina 的衣角。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Let's go. There's nothing in here...
entries.new: 走吧。这里什么都没有……
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: We kept moving at a good pace until we had searched through the remaining five crystal rooms in hallway B. They all looked the same, and nothing felt out of place.
entries.new: 我们一路走得挺快，把 B走廊里剩下的五间水晶展室都搜了一遍。它们看上去全都一样，也没有任何异样。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is it. We knew that if someone was hiding, it wouldn't be easy to find them.
entries.new: 到此为止了。我们本就清楚，若真有人藏着，也不会轻易被找到。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yeah. It's already past {time=10.} One more person is confirmed to be with us, so if she hasn't appeared yet, she must not intend to show herself.
entries.new: 是啊。现在已经过了 {time=10.}。已经确认多了一个人和我们在一起，如果她还没露面，那多半是不打算现身了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Sai and I considered that Naomi's body might've been hidden. If that's what happened, it's likely no one else is hiding. The main point that indicates otherwise is the suitcase, but if Katei lied about it, he could be the one who hid Naomi.
entries.new: ……我和 Sai 也考虑过，Naomi 的尸体可能被人藏了起来。若真是如此，恐怕就没有别人藏着了。唯一能推翻这个推断的，是那只手提箱；可如果 Katei 在手提箱的事上撒谎，藏起 Naomi 的人也许就是他。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: We'll have to move up, then. We might find something on the higher floors.
entries.new: 那我们就得往上走了。楼上也许能找到线索。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Our priority should be to understand the structure of this place and find Naomi. We'll have many hours to go after that, which won't make it easy for anyone to stay hidden.
entries.new: 我们的首要任务是弄清这里的结构，并找到 Naomi。之后还有很多时间，到那时谁想一直藏着就没那么容易了。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We approached the hallway C staircase.
entries.new: 我们走向 C走廊的楼梯。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Only employees ever go to the other floors. The structure of this building is like this...
entries.new: 只有员工才会去其他楼层。这栋楼的结构是这样的……
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Right now, we are on the crystal floor. The five floors above us are offices, and they were empty during the attack.
entries.new: 我们现在在水晶层。上面五层都是办公室，袭击发生时那里没有人。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Why are there so many offices?
entries.new: 为什么会有这么多办公室？
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: When the structure of the building was first expanded, it served the purpose of containing many offices that worked for Ashiya. This was before they thought of using the lowest floor as a sort of museum.
entries.new: 这栋楼最初扩建时，就是为了容纳许多为芦屋服务的办公部门。那时他们还没想到把最底层改成类似博物馆的地方。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: That was the case for a while, until the perception people had of this place shifted to what it is now: the single remaining entity of Ashiya in Yushibana and a tourist attraction point.
entries.new: 这种情况持续了一段时间，直到人们对这里的印象逐渐变成了如今的模样：芦屋在丰花唯一留存的设施，也是一处旅游景点。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Nowadays, not many people who work in the offices remain, and they closed entirely just this December. Ashiya doesn't make much use of them anymore, so they might disappear and be reworked eventually.
entries.new: 如今在办公室工作的人已经不多，而且这些办公室今年十二月刚刚全部关闭。芦屋已经不怎么使用它们，所以它们说不定迟早会被撤掉、重新改造。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: The seventh floor is the Ashiya floor, also called the attic. I explained that one earlier.
entries.new: 七楼是芦屋层，也叫阁楼。那一层我之前解释过了。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Can we go in there?
entries.new: 我们能进去吗？
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: There's no way. As I said, I've never entered it, and only a handful of people who remain here have. Ashiya are very fond of it since it's where they once lived, or at least that's what they claim. Regardless of the reason, they want to preserve it well.
entries.new: 不行。我说过了，我从没进去过，留在这里的人里也只有少数几个进去过。芦屋非常珍视那里，因为那里曾是他们的住处——至少他们是这么说的。不管出于什么原因，他们都想把它妥善保存下来。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: How would we go about getting in?
entries.new: 我们要怎么才能进去？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Like most places, you enter with a key. One that I don't have.
entries.new: 和大多数地方一样，得有钥匙才能进去。而我手上没有。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Katei pointed his finger up the stairs, where a door prevented us from making it all the way up.
entries.new: Katei 抬手指向楼梯上方，那里横着一扇门，我们没法一直走到顶。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I have the key for this one since it only keeps us from accessing the offices.
entries.new: 这扇门的钥匙我这儿有，它只是用来拦着不让人进办公区而已。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: He walked up and inserted another key of his in the keyhole. As he'd already done twice, he turned it.
entries.new: 他走上前，把自己的另一把钥匙插进锁孔，像前两次那样拧了一下。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Unlike previously, however, the door didn't appear to smoothly unlock.
entries.new: 可这一次，门锁并不像先前那样顺畅地打开了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What? It's not letting me.
entries.new: 怎么回事？拧不动。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Hold on.
entries.new: 等等。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai stepped up to him, twisted the knob, and pushed the door forward.
entries.new: Sai 走上前，转动门把手，把门推开了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was open.
entries.new: 门本来就没锁。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: O-Oh... That's strange. Sometimes this door is left open, but it's weird that it was now. Nobody has worked upstairs for two weeks.
entries.new: 啊、啊……这就怪了。这扇门有时候确实会忘了锁，可偏偏是现在……楼上已经两个星期没人办公了。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: It's not really strange. Naomi also had the key, right? It just means that she probably opened it or someone did with her key. If it was you, you're not very good at remembering whether you locked a door.
entries.new: 倒也没什么好奇怪的。Naomi 也有钥匙吧？那多半就是她开的门，或者是别人拿了她的钥匙开的。要是你自己开的，那你记性可真成问题，连门锁没锁都记不住。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'll ask one more time so you guys understand it better. Katei, you did not see anyone when you looked through the security cameras, right?
entries.new: 我再问一遍，好让你们都清楚。Katei，你看监控的时候，没看到任何人，对吧？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Correct.
entries.new: ……没错。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Then, once again, that's strange. It's very likely someone unlocked this door and went through it.
