entries.text: Yeah, that's what I thought. Do you know what these three open?
entries.new: 我也这么觉得。你知道这三把是开什么的吗？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That one opens the door in the floor 2 staircase. I don't know about the other two, though.
entries.new: 这一把开的是二楼楼梯间的门。另外两把我就不知道了。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: So she doesn't have the key for the cabinet?
entries.new: 这么说，她身上没有展示柜的钥匙？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Let me keep looking.
entries.new: 我再找找。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai searched through the remaining pockets, but they were all empty.
entries.new: Sai 又把剩下的口袋翻了一遍，里面全是空的。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It seems not. Her killer took the cabinet key after killing her, and we know who that was.
entries.new: 看来是没有。凶手杀了她之后拿走了展示柜的钥匙，而那个人是谁，我们都知道。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Katei looked at me while everyone else looked at him.
entries.new: Katei 看向我，其余人的目光却都落在他身上。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Don't try it again, Katei. You must have killed Naomi and then unlocked the cabinet with her key. You've proven yourself to be quite stupid a few times, so you must've hidden the Sekimeiya in a room you looked through hoping we'd ignore it.
entries.new: 别再耍这种把戏了，Katei。一定是你杀了 Naomi，然后用她的钥匙打开了展示柜。你已经不止一次证明自己有多蠢，所以你肯定把 Sekimeiya 藏在了自己检查过的某个房间里，指望我们不会去搜。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That's ridiculous. I'd have no reason to do that, let alone the time. It's baffling how you don't realize only Atsuki could've done this.
entries.new: 荒唐。我既没有理由那么做，也没有那个时间。真不明白你怎么会看不出来，能做到这件事的只有 Atsuki。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...What now?
entries.new: ……又怎么了？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You killed Naomi, so naturally, you got your hands on her key. Then, while you were looking at hallway A from the lobby, you went to the event room. You unlocked the cabinet and left the Sekimeiya in a room I had searched in order to frame me. There's no other way.
entries.new: 你杀了 Naomi，自然就拿到了她的钥匙。然后，你在大厅里盯着 A走廊的时候，去了活动室。你打开展示柜，把 Sekimeiya 藏进我搜过的房间，好嫁祸给我。除此之外别无可能。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Don't you know how risky that'd be? He could've been seen at any time.
entries.new: 你难道不清楚那有多冒险？他随时都可能被人看见。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Likewise, if you intend to blame me, you're implying I took the same risk.
entries.new: 同样，你若想把罪名安到我头上，就等于说我也冒了同样的风险。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: The difference is that Atsuki had a reason to move it: to frame me. If his plan succeeded, I would've been the main culprit. However, by hiding it, I wouldn't gain anything.
entries.new: 区别在于，Atsuki 有动机去转移它：为了嫁祸我。他的计划若成功，我就会成为头号嫌疑人。而我把东西藏起来，却什么也得不到。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Neither of your motives are enough, and Atsuki would've been more likely to be seen with the Sekimeiya. You're not going to convince anyone.
entries.new: 你们俩的动机都站不住脚，而且 Atsuki 拿着 Sekimeiya 更容易被人撞见。你这些话，说服不了任何人。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Why don't we do a thorough search, then? Let's search each other to see who has the key.
entries.new: 那不如彻底搜一遍？大家互相搜身，看看钥匙在谁身上。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Of course not. Nobody would be dumb enough to keep it on themselves. I bet you already disposed of it in another one of the rooms you inspected.
entries.new: 当然不会。没人会蠢到把钥匙带在身上。我敢打赌，你早就把它丢在你检查过的另一个房间里了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Even though he said that, I still showed my empty pockets.
entries.new: 他虽这么说，我还是翻出自己的空口袋给大家看。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki doesn't have a motive. Please, stop accusing him... There's so much blood, so this is where everything happened, and to do this to someone in front of a camera... You'd need to have a real reason for it.{w} We need to find the person who did this to Naomi. They made that noise earlier...{w} L-Look at Naomi's face. She must've been terrified, and being afraid of this happening might even be why she hid from us.
entries.new: Atsuki 没有动机，请你别再怀疑他了……这里血这么多，说明一切就发生在这儿；而且还是在镜头前对人下这种狠手……没有充分的理由，谁做得出来。{w}我们得找到对 Naomi 下手的凶手。刚才那阵动静就是那个人弄出来的……{w}你、你看 Naomi 的脸。她当时一定怕极了；也许正因为害怕会遭这种事，她才一直躲着我们。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: You said that, right, Akaro? That she looked preoccupied when she appeared. She didn't do anything, and the real person responsible took her life.
entries.new: Akaro，你刚才是这么说的吧？她现身的时候，神色像是心事重重。她什么都没做，是真正的凶手夺走了她的命。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: And why would they do that? It's true that she looked like the culprit, and that's why I still think she was. By killing her, they'd only be confirming that she was innocent.
entries.new: 那他们又为什么要这么做？她看上去确实像凶手，所以我还是认为她就是。杀了她，反倒只会证明她是清白的。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...Or involved in a way that's harmful for them. We need to know what happened to her and find who's actually behind it.
entries.new: ……又或者，她牵扯进了对他们不利的事。我们得弄清她身上发生了什么，找出真正的幕后之人。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...We shouldn't leave her like this, though. She doesn't deserve to spend eleven more hours lying face-up with that expression.
entries.new: ……不过，总不能让她就这么躺着。让她保持那副表情仰面躺上十一个小时，太不体面了。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: What, do you wanna cover it?
entries.new: 怎么，你是想把脸盖上？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Isn't that... what you do for corpses?
entries.new: 给遗体盖上，不都是这么做的吗？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: We should prioritize maintaining the crime scene.
entries.new: 我们得优先保护现场。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I don't think so... She died in this room, and cameras recorded it. There's nothing to preserve, and we can give her some dignity.
entries.new: 我不这么想……她就死在这间房里，监控全都拍下来了。没有什么需要保留的，倒不如让她走得体面些。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Her stance was understandable, and nobody wanted to argue against it. It was possible I'd get in trouble for it, but I went ahead and detached a curtain from a cabinet and laid it over Naomi's body, covering the face that communicated how she'd spent her last moments.
entries.new: 她的立场可以理解，也没人想再反驳。这么做或许会给我惹上麻烦，但我还是从展示柜上扯下一块遮布，盖在 Naomi 身上，遮住了那张诉说她最后时刻的脸。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Thank you... I'm sure she would appreciate it.
entries.new: 谢谢……她一定会感激的。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I'm not sure that was a great idea, but now let's make sure to find the person who did it. Doesn't it feel like they're taunting us, making noise to let us know they're there and refusing to appear?
entries.new: 这主意好不好，我可说不准；总之现在得把凶手找出来。他们故意弄出声响，让人知道他们在，却又始终不肯露面，不觉得这像是在挑衅我们吗？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: But even so, they wouldn't have had a chance to move the Sekimeiya.
entries.new: 可就算这样，他们也没机会动 Sekimeiya。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Can we really be sure? Our priority should be to find them. I don't think any of us did this. There's a real culprit who murdered Naomi and is responsible for the Sekimeiya vanishing. ...Who knows what else will happen if we don't stop them immediately?
entries.new: 真能这么肯定吗？我们得优先把他们找出来。我不认为我们之中有人做了这事。凶手另有其人，他杀了 Naomi，还让 Sekimeiya 消失了。……要是不马上拦住他，谁知道还会出什么事？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I don't know how they did everything or how they weren't found, but we have to hurry. They're somewhere on a higher floor right now, so let's find them.
entries.new: 我不知道他是怎么做到这一切的，又是怎么一直没被找到，但我们得抓紧。他现在就在上面某一层，走吧。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: We left the room behind, and with it Naomi's corpse, which lay under a beautiful red cloth. She had lost her life in the tower with us, and yet we knew nothing about her or the identity and intentions of her murderer. I was trying not to let it get the best of me, but my mind was all over the place. I couldn't allow anything to happen to me and Shiroya, and the moment I'd instantaneously moved between places kept replaying in my head.
entries.new: 我们离开了那间房，把 Naomi 的遗体留在那里，盖着一块艳丽的红布。她就在这座塔里、在我们身边丢了性命，可我们对她的来历、对凶手的身份和意图一无所知。我竭力不让自己被这些压垮，思绪却乱作一团。我不能让自己和 Shiroya 出任何事；我瞬间从一个地方移动到另一个地方的那一瞬，在脑中不断回放。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We met up with Erina and Isla and summarized the few conclusions we'd been able to draw. Once again, we had five floors to go through.
entries.new: 我们与 Erina、Isla 会合，把勉强得出的几点结论交流了一遍。眼下又有五层楼要逐层搜过去。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Were we going to find anyone a second time? It must've been almost {time=11}, implying that someone might've been able to remain unseen for two full hours.
entries.new: 这次还能再找到人吗？时间应该快到 {time=11} 了，也就是说，有人可能整整两个小时都没被任何人看见。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is starting to get old, so let's be fast. This person only wants to hide from us, and they're also being recorded by cameras, so our only goal is to find them and question them.
entries.new: 这种事都重复腻了，动作快点。对方只想躲着我们，而且全程都被监控拍着，所以我们唯一的目标就是找到他、问清他的来历。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Since it couldn't have been any of us, splitting up won't matter. Everyone make sure a floor is empty and then stay somewhere outside the offices. This way, someone who's hiding can only escape by moving between floors, and they'll be easily spotted.
entries.new: 既然不可能是我们当中的人，分头行动也无妨。每人负责确认一层没人，然后守在办公室外面。这样一来，躲着的人想逃，只能上下楼层，很容易被看见。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: After a few minutes, it'll be impossible not to have found them, so we'll all move back to this floor with that person in tow.
entries.new: 用不了几分钟，他们必然会被找出来；到时候我们带着人回到这一层。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I don't think this is needed at all.
entries.new: 我看根本没必要。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We went up the stairs, following Akaro. If none of us were the culprit or had ulterior motives, then the plan would work. It was only slightly faster than moving up progressively, but it'd be equally successful.
entries.new: 这比一层层往上查快不了多少，但同样管用。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We'll stay here, then.
entries.new: 那我们就留在这里。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Hm.
entries.new: 嗯。
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: ...Actually, never mind. This arrangement of yours is a great idea.
entries.new: ……算了，当我没说。你这个安排很好。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: After we checked that nobody was in the bathrooms, Erina and Isla were left behind on floor 2, free to enter the partitions. Sai said he'd inspect and wait on floor 3.
entries.new: Sai 说他负责三层，检查完就在那里等。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'll look through this one. The rest of you keep going up.
entries.new: 这一层我来查，其他人继续往上。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: With Akaro staying on the fourth floor, Shiroya and I remained on the fifth. Katei was left with the last one, and he said that he'd make sure nobody could stay hidden there.
entries.new: Akaro 留在四层，我和 Shiroya 留在五层。最后一层交给 Katei，他说会确保没人能藏在那里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We easily looked through our three sections. There was nobody there, so we stayed next to the elevator.
entries.new: 我们很轻松地查完了自己负责的三个区域。里面都没有人，我们便守在电梯旁。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We'll have to wait, then.
entries.new: 那就只能等了。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: We can head downstairs whenever Katei comes back.
entries.new: 等 Katei 回来，我们就下楼。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We have to find someone this time, right? Someone must've been on the crystal floor when we heard that noise.
entries.new: 这次总该能找到人吧？听到那个声音的时候，水晶层上一定有人。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I'd say so. Unless they can make it to the attic, the only way we could miss them is if someone purposely covers for them.
entries.new: 应该是。除非他能跑到阁楼去，否则唯一可能漏掉的情况，就是有人故意替他遮掩。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Are you tired? When did you wake up yesterday?
entries.new: 累不累？你昨天几点醒的？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Sometime in the afternoon. I'm okay, though, just a bit hungry.
entries.new: 下午吧。我还好，就是有点饿。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yeah, I'm the same. I'm glad I ate a bit before leaving. Do you not carry cereal bars with you anymore? You always used to have one or two in your purse.
entries.new: 我也是。幸好出门前吃了点。你现在不带麦片棒了？以前你包里总有一两根。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That was at school. I brought the ones I had when I came over, but I finished them off a few days ago. I wouldn't be surprised if they stopped people from bringing food in here anyway.
entries.new: 那是上学的时候。过来时我把手边的都带来了，前几天吃完了。再说，这里说不定本来就不让人带食物进来。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...Right. I didn't think about that.
entries.new: ……也是，我没想到这层。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I was thinking that if we want to go find that old cabin, we could do it tomorrow. It hasn't snowed in a bit, so that should help us get there. It was pretty far.
entries.new: 我在想，要是想去那座旧木屋看看，不如明天就去。有一阵没下雪了，路会好走些。那地方挺远的。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Are you sure it'll still be there? I don't think I remember how to get to it, and I'm sure it's changed a lot since then.
entries.new: ……你确定它还在吗？我都不太记得怎么走了。而且过了这么久，那里肯定变了不少。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: It wasn't that fragile of a cabin. I'm sure it held out against the weather, but maybe the door is buried in snow. We'll have to see.
entries.new: 那木屋没那么脆弱，风吹雪打应该扛得住。只是门说不定被雪埋了，到时候只能看了再说。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You know, I thought of something earlier. Do you remember Danny?
entries.new: 说起来，我刚才想到一件事。你还记得 Danny 吗？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...Danny?
entries.new: ……Danny？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Danny the tiger.
entries.new: 那只老虎 Danny。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Oh! That stuffed thing? Yeah, of course. It's been forever since I thought about that.
entries.new: 哦！那个玩偶？当然记得。好久没想起过它了。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I haven't been able to find him in years. I just thought that maybe I left him in that cabin.
entries.new: 我好几年都找不到他了。刚才在想，会不会是落在那个木屋里了。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: You think so...? You definitely brought him there a few times. Maybe I left something there too. Now I want to go even more.{w} Katei didn't mention a cabin in his story, but I'd be shocked if it was the same place. There are probably a few similar fields on that mountain.
entries.new: 会吗……？你确实带他去过几次。说不定我也在那儿落下了什么。这下我更想去了。{w}Katei 讲的事里没提到木屋，不过要真是同一个地方，我可要吃惊了。那座山上大概有好几片相似的草地。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Mmm. I'd be happy if we could find him. I used to have him with me all the time.
entries.new: 嗯。要是能找到他就好了。以前我一直把他带在身边。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yeah. We'll get through this. We'll find the person who made that noise and put an end to everything. There was a pretty big couch in the lobby, so you can probably rest there if you need to.
entries.new: 会的。我们一定能挺过去。等找到弄出那个动静的人，一切就都结束了。大厅里有张挺大的沙发，你要休息的话，在那儿躺一会儿应该没问题。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Shiroya didn't reply. I was forcing myself to be optimistic and distract her from what was going on, but it wasn't enough. Naomi's empty eyes weren't something she was going to easily forget. She lowered her shoulders, trying to loosen up, but her posture was still completely rigid.
entries.new: Shiroya 没有回答。我强作乐观，想把她的注意力从眼前的状况上引开，可这还不够。Naomi 那双空洞的眼睛，不是那么容易就能忘掉的。她垂下肩膀，像是想让自己放松下来，可整个人的姿态依旧僵硬。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Our arrangement was efficient, but if someone had gone to the sixth floor, Katei could pretend it was empty. Due to the attic door, we wouldn't be able to prove he lied unless we had the security footage.
entries.new: 我们的安排很高效，可万一有人去过六楼，Katei 只要一口咬定上面空无一人就行。有那扇阁楼门在，除非拿到监控录像，否则我们无法证明他在说谎。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, it seemed like Katei was serious about finding the culprit. If he hadn't been making that up, he would report his part of the search truthfully.
entries.new: 不过，Katei 似乎真的想找出凶手。如果他没说谎，那他负责的那部分搜查，应该会如实汇报。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As I thought of him, I heard muffled noises coming from above us. They were incredibly faint footsteps we could hear solely because of the pure silence surrounding us, which indicated that Katei was walking across the sixth floor.
entries.new: 正想着他，头顶便传来了隐约的声响。那脚步声轻得几乎听不见，全靠四周一片死寂才传到我们耳中——是 Katei 正走在六楼。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Do you think I could've time traveled?
entries.new: ……你觉得，我有没有可能穿越了？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Huh? I don't know. It's kind of unbelievable...{w} Do you think you did?
entries.new: ……诶？我不知道。这事有点难以置信……{w}你自己觉得呢？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I think so. Experiencing it myself makes me doubt that anything else could've happened.
entries.new: 我觉得是。亲身经历过之后，我实在想不出还有别的解释。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I see... How was it? Did it hurt at all?
entries.new: 这样啊……那是什么感觉？会痛吗？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Oh, no. It was immediate. Did I really disappear from your perspective?
entries.new: 不，一点也不痛。一瞬间就完成了。在你看来，我真的消失了吗？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Yes. I thought I must've imagined it somehow, but my first impression was that you instantly vanished. I actually ran up to the cabinet to check if you fell inside, but I could only see the gray Sekimeiya.
entries.new: ……嗯。我还以为是自己看花了眼，可第一眼看到的就是你突然不见。我还跑过去看展示柜，怕你是不是掉进去了，结果只看到灰色 Sekimeiya。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: If anyone else said that, I would've left it open for doubt. Someone else could deliberately lie to make me think I'd teleported when they knew what actually happened.{w} But I had to take Shiroya's experience at face value. If I intended to think of an alternative to time travel, I had to factor in her viewpoint as well.
entries.new: 换作别人这么说，我还会留个疑心。对方也许明知真相，却故意骗我，让我以为自己被传送了。{w}但 Shiroya 的亲身经历，我不能不当真。若想找出时间穿越之外的另一种解释，我就必须把她的视角也算进去。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'm also pretty sure I time traveled because of what happened on the sixth floor earlier. You saw me next to the offices and thought I'd moved over there, right?
entries.new: 之前六楼发生的事，也让我相当确信自己时间穿越了。你看到我在办公室那边，还以为是我自己走过去了吧？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Oh, that's right. When I got back, you were next to the elevator again. I was gonna bring it up, but you looked a bit nervous, and I thought something might've happened.
entries.new: 哦，对。我回来的时候，你又站在电梯旁边了。我本来想提这事，可你看起来有点紧张，我就以为是不是出了什么事。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: So you were the one who brought the elevator up?
entries.new: 那么，把电梯叫上来的人是你？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: It seems so...
entries.new: 看来是这样……
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Traveling to the past had caused her search to come up empty, but the circumstances of that were highly specific. For our second search, everyone was watching over a separate floor, so it was unlikely something like that would repeat.
entries.new: 穿越到过去，才让她的搜查扑了个空，可那种情形极为特殊。第二轮搜查时，每层楼都有人盯着，同样的事不太可能再发生。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I'm sorry. If I hadn't brought up coming here, this wouldn't have happened.
entries.new: ……对不起。要不是我提议来这里，也不会出这种事。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...You don't have to apologize for that. I wanted to go too.
entries.new: ……这事你不用道歉。我也是自己想来的。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Are you sure? Nothing has happened to us yet, but depending on what's really going on, we might be in danger. Someone is... dead.
entries.new: 你确定吗？我们目前还没出事，可要看事情真相如何，我们说不定也有危险。毕竟已经有人……死了。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I feel... horrible about what happened to Naomi, but it's likely she was involved with this plan in some way. There's no reason for anyone to target us.
entries.new: Naomi 的事……我心里也很难受。但她多半和这个计划有某种牵连。没有任何理由会让人盯上我们。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: But we're searching for the person who did it, right? That might be a motive in itself. They killed Naomi in front of the security cameras, so they're not afraid of being recorded. ...And there's also this teleportation.
entries.new: 可我们正在找凶手吧？这本身就可能成为动机。他们当着监控杀了 Naomi，根本不怕被拍下来。……再加上这次的传送。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Not only that, but a lot of things don't seem right, do they? How did the Sekimeiya disappear just now?
entries.new: 不止这样，还有好多地方都不对劲吧？刚才 Sekimeiya 是怎么消失的？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Well, someone must have used the key to open the cabinet...
entries.new: 这个嘛，肯定是有人用钥匙打开了展示柜……
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: But nobody could have. And if someone did, it was one of us seven. Or, I guess, either Sai or Akaro. You were looking at hallway A, right?
entries.new: 可没人能做到啊。真有人开了，也只能是我们七个人之一。或者……Sai 或 Akaro 吧。你当时在看 A走廊，对吧？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That sounded reasonable from her point of view. She wouldn't have kept track of Sai and Akaro while she'd looked through the hallway B rooms.
entries.new: 站在她的角度，这话很合理。她在 B走廊各房间里搜查时，不可能一直盯着 Sai 和 Akaro。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yes, but that's not really the case. Sai, Akaro, Katei, Erina, Isla, and an unknown person could've still done it.
entries.new: 对，但事实并非如此。Sai、Akaro、Katei、Erina、Isla，还有一个不明身份的人，都有可能做到。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: When I went to look inside the mechanical room, Katei, Erina, and Isla were looking at hallway A. During that time, they had the chance to enter the event room.{w} Although it would imply that they were either working together or threatened into silence.
entries.new: 我去查看机械室的时候，Katei、Erina 和 Isla 正看着 A走廊。那段时间里，他们有机会进入活动室。{w}只不过这样一来，就说明他们要么是同伙，要么是被威胁封了口。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Similarly, if they didn't keep watching the hallway or were working with an unknown person, that person could've also had the opportunity to enter. That doesn't make much sense to me, and it means that they had Naomi's key even before we found her body.
entries.new: 同样，如果他们没一直盯着走廊，或者和不明的第三人串通，那个人也有机会进去。我觉得这说不通，而且这样一来，他们在我们发现 Naomi 的尸体之前，就已经拿到了她的钥匙。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: But what you said about Sai and Akaro doesn't make much sense either because the Sekimeiya was found in the storeroom—in hallway A. Sai and Akaro were looking through hallway B, so they could've opened the cabinet by picking up the key from Naomi's body and then going to the event room.
entries.new: 不过你说 Sai 和 Akaro 那部分也说不通，因为 Sekimeiya 是在储藏室找到的——就在 A走廊。Sai 和 Akaro 当时在搜 B走廊，他们倒是可以先从 Naomi 的尸体上取走钥匙，再去活动室打开展示柜。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: But then they couldn't have left it inside one of the hallway A rooms.
entries.new: 可那样的话，他们没法把东西留在 A走廊的房间里。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yeah. The only way to do that would've been by cooperating with Katei and Erina. When I was in the mechanical room, either of them could've entered the event room knowing that their hallway B companion had unlocked the cabinet, or maybe they let them hide it.
entries.new: 是啊。要做到这一点，只能和 Katei、Erina 配合。我在机械室那段时间，他们俩中任何一个人都可以进活动室——只要知道 B走廊那边的同伙已经打开展示柜；也说不定，是他们把对方放进去藏的。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: So, in the end, the only possibilities are that either Katei and Erina are the culprits, worked with them, or were forced to keep quiet.{w} ...Nobody could've hidden it in the storeroom without being seen by both of them... and Isla too, I suppose.
entries.new: 也就是说，到头来只有几种可能：Katei 和 Erina 就是凶手，或者他们和凶手合作，或者他们被迫闭嘴。{w}……毕竟不管是谁，想在他们两人的眼皮底下把东西藏进储藏室都不可能……我想，还有 Isla。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That's right. And if it's true that no more keys exist and they weren't threatened, they must've been behind what happened to Naomi... They wouldn't have been able to unlock the cabinet otherwise, unless they cooperated with someone from hallway B.
entries.new: 没错。而且如果确实没有别的钥匙，他们也不是受人胁迫，那 Naomi 的事就一定是他们干的……否则他们打不开展示柜，除非和 B走廊的某个人联手。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: "At least three people are lying to us or nothing makes sense". That was the conclusion we'd come to, and Shiroya looked pretty defeated about it.
entries.new: 「至少有三个人在骗我们，否则一切都说不过去。」——这就是我们得出的结论。Shiroya 看上去相当泄气。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What you said earlier... that nobody from hallway B could've hidden the Sekimeiya in the storeroom... Could there be a way around that?
entries.new: 你刚才说的……B走廊的人不可能把 Sekimeiya 藏进储藏室……有没有办法绕过这一点？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I considered that it was Sai. He entered the storeroom and acted like he'd found the Sekimeiya inside, when in reality, he'd had it on him the whole time.
entries.new: 我也想过是 Sai。他进了储藏室，装成在里面找到了 Sekimeiya，其实东西一直带在他身上。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That's the only way I can think of, but it's not really possible. Technically, Sai could have hidden the Sekimeiya in his hip pack.{w} However, we talked for a bit before he went to examine hallway A, and his back was facing us when he entered the two rooms there.
entries.new: 我能想到的只有这一种，可实际上行不通。严格来说，Sai 可以把 Sekimeiya 藏进腰包里。{w}但他去查看 A走廊之前，我们还聊了一会儿，而他走进那边两个房间时是背对着我们的。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I'm sure that if the Sekimeiya had been there, one of us would've noticed. His pack would've looked bulkier than normal.
entries.new: 我敢说，要是 Sekimeiya 真在他身上，我们总有人会察觉。他的腰包会比平时鼓出来。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You're probably right. He wouldn't have any other way to keep it hidden.{w} ...So the only possibility is that Katei and Erina did it while you weren't there.
entries.new: 你说得大概没错。他也没有别的办法把它藏起来。{w}……那就只剩一种可能：是 Katei 和 Erina 趁你不在时动的手。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I think so... They must've had the key before we found Naomi, and only Katei could've killed her.{w} However, Katei can't be responsible just by himself since he wouldn't have been able to get the Sekimeiya before I went to the mechanical room. By that point, he was already with Erina and Isla.
entries.new: 我想是的……他们一定在发现 Naomi 之前就已经有钥匙了，而能杀她的只有 Katei。{w}可是单凭 Katei 一个人不行，因为在我去机械室之前，他拿不到 Sekimeiya。那时候他已经和 Erina、Isla 在一起了。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: When I left the mechanical room, Erina told me that nothing had happened. So she was either working with Katei, or she was threatened to keep quiet. Nothing works involving someone from hallway B acting on their own, and the only other possibility could be an extra person threatening Erina and Katei to keep quiet.{w} You were with your group in hallway C when you finished, so it's unlikely that person came down from a higher floor. They might've been in one of the hallway A rooms we checked.
entries.new: 我离开机械室时，Erina 告诉我什么都没发生。所以，她要么和 Katei 是同伙，要么是被威胁封了口。B走廊的人单独行动，怎么都说不通，剩下的可能只有一种：另有一个威胁 Erina 和 Katei 闭嘴的人。{w}你们结束时，你和你的小组在 C走廊，所以那个人不太可能是从更高楼层下来的。他或许就藏在我们查过的某个 A走廊房间里。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Hm...{w} Someone else was definitely on that floor, right? So that shouldn't be impossible.
entries.new: 嗯……{w}那一层确实还有别人吧？那样的话，也不算不可能。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That's true, and if someone was threatened like that, they wouldn't reveal the culprit's position now even if they found them... In fact, they might still be on the crystal floor.
entries.new: 确实。而且，如果真是被人那样威胁，就算现在找到了凶手，他们也不会说出对方的位置……说不定那人还在水晶层。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: So... maybe the way everyone spread out on these floors wasn't the best idea.
entries.new: 那么……或许大家这样分散在各层搜查，未必是个好主意。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I can hardly take myself seriously, but I have to think about time travel and teleportation too. I just don't want to miss possibilities, and... ones involving what should be impossible have now become potential realities. I can't deny what I experienced.
entries.new: 我自己都觉得这念头荒唐，可时间穿越和传送，我也非得考虑不可。我只是不想放过任何一种可能，而且……那些本该不可能的事，如今都成了可能的现实。我亲身经历的一切，无法否认。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I have no idea what the rules would be, but if the Sekimeiya grants time travel abilities, it makes a lot of sense that someone's chasing after it or trying to accomplish something with it. They could know more about its powers than we do—they might've been making use of them from the beginning.
entries.new: 我不清楚它遵循什么规则，但如果 Sekimeiya 真能赋予人时间穿越的能力，那有人追逐它、或想借它达成某种目的，就完全说得通了。他们对它的力量也许比我们了解得更深——说不定从一开始就在加以利用。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: But why would anyone bother hiding the Sekimeiya? No matter what I think, there doesn't appear to be a clear purpose since it would always be trivial to locate it if it's not brought to a locker or the attic.
entries.new: 但为什么会有人费心把 Sekimeiya 藏起来？无论怎么想，我都看不出明确的目的——只要不把它带进储物柜或阁楼，找到它从来都不是难事。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: But let's assume the culprit wanted to hide it in the storeroom, whatever their reason. If they truly did it with the time travel that occurs upon touching the Sekimeiya, it follows that in the future, they'll have access to it.{w} So someone could be ready to go to the past and hide it in the storeroom right this moment. They might intend to make it out of here with the Sekimeiya in some way.
entries.new: 不过，先假设犯人出于某种理由，想把它藏进储藏室。如果真是靠触碰 Sekimeiya 时发生的时间穿越办到的，那么到了未来的某个时刻，他们就能碰到它。{w} 也就是说，此刻可能正有人准备回到过去，把它藏进储藏室。他们或许打算以某种方式带着 Sekimeiya 离开这里。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: It teleports you to the past, doesn't it? One goal could be to make it to the past holding the Sekimeiya itself or other gemstones. It would appear as if they'd disappeared from inside the tower, and only one of us could be responsible. But I wasn't holding the Sekimeiya when I traveled to hallway A, so how would you go to the past with it?
entries.new: 那东西会把人传送到过去，对吧？其中一个目的，也许就是带着 Sekimeiya 本身或其他宝石回到过去。这样一来，他们看起来就像从塔里凭空消失了，而能办到这种事的人只可能在我们之中。可我传送到 A走廊时并没有拿着 Sekimeiya，那又要怎么带着它回到过去？
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Avoiding the two hallway groups is more than possible if someone used time travel: first, they lured us out of the event room by making the sound we heard.
entries.new: 如果有人用了时间穿越，要避开走廊里的两拨人并非难事：首先，他们弄出我们听见的声响，把我们引出活动室。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Then, they appeared inside the event room from the future.{w} I don't know what could determine the position you teleport to, because I appeared in hallway A when I hadn't been there twenty minutes before, but if the culprit touches the Sekimeiya while holding the cabinet key, they could appear inside the event room with it.
entries.new: 接着，他们从未来出现在活动室里。{w} 我不知道传送的落点由什么决定——二十分钟前我根本不在 A走廊，却还是出现在了那里；不过，如果犯人握着展示柜钥匙触碰 Sekimeiya，就有可能带着它一起出现在活动室。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Once we were all in hallway C, they got out of the event room and left it in the storeroom while they hid elsewhere.{w} If they had already lived through that portion of time, they could've known the entire sequence of events—that they would be safe in the event room until we found the Sekimeiya. But then they'd also know that it would be found right away, so why bother doing all this?
entries.new: 等我们全都进了 C走廊，他们便离开活动室，把东西留在储藏室，自己躲到别处。{w} 如果他们早已经历过那段时间，就可能知道整串事件的走向——知道自己在活动室里一直安全，直到我们找到 Sekimeiya。可这样一来，他们也该知道东西马上就会被发现，那又何必费这么多功夫？
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Regardless, that leaves open the possibility of the culprit still being on the crystal floor. They could've even disappeared by touching the Sekimeiya if it was necessary, and even though it was white when we found it, maybe it didn't make us travel because someone else had just used it.
entries.new: 无论如何，犯人仍有可能还在水晶层。必要时，他们甚至可以触碰 Sekimeiya 直接消失；虽然我们发现它时它是白色的，但也许只是因为有别人刚用过，它才没让我们穿越。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: My initial thought is some sort of cooldown: after I traveled, nobody else could travel. Once the cold restored it, it allowed for one more travel. That still doesn't explain the strange color change it underwent right as I touched it.
entries.new: 我最初想到的是某种冷却：在我穿越之后，其他人就无法再穿越；等冷却恢复，它才又允许了一次穿越。但这仍然解释不了我碰到它的瞬间，它为何会发生那种诡异的颜色变化。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: If we're chasing a culprit who has knowledge of how to disappear and go to the past easily, it makes a lot of sense that we haven't found them yet. It also explains why they're trying to hide from us when we would normally find someone right away in this building.
entries.new: 如果我们追的犯人懂得如何轻易消失、回到过去，那我们至今找不到人就说得通了。这也能解释他们为何要躲着我们——换作平时，在这栋楼里找人本该一找就能找到。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: But the person who lured us out of the event room would've had to go up the floors before traveling to the past, and they can't disappear from there since the Sekimeiya's still on the crystal floor.{w} ...Once again, though, the attic makes it possible.
entries.new: 可是，把我们引出活动室的人若想回到过去，必须先上楼；而既然 Sekimeiya 还在水晶层，他们就不可能从上边消失。{w} ……不过，说到底，阁楼又让这一切成为可能。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Nonetheless, if no time travel or teleportation was involved at all in what happened, Katei, Erina, and Isla know the truth of it. If it really was a factor, I wonder how far we are from understanding anything at all that's happened.
entries.new: 但反过来说，如果发生的一切根本不涉及时间穿越或传送，那么 Katei、Erina 和 Isla 就知道真相。若这些确实牵涉其中，我真不知道我们离弄清事情全貌还有多远。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Katei's coming.
entries.new: Katei 来了。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I anticipated his arrival thanks to the echoing footsteps. He came from the floor above.
entries.new: 脚步声在楼道里回响，我早已料到他会来。他是从上一层下来的。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did anything happen?
entries.new: 有什么情况吗？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...No. There was no one there, so as we agreed, I stayed on that floor for a while to make sure no one escaped there with the elevator. More than enough time has passed, so we should go back down.
entries.new: ……没有。那里空无一人。所以按我们说好的，我在那层守了一阵，确认没人能乘电梯从那里逃走。时间已经足够久了，我们该下去了。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: He shot me another incensed look, but I tried to ignore it.
entries.new: 他又怒气冲冲地瞪了我一眼，我尽量不去理会。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If anyone was here, they must've been found.
entries.new: 这里若真有人，早该被找出来了。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...Okay. Let's go to the crystal floor.
entries.new: ……好。去水晶层吧。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We took the stairs down. Akaro was waiting for us, uncertain of what to do. He also hadn't found anyone.
entries.new: 我们沿楼梯下去。Akaro 正在等我们，似乎不知该如何是好。他也一无所获。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: One floor below was Sai. According to him, the third floor was empty and nothing had happened after we'd left.
entries.new: 再下一层是 Sai。据他说，三楼空无一人，我们离开后也没发生任何事。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The situation was the same on the second, where Erina and Isla had remained. There was no point to it, but as we'd said earlier, we all moved down to the crystal floor.
entries.new: 二楼也一样，Erina 和 Isla 一直守在那里。虽然再查下去也没什么意义，但我们还是照先前说好的，一同下到了水晶层。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Well. Did anyone find the culprit and let them escape?
entries.new: 怎么样。有人找到犯人，又让人跑了吗？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Everyone stated that they had found no one. We'd just searched through the entire tower without a result, so the only remaining possibilities were that the culprit had access to the attic, that one of us was lying, or that they'd managed to escape by teleporting through time, which should've only been possible on the crystal floor.
entries.new: 每个人都表示没找到人。我们刚把整座塔搜了一遍，却毫无结果，剩下的可能便只有三种：犯人能进入阁楼；我们之中有人在撒谎；或者他们利用传送穿越时间，成功逃走了——而这本该只可能在水晶层发生。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...So that's a no?
entries.new: ……那就是没找到了？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We all kept quiet, as we'd already announced our results.
entries.new: 大家都没再作声，毕竟结果早已各自报过。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They have to be in the attic, then. We just searched every other floor, after all.
entries.new: 那就只可能在阁楼了。毕竟其他每一层我们都搜过了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: O-Oh, wait, I can actually think of another place where they could be.
entries.new: 啊、等等，我其实还能想到一个他们可能在的地方。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Are you sure...? We looked through the whole tower. The way we did it didn't allow for anyone to hide from us. Where else could they have been?
entries.new: 你确定……？整座塔我们都查过了。照我们那种搜法，没人能躲得过去。还能有什么地方？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: There.
entries.new: 那里。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Shiroya turned around and pointed at the elevator.
entries.new: Shiroya 转过身，指向电梯。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, inside the elevator? Nobody went into it, correct?
entries.new: 哦，电梯里？没人进去过，对吧？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: No one spoke up. Could someone have been inside the elevator the whole time, banking on us ignoring it?
entries.new: 没人应声。难道真有人一直藏在电梯里，赌我们不会去查？
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Which floor should it be on?
entries.new: 它现在应该停在哪一层？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: We were the last ones to use it. We called it from floor 5 to test which floor it stopped on when we followed it up.
entries.new: 最后用电梯的是我们。我们从五楼叫了它，想看看跟着它上楼时它会停在哪层。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That's good. If we left it here, they could've come out as soon as we went up. At least we don't have to search this floor again.
entries.new: 那还好。要是把它留在这层，我们一上楼，他们就能立刻出来。至少这层不用再搜一遍了。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: *sigh*
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Anything wrong?
entries.new: 怎么了？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Plenty. Wait a second.
entries.new: 问题不少。等一下。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Following the out of place sigh, he walked up to the elevator and pressed the button to call it.{w} After a few seconds, the orange light surrounding the button told us that it had arrived, and Sai immediately grabbed the handle.
entries.new: 那声突兀的叹气过后，他走到电梯前，按下呼叫按钮。{w} 几秒后，按钮周围的橙光亮起，说明电梯已经到了，Sai 立刻抓住了门把手。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Let's see, I suppose. There's no way anyone's inside. They would've gotten out as soon as they heard people leaving the floor it was on, and if they'd still been inside, they could've pressed any floor button before this one to stop it earlier.
entries.new: 那就看看吧。里面不可能有人。要真有人，听到有人离开电梯停的那层，早就出来了；就算还待在里面，也可以在到这一层之前随便按个楼层按钮，让它提前停下。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He opened the door. It was empty, as we'd all expected.
entries.new: 他打开门。里面空空如也，和大家预料的一样。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, I meant to ask you something, Katei. The instructions inside state that pressing the stop button will enable contact with an emergency line. Is that possible right now?
entries.new: 对了，我正想问你一件事，Katei。里面的说明写着，按下停止按钮就能接通紧急线路。现在还能用吗？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: No. Naturally, the alarm shuts that down. The line can enable communication both with the outside and the security room, but right now it's disabled completely.
entries.new: 不行。警报启动后，那功能自然就被切断了。那条线路可以联系外界，也能联系监控室，但现在已经被完全禁用。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...I'd strongly recommend that none of you touch it. It was originally installed knowing Xyn could try to secure the elevator, but there's no point in that now, and we left up clear instructions.{w} If you press it as the elevator is moving, it won't move again until permission is granted from outside, and given communication has been temporarily disabled, I fear nothing could be done until the exit unlocks.
entries.new: ……我强烈建议你们谁都别碰它。当初设置它，是考虑到 Xyn 可能会试图控制电梯；可现在已没有那个必要，我们也留下了明确的说明。{w} 如果在电梯运行时按下它，电梯在获得外部许可前都不会再动；而通讯眼下已被暂时切断，恐怕在出口解锁之前，谁也做不了什么。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: That's scary. We'll keep it in mind.
entries.new: 真吓人。我们会记住的。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Anyway, given how long it took to get here, it was on the fifth floor.
entries.new: 总之，看它过来花了这么久，刚才应该停在五楼。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You can tell?
entries.new: 这也能看出来？
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Yes. I've never used it, but it's fairly slow. The seconds I counted match up with it being on the fifth floor, assuming it doesn't take very long for the doors to close and to start moving.
entries.new: 能。我没用过它，但它慢得很。我数的秒数和它从五楼下来的时间对得上——前提是关门和启动花不了太久。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That would add five seconds at most.
entries.new: 那最多也就会多出五秒。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Which is what I added. I tried to open the door as soon as the button lit up, but since it didn't budge, it must light up before the inner doors open.
entries.new: 这正是我补上的那一点。按钮一亮我就试着开门，可门纹丝不动，所以按钮应该是在内侧门打开之前就亮的。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: But as you said, if someone stopped it before it got here, it would have taken longer. What if it was on the third floor and had someone stopped it on the second?
entries.new: 可照你这么说，要是有人赶在它到这儿之前把它拦下，那耗时就得更长。要是它本来在三楼，却在二楼被人按停了呢？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: No. That whole process would've taken even longer.{w} If it wasn't on the fifth floor, the only way I could get the time I counted is if the door was open before I called it.{w} This is kind of batshit, but if someone kept the door open upstairs and closed it a few seconds after I called it, it would've started to go down later than I expected. That would have made it seem like it was higher.
entries.new: 不对。那样一来，整个过程只会更久。{w}如果它本来不在五楼，我数出的这个时间，唯一的可能就是：我按按钮之前，门就已经开着了。{w}这话听着有点离谱，但假如楼上有人一直开着门，等我按了按钮几秒后才关上，那它开始下降的时间就比我预计的要晚。这样一来，看起来就像它原本停在更高的楼层。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: And why would anyone do that, let alone know when you called it?
entries.new: 可谁又会这么做？更别说还得知道你什么时候按的按钮。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: No idea, I'm just saying it's possible. Is there a light that indicates someone is trying to call it while the door's being kept open?
entries.new: 不知道，我只是说这有可能。有没有什么灯，能在门一直开着的时候显示有人在叫电梯？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: No such thing exists.
entries.new: 没有这种东西。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Then it's incredibly unlikely that's what happened.
entries.new: 那就几乎不可能是这么回事。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: So it was on the fifth floor, right? There's no point in thinking too hard about this.
entries.new: 所以它本来就在五楼，对吧？这事没必要想得太深。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Incorrect. There's a very big inconsistency with the elevator being on the fifth floor, but it has to do with something I haven't mentioned yet. I imagined someone else would've figured it out, though.
entries.new: 错了。电梯在五楼这一点，有个很大的矛盾，不过它牵涉到我还没提到的东西。我本以为别人会发现的。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What is it...?
entries.new: 是什么……？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I found it quite intriguing, and I wasn't gonna comment on it immediately if you hadn't brought the elevator up. Let me explain what I heard.
entries.new: 我觉得这事挺有意思，你要是没提起电梯，我本来也不打算马上说。先说说我听到了什么。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I was on the third floor, waiting right outside the offices. Imagine my surprise when I heard the elevator moving.
entries.new: 我当时在三楼，就在办公室外面等着。听见电梯在动的时候，我真是吃了一惊。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Wait, the elevator moved?
entries.new: 等等，电梯动了？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes. Did nobody else hear it?
entries.new: 对。你们都没听见？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: For the third time, one of Sai's answers was received with silence. Personally, I hadn't heard anything.
entries.new: 这已经是第三次，Sai 的回答换来一片沉默。至少我什么都没听见。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: See, what makes this weird is that I know I heard the elevator three times. Did not even one of you hear it?
entries.new: 你瞧，怪就怪在我很确定自己听见电梯响了三次。你们真的一个都没听到？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: No one had.
entries.new: 谁都没听到。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You heard it three times and didn't follow it?
entries.new: 你听见它响了三回，却没跟过去看看？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Of course not. I didn't know if it was going up or down, and we all agreed to stay put. I also didn't want to unwittingly bite some bait.
entries.new: 当然没有。我连它是上是下都分不清，而且我们说好了待在原地。我也不想稀里糊涂地咬上别人的诱饵。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Unfortunately, since there's no light that indicates the door's open on another floor, I couldn't know which floors it stopped on by counting the seconds as soon as I heard it moving.
entries.new: 可惜没有灯能显示别层的门是不是开着，所以我没法一听见它动就掐着秒数，算出它停在了哪几层。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: But three times? Surely something must've been happening.
entries.new: 可三次？那肯定出过什么事才对。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Who remained on each floor above me?
entries.new: 我上面每一层都有谁在？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Erina and Isla remained on the second floor, apparently you heard the elevator from the third, Akaro stayed on the fourth, Atsuki and Shiroya on the fifth, and I went up by myself to the sixth.
entries.new: ……Erina 和 Isla 留在二楼，看来你是在三楼听见的，Akaro 在四楼，Atsuki 和 Shiroya 在五楼，我一个人上了六楼。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: And when you went down, everyone was still on their appropriate floors, correct?
entries.new: 那你下去的时候，大家还都在各自该在的楼层，对吧？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yes.
entries.new: 对。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: A lot of things could've happened, but some people here have to be lying. After three trips, no matter where the elevator started from, anyone could've gone to a different floor and then back to their own.
entries.new: 可能发生的情况有很多，但这里一定有人说谎。它跑了三趟，不管起点在哪，任何人都能趁机去别的楼层，再回到自己那层。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yes, two trips would be required, and the third one could've been them calling the elevator for the first time.
entries.new: 的确，那样需要两趟，第三趟说不定才是那人第一次按电梯。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: That's wrong. That order of events is impossible.
entries.new: 这不对。这种先后顺序根本不可能。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The elevator was on the fifth floor, right? I could've only heard someone who called it from below me. If Akaro called it from floor 4, I wouldn't have heard it.
entries.new: 电梯最后在五楼，对吧？我只可能听见来自我下方楼层的呼叫。要是 Akaro 从四楼按的，我就听不见。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: So, if Erina and Isla called it and then I heard it two more times, the elevator would've stopped under me. And I just determined it was on the fifth. That couldn't have happened.
entries.new: 所以，如果是 Erina 和 Isla 叫的电梯，之后我又听见了两次，那电梯就一定在我下面停过。可我刚刚才认定它在五楼。这不可能发生。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: If anyone above me used it, I wouldn't have heard them calling it. The strange thing is that I heard it three times, and I'm sure of that.{w} This is the inconsistency here: even if someone above me used it, it would not have ended up on the fifth floor because I heard it three times.
entries.new: 要是我上面有人用它，他们按按钮的声音我不会听见。可怪的是我确实听见了三次，这点我敢肯定。{w}矛盾就在这儿：即便上面有人用过它，它也不该停在五楼，因为我听见它响了三次。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It was there initially, right? The first trip was the elevator going down, then it went up, and then down again. There is no other combination that works, of course. Despite that, the elevator ended up above me.
entries.new: 它本来就在那儿，对吧？第一趟是电梯往下，然后往上，再往下。当然，没有别的组合说得通。可即便如此，电梯最后还是停在了我上面。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We were a bit speechless, unaware of how to take all that.
entries.new: 我们一时无言，不知该怎么看待这一番话。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Erina, Isla, and Akaro. Are you sure you didn't hear the elevator even once?
entries.new: Erina、Isla、Akaro。你们真的连一次都没听见电梯响？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I didn't.
entries.new: 我没听见。
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: ...Me neither, but the first time was almost unnoticeable, so it's possible we missed it. We were far away from it.
entries.new: ……我也没有。不过第一次几乎听不出来，所以也有可能我们漏掉了。我们离得挺远。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I'm sure I didn't hear it either.
entries.new: 我也确定自己没听见。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: What the hell? I heard the elevator three times, so it had to be on floors 4 and 2 also three times.
entries.new: 搞什么？我听见了三次，那它经过四楼和二楼也应该各有三次。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Be honest. Are you just making this up? I'm sure I would've heard it at least once if it passed my floor multiple times.
entries.new: 说实话。你是不是在编？要是它从我这一层过了好几趟，我至少该听见一次。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: There's a way you would've missed it only once, but it's almost as unlikely.
entries.new: 确实有一种情形能让你漏听，而且只漏一次，但那同样几乎不可能。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What are you talking about?
entries.new: 你在说什么？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We understand, it couldn't have started on floor 5 if you heard it three times. So if you actually did, it must have been on floors 1 or 2 at the start.
entries.new: 我们明白，要是你真听见了三次，它就不可能在五楼起步。所以如果你没听错，它一开始只可能在1楼或2楼。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: As an example, what if it was on the second floor and then went to the fourth? After that, from the fourth to the second, then from the second to the fifth.
entries.new: 举个例子，假如它本来在二楼，然后去了四楼？接着从四楼下到二楼，再从二楼上到五楼。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Just now, we didn't hear any sound. We only knew the elevator was here because the button lit up. If it stops on your floor, you won't necessarily notice it.
entries.new: 刚才我们一点声音都没听到。只是按钮亮起，我们才知道电梯到了。电梯停在你那一层，你也未必会察觉。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Hm... So Erina and Isla couldn't have noticed it at all, and Akaro would only have had the chance to notice it when it went to the fifth.
entries.new: 嗯……那就是说，Erina 和 Isla 根本不可能察觉，而 Akaro 只有电梯上五楼那一趟才有机会察觉。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: And we wouldn't have heard it either when it stopped on ours.
entries.new: 它停在我们这层的时候，我们也一样听不见。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Well, hang on. This doesn't explain anything. Nobody got off on my floor.
entries.new: 等等。这什么都解释不了。没人从我这一层出去。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: ...I'm certain nobody got off on ours either. We were next to the offices, keeping an eye on the elevator from a bit away. We might've missed the button lighting up, but not someone getting out.
entries.new: ……我也确定没人从我们这层出去。我们就在办公室旁边，隔着一段距离盯着电梯。按钮亮没亮也许会有漏看，但有人出来绝不会看漏。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Yeah, I get that. So whoever was inside the elevator didn't open the door when they came to a stop.
entries.new: 嗯，我明白。也就是说，电梯里的人停下时并没有开门。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...And what would the purpose of doing that be? They're only alerting us that they're moving.
entries.new: ……这么做又能有什么目的？他们那样做，无非是在告诉我们有人在动而已。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I don't know, but you should understand that hearing the elevator three times already confirms that someone moved the elevator before we started searching. It's confirming the presence of a ninth person.
entries.new: 我不知道。但你该明白，电梯响了三次，这已经足以证明在我们开始搜查之前，就有人动过它。这等于证实了第九个人的存在。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It couldn't have been on the fifth floor, right? It was on one of the first two.{w} Why would someone move it like that when all it does is reveal them?
entries.new: 它不可能停在五楼吧？它本来在一楼或二楼中的某一层。{w} 这么做只会暴露自己，谁会干这种事？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Maybe it really was on the fifth floor... It's not completely impossible.{w} You heard it three times, Sai, and that put it below you. When we all came back here, someone got out and sent it up to the fifth before we called it. We wouldn't have heard it no matter where it was.
entries.new: 说不定它真的一直在五楼……也不是完全没可能。{w} Sai，你听见了三次，那就说明它当时在你下面。等我们都回到这里，有人出了电梯，赶在我们叫它之前把它送上了五楼。这样一来，不管它停在哪儿，我们都听不到。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: It could also be that it moved four times and you missed one. That'd solve everything easily, excluding who moved it, of course.
entries.new: 也可能它其实动了四次，而你漏听了一次。这样一切就都说得通了——当然，除了是谁动的之外。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: You know what I find to be the most likely scenario? That you're all deaf.
entries.new: 你们知道我觉着最有可能的情况是什么吗？是你们全都聋了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: These situations you're all presenting are ridiculous, so let me detail what probably happened.
entries.new: 你们说的这些情况都荒唐得很。还是让我来讲讲大概发生了什么吧。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: When I entered the storeroom and found the Sekimeiya, the rest of you remained in this hallway, next to the elevator. Someone, probably Katei, called it here knowing it'd be unnoticeable.
entries.new: 我进储藏室找到 Sekimeiya 的时候，你们其余的人都留在这条走廊里，就在电梯旁边。有人——多半是 Katei——把它叫到了这里，因为他知道这不会被人察觉。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Excuse me...! Are you blaming me again for something that doesn't make sense?
entries.new: 喂……！你又要拿这种毫无道理的事来怪我？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Yes. It could've been Akaro, Atsuki, or Shiroya—anyone who later searched above me.
entries.new: 没错。也可能是 Akaro、Atsuki 或 Shiroya——任何后来在我上方搜查的人。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Maybe someone wanted to create the illusion that it was impossible for anyone above me to use the elevator. I don't know.
entries.new: 也许有人想制造一种假象，让人觉得在我上方的人根本不可能用到电梯。谁知道呢。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: But this relies on knowing that we'd separate across the floors, all our positions, and that you'd both hear the elevator and not follow it.
entries.new: 可这得建立在事先知道我们会分层搜查、知道我们每个人的位置，还算准了你们俩听见电梯响也不会追过去的基础上。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Not too plausible, is it? It's also possible some hidden culprit moved it down before our search started, but the truth of the matter remains that we looked through this entire building and found nobody else. The sound we heard is no confirmation of anything.
entries.new: 听起来不太可信吧？也有可能在我们开始搜查之前，有个藏起来的人把它调了下去。但事实就是，我们搜遍了整栋楼，谁也没找到。我们听到的声音什么也证明不了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Once we were all in place, Katei used the elevator. He first called it up to the sixth floor, which I heard. Then, he took it down.
entries.new: 等我们都各就各位之后，Katei 用了电梯。他先把它叫上六楼，这我听见了。然后他乘着它下来了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Nobody saw the elevator stopping on their floor, but that's fine if he stopped here. I heard it three times no matter what happened, so that means it went down at least once. Since Erina and Isla didn't see anyone coming out, the times it went down must've been to the crystal floor.{w} Afterward, Katei took it back up, to the sixth. He knew it should've initially been on the fifth, so he sent it back there.
entries.new: 没人看见电梯在自己那层停下，可如果他停在这一层，那也说得过去。不管怎样，我听见它响了三次，也就是说它至少下降过一次。既然 Erina 和 Isla 都没看见有人出来，那它下降的时候一定是去了水晶层。{w} 之后，Katei 又把它送回六楼。他知道它起初应该停在五楼，于是又把它送回了那里。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That's not at all what happened, and I would've noticed that the elevator was far below me with how long it would take to arrive. I just can't wait to show you the security footage once this is all over and see the look on your face.
entries.new: 事情根本不是这样。要是电梯离我那么远，光是等它上来花的时间就够我察觉了。等这一切结束，我迫不及待要给你看监控录像，看看你到时候是什么表情。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I also really don't believe we would've missed the elevator three times.
entries.new: 我也实在不信我们会漏掉三次电梯声。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Shiroya's right. Even if it was a faint sound, we were paying attention right next to it.
entries.new: Shiroya 说得对。就算声音再轻，我们就守在旁边，不可能没留意。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I agree. No way we would have missed it.
entries.new: 我同意。我们不可能漏听。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: ...All I can say is that we didn't hear anything and nobody stopped on the second floor.
entries.new: ……我只能说，我们什么都没听见，也没有人在二楼停下。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: It's clear as day, isn't it? He's just making this up.
entries.new: 这不是明摆着吗？全是他编的。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Most likely. The elevator was where it should've been, after all. There's probably no inconsistency.
entries.new: 多半是这样。电梯毕竟就停在它该在的地方，大概本来就没有什么矛盾。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Just in case, all of you take a hearing test after we're out. At least one of you has to be lying—that's for sure.
entries.new: 以防万一，出去之后你们都去做个听力检查。你们当中至少有一个在撒谎——这点可以肯定。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: According to what you heard, someone got off here, right?
entries.new: 照你听到的，有人在这一层下了电梯吧？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yes, and we know what the reason would be. We didn't lock the cabinet the last time, so someone must've realized they had a free path to the Sekimeiya.
entries.new: 对。至于原因，我们也清楚。上次我们没锁展示柜，所以一定有人意识到自己可以毫无阻碍地接近 Sekimeiya。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Let's see if it's there, then. If it's not, that'll give you some credibility.
entries.new: 那就去看看它还在不在。要是不在，你的话倒还有点可信度。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Of course. We're in front of the stairs, so there was no reason to hurry. Let's see what we find.
entries.new: 当然。我们就站在楼梯前，没必要赶。去看看能发现什么吧。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That time, all of us went to the event room. We'd just looked through every single floor, and even though some things still didn't make sense, it felt pointless to guard the exit.
entries.new: 那一次，我们全都去了活动室。我们刚把每一层都搜过一遍，虽然还有些事说不通，但守着出口也没什么意义了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We entered through hallway A. As soon as we set foot inside, the status of the Sekimeiya became apparent.
entries.new: 我们从 A走廊进去。刚一踏进门，Sekimeiya 的状况就一目了然。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hm...
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: See? It's still here! Nobody came down at all.
entries.new: 看吧？它还在！根本没人下来过。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: That's what I thought. You're just trying to have a bit too much fun.
entries.new: 我就知道。你不过是有点玩过头了。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: That's true, but I did definitely hear the elevator, so I'm not sure what happened. They might've had another reason to come here.
entries.new: 确实。可我分明听见了电梯声，所以也说不清到底怎么回事。也许他们下来是另有目的。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'm confused. Do you think it was one of us or someone we still haven't found?
entries.new: 我有点糊涂了。你觉得是我们当中的某个人，还是我们还没找到的人？
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Who fucking knows? If it was one of us, it could have only been someone who was above me and is still lying.
entries.new: 谁他妈知道。要是我们当中的人，那只能是当时在我上方、到现在还在撒谎的那个。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: If it was someone else, there's one extremely tight explanation: unless someone is still working with the culprit, they would need to have been inside the elevator from the beginning.{w} The elevator would've been below me and not where it was left, but then all its movements become useless.
entries.new: 要是另有其人，那就只剩下一种极其勉强的解释：除非还有人跟犯人串通，否则那个人从一开始就得待在电梯里。{w} 那样电梯就会一直在我下方，而不是停在原来那个位置，可这样一来，它所有的移动也就毫无意义了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You might just be mistaken about the goal. Yes, if they wanted to come down here, there was no reason to ever send the elevator up. There's not much reason for someone to stay down here, though.{w} What you heard could've been someone going up to the attic. They get to hole up there and nobody sees anyone coming out.
entries.new: 也许只是你把目的想错了。的确，如果那人想来这一层，就没必要把电梯往上叫。不过，也没什么理由让人待在这一层。{w} 你听见的，可能是有人上阁楼去了。只要人躲在阁楼里，就谁也不会看见有人出来。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: So this person was in the attic, which is why we didn't find them. From there, they called the empty elevator up, went down once, and finally back to the attic again. Is that it?
entries.new: 所以那个人一直待在阁楼里，我们才没找到他。他从那儿把空电梯叫上去，下来一次，最后又回了阁楼。是这样吗？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Maybe, but I have no idea what the purpose would be. They also would have sent it to the fifth again. It'd explain why we didn't find anyone, and nobody would have to be lying.
entries.new: 也许吧，可我实在想不出这有什么目的。而且之后也得把电梯再送回五楼。这样一来，既能解释我们为什么谁都没找到，也不必有人撒谎。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You'd all still be deaf, and why would the culprit come here from the attic if they'd been here just minutes prior? Surely this same person made the noise we heard?
entries.new: 那你们还是全聋了。再说，如果犯人几分钟前才来过这里，又何必从阁楼再下来一趟？我们听到的动静，难道不是同一个人弄出来的？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: This is risky anyway. If anyone from below entered the elevator before they called it back up, you could make it to the attic without the need for the key.
entries.new: 这本来就很冒险。如果下面有人在电梯被叫上去之前就进了电梯，那不用钥匙也能上阁楼。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I guess so...{w} Meaning that it's really difficult to explain this unless one of us is lying.
entries.new: 大概吧……{w} 也就是说，除非我们之中有人在撒谎，否则这件事很难解释得通。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: And conveniently, we know of someone who's been lying from the beginning.
entries.new: 而巧的是，我们恰好知道有个人从一开始就在撒谎。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Talking about yourself, or Atsuki?
entries.new: 你是在说你自己，还是在说 Atsuki？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I'm not sure what to think anymore. If the Sekimeiya's still here, there's no reason to come down in such a risky manner.
entries.new: 我已经不知道该怎么想了。既然 Sekimeiya 还在这里，就没理由用那么冒险的方式下来。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Unfortunately, even though I was allowed to reason things out with time travel in mind, it didn't make them any easier. The issue of the motive was just as hard to settle despite the fact that I could create even more theories.
entries.new: 遗憾的是，就算我把时间穿越考虑进去，事情也没变得更容易。尽管我能提出更多理论，动机的问题还是同样难以确定。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I could suppose that someone was inside the elevator on the crystal floor and went to the attic. Then, the same person time traveled to the crystal floor. They wanted to go to the attic again, so they called the elevator and went back up.{w} It had significant risk, but it was another way to justify the likely truth of being lied to.
entries.new: 我可以这样假设：有人在水晶层进了电梯，上到阁楼。随后，同一个人穿越时间，回到了水晶层。因为想再去阁楼，就叫来电梯又上去了一趟。{w} 这样做风险不小，但也可以换个角度解释：我们确实很可能被人骗了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai looked at his watch and turned his wrist to show us the time. It was {time=11:20}, and right above it, the date was also shown: 2011-12-15.
entries.new: Sai 看了看表，把手腕转过来给我们看时间。上面显示 {time=11:20}，正上方还标着日期：2011-12-15。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It's been a pretty eventful couple hours. I wonder if we'll be able to figure everything out before our time runs out.
entries.new: ……这两个小时还真是多事。不知道我们能不能在时间耗尽之前把一切弄清楚。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Who cares about that? The police will investigate what happened a lot better than we can. We shouldn't keep overstepping this much.
entries.new: 谁管那个？事情经过，警方会查得比我们清楚得多。我们不该再这样越界了。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: They'll definitely question all of us. Not every camera works, so their understanding of what happens here will depend pretty heavily on our testimony.
entries.new: 他们肯定会挨个盘问我们。摄像头不是每个都好用，所以要弄清这里发生了什么，很大程度上得靠我们的证词。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Isla, whose mood had greatly diminished over time, was quietly looking at the Sekimeiya through the glass. Her friend's prediction ended up entirely incorrect, and Erina made an attempt to comfort her.
entries.new: Isla 的心情早已低落下去，只是隔着玻璃静静望着 Sekimeiya。她朋友的预言彻底落了空，Erina 试着安慰她。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Right as the atmosphere seemed to calm down a bit, something that we'd already experienced repeated itself.
entries.new: 气氛才稍稍缓和，那件我们已经经历过的事却又重演了一遍。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The Third Law
entries.new: 第三定律

entries.text: What the hell was that...!?
entries.new: 刚才那到底是什么……！？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I think it was a door closing again, but slightly quieter.
entries.new: 应该又是关门声，不过比上次轻一点。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We had no time to rest. We knew that a foreign sound implied another long search if we didn't get results immediately.
entries.new: 我们没工夫歇息。那种陌生的声响一旦响起，若不能立刻查出结果，就意味着又要耗上一轮漫长的搜查。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Since it hadn't come from close by, we didn't rush out like the previous time. Instead, Sai approached hallway A and opened the door.
entries.new: 这次声音不是从近处传来的，我们便没有像上次那样冲出去。Sai 走到 A走廊前，推开了门。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We can see the exit from hallway A. Splitting up was useless last time and only caused more questions, so let's stick together while making sure the exit is being guarded.
entries.new: 从 A走廊能看到出口。上次分头行动毫无用处，反而多出一堆疑问，这次就一起走，同时确保出口有人守着。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: For the first sound, we'd all rushed to the right door because it seemed like it came from hallway B. However, the location of what we'd just heard was harder to discern.
entries.new: 第一次听到声响时，我们都朝右边的门冲去，因为那声音像是从 B走廊传来的。可刚才这一声，却很难判断方位。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We'll stay next to the stairs.
entries.new: 我们守在楼梯旁边。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Isla didn't object. She already understood that we weren't playing around.{w} The procedure of opening every room started once again.
entries.new: Isla 没有反对。她早已明白，我们不是在闹着玩。{w}于是，我们又开始逐个开门检查了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Since the sound was distant, it was very possible the source was no longer on our floor. Regardless, we couldn't move any faster because so many rooms had cabinets where a person could hide.
entries.new: 声音既然来自远处，源头很可能已经不在这一层。可即便如此，我们也快不起来——太多房间里都有能藏人的展示柜。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Every door in hallway A was opened and closed until we acknowledged each room was empty. Since Erina and Isla were by the stairs, we moved on to hallway B after Akaro claimed the mechanical room was vacant too.
entries.new: 我们反复开关A走廊的每一扇门，直到确认每一间房都是空的。Erina 和 Isla 还守在楼梯旁，Akaro 也说机械室里没人，我们便转向了 B走廊。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We didn't relent despite quickly running out of rooms. The last time we'd gotten complacent, a body had suddenly appeared.{w} The event room, acting as the midpoint of the hallway, still stored the Sekimeiya. ...If a culprit remained with us, they were trapped within the few last rooms.
entries.new: 能查的房间很快见了底，我们却没有松劲。上次正是因为松懈，尸体才忽然出现。{w}位于走廊中段的活动室里仍存放着 Sekimeiya。……如果凶手还混在我们中间，那他就被困在最后这几间房里了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, nothing was found inside them. The room where Naomi had died, the last crystal rooms, the staff room, and the cleaning room were all devoid of life.
entries.new: 然而这些房间里一无所获。Naomi 死去的房间、最后几间水晶展室、员工室和清洁间，全都不见人影。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How does this keep happening!? There must be someone else here!
entries.new: 怎么会一而再、再而三地出事！？这里肯定还有别人！
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Maybe it's a ghost?
entries.new: 说不定是鬼？
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: A ghost, huh? That'd explain a lot.
entries.new: 鬼啊……这么一说，倒能解释不少事。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Ghosts don't exist. This is two times we've heard a noise, so it's clear a person caused them.
entries.new: 鬼是不存在的。这已经是第二次听到动静了，显然是人弄出来的。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I figured Isla was serious. We were chasing behind someone who could vanish, make sounds without being seen, commit crimes in front of security cameras, and create innumerable questions doing so.
entries.new: 我猜 Isla 是认真的。我们追在后面的那个人，能凭空消失，能在无人看见时弄出动静，能在监控摄像头前作案，还顺手留下一堆解不开的疑问。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Do we actually have to investigate upstairs again? Why don't we stop playing with the culprit and let the police handle this?
entries.new: 我们真得再上楼搜一遍？何必还陪凶手玩下去，交给警察处理不就行了？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Because I'm not fond of that idea. They made a sound twice and then disappeared. They must be conscious of what they're doing, so let's go up again without splitting up. We'll leave the elevator open here so that they can't use it.
entries.new: 因为我不喜欢这个主意。对方弄出两次声响，随后就消失不见。他做这些事肯定是有意为之，所以再上楼一趟，别再分头。电梯就保持在这一层敞着门，让他没法用。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Wait...{w} We're forgetting one place again.
entries.new: 等等……{w}我们又漏掉了一个地方。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Are we?{w} ...Oh, right. The bathrooms.
entries.new: 漏了吗？{w}……哦，对了，厕所。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...That's true. And nobody could've left them yet.
entries.new: ……确实。而且这段时间没人能从那里面出来。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The map indicated that the left door was the women's and the right one the men's. We walked up to them while Erina and Isla blocked access to the other floors.
entries.new: 地图上标着，左边是女厕，右边是男厕。我们走上前去，Erina 和 Isla 则守着通往其他楼层的路。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya went ahead and opened the women's bathroom; it was completely empty.
entries.new: Shiroya 上前打开女厕的门，里面空无一人。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Then, Sai grabbed the opposite knob and turned it to open its door.{w}{w=0.5} ...He seemed to be having trouble.
entries.new: 接着，Sai 握住另一扇门的把手，想要拧开。{w}{w=0.5}……他似乎拧不动。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I don't think I can open this.
entries.new: ……这扇门我打不开。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What? Is the door locked?
entries.new: 什么？门锁上了？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: It could be. You can lock it from the inside without a key.
entries.new: 有可能。里面不用钥匙也能反锁。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Are you sure it's locked? Try turning it the other way.
entries.new: 你确定是锁了？换个方向拧拧看。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Sai didn't even try it. He was clearly sure it wouldn't open and caught the implication of what Katei said.
entries.new: Sai 连试都没试。他显然确信门打不开，也听懂了 Katei 那句话里的意思。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There's someone inside...?
entries.new: 里面有人……？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I-I suppose there must be.{w} Hey! Open the door, you don't have any way to escape!
entries.new: 大、大概吧。{w}喂！开门，你逃不掉的！
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: We'd all seen the interior of that bathroom once before. There was nothing that could serve as a way out, so even if someone inside intended to wait us out, the police would end up breaking the door down.
entries.new: 那间厕所里面，我们之前都看过一次。没有任何能当出口的地方，所以就算里面的人想跟我们耗下去，最后也只会等来警察破门。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai crouched, trying to see through the gap.
entries.new: Sai 蹲下身，想从门缝往里看。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There's barely any space. I was hoping I could see shoes or something.
entries.new: 缝太窄了。我还想着能看见鞋子什么的。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Can you open the door for us, Katei?
entries.new: Katei，你能帮我们把门打开吗？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Hm... Now that you mention it, I might be able to.
entries.new: 嗯……你这么一说，我倒也许有办法。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: There was a keyhole next to the doorknob, so it was possible to unlock the door without the manual inner lock.
entries.new: 门把手旁边有个锁孔，所以不碰里面的手动锁，也能从外面开锁。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There's a key that unlocks all the bathrooms. We have it in case an accident happens or someone locks themselves inside for too long, but I've never used it.
entries.new: 有一把钥匙能打开所有厕所的门。备着是为了以防出事，或者有人把自己锁在里面太久，不过我一直没用过。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Which also means that someone with that key could've locked the door from outside.
entries.new: 也就是说，拿着那把钥匙的人，也可能从外面把门锁上。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yes. It's not a guarantee that someone is still inside.
entries.new: 对。所以不能保证里面一定还有人。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Every employee should have a key. I'll go check if I can find one in the security room. I think I recall seeing it in a drawer.
entries.new: 每个员工都应该有一把。我去监控室看看能不能找到，印象里好像在抽屉里见过。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Okay. We'll wait here.
entries.new: 好，我们在这儿等着。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Katei went off to hallway A while the rest of us remained in front of the door.
entries.new: Katei 朝 A走廊去了，其余人留在门前。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'll bring this to the security room. I don't want it to stay here.
entries.new: 这个我拿去监控室。我不想把它留在这儿。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: On his way, he grabbed the empty suitcase and disappeared with it. It didn't seem like a bad idea, because it would make it harder for the culprit if they wanted to retrieve it at some point.
entries.new: 他顺路拎起那只空手提箱，一并带走了。这主意倒不坏——凶手若想什么时候取回箱子，就没那么容易了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...So, if there's nobody inside, it'll mean that Naomi's killer likely took the bathroom key from her alongside the cabinet's.
entries.new: ……也就是说，如果里面没人，那杀害 Naomi 的凶手多半是从她身上拿走了洗手间和展示柜的钥匙。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: And you think Katei did it, right?
entries.new: 你觉得是 Katei 干的，对吧？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: If I had to pick somebody, it'd be him. I wonder if he had the key on him the whole time and wants to act like he found it in the security room.
entries.new: 真要挑一个人的话，只能是他。我在想，会不会钥匙一直就在他身上，他却想装成是在监控室找到的。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Didn't he ask to search everyone earlier? We could've found it.
entries.new: 他之前不是还提出要搜所有人的身吗？那样说不定就能找到钥匙了。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yes, but at that point, this door wasn't locked yet. He might not have planned to use it later, and even if we found it, he could have lied to us about what it was.
entries.new: 话是这么说，可那时这扇门还没锁。他未必打算之后再用那把钥匙；就算我们找到了，他也能随便编个说法，说那是什么东西。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: But he couldn't have locked this door, could he? That had to be related to the sound we just heard.
entries.new: 可这扇门不可能是他锁的吧？那肯定和我们刚才听到的声音有关。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: He definitely had a chance. It's likely someone above floor 3 took the elevator here, remember? Katei was on floor 6 and is the most likely person to have killed Naomi.
entries.new: 他绝对有机会。还记得吗？很可能是 3 楼以上的某个人坐电梯下来的。Katei 当时在 6 楼，是最有可能杀害 Naomi 的人。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He just said that every employee has one of these keys, so whoever locked the door could have gotten it from somewhere else.
entries.new: 他刚说过每个员工都有这种钥匙，所以锁门的人完全可能从别处弄到一把。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That's true, but everything keeps casting more and more doubt on Katei. First, let's see if anyone's inside. If we don't find anyone, Katei will be the most likely suspect once again.
entries.new: 的确如此，可所有迹象都在不断加深对 Katei 的怀疑。先看看里面有没有人吧。要是没找到人，Katei 就又会成为最有可能的嫌疑人。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Why do you think so? Even if nobody's inside, he must've been trying to hide something by locking this door. He wouldn't have told us how to unlock it.
entries.new: ……你为什么这么想？就算里面没人，他锁这扇门也一定是为了藏什么。他本来可不会把开锁的方法告诉我们。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Assuming he comes back with the key. The other possibility is that we're still dealing with an unknown person, someone who took the key off Naomi and wants us to spend a while in front of an empty bathroom...
entries.new: 前提是他真会带着钥匙回来。另一种可能是，我们面对的还是那个不明身份的人——他从 Naomi 身上拿走了钥匙，想让我们在一间空洗手间前白耗一阵子……
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Hm... It's the smell again...
entries.new: 嗯……又是那股味道……
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Smell? ...Oh, you're right. It's hard to tell, but it's there. The same as before.
entries.new: 味道？……哦，你说得对。虽然不太明显，但确实有。和之前一样。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: You say that, but I don't think it ever faded away. I've been noticing it the entire time I looked through these rooms.
entries.new: 话是这么说，可我觉得它压根就没散过。我在这些房间里查看时，一直都闻得到。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: We all visibly sniffed the air. I didn't notice it greatly, but I could somewhat pick out the strange smell from before. Shortly after that, we spotted Katei coming from the hallway. As soon as he made eye contact with us, he showed us a silver key in his hand.
entries.new: 我们几个人都不约而同地嗅了嗅空气。我闻得并不真切，但多少能分辨出之前那股怪味。没过多久，我们看见 Katei 从走廊那边走来。他一和我们对上视线，就亮出了手里的一把银色钥匙。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was... not doing too well the first time we noticed it, but I feel like I've smelled this before.
entries.new: 第一次闻到的时候，我……状态不太好，但我总觉得自己以前闻过这个味道。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Really...? I don't feel that way at all.
entries.new: 真的吗……？我完全没这种感觉。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I think it's this one.
entries.new: 应该是这一把。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Hm, it's not like any that Naomi had.
entries.new: 嗯，和 Naomi 的那些钥匙都不一样。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Oh? Of course not. This doesn't mean that her key must've been stolen, if that's what you're thinking. I doubt any employee would always have theirs, seeing as we never need them.
entries.new: 哦？那当然。如果你是在想她的钥匙一定被偷了，那可不见得。我们从来用不上这些钥匙，我不觉得会有哪个员工一直带在身上。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Fine. Just try to open the door.
entries.new: 好吧。你试着开一下门。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Katei sighed and inserted the key. It turned, showing that he'd picked the correct one.{w} The door made a clearly audible sound, and Katei proceeded to gently open it.
entries.new: Katei 叹了口气，把钥匙插了进去。钥匙转动了，说明他选对了。{w} 门发出一声清晰可闻的响动，随后 Katei 轻轻把门推开。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Once we saw what awaited inside, all of us froze, failing to comprehend what we were looking at.
entries.new: 看清里面的景象后，我们全都僵住了，一时无法理解眼前所见。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the fuck...?
entries.new: 这他妈是怎么回事……？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Th-This is impossible...
entries.new: 这、这不可能……
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We all must've experienced a strong feeling of déjà vu.{w} On the floor of the men's bathroom lay Naomi's unmoving body.
entries.new: 我们所有人一定都产生了强烈的既视感。{w} 男洗手间的地板上，躺着 Naomi 一动不动的尸体。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Instinctively, Erina ushered Isla aside, but she had already seen what was in the room.
entries.new: Erina 本能地把 Isla 拉到一旁，可她已经看见了房间里的东西。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Why the hell would anyone lock her body in here?
entries.new: ……到底为什么会有人把她的尸体锁在这里面？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...Lock her body in? Didn't we just look at it a second ago?
entries.new: ……把她的尸体锁起来？我们刚才不是才看过吗？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: She was right. We'd entered the room where Naomi died and seen her.
entries.new: 她说得没错。我们进过 Naomi 遇害的那个房间，还看到了她。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Or had we? Had we perhaps only seen the curtain that should've been covering her...? Everyone else was likely thinking the same, but Sai instructed us to take it slow.
entries.new: 又或者，我们真的看到了吗？也许我们看见的，只是那块原本该盖住她的遮布……？其他人多半也都在这么想，但 Sai 让我们先别急。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hold on. We can see that room from here, so there's no point in running to it. There's no security camera in the bathroom, so we need to make sure we don't miss anything right now.
entries.new: 等等。从这里就能看到那个房间，没必要跑过去。洗手间里没有监控摄像头，所以现在绝不能漏掉任何细节。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It felt like a pointless attempt, but I crouched to check Naomi's pulse like Sai did the first time.{w} I felt nothing.
entries.new: 我知道这多半是徒劳，但还是蹲下去探了探 Naomi 的脉搏，就像 Sai 第一次那样。{w} 我什么也没摸到。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What are you doing? Did you think she might've revived?
entries.new: 你在做什么？你以为她还能活过来？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: No... but this isn't right. There should be a bit of blood oozing from her, shouldn't there? But there's none. And the floor... it's completely clean.
entries.new: 不是……但这不对劲。她身上多少应该渗点血出来吧？可一滴都没有。还有地板……也干干净净。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What...? You're right—there's no blood at all.
entries.new: 什么……？你说得对——一点血都没有。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: At least this confirms that the lock wasn't set from the inside. Someone locked her inside with the key.
entries.new: 至少这能确认，锁不是从里面上的。是有人用钥匙把她锁在了里面。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: There's nothing else here... We need to check the other body.
entries.new: 这里没有别的了……我们得去看看另一具尸体。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We all ran to room B4 except for Erina and Isla, who stayed guarding the bathrooms and in sight of the stairs. In hallway B, in front of the event room, Naomi had died. We'd left her body under a curtain to preserve her dignity...
entries.new: 除了 Erina 和 Isla 留在洗手间旁看守、并守在能看见楼梯的地方，我们都跑去了 B4 室。Naomi 死在 B 走廊的活动室门前。为了保全她的体面，我们把尸体留在了遮布下……
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai forcibly opened the door. In very quick succession, another impossibility immediately appeared before us.
entries.new: Sai 用力推开门。紧接着，又一件不可能的事立刻出现在我们眼前。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The cloth's sides had been tainted by blood, which was all around it. In the middle of the huge, red circle was a bulge the size of a human.
entries.new: 遮布边缘被血浸染，四周也全是血。那个巨大的红色圆圈中央，有一块人形大小的隆起。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It can't be... She's still here.
entries.new: 不可能……她还在这里。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: We couldn't form a response. Her body was still beneath the curtain.
entries.new: 我们谁也说不出话来。她的尸体仍盖在遮布下面。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It appears Atsuki was correct, then. Something very out of the ordinary is going on.
entries.new: 看来 Atsuki 说对了。眼下发生的事非同寻常。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai ran out of breath at the end of his sentence. Not even he could easily fathom it.
entries.new: Sai 说到最后，气息都有些不稳。即便是他，也没法轻易想明白。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He approached the body and gently removed the curtain from it. The result was what we'd expected, yet it still seemed impossible. Naomi's corpse hadn't moved in the slightest.
entries.new: 他走近尸体，轻轻掀开遮布。结果和我们预想的一样，却仍旧显得难以置信。Naomi 的尸体一动也没动过。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the hell is this...?
entries.new: 这到底是怎么回事……？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Katei, let's get this out of the way. Does Naomi have a fucking twin?
entries.new: Katei，先把话说清楚。Naomi 是不是他妈有个双胞胎？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: U-Um... Not that I know. I wasn't close enough to her.
entries.new: 呃、嗯……据我所知没有。我和她没那么熟。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: A-A twin wouldn't explain this. Look here.
entries.new: 双、双胞胎也解释不了这个。你看这里。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Her suit had a product label by its neck, containing four numbers.
entries.new: 她这件防护服的领口处贴着一张产品标签，上面印着四个数字。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: 63-22? Was it the same in the bathroom?
entries.new: 63-22？浴室里那件也是这个号吗？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...Yes. I saw it when I felt for her pulse. Katei, you know Ashiya. Is that just a model number or something?
entries.new: ……对。我探她脉搏时看到的。Katei，你熟悉芦屋的产品吧。这会不会只是型号之类的编号？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...It isn't. Those are individual product run numbers.
entries.new: ……不是。那些是单件产品的生产流水号。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Then this is the exact same suit.
entries.new: 那这就是同一件防护服。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: So there's... no doubt that Atsuki was telling the truth. The killer used the Sekimeiya's powers to do this.
entries.new: 这么说……Atsuki 没说谎。凶手是用 Sekimeiya 的力量做到的。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Katei could no longer deny it; two identical dead bodies had appeared before him.
entries.new: 两具一模一样的尸体就摆在眼前，Katei 再也无从否认。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The Sekimeiya was still in the cabinet, so they must've returned it...
entries.new: Sekimeiya 还在展示柜里，那他们应该是把它放回去了……
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...A-All right. According to you guys, the Sekimeiya made Atsuki time travel. How would traveling through time lead to this?
entries.new: ……好、好吧。按你们的说法，是 Sekimeiya 让 Atsuki 穿越了时间。可时间穿越怎么会造成这种事？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: We don't know how it works. There might be more to it than it first seemed, but just consider this... What would happen if you tried to make a dead body time travel?
entries.new: 它到底怎么运作，我们也不清楚。也许内情比表面看到的更复杂。不过你们想一想……如果让一具尸体穿越时间，会怎么样？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Normally, you'd think nothing would happen, but what if the dead body actually traveled through time?
entries.new: 一般来说，大概会觉得什么都不会发生。可万一尸体真的穿越了呢？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Y-Yeah... Someone might've made Naomi's body time travel by touching it with the Sekimeiya.
entries.new: 对、对啊……也许有人用 Sekimeiya 碰了 Naomi 的尸体，让她穿越了时间。
entries.speaker: s
