entries.text: If they knew Naomi would appear in the bathroom, they could've locked it preemptively. If not, maybe they just moved the identical body inside and locked it. That has to be related to that noise we heard.
entries.new: 如果凶手事先知道 Naomi 会出现在浴室，就能提前把门锁上。否则，也许他只是把那具一模一样的尸体搬进去，再锁上门。这一定和我们听到的那声响有关。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: An identical body... We should inspect it more thoroughly. We don't know what happened, but that other Naomi might have something important on her.
entries.new: 一模一样的尸体……我们得再仔细检查一遍。虽然不知道发生了什么，但那个 Naomi 身上也许带着什么要紧的东西。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We didn't have much else we could do to figure anything out, so we went back to the bathroom.
entries.new: 除此之外，我们也没有别的办法查明什么，只好回到浴室。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The other Naomi hadn't moved.
entries.new: 另一个 Naomi 依旧一动不动。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Let me check...
entries.new: 让我看看……
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I watched Sai carefully to make sure he couldn't do anything in secret. All he did was check every pocket, and they were all empty.
entries.new: 我紧盯着 Sai，提防他暗中动手脚。可他只是把每个口袋都翻了一遍，里面空空如也。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Huh... She doesn't have any keys. Not even the keys that the other body had.
entries.new: 咦……她身上没有钥匙。连另一具尸体带着的那些钥匙也没有。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: So that theory was probably wrong. If whoever did this created an identical body in the past, it would've had the same keys.
entries.new: 看来那个推测多半不成立。如果凶手是在过去造出了一具一模一样的尸体，那它应该也带着同样的钥匙。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I-If that's how it worked... I'd think so.
entries.new: 如、如果真是那样……我想应该是吧。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Couldn't the culprit just have taken them?
entries.new: 难道不会是凶手把钥匙拿走了吗？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: But why? They didn't take them from the original body.
entries.new: 可为什么呢？原来那具尸体上的钥匙，他们就没拿走啊。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: There are two more things that don't hold up.{w} The clothes are the first. If Naomi's body traveled to the past, her clothes would've been stained with blood, just like they were at the time it traveled.{w} And second: you all saw me vanish when it happened to me, right? If the same thing happened to Naomi, the first body should've disappeared.
entries.new: 还有两点说不通。{w}第一是衣服。如果 Naomi 的尸体穿越到了过去，衣服上应该带着穿越那一刻的血迹。{w}第二：那件事发生在我身上时，你们都亲眼看到我消失了吧？如果 Naomi 也一样，那第一具尸体就该消失了。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Technically, with how little we knew, my points could've still been refuted.
entries.new: 不过严格说来，凭我们知道的这点东西，我提出的疑点未必不能驳倒。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "What if the replica of the body only takes into consideration the state of the body in the past?"{w} With the way I'd traveled, I couldn't be sure whether my then-present body had teleported into the past, or if the body I'd arrived in was identical to how it was at the point in time I appeared.
entries.new: 「如果复制出的尸体只还原它在过去那一时刻的状态呢？」{w} 以我自己的穿越经历，我分不清到底是当时的那具身体穿越回了过去，还是我抵达的那具身体，只是和我出现那一刻的状态一模一样。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If Naomi had gone back to the past far enough, to a point before her death, her clothes might've been clean. Even though she was alive at that point, if the body that had traveled was dead, she probably would've appeared dead in the past. ...Otherwise, she would have come back to life.
entries.new: 如果 Naomi 回到足够远的过去，远在她死之前，那她的衣服也许就是干净的。即便她在那个时间点还活着，只要穿越过去的是尸体，她在过去大概也会以死人的样子出现。……否则，她就会活过来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It also implied that the second body had been with us in the tower before we'd found the first one and had only just been shown to us. ...Given how we'd been unable to find the culprit, it couldn't be ruled out.
entries.new: 这也意味着，第二具尸体在我们发现第一具之前，就一直待在塔里，只是刚刚才出现在我们眼前。……既然我们始终找不到凶手，这种可能也无法排除。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is there another way to make this work? I've thought of a few things involving time travel, but now we have no other choice. There's nothing else that could begin to explain this, so what I went through has to be related to the truth of what happened.
entries.new: 还有别的解释能说得通吗？我想到过几种与时间穿越有关的可能，可现在已别无选择。除此之外，再没有别的东西能勉强解释这一切，所以我亲身经历的事，必然与真相有关。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: This body is dead, but there's no blood around it. Could it be that she appeared dead from the future and that's why no blood is anywhere? That her body is as it was when she was alive, yet her true state is from after her death?
entries.new: 这具尸体已经死了，周围却没有血迹。她会不会是死后才从未来出现的，所以哪里都没有血？身体还是她活着时的样子，实际状态却来自她死之后？
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The only other thing I can think of slightly contradicts my own experience, but it'd sound more believable if not for that.
entries.new: 我唯一还能想到的另一种可能，与我的亲身经历稍有矛盾。若没有这一点，它反倒更让人信服。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: It would only require the past to be malleable. I didn't personally change anything when I traveled back in time, but that's not enough reason to think that's impossible.
entries.new: 那只需要假设过去是可以被改写的。我自己穿越回去时没有改变任何事，但仅凭这一点，还不能断定那种事不可能发生。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: What if Naomi traveled back in time when she was alive? Two of them would've existed in the past. Then, all the culprit needed to do was kill both of them.
entries.new: 如果 Naomi 是在活着的时候穿越回过去的呢？那样过去就会同时存在两个她。凶手只要把这两个都杀掉就行了。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: This should never be possible; it's a paradox. By killing the Naomi who will travel to the past, you're making it impossible for the new one to exist.
entries.new: 这按理说绝不可能发生，那是个悖论。杀掉那个将要穿越回过去的 Naomi，就等于让新出现的那个无法存在。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: But I don't know if these kinds of paradoxes exist. What if Naomi's actions upon traveling made it impossible for her initial self to travel? Two of them would permanently exist at the same time, and us finding two dead bodies would work.
entries.new: 可我不知道这类悖论是否真的存在。假如 Naomi 穿越后的所作所为，让她最初的那个自己无法再穿越呢？那样两个她就会永久并存，我们找到两具尸体也就说得通了。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: However, if this isn't a possible occurrence in our universe, I can't think of anything else. The mere fact that traveling makes your body instantly disappear means that, without paradoxes, two of the same person couldn't exist at once as corpses.
entries.new: 不过，如果这种事在我们的世界里根本不可能发生，我就再也想不出别的解释了。光是穿越会让身体瞬间消失这一点，就说明在没有悖论的前提下，同一个人不可能同时以两具尸体的形式存在。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: To circumvent the paradox, I can suppose that a dead body can travel to the past and create a new dead body. This still hits the barrier of "the original body should've disappeared as soon as it traveled", but it's not absolute: maybe the first dead body will travel back in the future, and that's why it's still there.
entries.new: 为了绕过这个悖论，我可以假设尸体也能穿越回过去，并造出一具新的尸体。这仍然撞上「原本的尸体一穿越就该消失」这道坎，不过也并非绝对：也许第一具尸体将来会穿越回去，所以它至今还留在那里。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: And on top of all this, there has to be a motive. A motive for all of this to be happening. For a culprit to create this mess, to kill the same person twice, and for something with time traveling powers to be publicly exposed in this place. Is Xyn actually behind it...?
entries.new: 况且，这一切背后必定有动机。让这一切发生的动机。凶手为什么要制造这场混乱，为什么要把同一个人杀死两次，又为什么要把拥有时间穿越之力的东西在这座塔里公之于众。难道幕后真是 Xyn……？
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Nobody had said anything in a while. We were all dumbfounded, staring at the impossible image.
entries.new: 好一阵子，谁都没有开口。我们全都愣在原地，盯着那幅本不该存在的画面。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hm, that's interesting.{w} She has a bump on the back of her head. It's similar to her other body, but blood's not coming out of this one.
entries.new: 嗯，有意思。{w}她后脑上有一块肿包。和她另一具身体的情况相似，可这具没有流血。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Is that so?{w} Then this body isn't the same as when she was alive despite the lack of blood.
entries.new: ……是吗？{w}那么，这具尸体虽然没流血，状态却和她活着时并不一样。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Let's go test it. Let's try to understand how the Sekimeiya works.
entries.new: 去验证一下吧。试着弄清 Sekimeiya 是怎么运作的。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Hey! Stop!
entries.new: 喂！站住！
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: But Sai continued toward the event room, housing what we believed to be the center of every mystery.
entries.new: 可 Sai 径直朝活动室走去——我们认定，一切谜团的核心就在那里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: None of us wanted to stop him. Instead, we ran behind him, forcing Katei to follow us.
entries.new: 我们谁也没打算拦他，反而跟在他身后跑了起来，Katei 也只得跟上来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We entered the room at the same time and saw the Sekimeiya still in the cabinet.
entries.new: 我们同时走进房间，看见 Sekimeiya 仍在展示柜里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's good that we didn't lock this. Only the culprit has the key, so it only hurts us.
entries.new: 幸好我们没把这个锁上。钥匙只有凶手才有，锁上只会对我们不利。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai, you'll get all of us in trouble...
entries.new: Sai，你这样会把我们都牵连进去的……
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: What might get us in trouble is the murderer that's somewhere in this place. If something happens to the Sekimeiya, it's their fault.
entries.new: 会给我们惹上麻烦的，是藏在这地方某处的凶手。Sekimeiya 要是出了什么事，那也是他们的责任。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He proceeded to scroll down the glass and then took the Sekimeiya out.
entries.new: 他接着把玻璃罩滑下，将 Sekimeiya 取了出来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We stared at him as he held it in his hands. He remained nonchalant, and there was no reaction.
entries.new: 他把 Sekimeiya 捧在手里，我们全都盯着他。他依旧神色淡然，什么反应也没有。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Nothing?
entries.new: 什么都没发生？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Maybe I just cloned myself in the past—who's to know? I'm clearly still here, though.
entries.new: 也许我只是在过去复制了一个自己——谁知道呢？不过我可还好端端站在这儿。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Without asking, he dropped it between my hands. It was really cold, and it didn't send me anywhere. Its color wasn't changing either.
entries.new: 他问也不问，就把它丢进我两手之间。那东西冰凉刺骨，却没有把我送去任何地方，颜色也没有变化。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't understand it. Maybe the Sekimeiya didn't do anything and something else is the actual cause of this phenomenon.
entries.new: 我搞不懂。也许 Sekimeiya 根本什么也没做，造成这种现象的其实是别的东西。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: But it changed colors, right? Both when Atsuki touched it and when we put it here.
entries.new: 可它变过颜色，对吧？Atsuki 碰到它的时候，还有我们把它放上去的时候，都变了。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Let's keep it outside. We'll see if it happens again.
entries.new: 先把它放在外面吧。看看还会不会再发生。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I won't allow that.{w} I couldn't stop you from getting it out, but you only proved that the Sekimeiya isn't at all related to what's going on. Put it back in.
entries.new: 这我不允许。{w}你们取出来的时候我拦不住，可你们恰恰证明了 Sekimeiya 与眼下的状况毫无干系。放回去。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Mind if I go poke Naomi's body with it first? Something could happen.
entries.new: 不介意我先拿它去碰一碰 Naomi 的尸体吧？说不定会有什么反应。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You're losing your mind. That'd be beyond disgraceful.
entries.new: 你简直是昏了头。那样做就太不成体统了。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Katei took the Sekimeiya from my hands and put it in its cabinet.
entries.new: Katei 从我手里拿过 Sekimeiya，放回了展示柜。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh... I might've realized something.
entries.new: 哦……我好像想明白了一件事。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What is it?
entries.new: 什么事？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: It's not directly related to the Sekimeiya, but I just remembered something when you mentioned touching Naomi's body.
entries.new: 和 Sekimeiya 没有直接关系，不过你刚才说到去碰 Naomi 的尸体，让我想起了一件事。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: They all waited for me to continue and reveal something important, but I wasn't sure if I was right. Instead, I took off toward the room with the original body of Naomi.
entries.new: 他们都在等我接着说，等我说出什么重要的事，可我自己也不确定猜得对不对。于是我转身就朝存放着 Naomi 原本遗体的房间走去。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was followed in. Inside, I kneeled beside the body and looked around it.
entries.new: 他们跟了进来。我在遗体旁跪下，四下查看。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...What are you doing?
entries.new: ……你在做什么？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Good, it's still here.
entries.new: 很好，还在这儿。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I showed them the result of my successful search: the keyring we'd found in one of Naomi's pockets.
entries.new: 我把搜寻的成果亮给他们看——那串从 Naomi 的某个口袋里找到的钥匙。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What about this? Do you know what they're for?
entries.new: 那这个呢？你知道这些钥匙是开哪儿的吗？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Oh! Of course, this big one...
entries.new: ……啊！当然，这把大的……
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yes. I think it might be the key to the attic.
entries.new: 嗯。我觉得它也许就是阁楼的钥匙。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...A-Are you serious?
entries.new: ……你、你是认真的？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I am. We saw the keyhole upstairs, and it needed a big key like this one. The elevator has one too, but you can't really determine the shape of the key from it, so I understand why you didn't notice it.
entries.new: 认真的。我们在楼上见过那个锁孔，要开它就得用这么大的钥匙。电梯上也有一个锁孔，可从那儿看不出钥匙的形状，所以你当时没留意到，也难怪。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What do you say, Katei?
entries.new: 你怎么看，Katei？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Honestly, I can't tell. He could be right, but I'm not sure why Naomi would have it.
entries.new: ……说实话，我也说不准。他也许说得对，可我想不通 Naomi 为什么会有那把钥匙。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: So we could have access to the attic, where the culprit might've been hiding all this time.
entries.new: 这么说，我们就能进阁楼了——凶手说不定一直躲在那儿。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Not only that. If I'm right, we've had access for a while. We could've entered it during our last search.
entries.new: 不止如此。如果我没猜错，我们早就能进去了。上次搜寻的时候，我们本可以进阁楼。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: But I can't think we would've found someone there so easily. First, it would mean that they have another key. Second, they hid there knowing we had access to it. Third, they didn't take this key from Naomi.{w} ...And yet the one for the cabinet was taken.
entries.new: 但我不觉得我们能那么轻易就在那儿抓到人。第一，那意味着他们另有一把钥匙；第二，他们明知我们能进去，却还是躲在那里；第三，他们没有从 Naomi 身上拿走这把钥匙。{w}……可展示柜的钥匙却被拿走了。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: So maybe they don't care about us going to the attic.
entries.new: 也许他们根本不在乎我们进不进阁楼。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: This doesn't matter. Let's just go see if it fits.
entries.new: 这些都不重要。先去试试这把钥匙合不合用。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I removed the key from the set and was about to exit the room until Shiroya made us aware of something.
entries.new: 我从钥匙串上取下那把钥匙，正要走出房间，Shiroya 却提醒了我们一件事。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Where is Akaro?
entries.new: ……Akaro 人呢？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: We looked around in bewilderment. She was right: Akaro wasn't with us.
entries.new: 我们愕然地环顾四周。她说得没错，Akaro 没和我们在一起。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did he even come in here?
entries.new: 他到底有没有进来过？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We looked around hallway B, but it appeared empty. In front of us was the event room, which we could also see was empty through the door.
entries.new: 我们在 B走廊里四处张望，却不见半个人影。正前方就是活动室，透过门也能看出里面空无一人。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Where the hell did he go?
entries.new: 他到底跑哪儿去了？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Did he go off on his own? No way someone attacked him, right? It's hard to believe we wouldn't have heard anything, and restraining Akaro would require quite a bit of effort. This floor should've been clear too.
entries.new: 他是自己走开的？总不能是被人袭击了吧？真要是那样，我们不可能一点动静都没听见，何况要制住 Akaro 也得费不少力气。再说这一层本该只有我们才对。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We kept talking as we looked through the other hallway. Erina and Isla were still next to the stairs, alone.
entries.new: 我们一边说着，一边查看另一条走廊。Erina 和 Isla 仍守在楼梯旁，只有她们两人。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Do we try to go to the attic before looking for him thoroughly? It's just fantastic that someone disappeared as soon as we found our way in...
entries.new: 我们是先彻底找他，还是先去阁楼？偏在我们刚找到入口的当口有人不见了，可真会挑时候……
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: But he might be in danger...
entries.new: 可他也许有危险……
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: If he is in danger, he will be even if we search for him. If he walked away by himself, he wouldn't let us just find him again, and if the culprit took him, they've been dodging us for quite a while.{w} This is the first time we've been in this situation and have access to the attic, so we should go there first. Afterward, we'll move down if we haven't found him.
entries.new: 他要是真有危险，就算我们去找，他也一样有危险。如果是他自己走开的，就不会让我们轻易找到；如果是凶手把他带走的，那对方已经躲了我们这么久。{w}这是我们头一回既碰上这种局面，又能进阁楼，所以该先去那儿。之后要是还没找到他，我们再往下走。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: No. Akaro must still be here. Let's look for him.
entries.new: 不。Akaro 一定还在这儿。先找他。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...{w}Fine. He better have a very good reason if he separated from us on purpose.
entries.new: ……{w}好吧。他要是故意离开我们，最好有个像样的理由。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Do you really think he did...?
entries.new: 你真觉得他是故意的……？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Isn't he incredibly suspicious? He's been cooperative, but he's felt out of place from the beginning. He showed no interest in anything going on here, but he got trapped because he arrived so early.
entries.new: 他难道不可疑吗？他一直很配合，可从一开始就显得格格不入。这里发生什么他都不感兴趣，偏偏又因为来得太早被困住了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Aren't you in the same position?
entries.new: 你的处境不也一样吗？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: No, but you are. I came here out of curiosity.
entries.new: 不，你才是。我只是出于好奇才来的。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Regardless, hallway B was empty when we entered Naomi's room. If someone took him by surprise, they would've had to come from behind. Unless you wanna say that maybe they materialized right behind Akaro, it's a dubious thing to think, because we looked through this entire floor not long ago.
entries.new: 总之，我们进 Naomi 房间的时候，B走廊是空的。若有人趁其不备，也只能从背后下手。除非你想说那人凭空出现在了 Akaro 身后——这念头站不住脚，毕竟不久前我们才把这一层查了个遍。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: But the Sekimeiya's still here. What other reason could he have to vanish like that?
entries.new: 可 Sekimeiya 还在这里。除此之外，他还能有什么理由那样凭空消失？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I don't know, to make us waste time? Isn't that what the culprit has been doing from the beginning?
entries.new: 谁知道，也许是想让我们白白浪费时间？犯人从一开始不就在这么干吗？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We explained everything to Erina and Isla while Sai called the elevator. It was still on our floor, so it probably hadn't been used. If it had, we wouldn't have heard it, so we couldn't be sure. Erina and Isla would've needed to miss the button lighting up for a couple seconds.
entries.new: Sai 去叫电梯的时候，我们把事情的经过都跟 Erina 和 Isla 讲了一遍。电梯还停在我们这一层，所以应该没人用过。就算真有人用过，我们也听不见，无法确定。而 Erina 和 Isla 得刚好有几秒没看到按钮亮起来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He suddenly disappeared...? Nobody could've gone up.
entries.new: 他就这么突然消失了……？不可能有人上去啊。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Lend me the key, Atsuki. I wanna see if it fits.
entries.new: Atsuki，把钥匙借我。我看看能不能对上。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Here.
entries.new: 给你。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I gave him the big, brown key that I'd detached from the keyring. Sai took it and attempted to insert it in the keyhole inside the elevator.
entries.new: 我把从钥匙圈上取下的那把棕色大钥匙递给他。Sai 接过，试着把它插进电梯里的锁孔。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...You were correct. It's this one.
entries.new: ……你说得对。就是这把。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: As he turned it, the seventh button lit up, indicating it had become available.
entries.new: 他一转动钥匙，七楼的按钮就亮了起来，说明已经可以按了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Seriously? That's very strange...{w} I'm not sure you understand how restricted that place is. I'm not certain we should even go.
entries.new: 真的？这可太奇怪了……{w} 你们恐怕不明白那地方管得有多严。我甚至不确定我们该不该去。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Oh, we're going, but first we'll see if we can find Akaro here. The culprit must have another key to the attic, given they left this one on Naomi.
entries.new: 当然要去，不过先看看能不能在这儿找到 Akaro。既然他们把这一把留在了 Naomi 身上，那犯人手里肯定还有一把阁楼的钥匙。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: When Sai took the key out, the light surrounding the button turned off. Then, he handed it back to me. As I put it in my pocket, he carefully shut the elevator and let go before it was fully closed. By doing so, he created a small gap between the door and the elevator.
entries.new: Sai 拔出钥匙，按钮周围的灯随之熄灭。然后他把钥匙还给了我。我收进口袋时，他小心地把电梯门合上，在完全关严之前松了手，让门与门框之间留下一道细缝。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Good, this works. We can keep it open like this without sticking something in there. Later, if we do a thorough search, we'll be able to do this so nobody can call it.
entries.new: 很好，这样就行。不用塞东西，也能让门一直开着。之后要是我们仔细搜查，就可以这么办，免得有人把电梯叫走。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Since Akaro can only be here, let's see if we can find him real quick. After that, our priority is looking for something important in the attic.
entries.new: 既然 Akaro 只可能在这儿，那就赶紧找找他。找到之后，我们的首要任务就是去阁楼找一样重要的东西。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He closed the elevator again. We'd gotten used to the crystal floor searches, so it didn't feel like an imposing task anymore. Erina and Isla remained where they'd been while the rest of us chose individual rooms to look through, including the bathrooms and the mechanical room.{w} Every single one of them was empty, so we reunited by the stairs.
entries.new: 他重新把电梯门关上。水晶层的搜索我们已经习惯了，不再觉得是什么难事。Erina 和 Isla 留在原处，其余人各自挑了房间查看，连卫生间和机械室也没放过。{w} 每一间都是空的，我们于是回到楼梯旁会合。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Either Akaro managed to disappear or the culprit managed to make him disappear. The Sekimeiya didn't work for us earlier, so a lot of this isn't adding up. I'm not sure what Akaro has to do with this, but for now, let's get moving.
entries.new: 要么是 Akaro 自己消失了，要么是犯人让他消失了。方才 Sekimeiya 对我们毫无反应，所以很多地方都对不上。我不清楚 Akaro 与这件事有何关系，但眼下还是先走吧。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We can't all fit in the elevator, so let's go through the main door. It'd be better to stick together.
entries.new: 电梯装不下我们所有人，走正门吧。还是一起行动比较好。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I agree.
entries.new: 我也这么想。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Without wasting time, we moved through the floors to reach the sixth.{w} It was surreal not having Akaro with us. Naomi's second appearance eclipsed the oddity of his disappearance, but it was also something that I couldn't even begin to understand.
entries.new: 我们没多耽搁，一路穿过各层，来到了六楼。{w} Akaro 不在身边，这种感觉很不真实。Naomi 的第二次出现盖过了他失踪的诡异，可那本身也是我完全无法理解的事。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "The Sekimeiya didn't work for us earlier, so a lot of this isn't adding up."{w} Sai implied that the Sekimeiya must've caused Akaro's disappearance, but there was an important discrepancy: it was shut behind the glass. If it was involved, it worked in a way beyond what we knew.
entries.new: 「方才 Sekimeiya 对我们毫无反应，所以很多地方都对不上。」{w} Sai 话里的意思是，Akaro 的失踪必定出自 Sekimeiya 之手，可这里有个重要的矛盾：它当时还锁在玻璃罩内。若它真的参与其中，那起作用的方式也超出了我们的认知。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, I didn't see this door.
entries.new: 哦，我都没注意到这扇门。
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: It's my first time looking at it too. It's pretty sturdy—no way we'd be opening it without the key.
entries.new: 我也是头一回见到。这门相当结实——没有钥匙，我们根本打不开。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: They all looked at me expectantly. I took the key out of my pocket and inserted it into the keyhole. I'd been half expecting something to go wrong, but I was able to smoothly turn it and unlock the door to the mysterious attic.
entries.new: 他们都满怀期待地看向我。我掏出钥匙，插进锁孔。我原本还有些担心会出岔子，结果钥匙转动得很顺，神秘阁楼的门就这样开了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai quickly dragged the door open. There was a narrow staircase leading upward that obligated us to form a line.
entries.new: Sai 一把将门拉开。门后是一段向上延伸的窄楼梯，我们只能排成一列。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's pretty dark...
entries.new: 里面好黑……
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Hm... Do we need to go?
entries.new: 唔……我们非去不可吗？
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: These stairs are like this because there's no room directly above us. They had to link this door to the closest room. It wasn't an easy task, and there wasn't much space to make a wider staircase.
entries.new: 楼梯会成这样，是因为我们正上方没有房间。他们只能把这扇门接到最近的一间房去。这活儿不容易，也没有多少空间可以修更宽的楼梯。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...You saw the attic earlier through the cameras. It's a tidy floor in the layout of a normal household. Since not many people can access it, they didn't bother making a more pleasant entryway.
entries.new: ……你们之前通过监控看过阁楼。那一层收拾得很整齐，布局就像普通住家。能进去的人不多，所以他们也没费心弄个像样的入口。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: But won't we get in trouble for going in?
entries.new: 可我们进去，不会惹上麻烦吗？
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: We might. I'm advising you all not to keep going.{w} It's a restricted area, and I doubt Ashiya will be understanding even if our circumstances require this.
entries.new: 也许会。我是在劝你们别再往前了。{w} 那是禁区，就算我们是迫不得已，恐怕芦屋也不会通融。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Sai, who was in front, continued up the stairs.
entries.new: 走在最前面的 Sai 继续拾级而上。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The rest of us followed him and quickly reached the top of the short staircase, where we found another door at our left.
entries.new: 我们跟在后面，很快走完了这段不长的楼梯，在左侧又看到一扇门。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The space above wasn't large enough for all of us, so Erina and Isla could barely see the door. Sai grabbed the aged handle and realized that it was slightly open. Finally, he pushed open the last barrier preventing us from seeing what we were up against.
entries.new: 最终，他推开最后一道屏障，我们终于看清了要面对的东西。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A rusty creak rang out as the door slowly opened. Sai had to put unusual strength into it—the door kept getting stuck on the floor. Once he'd won that battle, I was able to see inside.
entries.new: 门缓缓打开，发出一声生锈的吱呀。Sai 不得不用上格外大的力气——门底老是卡在地板上。等他把门推开，我终于看清了里面。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Condemned
entries.new: 定罪

entries.text: It looked like an old living room, and not at all Japanese-styled. A sofa with a suitcase on it quickly came into view, along with a few lights hanging from the ceiling. I could see two more doors in the corner of the room, and as I thoroughly inspected it, I questioned why Sai hadn't yet moved.
entries.new: 那看起来像一间老旧的客厅，全然不是日式风格。一张放着行李箱的沙发很快映入眼帘，天花板上还吊着几盏灯。房间角落里另有两扇门。我仔细打量着四周，心里纳闷 Sai 怎么还没动。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Wait up. Look at the floor.
entries.new: ……等等。看地板。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I took it as if he'd been talking to me because I was the one with the best view. As soon as he pointed it out, I understood what he was looking at.
entries.new: 我站的位置看得最清楚，便以为他在对我说话。他这一提醒，我立刻明白他在看什么了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was someone here...
entries.new: 这里有人来过……
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What?
entries.new: 什么？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Yeah, there are footprints on the floor. Someone must've been here.
entries.new: 是啊，地板上有脚印。肯定有人来过。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: The entire floor was covered by a blue carpet, and any steps someone took on it would remain visible thanks to its thickness. Over time, they would become harder and harder to discern until they disappeared altogether. It was definite proof that someone had walked around there recently.
entries.new: 整片地面铺着蓝色地毯，地毯很厚，踩上去的脚印会一直留着。随着时间推移，痕迹会越来越淡，直至彻底消失。这足以证明，不久前有人在这里走动过。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yeah, someone must have been here. Sure. This is exactly why we couldn't find the person we were looking for. The second Naomi didn't have a keyring, so it's very possible they still have easy access to this place. That isn't exactly what I meant, though.
entries.new: 是啊，肯定有人来过。没错。我们找不到要找的人，原因就在这里。第二个 Naomi 身上没有钥匙圈，所以她很可能仍能随意进出这里。不过我想说的并不完全是这个。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Huh?
entries.new: 嗯？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Don't you see it? These footprints don't make sense. Nobody could've entered through this door.
entries.new: 你们没看出来吗？这些脚印说不通。不可能有人从这扇门进来。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It took me a moment to see why he'd said that since there were footprints right next to the door. The key to that statement was their origin.
entries.new: 门口明明就有脚印，我愣了一下才明白他为什么这么说。关键在于脚印的起点。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait, you're right... How did this happen?
entries.new: 等等，你说得对……这是怎么回事？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Against the wall before us was a red sofa. In front of it, the footprints began and walked up to the door Sai had opened. From there, they headed toward another door.
entries.new: 我们面前的墙边摆着一张红色沙发。脚印从沙发前开始，一直延伸到 Sai 打开的那扇门，随后又朝另一扇门去了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'm not sure what to gather from this, but once we enter, these footprints will fade away and merge with ours, so let's not disrupt the rightmost part of the room yet.
entries.new: 这能说明什么，我还不确定，但我们一进去，这些脚印就会淡去、和我们的混在一起，所以房间最右边那块先别碰。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Once Sai entered, I was free to do so as well, and the people behind me all slowly made their way into what seemed to be the living room.
entries.new: Sai 进去之后，我才跟着踏进去，身后的人也一个个慢慢走进了这间像是客厅的房间。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Next to the sofa was a modest table, and in front of it a shelf supporting an old but large CRT television.
entries.new: 沙发旁摆着一张不大的桌子，桌前是一个架子，上面搁着一台老旧而宽大的显像管电视。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the hell is this doing here...?
entries.new: 这东西怎么会在这儿……？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: He was talking about the suitcase. It looked like the one he'd taken from hallway C minutes prior, and it couldn't have somehow moved to the attic ahead of us since we hadn't heard the elevator. It had to be an entirely different suitcase.
entries.new: 他说的是那只手提箱。它看起来和他几分钟前从 C走廊拿走的那只一模一样。我们没听见电梯的动静，它不可能先一步跑到阁楼来，所以那必定是另一只手提箱。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's empty too, and it looks like the one downstairs. It's exactly the same suitcase.
entries.new: 里面也是空的，而且和楼下那只长得一样。根本就是同一只手提箱。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The same one, literally? Or do you mean the same model?
entries.new: 同一只，还是同一款？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Probably the same model, but honestly, I can't be sure. Naomi's body appeared twice, so this could still be the exact same suitcase depending on what happened.
entries.new: 大概是同一款吧，但说实话，我也说不准。Naomi 的尸体都出现过两次，所以视情况而定，这也可能真的是同一只。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Huh, look. It also has faint traces of smoke...
entries.new: 咦，你看，这上面也有淡淡的烟熏痕迹……
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Do they not belong to people who work here, Katei? There's no way two of these were snuck into the tower, right?
entries.new: Katei，这些难道不是在这里工作的人的东西吗？总不可能有两只这样的箱子被偷偷带进塔里吧？
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Three, in fact. One more was being carried by the person holding the stolen gemstones. And no, I don't recognize it at all.{w} More importantly, what is it doing here?
entries.new: 其实有三只。还有一只由那个拿着失窃宝石的人提着。而且，我完全不认识它。{w} 更要紧的是，它怎么会在这儿？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I looked around me. There were no visible security cameras, and I recalled that I hadn't seen the living room through the monitors. I was sure that one of us would've noticed the suitcase otherwise, and maybe even the person who had been hiding.
entries.new: 我环顾四周。看不到任何监控摄像头，而我也想起，之前在监视器画面上从没见过这间客厅。否则，我们之中总有人会注意到这只手提箱，说不定还会看到那个藏起来的人。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}Honestly, I have no idea. I'm not sure why they'd bring this here, no matter what its contents were. If they wanted to leave it behind, they could've done so downstairs, which is what we thought they did.
entries.new: ……{w}说实话，我完全想不通。不管里面装的是什么，我都想不出他们为什么要把这东西带上来。要是想丢下它，在楼下丢掉就行——我们本来也是这么以为的。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Right. What's the point of leaving one on the crystal floor and another one here?
entries.new: 是啊。一只丢在水晶层，一只放这儿，有什么意义？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Whatever it is, it's less strange than the footprints we've walked over. Atsuki and Shiroya realized it.
entries.new: 不管怎么说，这都比我们踩过的那串脚印正常。Atsuki 和 Shiroya 也发现了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The footprints started right in front of the suitcase, moved toward the staircase, and then to that door over there. What's past it?
entries.new: 脚印从手提箱正前方开始，朝楼梯那边去，然后到那边那扇门。门后是什么？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That door leads to the hallway. From there, you can access the elevator and the bedrooms. The other door you see leads to the kitchen, which is also connected to the hallway.
entries.new: 那扇门通向走廊，从那里能到电梯和卧室。你看到的另一扇门通向厨房，厨房也和走廊相连。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: But I see what you mean. If no more footprints exist, they couldn't begin by the sofa.
entries.new: 不过我明白你的意思。要是没有别的脚印，那它们就不可能从沙发那儿开始。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Well, no, they could. If someone spent a few hours on the sofa, the next time they walked around, their previous footprints would've faded away, so it would look as if the starting point was the sofa itself.
entries.new: 不，也不是不可能。如果有人在这沙发上待了几个小时，等他再走动时，之前的脚印早就淡掉了，看上去就好像起点是沙发本身。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: They could've also come from the kitchen, but they must've jumped onto the sofa to avoid leaving footprints, which sounds insane.
entries.new: 他也可能是从厨房过来的，但那样就得跳到沙发上，免得留下脚印——这听着也太荒唐了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai, careful not to step on the preexisting footprints, opened the door to the kitchen.
entries.new: Sai 小心翼翼地避开原先那些脚印，推开了通往厨房的门。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The floor here is different, so we won't be able to know if anyone came from the kitchen. Now, should we check everyone's shoes?
entries.new: 这里的地板不一样，所以没法判断有没有人从厨房过来。那么，要不要检查一下每个人的鞋？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What...?
entries.new: 什么……？
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Why do you think I preserved a few of these? Naturally, to check if one of us has been here already. Naomi's killer would've had a way in with the same key we used or the one that the other Naomi might've had.
entries.new: 你以为我为什么特意留着这几个脚印？当然是为了确认我们之中有没有人早就来过这里。杀害 Naomi 的凶手，可以用我们手里的钥匙进来，也可以用另一个 Naomi 可能有的那把。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: These are barely recognizable, though. We might not be able to compare them well.
entries.new: 可这些脚印几乎看不出形状了，恐怕很难比对。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That's fine. The size itself should be enough. ...Strangely, nobody should've been able to enter this place through the stairs we just came from because no footprints start there.
entries.new: 没关系，光看大小就够了。……奇怪的是，按理说没人能顺着我们刚走的那道楼梯进来，因为那里没有脚印的起点。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai opened the remaining door.
entries.new: Sai 打开了剩下的那扇门。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Look, this hallway has a wooden floor too, and I can see the elevator right there. Using that, anyone could've come up here with the key.
entries.new: 你看，这条走廊也是木地板，电梯就在那儿。只要有钥匙，谁都能乘电梯上来。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That sounded right. Our own footprints were still very much visible, so they wouldn't fade immediately. The door had gotten stuck on the floor when Sai tried to open it, and the markings from that were still on the carpet. However, we had no way to tell if it had been opened earlier.
entries.new: 这话有道理。我们自己留下的脚印还清晰可见，说明它们不会马上消失。Sai 推门时门曾卡在地板上，地毯上还留着那道痕迹。但那扇门之前有没有被打开过，我们无从判断。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was no way to jump to the sofa from the staircase, so accepting Sai's claim was reasonable. I looked up to see if I could notice a ceiling opening to drop from, but I didn't spot anything.
entries.new: 从楼梯那儿不可能跳到沙发上，所以接受 Sai 的说法也合理。我抬头看了看，想看看天花板上有没有能让人下来的开口，却什么也没发现。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Before I agreed with him fully, it was important to remember that we were likely up against someone cunning who was trying to mislead us while avoiding detection. Like Akaro said before he disappeared, it felt as if they had been taunting us at times.
entries.new: 但在完全认同他之前，有一点不能忘：我们的对手很可能十分狡猾，一面隐藏自己，一面设法误导我们。就像 Akaro 消失前说的那样，有时感觉对方简直是在戏弄我们。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If their intention was to play with our reasoning again, they could have intentionally made us think that the main door was unused and the elevator was the only method of entering.
entries.new: 如果对方又打算玩弄我们的推理，那他们完全可以故意让我们以为正门没人用过，电梯是唯一能进来的途径。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The key behind that was the state of the footprints. They'd clearly been there for a while, so it wasn't simple to determine the way they were facing. Even though we'd all interpreted the sofa to be the starting point, that wasn't guaranteed to be the case.
entries.new: 关键就在于脚印的状态。它们显然已经存在了一段时间，所以很难辨清朝向。尽管我们都把沙发当成了起点，可事实未必如此。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: To trick us, the culprit could've purposely walked from the door to the sofa. From there, making it to the kitchen without stepping on the floor again seemed easy, and they could've gone around the room through the hallway, then exited through the main door.
entries.new: 为了误导我们，凶手完全可以故意从门口走到沙发。到了那里，再进厨房似乎也不难做到不踩地板；之后还可以经由走廊绕行，从正门离开。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It sounded excessive, and it implied they'd left the suitcase there so that we would find it, but we still had to ask ourselves an important question: why would someone leave the key to the attic in Naomi's pocket when the Sekimeiya cabinet key was removed?
entries.new: 这听起来太过刻意，还意味着他们是故意把手提箱放在那儿让我们发现的。但我们仍得问自己一个重要的问题：既然 Sekimeiya 展示柜的钥匙被取走了，为什么会有人把阁楼的钥匙留在 Naomi 的口袋里？
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If they had known that we were going to look at the room, they might've prepared something like that. But I couldn't identify the goal of it, because the idea that they hadn't come from the main door didn't seem to contradict anything yet.
entries.new: 如果他们早就知道我们会来查看这个房间，或许就会做这种准备。可我推不出这样做的目的，因为「对方不是从正门进来的」这一设想，眼下似乎还不跟任何事实冲突。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}The more I stared at the footprints, the more I doubted whether they were facing the way I was thinking. I wasn't sure anymore, but I was confident that only one pair of shoes had left them.
entries.new: ……{w}脚印看得越久，我越怀疑它们的朝向是不是跟我想的一样。我已经拿不准了，但有一点我可以肯定：留下它们的只有一双鞋。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If they were backwards, there were more arrangements. Perhaps they entered from the staircase, went to the hallway to take the elevator down, and quickly returned from the staircase so they could walk over to the sofa.
entries.new: 如果方向是反的，那还有更多走法。也许对方从楼梯进来，去走廊乘电梯下楼，又很快从楼梯折返，好走到沙发那边。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Well, are you gonna show me your shoes, or do I need to compare your footprints?
entries.new: 那么，你是打算把鞋给我看，还是要我亲自比对脚印？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Look, mine are a little bigger, see? It's very simple.
entries.new: 看，我的鞋要大一些，看到了吧？很简单。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Fine, here. I know you're still suspecting me, but you must admit that mine are also considerably larger.
entries.new: 好，给你。我知道你还在怀疑我，但你得承认，我的鞋也大得多。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Hm...{w} Who did you steal those from?
entries.new: 嗯……{w}你这是从谁那儿偷来的？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'm not used to ruling you out so quickly. That's all.
entries.new: 我只是不习惯这么快就把你排除在外，仅此而已。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Unfortunately, we can't really look at Akaro's for the moment, but I'm sure they'd be bigger too.
entries.new: 可惜眼下没法查看 Akaro 的鞋，不过我敢肯定，他的也更大。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Anyway, Atsuki, you're next on the suspect list.
entries.new: 总之，Atsuki，下一个就轮到你了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: And I just let you know about the attic key?
entries.new: 而我刚刚才把阁楼钥匙的事告诉你？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Just show me your shoes. I'm pretty lost when it comes to the intentions of the culprit, anyway.
entries.new: 先把鞋给我看吧。反正凶手的意图，我到现在也没摸清。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He looked at them, and once again, there was no match.
entries.new: 他看了看，结果还是一样，对不上。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya?
entries.new: Shiroya？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: She left a footprint, and Sai looked at it for a few seconds with a conspicuous frown on his face.
entries.new: 她留下了一个脚印。Sai 盯着它看了几秒，眉头明显皱了起来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yours are awfully close, but I can't say for sure they're the same. The size is at least very similar.
entries.new: 你的鞋印和它非常接近，但我不能断言就是同一双。至少尺寸十分相近。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...So what? Are you gonna move me above Atsuki on your list?
entries.new: ……所以呢？你是打算在名单上把我挪到 Atsuki 前面去？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: This might give you enough points for that, but I'll admit I was only hoping for Katei's shoes to match. That would've meant a lot more than your size coinciding.
entries.new: 这或许能让你嫌疑大增，不过老实说，我本来只盼着能对上 Katei 的鞋。那可比你的尺码吻合更能说明问题。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Anyway, Erina, mind playing along too?
entries.new: 总之，Erina，你也来配合一下好吗？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You can see mine are slightly bigger too.
entries.new: 你也看得出来，我的也稍大一点。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: You're right. Let's see if we can find something else, then.
entries.new: 说得对。那我们再找找别的线索。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Are you not gonna look at mine?
entries.new: 你不看看我的吗？
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Oh... sure. Isla, do you understand what'll happen to you if your shoes match?
entries.new: 哦……当然。Isla，你明白要是你的鞋对上了，会有什么后果吗？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Don't worry. They're not even close.
entries.new: 别担心。差得远呢。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That's what I thought.
entries.new: 我就知道。
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Sai moved to the television and tried to power it on.{w} Nothing happened.
entries.new: Sai 走到电视机前，试着开机。{w}什么反应也没有。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I guess this is broken, seeing as it's plugged in.{w} ...Anyway, let's look around the area.
entries.new: 插着电却开不了，看来是坏了。{w}……算了，我们在这一带看看。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We started with the kitchen. It had an empty refrigerator, an oven, and some compartments to store food that no longer contained anything but dust.
entries.new: 我们先从厨房查起。里面有一台空冰箱、一只烤箱，还有几个储物格，如今除了灰尘，什么也没剩下。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Next, we all stepped over to the hallway. The floor was a little creaky, and the walls were beige. Everything about the place was old, but it was still well-preserved.
entries.new: 接着我们一起走到走廊。地板踩上去有些吱呀作响，墙壁是米色的。这里的一切都上了年头，却仍保存得相当完好。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This room used to serve as a storeroom, but it's empty now, and it seems the ceiling light stopped working. Pressing the switch isn't doing anything.
entries.new: 这间原本是储藏室，现在已经空了，顶灯似乎也坏了。按开关没有任何反应。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Hm...
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We ignored the elevator and began to look through the other rooms. According to Katei, the two doors farthest back led to bedrooms.
entries.new: 我们没去管电梯，开始查看其余房间。据 Katei 说，最里面的两扇门通向卧室。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There's a second floor?
entries.new: 还有一层？
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Inside the spacious bedroom, Isla noticed a ladder that led to a room above us. However, we should've already been on the highest floor.
entries.new: 宽敞的卧室里，Isla 发现一架梯子，通往我们头顶的房间。可我们按理已经身处最高一层了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, not quite. Back then, when this was a residence, it's true that the house had two floors. The second one wasn't fully preserved when the building was expanded, but as you can see, remnants are still present in these bedrooms.
entries.new: 哦，也不尽然。当年这里还是住宅的时候，这栋房子确实有两层。后来扩建时，二层并没有完整保留下来，不过如你所见，这些卧室里还留着它的痕迹。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Oh... What's up there, then?
entries.new: 哦……那上面是什么？
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Another bedroom like this one. These were used as double rooms back in the day, so Ashiya specified that the higher ones shouldn't be demolished.
entries.new: 和这间一样的另一间卧室。当年这里是双人房，所以芦屋特别交代过，楼上那几间不能拆。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I sat on the bed, still pretty tired from not sleeping the night before. It wasn't really comfortable due to how long it had gone unused, but the sheets made it look like it was still maintained daily.
entries.new: 我在床上坐下。前一晚没睡，我仍觉得相当疲惫。床因为闲置太久并不舒服，可那床单却让人以为它每天都有人打理。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stood up as soon as I noticed a security camera recording me. I definitely recalled seeing the bedroom through the monitors.
entries.new: 一发现监控摄像头正对着我，我立刻站了起来。我确实记得在监视器里见过这间卧室。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya, Isla, and I went up to the second level of the bedroom. Like Katei said, it was similar, and there were only two beds and a closet. I opened it, given that we were still looking for Akaro, but it only contained a few articles of clothing.
entries.new: 我、Shiroya 和 Isla 爬上卧室的二层。正如 Katei 所说，那里与下面相仿，只有两张床和一个衣柜。我们还在找 Akaro，我便打开了衣柜，里面只有几件衣服。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We went back down. Another door was in front of the bedroom.
entries.new: 我们回到下面。卧室正前方还有另一扇门。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It led to a mirrored version of the bedroom I'd seen, and it also had a ladder.
entries.new: 门后是与刚才那间卧室格局对称的另一间，同样有一架梯子。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Above, nothing was different. There were effectively four bedrooms on the floor.
entries.new: 上面别无二致。这一层实际共有四间卧室。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The final area was the bathroom. It had a shower, a shelf, and a modest carpet on the floor. It was bigger and fancier than the ones below, but the door didn't have a locking mechanism.
entries.new: 最后是浴室。里面有淋浴、一个架子，地上铺着一块不大的地毯。它比楼下的浴室更大、更讲究，门却没有锁。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The entire floor had a simple layout. According to Katei, the household used to be quite bigger in the past, but not much of that remained.
entries.new: 整层格局十分简单。据 Katei 说，这户人家从前要大得多，但留存下来的已经不多。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In addition, the hallway wasn't as long as the ones downstairs, meaning that the attic didn't make use of the whole space the large building provided, probably because it had been significantly expanded at one point.
entries.new: 此外，这条走廊不如楼下的长，也就是说，阁楼并没有占满这栋大楼的整个空间——多半是因为它曾在某一时期大幅扩建过。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We'd looked through every room while someone always remained in the hallway, so we'd determined that we were alone. Once we were done, Sai called us from the elevator.
entries.new: 我们查遍了每个房间，全程都有人守在走廊，因此确定这里没有别人。查完后，Sai 在电梯那边叫我们。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There are light switches everywhere, but every light was turned on. Is that normal?
entries.new: 到处都是电灯开关，可每盏灯都亮着。这正常吗？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yes, it doesn't mean anyone turned them on separately. The lights turn off automatically at night, and every morning we manually turn them all on at once, including the attic's. That's why the office floors were lit up as well.
entries.new: 正常，这并不代表有人一盏盏开过。灯在夜里会自动熄灭，每天早晨我们会手动把它们全部打开，阁楼的灯也一样。所以办公楼层同样亮着。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: That sounds like a huge waste.
entries.new: 听起来太浪费了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Katei nodded but stayed in the hallway's bend so that nobody could enter without him seeing. We realized Sai had called the elevator as soon as we saw the button lighting up.
entries.new: Katei 点了点头，仍守在走廊拐角，任何人进来都逃不过他的眼睛。我们看到按钮亮起，才意识到 Sai 已经按了电梯。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: All right, so we haven't found anyone. That's fair. As we said earlier, we now need to make sure to thoroughly inspect every floor, so we'll leave the elevator here and disable it by keeping the door open.
entries.new: 好，看来我们没找到人。行吧。就像刚才说的，接下来每一层都必须彻底查一遍，所以电梯就停在这儿，让门一直开着，这样它就没法运行了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Just like he'd done downstairs, he held it with his hands so that it wouldn't close. Once he let go of it, the door didn't have the force to close itself and remained stationary.
entries.new: 就像在楼下那样，他用双手扶住门，不让它关上。松手之后，门并没有自行合拢的力道，就那样停着不动了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If we make it all the way down without finding anyone, we'll have to consider some pretty outlandish things. Until then, we have to expect to at least find Akaro.
entries.new: 要是我们一路查到最下面还是没找到人，那就得考虑些相当离谱的可能了。在那之前，我们至少得指望能找到 Akaro。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We entered the living room. Sai and Katei went through the kitchen, as it was the last place anyone could've hoped to sneak in.
entries.new: 我们回到客厅。Sai 和 Katei 去查了厨房，因为那是谁想溜进来唯一还可能藏身的地方。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...What does this look like to you guys?
entries.new: ……你们看这个像什么？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I stopped them without giving them context. They weren't sure what I was referring to, so I made it clearer.
entries.new: 我叫住他们，却没说明缘由。他们不清楚我指的是什么，我便说得更明白些。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The footprints, I mean. They can look like an impossibility, but there's a simple explanation for them, right?
entries.new: 我是说那些脚印。它们看上去像是绝无可能，但其实有简单的解释，对吧？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Teleportation?
entries.new: 传送？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...Yes. Earlier, I did consider our mystery culprit teleporting to the attic. If they appeared next to the sofa, that'd be the natural beginning of their footprints.
entries.new: ……对。刚才我确实考虑过，那个神秘的真凶是传送进阁楼的。如果人就出现在沙发旁，那自然会成为脚印的起点。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Here's something else: these footprints probably belong to a woman. What's your shoe size, Shiroya?
entries.new: 还有一点：这些脚印多半属于一个女人。Shiroya，你穿多大码的鞋？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: And the only other person we know who could have a similar shoe size is Naomi. Furthermore, we found two Naomis, and on the sofa, where she would've teleported to, there's a suitcase that we've also seen before.
entries.new: 而另一个我们认识、可能穿相近鞋码的人，就是 Naomi。况且，我们遇到了两个 Naomi；在她本该传送到的沙发上，还放着一只我们之前也见过的手提箱。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: See? This is what I told you guys earlier. Naomi had the suitcase from the beginning. Once she teleported or time traveled to this living room, the suitcase was replicated and she must've left it here.
entries.new: 看吧？我早说过了。Naomi 从一开始就拿着手提箱。她传送或者穿越时间来到这间客厅之后，手提箱就被复制了一份，她一定是把它留在了这里。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Oh, are you just gung-ho about time travel now? You were ridiculing Atsuki for it earlier.
entries.new: 哦？你现在倒对时间穿越这么起劲了？刚才你还拿这个嘲笑 Atsuki 呢。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Well, it's become clear that something strange is going on. These footprints are even further proof.
entries.new: 事到如今，明摆着有古怪。这些脚印就是进一步的证据。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: If this is what happened, Naomi must've traveled here while she was holding the suitcase—before we found it on the crystal floor. That would mean two Naomis have existed for quite a while, and that not only did we miss both of them, they were also killed.{w} And let me tell you, there are some pesky contradictions down that line of thought. First, during the time Naomi could've been holding the suitcase, the Sekimeiya was in its cabinet. It wasn't locked inside, but we touched it and nothing happened to us. If that's how she time traveled up here, it again begs the question of why it worked for her.
entries.new: 如果真是这样，那 Naomi 一定是拿着手提箱穿越到了这里——在我们于水晶层发现它之前。也就是说，有两个 Naomi 同时存在了相当长一段时间，而我们不仅两个都没撞见，她们还都被杀了。{w} 不过我得说，这条思路上有几个挺麻烦的矛盾。第一，在 Naomi 可能拿着手提箱的那段时间里，Sekimeiya 一直在展示柜里。柜子并没有上锁，可我们碰过它，什么也没发生。如果她就是那样穿越上来的，那问题又回来了：为什么偏偏对她起了作用？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Honestly, I assumed that being outside the cabinet without refrigeration was what made the Sekimeiya transport Atsuki into the past. However, the fact that we found the Sekimeiya still in its cabinet minutes before seeing that suitcase might imply that was wrong.
entries.new: 说实话，我原本以为，是离开展示柜又没有冷藏，才让 Sekimeiya 把 Atsuki 送回了过去。但我们看到那只手提箱的几分钟前，Sekimeiya 还好好待在展示柜里——这一点恐怕说明我想错了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'm not wrong, right? If Naomi touched it while it was out of the cabinet, we would've found it outside.{w} The next contradiction is what we talked about earlier: Naomi would've disappeared upon traveling, so we couldn't have found her corpse and the suitcase twice.
entries.new: 我没说错吧？如果 Naomi 是在它离开展示柜的时候碰了它，那我们本该在柜外发现它。{w} 下一个矛盾就是我们之前谈过的：Naomi 一穿越就会消失，那她的尸体和手提箱就不可能被我们发现两次。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I get what you're saying regarding the Sekimeiya, but after traveling back, she could've gone downstairs to pick it up from the floor. She would've known where she'd traveled from, so she could've returned it to the cabinet.
entries.new: Sekimeiya 那部分我听明白了。可她穿越回来之后，可以下楼把它从地上捡起来。她应该知道自己是从哪儿穿越过去的，自然也就能把它放回展示柜。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Incorrect, I think.{w} Remember what Katei said after we got the Sekimeiya out of the cabinet?
entries.new: 我觉得不对。{w} 你还记得我们把 Sekimeiya 从展示柜里拿出来之后，Katei 说了什么吗？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...What did I say?
entries.new: ……我说什么了？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: That you restored power to the elevator. According to you, the alarm disabled it.
entries.new: 你说你把电梯的电源恢复了。按你的说法，是警报让电梯停下的。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Oh, right. I got it running again after I stopped trying to understand what caused the power outage.
entries.new: 哦，对。我不再去琢磨停电是怎么回事之后，就把它重新弄好了。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I see, so Naomi couldn't have used the elevator before we saw the Sekimeiya in the cabinet, and right after that, we saw the suitcase in hallway C, which probably means that Naomi would've already traveled.
entries.new: 原来如此。也就是说，在我们看到 Sekimeiya 还留在展示柜里之前，Naomi 用不了电梯；而紧接着，我们就在 C走廊看到了手提箱。这么说来，那时的 Naomi 应该已经穿越过了。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What? She could've just left through the staircase.
entries.new: 什么？她走楼梯出去不就行了。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: No, I don't think so. It's likely that the first time we heard the elevator moving down, Naomi used it from here. There's still no other explanation for that, and there's something else that makes me think she couldn't have exited through the door. That's the last contradiction I can point out.
entries.new: 不，我看不是。我们第一次听见电梯往下走，多半就是 Naomi 从这里坐的。这件事至今没有别的解释。而且还有一点让我觉得她没法从门口出去——这是我能指出的最后一个矛盾。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: When Naomi traveled with the suitcase, it's very safe to assume she also had her keys. She had them before the smoke appeared and when we found her first corpse. Her cabinet key had been removed, but that probably only happened after she was killed.
entries.new: Naomi 带着手提箱穿越的时候，几乎可以肯定钥匙也在她身上。烟雾出现之前她带着钥匙，我们第一次发现她尸体时钥匙也在。她的展示柜钥匙被取走了，但那多半是她死后的事。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Now recall the footprints we found here. They start next to the sofa, go over to the staircase, then toward the hallway door.
entries.new: 再想想我们在这儿找到的脚印：从沙发旁边开始，走向楼梯，然后折向走廊的门。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Oh, so Naomi's first movements after appearing would've been to try leaving through the staircase.
entries.new: 哦，所以 Naomi 出现之后，第一反应就是试着从楼梯离开。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Exactly. And despite that, she went back to the hallway. The reasonable explanation is that she didn't have the key to get out.
entries.new: 正是。可即便如此，她还是回到了走廊。合理的解释只有一个：她没有能出去的钥匙。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Then why would she go to the door?
entries.new: 那她为什么还要去门口？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: To try opening it? Maybe she thought she still had her keys, but when she went down the stairs and was about to take them out, she realized she didn't have them. Her only way out was through the elevator, so she came back up and went to the hallway. Eventually, she must've used it when the power came back.
entries.new: 想试着开门吧？也许她以为自己还带着钥匙，可下了楼梯正要掏的时候，才发现钥匙不在身上。她唯一的出路就是电梯，于是又折回来去了走廊。最后来电的时候，她一定是坐电梯下去了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Since the footprints are all similar, there's only one other explanation that makes sense to me: she had the key and exited the room. Either before or after all this, she entered the attic again and went straight to the hallway.{w} But the footprints were all in similar condition, so there must not have been a lot of time between them. I'm not sure why she'd enter again only to use the elevator and go down. ...If she didn't want to be noticed, the elevator noise wouldn't do her any favors.
entries.new: 既然这些脚印的状况都差不多，那在我看来，就只剩下一种说得通的解释：她带着钥匙，离开了房间。在这之前或之后，她又进了阁楼，径直走向走廊。{w} 可所有脚印的新旧都相差无几，说明中间隔的时间并不长。我不明白她为什么又进来一趟，只为坐电梯下楼。……如果她不想被人发现，电梯的动静可帮不上她半点忙。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: She thought she'd have her keys, then...? Maybe she didn't know that much about the Sekimeiya even though she used it so early on.{w} I think that makes the most sense. She would be the second Naomi we found. I still don't understand how we missed her if she was the one who took the elevator down, or who killed her, but the truth is that we didn't find any keys on her body.
entries.new: 她以为自己还带着钥匙，结果……？也许她虽然很早就用上了 Sekimeiya，对它却了解不多。{w} 我觉得这样最说得通。她就是我们发现的那个第二个 Naomi。如果坐电梯下楼的是她、杀她的也是那个人，我到现在还是想不通我们怎么会漏掉；但事实就是，她身上没有钥匙。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: And the person who killed her didn't remove them the first time, so they wouldn't have cared if the second Naomi had them either.
entries.new: 而第一次杀她的人并没有拿走钥匙，所以第二个 Naomi 身上有没有钥匙，对方也不会在意。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: The footprints painted a clear picture: she thought she had keys she didn't have. Was that due to the travel itself, or had she lost them beforehand?
entries.new: 脚印把事情的轮廓勾勒得很清楚：她以为自己带着钥匙，其实并没有。这是穿越本身造成的，还是她在那之前就已经把钥匙弄丢了？
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Let's head back down for now. When we get to the crystal floor, we'll know if the footprints could've belonged to her. If not, Shiroya's gonna have to move up a few spots on the naughty list.
entries.new: 先下楼吧。到了水晶层，就能知道那些脚印是不是她的。如果不是，Shiroya 在嫌疑人名单上的排名可就要往前挪几位了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: There was no point in arguing that, so we made our way to the sixth floor. Through normal means, there was no way anyone could still be in the attic, so we didn't have to worry about the elevator for once.
entries.new: 争下去也没有意义，我们便动身前往六楼。按常理，阁楼里不可能还有人，所以我们难得不必再为电梯提心吊胆。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We followed an exceedingly simple plan: Erina and Isla remained outside the office partitions while the rest of us looked through them. Only one person was needed for that, but by grouping up, we avoided picking one single person to do the important and potentially dangerous job.
entries.new: 我们照着一个再简单不过的方案行事：Erina 和 Isla 守在办公隔间外面，其余人进去逐一查看。这活儿本来一个人就够了，但大家结伴行动，就不必单挑出某个人去承担这件重要又可能危险的事。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Afterward, we inspected the bathrooms. Opening the doors was enough to determine they were desolate, but we remained on high alert after what we'd found in the crystal floor's bathroom.
entries.new: 之后我们去查看洗手间。门一开就足以确认里面空无一人，但有了水晶层洗手间里的发现，我们仍旧不敢松懈。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When we finished with floor 6, we were sure that nobody else was on the two highest floors, so we went down to repeat the process.
entries.new: 六楼查完，我们已经能确定最高的两层没有别人，于是下楼重复同样的流程。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The fifth floor wasn't any different. Even though we believed that Akaro and whoever the culprit was had to be somewhere in the tower, they would never remain on an office floor if they intended to hide.{w} Since we knew that, the most important reason why we were following that procedure was to isolate the crystal floor and be able to thoroughly look there once again.
entries.new: 五楼也没什么两样。尽管我们相信 Akaro 和真凶一定还在塔里的某处，可他们若想藏身，绝不会留在办公楼层。{w} 正因为如此，我们走这套流程最重要的目的，是把水晶层孤立出来，好在那里再彻底搜查一遍。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As the search of the fourth floor was completed without an issue, I wondered again what might've happened to Akaro. Even if he'd been able to travel through time, it wouldn't have made things much different, since that would mean we'd failed to spot the extra Akaro at some point.
entries.new: 四楼的搜查也顺利结束，我却又一次琢磨起 Akaro 究竟出了什么事。就算他真能穿越时间，局面也不会有太大不同——那意味着我们在某个时刻漏看了多出来的那个 Akaro。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Of course, that was assuming he'd undergone a similar experience to mine. If he'd traveled much farther into the past or appeared outside the tower, we'd be unable to find him again. Maybe we'd find him outside once the shutter retracted, but we couldn't think about that until our search ended with no results.
entries.new: 当然，这得假设他经历的事和我类似。要是他被送去了更遥远的过去，或者出现在塔外，我们就再也找不到他了。也许等卷帘门升起后，我们能在外面找到他——但在搜查一无所获之前，还轮不到考虑这些。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We hadn't found traces of a single person as we stepped on the last set of stairs, and unless we wanted to toss in the possibility of someone recently teleporting upstairs, nobody could've remained anywhere but on the crystal floor. There was no point in considering that Erina and Isla could've let the culprit pass deliberately, so we put our full focus on the final floor.
entries.new: 踏上最后一段楼梯时，我们连一个人的踪迹都没发现。除非要把「有人刚刚传送到楼上」这种可能也算进去，否则除了水晶层，哪里都不可能还藏着人。怀疑 Erina 和 Isla 故意放走真凶也没有意义，于是我们把全部注意力放在了最后一层。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You two stay here again. We'll do this quickly.
entries.new: 你们两个还是留在这里。我们速战速决。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: We were about to begin when something caught our attention. From where we were, we could see that the door to the men's bathroom was slightly open.
entries.new: 我们正要开始，某样东西却吸引了注意。从我们站的位置，能看见男洗手间的门微微开着。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did we leave it like that...?
entries.new: 我们走的时候，门是开着的吗……？
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: The rest of us weren't sure either, but we'd all felt something was off. We still instructed Erina and Isla to stay next to the stairs and approached the bathroom with caution.
entries.new: 剩下的人也都拿不准，但大家都察觉到不对劲。我们还是让 Erina 和 Isla 守在楼梯旁，自己则小心地靠近洗手间。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As soon as we peeked inside, we knew we'd been right: the door had been opened farther. Next to Naomi's body was the toilet, and on top of it, Akaro sat, focusing his gaze on the wall in front of him.{w} When he noticed us, he slowly turned his head to the door and stood up.
entries.new: 我们往里一探，就知道果然没错：门被推得更开了。Naomi 的尸体旁边是马桶，Akaro 就坐在上面，目光直直盯着面前的墙。{w} 察觉到我们，他缓缓把头转向门口，站了起来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Akaro? What are you doing?
entries.new: ……Akaro？你在做什么？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: By which she means, where the fuck did you go?
entries.new: 她的意思是，你他妈到底跑哪儿去了？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...{w}He barely reacted to our presence.{w} ...He slowly turned his head again and spent a few seconds in silence until he acknowledged us.
entries.new: ……{w}他对我们的到来几乎没有反应。{w}……他又缓缓转过头，沉默了几秒，才像是终于认出了我们。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hey. I have a question...
entries.new: 喂。我有个问题……
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: He took a bit of time to stand up. Maintaining a plain expression and breathing deeply, seemingly to calm his nerves, he spoke.
entries.new: 他花了一会儿才站起来。他脸上没什么表情，深深吸了口气，像是在平复心绪，然后开口。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai, you had a wristwatch, right? What... time is it?
entries.new: Sai，你带着手表吧？现在……几点了？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: What?{w} It's {time=11:36.}
entries.new: 什么？{w} 现在是 {time=11:36.}。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: {time=11:36.} So it had been sixteen minutes since we'd heard the noise in the event room. It felt like more time had passed since the contents of those minutes had been dense, but it didn't seem wrong.
entries.new: {time=11:36.} 也就是说，从我们听到活动室传来声响起，已经过了十六分钟。那段时间里发生的事太多，感觉上不止过了这么久，但细想也并不矛盾。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: {time=11:36}, I see. Of course, it appears you were wrong, Atsuki. We didn't travel through time...
entries.new: {time=11:36}，原来如此。看来你确实弄错了，Atsuki。我们并没有时间穿越……
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: "We"? Did you travel too?
entries.new: 你说的「我们」？你也穿越了？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: No, I just said I didn't. I think... we just hallucinated or something...
entries.new: 不，我刚说了没有。我想……我们只是产生了幻觉之类的吧……
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Oh...! Akaro, where were you?
entries.new: 啊……！Akaro，你刚才在哪儿？
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: We were looking for you.
entries.new: 我们刚才一直在找你。
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Erina and Isla came to us once they realized we'd found something. From where we were, we could still see the stairs, so if someone went up, we'd at least spot them.
entries.new: Erina 和 Isla 察觉到我们发现了什么，就过来和我们会合。我们所在的位置还能看到楼梯，所以如果有人上楼，我们至少能看见。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You hallucinated...? What exactly happened, and why did you disappear?
entries.new: 你产生了幻觉……？到底发生了什么，你又为什么会消失？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I disappeared? Right, it seemed as if I teleported, and I heard some noise. I was still here, though, and after that... I just waited here until you appeared.
entries.new: 我消失了？对，感觉像是被传送了一样，还听到了一些响动。可我其实一直在这里，之后……我就一直在这儿等着，直到你们出现。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: ...Why did you wait here? What made you teleport?
entries.new: ……你为什么要在这里等？又是什么让你传送的？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: For some reason, Akaro was somewhat unresponsive. Was the cause... the teleportation itself? It might've been a shock, but at no point had I experienced a similar effect.
entries.new: 不知为何，Akaro 有些反应迟钝。原因……是传送本身吗？那或许是种冲击，可我自己经历时，从未有过类似的感觉。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked around the hallways a bit, and then I felt like waiting here. And I'm not sure what caused it. Maybe... it was the Sekimeiya.
entries.new: 我在走廊里转了一圈，然后就想在这里等着。至于原因，我也说不准。也许……是 Sekimeiya 吧。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Are you sure? We touched it right before you vanished and nothing happened.
entries.new: 你确定？你消失之前我们也碰过它，什么都没发生。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Well, yeah... I'm not sure, then.
entries.new: 嗯，是啊……那我就不知道了。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: It doesn't make sense. I thought about it earlier.{w} If you touched the Sekimeiya, why was it shut in the cabinet after you disappeared?
entries.new: 这说不通。我之前就想过。{w}如果你碰过 Sekimeiya，那你消失之后，它为什么还锁在展示柜里？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Huh...?{w} I don't know.
entries.new: 咦……？{w}我不知道。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Akaro, just tell us exactly what happened.
entries.new: Akaro，你就把发生的事原原本本告诉我们。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I am. It seemed as if I teleported, and then I searched around a bit, very confused. ...I waited in here until you showed up. Nothing else, and the time makes it clear: I didn't time travel. At most, I could have teleported, but I think something was wrong with me, and I imagined it.
entries.new: 我说的就是实话。当时像是被传送了一样，之后我满心困惑地四处找了一圈。……然后就在这里等到你们出现。除此之外什么都没有，从时间上看也很清楚：我没有时间穿越。顶多就是被传送了，可我觉得是自己哪里不对劲，产生了错觉。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: You didn't imagine anything. You actually disappeared.
entries.new: 你没有产生错觉。你是真的消失了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: No... I did, I did imagine it. Teleporting is impossible.
entries.new: 不……就是错觉，肯定是我的错觉。传送是不可能的。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Well, we found the key to the attic. Naomi had it. We went up and looked for you, but we didn't find anything.
entries.new: 总之，我们找到了阁楼的钥匙，在 Naomi 身上。我们上去找过你，却一无所获。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I see.
entries.new: 原来如此。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I had no idea what had happened to him. Had teleporting changed him so much? It was reasonable to conclude that he was making it all up. The Sekimeiya hadn't worked for us, so why would he have been able to travel? And according to him, he hadn't moved through time, just space...
entries.new: 我完全不明白他到底出了什么事。传送会把他变成这样吗？认为他在编造，也合情合理。Sekimeiya 对我们没起作用，他怎么就能穿越？而且照他的说法，他没穿越时间，只是移动了空间……
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In other news, these shoes match. It's likely Naomi was in the attic.
entries.new: 另外，这双鞋是配对的。Naomi 多半去过阁楼。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Shiroya, don't you want to cover her body again?
entries.new: ……Shiroya，她的遗体不打算再盖上吗？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Huh...? Oh, yes, we should do that too.
entries.new: 咦……？哦，对，是该这么做。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...We all looked at each other, wondering what to think. No cameras existed in the bathroom, but since they were functional in hallway C, it was probably fine to at least do that much. However, Akaro's question had come out of left field.
entries.new: ……我们面面相觑，不知该作何感想。浴室里没有摄像头，但 C走廊的摄像头还运作着，至少做到这一步应该无妨。只是，Akaro 忽然问出这句话，实在太突兀了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai and Shiroya went off on their own. They came back at the same time, and Shiroya was holding a velvet curtain.
entries.new: Sai 和 Shiroya 分头行动，又同时回来了。Shiroya 手里抱着一条天鹅绒遮布。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The Sekimeiya's still there. I touched it too, and nothing happened.
entries.new: Sekimeiya 还在那儿。我也碰过了，什么都没发生。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Akaro, did you touch it? What caused your teleportation?
entries.new: Akaro，你碰过它吗？到底是什么引发了传送？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I did. I think touching it is what triggered it.
entries.new: 碰过。我想，就是碰到它才触发的。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Why did you touch it? Didn't we all go to the next room? We had just touched it too.
entries.new: 你为什么要碰它？我们不是都去了隔壁房间吗？我们才刚碰过它。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Did you wanna steal it, maybe?
entries.new: 难不成，你是想把它偷走？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: As Shiroya covered Naomi's body with the curtain, Akaro took a few seconds to think about it.
entries.new: Shiroya 用遮布盖住 Naomi 的遗体时，Akaro 花了几秒钟考虑这个问题。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was only curious since I hadn't personally touched it yet. I didn't expect anything to happen.
entries.new: 我只是好奇，毕竟我自己还没亲手碰过。我没料到会出什么事。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: And where did you appear? We searched for you.
entries.new: 那你出现在哪里？我们找过你。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...Somewhere in hallway C, I think.
entries.new: ……我想，是在 C走廊的某处。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: That's not possible. We searched all around this floor, and you weren't here.
entries.new: 这不可能。这一层我们全找遍了，根本没见到你。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Oh, that's right. I did see and hear you searching, but you didn't see me. I never left this floor...
entries.new: 哦，对了。你们找我的时候，我确实看到也听到了，可你们看不见我。我一直没离开过这一层……
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: ...What? That should be impossible.
entries.new: ……什么？那应该不可能。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It's not, because it's what I experienced myself... After that, I stayed here until now.
entries.new: 并非不可能，因为那是我亲身经历的……之后我就一直待在这里，直到现在。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I had no idea how to interpret what he was saying.{w} At my side, Naomi's body rested under a beautiful cloth that practically occupied the entire bathroom floor. Given the surroundings, it wasn't the most respectful thing, but we couldn't do much else for her.
entries.new: 我完全不知道该如何理解他的话。{w}我身旁，Naomi 的遗体躺在一块几乎铺满整个浴室地面的漂亮布料下。在这种地方，这算不上多么体面的做法，可我们能为她做的也只有这些了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...So you didn't see the culprit? Or go to the other floors? We entered the attic. ...Don't you want to go?
entries.new: ……那你没看见凶手？也没去其他楼层？我们已经进过阁楼了。……你不想去吗？
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: No... not yet. You guys go, and I'll follow in a bit.
entries.new: 不……暂时不去。你们先走吧，我过一会儿再上去。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: We can wait for you.
entries.new: 我们可以等你。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: No, please, leave me alone for a bit longer. I'm still a bit curious about what this attic might be, so I'll go up shortly.
entries.new: 不用了，请让我一个人再待一会儿。我对这阁楼究竟是怎么回事还有点好奇，很快就会上去。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Are you serious? You'll have some explaining to do.
entries.new: 你认真的？到时候你可得好好解释清楚。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yes... Just leave me here for now.
entries.new: 嗯……暂时就让我留在这里吧。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: All of us hesitated, baffled. We'd expected to get answers from Akaro if we found him, but he'd only given us more questions. It was possible he was just acting, but that wouldn't explain his disappearance. If he was correct, the Sekimeiya only made him travel through space...
entries.new: 我们都迟疑了，满心困惑。本以为找到 Akaro 就能得到答案，结果他却只让我们生出更多疑问。他也许只是在演戏，可这解释不了他的消失。若他所言属实，Sekimeiya 只是让他穿越了空间……
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It couldn't be. He couldn't have appeared in hallway C, or we would've found him. ...He was either lying or had a mistaken perspective.
entries.new: 不可能。他若真的出现在 C走廊，我们不可能找不到他。……他要不是在说谎，就是他的认知出了偏差。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Was there any other choice? I could only theorize that maybe our perspective was wrong instead, but I couldn't come up with an explanation beyond that.
entries.new: 还能有别的解释吗？我只能推测，也许出错的反而是我们的认知，可除此之外，我再也想不出任何解释。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I wasn't content with Sai's claim, so I made sure to check the event room. The mysterious egg was still inside the cabinet, and as Sai had done, I went ahead and touched it, receiving no response.
entries.new: 我对 Sai 的说法并不放心，便特意去了活动室确认。那颗神秘的蛋仍摆在展示柜里，我像 Sai 那样伸手碰了碰，毫无反应。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I lowered the curtain again and headed toward the stairs.
entries.new: 我把遮布重新放下，朝楼梯走去。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Why would it have worked for Akaro? Why had it worked for me the other time? And what about when Naomi traveled, since it was basically confirmed that she appeared in the attic...? Was there a recurring factor among the times it had worked?
entries.new: 为什么在 Akaro 身上就起了作用？之前在我身上又为什么能生效？还有 Naomi 那次穿越，既然基本可以确定她到过阁楼……？这些成功的情形之间，是否存在某种共同点？
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Ultimately, we went up again. We hoped that Akaro would soon regain his composure so that we could draw more information out of him, but if he truly wasn't stable, it was best to leave him be. We told him that the elevator might still be disabled by the time he decided to go up and that we'd leave the door on floor 6 unlocked.
entries.new: 最终，我们还是上去了。我们盼着 Akaro 能尽快平复下来，好从他口中问出更多消息；可若他当真情绪不稳，还是别去打扰为好。我们告诉他，等他想上楼时，电梯说不定还没恢复，六楼的门我们会留着不锁。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We moved back up, unaware of what our goal had become and knowing that we hadn't thoroughly inspected the crystal floor. It was technically possible someone remained down there, as the sound we'd heard in the event room was yet to be explained, but we decided to ignore that and go along with what Akaro asked.
entries.new: 我们又回到了楼上，说不清目的已经变成了什么，只知道水晶层还没彻底查过。严格来说，下面可能还有人——我们在活动室听到的声响至今没有解释——但我们还是决定不再理会，照 Akaro 说的做。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Going up and down the stairs so often was getting tiring, but we couldn't take the elevator.
entries.new: 这样上上下下地爬楼梯，实在累人，可电梯又坐不了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Had Akaro really only teleported without moving through time? I kept circling around that detail.{w} Since we knew barely anything about the mechanism behind the Sekimeiya, I couldn't definitely object. However, I estimated that I went about twenty minutes to the past. If that was variable, it was possible Akaro hadn't realized he'd gone less than a minute to the past thanks to the time on Sai's wristwatch.
entries.new: Akaro 真的只是传送，而没有穿越时间吗？这个细节在我脑中反复打转。{w}我们对 Sekimeiya 背后的原理几乎一无所知，我自然无法断言不对。但按我的估计，我大约回到了二十分钟之前。倘若穿越的幅度并不固定，那 Akaro 或许只是凭 Sai 手表上的时间，没能察觉自己其实只回到了不到一分钟之前。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Walls Of Glass
entries.new: 玻璃之墙

entries.text: We entered the attic again. We'd left the door unlocked, and the key was still inserted in its hole. Since we didn't have anything in mind, we dispersed ourselves throughout the few rooms, waiting for Akaro's arrival.
entries.new: 我们再次走进阁楼。门没有锁，钥匙也还插在锁孔里。反正也没什么头绪，我们便分散到几个房间里，等 Akaro 过来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai and Katei remained in the living room while Shiroya, Erina, Isla, and I entered the right bedroom. We'd been a group earlier, so staying together felt right. Shiroya and I threw ourselves onto the spacious bed and tried to rest for a bit, both of us pretty worn down.
entries.new: Sai 和 Katei 留在客厅，我则与 Shiroya、Erina、Isla 进了右侧的卧室。先前我们几个就一直待在一块儿，如今凑在一起也更安心。我和 Shiroya 一头扑到宽敞的床上，想歇一会儿——两个人都已经相当疲惫了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The other two mimicked us and sat at our side.
entries.new: 另外两人也学着我们的样子，在我们身旁坐下。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: *yawn*
entries.new: 哈啊——
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Are you tired?
entries.new: 你困了？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yes... I hate waking up so early. Mom made me set my alarm to {time=6.}
entries.new: 嗯……我最讨厌起这么早了。妈妈非要我把闹钟定在 {time=6.}。
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: That early? Do you live far from the tower?
entries.new: 那么早？你住得离塔很远吗？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: No, but I knew a lot of people would come today. I wanted us to be some of the first visitors so that I could drop Isla off at school afterward.
entries.new: 不远，不过我知道今天会有很多人来。我想让我们赶在头一批进去，这样之后还能送 Isla 去学校。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I see. You must be pretty happy that you'll get to skip the entire school day.
entries.new: 原来如此。能翘掉一整天的课，你一定很高兴吧。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yeah, but I already knew that would happen.
entries.new: 嗯，不过我早就知道会这样了。
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: ...Oh, right.
entries.new: ……啊，也对。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: So, is this the first time you came here?
entries.new: 话说回来，你是第一次来这里吗？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yup. I didn't know this place was so cool.
entries.new: 对呀。我都不知道这里这么厉害。
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: That's surprising. With how much you seem to like gemstones, I figured you would've come here before.
entries.new: 这倒让我意外。看你这么喜欢宝石，我还以为你以前来过呢。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: She's had many passing interests. She just got back from school one day and told me she wanted to come to this place.
entries.new: 她感兴趣的东西多了，都只是一阵风。有天放学回来，她突然就跟我说想来这儿。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Because Amelie came to school with a really pretty bracelet. She said it was... uh, athemist like the ones in Ashiya Tower. She let everyone touch it but me. I don't know why, but she doesn't like me.
entries.new: 因为 Amelie 戴着一条特别漂亮的手链来学校。她说那是……呃，紫水晶，跟芦屋塔里的一样。她让大家都摸，就我不行。我也不知道为什么，她就是不喜欢我。
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: ...I see. That's why you looked so happy downstairs.
entries.new: ……我明白了。难怪你在楼下看起来那么开心。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I actually told her that I didn't want to bring her here at first. I should've just stuck to that, but she kept mentioning it, and when she's infatuated with something, she doesn't talk about anything else. ...I caved in too quickly.
entries.new: 其实我一开始就跟她说过，不想带她来。我要是坚持住就好了，可她一直提，一旦迷上什么，嘴里就再没别的了。……我松口松得太快了。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: That was only when Amelie said that her parents wouldn't let her go see the Sekimeiya. She was saying really ugly things about her mom, but she always buys her anything she asks for. I don't get it.
entries.new: 那是后来 Amelie 说她爸妈不让她去看 Sekimeiya 才开始的。她把她妈妈说得可难听了，可她妈妈明明她要什么就给买什么。我搞不懂。
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: It's good that you're not like that. I'm sure she'll be embarrassed about that when she's older.
entries.new: 你不像她那样，这很好。等她长大些，一定会为自己说过的话害臊的。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Everyone really likes her, though. I don't hate her, but she's really mean sometimes.
entries.new: 可是大家都很喜欢她。我也不讨厌她，只是她有时候真的很刻薄。
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: So you live in Yushibana, right? You probably go to the same school Atsuki and I attended. There were some people like that when we were your age, but they all matured eventually. I think that's an effect of there being so few people.
entries.new: 那你住在丰花，对吧？你上的多半就是我和 Atsuki 念过的那所学校。我们像你这么大的时候，也有几个那样的人，不过后来都慢慢懂事了。我想，这大概跟这里人少有关吧。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Oh! You went to my school? Do you know Miss Bisky?
entries.new: 哦！你也上我的学校？你认识 Bisky 老师吗？
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: The teacher?
entries.new: 你说老师？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah!
entries.new: 对呀！
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: She still works there? I remember her, yeah. She was always really nice to us.
entries.new: 她还在那儿教书？我记得她，嗯。她一直对我们特别好。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: She's my favorite teacher. I'll tell her that I met you two.
entries.new: 她是我最喜欢的老师。我要告诉她，我碰到你们俩了。
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: I'm surprised she's still there. She was pretty old when she taught us.
entries.new: 她居然还在，真让人意外。教我们那会儿，她年纪就已经不小了。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: She knew we were going to come here, so she might be a bit worried if she heard about what happened. She's usually the person behind Isla's sudden interests. One day, she told her that she had an aquarium at home. The next few weeks, I didn't hear about anything except wanting to go to an aquarium.
entries.new: 她知道我们要来这儿，要是听说了发生的事，说不定会有点担心。Isla 那些突然冒出来的兴趣，多半都是她带起来的。有一天她跟 Isla 说自己家里有鱼缸，接下来好几个星期，我就没听她提过别的，全是想去看鱼缸。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Do you remember how interested you became in fish out of nowhere? Where did that passion go? Did you read all the books I bought you?
entries.new: 你还记得自己当初怎么突然迷上鱼的吗？那股热情跑哪儿去了？我给你买的那些书，你都读完了吗？
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I still love them! And yes, I read all of them. Did you know that fish can get sunburned when they're near the surface?
entries.new: 我现在也还喜欢呀！而且那些书我全读完了。你知道吗，鱼游到水面附近的时候也会被晒伤？
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: I prefer them pan-seared.{w} Why are you all on the bed? We didn't inspect this floor that thoroughly, so you should be looking for clues.
entries.new: 我倒更喜欢煎的。{w}你们都赖在床上干什么？这一层我们还没仔细查过，该去找线索才对。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Why don't you do that?
entries.new: 那你怎么不去找？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Sorry, I need to keep my eyes on Katei in case he kills Naomi a third time. Let me know if you find something.
entries.new: 抱歉，我得看紧 Katei，提防他第三次对 Naomi 下手。你们要是查到什么，跟我说一声。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Sai is so weird.
entries.new: ……Sai 真奇怪。
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Yeah, maybe you should forget what I said about people here maturing.
entries.new: 是啊，刚才我说这里的人总会懂事——你就当我没说过吧。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: He doesn't go to our school, right? He's around our age, and I don't think I've seen him before.
entries.new: 他不跟我们上一个学校吧？年纪跟我们差不多，可我好像从没见过他。
entries.speaker: a
