entries.text: He might go to the one outside town. I don't know him either.
entries.new: 他说不定上的是镇外那所。我也不认识他。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Instead of doing what Sai said, we reclined on the bed. Unlike me, Shiroya had always been good at dealing with kids. The tone of her voice changed significantly when she talked to Isla. I wished the conversation would continue just so that I could keep hearing it.
entries.new: 我们没有照 Sai 说的去做，反倒又躺回了床上。与我不同，Shiroya 一向很会应付小孩子。她和 Isla 说话时，语气变了许多。我甚至盼着这场对话别停，好让我一直听下去。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The three of them had all been holding something to contain their belongings. Just like Sai had his hip pack, Shiroya carried a modest purse she'd had for a long time. Isla had a child-sized shoulder purse, and Erina had a bigger, black purse with her.
entries.new: 她们三个都带着装东西的包。就像 Sai 有他的腰包一样，Shiroya 拎着一只用了很久的普通手提包；Isla 背的是儿童尺寸的挎包；Erina 则带着一只更大的黑色手提包。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Something caught my attention, so I stood back up.
entries.new: 有什么东西引起了我的注意，我便站了起来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What are you looking at? That's mine.
entries.new: 你在看什么？那是我的。
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: I couldn't see inside Shiroya's or Erina's, but Isla's had remained slightly open while she was lying face-up. Inside, something felt out of place.
entries.new: Shiroya 和 Erina 的包我看不到里面，可 Isla 仰面躺着时，她的包一直半开着。里面的某样东西显得格格不入。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What's that for?
entries.new: 那是做什么用的？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Hm? That's my purse. I don't use it every day, but I took it today.
entries.new: 嗯？那是我的包。我平时不是每天都用，不过今天带上了。
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: I mean that device.
entries.new: 我是说那个装置。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Device? What are you talking about?
entries.new: ……装置？你在说什么？
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Erina and Isla got up and frowned when they saw what had intrigued me.
entries.new: Erina 和 Isla 站起身来，看到引起我注意的东西后，眉头都皱了起来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Oh, is that a recorder? It has a play and record button.
entries.new: ……哦，这是录音笔吧？上面有播放键和录音键。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: What...? I don't know. I've never seen it.
entries.new: 什么……？我不知道。我从没见过这东西。
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: It was inside your purse. Where did you get it?
entries.new: 它就在你的手提包里。你从哪儿弄来的？
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I just said I've never seen it before... I don't know what it's doing here.
entries.new: 我刚说了，我从来没见过它……我也不知道它怎么会在这儿。
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: ...Are you making things up again? What's it doing in your purse if you've never seen it before?
entries.new: ……你又在编故事了？既然从没见过，它怎么会在你包里？
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I'm telling you that I don't know!
entries.new: 我说了我不知道！
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: It wasn't very big, but it occupied most of the space in the purse. It was hard to believe anyone could've dropped it inside while Isla had been wearing it, and I hadn't seen her leaving it behind anywhere and giving someone an opportunity to plant an object in it. Shiroya grabbed the device and began to fiddle with it.
entries.new: 它并不算大，却占去了手提包里大半的空间。要说在 Isla 拎着包的时候有人能把它塞进去，实在难以想象；而且我也没见她把包放在哪里，让人有机会往里面放东西。Shiroya 拿起那装置，摆弄了起来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There's a record button and a recording saved. I think we can listen to it. This seems to be a speaker.
entries.new: 有个录音键，里面还存着一段录音。应该可以听。这大概是个扬声器。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: On one side of the recorder, a symbol indicated that audio could come out of it. On the back was a slot for an SD card, but there wasn't one inserted.
entries.new: 录音笔的一侧印着一个符号，表示声音可以从那里放出。背面是一个 SD 卡插槽，但里面没有插卡。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When Shiroya pressed the "record" button, a message appeared. It said: "Delete previous recording before starting a new one".{w} Instead of doing that, Shiroya selected the single audio track with the circle pad and pressed the play button.
entries.new: Shiroya 按下「录音」键，屏幕上跳出一行提示：「删除已有录音后方可开始新录音」。{w} 她没有照做，而是用圆形摇杆选中了唯一的那段音频，按下播放键。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A time bar appeared on the screen. Static started playing immediately, and we frowned, waiting for something else to happen.{w} On the screen, the seconds ticked up for a while as the static went on. ...Were we hearing footsteps?{w} Eventually, that noise was interrupted by a very loud one. It sounded as if someone had sat right next to us. Then, that person heaved a sigh, and as soon as they started speaking, we recognized who they were.
entries.new: 屏幕上出现了一条时间轴。沙沙的杂音随即响起，我们皱起眉，等着别的动静。{w} 杂音持续着，屏幕上的秒数一点点往上跳。……那是脚步声吗？{w} 不久，那阵杂音被一阵很响的动静打断了，那动静听起来就像有人在我们身旁坐了下来。接着，那人长叹一口气，刚一开口，我们就认出了那是谁。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Well... what do we do now?
entries.new: 那么……现在怎么办？
entries.speaker: ak2

entries.text: We immediately recognized it as Akaro's voice.
entries.new: 我们立刻听出那是 Akaro 的声音。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wh-Why did I have this?
entries.new: 为、为什么我会有这个？
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Does it show the date anywhere?
entries.new: 上面有显示日期吗？
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: No... there's nothing like that.
entries.new: 没有……没看到这类东西。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: What do you want to do? We might've been here for more than a month and the exit's not open. Unless you wanna take down the shutter by hand, we can only keep waiting.
entries.new: 你想怎么办？我们可能已经在这儿待了一个多月，出口还是没开。除非你想徒手把卷帘门拆下来，否则只能继续等。
entries.speaker: sai2

entries.text: Shiroya's eyes met mine in disbelief. "More than a month"? Our fear was amplified by the next sentence we heard.
entries.new: Shiroya 难以置信地看向我。「一个多月」？紧接着传来的那句话，让我们更加害怕了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't get it. What the hell happened? Did Ashiya just abandon their own building with us inside...? And we thought we'd be free after twelve hours...
entries.new: 我不明白。到底出了什么事？芦屋就这么把自己楼里的人丢下不管了……？我们还以为熬过十二小时就能出去……
entries.speaker: ak2

entries.text: What...!? Th-This can't mean...?
entries.new: 什么……！？这、这该不会是说……？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: And once again, the recording hammered us with the hardest hit yet.
entries.new: 而录音又一次给了我们最沉重的一击。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki, what are you thinking about? Do you have any more ideas...? And hey, Erina, what's with that face?
entries.new: Atsuki，你在想什么？还有什么主意吗……？还有，Erina，你那是什么表情？
entries.speaker: sai2

entries.text: It almost seemed as if Sai had been talking to us directly. We were speechless, wondering if we were there too.
entries.new: 那语气几乎就像 Sai 在直接对我们说话。我们说不出话来，心里揣测着——我们是不是也在那里？
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What, not going to answer?
entries.new: 怎么，不打算回答？
entries.speaker: ak2

entries.text: Then, we heard the recorder play the sound of a door being pushed, and following it, gasps. Expressions of pure shock filled our ears, which perfectly conveyed the bewilderment shared by everyone who'd been recorded.
entries.new: 接着，录音笔里传出推门的声音，随后是一片倒抽冷气的声音。纯粹的震惊透过那些声音灌进我们耳中，把被录下的所有人的茫然传达得淋漓尽致。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Isla...! What the hell!?
entries.new: Isla……！搞什么鬼！？
entries.speaker: sai2

entries.text: What...? Isla, when did this happen?
entries.new: 什么……？Isla，这是什么时候的事？
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: She indicated that she had no idea with a gesture, so we kept waiting while the device emitted nothing but silence.
entries.new: 她做了个手势，表示自己毫不知情。于是我们继续等着，装置里只剩一片寂静。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hey, answer us...! Wh-What are you looking at!?
entries.new: 喂，回答我们啊……！你、你在看什么！？
entries.speaker: ak2

entries.text: ...{w}Where am I...?
entries.new: ……{w}我这是在哪儿……？
entries.speaker: il2

entries.text: Wh-What do you mean? We're still in Ashiya Tower. Do you not remember?
entries.new: 你、你说什么？我们还在芦屋塔里啊。你不记得了？
entries.speaker: sai2

entries.text: No, I know. What I mean is... what happened to me? Where am I?
entries.new: 不，我知道。我是说……我到底怎么了？我在哪儿？
entries.speaker: il2

entries.text: What?
entries.new: 什么？
entries.speaker: ak2

entries.text: Akaro's confusion must've been shared by the rest of us. What kind of question was that, regardless of the context?
entries.new: Akaro 的困惑想必也是我们所有人的困惑。不管放在什么情境下，那都是个莫名其妙的问题。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No... I should be...
entries.new: 不对……我应该在……
entries.speaker: il2

entries.text: Following that, there were a couple of unsteady, heavy footfalls, most likely someone staggering. During the next few seconds, Isla cried, and nobody spoke, inside or outside the recording.
entries.new: 紧接着，响起两三下沉重而不稳的脚步声，多半是有人踉跄了一下。接下来的几秒里，Isla 叫了一声，录音里外都没有人说话。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Huh...?{w} I've never... done this.
entries.new: 咦……？{w}我从来没……做过这种事。
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: I-Isla, what's gotten into you? ...What are you holding?{w} And Erina, why aren't you doing anything!?
entries.new: Isla，你、你这是怎么了？……你手里拿的是什么？{w} 还有 Erina，你怎么什么都不做！？
entries.speaker: ak2

entries.text: With a final sob... the recording ended.{w} The screen left us with a button to rewind the audio, and we remained motionless, with expressions we'd never worn before.
entries.new: 随着最后一声啜泣……录音结束了。{w} 屏幕上只剩下一个倒回音频的按钮，我们一动不动，脸上挂着从未有过的神情。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd fallen unconscious from a smoke attack, probably traveled to the past, and found two dead bodies that belonged to the same person. However, the sensation left by that bizarre recording surpassed all of those.
entries.new: 我因烟雾袭击昏了过去，多半是经历了时间穿越，还发现了两具属于同一个人的尸体。可那段诡异录音留下的感触，比这一切都更强烈。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It said that we'd be here for over a month. It's not possible, right? Even if the exit doesn't open, the people outside would find a way to rescue us.
entries.new: 录音里说我们会在这儿待一个多月。这不可能吧？就算出口不开，外面的人也会想办法来救我们。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Y-Yes. This must be a trap created by Sai and Akaro.
entries.new: 对、对。这一定是 Sai 和 Akaro 设下的圈套。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Usually, I would have also jumped to that possibility, but Isla was in that recording too. Could she have been in on it?
entries.new: 换作平时，我也会马上想到这种可能，可那段录音里也有 Isla。难道她也参与其中？
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I remembered Isla's "friend". Were Sai and Akaro somehow involved in everything?
entries.new: 我想起了 Isla 的「朋友」。难道 Sai 和 Akaro 与这一切都有关联？
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You and Atsuki were mentioned as if you were there, but you didn't actually say anything. And Katei and I weren't mentioned at all, but with how short it was, that doesn't mean anything.
entries.new: 录音里提到你和 Atsuki，好像你们也在场，可你们其实一句话都没说。至于我和 Katei，根本没被提到——不过录音那么短，这也说明不了什么。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: It didn't mean anything, but it was still unsettling. According to the recorded Sai, I'd been quiet for a while and Erina's behavior had also been strange.
entries.new: 说明不了什么，却仍让人心里发毛。按录音里 Sai 的说法，我沉默了很长一段时间，Erina 的举动也有些反常。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If we were to believe the contents of the recording, it meant that it had somehow traveled to the past from one month in the future. I couldn't even imagine why and how that would've happened.
entries.new: 若录音的内容属实，那就意味着它不知怎么从一个月后的未来回到了过去。至于其中的缘由和方式，我根本无从想象。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Isla, sorry to ask again, but be as honest as you can. Have you really never seen this device? Have you really never spoken the words we just heard? And do you really not know anything about it?
entries.new: Isla，抱歉再问一次，但请你尽量说实话。你真的从没见过这个设备？我们刚才听到的那些话，你真的从没说过？关于它，你真的什么都不知道？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I promise... I have no idea where this came from, and I never said any of that... You believe me, Tanya, right?
entries.new: 我保证……我不知道这东西是从哪来的，那些话我也从没说过……坦桑娅，你相信我的，对吧？
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Y-Yes, but this is surreal.
entries.new: 是……是的，可这也太不可思议了。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Isla had begun to sound like she had in the recording, trying not to break down. The four of us had just been handed a month-long sentence with no bail, and it sounded as if it could be extended indefinitely.
entries.new: Isla的语气已经和录音里一样了，强撑着不让情绪崩溃。我们四人刚被判了一个月、不得保释的刑期，而这刑期听上去还可能无限延长。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Don't worry. This recording must've been manipulated. There are plenty of things in it that don't make sense.
entries.new: 别担心。这录音肯定被人动过手脚。里面说不通的地方多得是。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Of course, as Shiroya said, we'll be rescued if things go wrong when the exit is supposed to open. There's no food here, so it's impossible we could be here for an entire month. Akaro and Sai sounded perfectly healthy, didn't they?
entries.new: 当然，就像Shiroya说的，出口该打开时若出了岔子，会有人来救我们。这里没有食物，我们不可能在这儿待上整整一个月。Akaro和Sai听起来都很健康，不是吗？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That's right. I bet they didn't think this through. There's still nine hours until we can leave, but no more than that. Don't believe any of this, Isla. We're fine. We'll all be fine.
entries.new: 没错。我看他们根本没想周全。我们还要九个小时才能离开，但也仅此而已。别信这些，Isla。我们没事。大家都会没事的。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Like Isla, I was looking forward to making it out a lot more than I appeared. I wanted my life to get back on track and go to the mountains with Shiroya as we'd agreed.
entries.new: 和Isla一样，我比表面上更盼望能出去。我想让生活回到正轨，想按约定和Shiroya一起去山里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The thought of remaining imprisoned crushed down on my shoulders. We had come to the tower for the purpose of getting a fresh start, and the recording threatened to turn all of that on its head once again.
entries.new: 一想到还要被困在这里，我的双肩就像被压垮了一般。我们来这座塔，本是为了重新开始，而那段录音却可能把这一切再次掀翻。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I believe we heard something else that stood out. Apart from what Isla said, the way Sai phrased it...{w} "We might've been here for more than a month."{w} ...This "might've" is very odd.
entries.new: 我觉得还有一处很突兀。除了Isla说的那些，Sai的措辞……{w}「我们可能已经在这里待了一个多月。」{w}……这个「可能」很反常。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Oh, that's right... Why would he not be sure?
entries.new: 哦，对……他为什么会不确定？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: It's true that we could easily lose track of time after spending a month locked in here, but we could know how long it's been just by looking at the date.
entries.new: 在这里关一个月，确实容易记不清时日，可只要看看日期，就能知道过了多久。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: And on the crystal floor, we have a computer that displays it. Even Sai himself has a watch in case the computer stopped working.
entries.new: 而且水晶层有台电脑会显示日期。就算电脑坏了，Sai自己也带着手表。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: It has to be a trick, and one that's easy to see right through. Someone must've put this recorder in your purse.
entries.new: 这肯定是个把戏，而且一眼就能看穿。一定是有人把录音笔塞进了你的手提包。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Do you know when that could've happened?
entries.new: 你知道那可能是什么时候的事吗？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: No... I had it the whole time since we left home.
entries.new: 不知道……从家里出来以后，它一直都在我身上。
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: When you entered the tower, a guard looked at your purse, right? Do you remember if it was there?
entries.new: 你进塔的时候，警卫检查过你的手提包，对吧？你还记得那时它在不在吗？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I-I don't know. I didn't look, I just gave it to him.
entries.new: 我……我不知道。我没看，直接把包递给他了。
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: ...{w}Isla, mind telling us the identity of your friend now? She could've had access to it, and somehow, she knew this incident would happen. Not only that, but she lied to you, right? About the number of people and when she said that nothing bad would happen.
entries.new: ……{w}Isla，现在能告诉我们你那位朋友是谁了吗？她有可能接触过这支录音笔，而且不知怎么就知道会出事。不止如此，她还骗了你，对吧？人数上骗了你，还说不会出什么事。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: N-No! She has nothing to do with this, I promise! She was wrong, but she didn't lie. She's waiting for me outside, and I don't wanna leave her alone for long. Christmas is in ten days, and we promised we'd spend it together...
entries.new: 不……不是的！这事跟她没关系，我保证！她只是说错了，没有撒谎。她还在外面等我，我不想把她一个人撂太久。再过十天就是圣诞节，我们约好一起过的……
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Before I could press her further, the door opened and Sai appeared with Katei behind him. They forcibly stepped in and closed the door again.
entries.new: 我还没来得及追问，门就开了，Sai走进来，Katei跟在后面。两人硬挤进门，又把门关上了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hey guys. I found a little thing.
entries.new: 各位。我发现了点小东西。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Can you just say what it is already?
entries.new: 你倒是直接说是什么啊。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Yes, that's why we came here. It wouldn't have been the same without them.
entries.new: 对，我们就是为这个来的。没有他们可就不一样了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I thought about it. Was Sai hiding something from us? If he was, it must've been something pretty significant.
entries.new: 我琢磨了一下。Sai是不是有什么瞒着我们？要真是这样，那一定不是小事。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Instead of asking questions, we waited for what he had to say. While he wasn't paying attention, Erina put the recorder back inside Isla's purse to avoid being questioned. Isla and Erina could easily be called suspicious if anyone knew they had it.
entries.new: 我们没有追问，只等着他开口。趁他没注意，Erina把录音笔放回了Isla的手提包，免得被人问起。要是有人知道录音笔在她们手上，Isla和Erina很容易被当成嫌疑人。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Who wants to read this?
entries.new: 谁想看这个？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai was holding a folded piece of paper. Since there were no volunteers, he handed it to me.
entries.new: Sai手里拿着一张折起来的纸。没人应声，他便递给了我。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You've been chosen. I found this in a drawer in the kitchen.
entries.new: 就你了。这是我在厨房抽屉里找到的。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I sighed faintly and began to read.
entries.new: 我轻轻叹了口气，读了起来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "Sir, I have done as you instructed, and I didn't spot any difference in the attic since Xyn's last attack. I believe it wasn't targeted."
entries.new: 「先生，我已经照你的吩咐做了，从Xyn上次袭击之后，阁楼里没有发现任何异常。我觉得那并不是针对这里。」
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: "I've finished this month's preservations, but some paint has begun to wear off, so next month I'll attempt to fix that on my own. Until then, thank you for your trust and let me know if you have any new requests."
entries.new: 「本月的养护工作已经完成，不过有些漆面开始脱落，下个月我会试着自己修补。在那之前，谢谢你的信任，若有新的吩咐请告诉我。」
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: "Naomi".
entries.new: 「Naomi」。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...It's a letter from Naomi?
entries.new: ……这是Naomi写的信？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Precisely—your ears do work. It sounds as if Naomi was tasked with keeping this attic tidy. It's addressed to the head of the Ashiya family, who must've lived here back in the day.
entries.new: 正是——看来你的耳朵没毛病。看样子Naomi负责打理这间阁楼。信是写给芦屋家当主的，当年住在这里的想必就是那位。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...I see.
entries.new: ……原来如此。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Understand? It means that Katei has lied yet again! It's great, he never stops. We're going to set a world record at this rate.
entries.new: 明白了吗？这就是说Katei又撒了一次谎！真棒，他这谎话简直没完没了。照这势头，我们都要破世界纪录了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I suppose you're right. He must've known about this, so finding the attic key in Naomi's pocket shouldn't have been a big surprise.
entries.new: 我想你说得对。他肯定早就知道这事，所以在Naomi口袋里找到阁楼钥匙，本不该让人那么吃惊。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I didn't know. I don't look through these cameras very often, and according to this letter, she worked here once a month. It makes sense that I never saw her.
entries.new: 我不知情。我不常翻看这些监控，而信上说她每月来这里工作一次。我没见过她，也说得通。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Holy shit, Katei. You know that you're fucked once we get out, right? You said that you work here with Naomi and that she tried to personally convince you of her innocence earlier because of that.{w} ...But you didn't know what her job entailed?
entries.new: 我靠，Katei。你知道出去以后你就完了，对吧？你说过你和Naomi在这里共事，还说她之前就是因为这个才亲自来找你、想让你相信她清白。{w}……可你竟然不知道她负责什么？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I didn't. It's not my business to know what everyone does. I certainly didn't see her often, so I never knew exactly what her work was.
entries.new: 不知道。别人做什么，不该由我过问。我确实不常看到她，自然一直不清楚她的具体工作。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Yeah, of course. She's probably been handling this floor by herself for years, and you, who takes care of the security of the entire building, never knew that. This letter mentions Xyn, so it must be recent enough, most likely from last month.
entries.new: 是啊，当然了。她大概一个人打理这一层好几年了，而负责整栋楼安保的你，却全然不知。这封信提到了Xyn，说明它是最近写的，多半就是上个月的。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It must've happened when I wasn't present in the tower, since I only have the night shift every two weeks. For example, if she only came the first day of every month, I would never have seen her.
entries.new: 那一定是在我不在塔里的时候发生的。我每两周才上一次夜班。比方说，她若只在每月第一天来，我就永远碰不上她。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Was it not a second ago when you said you'd seen her a few times?
entries.new: 你刚才不是还说你见过她几次吗？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Katei never answered, but he looked enraged during the moments of silence that followed.
entries.new: Katei始终没有回答，但在随后的沉默里，他满脸怒容。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Well, it seems Naomi had direct communication with Ashiya and she was a trusted individual tasked with maintaining this special floor. I bet that's why she was chosen for her new job and told the secret of the Sekimeiya's true purpose.
entries.new: 看来Naomi与芦屋本人有直接联系，是个受信任的人，负责维护这一特殊楼层。我敢说，正因如此她才被选中去执行新任务，还被告知了Sekimeiya真正用途的秘密。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...None of us appeared to care much about the letter given what we'd just heard. Sai was excited to find something that strengthened his suspicions about Katei, but we'd all accepted at some point that he was lying about a number of things. It was routine.
entries.new: ……听了刚才那些话，我们似乎都没太把这封信放在心上。Sai发现能让他更怀疑Katei的东西，兴奋得很，但我们早就在某个时候接受了：他在不少事情上都在撒谎。这已是常态。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We heard the sound of a zipper being unfastened coming from the bed.
entries.new: 床边传来拉链被拉开的声响。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Hey, Shiroya, what's that?
entries.new: ……喂，Shiroya，那是什么？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We all turned to her and saw a key in her hand.
entries.new: 我们一齐看向她，只见她手里拿着一把钥匙。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did you get that from your purse? Isn't that...?
entries.new: 你从包里翻出来的？那不是……？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yes, it's the cabinet key. The Sekimeiya cabinet's.
entries.new: 嗯，是展示柜的钥匙。Sekimeiya 展示柜的。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I-I think it is. It was inside.
entries.new: 大、大概吧。它就在里面。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: What were you looking for?
entries.new: 你在找什么？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Oh, nothing. I don't know how this got here, though...
entries.new: 啊，没什么。只是我不知道这东西怎么会在包里……
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: She wouldn't admit it, but after Isla found something so bizarre inside her own purse, Shiroya must've felt the need to check hers too—and it yielded a result.
entries.new: 她不肯承认，可Isla从自己包里翻出那么离奇的东西之后，Shiroya想必也想查查自己的包——而这一查，还真查出了名堂。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I see, so you had the key. Very interesting.
entries.new: 原来如此，钥匙在你手上。真有意思。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Someone had to put it in here without me noticing.
entries.new: ……肯定是有人趁我不注意塞进来的。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...Is that so? Don't I get to suspect you?
entries.new: ……是吗？那我是不是也该怀疑你？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I mean, it wasn't inside, but in this side pocket that should've been empty and where anyone could've easily dropped it.
entries.new: 我的意思是，它不在主袋里，而是在这个侧袋——本来该是空的，谁都能轻易塞进去。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I suppose you would've left it in the main section, where the zipper could hide it. I'm fine believing that.
entries.new: 换作是你，应该会把它留在主袋里，拉链一拉就藏住了。这个说法我倒愿意相信。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Before we realized that this key was missing from the first Naomi, only the real culprit or the group that inspected hallway B could've picked it up. So Shiroya, Sai, and Akaro.
entries.new: ……在我们察觉第一个Naomi身上缺了这把钥匙之前，能拿到它的只有真凶，或者检查B走廊的那几个人。也就是Shiroya、Sai和Akaro。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Sai, who searched the room with Naomi?
entries.new: Sai，当时和Naomi一起搜查房间的是谁？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Akaro.
entries.new: Akaro。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: So he could've picked it up and later dropped it inside Shiroya's purse. However, he couldn't have unlocked the Sekimeiya cabinet, right?
entries.new: 那他可能捡到钥匙，之后又塞进Shiroya包里。可是，他不可能打开Sekimeiya的展示柜，对吧？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Yes. Nobody entered the event room.
entries.new: ……对。没人进过活动室。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Okay, then the only suspects are Sai, Akaro, and whoever the killer was. Shiroya didn't enter Naomi's room, so she couldn't have even picked that key up.
entries.new: 好，那可疑的就只剩Sai、Akaro，还有凶手。Shiroya没进过Naomi的房间，连捡到那把钥匙的机会都没有。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Surely she could've if she killed Naomi, right? I know she's supposed to have an alibi, but remember that you traveled to the past and anyone might've been able to appear on the crystal floor.
entries.new: 要是她杀了Naomi，那不就捡得到了？我知道她有不在场证明，可别忘了你穿越到了过去，谁都有可能出现在水晶层上。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The real suspect here is obviously Sai.{w} Akaro couldn't have done anything with the key, but Sai could've unlocked the cabinet because he was outside the hallway B rooms during the search.
entries.new: 这里真正可疑的显然是Sai。{w}Akaro就算拿到钥匙也做不了什么，可Sai能打开展示柜——搜查的时候，他人就在B走廊的房门外。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: But I didn't do it, and I definitely couldn't have hidden the Sekimeiya in the storeroom, so ultimately, the only suspect here is Katei, who killed Naomi. Shiroya's been wearing her purse off to her side, so it wouldn't be too hard to hide a small key in there without her knowing.
entries.new: 可我没做过，也绝不可能把Sekimeiya藏进储藏室，所以到头来，唯一可疑的就是杀了Naomi的Katei。Shiroya的包一直挂在身侧，想不让她察觉地塞一把小钥匙进去，并不难。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: God! I didn't kill Naomi, and if I had to hide a key, I'd hide it in a room. If I put it in someone's purse, I'd at least make sure they could actually be suspected. Shiroya couldn't have picked it up, so there's no reason to do that.
entries.new: 天哪！我没杀Naomi。要藏钥匙，我会藏在房间里。真要塞进谁的包里，至少也得挑个确实会被怀疑的人。Shiroya根本不可能捡到钥匙，我这么做毫无道理。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Can you think of who could've had the best chance to do it?
entries.new: 你觉得谁最有机会下手？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...No. I'm sure anyone could have done it at some point.
entries.new: ……想不出。我想，谁都有可能在某时某刻下手。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: We'll have to call Akaro out when he comes. You still haven't searched around here?
entries.new: 等Akaro回来，得当面问问他。这附近你们还没搜过吧？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...We haven't. What's there to find?
entries.new: ……没搜。这里能有什么？
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: We search precisely to figure that out. This letter was pretty well-hidden, and there are a few drawers and hiding spots I can see around here.
entries.new: 搜过才知道有什么。那封信藏得就够隐蔽，而且我一眼就看到这儿有几处抽屉和能藏东西的地方。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Fine, let me look around.
entries.new: 好吧，我来看看。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I stood up from the bed and casually crouched to open some drawers. I could see some worn out papers, expired promotions, and some more ancient stuff that wouldn't be any use.
entries.new: 我从床上起身，顺手蹲下拉开几个抽屉。里面有几张破旧的纸、过期的宣传单，还有些更老旧、派不上用场的东西。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: While everyone watched me, I moved through the drawers until something notable caught my attention. It was, again, a key.
entries.new: 大家看着我，我把抽屉逐一翻过，直到某样东西引起了我的注意。又是一把钥匙。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Do you recognize this, Katei?
entries.new: Katei，你认得这个吗？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Oh, yes. It's the key to this bedroom. The only one that remains.{w} The other bedroom also has one, but the keys shouldn't be interchangeable.
entries.new: 啊，认得。这是这间卧室的钥匙，仅剩的一把。{w}另一间卧室也有一把，不过两把钥匙应该不能通用。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I see. It still won't help us much, then.
entries.new: 这样啊。那还是帮不上什么忙。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I finished looking through the drawers without finding anything else. There was a wardrobe upstairs, but I didn't bother going. Instead, I looked at the door and found the keyhole I'd ignored. There was also a chain that would lock the door from the inside without needing a key.
entries.new: 我把抽屉翻完，再无别的发现。楼上有个衣柜，我懒得上去，转而看向房门，注意到了之前忽略的锁孔。门上还有一条链子，不用钥匙就能从里面把门锁上。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Wait, was there a chain in the other room as well?
entries.new: ……等等，另一间房里也有这种链子吗？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Not anymore. It broke years ago, so only this bedroom has one.
entries.new: 现在没有了。几年前就坏了，只有这间卧室还留着一条。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Oh.
entries.new: 哦。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...I'm not sure what Akaro's doing down there, but I'll look around a bit more until he comes since it's clear you're all slacking off.
entries.new: ……不知道Akaro在下面磨蹭什么。既然你们一个个都在偷懒，那我就再多看看，等他上来。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I wasn't sure what exactly he expected to find, but he went up the ladder. It wasn't so much that we were slacking off; rather, the recording had sapped every trace of our remaining initiative.{w} I sat down again and blankly stared at my lap.
entries.new: 我不确定他究竟指望找到什么，但他还是爬上梯子去了。我们倒也不是偷懒；那段录音把我们所剩的一点干劲都抽干了。{w}我重新坐下，茫然地望着自己的膝盖。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I can't come to a likely conclusion. How could the recording be fake? If Isla isn't hiding anything important from us, it's clear that we have to basically consider it as truthful after everything that's already happened.
entries.new: ……我得不出什么像样的结论。那段录音怎么可能是假的？如果Isla没瞒着我们什么要紧的事，那么经历了这一切之后，我们基本只能把它当真。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: However, if this recording is going to occur in the future, why did we find it now? And most importantly, why did we find it inside Isla's purse when she doesn't think anyone had the chance to put it there?
entries.new: 可是，如果这段录音是将来才会发生的事，为什么我们现在就找到了它？最关键的是，为什么它会在Isla的包里——而她认为根本没人有机会把它放进去？
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: It can still be some sort of bizarre trap. One that involves Isla as a participant with the intention of making us believe we won't be free in nine hours.
entries.new: 这仍可能是某种古怪的陷阱。让Isla也参与其中，目的就是让我们相信九小时后我们仍然脱不了身。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Moreover, we've already heard the recording. If we're still here in a month, why would anyone record anything? What would the point of recording a few minutes of a random conversation be? Why would the person behind it even have a voice recorder inside the tower, and how would it travel back to us?
entries.new: 况且，录音我们已经听过了。如果我们一个月后还困在这里，那还有谁会去录什么音？把一段闲谈录下几分钟，又有什么意义？设下这一切的人为什么会在塔里带着录音笔，那录音笔又怎么会回到我们手上？
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: When I time traveled, it seemed like causal loops are the way things work. It follows that if we let Sai and Akaro listen to the recording, the chances that it'll happen in the future will vanish. There's no way they would repeat everything exactly as they heard it. Although if the twelfth hour comes and we're still trapped, we'll have to let them know what our future looks like.
entries.new: 我时间穿越的时候，事情似乎就是按因果循环的方式运转的。如此说来，只要让Sai和Akaro听了这段录音，它将来发生的可能性就会消失——他们绝不可能一字不差地照着自己听到的内容重演一遍。不过，要是第十二个小时到了，我们仍被困在这里，那就只能让他们知道我们未来会是什么样子。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: My initial reaction was that not letting anyone else listen to the recording was the smarter choice. It would prevent fear, commotion, being suspected, and potentially falling into a trap.{w} That just so happened to go along nicely with the way the universe seemed to function, as letting Sai or Akaro listen to the recording could've immediately made its own existence an impossibility.
entries.new: 我最初的反应是，不让其他人听这段录音才是明智之举。这样能避免恐慌、骚动、被人怀疑，也能避免落入陷阱。{w}而这恰好与这个宇宙运作的方式不谋而合——一旦让Sai或Akaro听了录音，录音本身的存在就可能立刻化为不可能。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't want to believe it.{w} It was a chilling thought in many ways. I had a dog and a cat to take care of. Being locked away for a month would end the worst way possible if the people outside neglected both them and us at the same time.
entries.new: 我不愿相信。{w}这个念头在许多方面都叫人发寒。我家里还有一只狗和一只猫要照顾。要是被困上一个月，外面的人又同时不管它们和我们，结局会糟糕到极点。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Meanwhile, the cabinet key appearing in Shiroya's purse had a much straighter line of reasoning. I silently gestured at her so that she'd come to the hallway with me. Outside, I closed the door behind us while she looked slightly confused.
entries.new: 相比之下，展示柜钥匙出现在Shiroya包里这件事，脉络就清楚得多。我默默朝她打了个手势，让她跟我到走廊。到了外面，我随手带上房门，她一脸不解。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did you think of something?
entries.new: 你想到什么了？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Sort of... I think we must have something backward. I think I know what happened with the key. ...It was put in your purse by whoever picked it up from Naomi's body.
entries.new: 算是吧……我觉得我们一定有一处搞反了。关于那把钥匙，我大概知道是怎么回事了。……捡到 Naomi 身上那把钥匙的人，把它放进了你的包里。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah, I was probably the easiest target.
entries.new: 是啊，我大概是最容易被盯上的目标。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Exactly, which is why if the person who killed Naomi did it, they wouldn't have chosen you. They would've chosen a possible suspect or a spot within a room that a suspect had access to.
entries.new: 正是如此。所以，如果动手的是杀害 Naomi 的凶手，就不会选你。他会选一个可能的嫌疑人，或者选嫌疑人进得去的房间里的某个位置。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The first time it disappeared, the Sekimeiya was in a cabinet in the room where Naomi died. However, the cabinet in the event room hadn't been locked, so the key wasn't needed.{w} Then, we split up between both hallways and the Sekimeiya was taken. That's when the key was used.
entries.new: 它第一次消失时，Sekimeiya 就放在 Naomi 遇害那个房间的展示柜里。可活动室的展示柜当时没上锁，用不着钥匙。{w}后来我们分成两路去搜走廊，Sekimeiya 被人拿走了——那一次才用上了钥匙。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Later, when we returned from the higher floors without finding anyone, the Sekimeiya hadn't been stolen yet. It was still in the cabinet. ...And according to Sai, someone took the elevator down.{w} I don't think the killer's intention was to take the Sekimeiya.{w} If it had been, and they'd purposely removed the cabinet key from Naomi's set, they wouldn't have taken the Sekimeiya while we'd been searching both hallways. They would've waited for us to leave, and they wouldn't have dropped the key in your purse.
entries.new: ……后来我们从楼上下来，一个人也没找到，那时 Sekimeiya 还没被拿走，仍然在展示柜里。……而且据 Sai 说，有人坐电梯下过楼。{w}我不认为凶手的目标是拿走 Sekimeiya。{w}若真是如此，又特意从 Naomi 的钥匙串上取下了展示柜的钥匙，就不会在我们分头搜两条走廊的时候动手。他会等我们离开，也不会把钥匙丢进你的包里。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: So someone took an opportunity after we found Naomi's body.
entries.new: 也就是说，有人是在我们发现 Naomi 的尸体之后才找到机会的。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yeah. The culprit spent time removing it from her set of keys but didn't take the attic key.{w} All of us found Naomi's body at the same time, and even though I disappeared, you're positive nobody could've picked the key up before I came back, right?
entries.new: 对。凶手花时间把钥匙从她那一串上拆下来，却没有拿阁楼的钥匙。{w}我们发现 Naomi 尸体时大家都在场，而且就算我消失了一阵，你也很肯定在我回来之前没人能捡走那把钥匙，对吧？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I am, and even more so if they had to take it off the keyring.
entries.new: 我很肯定，更别说还得把它从钥匙圈上取下来。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: In that case, when we left her body to put the Sekimeiya in the event room cabinet, it's very likely she still had all of her keys. The people that could've picked it up from that point on were your group and the person who made the sound—someone who couldn't have gone on to use it to unlock the cabinet. It's also likely they were the true culprit, seeing as they didn't pick it up after killing Naomi.
entries.new: 既然如此，我们离开她的尸体、去把 Sekimeiya 放进活动室展示柜的时候，她身上的钥匙很可能还是齐全的。从那时起能捡到钥匙的，只有你们那一组人，还有发出声响的那个人——而那个人不可能拿它去打开展示柜。而且，既然那个人杀了 Naomi 之后没有捡走钥匙，他很可能才是真凶。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It goes back to what we said earlier: the suspects are pretty much only Sai and Akaro.
entries.new: 这就回到刚才说的：嫌疑人基本上只剩 Sai 和 Akaro。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I began moving toward the living room, and Shiroya followed me without asking anything.
entries.new: 我动身往客厅走，Shiroya 一言不发地跟了上来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Akaro entered the room where Naomi died, but he couldn't have unlocked the cabinet. Sai, though, had the chance to do both things. If the search ended while one of them still had the key, they would've chosen to leave it in your purse because you were in their group.{w} You also investigated hallway B, so if Sai hadn't denied it, you could've had a chance to get the key too.
entries.new: Akaro 进过 Naomi 遇害的房间，但他不可能打开展示柜。Sai 却两件事都有机会做。如果搜查结束时钥匙还在他们某个人手上，他们会把钥匙留在你包里，因为你跟他们同组。{w}你也在 B走廊搜过，所以要不是 Sai 否认，你本来也有机会拿到那把钥匙。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: And then Akaro started acting weirdly, purposely remaining on the crystal floor all by himself.
entries.new: 然后 Akaro 就开始举止反常，故意一个人留在水晶层。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...Yeah. None of this makes sense because we found the Sekimeiya in the storeroom. This part is what feels like we might have it backward.
entries.new: ……是啊。这些全都说不通，因为我们是在储藏室找到 Sekimeiya 的。问题就出在这里——感觉我们可能有一处搞反了。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: How so?
entries.new: 怎么说？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I'm not sure yet, because I doubt there could've been any normal method to make the Sekimeiya appear there. Maybe it has to do with its powers, but I think we should look through hallway B in case we can find hints of what actually happened.
entries.new: 我还没想清楚。我不觉得有什么寻常办法能让 Sekimeiya 出现在那种地方。也许跟它的力量有关，不过我想先去 B走廊查一遍，说不定能找到线索，弄清究竟发生了什么。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Without an objection, we continued heading down. I wasn't exactly sure what line we were pursuing, but I knew something strange had to have happened with the hallway B group.
entries.new: 她没有反对，我们便继续往下走。我其实不太确定我们究竟在追哪条线，但我知道 B走廊那一组人身上一定发生过什么古怪的事。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When the Sekimeiya was hidden in room B4, where we first found Naomi...{w} It was hidden inside a temperature regulation cabinet, and that would have happened at a time where we didn't know that the cabinets had inner compartments yet.
entries.new: Sekimeiya 最初被藏起来，是在水晶展室 B4——也就是我们第一次发现 Naomi 的地方……{w}它被藏进了一个控温展示柜，而那会儿我们还不知道这些柜子设有内层隔间。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Anyone could've secretly known this, but think about Katei's perspective. Suripo told him that gemstones had been stolen from a room, and he didn't know which one.{w} Therefore, he had no reason to think they had been gemstones on display instead of the ones kept in those inner compartments, right? ...But the first time we searched, he never looked in those or let us know about them.
entries.new: 这事谁都可能私下知道，但站在 Katei 的立场想想。Suripo 只告诉他有间展室的宝石被偷了，却没说是哪一间。{w}那么他也没理由认为丢的是展出的宝石、而不是内层隔间里存放的那些，对吧？……可我们第一次搜查时，他从没去看过那些隔间，也没跟我们提过。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Maybe he wanted to keep them a secret.
entries.new: ……也许他想把那些东西藏着不说。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: It's possible.
entries.new: 有这个可能。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: As soon as we reached floor 5, we faintly heard someone approaching.
entries.new: 刚到五楼，我们就隐约听见有人靠近。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Oh, hey. Were you coming for me?
entries.new: ……哦，是你们。你们是来找我的？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Sort of... The others are waiting for you in the attic, but we'll go right back up in a bit. What were you doing down there?
entries.new: 算是吧……其他人都在阁楼等你，我们待会儿就上去。你刚才在下面做什么？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Nothing, as I said. I stayed where I was for a few more minutes, sorting my thoughts out.
entries.new: 什么也没做，我说过了。我就在原地多待了几分钟，理了理思绪。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Any reason why you chose a bathroom with a body to stay in?
entries.new: 你偏要待在一间有尸体的洗手间里，是有什么理由吗？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I don't think so... I'll be going. I'm sure Sai's eager to question me.
entries.new: 没有吧……我走了。Sai 肯定正等着审我呢。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: He took off without waiting for a response.
entries.new: 他没等我们回应，径直走了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Maybe he's back to normal. He looked really off earlier.
entries.new: 也许他恢复正常了。刚才他那样子很不对劲。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: He did... I'm not sure how it was for him, but he must've experienced something completely unnatural.
entries.new: 确实……我不知道他那边是什么感受，但他肯定经历了某种完全不合常理的事。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We continued moving down as we wondered what exactly had been up with Akaro.
entries.new: 我们一边往下走，一边琢磨 Akaro 到底出了什么状况。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He said he only teleported and the Sekimeiya was the trigger. Do you believe him?
entries.new: 他说自己只是被传送了，而 Sekimeiya 就是触发点。你信吗？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I'm not sure. It probably was caused by the Sekimeiya in some way, but right before that point, it didn't have any effect on us. I thought earlier that maybe he just traveled a few seconds to the past, which would have been unnoticeable.
entries.new: 不好说。多半是 Sekimeiya 以某种方式造成的，可在那之前，它对我们没有任何影响。我之前想过，也许他只是回到了几秒之前，短得根本察觉不到。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Oh, that's true. But he said he still appeared on the crystal floor, so I think he would've noticed it, and we should've seen him...
entries.new: 哦，也对。可他说自己还是出现在水晶层，那他应该会察觉，我们也该看见他才对……
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yeah... Maybe the shock stopped him from thinking properly, I don't know. I also wonder why he didn't show himself if he was right there the whole time and saw us. And there's still the fact that if he really touched the Sekimeiya, we shouldn't have seen it behind the glass in the cabinet.
entries.new: 是啊……也许是冲击太大，让他没法好好思考，我也说不准。我还想不通，他如果一直都在那儿、也看见我们了，为什么不出声。还有就是——如果他真碰过 Sekimeiya，我们就不该在展示柜的玻璃后面看见它。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: None of it makes much sense.
entries.new: 这些怎么看都说不通。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...{w}I'm already doubting what I said regarding the Sekimeiya's disappearance.
entries.new: ……{w}我刚才说的那些关于 Sekimeiya 消失的推论，我已经开始怀疑了。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Hm?
entries.new: 嗯？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I said that if Naomi's killer took her key, they would've waited before taking the Sekimeiya; they wouldn't have done it while we were all searching the crystal floor.{w} That's not definitely true, though. If Sai or Akaro took the key, they would've waited too.
entries.new: 我说过，如果拿走钥匙的是杀害 Naomi 的凶手，他应该会等到以后再拿 Sekimeiya，不会挑我们全都在水晶层搜查的时候动手。{w}但这也不一定。换成 Sai 或 Akaro 拿了钥匙，他们同样会等。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...{w}Yeah.{w}{w=0.4} They would've kept the key until a better chance came.
entries.new: ……{w}是啊。{w}{w=0.4} 他们会把钥匙留到更好的机会再动手。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Right?{w} But instead, the Sekimeiya was taken while the search was going on.{w} Why? There has to be a reason why they didn't wait.{w} After all, the fact that it happened during the search feels wrong, because it means that nobody who searched could've done it.{w} How did they do it? Whoever hid the Sekimeiya took advantage of the search to appear clean—they didn't wait for a calmer opportunity.
entries.new: 对吧？{w}可事实是，Sekimeiya 偏偏在搜查途中被拿走了。{w}为什么？他们没有等下去，一定有原因。{w}毕竟事情发生在搜查期间，这点很不对劲——那等于说，参与搜查的人都不可能下手。{w}那他们究竟是怎么做到的？藏起 Sekimeiya 的人借搜查洗清了自己，没有等更稳妥的时机。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It's so confusing! People in both hallways could've worked together when I wasn't looking, but is that really it...?{w} It doesn't make any sense! They rushed to hide the Sekimeiya in the storeroom, but they didn't rush to take it out of the cabinet the next time we left the crystal floor. In fact, it should still be there.
entries.new: 太乱了！两条走廊上的人完全可能趁我不注意串通好，可真是这样吗……？{w}完全说不通！他们急着把 Sekimeiya 藏进储藏室，可下一次我们离开水晶层时，他们却不急着把它从展示柜里取出来。照理说，它应该还在那儿才对。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Damn it... I don't want to baselessly suspect everyone, but I don't know how else to approach this.
entries.new: 可恶……我不想毫无根据地怀疑所有人，可除此之外我实在不知道该怎么查。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It's okay, Atsuki. You're just trying to be careful. I wish I could be more help.
entries.new: 没关系，Atsuki。你只是谨慎罢了。要是我能帮上更多忙就好了。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: We arrived at the crystal floor. If no one was hiding nearby, we were the only people there. It was fainter, but as we walked down the last staircase, we could still perceive the smell from earlier.
entries.new: 我们到了水晶层。附近若没人躲着，这里就只有我们两个。走下最后一段楼梯时，先前那股气味还闻得到，只是淡了许多。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Perhaps because nothing about it made sense, we instinctively went to check the second of Naomi's bodies, the place where Akaro had remained.
entries.new: 也许是因为一切都毫无道理，我们下意识地先去查看 Naomi 的第二具尸体，也就是 Akaro 之前停留的地方。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't think anything's different here.
entries.new: 这里看起来没什么异常。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It looks the same. Someone must've locked her inside, and that was the sound we heard...
entries.new: 和之前一样。一定是有人把她锁在了里面，我们听到的声音就是这个……
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: If so, then they should've still been somewhere while we searched.
entries.new: 若真是这样，那我们搜查的时候，那个人应该还在什么地方才对。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Well, when we heard the sound, we all went out of the event room toward hallway A. From there, we could see the staircase and elevator, so we know nobody ran up a floor after that.
entries.new: 唔，听到声音的时候，我们全都出了活动室，朝 A走廊走去。从那里能看见楼梯和电梯，所以之后没人跑上一层楼，这点可以确定。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: If the person responsible expected that and quickly entered the event room from hallway B just behind us, they might've been able to use the Sekimeiya to escape. We still don't know how it works, and we locked the cabinet, but it's possible...
entries.new: 如果那个人料到这一点，趁我们刚走，立刻从背后的 B走廊进入活动室，说不定就能用 Sekimeiya 逃走。我们至今不清楚它的运作原理，展示柜也锁上了，可这还是有可能……
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: It supposedly made Akaro travel later, so that could be right. It might just be inconsistent about when it actually does something.
entries.new: 据说它后来让 Akaro 穿越了时间，所以这也有可能。也许它究竟何时才会发动，本来就没什么定数。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: But then they wouldn't have relied on it to escape. If they used it, they must've known how to properly use it.{w} There's still the same problem, though. The glass in the cabinet would have been down.
entries.new: 可那样的话，他们就不会靠它逃走了。既然用了它，说明他们懂得怎么正确使用。{w} 不过老问题还在——展示柜的玻璃罩应该是放下来的。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That's right...
entries.new: 说得也是……
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: As the conversation had once again shifted to the Sekimeiya's mechanics, we walked to the center of the floor.
entries.new: 话题又一次转到 Sekimeiya 的运作原理上，我们一路走到了楼层中央。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We entered through hallway B and found ourselves in the barren space, only shared by the covered cabinet. The darkness in there was a stark reminder that we'd been victims of an attack, and one that was most likely far from over. I walked up to the cabinet as I spoke.
entries.new: 我们从 B走廊进去，眼前是一片空荡荡的空间，唯有蒙着布罩的展示柜与我们作伴。室内的昏暗无时无刻不在提醒我们：我们遭遇了袭击，而这场袭击多半远未结束。我一边说，一边走到展示柜前。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Do you still have the key?
entries.new: 钥匙还在你身上吗？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: No, it must still be on the bed, assuming nobody picked it up. I didn't wanna just put it back in my purse.
entries.new: 不在，应该还留在床上，前提是没人捡走。我可不想就那么塞回包里。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: So the potentially solitary method to unlock the cabinet was in anyone's possession. I raised the curtain, hoping to finally get more information on what the Sekimeiya could really do.
entries.new: 也就是说，那把很可能是唯一能打开展示柜的钥匙，现在在谁手里都不奇怪。我掀开遮布，盼着这回能多了解一些 Sekimeiya 的能耐。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, instead of helping us piece things together, it appeared the curtain was only covering more questions. Behind it, the glass only protected a cushion, as the Sekimeiya had once again disappeared.
entries.new: 然而，遮布没能帮我们拼出真相，掀开之后反而只露出更多疑问。玻璃罩后面护着的不过是一块坐垫——Sekimeiya 又一次不见了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It's not here? Didn't you see it just before we went up?
entries.new: ……不见了？我们上楼之前，你不是还亲眼见过它吗？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I-I did... I even touched it.
entries.new: 见、见过的……我还摸过它。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Then was Akaro just acting? He could've easily taken it out...
entries.new: 那 Akaro 只是在演戏？他很容易就能把它拿走……
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Unless we assume an unknown culprit is somehow still here, it was him. He did tell us to leave him alone, but I have no idea why he'd want to hide it.
entries.new: 除非我们认定有个不知名的人物还藏在这里，否则只能是他。他确实让我们别去打扰他，可我想不通他为什么要把它藏起来。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: This question still pisses me off. Why would anyone hide the Sekimeiya? There's nothing to gain from it because we can always find it by just searching thoroughly.
entries.new: 这事到现在还让我火大。谁会无缘无故把 Sekimeiya 藏起来？这么做一点好处也没有，只要仔细搜一遍，我们总能找到。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: There might be another reason... What if what they're trying to do is remove it from the cabinet instead of hiding it?
entries.new: 也许还有别的缘由……万一对方的目的不是藏它，而是把它从展示柜里取出来呢？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Just removing it? Oh, because of the temperature?
entries.new: 只是取出来？哦，因为温度？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Maybe. The first time, we found it inside a cabinet that could keep it cool, but it wasn't powered on. It might be related to that.
entries.new: 也许吧。第一次发现它时，它就在一个能给它降温的展示柜里，可那个柜子并没有通电。说不定和这有关。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: They could just unplug this cabinet, which would be much harder to notice. By moving it, they also exposed themselves in front of the cameras.
entries.new: 他们大可以拔掉这个柜子的插头，那样更难被人察觉。把东西挪走，反而让自己暴露在监控摄像头下。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I looked behind just in case, and the cabinet's plug was still inserted into the outlet.
entries.new: 我以防万一朝后面看了一眼，展示柜的插头还好端端插在插座上。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The cameras make me think that the culprit doesn't mind being seen. It'd make sense if it was always Akaro, because he's leaving himself as the only suspect by hiding the Sekimeiya now anyway.
entries.new: 摄像头的事让我觉得，犯人并不介意被人看见。如果从头到尾都是 Akaro，那就说得通了——反正他现在把 Sekimeiya 藏起来，等于把自己变成了唯一的嫌疑人。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: But to accomplish everything, he needs to have used the Sekimeiya's powers multiple times and still did his best to always hide from us. Whoever the culprit is, why do they care so much about avoiding us but aren't fazed by the cameras?
entries.new: 可要办成这么多事，他必须多次动用 Sekimeiya 的力量，同时还得千方百计避开我们。不管犯人是谁，为什么如此在意避开我们，却对摄像头毫不在乎？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...I don't know. They must've caused the power outage in the security room, but all that did was stop us from looking at the recordings. The cameras are still working, so once everyone outside can get back in, they'll be able to look through all of it.
entries.new: ……我不知道。监控室的停电肯定是他们搞的，可那顶多只让我们没法查看录像。摄像头还在正常工作，等外面的人能进来，就能把全部录像翻一遍。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: It might just be that they're confident in their plan. If they intend to vanish as soon as Ashiya enter this place, even if their identity is exposed, they'd still be long gone.
entries.new: 也许只是因为他们对自己的计划有把握。若他们打算一等芦屋的人进来就消失，那么即便身份败露，人也早已远走高飞了。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The fact that they're trying so hard to avoid being seen by us might mean that we already know them. If they're making use of the Sekimeiya, understand how it works, and are creating an alibi for themselves, we could just restrain them once we know who they are. It's like they're hiding the Sekimeiya while also hiding themselves thanks to it.
entries.new: 他们如此费尽心机躲着我们，或许说明我们本就认识这个人。若此人一面利用 Sekimeiya、摸清了它的用法，一面又替自己制造不在场证明，那只要我们查明身份，就能直接把他控制住。就好像他一边把 Sekimeiya 藏起来，一边又借它把自己也藏了起来。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: And at the same time, the fact that Akaro is the main suspect could mean that he isn't responsible; every other action performed by the culprit has managed to keep their identity hidden, but this would directly reveal it.
entries.new: 而与此同时，Akaro 成了头号嫌疑人，这反倒可能说明他并非幕后之人：犯人其余每一步都成功掩住了自己的身份，唯独这一手会直接把自己暴露出来。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Even though Katei has always looked like the most suspicious person, he could've accomplished almost everything through normal means. At no point was it necessary for him to use the Sekimeiya for anything, and it's very likely the culprit has been making use of it to stay out of sight and remain less suspicious.
entries.new: 尽管 Katei 一直显得最可疑，但他几乎每件事都能用寻常手段办到。他从未有过非用 Sekimeiya 不可的时候，而真正的犯人很可能一直在借它藏身，让自己显得没那么可疑。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: So the blame just falls on Katei?
entries.new: 所以怀疑就全落到 Katei 头上了？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I doubt it's just that. He's still hiding a bunch of things for sure. Regarding the Sekimeiya, the attic, and the way we got trapped.
entries.new: 恐怕不止如此。他肯定还瞒着不少事。关于 Sekimeiya、阁楼，还有我们是怎么被困住的。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: For now, since we're here, we could try to find the Sekimeiya. The others must be questioning Akaro and, well, wondering where we are. There aren't many places to hide it, and if we do find it, we could learn something important. Assuming Akaro didn't do it, it means that someone else took advantage of him being distracted.
entries.new: 眼下既然来都来了，我们就试着找找 Sekimeiya 吧。其他人想必正在盘问 Akaro，嗯，也在想我们跑哪儿去了。能藏东西的地方不多，真找到了，说不定能有重要发现。假如不是 Akaro 干的，那就说明有人趁他分神下了手。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It could've been an "unknown culprit", but Sai and Katei were actually viable suspects too, as they'd claimed to be in the living room while we'd been occupied by an impossible recording. They would've had just enough time.
entries.new: 那可能是「不知名的犯人」，但 Sai 和 Katei 其实同样有嫌疑。我们被那段根本不可能存在的录音缠住时，他们声称自己在客厅，时间刚好来得及。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Or would you prefer to go back to the attic? Sorry, I just dragged you all the way down here without asking you. Being alone could be dangerous, so we can go back if you want.
entries.new: 还是说，你更想回阁楼？抱歉，我没问一声就把你一路拖到这儿。一个人待着可能危险，你想回去的话，我们就回去。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...No, I'd like to look for it.{w} We were going to look through hallway B, so let's start with that. If we figure out how the Sekimeiya appeared in the storeroom, we might be able to find out who did it.
entries.new: ……不用，我想找找看。{w} 我们本来就打算把 B走廊查一遍，就从那里开始吧。要是能弄清楚 Sekimeiya 是怎么出现在储藏室的，也许就能查出是谁干的。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I nodded. It wasn't impossible someone was hiding, but they could've easily left already, and it wasn't our goal to begin a full search of the building. We intended to find the Sekimeiya, which was more likely to be on the crystal floor.
entries.new: 我点了点头。不能说没人藏在这里，但对方也完全可能早就离开了，况且我们的目的并不是把整栋楼搜个底朝天。我们要找的是 Sekimeiya，而它更可能在水晶层。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Which room do we start with?
entries.new: 先从哪一间开始？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It shouldn't matter. I think that's the first one Akaro looked through.
entries.new: 哪一间都无所谓吧。我记得那是 Akaro 最先查的一间。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: We walked to room B3 in silence...{w} It was undeniable that staying put somewhere was much safer than being there by ourselves; someone had died, and we were up against an elusive unknown...
entries.new: 我们沉默着走向 B3 展室……{w} 不可否认，待在原地比我们俩单独行动要安全得多。已经有人死了，而我们面对的是一个行踪难测的不明人物……
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We'd even heard that bizarre recording just minutes ago, but we were trying to understand what had happened to the Sekimeiya.
entries.new: 就在几分钟前，我们才听过那段诡异的录音，如今却一心想着查清 Sekimeiya 究竟出了什么事。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After all, it made me travel through time.{w} We hadn't spoken about it at length, but it was evident both of us wanted to understand how it worked...
entries.new: 毕竟，它让我穿越了时间。{w} 这件事我们还没细谈过，但显然，我们俩都想弄明白它到底如何运作……
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...We opened the door and entered without high hopes.
entries.new: ……我们推开门走进去，并没有抱多大期望。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I started with the rightmost cabinets. Only a few of them could be opened up, but there was always space behind and under them, making it a considerably lengthy process.
entries.new: 我从最右边的展示柜开始查。能打开的只有少数几个，但柜子后面和底下总有空隙，查起来相当费时。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Just as I thought that, Shiroya spoke.
entries.new: 我正这么想着，Shiroya 开口了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: W-Wait, it's here.
entries.new: 等、等一下，它在这儿。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I turned around abruptly. Shiroya was looking inside the cabinet she'd started with. I approached her, thinking that perhaps I'd misheard.
entries.new: 我猛地转过身。Shiroya 正往她最先查看的那个展示柜里看。我走过去，心想也许是我听错了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Do you mean the Sekimeiya?
entries.new: ……你是说 Sekimeiya？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes... Look, it's under the cushion, and there's a lot of space beneath it too. I thought I saw a slight bump, so I checked.
entries.new: 嗯……你看，就在坐垫下面，垫子底下空间也不小。我好像看到有个地方微微凸起，就查了一下。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I spotted it when I got closer. Shiroya had removed the cushion with the gems, which uncovered the space beneath it. There, the Sekimeiya was hidden.
entries.new: 走近之后我就看见了。Shiroya 拿开了嵌着宝石的坐垫，露出底下的夹层。Sekimeiya 就藏在那里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...So, once again, out of all the places to choose from, they chose to hide it in a room with security cameras.
entries.new: ……结果他又一次，在所有能挑的地方里，偏偏选了间装着监控摄像头的展室来藏它。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We'd gotten used to our searches not ending as desired, so such a quick result threw me off.
entries.new: 我们早已习惯搜寻无果，这么快就有了结果，反倒让我一时愣住了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It can't have been here for very long. What do we do? Do you wanna try to, um... activate it?
entries.new: 它应该没在这里放多久。我们怎么办？你要不要试着，呃……启动它？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...The last time, it worked right after it was hidden. It's obvious that the culprit is behind this, so by learning how it works, we might be able to understand a few things.
entries.new: ……上次，它刚被藏起来就发动了。这背后显然是犯人在搞鬼，所以只要弄明白它的运作方式，或许就能看清一些事。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That's true, but won't it be dangerous? ...You saw how Akaro reacted.
entries.new: 话是没错，可这样不会很危险吗？……你也看到 Akaro 的反应了。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I felt fine the last time. I also touched it before going to the attic and nothing happened, so it's possible it won't be any different now.
entries.new: 上次我没什么感觉。去阁楼之前我也碰过它，什么都没发生，所以这次说不定也一样。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It might've been dangerous, but I wanted to know if going to the past was truly achievable. I felt overwhelmed by the simple-looking object I had in front of me.
entries.new: 这或许很危险，但我想确认回到过去是否真的可行。眼前这件东西看着不起眼，却让我心绪难平。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I see. ...Try it, then.
entries.new: 原来如此。……那就试试吧。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: If it works, I'll go back to the past again. If that happens, it means that I might already be outside the door, waiting for the past me to travel. Assuming that's the case, I'll come in as soon as I disappear to meet back up with you. Keep looking at the Sekimeiya in case it changes colors.
entries.new: 要是成功了，我会再次回到过去。这样一来，就说明我可能已经等在门外，等着过去的我穿越。若果真如此，等我一消失，我便会立刻进来与你会合。你继续盯着 Sekimeiya，以防它变色。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: A-All right.
entries.new: 好、好的。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Was another version of me... right outside the room?{w} If we went to look and that version acted surprised to be found... assuming the past couldn't be changed and only looked at from a different perspective, it would mean that I needed to travel to the past and recreate a fake reaction.
entries.new: 另一个我……就在房间外？{w} 如果我们出去查看，而那个我装作被发现时很惊讶……假设过去无法改变，只能从另一个角度去观察，那就意味着我得回到过去，把那个假反应重新演一遍。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Something like that was ridiculous; if we went to check outside, that version of me would know that we'd done so and would hide accordingly. It was pointless to even try it, as we didn't know if the travel would work in the first place.
entries.new: 这种事太荒唐了。我们真去外面查看，那个我自然会知道，并会相应地躲起来。况且连穿越能不能成功都还不知道，贸然去试也毫无意义。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'll touch it. If nothing happens, let's bring it upstairs. Leaving it in the cabinet would just provide the culprit with another opportunity to hide it, assuming it wasn't Akaro's doing.
entries.new: 我来碰它。要是没反应，我们就把它搬到楼上。如果这不是 Akaro 干的，把东西留在展示柜里，只会再给犯人一次藏起它的机会。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah.{w} I'll wait here. I'm a little scared to touch it, but I think it's better if one of us stays here.
entries.new: 嗯。{w} 我在这里等着。我有点怕碰它，不过我觉得还是留一个人在比较好。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I agree.
entries.new: 我也这么想。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I stretched my arm toward it. Hesitant at what was about to happen, Shiroya backed up while I shortened the distance between my hand and the Sekimeiya.{w} As soon as I made the slightest physical contact with it, I felt a ridiculously painful burn on my fingers. It lasted less than a split second, and I was somewhere else.
entries.new: 我朝它伸出手。Shiroya 似乎对即将发生的事有些迟疑，向后退开；我的手则一点点靠近 Sekimeiya。{w} 指尖刚触到它，一阵剧烈的灼痛便从手指上窜起。那感觉只持续了不到半瞬，下一刻，我已身在别处。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Behind Bars
entries.new: 铁窗之后

entries.text: Before I could comprehend that it worked, I fell to the floor and hurt myself. Disoriented, I looked around.
entries.new: 我还没反应过来它真的生效了，人已摔在地上，磕得生疼。我晕头转向地环顾四周。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It took me a few seconds to recognize where I was. In front of me were blank screens, and my surroundings were overall dim. It was the security room.{w} My pose had also changed. I'd appeared in front of the desk and immediately fallen backward, hitting my back on the chair.
entries.new: 我花了几秒钟才认出自己在哪。面前是一排黑着的屏幕，四周光线昏暗。这里是监控室。{w} 我的姿势也变了——我出现在桌前，随即向后摔倒，后背撞上了椅子。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the fuck...? Was I sitting...?
entries.new: 搞什么鬼……？我刚才……是坐着的？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That was what it felt like. I'd been sitting on top of nothing, which resulted in my fall.
entries.new: 感觉就是这样。我方才像是坐在了一片虚空上，所以才会摔倒。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I sighed and stood up. It had worked again, and I'd appeared in the security room instead. I was about to exit the room when I realized that I had a much smarter option.
entries.new: 我叹了口气，站起身。它又生效了，而这次我出现在监控室。我正要出门，忽然想到还有一个更聪明的办法。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I dragged the chair I'd knocked away back to its place and sat on it. Then, I moved the mouse around to power on the screens.
entries.new: 我把撞开的椅子拖回原位，坐了上去，然后晃了晃鼠标，让屏幕亮起来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They all lit up at once, which made me squint momentarily.{w} ...The large desktop appeared, but I only directed my eyes at the lower right side of the middle screen.{w} {time=11:10} was the time that I saw.
entries.new: 所有屏幕同时亮起，刺得我眯了眯眼。{w} ……大桌面显现出来，我只把视线投向中间屏幕的右下角。{w} 上面显示的时间是 {time=11:10}。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I did go back to the past once again... This is confirmation that I wasn't going crazy.
entries.new: 我确实又一次回到了过去……这证明我没有发疯。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The last time we checked the time, Sai said it was {time=11:36}, and he already confirmed to me that his time is the same as this computer's.
entries.new: 上次看时间时，Sai 说当时是 {time=11:36}，而且他已经跟我确认过，他的时间和这台电脑一致。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I'd estimate that after that point, fifteen more minutes passed until I touched the Sekimeiya, which means that I went approximately forty minutes into the past.
entries.new: 我估计从那时起又过了十五分钟，我才碰到 Sekimeiya，也就是说，我回到了大约四十分钟前。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Forty minutes... twice the last amount. Is that a coincidence...?
entries.new: 四十分钟……是上次的两倍。这会是巧合吗……？
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: It could just be that the amount of time traveled is also determined randomly. I thought earlier that could be the case with the location you go to, but given I appeared sitting down right in front of this desk, there must be more to that.
entries.new: 也可能穿越的时间长度同样是随机决定的。我之前就想过，落点或许也是如此；但既然我出现时正坐在这张桌前，事情肯定没那么简单。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: At this point in time, I should be on the fifth floor with Shiroya. At {time=11:20}, we were all inside the event room after regrouping, discussing the elevator movements.
entries.new: 此刻，我应该正和 Shiroya 在五楼。到了 {time=11:20}，我们已经重新会合，都在活动室里讨论电梯的异动。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: When we heard a noise...{w=0.5} that's right!{w=0.4} I can attempt to see what made it, and most importantly...{w} what happened to Naomi.
entries.new: 我们听到声响的时候……{w=0.5}对了！{w=0.4} 我可以试着去看看那声音是从哪儿来的，更重要的是……{w} Naomi 到底出了什么事。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I tensed up. It was possible a murder was about to occur. We'd deemed the bathroom empty before searching the other floors, and I was in the timeframe where the second Naomi had died.
entries.new: 我浑身一紧。也许一场谋杀即将发生。我们在搜查其他楼层前，曾确认洗手间里空无一人，而我现在正处在第二个 Naomi 死去的那段时间里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I exited the security room slowly. We'd searched through the whole floor before going up, so there shouldn't have been anyone hiding who I didn't know about. However, the elevator movements still remained unexplained. Someone had arrived on the crystal floor while we'd been investigating the others.
entries.new: 我慢慢走出监控室。我们上楼前搜过整层，按理说不该有我不知道的人躲在这里。可是电梯的异动仍然无法解释。在我们调查其他楼层时，有人来到了水晶层。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Could I even consider preventing Naomi's death? If causal loops were how time travel worked, I wouldn't be able to. ...Did I have a way to be sure, though?
entries.new: 我难道真能考虑去阻止 Naomi 的死吗？如果时间穿越遵循的是因果循环，那我就做不到。……可是，我有办法确认这一点吗？
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even though what happened the first time indicated that modifying the past wouldn't happen, the only way I could learn that with certainty was by attempting it.
entries.new: 难道我真的可以尝试去阻止 Naomi 的死吗？如果时间穿越遵循的是因果循环，那我就做不到。……可是，我有办法确认这一点吗？
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Incidentally, by attempting to change the past, I was putting myself at risk. We hadn't found my dead body, so I could feel a bit calm in that regard. However, if my actions could alter the past, that would no longer be valid.
entries.new: 话说回来，尝试改变过去，也等于把我自己置于危险之中。我们还没有发现我的尸体，所以这一点还能让我稍微安心。可如果我的行动真能改变过去，那我就不能这么安心了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Should I be worried about that? If I try to prevent Naomi's death and subsequently die for it, that could make my time travel an impossibility and lead into an obvious paradox. How would the universe handle that? Would it even allow it?
entries.new: 我该为此担心吗？如果我试图阻止 Naomi 的死，并因此丧命，那我的时间穿越就会变得不可能，进而导向一个显而易见的悖论。宇宙会怎么处理这种情况？它会允许这种事发生吗？
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Maybe anything I try to change the past will be completely futile. I just have to wait and see what I can do.
entries.new: 也许我想改变过去的任何尝试都会彻底徒劳。我只能等着看，自己究竟能做到什么。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: From hallway A, I saw people walking down the stairs. I dashed toward the lobby, knowing that they wouldn't see me.
entries.new: 我从 A走廊看见有人正走下楼梯。我知道他们不会看见我，便朝大厅跑去。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They've already come, so the elevator movements have already occurred. It's possible Naomi's already dead. Did I appear too late to see what happened...?
entries.new: 他们已经来了，说明电梯已经动过了。Naomi 可能已经死了。我出现得太晚，没能看到经过吗……？
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I moved to hallway B. I knew we'd shortly enter the event room through the opposite door, so I'd be safe there.
entries.new: 我转移到了 B 走廊。我知道我们很快就会从另一扇门进入活动室，所以待在那里应该安全。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Are they really not going to see me...? I went forty minutes into the past, and even though nobody claimed to have seen me, it appears I was always on this floor...
entries.new: 他们真的不会看见我吗……？我回到了四十分钟前，虽然没人说见过我，但我似乎一直待在这一层……
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I approached the bathrooms slowly, trying to remain silent. From the middle of the hallway, though, I noticed that something important hadn't happened yet.
entries.new: 我放轻脚步，慢慢靠近洗手间。可走到走廊中段时，我注意到一件重要的事还没有发生。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The door... It's open.
entries.new: 门……开着。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: We'd found the bathroom door locked, and inside was Naomi's body. Since it wasn't locked at that moment, something was bound to happen if I just watched from a distance.
entries.new: 我们发现时，洗手间的门是锁着的，里面躺着 Naomi 的尸体。既然此刻门还没有锁，只要我远远看着，就一定会有什么事发生。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Unfortunately, the door was only barely ajar, so I couldn't see inside.
entries.new: 可惜门只开了一条细缝，我看不见里面。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I kept moving and entered the cleaning room, which would provide me with the best view of the bathrooms without being spotted.
entries.new: 我继续往前走，进了清洁间。这里既能清楚看到洗手间，又不容易被人发现。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A little paranoid, I looked behind me to make sure there was no one else there.
entries.new: 我有些疑神疑鬼，回头确认身后没有别人。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Who's going to appear? Will I be able to see the killer's identity? Naomi might also show up at any moment, but from where?
entries.new: 接下来出现的人会是谁？我能看清凶手的身份吗？Naomi 也可能随时出现，可她是从哪里来的？
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: This floor was empty, and the rest up to the attic were just investigated too... Maybe whoever's about to appear will travel from the future if they haven't been in the attic the whole time.
entries.new: 这一层空无一人，往上直到阁楼的其他楼层也都刚查过……如果那个人并非一直待在阁楼里，接下来出现的人或许就是从未来穿越而来的。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: It's unlikely anyone exited the attic through the main door, given the footprints. Even though the elevator should've been on the fifth floor, it was below the third. Someone from the attic could've called it, arrived here, and then sent it back up with no one inside. That'd fall into place with what Sai heard.
entries.new: 从脚印来看，不太可能有人从正门离开阁楼。电梯本该停在五楼，实际却停在三楼以下。也许有人从阁楼叫了电梯，来到这一层，又让空电梯返回楼上。这样就能和 Sai 听到的动静对上了。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: It also means that person must now be on this floor, and most importantly, that Shiroya and I missed the elevator's sound three times. Is that really a possibility...?
entries.new: 这同时也意味着，那个人此刻一定就在这一层；更要紧的是，Shiroya 和我竟然三次都没听见电梯的声音。这种事真的可能吗……？
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I kept watching for a few minutes. Eventually, the indistinct voices I'd been hearing faded away, indicating that the group had gone to the event room.
entries.new: 我又继续观察了几分钟。耳边那些若有若无的说话声终于渐渐远去——那群人应该是去了活动室。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It has to happen at any moment. We did hear a noise, and the door hasn't been locked yet.
entries.new: ……应该就在这一两分钟内了。我们确实听到过响声，而那扇门还没有上锁。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I remained motionless, peeking through the small gap in my door. Was I about to witness a murder? Would I see a person popping into existence out of nowhere? Where would they go then?
entries.new: 我一动不动，透过门缝往外看。我这是要亲眼目睹一场凶杀吗？还是会看见一个人凭空出现？那之后，那个人又会去哪里？
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If the second Naomi isn't dead yet, both her and the culprit have to come. One of them is accounted for given the elevator movements, but what about the other one? ...Or were both of them responsible for the elevator trips?
entries.new: 如果第二个 Naomi 还没有死，那她和凶手就都得来过这里。按电梯的动静，其中一个人的行踪已经能对上，那另一个呢？……又或者，那几趟电梯本就是他们两个都有份？
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Before I could continue imagining all sorts of scenarios, it began. Naomi was coming from hallway C.
entries.new: 我还没来得及继续设想各种情形，事情就开始了。Naomi 正从 C 走廊那边走来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There she is...! Should I show myself?
entries.new: 她来了……！我要不要现身？
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I couldn't decide if that was a good idea. There was still no culprit to be found, so I chose to hold off.
entries.new: 我拿不准这样做是否妥当。连凶手的影子都没见到，我决定先按兵不动。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Akaro's description of Naomi's face fell short of her actual expression. She was visibly terrified, breathing heavily, moving oddly, and stopping in place every few seconds.
entries.new: Akaro 对 Naomi 神情的描述，远不及她此刻的真实模样。她显然惊恐到了极点——呼吸急促，动作透着古怪，每隔几秒就停在原地。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even though I was a fair distance away, I saw pure distress all over her. What had she experienced? Did she know her own body had been found?{w} Was she aware of what would happen to her...?
entries.new: 尽管隔着一段距离，我也能一眼看出她满心惶恐。她究竟经历了什么？她知不知道自己的尸体已经被发现了？{w}她清不清楚自己接下来会落得什么下场……？
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She must've traveled to the past at least once, or her own existence wouldn't make sense...
entries.new: 她至少穿越回过去一次，否则她的存在本身就说不通……
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Finally, after a very long breath that seemed to give her some confidence, she did what I thought she'd do: she headed toward the bathrooms.
entries.new: 终于，她长长地呼出一口气，仿佛从中汲取了些许勇气，然后做出了我预料中的举动——朝洗手间走去。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She opened the women's and looked inside it. It appeared she was searching for something, and given she didn't look around very much, it might've been a person.
entries.new: 她推开女洗手间的门，往里看了看。她似乎在找什么，但她没怎么四处看，那要找的或许是一个人。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Quickly, something caught her attention inside the other bathroom. I couldn't know what it was, but as she placed her hand on the doorknob, her stance gave away that she was wary of whatever was behind the door.
entries.new: 很快，另一间洗手间里的什么动静吸引了她的注意。我不知道那是什么，但光看她握上门把的姿势，就能看出她对门后的东西心存戒备。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I hadn't seen anything strange happening in the bathroom since I'd begun watching. Was it possible that someone had been there the whole time?
entries.new: 从我盯梢开始，洗手间里一直没出现任何异常。难道真的有人一直待在里面？
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Naomi opened the door carefully, keeping her guard as high as it could've been.{w} I bit my lip tightly. When the door was open, she looked inside.
entries.new: Naomi 小心翼翼地推开门，戒备已经到了极点。{w}我用力咬住嘴唇。门开之后，她朝里面望去。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Since the knob was on the left, it was impossible for me to see what she'd seen, but her tension slightly lowered once she saw the contents of the tiny room. At the same time, mine increased, as I knew what was probably about to happen.
entries.new: 门把在左侧，我根本看不到她所见的情形；但那间狭小房间里的景象似乎让她稍稍放松了紧绷的神经。与此同时，我的心却提得更紧了——我清楚接下来多半会发生什么。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was too far to hear her, but she was speaking. Someone had really been inside the bathroom the entire time.
entries.new: 距离太远，我听不见她的声音，但她在说话。洗手间里真的有人，而且一直待到现在。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It didn't make sense. That person had to be the source of the elevator movements, so where had Naomi come from? She didn't have the attic key, and she couldn't have come from the future either, as that was about to become impossible...
entries.new: 这说不通。电梯的动静只能出自那个人之手，那么 Naomi 又是从哪儿冒出来的？她手里没有阁楼的钥匙，也不可能是从未来过来的——毕竟那很快就将变成不可能……
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Out of nowhere, Naomi's body was pulled from the inside.{w} I felt as if my heart was pulled along with her. I couldn't see her anymore, and two people were in the bathroom, their figures hidden from me.
entries.new: 冷不丁地，Naomi 的身体被从里面拽了进去。{w}我的心仿佛也跟着被拽走了。她的身影消失了，洗手间里有两个人，我却一个也看不见。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd probably never had the chance to stop it, and a camera must've at least caught the image of her murderer, but during the few seconds that I was pathetically scared without actually being in danger, I knew that the life of a person was being taken right in front of me. Despite my future knowledge and advantageous position, I hadn't done anything to prevent it.
entries.new: 也许我从来就没有机会阻止，而监控至少应该拍下了凶手的模样。可就在那几秒里，我明明身处安全之地，却怕得如此可悲——我清楚地知道，一条人命正在我眼前被夺走。我明明知晓未来，又占着这样的位置，却什么都没做。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd been thinking that at least the culprit would have to escape while I watched until I realized how inhuman that was.
entries.new: 我竟一直想着，至少凶手逃走的时候，我总能看在眼里——直到我意识到，这念头有多冷酷。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The universe wouldn't allow me to change the past? That was ridiculous, and if anything, it was providing me with a way to do it.{w} I bolted to the bathroom as fast as I could. I definitely still had time to change the past.
entries.new: 宇宙不许我改变过去？荒唐。真要说的话，它反倒给了我改变过去的机会。{w}我拼尽全力冲向洗手间。我绝对还有时间改变过去。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It wasn't too late, and I could trap the culprit inside. I wouldn't let them escape, and it would change the past in some way.
entries.new: 还来得及，我可以把凶手困在里面。我绝不会让他逃掉——这样一来，过去多少会被改变。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But that thought evaporated when I heard a sound in front of me.{w} Before I could reach the bathroom, the door was forcefully shut from the inside and then locked. I recognized the sound as soon as I heard it: it was the one we'd heard from the event room.
entries.new: 然而身前传来的一声响，让这个念头瞬间消散。{w}我还没跑到洗手间，门就从里面被用力关上，随后落了锁。那声音我一听就认了出来——正是我们在活动室里听到过的响动。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...How? It should've been impossible since the killer was still inside. However, I didn't have time to think about it. Faster than I'd ever run, I scrambled to the stairs, knowing that in less than a couple seconds, Erina's gaze would seal off the entire floor.
entries.new: ……怎么可能？凶手明明还在里面，这门理应锁不上才对。可我无暇细想，用前所未有的速度奔向楼梯——我知道，不出几秒，Erina 的视线就会封死整层楼。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I made it before I was spotted only because I'd reacted fast enough, but... it didn't make any sense.{w} We were going to search through the entire floor and find no culprit.
entries.new: 全靠反应够快，我才赶在被发现之前脱身，可是……这一切根本说不通。{w}我们接下来会把整层楼搜个遍，却一个凶手都找不到。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Were Erina and Isla going to let them escape? If so, I was about to see it, and since I was one floor higher, I could hear the elevator too. It was still on the crystal floor.
entries.new: Erina 和 Isla 会放任凶手逃走吗？如果是，那我很快就能亲眼看到。而且我高了一层，电梯的动静也听得见——它现在还停在水晶层。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Once again, I waited, watching over the stairs from afar.{w} However, a couple minutes later, nobody had gone up. At that time, we were already next to the locked door, and we would only find Naomi inside.
entries.new: 我再次等待着，远远盯着楼梯。{w}可几分钟过去了，没有一个人上来。那时我们已经站在那扇锁着的门前，而我们只会在里面找到 Naomi。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The way we'd coordinated ourselves back then had been effective. Erina and Isla prevented me from going down and seeing what happened to Akaro, which was also something I'd wanted to find out.
entries.new: 当时我们的分工确实奏效。Erina 和 Isla 拦住了我，让我没法下楼去看 Akaro 出了什么事——而那也正是我想弄清楚的。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So, by rushing to the door, I didn't change anything.{w} That always happened, and yet we didn't find the person who should've been inside. Like I thought, the past won't change. As soon as I determined that I was going to do it, I was blocked off.
entries.new: 也就是说，我冲向那扇门，什么也没能改变。{w}事情总是如此，可我们依然没找到那个本该在里面的人。果然，过去无法改变。我刚下定决心要动手，路就被堵死了。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Although before I say that for sure, I have to verify that they really didn't find someone and that everything is happening as I remember.
entries.new: 不过在下定论之前，我必须确认他们真的没找到人，确认一切都和我记忆中一样在发生。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: ...{w}But this means that something happened to the killer. Did they go back to the past before we found them? They locked the door as soon as I approached it, so they must've escaped after that point.
entries.new: ……{w}可这就意味着凶手出了什么事。他们是在被我们发现之前回到过去了吗？我一靠近，门就被锁上了，所以他们一定是在那之后才逃走的。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: There's a big problem. The Sekimeiya is currently in the event room. It's clear that under some circumstances, it does make you travel to the past, but they couldn't have used it unless we're severely misunderstanding how it works.
entries.new: 这里有个大问题。Sekimeiya 现在就在活动室里。在某些情况下它确实会让人穿越回过去，这一点已经很明确了；可凶手不可能用到它——除非我们严重误解了它的运作方式。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: If touching it physically is a requirement to travel, anyone inside the bathroom couldn't have used it. Is there any way to get around that?
entries.new: 如果穿越的前提是亲手触碰它，那洗手间里的人根本用不上它。有没有什么办法能绕开这一点？
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: For example, since we had inspected the whole floor earlier, it's very likely that the culprit appeared from the future. Could they have brought the Sekimeiya with them and then used it to escape from the bathroom?
entries.new: 比方说，既然我们先前已经查过整层楼，那凶手极有可能是从未来过来的。会不会是他们把 Sekimeiya 一起带了过来，再靠它从洗手间逃走？
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I don't know how that would be possible. The Sekimeiya is the cause of the travels, so you shouldn't be able to travel with it too.
entries.new: 这怎么可能做到，我想不通。Sekimeiya 本身就是穿越的起因，没道理能带着它一起穿越。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: So then, what method could they have used to disappear like that...? Why did they kill Naomi? And while we're at it, who the fuck is this person?
entries.new: 那么，他们究竟用了什么法子，才能那样凭空消失……？又为什么要杀 Naomi？还有——这个人他妈到底是谁？
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: "Someone who will travel to the past".{w} We have that person: Akaro.{w} He's about to travel to the past right now, but for some reason, we won't find him again until later.
entries.new: 「一个将要穿越回过去的人」。{w}我们正好有这么一个人：Akaro。{w}他马上就要穿越回过去了，可不知为何，我们要等到更晚些才会再次找到他。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Did he have a way to escape the bathroom? Was he the one who shut and locked the door before I reached it...?
entries.new: 他有办法逃出洗手间吗？在我赶到之前把门关上并上锁的，难道就是他……？
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: My whole body felt like a coiled spring, and I'd been continuously biting my lip. I couldn't get the thought that I'd let Naomi die out of my head.
entries.new: 我全身像绷紧的弹簧，嘴唇也被自己咬了一遍又一遍。我让 Naomi 死了——这个念头怎么也甩不掉。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...How was that even possible, though!? She had died twice!
entries.new: ……可这怎么可能！？她已经死过两次了！
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I made a plan in my head: if Akaro was responsible, he had to be the one who'd hidden the Sekimeiya while we were in the attic.{w} We'd walk up in a few minutes, and I knew for a fact that we wouldn't look through every floor.
entries.new: 我在心里盘算：如果凶手是 Akaro，那么趁我们待在阁楼的时候把 Sekimeiya 藏起来的人一定是他。{w}再过几分钟我们就会上去，而我清楚地知道，我们不会逐层搜查。
entries.speaker: i
