entries.text: As long as I hid myself in a partition, I wouldn't be seen. Afterward, I could go down again and see who'd hidden the Sekimeiya. Once more, I'd have a chance to see the murderer firsthand.{w} And if Akaro had been telling the truth about seeing us during our inspection, I would see him for sure.
entries.new: 只要躲在隔断后面，就不会被发现。之后我可以再下去一趟，看看究竟是谁藏起了 Sekimeiya。这样我又有机会亲眼见到凶手。{w}而如果 Akaro 说他在我们搜查时看见了我们，这话属实，那我就一定能看见他。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I recalled our movements downstairs. Erina and Isla stayed in place, observing the path between floors while the rest of us moved back and forth between the two rooms with their individual Naomis. Eventually, after exiting the event room, we lost track of Akaro.
entries.new: 我回想了一下我们在楼下的行动。Erina 和 Isla 留在原处，盯着楼层之间的通道；其余人则来回奔走于两个房间之间，两个房间里各有一个 Naomi。最后，走出活动室之后，我们就跟丢了 Akaro。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We'd searched through the whole floor after that, and I could attempt to repeat that myself.{w} I waited out the brief time until there was a safe way down.
entries.new: 那之后我们把整层楼搜了一遍，而我也可以试着照做一遍。{w}我熬过那段短暂的时间，等到能安全下楼的时候。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After four or five minutes, I saw the group coming up the stairs. We were going to the attic, which confirmed that Erina and Isla had never gone anywhere. They were definitely watching the entire time.
entries.new: 四五分钟后，我看见一行人沿着楼梯上来。我们正要前往阁楼——这也证实了 Erina 和 Isla 自始至终都守在原处。她们一定全程都在盯着。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I slipped into the offices to avoid being seen.
entries.new: 我闪身躲进办公室，以免被发现。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When the group was gone, I slowly stepped out. Nobody had the chance to pass by after them—I'd been watching the glass from the second partition.{w} The crystal floor was isolated, and according to Akaro, he had to be there.
entries.new: 等一行人离开后，我才慢慢走出来。他们走后没人再经过——我一直从第二道隔断后面盯着玻璃。{w}水晶层是封闭的，而按 Akaro 的说法，他一定就在那里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I moved down. I couldn't do an optimal search since I was only one person, but I should've been able to find someone who wasn't deliberately hiding from me.
entries.new: 我下了楼。只靠我一个人，搜查不可能做到滴水不漏，但只要对方没有刻意躲着我，我总该能找到人。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Akaro specifically said he'd only "teleported". Regardless of the veracity of that, he had to still be on the crystal floor.
entries.new: Akaro 特别强调过，自己只是「传送」过去的。这话是真是假暂且不论，他应该仍待在水晶层。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I opened the door to the elevator, revealing its barren interior.
entries.new: 我打开电梯门，里面空无一物。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Next, I looked at the bathrooms, which only contained Naomi's body the way I remembered leaving it—not yet covered by a curtain. It was further confirmation that I was reliving something I'd already experienced, just from another viewpoint.
entries.new: 接着我又去看了卫生间。里面只有 Naomi 的遗体，和我记忆中离开时一样——还没有被遮布盖住。这进一步证实，我正从另一个视角重温已经经历过的事。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Akaro had stated that he didn't go up any floors, so even though I couldn't keep track of the entire area, he had to be lying if I didn't see him.
entries.new: Akaro 说过自己没有上过任何一层楼。我虽然无法盯住整片区域，但只要没看到他，那他就是在说谎。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I began looking through every room. I'd seen other people do it, but I'd never personally been the one to inspect.{w} Investigating like that felt a bit paradoxical: if Akaro was in one of the rooms, he would see me even though he'd never mentioned it to us. Despite that, I continued.
entries.new: 我开始逐间查看。以前都是看别人这么做，自己从没亲手查过。{w} 这样查总觉得有点矛盾：假如 Akaro 就在某个房间里，他会看到我，可这件事他从没跟我们提过。尽管如此，我还是继续查了下去。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The cleaning and staff rooms were empty, and so were the first few crystal rooms. Once I entered the event room, I saw the Sekimeiya still there, revealing that it would soon be moved.
entries.new: 清洁间和员工室都空着，最初的几间水晶展室也一样。走进活动室时，我看到 Sekimeiya 还在原处，这说明它很快就会被转移。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I continued with the remaining rooms in hallway B, which all appeared empty. Even though Akaro's body was the biggest out of everyone's, he could still fit inside a cabinet. It was outlandish to think he would hide in one, but I couldn't ignore them just because of that.
entries.new: 我接着查完 B 走廊剩下的房间，全都空荡荡的。Akaro 虽然是我们当中块头最大的，可要藏进展示柜也不是不可能。他会躲在那种地方，想想都荒唐，但我也不能因为这个就不去看一眼。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After the mechanical room, I began the hallway A search.{w} A few minutes later, I'd confirmed that it was fully vacant.
entries.new: 查完机械室，我开始搜 A 走廊。{w} 几分钟后，我确认那里一个人也没有。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I knew how suspicious that was. Surely, if Akaro was there and wasn't up to anything, he would've been drawn in by the noise. I should've seen him.
entries.new: 我知道这有多可疑。如果 Akaro 就在那里、又没有做什么见不得人的事，他一定会被声响引来。我本该看到他的。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Had he seen me all by myself and avoided me? If so, he would know that I was about to travel to the past when he saw me and Shiroya heading downstairs—we'd told him that we all stayed together the whole time...{w} If he'd hidden the Sekimeiya, he would be aware that we were about to find it. And despite that, he hadn't stopped or questioned us.
entries.new: 难道他看到我独自一人，就故意避开？如果真是这样，那他看见我和 Shiroya 下楼时，就该知道我们马上要穿越到过去——我们跟他说过，大家一直待在一起……{w} 如果他藏起了 Sekimeiya，也清楚我们即将找到它。可他并没有拦下我们，也没有多问。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I moved to the cleaning room again, knowing that Akaro would eventually enter the men's bathroom. Immediately, I noticed two things.
entries.new: 我重新回到清洁间，心里清楚 Akaro 迟早会走进男卫生间。我一进去就注意到两件事。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: One: the bathroom's door looked exactly like it had when we'd come back down. We'd seen that it looked different from how we'd left it.
entries.new: 第一，卫生间的门和我们下楼回来时看到的一模一样。当时我们就发现，它跟我们离开时的样子不同。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The second thing I noticed was that I'd been responsible for it. I had looked inside it and left the door slightly more open than it had been.
entries.new: 第二，造成这一点的人正是我自己。我往里面看了一眼，把门留得比原来更开了一些。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the hell was up with that bathroom? I knew Akaro would be inside it in a few minutes, but the door threw me for a loop.
entries.new: 那间卫生间到底是怎么回事？我知道再过几分钟 Akaro 就会待在里面，可那扇门让我摸不着头脑。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Unable to piece together what was happening, I stood still, waiting for what was bound to occur. At the point Akaro asked Sai for the time, it was {time=11:36.}
entries.new: 我怎么也理不清正在发生什么，只好站在原地，等待注定要发生的事。Akaro 向 Sai 问起时间的那个时候，是 {time=11:36.}
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After the time I'd taken to investigate every room, I didn't have to wait very long before I saw the others appearing from the other side of hallway C. They had just searched every upper floor after visiting the attic for the first time.
entries.new: 查遍所有房间花了不少时间，所以我没等多久，就看见其他人从 C 走廊的另一头出现。他们刚第一次去过阁楼，又把上面每一层都搜了一遍。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They noticed the difference with the bathroom's door and went to check it. Inside, they saw Akaro.
entries.new: 他们察觉到卫生间门的异样，便过去查看。里面正是 Akaro。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't completely rule out that he'd entered it, but the position of the door indicated otherwise. ...Something extremely peculiar had happened inside that small room.
entries.new: 我不能完全排除是他自己走进去的，但门的位置说明并非如此。……那间狭小的房间里，发生过某种极为诡异的事。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After a bit, Sai turned around and headed toward the event room at the same time that Shiroya went to grab a curtain. I reacted fast enough to avoid being seen, but I hadn't anticipated it. Regardless, everything was happening just as I'd already experienced it.
entries.new: 过了一会儿，Sai 转身走向活动室，与此同时 Shiroya 去取遮布。我反应够快，没被他们看见，不过我没料到会来这么一下。不管怎样，一切都和我已经经历过的一模一样。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What had happened to Akaro? The truth was likely obscured behind his odd claim—his lack of time travel.
entries.new: Akaro 究竟遭遇了什么？真相恐怕就藏在他那句古怪的话背后——他没有时间穿越。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When he'd disappeared from our side, we were unable to find him. Before that point, Naomi's killer also vanished completely from the bathroom. And Akaro, who we found there, claimed to have only teleported. Properly piecing all that together had to reveal the truth or form another piece to place somewhere.
entries.new: 他从我们眼前消失后，我们怎么也找不到他。而在此之前，杀害 Naomi 的凶手也从卫生间里彻底消失。后来我们在那里找到的 Akaro，却说自己只是传送了过去。把这些线索好好地拼到一起，要么能揭示真相，要么能成为另一块待安放的拼图。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But despite thinking that, I couldn't decide whether to suspect him or not, because I still didn't fully understand the way the Sekimeiya worked. The little I did know was contradicted by everything I'd witnessed from my new point of view.
entries.new: 可话虽如此，我仍拿不定该不该怀疑他，因为我对 Sekimeiya 的运作方式还远远谈不上了解。我仅有的那点认知，又被我从新视角目睹的一切推翻了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After my past self went to check the Sekimeiya, everyone but Akaro left.{w} I saw Isla's and Shiroya's purses, and they were oblivious of what they were carrying. No matter how much I thought about the abnormal death of the second Naomi, the recording that the four of us were about to hear had remained in the back of my mind.
entries.new: 过去的我去确认 Sekimeiya 之后，除了 Akaro，其他人都离开了。{w} 我看到了 Isla 和 Shiroya 的手提包，而她们对自己带着什么毫不知情。无论我怎么琢磨第二个 Naomi 那场不寻常的死亡，我们四人即将听到的那段录音始终盘踞在我脑海深处。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Being abandoned inside the building for a month, buying into some trick, falling into disarray along with Shiroya... The last thing I wanted was to be a victim of any of that.
entries.new: 被丢在这栋楼里整整一个月、中了某个圈套、再和 Shiroya 一起陷入混乱……我最不愿意的，就是成为这些事里的受害者。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: From that spot, I kept watching. I knew the Sekimeiya would be moved before Shiroya and I returned, and the cleaning room provided me with a way to look at Akaro while listening to the event room and the room I'd traveled from. If either door was opened, I was fairly certain I'd hear it.
entries.new: 我待在那处继续观望。我知道在我和 Shiroya 回来之前，Sekimeiya 会被移走；而待在清洁间，既能看着 Akaro，又能听见活动室和我穿越出来的那个房间的动静。无论哪扇门被打开，我都有把握听到。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In a bit more than ten minutes, I would reach my own present and meet up with Shiroya again. I still had an important chance to understand what was going on.
entries.new: 再过十几分钟，我就会回到自己的现在，与 Shiroya 会合。我仍有一个重要的机会去弄清事情的真相。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...So my thoughts fixated on the culprit. The person responsible for everything.
entries.new: ……于是我的思绪锁定在了犯人身上。那个该为一切负责的人。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The incident, the two murders, and hiding the Sekimeiya. At first, since we hadn't known what the Sekimeiya was capable of, we'd strongly considered someone else was trapped with us and that they were behind it all. However, that was no longer as concrete.
entries.new: 那起事件、两桩命案，还有藏起 Sekimeiya。起初我们不知道 Sekimeiya 有什么能耐，便强烈怀疑另有某人和我们一起被困在这栋楼里，一切都是那人所为。可现在，这个想法已不那么确凿了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The culprit had used the Sekimeiya and possessed knowledge of it. I'd been pretty sure of that already, but seeing them vanish from the bathroom was a stark confirmation. They knew what they were doing, and they were consciously escaping from us.{w} While it was possible that a ninth person was present, thanks to the Sekimeiya, it wasn't necessarily the case. Everything that the "culprit" had done could've been done by one of us as long as they had knowledge of the Sekimeiya's mechanics.
entries.new: 犯人使用过 Sekimeiya，也了解它。这一点我早就很有把握，但亲眼看着对方从卫生间消失，才算得到了确凿的印证。那人清楚自己在做什么，也有意识地躲避我们。{w} 借助 Sekimeiya，确实可能存在第九个人，但也未必如此。只要掌握了 Sekimeiya 的运作原理，『犯人』做过的一切，我们当中任何人都能做到。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai had previously brought up the idea that Katei originally found the Sekimeiya. If so, he was a good candidate to know how it worked. However, he'd repeatedly told us to keep it in the cabinet while it had already been removed three times.
entries.new: Sai 之前提出过，最初发现 Sekimeiya 的人可能是 Katei。若果真如此，他很可能了解它的用法。可他一再叮嘱我们把 Sekimeiya 放回展示柜，而它已经被取走三次了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The power outage, hiding the Sekimeiya in the storeroom, the two killings of Naomi, and whatever might've happened in the attic... I still couldn't explain any of that, but something odd had happened in every one of those instances, meaning that the person responsible must have deliberately used the Sekimeiya to their advantage.
entries.new: 停电、把 Sekimeiya 藏进储藏室、Naomi 的两次死亡，还有阁楼里可能发生过的事……这些我依然一件都解释不了，但每一桩里都出现了反常之处。也就是说，那个人一定是有意利用 Sekimeiya 为自己谋利。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So then, who were they? What was their purpose? I never stopped asking myself that last question. Why did they need to kill Naomi?{w} Did their bizarre plan involve trapping us inside the building for the next few weeks...?
entries.new: 那么，那人是谁？目的又是什么？我一直在不停地问自己最后那个问题。为什么非要杀掉 Naomi？{w} 难道那人荒唐的计划，就是把我们关在这栋楼里好几个星期……？
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I reassured myself that there was no way they could accomplish that...{w} However, it was undeniable that the cameras recorded them. They surely intended to prevent anyone outside from viewing the recordings. We'd already seen an "Access Denied" message, after all.
entries.new: 我安慰自己，这种事他们绝不可能办到……{w} 可监控摄像头拍下了他们，这一点无可否认。他们一定打算阻止外面的人看到这些录像。毕竟，我们已经见过「拒绝访问」的提示了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even though it was clear that Katei was the most suspicious person there, he had also gotten more and more questionable by the second. That was what made me hesitant.
entries.new: Katei 显然是这里最可疑的人，但他身上的疑点也一分一秒地越积越多。正是这一点让我犹豫不决。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I continued waiting. At around {time=11:50}, I'd travel to the past, and before that, the Sekimeiya would be stolen and Akaro would leave. At least I was safe where I was—I knew Shiroya and I hadn't entered the cleaning room.
entries.new: 我继续等待。大约 {time=11:50}，我会穿越到过去；在那之前，Sekimeiya 会被偷走，Akaro 也会离开。至少我待的地方是安全的——我清楚我和 Shiroya 没有进过清洁间。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Like before, the minutes passed and nothing changed. I couldn't see Akaro inside the bathroom, but I knew he was still there, and he'd also told us that he didn't leave until he went to the attic.
entries.new: 和之前一样，时间一分分过去，什么也没发生。我看不见卫生间里的 Akaro，但我知道他仍待在里面；他也告诉过我们，自己一直待到去阁楼才离开。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even though I knew I'd hear him, I kept glancing at the other side of the hallway every once in a while. If Akaro was responsible for the Sekimeiya's disappearance, though, he'd have to move first.
entries.new: 明知能听见动静，我还是时不时朝走廊另一头瞥上一眼。不过，如果 Sekimeiya 的消失是 Akaro 造成的，他总得先有所行动。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't know what I was about to see, but in the meantime, the floor was completely silent. There were no traces of anyone else, and Akaro didn't appear to have been lying for the time being.
entries.new: 我不知道接下来会看到什么，但此刻这一层安静至极。没有任何其他人的痕迹，至少到目前为止，Akaro 似乎没有说谎。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A few more minutes passed; our past selves were occupied with listening to the recording. {w} There wasn't a lot more time left until we'd appear, but I knew for sure that Akaro would first exit the bathroom.
entries.new: 又过了几分钟，过去的我们正忙着听录音。{w} 距离我们出现已经没有多少时间了，但我确信 Akaro 会先从卫生间出来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Or was that necessarily the case? Hadn't I just experienced someone vanishing from that same bathroom? I started to feel uncertain, but that sensation quickly disappeared. About eight minutes after the group had disappeared, Akaro did, in fact, leave the bathroom.
entries.new: ……真是这样吗？我不正是刚刚才经历过有人从同一间卫生间里消失吗？一丝不安涌了上来，但很快便消散了。那伙人离开大约八分钟后，Akaro 果然走出了卫生间。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He looked tired and still a bit groggy. After breathing deeply, he walked off toward the stairs and disappeared from my field of vision.{w} We'd told him the elevator wasn't functional, so he went up by foot. That meant Shiroya and I were about to head down.
entries.new: 他看上去很疲惫，还带着几分昏沉。深吸一口气后，他朝楼梯走去，从我的视野里消失。{w} 我们告诉过他电梯不能用，所以他只能走上去。这也意味着，我和 Shiroya 马上就要下楼了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Similarly, the Sekimeiya was about to be stolen. Keeping an eye on hallway B, I moved toward the bathroom, as I still felt something was off with it. I quickly saw the curtain on the floor, covering Naomi.
entries.new: 同样地，Sekimeiya 也快被偷走了。我一边留意着 B走廊，一边朝卫生间走去，总觉得那里有些不对劲。很快我就看到了铺在地上、盖住 Naomi 的遮布。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The killer had disappeared from the inside, and Akaro might have appeared in the same place. I'd thought that someone could only travel by making physical contact with the Sekimeiya, so I wanted to see if that was somehow possible from the bathroom.
entries.new: 凶手从里面消失了，而 Akaro 或许就出现在同一个地方。我一直以为，人必须与 Sekimeiya 有实际接触才能穿越，所以想看看在那间卫生间里是否可能存在别的途径。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There weren't many places to check. I looked in the toilet, in the water tank, and in the garbage can. I couldn't find anything of importance.
entries.new: 可以检查的地方并不多。我看了马桶、水箱和垃圾桶，没找到任何要紧的东西。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No Sekimeiya that had traveled from the future, and nothing that indicated how someone would disappear from the inside. Only the Sekimeiya could've made the culprit disappear, and there was no way it had vanished through the toilet...
entries.new: 没有从未来穿越而来的 Sekimeiya，也没有任何能说明人如何从里面消失的线索。能让犯人消失的只有 Sekimeiya，而它绝不可能从马桶里消失……
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was checking the bathroom about twenty minutes after the culprit had escaped it, but that shouldn't have mattered. When we'd first discovered Naomi's body, nobody had the chance to remove anything because I was the only person to even set foot inside. After that, Erina and Isla were watching from the stairs, so moving around the area was also impossible.
entries.new: 我检查卫生间时，距离犯人从那里逃走已经过了二十分钟左右，但这本该无关紧要。最初发现 Naomi 的遗体时，没人有机会取走任何东西，因为踏进那间卫生间的只有我一个人。之后 Erina 和 Isla 一直守在楼梯那边看着，想在那片区域动手脚也不可能。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Once the group moved to the attic, I'd quickly come back from the second floor and opened the door to see if Akaro was present. There were a few seconds around then where someone could've tampered with the bathroom's interior, but since we'd just searched through the entire floor, they needed to have traveled from the future...{w} I could justify it like that, but there was hardly any chance of it.
entries.new: 那伙人一去阁楼，我便立刻从二楼折返，打开门确认 Akaro 在不在。就在那前后几秒里，确实可能有人对卫生间内部动过手脚；可我们刚把整层搜过一遍，那人就必须是从未来穿越过来的……{w} 这样解释也说得通，但几乎没有这种可能。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After that, I checked every room on the floor. Someone could've entered the bathroom at that time, but the door hadn't moved when I returned to the cleaning room—it would be open wider if someone went through it.
entries.new: 之后我查遍了这一层的每个房间。那段时间里，有人可能进过卫生间，可我回到清洁间时，那扇门并没有动过——若有人进出，它会开得更大。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So the state of the bathroom was almost certainly identical to how it was when we found Naomi's body, and there was nothing that allowed the culprit to escape. If you could travel back in time and bring the Sekimeiya with you, that was one method, but nothing indicated it was possible.
entries.new: 所以卫生间的状态，几乎可以肯定和发现 Naomi 遗体时完全一样，里面没有任何能让犯人逃走的办法。假如人能带着 Sekimeiya 一起穿越回过去，那倒算一种方法，可没有任何迹象表明这行得通。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}Could the key to what happened have been removed by Akaro? Whatever it was, had he left the bathroom with it just then...?
entries.new: ……{w}难道那件事的关键，是被 Akaro 拿走了？不管那是什么，他刚才离开卫生间时，是不是就把它带在身上……？
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He had nothing in his hands when he left. Aside from that, he only had a couple small pockets in his pants.
entries.new: 他离开时两手空空。除此之外，他裤子上只有几个很小的口袋。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Out of the blue, I heard a sound while I was still watching hallway B. The sound itself didn't surprise me since I knew someone else had to be skulking around to hide the Sekimeiya.
entries.new: 我还盯着 B走廊，忽然听见一声响动。声音本身并不让我意外——要把 Sekimeiya 藏起来，本来就得有另一个人在暗处活动。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Trying not to announce my presence, I observed the hallway, knowing that it couldn't yet have been me and Shiroya. Nobody appeared to be there, which was odd.{w} Shortly after, I heard another sound come from the opposite hallway.
entries.new: 我尽量不暴露自己，只静静观察着走廊。那个时间点，弄出动静的不可能是我和 Shiroya。可那里似乎空无一人，这就怪了。{w} 没过多久，对面的走廊又传来一声响动。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I approached hallway A, a little nervous. As soon as I peeked in, I saw who else was there.
entries.new: 我怀着几分紧张走近 A走廊，探头一望，便看清了那边的人是谁。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Thunderhead
entries.new: 雷云

entries.text: It was Sai...{w} He had made the sound and was in front of the event room... However, that shouldn't have been possible. At that moment, he was in the attic. We'd left him in the bedroom after he climbed the ladder to look around.
entries.new: 是 Sai……{w} 声音是他弄出来的，人就站在活动室前……可这根本不可能。那一刻，他明明在阁楼。他爬上梯子四处看过之后，我们就把他留在了卧室里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: While I paused, unsure of how to react, he noticed me. As if he'd seen a deadly creature, he visibly recoiled. He had clearly not expected to see me there, and once we made eye contact, he was left petrified just like I was.
entries.new: 我一时愣在原地，不知该如何反应，他倒先看见了我。那副模样，像是撞见了什么致命的东西，整个人明显往后一缩。他显然没料到会在这里遇上我；四目相对之后，他僵住了，我也一样。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't know what his next action would be, so I moved over to him. I was half expecting him to run away, but he stood immobile, waiting for me to arrive.
entries.new: 我猜不透他接下来会做什么，索性朝他走过去。我心里半以为他会转身就跑，他却一动不动，站在原地等我走近。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Um.{w=0.4} Hey,{w=0.3} Atsuki.{w=0.4} How are you doing?
entries.new: ……呃。{w=0.4} 那个，{w=0.3} Atsuki。{w=0.4} 你还好吗？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I quickly noticed it. He was pretending not to know what he was carrying in his hip pack.
entries.new: 我立刻就注意到了——他正装作不知道自己腰包里装着什么。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: All's good—trying to get the most out of my imprisonment. What about you?
entries.new: 还行，尽量让这段被囚禁的日子过得有滋有味。你呢？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Coincidentally, me too. Has that led you anywhere?
entries.new: 说来也巧，我也是。有什么收获吗？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...{w}Let's go to the lobby.
entries.new: ……{w}去大厅吧。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Huh? Why?
entries.new: 咦？为什么？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I don't know, so we don't freeze the world or something.
entries.new: 说不上来，免得我们一个不小心把世界给冻住了之类的。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Shiroya and I were about to arrive. To avoid anything undesirable, we walked to the lobby even though I didn't elaborate further to Sai.
entries.new: 我和 Shiroya 马上就要到了。为免节外生枝，我们一同走向大厅，尽管我没有向 Sai 多作解释。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Do you like it better here?
entries.new: 你更喜欢这里？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Yes. Let's not be too loud, either. Anyway, where were you gonna bring that?
entries.new: ……嗯。说话也别太大声。话说回来，你打算把那东西带到哪儿去？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Bring what?
entries.new: 带什么？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What you're hiding there.
entries.new: 你藏在那儿的那个东西。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Sai frowned. He tilted his head down, toward his hip pack. Without changing his expression, he unzipped it, and {tip=future}the Sekimeiya was uncovered{/tip}.
entries.new: Sai 皱起眉，低头看向自己的腰包。他面无表情地拉开拉链，{tip=future}露出了里面的 Sekimeiya{/tip}。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the...?
entries.new: 什……什么？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: This is going to sound funny, but I had no idea this was here.
entries.new: 说出来你大概不信，我完全不知道它在里面。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Additionally, the Sekimeiya wasn't white. It was gray—the same shade it had shifted to the last time.
entries.new: 而且，那 Sekimeiya 并不是白色的，而是灰色——和它上一次变色后的深浅分毫不差。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It does sound funny. Did you accidentally get it from the cabinet and put it there? Or did it maybe teleport inside?
entries.new: 确实难以相信。是你无意间从展示柜里拿了它、顺手塞进去的？还是它自己传送进去的？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: More importantly, how did you get here?
entries.new: 更重要的是，你怎么会到这儿来？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You mean that I shouldn't be here, right? I figured. And no, I definitely didn't put it in here. It's not heavy at all, so I didn't notice I had it.
entries.new: 你的意思是我不该出现在这儿，对吧？我就知道。还有，不是，我绝对没把它放进去。它一点也不重，所以我根本没察觉到。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He took it out. It didn't make him travel, and nothing seemed to have happened.
entries.new: 他把 Sekimeiya 拿了出来。什么事也没有发生——他并没有因此穿越。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Well, that's hard to believe. Right now, the Sekimeiya has disappeared. You must've taken it out and just been about to hide it.
entries.new: 这话很难让人信服。就在刚才，Sekimeiya 明明不见了。肯定是你把它取出来，正准备藏起来。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...The past Shiroya and I had surely already arrived. We went to the bathroom first, and then to the event room.{w} ...So if Sai had the Sekimeiya, had I interrupted his actions, thereby changing the past?
entries.new: ……过去的我和 Shiroya 肯定已经到这里了。我们先去了洗手间，然后才到活动室。{w} ……那么，既然 Sekimeiya 在 Sai 手上，是不是我打断了他的行动，把过去给改变了？
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If that was it, my travel would become impossible. Was something terrible about to happen...? None of my other actions had resulted in anything similar.
entries.new: 若真是如此，我恐怕就无法穿越了。难道要出什么可怕的事……？可我之前的每一个举动，都没造成过类似的后果。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hm...{w} Yeah, I did see the Sekimeiya disappeared. Was it Akaro, or was it you?
entries.new: 嗯……{w} 对，我确实看见 Sekimeiya 不见了。拿走它的是 Akaro，还是你？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It wasn't either of us. I heard Akaro going up the stairs as soon as he left the bathroom, so it wasn't him. I couldn't look at both hallways at the same time, so I can't be sure that you did it, but you just so happen to be holding it.
entries.new: 我们两个都没有。Akaro 一出洗手间，我就听见他上楼去了，所以不是他。我没法同时盯住两条走廊，因此不能断定是你干的——可东西偏偏就在你手上。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Apparently, I am. You traveled from the future, right?
entries.new: 看来确实在我手上。你是从未来穿越过来的，对吧？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Why, because I shouldn't be here?
entries.new: 怎么，就因为我不该出现在这儿？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Maybe.
entries.new: ……也许吧。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I might've traveled, yes. You did too, right?
entries.new: 也许我确实穿越过。你也一样，对吧？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Me? Don't be stupid. I don't know where the Sekimeiya is. I was just searching for it, and it seems I didn't realize I had it.
entries.new: 我？别傻了。我连 Sekimeiya 在哪儿都不知道。我一直在找它，结果好像根本没意识到它就在我自己身上。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...I had no idea how I was supposed to take that. I was about to travel with the Sekimeiya from room B3, so why did Sai have it? Of course, believing that he didn't know it was in his hip pack was ridiculous.
entries.new: ……我实在不知道该怎样理解这番话。我明明马上就要从 B3 室带着 Sekimeiya 穿越，它怎么会在 Sai 手里？当然，要说他不知道自己的腰包里装着它，那也太荒唐了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You definitely traveled, right? Did you already have it in your hip pack when you appeared? Is that what you mean?
entries.new: 你肯定是穿越过的吧？你出现的时候，它就已经在腰包里了？你想说的是这个意思？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...That's an interesting thought, even though I didn't travel.
entries.new: ……这想法倒有意思，可惜我并没有穿越。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: If that had happened, it meant that the Sekimeiya traveled with him too, but what would the reason for that be?{w} ...And even then, who hid the Sekimeiya from the cabinet? It was a fact that we'd seen it empty, but I didn't notice anyone entering the room where Shiroya found it.
entries.new: 若真是那样，就说明 Sekimeiya 也跟着他一起穿越了——可这又是出于什么缘由？{w} ……再说，究竟是谁把 Sekimeiya 从展示柜里拿走的？我们确实亲眼见过展示柜是空的，可我也没见有人进过 Shiroya 找到它的那个房间。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It turned white again...
entries.new: 它又变白了……
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You're right. How bizarre.
entries.new: 没错。真是怪事。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai had put the Sekimeiya back in his pack, and out of nowhere, it changed colors again, recovering its white glow.
entries.new: Sai 已经把 Sekimeiya 放回包里，它却毫无征兆地再次变色，重新泛起白色的光泽。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So, it went back to normal without needing a lower temperature.
entries.new: 这么说，不用降温它也恢复正常了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Maybe it works again, then. Why don't you try touching it?
entries.new: 那它说不定又能用了。你要不要碰一下试试？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Because that'd be very stupid of me. I'd disappear and leave the Sekimeiya here with you. What if you're the one who keeps hiding it?
entries.new: 那可就太蠢了。我一消失，Sekimeiya 就留在这里了。万一一直藏它的人就是你呢？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I don't want to hide it anywhere, and you'd appear in the past. You could make it here the moment you disappear to prevent me from hiding it.
entries.new: 我根本不想把它藏到任何地方。而且你会出现在过去——你完全可以在消失的那一刻赶回这里，阻止我把它藏起来。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That's assuming I appear inside the tower. If I appear outside, you could do anything you wanted with it.
entries.new: 前提是我能出现在塔里。要是我落在塔外，那东西就随你处置了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He zipped the Sekimeiya inside his pack.
entries.new: 他把 Sekimeiya 塞进背包，拉上了拉链。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}I didn't respond, but he wouldn't break the silence before I did.
entries.new: ……{w}我没有出声，而在我开口之前，他也不会打破沉默。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Do you really expect me to believe that you're not going to run off with it? Come on, Sai. I get how you work at this point, more or less.
entries.new: 你真以为我会相信你不会带着它跑掉？得了吧，Sai。你是什么路数，我多少也摸清了。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What does that mean, exactly?
entries.new: 这话具体是什么意思？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You just like seeing how things play out. You took the Sekimeiya and did something to end up here. I'm not Katei, and you know I'm trustworthy, so why are you trying to lie to me?
entries.new: 你就是喜欢看事情怎么发展。你拿了 Sekimeiya，做了点什么，才落到这里。我不是 Katei，你也清楚我信得过，那你为什么还要骗我？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I'd never lie to you, Atsuki. You know that. We're partners. This brief time we've spent together has awoken my deepest feelings for you, in fact.
entries.new: 我怎么会骗你呢，Atsuki。你清楚得很。我们是同伴。事实上，这短短一段相处，已经唤醒了我对你最深的感情。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Can you stop fucking with me just for the sake of it? I want this gem put back in the cabinet. That's all.
entries.new: ……你能不能别没事就耍我？我只想把这颗宝石放回展示柜。就这样。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I'd love to do that. I was just following your orders. You haven't told me to move since you brought me here, so I was waiting for your next command.
entries.new: 我很乐意。我一直都在听你的命令。你把我带到这里以后，就没再叫我动过，所以我一直在等你下一句吩咐。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Put it back in the cabinet.
entries.new: 放回展示柜。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Did you not hear me?
entries.new: 你没听见吗？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I heard you.
entries.new: 听见了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Oh, was that all? What cabinet? There are almost a hundred of them.
entries.new: 哦，就这样？哪个展示柜？这里少说也有一百个。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...The one in the event room.
entries.new: ……活动室那个。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That one, huh? Sure thing.{w} Give me a second, though. This is my self-reflection moment of the day.
entries.new: 那个啊？行。{w}不过等我一下。这是我今天的自我反省时间。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What the hell was with his face? His appearance was totally blank.
entries.new: 他那张脸到底是怎么回事？整张脸一点表情都没有。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stared at the floor for a while, thinking to myself while Sai let me be. He didn't seem to want to move, so I just observed him in silence.
entries.new: 我盯着地板看了一会儿，Sai 没来打扰，让我自己待着。他似乎不打算动，我便静静地观察他。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It wasn't like I wanted to get into a fight with him, but he clearly had a problem with me. He shifted his weight from one leg to the other in the few minutes we spent in silence, sighing slightly as well. I ran in circles mentally, getting nowhere fast in understanding what the hell was up with him or what had happened with the Sekimeiya.
entries.new: 我并不是想跟他吵，但他显然对我有意见。沉默的那几分钟里，他不住地把重心从一条腿换到另一条腿，还轻轻叹了口气。我翻来覆去地想，却怎么也想不明白他到底是怎么回事，也弄不清 Sekimeiya 究竟发生了什么。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}I should have already disappeared, assuming things happened as I remember them. Shiroya must be waiting. Follow me. Got it?
entries.new: ……{w}如果一切和我记得的一样，那我现在本该已经消失了。Shiroya 一定还在等。跟我来，明白吗？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Sure. I gotta say, it's not the same without mint tea.
entries.new: 好啊。不过说真的，没有薄荷茶就是差点意思。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I walked to the hallway B room where we'd found the Sekimeiya.
entries.new: 我走向 B走廊的那个房间，我们就是在那儿找到 Sekimeiya 的。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was empty.
entries.new: 里面空无一人。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Sh-She's not here.
entries.new: ……她、她不在这儿。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Did your girlfriend abandon you? That's tragic.
entries.new: 被女朋友抛弃了？真是悲剧。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I stepped in farther, but I stopped right as I heard Sai taking off behind me.
entries.new: 我又往里走了几步，却听见身后 Sai 撒腿就跑，当即停下脚步。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hey! Stop!
entries.new: 喂！站住！
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I turned around to chase after him. Fortunately, I'd reacted fast enough to grab him as he was opening the door to the event room.
entries.new: 我转身追了上去。好在我反应够快，在他正要推开活动室的门时一把抓住了他。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...What the fuck are you doing?
entries.new: ……你他妈在干什么？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You're fast. I just got really antsy to see if the Sekimeiya was here. That's all.
entries.new: 你跑得真快。我就是迫不及待想看看 Sekimeiya 在不在。仅此而已。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You were totally running from me. And here, you can see that it's not.
entries.new: 你分明就是在逃。这里你也看见了，它不在这儿。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah, it appears I'm holding it.
entries.new: 是啊，看起来它在我手里。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The sudden acceleration wore me out for a moment, so I breathed heavily for a few seconds. I had no idea what Sai was doing there, and it seemed Shiroya had gone somewhere as well.
entries.new: 猛地一冲让我一时有些吃不消，喘了好几秒粗气。我完全不知道 Sai 为什么会在这儿，而 Shiroya 似乎也不见了踪影。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Anyway, put it inside.
entries.new: 总之，把它放回去。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The Sekimeiya? Of course, that's what I was gonna do. Let me try not to touch it.
entries.new: Sekimeiya？当然了，我本来就打算这么做。我尽量不直接碰它。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He unzipped his pack and hid his hand under his sleeve.
entries.new: 他拉开背包拉链，把手缩进袖子里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Since keeping the Sekimeiya in the pack doesn't make me travel, it could be that it requires physical contact with your skin. I'll try to only touch it with my shirt.
entries.new: 既然把 Sekimeiya 放进背包不会让我穿越，那可能就是需要皮肤直接接触。我试试只用衣服碰它。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He held it in his hand, which was covered by cloth. He didn't disappear, so what he said made sense. Then, I scrolled open the glass for him, and he placed the Sekimeiya on top of the cushion. Finally, I closed the glass again.
entries.new: 他用裹着布的手托着它。他没有消失，说明他说的有道理。接着，我替他把玻璃罩推开，他将 Sekimeiya 放到软垫上。最后，我又把玻璃合上。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I suppose I was correct.
entries.new: 看来我说对了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Maybe, but touching it has done nothing a few times. It's possible it wouldn't have worked even if you'd touched it directly.
entries.new: 也许吧，但之前也有几次碰了它什么也没发生。说不定就算你直接碰它，也不会有事。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Uh... I doubt it, actually. Feel this.
entries.new: 呃……我倒是觉得不会。你摸摸这个。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He touched my arm with his sleeve.{w} It was hot.
entries.new: 他用袖子碰了碰我的手臂。{w}很烫。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It wasn't hot at all when it was gray, but now it is—even the pack is. I bet something would happen if I touched it. That's probably why the refrigeration is needed.
entries.new: 它还是灰色的时候一点也不烫，现在却烫了——连背包都是。我敢说，要是我碰它，肯定会出事。大概就是因为这个才需要冷藏。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: But that's strange. We took it out of the cabinet earlier and touched it while it was white, but it was still cold.
entries.new: 可这就怪了。我们之前把它从展示柜里拿出来，它还是白色的时候也碰过，可它当时是凉的。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Maybe something else is needed to activate it. Who knows?
entries.new: 也许还要别的条件才能激活它。谁知道呢。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Whatever. What are you doing here? You should still be in the attic.
entries.new: 算了。你为什么会在这里？你现在应该还在阁楼才对。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: And I am. Consider the me you're talking to right now as a ghost.
entries.new: 我确实在那儿。你就把正在跟你说话的我看成幽灵吧。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Are you just fucking with me? You traveled to the past, just like I did.
entries.new: ……你又在耍我？你跟我一样，穿越到了过去。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: No way. Traveling to the past is impossible.
entries.new: 怎么可能。回到过去根本不可能。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You're getting irritating. I admitted I traveled to the past, so just do the same.
entries.new: 你越来越烦人了。我都承认自己穿越到过去了，你也照做不就行了。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Don't get me wrong, I would if I had. It's just that I haven't. I haven't traveled in time, teleported, or activated the Sekimeiya successfully even once.
entries.new: 别误会，我要是真做过，自然会承认。问题是我没做过。时间穿越也好，传送也好，成功启动 Sekimeiya 也好，我一次都没做到过。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That's bullshit. How can you be here, then? It's not possible.
entries.new: 胡说。那你怎么会站在这里？这根本不可能。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You said I should be in the attic, right? Consider this: what if I touch the Sekimeiya in a bit to go back to the past, then go to the attic? I don't have to be the version that's already traveled. I can be the original.
entries.new: 你说我本该待在阁楼里，对吧？那你不妨想想——要是我过一会儿去碰 Sekimeiya，回到过去，然后再去阁楼呢？在这里的不一定是已经穿越过的那个我，也可以是原本的我。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...So, at some point, the Sai that was around us changed places with you?
entries.new: ……也就是说，某个时候，一直和我们在一起的 Sai，和你换了位置？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Of course not. I was only letting you know that it's not impossible. I'm telling you, just treat me as a ghost you hallucinated. I can't be here, you know? I'm in the attic.
entries.new: 当然不是。我只是想告诉你，那并非不可能。我说了，你就当我是你幻想出来的幽灵吧。我本来不可能在这儿，不是吗？我在阁楼里。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Why are you being so stubborn? After Shiroya and I headed downstairs, you did too. Then you traveled to the past, and that's why you're here now.
entries.new: 你为什么这么固执？我和 Shiroya 下楼之后，你也跟着下去了。然后你穿越回过去，所以现在才会出现在这里。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Except that won't happen. You might not believe me, but it's the truth.
entries.new: 只可惜那不会发生。你也许不信，但这是实话。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Then how can you be here?
entries.new: 那你怎么会在这里？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Are you sure I truly am? Am I not a figment of your imagination?
entries.new: 你确定我真的在这里？说不定我只是你凭空想出来的。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...You're not.
entries.new: ……你不是。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I suddenly thought of something I could corner him with.
entries.new: 我忽然想到一个能逼他就范的办法。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I grabbed Sai's hand. It was definitely corporeal: he was no ghost. Without explaining, I dragged him to the security room.
entries.new: 我抓住 Sai 的手。那触感分明是实实在在的躯体，他绝不是什么幽灵。我二话不说，把他拽去了监控室。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Immediately, I noticed something odd.
entries.new: 一进门，我就察觉到了异样。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai, did you enter this room?
entries.new: Sai，你进过这个房间吗？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Didn't we all enter it at some point?
entries.new: 我们不是都进来过吗？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Did you enter it during the past forty minutes?
entries.new: ……最近四十分钟里，你进来过吗？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: No, I didn't.
entries.new: 没有。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That's strange, because the door wasn't completely shut. And look, the computer isn't suspended.
entries.new: 那就怪了，门并没有完全关严。而且你看，电脑也没有进入休眠。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: And so what, I must've entered it?
entries.new: 那又怎样？难道就一定是我进来过？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I walked forward to see the time displayed on the computer. It said it was {time=11:57.}
entries.new: 我走上前去看电脑上显示的时间。上面显示的是 {time=11:57.}
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I used this computer 47 minutes ago, at {time=11:10.} You determined that Katei wasn't in this room during the attack thanks to the sleep timer, so it must be more than 45 minutes.
entries.new: 我四十七分钟前用过这台电脑，那时是 {time=11:10.}。你之前靠休眠计时推断出袭击发生时 Katei 不在这个房间里，所以间隔一定超过四十五分钟。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes, fifty minutes of inactivity are needed for the computer to power off the screens.
entries.new: 没错，电脑要闲置五十分钟，屏幕才会断电。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: So if we wait these remaining three minutes, we'll be able to see if I was the last person to use the computer. If the screens stay on, someone else used it.
entries.new: 所以只要再等三分钟，就能看出最后一个用电脑的人是不是我。如果屏幕一直亮着，那就是别人用过。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Brilliant.
entries.new: 真高明。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Also, the last time this door should've been opened was earlier, when we searched through the entire floor. We made it a point to close every door when we were done for efficiency, so it would be harder for anyone hiding to move between rooms.
entries.new: 另外，这扇门上一次被打开，应该还是早些时候我们搜遍整层楼的时候。当时我们说好，搜完一处就把每扇门都关上，这样藏起来的人想在房间之间移动就没那么容易了。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah, I saw the computer was powered on, which told me that someone had used it in the past hour. The others didn't pay much mind to it, and neither did you. After that, we closed the door.
entries.new: 是啊，我看到电脑开着，就知道这一小时里有人用过。其他人没怎么在意，你也没有。之后我们把门关上了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: So you remember. Good.{w} Despite that, it was open a little bit just now. Someone must have come in here. This door isn't loose, and it won't open all by itself.
entries.new: 看来你记得。很好。{w}可刚才那扇门却开了一条缝。一定是有人进来过。这扇门并不松，不会自己开的。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes, and? Do you think it was me?
entries.new: 是，然后呢？你觉得是我？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Well, I found you in hallway A, and you said you were searching for the Sekimeiya. Did you really not enter this room?
entries.new: 我在 A 走廊找到你的，你说自己在找 Sekimeiya。你真的没进过这个房间？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I didn't. And even if I had, would you have anything to say?
entries.new: 没有。就算我进来过，你又能说什么？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'm not sure yet. Let me tell you the reason I brought you here.
entries.new: 我还没想清楚。先说说我带你来这里的理由吧。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Show me your wristwatch.
entries.new: 把你的手表给我看看。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...My what?
entries.new: ……我的什么？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It's hidden beneath your sleeve, but I saw you still have it. This is the only room that provides us with the current time, so show me what your own watch displays.
entries.new: 你把它藏在袖子里，但我看见你还戴着。这里只有这个房间能告诉我们现在的时间，所以让我看看你自己的表显示的是几点。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Why?
entries.new: 为什么？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Because it might reveal your lie.{w} Let's say you traveled from {time=12:10.} It's possible the time displayed would now be something like {time=12:20.}
entries.new: 因为它也许能揭穿你的谎话。{w}假设你是从 {time=12:10.} 穿越过来的，那表上现在显示的时间很可能就是 {time=12:20.} 之类。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I see. That would reveal that I've come from the future. It's a smart idea.{w} I even said earlier that my time matches the computer's, didn't I?
entries.new: 原来如此。那样就能看出我是从未来来的。这主意很聪明。{w}我先前还说过，我的时间和电脑上的一致，对吧？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...You did.{w} If your time's ahead, you time traveled. If it's the same, it's possible that the body you appear with is identical to how it was at that point in time. That would help us confirm what happened with the second Naomi.
entries.new: ……你确实说过。{w}如果你的时间超前，那你就是穿越了。如果时间相同，那也许你出现时的身体和那个时间点上的身体完全一致。这能帮我们弄清第二个 Naomi 身上发生的事。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What if someone edited the computer's time? It'd be trivial.
entries.new: 要是有人改过电脑的时间呢？那可不是什么难事。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Well, if someone did that, it would've been you. The door was opened, and the screens are still lit. Although I did check the time fifty minutes ago, so I guess it couldn't have been modified recently. Technically, I guess you could have changed your wristwatch's time instead.
entries.new: 要说有人动过手脚，那也只能是你。门被打开过，屏幕还亮着。不过五十分钟前我确认过时间，所以最近应该没被改过。严格来说，你倒是有可能改了自己手表的时间。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I actually don't even know how to do that.
entries.new: 我其实根本不会调。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Just as he said that, the computer entered sleep mode.
entries.new: 他话音刚落，电脑就进入了休眠。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Well, unfortunately, there goes your little theory.
entries.new: 可惜，你那套小推论泡汤了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: So did someone enter this room and not use the computer? There's no way the door just opened.
entries.new: 这么说，有人进了这个房间却没碰电脑？门总不可能自己打开。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Who knows?
entries.new: 谁知道呢？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Just show me your watch.
entries.new: 少废话，把手表给我看。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: My what?
entries.new: 我的什么？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Your watch.
entries.new: 你的手表。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: But I'm watching you right now.
entries.new: 可我现在就在看着你。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He clearly had a problem with showing me the time, so I knew I was correct. I quickly positioned myself in front of the door so that he couldn't escape again.
entries.new: 他明显不想让我看时间，我便知道自己没猜错。我立刻站到门前，挡住他的去路，免得他又溜走。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If you don't want to, you can just admit that you traveled. It's not very hard to figure out.
entries.new: 你要是不愿意，大可直接承认自己经历了时间穿越。这并不难猜出来。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: After he spent a few more seconds in silence, I decided to act first. I grabbed his arm and looked at the miniature screen on his wrist.
entries.new: 他又沉默了几秒，我决定抢先行动。我抓住他的胳膊，看向他腕上的微型屏幕。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...What?{w} Did you just do this?
entries.new: ……什么？{w}这是你刚才弄的？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Huh? What's the time?
entries.new: 嗯？现在几点？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Don't be stupid. {tip=9999}It's broken{/tip}.
entries.new: 别装傻。{tip=9999}它坏了{/tip}。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: E-Excuse me?
entries.new: 什、什么？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The screen was blank. Nothing was being displayed on it.
entries.new: 屏幕一片空白，上面什么也没有显示。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Really...? When did it stop working?
entries.new: 真的……？它什么时候坏的？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Are you just fucking with me again? Did you do this right now, somehow?
entries.new: 你他妈又在耍我？是不是刚才动了什么手脚？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I didn't do anything. You were looking at me. I didn't even touch the watch.
entries.new: 我什么都没做。你一直看着我，我连表都没碰。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I couldn't object to that. Even though he'd been buying time, he hadn't touched it at all.
entries.new: 这一点我无法反驳。他刚才虽然一直在拖延，却确实没有碰过表。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You might have anticipated I was gonna ask this and disabled it as soon as we entered this room.
entries.new: 你也许早就料到我会问，所以一进这房间就让它失灵了。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It's flattering if you think I did that, but honestly, I have no idea what happened. I've had it for a long time, so perhaps the battery ran out. I don't even know how I'd "disable" it.
entries.new: 你会这么想，倒是抬举我了。不过说实话，我也不知道发生了什么。这表我用了很久，大概是电池耗尽了吧。我甚至不知道该怎么让它「失灵」。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Let me look at it.
entries.new: 让我看看。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I was already grabbing his arm, so I inspected the wristwatch a bit more. It had two buttons on its sides, probably to edit the time and other parameters.
entries.new: 我本来就抓着他的胳膊，便顺势仔细端详起那块腕表。表侧有两个按钮，大概是用来调整时间和其他参数的。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Can you remove it?
entries.new: 能把它摘下来吗？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes. I take it off every night.
entries.new: 能。我每晚都会摘下来。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...You've become pretty uncooperative. Just take it off.
entries.new: ……你还真是越来越不配合了。摘下来吧。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Are you confiscating it? You've taken a liking to this watch.
entries.new: 你是要没收吗？看来你挺喜欢这块表的。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: While he continued speaking in his frivolous tone, he handed it to me. I'd gotten curious about what happened since Sai clearly didn't want to show me his watch at all.
entries.new: 他仍用那副轻佻的语气说着，一边把表递给我。Sai 明明一点也不想让我看表，我反而更想知道究竟出了什么事。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How did you do it? I don't see a power button.
entries.new: 你是怎么弄的？我没看见有电源键。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I didn't do anything. It just so happened to run out of battery now.
entries.new: 我什么都没做。只是碰巧在这个时候没电了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That'd be a little too convenient.
entries.new: 那未免也太巧了。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You can call it fate. Don't worry, though, I didn't have anything to hide in the first place.
entries.new: 你就当是命运吧。不过别担心，我本来也没什么好隐瞒的。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: On the backside of the watch, there was a slot for the battery. It took some effort, but I opened it to see a single lithium battery.
entries.new: 表背有一个电池槽。我费了点劲才把它打开，里面装着一枚锂电池。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How long have you had it for?
entries.new: 这表你用了多久？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: A few years.
entries.new: 几年吧。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: How many, approximately?
entries.new: 大概几年？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Seven or eight.
entries.new: 七八年。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Maybe it would have run out now, but I'm not sure. Lithium batteries are more expensive, but they last a very long time. They outlast plenty of devices.
entries.new: 也许到现在确实该没电了，但我不确定。锂电池虽然贵些，却很耐用，寿命比许多设备都长。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Hey, you're pretty good. In that case, maybe the watch itself broke.
entries.new: 嘿，你懂得还挺多。那样的话，说不定是表本身坏了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It looks perfectly fine to me.
entries.new: 我看它一点问题都没有。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Unfortunate, then. I'm curious about what happened too, but it might be a bigger mystery than we thought.
entries.new: 那就可惜了。我也很好奇到底怎么回事，不过也许比我们想的还要蹊跷。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You're ridiculous. You know exactly what you did to avoid being exposed.
entries.new: 你可真会装。为了不被拆穿，你动了什么手脚，自己心里清楚。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I think you're the one being silly here. First, I didn't have anything to hide, and second, I did nothing to this watch. I take good care of it, so I wouldn't break it on a whim.
entries.new: 我看胡闹的人是你。第一，我没什么可隐瞒的；第二，我没对这块表做过任何事。我一直很爱惜它，不会无缘无故弄坏。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...{w}You know, remember upstairs, in the attic?{w} I looked through a few drawers and found a bunch of useless junk. I believe I might've seen a compatible battery somewhere.
entries.new: ……{w}说起来，你还记得楼上的阁楼吗？{w}我翻过几个抽屉，里面全是没用的杂物。我好像在哪见过能配上的电池。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...And you were talking about conveniences. You're pretty insistent.
entries.new: ……亏你刚才还说太巧了。你还真是穷追不舍。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I want to know what happened. It's not uncommon to have a couple batteries like this lying around. It's also true that I didn't see you mess with the watch, and since it's not damaged, the most likely explanation is a faulty battery or that it actually was time for it to run out. Let's see if we can power this back on.
entries.new: 我想知道到底发生了什么。家里随手放着几块这种电池也不稀奇。而且我确实没看见你碰表；既然表没有损坏，最有可能的就是电池出了问题，或者它真的到了该没电的时候。我们试试能不能让它重新开机。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: This watch doesn't receive the time from a satellite. You sounded pretty convincing earlier when you said that you didn't know how to edit the time. Maybe you just didn't foresee this at all and the battery actually stopped working.{w} If the battery ran out when the displayed time was, say, {time=12:10}, it could pick up from there when we put in a new one—watches like that exist. Also, this watch was working just earlier, when you said it was {time=11:36.} Let's see what happens when we insert a new battery.
entries.new: 这块表不是靠卫星对时的。你刚才说自己不会调时间，听起来倒挺像那么回事。也许你根本没料到这一步，电池是真的耗尽了。{w}如果电池耗尽时，表上显示的时间是比如 {time=12:10}，那换上新电池后，它可能会从那个时间继续走——市面上确实有这种表。而且，刚才你说时间是 {time=11:36.} 的时候，这块表还在正常走着。我们换上电池，看看会怎么样。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Are you being serious...? We can't go to the attic.
entries.new: 你是认真的……？我们可不能去阁楼。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I bet I know why. You're up there and we'd see your past self. Additionally, you don't remember anyone going up.{w} Where did you stay? We could just avoid anyone else.
entries.new: 我大概知道原因。你就在上面，我们一上去就会遇见过去的你。再说，你也不记得有人上去过。{w}你当时待在哪里？我们避开其他人就行。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You're getting annoying. I don't know what the people above us are doing.
entries.new: 你越来越烦人了。我不知道楼上那些人现在在做什么。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Let's go, then.
entries.new: 那就走吧。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Where did you see the battery?
entries.new: 你在哪儿看见的电池？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: In the living room, under the television.
entries.new: 客厅，电视机下面。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Hm, okay. Let's be quick.
entries.new: ……嗯，好吧。动作快点。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That works.
entries.new: 也行。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I made sure to keep my grip on Sai's sleeve so that he couldn't escape. I hadn't disregarded Shiroya, so before moving up, I looked through hallway B and still found no trace of her.
entries.new: 我牢牢攥着 Sai 的袖子，免得他跑掉。我也没把 Shiroya 忘在一边，上楼之前先看了一遍 B走廊，仍旧不见她的踪影。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I started to get a bit worried. She wouldn't have gone off anywhere.
entries.new: ……我开始有些担心了。她总不至于自己跑到别处去。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd entered the room soon after we'd left, and she no longer seemed to be on the crystal floor... She couldn't have been attacked, could she? We would've heard a yell, and there hadn't been that much time for anything to happen.
entries.new: 我们离开没多久，我就进过那间房，那时她似乎已经不在水晶层了……总不会是被袭击了吧？真出了事，我们该听见喊声，而且那么短的时间也来不及发生什么。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: By going to the attic, I could also check whether she was on the higher floors. For that reason and because the elevator was still supposed to be disabled, we took the stairs up.
entries.new: 去阁楼的话，也能顺便确认她在不在上面的楼层。出于这个考虑，加上电梯据说还没恢复，我们便走了楼梯。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We circled through every floor without finding her.{w} The attic was unlocked, so we went up the last, narrow staircase and entered the living room.
entries.new: 我们把每一层都绕了一遍，还是没有找到她。{w}阁楼没有上锁，我们便沿最后那段窄楼梯上去，走进了起居室。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The floor showed we'd surpassed the time we'd gone down—I could see Shiroya's and my own footprints heading out. I looked at them for a few seconds, but it was difficult to determine if anyone had left after us.
entries.new: 从地面的痕迹看，已经过了我们下楼的时间——我能看见自己和 Shiroya 往外走的脚印。我盯着看了几秒，却很难判断之后有没有人离开。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It should be here.
entries.new: 应该就在这里。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I kneeled down and opened a drawer. I had to let go of Sai's hand, but he didn't run away. He at least seemed to be genuinely confused about what happened to his wristwatch.
entries.new: 我蹲下身拉开抽屉，不得不松开 Sai 的手，但他没有跑。至少手表这件事，他看上去是真的摸不着头脑。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yeah, here it is.
entries.new: 嗯，就在这里。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: All right. Let's leave.
entries.new: 好。走吧。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: If he wanted to leave, the most likely reason was that he'd lived through that time already and knew the people who were still in the bedrooms wouldn't notice us. If that was the case, there was no point in defying what he'd experienced.
entries.new: 他想走的话，最可能是因为他已经经历过那段时间，知道还留在卧室里的人不会注意到我们。若是这样，违背他亲历过的事情也没有意义。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Both of us stepped out of the living room. Before moving down, I looked at the floor one last time, making a mental note of the arrangement of footprints for later.
entries.new: 我们两人走出起居室。下楼之前，我又最后看了一眼地面，把脚印的分布默默记在心里，留待之后对照。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Will it work?
entries.new: 能用吗？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yes, I think so. It should be compatible with your watch.
entries.new: 能吧。应该和你的手表配得上。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It was still inside its original package, so it hadn't been used at all. It took me a couple of minutes to get it out with no tools, and as soon as I succeeded, it became clear that it would easily fit. It looked the same as the one that was already inside the wristwatch.
entries.new: 它还装在原包装里，一次都没用过。手边没有工具，我花了几分钟才弄开，取出来一看就知道尺寸正合适，和手表里原来那颗一模一样。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I uncovered the battery slot again and removed the original battery. I headed to the first partition and left it in a drawer since I didn't have a proper place to dispose of it.
entries.new: 我再次打开电池槽，取出原来的电池。这里没有合适的地方丢弃，我便走到第一个隔间，把它留在了抽屉里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After that, I put the new one in place. It was small, so it took me a bit, but it fit perfectly. Finished, I put the cover back on and left the packaging in the same drawer.
entries.new: 之后我装上新的那颗。电池很小，费了些工夫，但装得严丝合缝。弄完后我盖回表盖，把包装也留在了同一个抽屉里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Anything?
entries.new: ……怎么样？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I turned the watch around and immediately saw that something had changed.
entries.new: 我把手表转过来，立刻看出有哪里变了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It did, but I was wrong.
entries.new: 确实变了，不过是我猜错了。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...I told you. I wasn't hiding anything.
entries.new: ……我说过了，我什么都没藏。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That's not quite what I meant. Look.
entries.new: 我不是那个意思。你看。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I showed him what the screen displayed.
entries.new: 我把屏幕上的内容给他看。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The four digits displaying the time showed a "--:--", which most likely indicated that no time had been set.{w} I would have assumed that the battery removal reset the internal system if not for what was above the time.
entries.new: 显示时间的四个数字变成了“--:--”，多半表示还没有设定时间。{w}若不是时间上方的显示，我本会以为拆电池把内部系统重置了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That's strange... It might've been like this when I first got the watch.
entries.new: 奇怪……我刚拿到手表的时候，说不定就是这个样子。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: This should be displaying the current date, right?
entries.new: 这里显示的本该是当前日期，对吧？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes.
entries.new: 对。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...It wasn't.
entries.new: ……并不是。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The date, above the time, showed "9999-12-31".
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I suppose there was no point to my plan, then. I don't know if you purposely arranged this, but something definitely happened to this watch.
entries.new: ……看来我这个计划是白费了。我不知道这是不是你刻意安排的，但这块手表肯定出过什么事。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It still works, though. The battery had to be the problem. Give it to me.
entries.new: 不过它还能用。问题肯定出在电池上。给我吧。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I handed it over, and he began to fiddle with the buttons.
entries.new: 我递过去，他便开始拨弄按钮。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I see, I can easily set the time with these.
entries.new: 原来如此，用这些按钮很容易就能调时间。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The time began displaying numbers, and Sai set it to {time=4:00.}
entries.new: 时间重新显示出数字，Sai 把它调成了 {time=4:00.}
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I really don't get what happened, but I'm glad I won't have to get rid of it. I'll make sure to thank Ashiya for the new battery too.
entries.new: 我还是搞不懂到底怎么回事，不过不用把它丢掉就好。新电池的事，也得好好谢谢芦屋。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I wanted to object again, but I couldn't find the words. I didn't know anymore if Sai was aware of what had happened.
entries.new: 我还想再反驳，却找不到话说。我已经不知道 Sai 到底清不清楚发生了什么。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You traveled to the past, right?
entries.new: 你是穿越到过去的，对吧？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Me?
entries.new: 我？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Let's say you appeared in hallway A. I'll even believe what you said: you realized the Sekimeiya was gone and failed to notice it was in your hip pack.
entries.new: 就假设你出现在 A 走廊。你说的那些我也愿意相信：你发现 Sekimeiya 不见了，却没注意到它就在你的腰包里。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You have a watch, so you would've looked at it to find out how far back you went.{w} Did you do that?
entries.new: 你带着手表，肯定会看一眼，好知道自己回到了多久以前。{w}你看了吗？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...{w}I didn't.{w} However, I didn't travel to the past either, so your question is pretty pointless.
entries.new: ……{w}没有。{w}不过我根本没穿越到过去，你这个问题毫无意义。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The date was the odd point. Swapping the batteries shouldn't have changed it to "9999-12-31", and it was unlikely Sai edited it. Needless to say, it was the highest date the format of the watch would allow.
entries.new: 蹊跷的是日期。只换电池，不该把它变成“9999-12-31”，也不像是 Sai 改的。不用说，那是手表格式所能显示的最大日期。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Anyway, let's go back down.
entries.new: 总之，先下去吧。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: To the crystal floor?
entries.new: 去水晶层？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes. I have something to do.
entries.new: 对。我有点事要办。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...All right.
entries.new: ……好吧。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We started moving down. I didn't know what Sai planned to do, but I still had to find Shiroya, who most likely was somewhere below us.
entries.new: 我们开始下楼。我不知道 Sai 打算做什么，但我还得找到 Shiroya——她多半就在下面某处。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya's not currently in the attic, right?
entries.new: Shiroya 现在不在阁楼里，对吧？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Who's that?
entries.new: 谁啊？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I let it go before he got on my nerves.
entries.new: 我赶在他惹我心烦之前，不再追问了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We silently walked all the way down. At first glance, the floor still appeared desolate.
entries.new: 我们默默往下走了一路。乍看之下，这层楼依旧一片荒凉。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What did you want to do?
entries.new: 你本来打算做什么？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Oh, let's go to the security room.
entries.new: 啊，去监控室吧。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Through hallway A, we began walking toward it. His pace was slow, and I'd been in front of him the whole time.
entries.new: 我们穿过A走廊，朝那里走去。他脚步很慢，我一路都走在他前头。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Once I was about to reach the doorknob, I heard a sound behind me.
entries.new: 我正要伸手去够门把，身后传来一声响动。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I saw an empty hallway as I heard the event room closing.
entries.new: 走廊空无一人，同时我听见活动室的门合上了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Upon realizing I'd lowered my guard, I sprinted as fast as I could.
entries.new: 我这才意识到自己松懈了，立刻拔腿狂奔。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I entered the event room, but it was empty. By the time I opened the door to hallway B, I'd lost him.
entries.new: 我冲进活动室，里面空无一人。等我推开通往B走廊的门，已经不见他的踪影。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Every door around me was closed except the lobby's. I didn't know where he'd gone, but as soon as I picked the wrong path, Sai would escape.
entries.new: 四周的门都关着，只有通往大堂的那扇开着。我不知道他去了哪里，可只要我选错方向，Sai 就会溜掉。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Running toward hallway C meant facing the task of searching through every floor, and going to the lobby meant that he could already have been in hallway A. Instead, I opened a bunch of doors in hallway B hoping he'd taken shelter in one of them, as I couldn't hear the distant sound of running footsteps.
entries.new: 往C走廊追，意味着要把每一层都搜一遍；去大堂，又可能他早已绕进A走廊。我索性在B走廊一连推开几扇门，指望他躲进了其中一间——毕竟远处并没有传来奔跑的脚步声。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They were all empty, and I didn't bother searching too deeply into them.{w} I understood what Sai's business on that floor was. He needed us to go there to have a chance at escaping—he had no way of dodging me on the upper floors.
entries.new: 里面全是空的，我也没心思一间间细查。{w}我明白 Sai 为什么要在这层动手脚了：他需要我们来到这一层，才有机会脱身——在楼上，他根本甩不开我。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I sighed. Perhaps I should've expected it, but I didn't blame myself too much. I'd lost Sai, and he'd accomplished his goal of ditching me. Just in case, I went to the security room, where he said he wanted to go.
entries.new: 我叹了口气。或许我早该料到，不过也没太责怪自己。Sai 从我手里溜了，他成功甩掉了我。为防万一，我还是去了他说想去的监控室。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was empty, and the computer remained suspended. In a corner, I saw the suitcase that Katei had brought there from hallway C.
entries.new: 里面空无一人，电脑仍停在休眠状态。角落里放着 Katei 从C走廊搬来的那只手提箱。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What was Sai's deal, exactly? Maybe I'd have a better idea once I returned to the attic, but I still needed to find Shiroya.
entries.new: Sai 到底在打什么主意？也许回到阁楼后能想明白些，但当务之急还是找到 Shiroya。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I went to look at the computer's time, which read {time=12:18.}{w} I sat on the chair and sighed in exasperation for a few seconds. There were plenty of things to think about, but instead my mind went to something that continued to gnaw at me.
entries.new: 我去看了电脑上的时间，显示为 {time=12:18.}{w} 我在椅子上坐下，懊恼地叹了几秒钟的气。该想的事多得是，我的思绪却偏偏飘向那件一直耿耿于怀的事。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai's watch. More specifically, the date "9999-12-31".
entries.new: Sai 的手表。更确切地说，是上面那个日期——「9999-12-31」。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: When I found Sai, he should've been in the attic. This means that it's very possible he traveled through time in some capacity, even though he kept denying it. If he did, his watch would've done the same.
entries.new: 我找到 Sai 的时候，他本该待在阁楼里。也就是说，他很可能以某种方式进行了时间穿越，尽管他一直否认。若果真如此，他的手表也该一同穿越。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: "9999-12-31" hints at that even further.{w} It's the highest date the watch could display, so it could be linked to another common concept related to time travel: loops.
entries.new: 「9999-12-31」更是加深了这个猜想。{w}那是手表能显示的最大日期，因此可能与时间穿越的另一常见概念有关——循环。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Looping through time—reliving the same portion of time over and over. I'm jumping to this thought not only because of the date, but also because the battery ran out before the time it was supposed to.
entries.new: 在时间里循环——反复重历同一段时间。我之所以会想到这个，不仅因为那个日期，也因为电池在预计耗尽之前就没了电。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: For example, if the watch is in the process of traveling from {time=12:20} to the past, until it reaches the travel point, the time displayed would increase per travel. If that's repeated infinite times, the date would eventually hit its maximum value and stay there.
entries.new: 举例来说，如果手表正从 {time=12:20} 向过去穿越，那么在抵达穿越点之前，每穿越一次，显示的时间就会增长。如此重复无数次，日期终会达到最大值，并停在那里。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: If the watch had repeated that process infinitely when I saw it, the date could make a bit of sense. Similarly, every few years, the battery would run out, so replacing it would allow the time to continue advancing.
entries.new: 如果我看到手表时，它已经将这一过程重复了无数次，那这个日期就勉强说得通了。同理，每隔几年电池就会耗尽，换上新的，时间便能继续向前。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: So, assuming something of the sort is what happened, is it a coincidence that I just so happened to experience the loop in which the battery had to be replaced?{w} There would be times in which the watch would appear functional and ones in which the date wouldn't have reached the year 9,999 yet. All of those would have to reach the same loop point, which contradicts the way I thought this worked, because traveling to the past would end up modifying it in different manners.
entries.new: 那么，假设事情正是如此，我恰好碰上需要更换电池的那一轮循环，难道只是巧合？{w}有时手表看上去还正常，有时日期尚未走到9999年。这些情况最终都得汇入同一个循环点，这与我设想的运作方式相矛盾——毕竟穿越回过去，会以各不相同的方式改变它。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: But I suppose it's pointless to think about this because a bunch of other contradictions prevent anything like that from ever happening.
entries.new: 不过再想下去也是徒劳，因为还有一堆矛盾之处，让这种事根本不可能发生。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: To begin with, if the wristwatch had traveled back insane amounts of times, it would have physically degraded. If it had survived at least the 8,000 years needed to reach 9,999, the metal would've appeared rusty, and it's hard to believe it wouldn't have just disintegrated instantly.
entries.new: 首先，这只腕表若穿越了难以计数的次数，早就该出现物理上的损耗。它至少要撑过八千年才能走到9999年，金属理该锈迹斑斑，很难相信它不会瞬间崩解。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Also, Sai had to be the one to bring it back through time, so he'd be older, and he couldn't have existed for the same number of years without dying. This would be circumvented if going to the past replicated your past body, but then the watch's date and time would reset after every travel too.
entries.new: 再者，把手表带回过去的人必须是 Sai，那他就得一同变老，不可能活过那么多年还不死。若穿越回过去会复制你过去的身体，这一点倒能绕开，可那样一来，手表上的日期和时间每穿越一次也该重置。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: This is not how the Sekimeiya works. If you travel thirty minutes to the past, during those thirty minutes, two versions of you exist at the same time. If Sai went back with his watch that many times, he would have created a new copy of himself each travel.
entries.new: Sekimeiya 并不是这样运作的。你若穿越回三十分钟前，那三十分钟里就会同时存在两个你。Sai 若带着手表回去过那么多次，每一次都会造出一个新的自己。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: That isn't all. Naturally, I'm thinking about this to justify the watch's date, but there's no apparent reason why Sai would travel back to the same spot more than once.{w} And if he somehow could circumvent aging, it'd mean that after the point he traveled from, he couldn't exist anymore; if there is a point in time in which he always travels back, he could never make it past that point. Despite that, I'm sure that if I go to the attic right now, I'll see him.
entries.new: 还不止这些。我这样推想，自然是为了解释手表上的日期，可 Sai 根本没有理由一次又一次回到同一个时间点。{w}而就算他有办法绕开衰老，那也意味着他从某个时间点穿越离开后，便无法再存在于此后；倘若存在一个他总会穿越回去的时刻，他就永远越不过那一刻。尽管如此，我确信此刻回到阁楼，仍能见到他。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The origin of the Sai I was talking to a few minutes ago should give me some insight, but I'm not sure how much, because he himself seemed unaware of what happened to his watch.
entries.new: 几分钟前和我说话的那个 Sai，他的来历应该能提供些线索，但能有多少，我也说不准——毕竟连他自己似乎都不知道手表出了什么事。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Did the date go up to the year 9,999 for no reason? Was it a malfunction, maybe? Tied with the battery's loss of power, it seems like a bit of a stretch to treat it as one.
entries.new: 日期会无缘无故跳到9999年吗？也许只是故障？可若再把电池耗尽一并算上，单以故障解释，未免牵强。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The facts are as follows: Sai probably only traveled once because countless versions of himself didn't exist at the same time. The watch can't be in a regular time loop because the Sekimeiya doesn't work like that and because the watch would physically degrade before reaching the year 9,999.{w} And yet the date reached its highest possible value. I really feel that something of significance might be the cause behind it...
entries.new: 事实如下：Sai 大概只穿越过一次，因为并不存在无数个同时并存的他自己。手表也不可能处在寻常的时间循环里，一来 Sekimeiya 不是那样运作的，二来手表在抵达9999年之前就会先一步损耗殆尽。{w}可日期偏偏走到了它的最大值。我总觉得，背后或许有什么要紧的东西在作祟……
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: One last important thing I can take from this is that if the watch's status was caused by Sai traveling to the past, adding that he was surprised to see it disabled and that it was working at {time=11:36}, it's possible that he hadn't yet traveled by that time.
entries.new: 最后还有一点值得留意：倘若手表的状态是 Sai 穿越回过去造成的，那么再考虑到他看见手表停摆时的惊讶，以及 {time=11:36} 时它还正常运转，他到那个时刻为止，或许还没有穿越过。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I also had to keep in mind that Sai had some good reason to escape from me and that he was in the middle of doing something when I found him. The battery's power running out also felt like it was pretty important, but I couldn't reach any conclusion regarding that.
entries.new: 我也不能忘记，Sai 甩开我一定有他的理由，而且我找到他时，他正做某件事做到一半。电池耗尽这件事似乎也颇为关键，可我对此得不出任何结论。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I shifted my focus. I had to find Shiroya, but I'd already looked through the crystal floor twice.
entries.new: 我收回思绪。我得找到 Shiroya，可水晶层我已经找过两遍了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Being in front of the computer made me think of the cameras. It was possible the system had restored, so I tried to see if I could do something with it and find out where Shiroya and Sai were.
entries.new: 坐在电脑前，我想起了监控摄像头。系统说不定已经恢复，于是我试着看看能否操作它，查明 Shiroya 和 Sai 的下落。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I clicked on the program with a security camera icon. The text "logged in as Katei Kuiji" was still on the bottom. When I noticed it, I wondered if Katei intentionally left his account logged in to use the excuse that anyone could've used it.
entries.new: 我点开了那个带监控摄像头图标的程序。底部的「以 Katei Kuiji 身份登录」字样还在。看到这行字，我不禁猜想，Katei 是不是故意让账号保持登录，好在必要时推说谁都能使用它。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Next, I pressed "Initialize Camera Monitoring", but as before, I was met with a message box containing the "Couldn't detect video footage" text. Trying to look at the archived footage yielded no result either.{w} In the lower right corner was a button that read "Power system off", but it was grayed out.
entries.new: 接着我按下「初始化摄像头监控」，可和之前一样，弹出的仍是一个写着「未检测到视频画面」的提示框。想查看存档录像同样毫无结果。{w}右下角有个「电源系统关闭」的按钮，却是灰色的，无法点击。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was a messy and hard to follow interface, so the only thing I recognized was a symbol of a wrench that was probably the settings menu.
entries.new: 界面杂乱难懂，我只认出那个扳手图标，大概就是设置菜单。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When I clicked on it, a panel with several options appeared. One in particular caught my eye: "Footage".
entries.new: 点开之后，弹出一个列着若干选项的面板。其中一项格外醒目：「录像」。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A new screen appeared after selecting it, showing the path where the recordings could be found. The set path was "B:\Archived", which sounded simple enough.
entries.new: 选中后跳出新的界面，显示录像的存放路径。设定的是「B:\Archived」，听上去倒简单明了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In case the program was the cause of the issue, I went ahead and looked for that specific folder. "B:\" indicated that it wasn't saved on the main drive.
entries.new: 为防问题出在程序本身，我干脆去找那个文件夹。「B:\」说明它并非存放在主硬盘上。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I searched for it, but I couldn't find it. No extra drive appeared to exist whatsoever, so it made sense that the footage wasn't being detected.
entries.new: 我找了一遍，却没有找到。根本不存在什么额外的硬盘，录像检测不到也就说得通了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I kept looking, but to no avail. I performed a thorough search for the word "Archived", but none of the results interested me. The time had been passing fast, and I didn't want to waste any more of it. The computer displayed {time=12:31.}
entries.new: 我继续翻找，依旧一无所获。我把「Archived」这个词彻底搜了一遍，结果没有一条让我感兴趣。时间流逝得飞快，我不想再浪费下去。电脑显示的时间是 {time=12:31.}
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stood up from the chair. I had to search through the entire floor, but going to the attic for aid was potentially a better choice. Although I didn't think Shiroya would go hide, searching alone was never ideal.
entries.new: 我从椅子上起身。整层楼都得搜一遍，但回阁楼求助或许是更好的选择。我虽然不认为 Shiroya 会躲起来，可独自搜寻终究不是办法。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Once I left the room, I was once again met with the cold silence of a barren floor. The door closing behind me didn't echo as well as it should've because the smoke cover on the ceiling didn't allow the sound to bounce back properly.
entries.new: 我一走出房间，迎面又是空旷楼层那冰冷的寂静。身后关上的门没有像应该的那样发出回响，因为天花板上的隔烟层让声音无法正常反射。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Despite that, I still noticed the sound of someone approaching from hallway C.
entries.new: 尽管如此，我还是听见有人从C走廊走来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was Shiroya. As soon as she saw me, she sped up with a concerned look. As if I were her reflection, I reacted the same way.
entries.new: 是 Shiroya。她一看见我，便带着忧色加快了脚步。我像照镜子一样，也做出了同样的反应。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Where were you...!? Are you okay?
entries.new: 你跑到哪儿去了……！？没事吧？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Y-Yeah, I'm fine... I've been on this floor, for the most part. I was searching for you.
entries.new: 嗯、嗯，我没事……我基本一直待在这层。刚才在找你。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I went to the room where you said you'd return to, but you weren't there...
entries.new: 我去了你说会回来的那个房间，可你不在……
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: You went there? You just had to wait.
entries.new: 你去了？明明只要等着就好。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: No... Right as you touched the Sekimeiya, I disappeared too.
entries.new: 不是……就在你碰到 Sekimeiya 的那一刻，我也消失了。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...{w}Those words came as a surprise, so I forced my breathing to remain normal.
entries.new: ……{w}这话出乎我的意料，我强自让呼吸保持平稳。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You traveled too? At the same time...?{w} Why did I never see you, then?
entries.new: 你也穿越了？同一时间……？{w}那为什么我一直没见到你？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Well... Just as you touched it, I appeared on the second floor, inside the offices. It was disorienting, like I changed places instantly. That's what happened to you too, right? I thought your travel might've somehow taken me along with you.
entries.new: 这个……就在你碰到它的瞬间，我出现在了二楼的办公室。那种感觉让人晕头转向，就像瞬间换了个地方。你也是这样吧？我还以为是你穿越时，把我也一起带上了。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I couldn't believe it was real... Talking about it and having it happen are two totally different things. Where did it send you?
entries.new: 我实在不敢相信那是真的……听说和亲身经历完全是两回事。它把你送到了哪里？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I appeared in the security room. Do you know how far back you went?
entries.new: 我出现在了监控室。你知道自己回到了多久以前吗？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I think so. I spent a few minutes sitting down since I could barely understand what happened... Then I went to the attic to confirm I'd really traveled back in time. When I saw that the door was still locked, I figured it had really happened.
entries.new: 应该是吧。我当时几乎没弄明白发生了什么，坐着缓了几分钟……然后去了阁楼，想确认自己是不是真的回到了过去。看到门还锁着，我才确定这一切真的发生了。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Eventually, I started to go back down until I heard sounds approaching me from below that made me hide on the fourth floor. It was a group of people, so I thought it was us when we first entered the attic.
entries.new: 后来我往下走，听到下面有动静朝我这边来，只好躲到四楼。来的是好几个人，我还以为是我们最初进阁楼时的那群人。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I figured I could go to the crystal floor to look at the time. I looked at the computer and estimated I'd gone back about forty minutes.
entries.new: 我想可以去水晶层看看时间。我看了电脑，估计自己回到了大约四十分钟前。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: So you opened the door to the security room... We both traveled the same amount of time, then.{w} I-I see... I was in the cleaning room when you came down, so we didn't see each other.
entries.new: 所以监控室的门是你打开的……那我们俩穿越的时间一样。{w}我、我明白了……你下来的时候我在清洁间，所以我们才没碰面。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Hm...{w} The others returned and then went up again. I knew they were going to the attic, so I followed them to see if everything was actually repeating.{w} I didn't go up immediately, so when I got there, Sai and Katei were already in the bedroom. I entered and listened from the hallway, and they were saying the same things as before.
entries.new: 嗯……{w}其他人回来后，又上去了。我知道他们要去阁楼，就跟上去看看一切是不是真的在重演。{w}我没有立刻上去，所以等我到的时候，Sai 和 Katei 已经在卧室里了。我进了阁楼，在走廊里听着，他们说的和之前一模一样。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I was so scared of being seen, Atsuki. If the past changes, do things just... unravel?
entries.new: 我好怕被人看见，Atsuki。要是过去被改变，事情会不会就……彻底崩坏？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I have no idea. Nobody noticed me this entire time, so it was all consistent with the past that we know. I think nothing changed. Everything I experienced with people from the past was just me observing them without them knowing I was there, so nothing deviated. I even tried to change the past by saving the second Naomi, but it was useless.
entries.new: 我完全不知道。这段时间一直没人注意到我，所以一切都和我们所知的过去吻合。我想什么都没改变。我和过去那些人的接触，都只是我在旁边看着他们，而他们不知道我在场，所以没有任何偏离。我甚至试过救下第二个 Naomi 来改变过去，但毫无用处。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Anyway, Sai and Katei really didn't leave the attic, did they...?
entries.new: 总之，Sai 和 Katei 真的没有离开阁楼，对吧……？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I don't think so, no. I knew we'd be going down in a bit, so I hid in the floor 6 offices. I stayed there for a while so Akaro didn't see me as he went up. Then I came here to meet with you, but you weren't in the room.
entries.new: 我想是没有。我知道我们过一会儿就要下楼，就躲进了六楼的办公室。我在那里待了一阵，免得 Akaro 上楼时看见我。之后我来这里找你，可你不在房间里。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I wasn't...? I suppose I might've spent a few minutes with Sai in the lobby, but I thought you'd stay there.
entries.new: 我不在……？我可能在大厅和 Sai 待了几分钟，但我以为你会留在那里。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: With Sai? But he was in the attic. What do you mean? I waited a bit in the room until I got worried something had gone wrong. I saw the Sekimeiya too. It was still where we left it, but it changed colors to the gray from before.
entries.new: 和 Sai 一起？可他当时在阁楼啊。你是什么意思？我在房间里等了一会儿，后来担心出了什么差错。我也看到了 Sekimeiya。它还在我们放下的地方，但颜色变成了之前那种灰色。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: So activating it is what powers it off like that.
entries.new: 所以启动它就会让它那样关闭。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Probably, but I didn't try to touch it again. I closed the cabinet before I looked around this floor briefly, and I thought that you might be back in the attic. I went there, but not much had seemed to change.{w} I stayed in the hallway to listen to the conversation going on in the bedroom. Even if they'd seen me, it wouldn't have mattered much since we had just left from their perspective.
entries.new: 大概吧，不过我没敢再碰它。我先关上展示柜，把这一层大致看了一圈，然后想你可能已经回阁楼了。我上去后，发现似乎没多少变化。{w}我留在走廊里听卧室里的谈话。就算被他们看见，也没什么大不了的，因为从他们的角度看，我们才刚刚离开。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: At that point, Sai was still there, right?
entries.new: 那个时候，Sai 还在那里，对吧？
entries.speaker: a
