I'd purposely put it horizontally behind the cabinet's so that Sai would press his hand on it and only notice the bigger shape at the front.{w} Fortunately, I'd been able to abuse his minor surprise by taking out the cabinet key and leaving the smaller one inside. When the body inspection proceeded, he assumed the right pocket was clean and didn't check it again.
entries.new: 储物柜的钥匙很小。我故意把它横着塞在展示柜钥匙后面，这样 Sai 摸到时，只会注意到前面那个更大的轮廓。{w}幸好我借着他那点意外的空当，把展示柜钥匙取了出来，小钥匙仍留在口袋里。之后继续搜身时，他便以为右边口袋已经查过，没有再检查一遍。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Hm, what's this?
entries.new: ……嗯，这是什么？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I looked up. Sai was feeling one of Katei's pockets, and it appeared he'd found something inside. That time, it was Sai who first put his hand in and retrieved, yet again, a key.
entries.new: 我抬起头。Sai 正在摸 Katei 的一个口袋，似乎在里面摸到了什么。这一次是 Sai 先把手伸进去，掏出来的又是一把钥匙。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, right. I'd also forgotten I had this.
entries.new: 哦，对。我也忘了自己身上有这个。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: We all recognized it. It was the old-looking key we'd found on the floor of hallway A.
entries.new: 我们全都认了出来。那是我们在 A走廊地板上捡到的那把看起来很旧的钥匙。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Didn't you say you'd keep it somewhere safe?
entries.new: 你不是说要把它放到安全的地方吗？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I forgot, but don't worry. My pocket is plenty safe.
entries.new: 忘了，不过放心吧。我口袋里就很安全。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: After staring at it, Sai put the key back in.{w} In the next pocket, he found something else. For the third time in a row, they were keys.
entries.new: Sai 盯着它看了半晌，把钥匙放了回去。{w}他又在下一个口袋里摸到了别的东西。连续第三次，都是钥匙。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You know these four as well. One is for the bathrooms, another is for the security room, this one opens my locker in the staff room, and this one is for the door leading to floor 2.
entries.new: 这四把你们也见过。一把是洗手间的，一把是监控室的，这把开我在员工室的储物柜，还有这把是通往二楼那扇门的。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Silently, Sai finished the inspection without finding anything else. Still unsatisfied, he took out all the keys once again and attempted to insert them into the door's keyhole.
entries.new: Sai 没再说什么，把剩下的检查做完，别无所获。他似乎仍不满意，又把所有钥匙取出来，逐一试着插进门上的锁孔。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They don't work.{w} You're done, then.
entries.new: 都开不了。{w}那你也查完了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He gave the keys back to Katei, and before the next person could be examined, I voiced a thought.
entries.new: 他把钥匙还给 Katei。下一个人还没开始检查，我便说出了心里的一个念头。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That first key... Could it be for the hidden door we found?
entries.new: 最先那把钥匙……会不会就是开我们找到的那扇暗门的？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I just thought the same thing. Both have this feeling of being fairly old, and there's no other door in this building that does.
entries.new: 我也刚想到这个。两样东西都让人觉得相当旧，而这栋楼里也没有别的门给人这种感觉。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Huh. You might be right, actually.
entries.new: 嚯。说不定还真是这样。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: We thought the culprit dropped it in a hurry. If that's what happened, it could be why they had to remove the handle.
entries.new: 我们原本以为，是犯人匆忙间把它掉在了那里。如果真是这样，也许正因如此，他们才不得不把门把手拆掉。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: But the key spent a long time on the floor, so why didn't they retrieve it before we found it? They already left the suitcase in hallway C at some point.
entries.new: 可那把钥匙在地板上放了很久。他们为什么没在我们发现之前把它捡回去？毕竟他们不知什么时候就已经把行李箱留在了 C走廊。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We went quiet at the mention of the suitcase. We'd more or less assumed that Naomi had left it there, but we weren't sure anymore.
entries.new: 一提到行李箱，大家都沉默了。我们之前大致认定是 Naomi 把它留在那里的，可如今已经不敢肯定了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You're right... Maybe they wanted to avoid every possibility of being spotted and didn't want to step into hallway A.{w} The fingerprints that you saw... Are they clear enough to be useful? If the police can figure out who they belong to, that could be a path to the culprit.
entries.new: 你说得对……也许他们想杜绝一切被人看到的可能，所以不愿意踏进 A走廊。{w}你看到的那些指纹……清晰到能派上用场吗？如果警方能查出指纹属于谁，那或许就是追到犯人的一条线索。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'm not sure. The clear ones were all replaced by mine, but there might've been some more around because you need to push the wall in order to open it.
entries.new: 不好说。清晰的那几枚全被我的指纹盖掉了，不过周围可能还有别的，毕竟得推开那面墙才能把门打开。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I see. If whoever it is doesn't go erase them upon realizing that we found them, some should still remain. But if they're one of us, the fingerprints won't mean anything since it won't be provable that they were left before we found the door.
entries.new: 原来如此。如果那个人意识到我们已经发现了门，却没有去擦掉指纹，那应该还会留下一些。可要是犯人就在我们之中，指纹就没有意义了，因为无法证明那是在我们发现门之前留下的。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yeah. There's one more thing, too.{w} When we discovered the secret door, my first thought was that someone bypassed our searches by hiding there.
entries.new: 嗯。还有一点。{w}我们发现那扇暗门时，我首先想到的是，有人藏在那里，躲过了我们的搜查。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: However, even though the light wasn't very bright, what Shiroya and I initially saw were three distinguishable fingerprints. I don't think any were overlapping.
entries.new: 可是，尽管光线并不算亮，我和 Shiroya 最初看到的却是三枚清晰可辨的指纹。我记得它们并没有互相重叠。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You mean that the door was only recently opened once?
entries.new: 你的意思是，那扇门最近只被打开过一次？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: From hallway A, maybe. If it was only opened once, it can't be that someone went to hide there all the times we searched unless they spent hours inside. Maybe that proves it wasn't one of us.
entries.new: 从 A 走廊来看，或许吧。如果只开过一次，那就不可能每次我们搜查时都有人躲进去——除非他们在里面待了好几个小时。这也许能证明，犯人不在我们之中。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Huh...{w} I suppose they could've used the Sekimeiya to teleport inside without opening the wall, but that doesn't sound likely.{w} Anyway, who's next?
entries.new: 唔……{w}要说他们用 Sekimeiya 传送进去，根本不用开墙，倒也不是不可能，但听上去可能性不大。{w}总之，下一个是谁？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Shiroya volunteered.{w} In her case, nothing was found in her clothes. Her purse was almost empty and only contained a wallet, two of the three tickets we'd bought for the event, our personal identification to match the tickets, and the key to my house.
entries.new: Shiroya 主动上前。{w}她身上什么都没搜出来。她的手提包里几乎空无一物，只有一只钱包、我们为活动买的三张票中的两张、与票对应的身份证明，以及我家的钥匙。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Akaro was next. In the same way, his inspection was handled quickly, and once again, personal keys, his identification, and his own entrance ticket were all we found on him. It wasn't surprising, as the same kind of body search would also be performed before entering the tower.
entries.new: 接着是 Akaro。同样，他的检查很快就结束了，从他身上找到的依旧只有他自己的钥匙、身份证明和入场券。这并不奇怪，毕竟进塔之前也会进行同样的搜身。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: All right, done. Finally, I don't mean to suspect you, Erina, but ignoring you would defeat the purpose of what you're trying to accomplish.
entries.new: 好，结束了。最后，Erina，我不是想怀疑你，可要是跳过你，你想达成的目的就落空了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...I know. That's fine.
entries.new: ……我知道。没关系。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: She moved ahead. Usually, it would've been worth considering that the person who proposed the arrangement had a secret reason, but I knew Erina was genuine. Sai gently made sure she hadn't been concealing anything, and by letting us know that her purse was clean as well, he put an end to our last measure.{w} Personal keys and identification had also been found in her purse. We were specifically searching for hidden keys, so even though it was normal we all possessed ours, Sai made sure to confirm that their shape didn't match the bedroom door's.
entries.new: 她走上前。通常来说，提出这个办法的人也许有别的盘算，但我知道 Erina 是真心实意的。Sai 温和又仔细地确认她没有藏任何东西，又告诉我们她的手提包也没有问题，我们最后一道措施就此结束。{w}她的包里同样只有她自己的钥匙和身份证明。我们要找的正是藏起来的钥匙，因此虽然人人带着自己的钥匙再正常不过，Sai 还是逐一确认了它们的形状与卧室门锁不符。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Good, this went well. Now, doing what I explained should be easy.
entries.new: 很好，很顺利。那么，按我说的去做应该不难。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Since nobody had any complaints, I took one screwdriver out of a drawer and compared it with the screws that kept the door's handle attached.
entries.new: 既然没人有意见，我从抽屉里拿出一把螺丝刀，对着固定门把手的那几颗螺丝比了比。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It'll work. It's not a perfect match, but it'll definitely suffice.
entries.new: 行得通。虽说不是完全吻合，但绝对够用了。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We wanted to hide the key and outer handle outside, right? There's not much of a point to it since the chain will prevent anyone from entering, but can you think of a good place to hide it?
entries.new: 我们是要把钥匙和外把手藏到门外吧？反正有门链挡着，谁也进不来，其实意义不大——不过，你能想到什么藏东西的好地方吗？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I feel like under the bathroom carpet is good enough. Like you said, it's not too important.{w} Regarding the handle, no great spot comes to mind, but it doesn't matter anyway. The attic's full of removable handles, so someone outside could probably unscrew one to use it on the door if they really wanted to open it. In case that happens, we have the chain to rely on.
entries.new: 我觉得藏在卫生间地毯下面就可以了。就像你说的，这本来也不太重要。{w}至于外把手，我一时想不出什么好地方，不过反正无所谓。阁楼里可拆的把手多得是，外面的人若真想开门，卸一个下来装上去就行。真到那一步，还有门链拦着。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah, that sounds fine.
entries.new: 嗯，就这样吧。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: From the hallway, we clearly saw Sai leaving the key under the carpet without any kind of trick involved.
entries.new: 站在走廊里，我们看得清清楚楚，Sai 把钥匙塞到地毯下，没耍任何花招。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There it is. Only one thing to do, then.
entries.new: 找到了。那就只剩一件事要做了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We all moved back inside. With the big screwdriver, I removed the four screws of the inner handle, which fell on my hands.
entries.new: 我们一行人重新回到屋里。我用那把大螺丝刀拧下内侧把手的四颗螺丝，把手落在我的手上。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It'd be great if we could use this on the storeroom door.
entries.new: ……要是这法子能用在储藏室的门上就好了。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: We should all get ready to face the consequences of this. Don't be surprised if Ashiya blows this tiny action out of proportion.
entries.new: 大家都做好承担后果的准备吧。芦屋就算把这点小事大做文章，也不足为奇。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: We get it. That's fine, they can do what they want.
entries.new: 我们知道。无所谓，随他们怎么折腾。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I unscrewed the outer handle too and left both of them under the bed in the opposite bedroom.{w} In the door, only one hole became visible, as the keyhole wasn't found on the handles themselves. I made sure that the door couldn't be opened through the hole. A very short metal cylinder was poking out, but it was incredibly tight; we weren't going to turn it from the inside. When I was certain, I asked one last time.
entries.new: 外侧的把手我也一并卸下，两个都放到对面卧室的床底。{w}门上只露出一个孔，因为锁孔并不在把手上。我确认过，光凭这个孔打不开门。孔里探出一小截金属圆柱，但卡得极紧，从内侧根本拧不动。确认无误后，我最后问了一次。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Okay, this is it. If I close this door, we won't be able to open it again. Any final objection?
entries.new: 好，就到这里。这扇门一旦关上，我们就再也打不开了。还有人有异议吗？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I looked at the five of them, who knew what their next six hours would be like. Nobody opened their mouth, so I proceeded with the most important action.
entries.new: 我看了看他们五人——接下来六个小时会怎么过，他们心里都清楚。没有人开口，我便开始了那最关键的一步。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Slowly, I pushed the door forward. There was no friction against the floor, so I applied force until it satisfyingly set into place.
entries.new: 我缓缓把门往前推。门底与地面毫无摩擦，我一点点加力，直到它干脆地合到位。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...We'd sealed ourselves in. Surprisingly, it had taken a fair amount of concord. It was clear that nobody wanted to oppose the request because Erina made it. Any regrets were no longer meaningful.
entries.new: ……我们把自己封在了里面。出乎意料的是，这需要相当的齐心协力。显然，因为是 Erina 提出的请求，谁都不愿反对。事到如今，后悔也没有意义了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As the icing on the cake, we set the chain. I attempted to pull the door inward and push it outward, and as expected, it didn't budge. It had become a barrier from both sides, and the only way to unlock it would be telling the police where we'd left the key and detaching the chain for them. Cooperation from both sides was needed.
entries.new: 最后，我们又挂上了门链。我试着把门往里拉、往外推，果然纹丝不动。这扇门从两侧都成了屏障，要打开它，唯一的方法就是告诉警察钥匙放在了哪里，再替他们把门链取下——必须两边配合才行。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Now we wait. We could do with a deck of cards.
entries.new: 接下来就是等了。要是有副扑克牌就好了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We don't have any, so just try to stay still and quiet for once. You have been enough of a handful for one day.
entries.new: 没有牌。你就安安静静待着吧，哪怕就这一回。今天你惹的麻烦已经够多了。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Katei, there's a lot of resentment within you. How does it feel to know that after we wait six hours, you're gonna go straight to prison?
entries.new: Katei，你心里怨气可不小。等这六个小时过去，你下一步就是直接进监狱，作何感想？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I haven't done anything, so that won't happen.
entries.new: 我什么都没做，不会发生那种事。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Well, Ashiya doesn't seem to think the same, remember? Wasn't your authority revoked?
entries.new: 是吗，可芦屋好像不这么看，记得吗？你的权限不是已经被撤了吗？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...What's the time?
entries.new: ……现在几点了？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Did nothing else happen to your watch? Seems like it's still working fine.
entries.new: 你的表后来没再出别的问题？看起来走得挺正常。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Excuse me?
entries.new: 你说什么？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Oh, you know about that? Yeah, we fixed it earlier.
entries.new: 哦，你知道这事？是啊，之前就修好了。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...What?
entries.new: ……什么？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes, when we were waiting in the lobby, before you two appeared.
entries.new: 对，就在大厅等着的时候，你们俩还没来。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Wh-What?
entries.new: 什、什么？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...You didn't know? Sai asked me if I had lithium batteries because his watch wasn't working. He didn't mention that part when he told you what happened, but it was insignificant.
entries.new: ……你不知道？Sai 的表停了，问我有没有锂电池。他跟你讲经过的时候没提这一段，不过那也无关紧要。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: That's right. How did you know that, Atsuki?
entries.new: 没错。Atsuki，你是怎么知道的？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I wasn't talking about that. It didn't work once before that point. You're still claiming that wasn't you, right?
entries.new: 我说的不是这件事。在那之前，它已经停过一次了。你仍然坚持说那不是你干的吧？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Probably, since I don't know what you're talking about. It was convenient that Katei had the right type of battery in the security room.
entries.new: 大概吧，反正我不知道你在说什么。好在 Katei 在监控室里正好有这种电池。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What time and date was displayed when you changed the battery?
entries.new: 你换电池的时候，表上显示的是几月几日、几点？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Some minutes earlier than the time shown on the computer, which is when it must've stopped working. Then, I synced it properly again.
entries.new: 比电脑上显示的时间早几分钟，应该就是那时候停的。然后我重新把它校准了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Is that so...?
entries.new: 是这样吗……？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I don't know what you two are talking about, but I bet Sai failed at looking innocent again, right?
entries.new: 我不知道你们俩在说什么，不过我猜 Sai 又没装出那副无辜的样子，对吧？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Your irony knows no limits. Are you already thinking about how you'll lie to the police?
entries.new: 你这讽刺真是没完没了。你已经在琢磨怎么跟警察说谎了吧？
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Stop. We decided to stay here to end these discussions.
entries.new: 够了。我们决定留在这里，就是为了让这些争论到此为止。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I know. We're already locked in, though, so I have to rub it in Katei's face. I bet he's crying internally since his plan can't be finished now.
entries.new: 我知道。不过反正门已经锁了，我总得当面挖苦 Katei 几句。他的计划这下完不成了，心里肯定在哭吧。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...But Katei was right. Sai had noticed his watch stopped working again, so like I did, he asked for lithium batteries. That was further indication that he remembered the time he and I fixed the watch.
entries.new: ……但 Katei 说得没错。Sai 发现自己的表又停了，于是和我当初一样，找人要锂电池。这进一步说明，他记得他和我一起修表的那一次。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I'll go up and wait there.
entries.new: ……我到楼上去等。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Before the conversation snowballed again, Erina was the one who stopped Sai. To get as far from the door as possible, she chose to go rest in the upper bedroom. I knew that the illusion of tranquility was well achieved there, so taking advantage of her opening, I decided to follow her.
entries.new: 在话题再度失控之前，是 Erina 出面拦住了 Sai。为了离大门越远越好，她选择去楼上的卧室休息。我知道那里能很好地营造出安宁的假象，于是趁她提出这个建议，决定跟上去。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We will too. Separating ourselves into two groups of three will be the best way to utilize the space.
entries.new: 我们也上去。分成两组、每组三人，最能利用好这块地方。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Taking my cue, Shiroya went up with me. It seemed that Erina wanted to distance herself from the commotion that Sai and Katei continued to spawn, so by claiming the upstairs area for ourselves, we at least had a chance to remain unbothered for a long time.
entries.new: Shiroya 会意，随我一起上了楼。Erina 似乎想远离 Sai 和 Katei 不断掀起的喧闹，我们把楼上这块地方占下来，至少能有一阵子不受打扰。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Erina was sitting on a bed. She didn't pay much attention to our presence, so we silently sat on the opposite one.{w} Although six hours still had to pass, I promptly realized that I was still exhausted. It was possible I could sleep and fast-forward to {time=21.}
entries.new: Erina 坐在一张床上，没怎么理会我们，我们便默默坐到对面那张床上。{w}虽说还有六个小时要熬，我很快意识到自己依旧疲惫不堪。说不定睡一觉，就能直接睡到 {time=21.}。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We'd closed the hatch, so we couldn't hear the people under us. If they decided to keep arguing with moderate voices, we wouldn't hear it.
entries.new: 我们把盖板合上了，所以听不见楼下的人。就算他们打算压低声音继续吵，我们也听不到。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was time to disconnect. I'd been actively trying to piece everything together, but after choosing to abandon that, only time would force me to go back, in the case that something horrible awaited us at the end of the road.{w} At least, that was what I'd been ready to accept.
entries.new: 我该停止想这些了。我一直在努力想拼凑出全貌，但既然选择放手，就只有时间能逼我重新面对——假如路的尽头真有什么可怕的东西在等着我们。{w}至少，我已经准备好接受这一点了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You two didn't do anything to Isla, right...?
entries.new: 你们俩没对 Isla 做什么吧……？
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Taking both of us by surprise, Erina broke the silence she had set up. We raised our heads to see her deep eyes peering at us.
entries.new: Erina 忽然开口，打破了自己先前营造的沉默，我和身旁的人都吃了一惊。我们抬起头，正对上她那双深邃的眼睛。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Absolutely not...! We were sleeping in the other bedroom when everything happened.
entries.new: 绝不可能……！事情发生的时候，我们都在另一间卧室里睡觉。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Is it possible one of you left while the other was sleeping?
entries.new: 有没有可能，你们中的一个趁另一个睡着时离开过？
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...There's no way that happened.
entries.new: ……那不可能。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Do you two... trust each other that much even though there's a... a killer around? Are you two related? I saw that only one of you had house keys.
entries.new: 你们俩……就算附近可能有个……杀人凶手，你们还这么信任彼此吗？你们是亲属吗？我看见你们中只有一个人带着家门钥匙。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...We're just friends. Unfortunately, we have no way to prove it, but I promise that we left after... Isla was found.
entries.new: ……我们只是朋友。可惜我们没法证明这一点，但我保证，我们是在……Isla 被发现之后才离开的。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Earlier, I thought that Sai had a point. Why did you go straight to the lobby from hallway B without looking at the cleaning room?
entries.new: ……刚才我觉得 Sai 说得有道理。你们为什么从 B走廊直接去了大厅，却没看一眼清洁间？
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...That was my mistake. I should've acted as if we had already seen the cart and the missing Sekimeiya, but without a second thought, I had tried to appear surprised to make it seem like we'd never entered the room and couldn't have hidden it.
entries.new: ……那是我失策了。我本该表现得像是早就见过那辆推车和不见了的 Sekimeiya，可我却想都没想就装出惊讶的样子，好让人以为我们从未进过那个房间，也不可能把它藏起来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It might sound iffy, but what we said earlier was the truth. We went to the bathroom and then checked the event room and the lobby, where we thought people could be.
entries.new: 听起来也许不太可信，但我们之前说的都是实话。我们去了洗手间，然后去活动室和大厅看了看，觉得那里可能会有人。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Then, is Katei the only person who could've done it?
entries.new: 那么，能做到这件事的只有 Katei 一个人吗？
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Him...? Right, a lot of things regarding his whereabouts still don't make sense, but it shouldn't be that straightforward. It could've been an accident caused by the Sekimeiya.
entries.new: 他……？也对，关于他行踪的许多事情仍然说不通，但事情应该没这么简单。也可能是 Sekimeiya 造成的一场意外。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It was no accident. Isla saw something inside that cabinet, so she must've been lured there. Katei could've made her disappear; he's known about the Sekimeiya for longer than anyone else.{w} Then, he showed up after he left Isla's body in the cabinet... You two have experienced what the Sekimeiya does, but I don't know how to think about it.
entries.new: 那不是意外。Isla 在展示柜里看见了什么，所以一定是被人引过去的。Katei 可能让她消失了；他了解 Sekimeiya 的时间比任何人都长。{w} 然后，他把 Isla 的遗体留在展示柜里，自己又现身了……你们俩已经见识过 Sekimeiya 的作用，可我不知道该怎么看待这件事。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: It's possible that she... was sent to the cabinet from the future, right? Isn't that similar to something you said a while ago? If that happened, it could've been anyone, but she would have to still... be alive.
entries.new: 有没有可能，她……是从未来被送到展示柜里的？这和你之前说的某件事不是很像吗？如果真是这样，那谁都可能做到，但她必须还……活着。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: It was clear that Erina was attaching herself to the slightest gleam of hope that still persisted. The recording "proved" that Isla would be alive in the future, so Erina needed the time to pass to know if there was any trust left to be placed in it. She must've suggested waiting in the room in the hope of nothing occurring at {time=21.}
entries.new: 看得出来，Erina 正紧紧抓住最后一丝尚存的希望。那段录音「证明」了 Isla 在未来会活着，所以 Erina 需要等时间过去，才能知道它是否还值得相信。一定是她提议在房间里等到 {time=21.}，盼着那时什么都不会发生。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I've been thinking about it, but I don't know what could've happened. I-I'm sorry...
entries.new: 我一直在想这件事，可我也想不出究竟发生了什么。对、对不起……
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I wanted to give her even more hope, but I stopped myself, knowing that it would only make things worse if I was wrong. Even if Isla would somehow be alive in a month, her fate had already been shown to us: she would end up dead in the crystal floor's cabinet even if she had to travel there from a month in the future.
entries.new: 我本想再给她一些希望，但还是忍住了。我知道，如果我猜错了，只会让事情更糟。就算 Isla 一个月后真的还活着，她的命运也已经摆在我们眼前：即便她不得不从一个月后的未来穿越到那里，最终也会死在水晶展室的展示柜里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: At least, that was what I thought until I remembered that the two Naomi bodies defied that belief.{w} I believed that no matter what had happened to Isla, being dead inside the cabinet had to be the end of her path. However, two identical corpses hinted that the Sekimeiya could have some sway even after death. That was the actual hope Erina had to rely on—the recording didn't guarantee a bright future even if it turned out to be legitimate.
entries.new: 至少，我原本是这么想的——直到我记起那两具 Naomi 的遗体，这个念头才被推翻。{w} 我曾相信，无论 Isla 遭遇了什么，死在展示柜里都必然是她这条路的终点。然而，两具一模一样的尸体暗示着，Sekimeiya 在死后仍可能施加某种影响。那才是 Erina 真正能依靠的希望——即使那段录音是真的，也并不能保证一个光明的未来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In that instant, I felt a bubble of hope growing in my head.{w} The Sekimeiya hadn't caused any apparent effect when it touched Isla's dead body, even though we might not have seen it immediately. If that had created a living version of her at an earlier point in time like I speculated with Naomi... My thoughts were directed to Miiya once again.
entries.new: 那一瞬间，我脑中仿佛有一簇希望的泡沫在膨胀。{w} Sekimeiya 触碰到 Isla 的遗体时，并没有造成任何明显的效果——尽管我们也许没能立刻看出来。如果它像我对 Naomi 的推测那样，在更早的时间点创造出了一个活着的她……我的思绪又一次转向了 Miiya。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...But that bubble popped as soon as images of her burnt pieces of flesh appeared in my mind. The Sekimeiya had to exist somewhere two weeks in the past, but how could I touch a body that had been blown to pieces?
entries.new: ……可她的身体被烧成焦黑碎块的画面一浮现在脑中，那个泡沫便立刻破灭了。两周前的过去里，Sekimeiya 必定存在于某处，可我要怎么去触碰一具已经被炸成碎片的身体？
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I forced myself to stop thinking. The three of us present in the room had all lost someone very dear to us, and we all silently prayed that somehow they could be brought back.
entries.new: 我强迫自己不再想下去。房间里的三个人都失去了珍视的人，我们都在心里默默祈祷，盼着他们能以某种方式回来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was cruel to consider that there was a culprit somewhere who had killed at least once, possessing a higher knowledge of how the Sekimeiya worked—exactly what all of us needed the most.
entries.new: 一想到那个至少杀过一人的凶手就在某处，而且对 Sekimeiya 的运作方式了解得比我们更深——那恰恰是我们所有人最需要的东西——我就觉得无比残酷。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It's my fault, isn't it? It doesn't matter who did it... I brought her here.
entries.new: ……都怪我，对吧？不管是谁下的手……是我把她带到这里来的。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: What?
entries.new: 什么？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I bought the tickets for today... to make Isla happy. And instead, she...
entries.new: 我买今天的票……是想让 Isla 开心。结果她却……
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: It should have been me. Why would anyone want to hurt Isla?
entries.new: 该遭殃的人是我才对。为什么会有人想伤害 Isla？
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I had no idea how to respond to something as dark as that, and Shiroya clearly didn't either. We lapsed into silence for a few minutes. Part of Erina, I was sure, believed that Isla was still alive somewhere, while another part accepted that she was dead and already mourned her.
entries.new: 面对如此沉重的话，我不知该如何回应，Shiroya 显然也一样。我们沉默了好几分钟。我确信，Erina 心里一部分仍相信 Isla 还在某处活着，另一部分却已经接受她的死，开始为她哀悼。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Do you know about Akashic Park?
entries.new: ……你们知道阿卡西公园吗？
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: The amusement park?
entries.new: 那座游乐园？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yes.
entries.new: 嗯。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I'd heard about it. It was a few hours away from Yushibana. Apparently, it was surrounded by mountains, and it competed worldwide for the largest park in size. Its selling point was that it contained "all possible configurations of every ride in the world", so despite my low interest, it had piqued my curiosity more than once.
entries.new: 我听说过。它离丰花有几个小时的路程。据说那座公园四面环山，还在面积上与世界各地的公园争第一。它的卖点在于汇集了「世界上所有游乐设施的一切可能形态」，所以尽管我兴趣不大，它也不止一次勾起了我的好奇。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You might've thought Isla was obsessed with the gems downstairs, but that didn't even come close to how much she wanted to go there. ...She brought it up countless times, but it's really expensive, and I've always been a bit afraid of ride malfunctions.
entries.new: 你或许以为 Isla 对楼下的宝石很着迷，可那远比不上她想去那里的程度。……她提过无数次，可那里实在太贵，而且我一直有点害怕游乐设施出故障。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I was going to have more money than usual this month since it's the end of the year. I decided to finally give in and surprise her with a trip after Christmas...
entries.new: 这个月是年底，我手头会比平时宽裕一些。我终于决定松口，等圣诞节过后带她去旅行，给她一个惊喜……
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I told her about it less than a week ago, in case she preferred to hold off with the money and plan a trip during the summer instead. Even though she was really excited at first, she actually told me that she didn't want to go.
entries.new: 不到一周前，我把这件事告诉了她，想着她也许更愿意先把钱留一留，改到夏天再安排旅行。她起初明明很兴奋，最后却说自己不想去了。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I couldn't believe it, but she said that she didn't want to leave her friend alone while she went to have fun. At one point, she also said that she would only come to see the Sekimeiya because I already bought the tickets and she didn't want to make me waste money... even though she started to talk about her friend before we got the tickets.
entries.new: 我真不敢相信，可她说她不想自己出去玩，把朋友一个人丢下。她还一度说过，她会来看 Sekimeiya，只是因为我票都买好了，她不想让我浪费钱……可她在我们买票之前就已经开始提起那个朋友了。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I told you the other ways her behavior changed, right? I forgot one. Sometimes, she hid something from me. A small object, I believe.
entries.new: 我跟你说过她行为上的其他变化，对吧？我漏了一点。有时候，她会背着我藏东西。我觉得是个很小的物件。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Huh?
entries.new: 咦？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That's what it felt like. I noticed... a few times, she'd keep her hand in a fist for a long time. If I asked her to show me what she was hiding, she would run off, so I had to ignore it. It must've been something very small.
entries.new: 给我的感觉就是这样。我注意到……有好几次，她一直攥着拳头，很久都不松开。要是我让她把藏着的东西给我看，她就会跑开，所以我也只能装作没看见。那一定是个很小的东西。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I can't get it all out of my head... Whatever happened to Isla started weeks ago, and I never realized it.
entries.new: 这些事一直在我脑子里打转……Isla 遭遇的一切从几周前就开始了，可我从没察觉。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: All of that was difficult to respond to, so I stayed quiet. However, Shiroya said something far from the shallow answers I'd kept to myself.
entries.new: 这些话我都不知道该怎么接，只好沉默。可 Shiroya 说出口的话，与我压在心底的那些浅薄回答截然不同。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hold on... Erina, I might know who Isla's friend was.
entries.new: 等等……Erina，我或许知道 Isla 的朋友是谁。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Wh-What...? Who?
entries.new: 什、什么……？是谁？
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I frowned. How could she have known that? The only ideas I'd kept in mind were an imaginary friend, a Xyn member, and a staff member from the tower.
entries.new: 我皱起眉。她怎么会知道？我心里想到过的可能，只有虚构的朋友、Xyn 的成员，以及塔里的工作人员。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'm not sure if it makes sense... When we learned about her friend's story, we hadn't experienced the Sekimeiya's powers yet. But just now... I thought of something that could make a lot of sense.
entries.new: 我不确定这讲不讲得通……我们听说她那位朋友的事时，还没亲身经历过 Sekimeiya 的力量。但刚才……我想到了一种很可能成立的解释。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Apparently, she and her friend were living together, but you said that was impossible since you hadn't seen her.
entries.new: 按她的说法，她和那位朋友住在一起，可你说那不可能，因为你从没见过那个人。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Could it be that her friend was herself? After traveling to the past?
entries.new: 会不会那位朋友就是她自己？在穿越到过去之后？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...{w}With that sentence, the huge but simple possibility opened up in my mind. I hadn't considered it at all since I'd been blinded by conspiracies, but I immediately understood why Shiroya reached that idea.
entries.new: ……{w}听到这话，一个巨大却简单的可能性出现在我脑中。此前我完全没想到，因为我一直被种种阴谋猜测蒙住了眼，但我立刻明白了 Shiroya 为什么会想到这一点。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: H-Herself...? What are you talking about!? I would've seen her!
entries.new: 她、她自己……？你在说什么啊！？我肯定会看见她的！
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I... think Shiroya might be right.
entries.new: 我……觉得 Shiroya 也许说得对。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What?
entries.new: 什么？
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: You would've seen her, yes. You said that she started to disobey you sometimes, and you even found her at home once instead of being at school.
entries.new: 你确实见过她。你说过她有时会不听你的话，还有一次，你发现她没去上学，就待在家里。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Right. They were actively keeping her identity from you because they felt like they couldn't reveal that another Isla had appeared, but when one of them went to school or to do what you instructed her to do, the other couldn't follow. During those instances, you could have been seeing the Isla who came from the future.
entries.new: 对。她们一直在刻意向你隐瞒她的身份，因为她们觉得不能让人知道又出现了一个 Isla。可当其中一人去上学，或者照你的吩咐去做事时，另一个就没法跟着。那种时候，你看到的很可能就是从未来来的那个 Isla。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Wh-What...? Did I just imagine that her behavior changed? She distanced herself and spent much less time with me...
entries.new: 什、什么……？她态度变了，难道只是我的错觉？她开始疏远我，陪我的时间少了很多……
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Then this is one of the few things that explains it. Why else would she hide a friend from you? She didn't have bad intentions, and neither did her friend.
entries.new: 这么说，能解释这一切的也就只有这个了。不然她为什么要把一个朋友藏起来不让你知道？她没有恶意，她的朋友也没有。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: "We watched my favorite movie together, and it was her favorite too!" "She went to the aquarium last month, just like us!" I recalled a few things Erina had said.
entries.new: 「我们一起看了我最喜欢的电影，那也是她最喜欢的！」「上个月她去了水族馆，和我们一样！」我想起了 Erina 说过的几句话。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The way Isla described her friend made it sound as if she'd made up a persona that had her own traits and experienced the same events. However, it was herself from the future, wasn't it...? She wasn't lying.
entries.new: Isla 描述那个朋友的方式，听起来就像她凭空编出了一个人物——带着她自己的特质，经历着同样的事。可那其实就是未来的她自己，不是吗……？她没有说谎。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Why else would she refuse to go to the amusement park? Both of them couldn't go at once, so she must not have wanted to leave her behind, knowing firsthand how much she wanted to go too.
entries.new: 不然她为什么不肯去游乐园？两个人没法同时去，而她比谁都清楚对方有多想去，所以才不愿把对方一个人留下。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Then, right now, she's outside...!
entries.new: 那么，她现在就在外面……！
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Isla... specifically said her friend was waiting for her outside.
entries.new: Isla……她特意说过，她的朋友在外面等她。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That has to be it! She will exist in a month!
entries.new: 一定是这样！一个月后她就会存在了！
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...I didn't want to deny it, but it wasn't that simple.{w} In fact, nothing about her fate had changed.{w} I could assemble things the following way: "when Isla disappeared from the cabinet, she went far into the past. The range should've been a lot bigger, but we might be wrong about that part. In a month, that Isla will somehow enter the tower".
entries.new: ……我并不想否认，可事情没那么简单。{w} 事实上，她的命运丝毫没有改变。{w} 我只能这样拼凑：『Isla 从展示柜里消失时，去到了很久以前的过去。重叠范围本该大得多，不过这一点也许是我们弄错了。一个月后，那个 Isla 会以某种方式进入塔里。』
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Tragically, no matter what I thought up, the following step had to be: "Isla travels to the past and ends up dead in the cabinet". There was no way to end it differently.{w} However, even though the voice recorder had appeared in Isla's purse, the origin of it was still unexplained with that theory.
entries.new: 可悲的是，无论我怎么设想，下一步都只能是：『Isla 回到过去，最后死在展示柜里。』没有别的结局。{w} 然而，尽管录音笔出现在 Isla 的包里，这个说法仍然解释不了它的来历。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Erina's head lowered, and her expression went back to how it had been minutes before.
entries.new: Erina 低下头，神情又变回了几分钟前的样子。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I don't know. I appreciate that you want to believe Isla, but there's no way what she said was true. You remember what her friend supposedly told her about today's incident, right?
entries.new: ……我不知道。你想相信 Isla，这份心意我明白，可她说的不可能是真的。你还记得她那个朋友对今天的事是怎么说的吧？
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...I'd tried to leave the major inconsistency for the end, but Erina was right.
entries.new: ……我本想把这个最大的矛盾留到最后，可 Erina 说得对。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "Hm... She told me that something would happen in the tower, but not to worry. She said that if we stayed calm in one place, nobody would be hurt. And she promised I'd be able to see and touch the Sekimeiya, so she was right, wasn't she?"
entries.new: 『嗯……她告诉过我，塔里会出事，但不用担心。她说只要我们待在一个地方别乱动，就不会有人受伤。她还保证我能见到 Sekimeiya，还能摸到它——她没说错，对吧？』
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yeah... According to her, there was going to be no danger. ...And she said that only seven people would get trapped.
entries.new: 嗯……按她的说法，不会有什么危险。……她还说，只有七个人会被困住。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Exactly. There's no way she'd say those things after seeing Naomi's body and after everything else that happened.
entries.new: 正是。在见过 Naomi 的尸体、又经历了后来那些事之后，她绝不可能说出这种话。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Actually, this isn't what I'm the most worried about. Thinking about it conceptually, this is something that cannot work.
entries.new: 其实，我最担心的还不是这个。从道理上想，这件事根本不可能成立。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Conceptually...? You have time traveled, right? Things that would normally be impossible are happening. You've said so yourself.
entries.new: 从道理上……？你不是已经时间穿越了吗？本来不可能的事正在发生。这话是你自己说的。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: That's not what I mean. We've come to the conclusion that the past can't be changed, so what we're suggesting is that Isla met her own self who had traveled from the future. They kept her existence hidden from you, and the friend let the original Isla know about today's events.
entries.new: 我不是那个意思。我们已经得出结论：过去无法改变。所以现在这套说法等于在讲，Isla 遇见了从未来穿越回来的自己。她们一起向你隐瞒了另一个人的存在，而那个『朋友』把今天会发生的事告诉了原本的 Isla。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Ignoring that what she was told was incorrect, the next step is flawed. She can't go back to the past and "relive what she experienced". She would have to replicate exactly what her friend had done and said, as the past would occur exactly as it already had. There's naturally no way she would willingly do that.
entries.new: 暂且不管她听到的内容本身就出了错，接下来的环节也说不通。她不可能回到过去，『重历一遍自己的经历』。她必须把那位朋友做过的事、说过的话一模一样地重演，因为过去会原封不动地重演。她当然不可能心甘情愿这么做。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Isla said they'd been hanging out a lot, so as I said, conceptually, it's incredibly unreasonable to think that she spent the time as her friend knowing how everything would play out.{w} You saw her once when she hadn't gone to school, which should be an impossibility since she would've known you would see her, and she would've avoided that.
entries.new: Isla 说她们经常一起玩，所以正如我所说，从道理上讲，要认为她以朋友的身份度过那段时光、而且明知一切会怎么发展，实在荒唐透顶。{w} 有一次你看见她没去上学，这本来不可能发生——她明知会被你撞见，就该避开才对。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I see... Y-You're right. It's not possible. I hadn't seen it like that...
entries.new: 原来如此……你、你说得对。这不可能。我之前没往这方面想……
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Everything we think about goes back to the same core: we don't really understand how the Sekimeiya works. We can't say it's not possible, but the way we're currently thinking about it can't function.
entries.new: 我们想到的一切最后都绕回同一个核心：我们并不真正了解 Sekimeiya 是怎么运作的。我们不能断定它不可能，可按我们现在的思路，这条路走不通。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I've made up arbitrary rules to explain a few things that have occurred, but as long as they work, we can't discard them. If traveling so long to the past made Isla's memory fuzzy, for example, she might not have remembered the time she spent with herself.
entries.new: 为了解释已经发生的几件事，我临时编了些规则，可只要它们还成立，我们就不能丢掉。比如说，穿越到那么久远的过去让 Isla 的记忆变得模糊，那她也许就不记得和自己相处的那段时光了。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: From her perspective, that would've been happening for the first time, so she would've acted on her own without being aware that she was repeating everything. She would've also misremembered what occurred today and given Isla false information that she trusted completely.
entries.new: 从她的角度来看，那些事都是第一次发生，所以她会按自己的意愿行动，根本不会察觉自己是在重演一切。她还会记错今天发生的事，把错误的消息告诉 Isla，而 Isla 却完全相信了。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: All right... Thank you.
entries.new: 好吧……谢谢你。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Instead of continuing, Erina turned around and lay on the bed while Shiroya and I looked lost. Her idea had a lot of promise, but it appeared ultimately impossible until we had more information.{w} I'd usually been able to create a patchwork design out of the loose ends of a theory, but in that case, I couldn't think of anything else. Needless to say, I didn't think any part of my memory had been erased upon traveling—although, to be fair, perhaps I wouldn't have realized it.
entries.new: Erina 没有再说下去，转身躺倒在床上，我和 Shiroya 则愣在原地。她的设想很有希望，但在掌握更多线索之前，似乎终究行不通。{w} 换作平时，我总能把理论里那些散落的线头拼成一个勉强自洽的轮廓，可这一次，我再也想不出别的了。不用说，我并不认为自己在穿越时丢失了某段记忆——不过话说回来，就算真丢了，我大概也不会察觉。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Were we completely off-base? Was it all just a scheme planned by someone? Before I gave up on the idea, an extra piece of the puzzle that we'd ignored came back to me.
entries.new: 难道我们完全想错了方向？这一切会不会只是某个人布下的局？在我放弃这个念头之前，一块被我们忽略的拼图又浮现在脑海里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Where am I...?
entries.new: ……{w}我这是在哪儿……？
entries.speaker: il2

entries.text: Wh-What do you mean? We're still in Ashiya Tower. Do you not remember?
entries.new: 你、你说什么？我们还在芦屋塔里啊。你不记得了？
entries.speaker: sai2

entries.text: No, I know. What I mean is... What happened to me? Where am I?
entries.new: 不，我知道。我是说……我到底怎么了？我在哪儿？
entries.speaker: il2

entries.text: "Following that, there were a couple of unsteady, heavy footfalls, most likely someone staggering. During the next few seconds, Isla cried, and nobody spoke, inside or outside the recording."
entries.new: 『紧接着，是两下沉重而不稳的脚步声，多半是有人踉跄了几步。接下来几秒里，Isla 哭了，录音里外都没有人说话。』
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Those were words said by Isla, and they were scheduled to happen in about a month. Was the dark meaning behind Isla's future actions... that she'd discovered the fate that awaited her?
entries.new: 那是 Isla 说的话，而它注定会在约一个月后发生。Isla 未来的那些举动，背后暗藏的含义……难道是她已经发现了等待自己的命运？
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Had she found out that she had died and that her fate had been sealed?
entries.new: 她是否已经知道，自己死了，命运早已注定？
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "...What happened to me? Where am I?" I remembered the agonizing way that sounded.
entries.new: 『……我出了什么事？我到底在哪儿？』我记得那声音听起来有多么痛苦。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I breathed deeply, but anxiety began to crawl up my back, exacerbated by my own lack of knowledge.{w} I hated exploring all sorts of options without knowing if I'd ever find the truth. Isla's bleak ending had already been revealed to us, making the process of putting together its outline all the more draining.
entries.new: 我深深吸了口气，焦虑却沿着脊背爬上来。因为对真相一无所知，这份焦虑越发强烈。{w} 我讨厌在不知道能否找到真相的情况下，把所有可能性都试一遍。Isla 凄惨的结局已经摆在我们眼前，要把它的轮廓拼出来，就更让人心力交瘁。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya was resting her head on top of a large pillow. We'd been there for a little while, and the people below us hadn't interrupted us yet. It seemed like relaxing would be an actual option.
entries.new: Shiroya 把头枕在一个大枕头上。我们在这儿已经待了一阵，下面的人始终没来打扰。看来放松一下确实可行。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I climbed over Shiroya and lay down, making contact with the cold wall. She was occupying both pillows, so I knew I'd have a hard time staying in a comfortable position. Trying to not mind it, I closed my eyes.
entries.new: 我越过 Shiroya 躺下，背贴上冰冷的墙壁。两个枕头都被她占了，我知道自己很难保持舒服的姿势。我尽量不去在意，闭上了眼睛。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As usual, attempting to keep my mind blank was futile, but the contents of what tormented me were very different. Time travel, a smoke attack, body doubles, murders, suspicion... What kind of mess were we in?
entries.new: 和往常一样，想让脑子一片空白只是徒劳，但折磨我的东西已经全然不同。时间穿越、烟雾袭击、冒牌货、杀人、猜疑……我们到底卷进了怎样的乱局？
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was aware that there was no guarantee I'd ever feel my own bed again, depending on what the truth around us really was. Ironically, the stiff bed began to help me get rid of those thoughts, and my senses slowly faded away.
entries.new: 我心里清楚，真相如何尚未可知，我未必还能再躺回自己的床上。讽刺的是，这张硬邦邦的床反倒帮我把那些念头赶了出去，我的意识也慢慢模糊了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Nobody moved for many minutes.
entries.new: 有好几分钟，谁也没有动。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki! Who do you think you are!?
entries.new: Atsuki！你以为你算什么东西！？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I was about to lose touch with reality when a sound brought me back to my surroundings. The three of us were startled simultaneously and looked at the hatch that had just opened.
entries.new: 我正要彻底脱离现实，一个声响把我拉回了当下。我们三人同时一惊，望向那扇刚被打开的活板门。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Katei appeared through the hatch with a dour expression. Since he'd addressed me, I tried to stand up, but I could only support my torso with an arm.
entries.new: Katei 沉着脸从活板门里钻了出来。他既然叫了我，我便想站起来，却只能用一条手臂撑起上半身。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki!{w} Did you really think you could get out of this with simple threats? Those will not work on me, so once we make it out, you can say goodbye to your normal life.
entries.new: Atsuki！{w} 你真以为几句威胁就能把这事了结？威胁对我没用。等我们出去，你就跟正常生活告别吧。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I couldn't comprehend a word of what he was saying. He'd sat on the bed and put his face up close to mine. His eyes told me that he was being serious, but I couldn't help but respond with an exaggerated frown.
entries.new: 他的话我一个字也没听懂。他坐到床上，把脸凑到我面前。他的眼神说明他是认真的，我却忍不住夸张地皱起眉来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Are you listening to me!?
entries.new: 你到底有没有在听我说话！？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: What the hell are you on about...?
entries.new: 你他妈到底在胡说些什么……？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Stop with your façade. It all makes sense, and I know Shiroya must be working with you.
entries.new: 别再装了。一切都说得通，Shiroya 一定和你是一伙的。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...Huh?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: For a second, I thought he might've figured out we'd hidden the Sekimeiya and decided to blow it out of proportion.
entries.new: 有那么一瞬，我甚至以为他察觉了我们藏起 Sekimeiya 的事，要拿它大做文章。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Don't worry, Erina, I know he's been threatening you from the start. We're all locked up here, so now he can't pull one of his tricks.
entries.new: 别怕，Erina，我知道他从一开始就在威胁你。现在我们都被关在这里，他耍不出什么花招了。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: When I left the lobby earlier, you were who followed me, not Sai. However, you made the others cover for you. That wasn't a smart move, idiot.
entries.new: 刚才我离开大厅的时候，跟上来的人是你，不是 Sai。可你让其他人替你圆谎。这可不是什么聪明的做法，蠢货。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I didn't realize that everything was a fabrication. You killed the first Naomi and had everyone else lie about it. That's why you made up the elevator noise: to frame me or someone else.
entries.new: 我竟没看出来，这一切都是编出来的。第一个 Naomi 是你杀的，还让别人替你撒谎。电梯的响动也是你编的——为了嫁祸给我，或者别人。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Are you fucking out of your mind...? Why would I want to frame you if everyone else was covering for me?
entries.new: 你他妈脑子坏掉了吗……？既然所有人都替我遮掩，我干嘛还要嫁祸你？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Do not try to change the facts. When the second Naomi died, conveniently, I ended up on floor 6 while you and everyone you'd threatened were under me. That's why you could all act as if you had an alibi for her death.
entries.new: 别想歪曲事实。第二个 Naomi 死的时候，我偏偏在六楼，而你和你威胁过的所有人都待在我楼下。所以你们才能个个装出有不在场证明的样子。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: You knew about the attic key and had been here already. You could've had every key from the beginning.
entries.new: 你早就知道阁楼钥匙的事，也早就来过这里。说不定从一开始，所有钥匙就都在你手上。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...Right! How did I ignore such suspicious behavior? You and Shiroya left the attic and didn't come back for fifty minutes! And then the Sekimeiya mysteriously disappeared!
entries.new: ……对了！这么可疑的举动，我怎么就没在意？你和 Shiroya 离开阁楼，整整五十分钟没回来！紧接着 Sekimeiya 就不翼而飞了！
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: But you instructed Sai to immediately act suspiciously as soon as we went down to confuse me.
entries.new: 可你还指使 Sai，我们一下去，他就立刻做出可疑的举动，好扰乱我的判断。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Despite everything that had occurred, my bewilderment thus far couldn't compare to what I felt from the words I was hearing.
entries.new: 此前无论出了多少事，都比不上此刻这些话带给我的错愕。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And then... Isla died. You were behind that, right? You tried to make us believe that you were sleeping as it happened! How did I swallow that lie...?{w} Shiroya found the hidden passage in the storeroom? How was I so stupid...? You were about to use it...!
entries.new: 然后……Isla 死了。那也是你干的吧？你还想让我们相信，事发时你正在睡觉！我怎么就信了这种鬼话……？{w}Shiroya 在储藏室里找到了暗门？我怎么这么蠢……？你本来就要用那扇门……！
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Before showing up in the lobby, you came from hallway B! You were too stupid to appear from hallway A after removing the Sekimeiya from the cleaning room!
entries.new: 出现在大厅之前，你是从 B走廊过来的！你把 Sekimeiya 从清洁间拿走之后，蠢到连从 A走廊现身都想不到！
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: No wonder you sided with Erina and wanted everyone to stay locked in here. After all, you'd hidden the Sekimeiya and could safely sleep like you were doing just now. Did you actually think any of this would work?
entries.new: 难怪你要站在 Erina 那边，还巴不得所有人都锁在这里。毕竟 Sekimeiya 已经藏好了，你大可以像刚才那样安心睡觉。你真以为这一套能行得通？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...{w}Are you just fucking around, or are you really this dumb?
entries.new: ……{w}你是在耍我，还是真就蠢到这个地步？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I suppose you're not going to give up. You two are the culprits behind this incident.{w} Why were you in the first group of the guided visit when you've shown no interest in the gems? Now that I've learned about it, you must confess. I know you didn't attempt to threaten me individually since I work here and there's no way I'd give in to you.
entries.new: 看来你是不会认了。这起事件就是你们俩干的。{w}你对宝石从来没什么兴趣，为什么偏偏排在参观的第一批？既然我已经查清了，你就老实交代吧。我知道你没单独来威胁我——我在这里工作，绝不可能向你低头。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I'm having a hard time following. Do you actually believe what you're saying?
entries.new: 我实在跟不上你的思路。这些话，你自己信吗？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Katei's face shifted. I couldn't understand what was happening.
entries.new: Katei 的脸色变了。我看不懂眼前究竟在发生什么。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I never thought you were brilliant, but come on. There are some huge inconsistencies with everything that you said. What's gotten into you?
entries.new: 我从来没觉得你有多聪明，可这也太离谱了。你刚才说的那些，前后矛盾一大堆。你到底怎么了？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Instead of replying, he looked at Erina. Upon seeing that she didn't immediately corroborate his story, he breathed faintly to keep calm.
entries.new: 他没有回答，而是看向 Erina。见她并没有立刻附和，他轻轻吸了口气，努力让自己镇定下来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'm serious, tell me. Did you just rub some brain cells together for this and come here thinking that you'd cracked the mystery? I discarded a few theories earlier because they relied on you being completely brainless, but now I should reconsider them.
entries.new: 我是认真的，回答我。你就把脑子里那点东西凑了凑，跑到这儿来以为案子破了？我之前舍弃过几种推论，因为它们都要求你完全没脑子；现在看来，我该把它们重新捡起来了。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Once again, he decided to remain quiet.
entries.new: 他依旧选择沉默。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Subsequently, he retraced his steps and looked through the hatch. My perception of him had been changing as time advanced, but it had suddenly taken a significant turn. I still hadn't processed a few of the things he said.
entries.new: 随后，他退回原路，透过活板门往下看。随着时间推移，我对他的看法一直在变，此刻却突然出现了一个大转折。他刚才说的几句话，我还没能理清。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the hell...? That son of a bitch...!
entries.new: 搞什么……？那个混蛋……！
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...It was time to stand up. I moved first since Katei had forcefully changed my mood. I walked up to him, and ignoring his awkwardly placed body, I kneeled down, trying to understand what he was looking at.
entries.new: ……该起身了。Katei 硬是搅乱了我的情绪，于是我第一个动了。我走到他身旁，不去理会他那别扭的姿势，蹲下身，想看清他究竟在看什么。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...What? There's no way...
entries.new: ……什么？不可能……
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Sai and Akaro weren't there.{w} From the hatch, I could see the entire lower bedroom devoid of any human presence.
entries.new: Sai 和 Akaro 不在那里。{w}透过活板门望下去，下面整间卧室里不见半个人影。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Where are they? They couldn't have left...
entries.new: 他们人呢？不可能走得掉啊……
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I went down the ladder.{w} They weren't in the wardrobe or under the bed.{w} Countless questions hammered from inside my head, but I immediately went to check the door.
entries.new: 我顺着梯子下去。{w}衣橱里没有，床底下也没有。{w}无数疑问在脑中敲打，可我还是先去查看房门。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The chain isn't set.
entries.new: 门链没有扣上。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I said that out loud to inform the others who still remained upstairs. I attempted to get the door to open, but it still was locked in place.
entries.new: 我出声说出来，好让还留在楼上的人听见。我试着把门弄开，门却依旧锁得死死的。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't get it... How did they do it?
entries.new: 我搞不懂……他们到底是怎么做到的？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: It had to be around {time=15:30.} I doubted we'd been in the bedroom for more than 25 minutes. No matter what had happened, it was clear that calmness wasn't what awaited us.
entries.new: 那时应该差不多是{time=15:30.}了。我们在卧室里待的时间，想必不超过二十五分钟。无论发生了什么，有一点很清楚：等着我们的绝不是平静。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...At first, Sai began telling me that you'd threatened him and went into detail explaining how you'd managed to accomplish everything.
entries.new: ……一开始，是 Sai 跟我说你威胁过他，还详细讲了你到底是怎么做成这一切的。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I didn't believe him at all, but he started to make some compelling arguments. It was Sai, though, so I didn't take him seriously.
entries.new: 我根本不信他，可他说的渐渐有了几分说服力。不过那是 Sai，所以我也没有当真。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: However, even though Akaro had been looking at him with skepticism from the start, after a while, he confirmed Sai's story and gave us his version. He said you'd threatened him too, that Erina had fallen victim as well.
entries.new: 然而，Akaro 虽然从一开始就满脸怀疑地看着他，过了一会儿却证实了 Sai 的说法，还讲了他自己那一版。他说你也威胁过他，Erina 同样遭了你的毒手。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I'm sorry... But at that time, everything was pieced together, and I truly believed them.
entries.new: 对不起……可当时所有事情都能拼得严丝合缝，我真的信了他们。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: This is too much... So they escaped after you went through the hatch?
entries.new: 这也太离谱了……所以他们是在你从活板门下去之后逃走的？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I don't know how, but yes.
entries.new: 我不知道他们是怎么做到的，但没错。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I had no idea what was happening. Leaving should've been impossible, let alone in such a short time.
entries.new: 我完全不明白发生了什么。离开本来就不可能，更别说在这么短的时间内了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Both of them probably wanted you to go up so they could leave without being seen.
entries.new: 他们俩大概就是想让你上楼去，好趁机悄悄离开吧。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: And your stupidity was the perfect base for that to work. Like flour in a cake.
entries.new: 而你的愚蠢正好成了最合适的底子。就像蛋糕里的面粉一样。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Maybe the lock could be forced with something like a card, but it'd take a long time. There's no way they could've escaped in less than a minute.
entries.new: 也许能用卡片之类的东西把锁撬开，但那得花很长时间。不到一分钟就逃出去，根本不可能。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: The chain isn't set, so they definitely left through the door.
entries.new: 门链没挂上，所以他们一定是从门离开的。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Would we not have heard it if they'd forced it open? Maybe it was removed as a trick, to make us think they used the door.
entries.new: 要是他们硬撬开的，我们怎么会没听见？也许门链是故意摘下来的，好让我们以为他们走的是门。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I hated that feeling. We'd been shoved into another mystery without solving anything, and Sai's plan had worked. Additionally, it appeared that Akaro had no problem working with him to create a story where I was the main culprit.
entries.new: 我讨厌那种感觉。什么都没查清，我们又被推进了另一桩谜团里，而 Sai 的计划已经得逞。更糟的是，Akaro 似乎毫不介意与他联手，编出一个以我为主谋的故事。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We would've left eventually, but the notion that nobody would be able to go back to the past if we stayed there was already obsolete. It had become possible for Sai and Akaro to appear in the past, if that was part of their intent.
entries.new: 我们迟早会离开，可「只要守在这里，就没人能回到过去」这个念头早已作废。只要 Sai 和 Akaro 有意，他们出现在过去已成为可能。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even though Erina hadn't reacted strongly, there was an important implication: Sai and Akaro worked together, so they could've orchestrated the recording if they'd either worked with Isla or threatened her.
entries.new: 尽管 Erina 没有太大反应，这里却藏着一个要紧的含义：Sai 和 Akaro 是一伙的，那么只要他们与 Isla 合作，或者胁迫她，那段录音就完全可能由他们策划。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Does it even matter? This is the logic Sai used when Shiroya and I left the attic: if something happens, it'll be their fault. Can we not apply it now?
entries.new: 这有意义吗？Shiroya 和我离开阁楼时，Sai 用的就是这套逻辑：一旦出了事，错都在对方。现在就不能照用吗？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Admittedly, I was tired, and my body demanded me to sleep again.
entries.new: 说实话，我确实累了，身体又在催我睡过去。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You're crazy. They played us like this!
entries.new: 你疯了。他们就这么把我们耍了！
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: They played you. Do you want to break the door open? We agreed to stay here until the police come, and now we've learned who the culprits were. They must've had a goal in mind, and it's very likely they accomplished it already. You can go search for them if you think that'll do anything.
entries.new: 你被耍了。你想把门砸开吗？我们说好了留在这里等警察来，如今已经知道犯人是谁了。他们肯定早有目的，而且很可能已经达成了。你要是觉得追上去有用，尽管去追。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I was exhausted. I let my body fall onto the bed at my side and disconnected from the conversation.
entries.new: 我筋疲力尽，索性任身体倒向旁边的床，退出了这场对话。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Katei began knocking on the door and yelling. I didn't know what to think, as I couldn't bring myself to completely trust his story. If everything actually happened like he said, Sai and Akaro would have clearly communicated that they had ulterior motives—which they'd managed to keep mostly hidden until that point—even though they escaped.
entries.new: Katei 开始砸门叫喊。我却不知道该作何感想，因为我没法完全相信他的说法。若事情真如他所说，Sai 和 Akaro 就是明明白白地表明了自己另有图谋——而此前他们几乎一直藏得很好——哪怕他们已经逃了出去。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Leaving anyway meant that they'd needed to get out so badly, they didn't care.
entries.new: 即便如此也要离开，说明他们急于脱身，已顾不得掩饰。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: *sigh* Should we try to leave? They were probably hoping we'd still stay here after they escaped, which is why they blatantly did so.
entries.new: 唉……我们要不要也试着离开？他们多半就盼着他们逃了之后我们还守在这儿，所以才敢做得这么明目张胆。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I don't want to. I'm not sure what Akaro's deal is, but if Sai was the only one to escape, I would've thought that his motive was to make us chase after him to undo the bedroom lock.{w} If they're still in the tower, there's not much they can do. They can go to the past or hide the Sekimeiya, but they'd still be trapped in here. Even if they went far back enough to exit the tower, there's no reason for us to chase them.
entries.new: 我不想走。Akaro 到底想干什么我不清楚，但如果只有 Sai 一个人逃了，我会以为他的动机是引我们去追，好让我们从里面解开卧室的锁。{w} 他们若还留在塔里，能做的不多。回到过去也好，把 Sekimeiya 藏起来也好，终究还是困在这里。就算他们回到足够早的时候离开这座塔，我们也没有追上去的理由。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: But what if one of them had the handle for the hidden exit? They could leave with the Sekimeiya!
entries.new: 可万一他们中有人拿到了暗门的把手呢？那样就能带着 Sekimeiya 离开！
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Then they're already gone. However, if they could open it, they would've done that earlier.
entries.new: 那他们早就走了。不过，要是他们能打开，之前就该动手了。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Th-They could've figured out a way to open the door after they found it!
entries.new: 他、他们可能在找到门之后想出了打开的办法！
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Katei sighed in exasperation and set the chain again. The key was outside, so the chain would prevent Akaro and Sai from returning.
entries.new: Katei 无奈地叹了口气，重新挂上门链。钥匙在外面，门链能防止 Akaro 和 Sai 回来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "Why is the culprit hiding the Sekimeiya if we'll be able to find it?" That recurring question felt similar to our present situation.{w} What could they have wanted to achieve by making it out? Unless they wanted to experiment with the Sekimeiya or hide it, the only reason I could produce was that they'd needed to go back in time to finish something off.
entries.new: 「既然我们迟早能找到，犯人为什么要藏起 Sekimeiya？」这个反复出现的问题，与眼前的处境颇为相似。{w} 他们逃出去究竟想达成什么？除非是为了试验 Sekimeiya 或者把它藏起来，我能想到的唯一理由，就是他们需要回到过去，了结某件事。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The other question was a lot more intriguing to me: how had they escaped? There was time to break the door open, and there was no way we'd missed a hidden person who'd opened it from the outside.
entries.new: 另一个问题更让我在意：他们是怎么逃出去的？时间足够他们破门，而我们也不可能漏掉某个躲在暗处、从外面开门的人。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: To open the door, the key would have been needed. There was no other way to accomplish it. However, we knew it couldn't have been inside the bedroom.{w} As I'd thought earlier, the only way to undo the lock was by using the key from the outside and then unsetting the chain from the inside.
entries.new: 要开门就必须有钥匙，此外别无他法。可我们知道，钥匙不可能在卧室里。{w} 正如我之前所想，解开这道锁的唯一办法，是用钥匙从外面开锁，再从里面摘掉门链。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: With my eyes closed and without giving it much thought, I could reach a very easy explanation, similar to what Sai proposed before we'd locked ourselves in the bedroom:{w} "they left through the door and went to the past with the Sekimeiya. Then, they opened the bedroom's door with the key that we hid under the bathroom carpet. To escape, they simply pulled the door open from the inside, which would've been slightly open".
entries.new: 我闭着眼，几乎不必多想，就得出一个极其简单的解释，与 Sai 在我们把自己锁进卧室前提出的说法如出一辙：{w}「他们从门离开，带着 Sekimeiya 回到过去。然后用在浴室地毯下藏着的钥匙打开了卧室的门。要出去，只需从里面把门拉开——那时的门应该已经开了一条缝。」
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was reminiscent of the first bootstrap paradox concept I'd thought of a few hours earlier. The clean, brief way they'd managed to escape could have been an indication that it was accepted in our universe.
entries.new: 这让我想起几小时前自己刚想到的第一个自举悖论。他们逃脱的方式如此干净利落，或许正说明这个解在我们的宇宙里被接受了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was an inherent property of those types of paradoxes: they had no origin. They were closed loops that occurred with no root or motive whatsoever.
entries.new: 这类悖论有一个固有的性质：它们没有起源。它们是无根无由、凭空成立的闭环。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Their escape method, though, had a real origin.{w} Sai's and Akaro's thoughts.
entries.new: 然而他们的逃脱方式，却有着真实的起源。{w} Sai 和 Akaro 的念头。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If one of them had thought of the way to escape, the final thing they needed to perform it was the universe's approval. They would've set an intangible origin of the loop, making it fundamentally different from a causal loop.
entries.new: 只要他们之中有一人想到了逃脱的办法，要付诸实施，最后差的就只是宇宙的认可。他们为这个循环设下了一个无形的起点，使它从根本上区别于因果循环。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The key to the Sekimeiya cabinet isn't there...
entries.new: Sekimeiya 展示柜的钥匙不见了……
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Wh-What?
entries.new: 什、什么？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I'd realized that to accomplish that sort of plan, they had to escape with the cabinet key to be able to go to the past. Upon turning my head, I'd seen that it wasn't on top of the drawers where I'd left it anymore.
entries.new: 我这才意识到，要实现那样的计划，他们必须带着展示柜的钥匙逃走，才能回到过去。我转过头，发现它已经不在我原先放的那个抽屉顶上了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the hell did they want to do?
entries.new: 他们到底想干什么？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: In short, Sai and Akaro could've attempted one type of escape route: they knew where the Sekimeiya was, so they were in reach of one of the points necessary to accomplish the creation of the loop. After thinking of the way things would play out, they baited Katei out of the room. Subsequently, they left through an unlocked door.
entries.new: 简而言之，Sai 和 Akaro 可能尝试的逃脱路线是这样的：他们知道 Sekimeiya 的位置，所以具备了完成循环所必需的其中一个条件。想清楚事情会如何发展后，他们把 Katei 引出房间，随后从一扇没上锁的门离开了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The last thing they had to do was travel back in time and unlock the door. If a result of their travel hadn't incited the idea to travel in the first place, their loop had a clear starting point. It also implied they were both culprits in the incident—we knew that any culprit possessed higher knowledge of the Sekimeiya's mechanics and limits.
entries.new: 他们最后要做的，就是回到过去，打开那道锁。只要他们穿越的结果并没有反过来催生穿越的念头，这个循环就有明确的起点。这也意味着他们二人都是这起事件的犯人——我们早已知道，任何犯人都对 Sekimeiya 的机制与极限掌握着更高一层的知识。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was a slight problem: unlocking the door from the outside would make a bit of noise. If it happened before they thought of the concept, the loop would have no origin, as the noise itself would tell them what to do.{w} I couldn't think of a way to circumvent it easily. If the key could fit under the door, their future selves could've slid it inside. However, the gap wasn't big enough, or else we would've simply locked ourselves in and slid it out of the bedroom.
entries.new: 但有个小问题：从外面开锁会发出一点声响。如果这声响在他们想到这个主意之前就已经出现，循环就没有起点，因为那声响本身就会告诉他们该怎么做。{w} 我一时想不出轻易绕开这点的方法。要是钥匙能从门缝底下塞进去，未来的他们就可以把钥匙送进来。可惜门缝不够宽——否则我们只要把自己锁进卧室，从门缝把钥匙推出去就行了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Beyond that concept, I felt that Katei's story was iffy. As likely as it was that Sai and Akaro could've conspired together, nothing told us Katei hadn't been in on it too.{w} They could've spent half an hour unlocking the door and then made it seem as if they'd magically escaped. Katei immediately suggested unlocking the bedroom to us, making for a simple motive if all three of them were secretly against Erina's request.
entries.new: 除了这一点，我还觉得 Katei 的说法有些可疑。Sai 和 Akaro 合谋的可能性固然不小，可也没有任何证据能说明 Katei 没有参与其中。{w} 他们大可花上半个小时慢慢开锁，再装作是凭空逃了出去。而 Katei 立刻提议替我们打开卧室门——若这三人暗地里都反对 Erina 的要求，动机就再简单不过了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai! Akaro! What the hell are you trying to do!?
entries.new: Sai！Akaro！你们到底想干什么！？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Katei continued knocking on the door, acting accordingly for someone who'd been played as badly as him.
entries.new: Katei 继续砸门，那副样子倒确实像是被人耍得这么惨的人该有的反应。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hey! Sai! Akaro!
entries.new: 喂！Sai！Akaro！
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Yes, Katei. I'm sure they'll come back if you ask nicely.
entries.new: 是啊，Katei。你好好说，他们一定会回来的。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Are you not worried at all about what they could be trying to do?
entries.new: 你就一点也不担心他们想做什么吗？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Not very much. If they're the culprits, we're safer now that they left. All they can do is go back in time, which sounds fairly harmless at this point—and unavoidable.
entries.new: 不怎么担心。若他们真是犯人，他们走了我们反而更安全。他们能做的无非是回到过去，事到如今那听起来也没什么害处，而且无法避免。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You're right there. It's now clear that they were the culprits, so if they come back, we won't let them in.
entries.new: 这倒是。现在已经清楚他们就是犯人，要是他们回来，我们绝不放他们进来。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Sure, so you can stop with the knocking. They have the Sekimeiya, though, so I'm betting they could teleport back inside if they really wanted to.
entries.new: 嗯，所以你别再砸门了。不过 Sekimeiya 在他们手上，我猜他们真想回来的话，大可以直接传送进来。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...That's not a great thought to keep in mind.
entries.new: ……这可不是什么让人安心的念头。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Katei stepped aside. It appeared we'd decided to stay.
entries.new: Katei 退到一旁。看来我们都已经决定留下来了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even though Shiroya and Erina hadn't given their input, I figured they wanted that too and were likely dumbfounded by the fact that our self-imposed imprisonment hadn't even lasted for thirty minutes.
entries.new: Shiroya 和 Erina 虽然没有表态，但我想她们也是这个意思，而且多半被我们这场自作自受的囚禁没撑过三十分钟的事实弄得哑口无言。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Cable-Stayed
entries.new: 斜拉桥

entries.text: Synchronized, we all looked at the door. As we thought, Katei was no longer in front of it.
entries.new: 我们像是约好了一样，一齐望向门口。果不其然，Katei 已经不在门边了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the...? Did they come back?
entries.new: 搞什么……？他们回来了？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...Hey! Who is it!?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: It's me. What are you doing here?
entries.new: 是我。你在这儿做什么？
entries.speaker: q

entries.text: Without a doubt, Akaro was behind the door.
entries.new: 门外的人，毫无疑问就是 Akaro。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Don't play dumb. We won't let you in!
entries.new: 别装傻。我们不会让你进来的！
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Wait, wh-who...?{w} What the fuck happened to this handle...?
entries.new: 等等，谁、谁啊……？{w}这门把手怎么他妈搞成这样……？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Ignoring Katei's assertion, Akaro began to forcefully attempt to open the door. We understood he had the key, as we heard it being turned over and over.
entries.new: Akaro 没理会 Katei 的话，开始用力扳门。我们听见钥匙反复转动的声音，便知道钥匙在他手上。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the hell are you doing!? You're not getting back in!
entries.new: 你到底在干什么！？你别想再进来！
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: But he was mistaken. After a few seconds of Akaro's struggle, the chain burst out and the door opened. Akaro's figure was behind it, and we saw the key placed in the outer keyhole.
entries.new: 然而他失算了。Akaro 折腾了几秒，链条便脱开，门随之打开。Akaro 就站在门外，钥匙插在外侧的锁孔里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...That's not a very good chain.
entries.new: ……这链条可真不结实。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What do you think you're doing!? Where's Sai!?
entries.new: 你究竟想干什么！？Sai 在哪！？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Everyone was speechless. The chain hadn't broken, but it had been forced open. It was old, so it wasn't too surprising. Apparently, my plan had an obvious hole from the start.
entries.new: 众人一时无言。链条并没有断，只是被硬生生拽脱了。那链条本就老旧，倒也不足为奇。看来我的计划从一开始就有一个明显的破绽。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Strangely, Akaro wore a very confused expression. He looked at us one by one.
entries.new: 奇怪的是，Akaro 一脸困惑，挨个打量着我们。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the fuck...? Who are you?
entries.new: 搞什么鬼……？你谁啊？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Seconds of silence followed. Nobody knew how to answer, as we weren't sure who that had been directed at.
entries.new: 随后是几秒的沉默。谁也不知该如何回答，因为没人确定他这句话是对谁说的。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Who, me...?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Yes!
entries.new: 对！
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: ...What's your game? Are you going to pretend you don't recognize me?
entries.new: ……你打的什么主意？打算装作不认识我？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Akaro responded by looking at the rest of us, expecting to be backed up. However, his confusion only grew when he realized we found his words to be the strange ones.
entries.new: Akaro 转头看向我们其余人，指望有人附和。可当他发现我们反倒觉得他这话才奇怪时，脸上的困惑更深了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Excuse me? Why are you all looking at me like that? Where the fuck did this man appear from?
entries.new: ……什么？你们干嘛都这么看着我？这人他妈是从哪儿冒出来的？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: You will not trick me twice.
entries.new: 你别想再骗我第二次。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Where's Sai?
entries.new: Sai 在哪？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Sai? I have no idea. He left the room earlier and didn't come back. What are you all even doing here?
entries.new: Sai？我完全不知道。他早些时候出了房间，就没再回来。你们到底在这儿干什么？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: As I saw how lost he looked, I began to take him seriously. He sounded genuine, but not a thing he was saying made sense.
entries.new: 看他那副茫然的样子，我开始认真对待他的话。他语气诚恳，不像作假，可他说的话没有一句说得通。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What do you mean? Do you really not remember Katei?
entries.new: 你什么意思？你真的不记得 Katei 了？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Katei? Is that his name?{w} Where should I remember him from?
entries.new: Katei？他叫这个名字？{w}我该在哪儿见过他？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: He's been with us the whole time.
entries.new: 他一直和我们在一起。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: He took a few seconds to answer, during which he eyed me like I'd gone insane.
entries.new: 他停了几秒才回答，那期间他看我的眼神，就像我已经疯了一样。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Why... are you all lying? What's happening?
entries.new: 为什么……你们为什么要撒谎？到底出什么事了？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: ...H-Huh? What do you mean?
entries.new: ……啊、啊？你什么意思？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Out of nowhere, he looked at Shiroya. Like the rest of us, she was taken aback, as the two of them had barely exchanged words since we'd gotten trapped.
entries.new: 他冷不防看向 Shiroya。她和我们一样愣住了——自从被困在这里，他们两个几乎没说过几句话。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I mean... what I said. Why are you all here?
entries.new: 我是说……我刚才问的。你们为什么都在这儿？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: We tried to stay put in one place together. Do you not remember that?
entries.new: 我们不是一直守在同一处地方吗。你不记得了？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: No, I do. That doesn't answer my question, though.
entries.new: 不，我记得。可这没回答我的问题。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: How does it not answer your question? You and Sai escaped, and now you came back.
entries.new: 怎么没回答？你和 Sai 逃了出去，现在又回来了。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What!? That's not true! I didn't escape.
entries.new: 什么！？胡说！我根本没逃出去。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I couldn't quite grasp it, but something felt off about Akaro's behavior. Past his bizarre claims, he seemed more aggressive, and his voice sounded more composed. Not only that, but he'd been fixing his gaze on Shiroya.
entries.new: 我说不清，但 Akaro 的样子有哪里不对劲。除了那些古怪的说辞，他的态度更咄咄逼人，声音却更沉稳。不仅如此，他的目光一直落在 Shiroya 身上。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Akaro, why did you come back? Do you intend to stay here again?
entries.new: Akaro，你为什么回来？是打算再待在这里吗？
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: The door was locked, so were you all waiting here? I'm very confused.
entries.new: 门是锁着的，所以你们就都在这儿等着？我实在搞不懂。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: What you are is a lying piece of shit. Do you think you can simply come back acting as if nothing happened?
entries.new: 你就是个满嘴谎话的混蛋。你以为回来装成没事人，就能糊弄过去？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I don't know who you are, but don't yell at me. I'm not opposed to staying here, but you'll all need to explain yourselves.
entries.new: 我不知道你是谁，但别冲我吼。留在这里我不反对，不过你们得把话说清楚。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Erina moved forward and took the key out of the door. She brought Akaro inside, closed the door, and locked it. Then, she set the chain again.
entries.new: Erina 走上前，把钥匙从门上拔下。她带 Akaro 进了屋，关上门锁好，又把链条重新挂上。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even if the chain can be ignored from the outside, we'll easily hear it if someone tries to force it open again.{w} I was probably wrong before. We should've kept the key inside to avoid all this. I'll keep it with me. This way, if Sai comes, he won't be able to enter or let anyone leave easily.
entries.new: 就算外面的人能无视链条，只要有人再想硬撬，我们很容易就能听见。{w}之前是我错了。钥匙本该留在里面，也不会闹出这些事。钥匙我来保管。这样，就算 Sai 来了，他也进不来，也没法轻易把谁放出去。
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: What about Isla? Aren't you going to go get her?
entries.new: Isla 呢？你们不去接她吗？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: None of us could believe what we were hearing. Had he forgotten what had happened, or was he talking about her dead body?
entries.new: 我们谁都不敢相信自己的耳朵。他是忘了发生过什么，还是在说她的尸体？
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't know what you're trying, but it's futile. You're revealing your true colors by trying to play dumb.
entries.new: 我不知道你在耍什么花招，但都是白费。你装傻充愣，反倒露了馅。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...I don't understand anything. I saw that the elevator was fixed, but how did you all get here?
entries.new: ……我完全不明白。电梯是修好了，可你们是怎么上来的？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Again, such an ambiguous question couldn't be answered by any of us since we didn't comprehend its meaning.
entries.new: 又是这种含混的问题，谁也答不上来，因为我们根本听不懂他在问什么。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...The elevator? That was fixed a long time ago. And where do you mean...?
entries.new: ……电梯？那早就修好了。你说的是哪儿……？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Here, the Ashiya floor.
entries.new: 这里，芦屋这一层。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Uh... With the key Naomi had. Do you actually not remember that?
entries.new: 呃……用 Naomi 手里那把钥匙啊。你是真的不记得了？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Are you fucking with me...?
entries.new: 你他妈在耍我……？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: She's not. What's wrong with that?
entries.new: 她没有。这有什么奇怪的？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Well... I don't get it. Where was the key, exactly?
entries.new: 这……我不明白。那把钥匙到底在哪儿？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: In one of her pockets.
entries.new: 在她身上的一个口袋里。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: But... there's no way.
entries.new: 可是……这不可能。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Do you not remember that Naomi died?
entries.new: 你不记得 Naomi 已经死了吗？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What? No... I mean, when was her body found?
entries.new: 什么？不……我是说，她的尸体是什么时候被发现的？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Many hours ago.
entries.new: 好几个小时前。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Akaro closed his eyes and took a deep breath. He was as confused as us.
entries.new: Akaro 闭上眼，深吸了一口气。他和我们一样困惑。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Are you all lying to me?
entries.new: 你们都在骗我吗？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: That's funny of you to say. Wasn't it you who told me that Atsuki had been threatening everyone?
entries.new: 你这话说得倒好笑。不是你对我说，Atsuki 一直在威胁所有人吗？
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Excuse me...? I never said that.
entries.new: 什么……？我从没说过那种话。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: My head was going numb. I had no way to interpret what I was hearing.
entries.new: 我的脑子开始发麻。我完全无法理解自己听到的话。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is ridiculous. Did you all go insane?
entries.new: 太荒唐了。你们都疯了吗？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: If you're being sincere, it's clear that your memories contradict ours. What time do you think it is?
entries.new: 如果你说的是真心话，那你的记忆显然和我们的对不上。你觉得现在几点？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I have no idea, but I don't think it's {time=16} yet.
entries.new: 我不知道，但我想还没到 {time=16}。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Right, that matches the current time. What do you remember, beginning at the start of our imprisonment?
entries.new: 对，和现在的时间吻合。从我们被关起来的那一刻起，你都记得什么？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Atsuki, please don't tell me you're playing along. He's trying to manipulate us, and this time it's a lot more obvious.
entries.new: Atsuki，别告诉我你还要顺着他的话说下去。他在操纵我们，这次明显得多。
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Shut up. As I said, we stayed put, but eventually, you all left. Then, I went to find you and I heard knocks coming from here.
entries.new: 闭嘴。我说过了，我们待在原地，可后来你们全都走了。我去找你们，就听见这边传来敲击声。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: That's not how it happened. You and Sai were the only ones who left. Do you not remember anything from the time before we started to wait?
entries.new: 事情不是这样。离开的只有你和 Sai。我们开始等待之前的那段时间，你一点都想不起来吗？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I understood why Katei didn't want me to humor Akaro, but not too long ago, I'd considered the possibility that the Sekimeiya could cause memory loss. I wanted to know if that was possible, as it could've let Isla's story occur as we'd imagined it.{w} If Akaro had traveled through time after escaping, it could have been the direct cause of the state he was in.
entries.new: 我明白 Katei 为什么不想让我顺着 Akaro 的话说，可就在不久前，我还考虑过 Sekimeiya 是否会造成记忆缺失。我想确认这种可能是否成立，因为若真如此，Isla 的说法就有可能如我们所设想的那样成立。{w}如果 Akaro 是在逃出去之后穿越了时间，那很可能就是他变成现在这样的直接原因。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I-I'm having trouble understanding what you're referring to. Before we started to wait? We investigated the building, and Naomi appeared briefly just to disappear again.
entries.new: ……我、我听不懂你在指什么。我们开始等待之前？我们调查了这栋楼，Naomi 短暂露过面，随后又消失了。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: That's not true. You were surprised that Naomi's body was found, but not that she died. Subconsciously, you must've known that, but you didn't remember finding her. Is that right?
entries.new: 不对。你惊讶的是 Naomi 的尸体被找到了，而不是她死了。潜意识里你肯定知道这件事，却不记得自己发现过她。是这样吧？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Are you sure that nothing happened right before we began to wait?
entries.new: 你确定我们开始等待之前什么都没发生吗？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I don't know what you're talking about.
entries.new: 我不知道你在说什么。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: We found a hidden passage in the storeroom, and a door that could lead outside.
entries.new: 我们在储藏室里发现了一条暗道，还有一扇也许能通到外面的门。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You can't be serious. A hidden exit? Why are we still here, then?
entries.new: 你在开玩笑吧。秘密出口？那我们为什么还待在这里？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: We had no way to open it. Do you really not recall any of that?
entries.new: 我们打不开。你真的一点都不记得？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I don't, because it didn't happen. There are no gaps in my memory, so don't treat me as if I'm delusional. Shiroya, tell me, is this some sort of trap?
entries.new: 不记得，因为根本没发生过。我的记忆没有缺口，别把我当成妄想症。Shiroya，你说，这是什么陷阱吗？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.new: ……不、不是的？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I understand. That's fair, I suppose.
entries.new: 我明白了。这也难怪。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I'm sorry to sound so blunt, but is there a reason why you keep talking to her specifically?
entries.new: 恕我说得直白，你为什么总是特意找她说话？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Huh...{w} I don't know how to answer this. I sympathize with you two, as I've already said. That's why it's surprising to see you lying like this.
entries.new: 嗯……{w}这我该怎么回答。我已经说过，我同情你们二位。正因如此，看到你们这样撒谎才叫我意外。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: You're really saying that this guy has been with us the whole time... I suppose I deserve this treatment, don't I? Why don't you be straight with me, then?
entries.new: 你们居然说这家伙一直和我们待在一起……看来我活该被这样对待，是吧？那你们何不干脆跟我直说？
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Akaro... What the fuck are you talking about?
entries.new: Akaro……你他妈到底在说什么？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You sympathize with us...?
entries.new: 同情我们……？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Just drop it.
entries.new: 别提了。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: What the hell does that mean!? Everything about you has been suspicious from the start!
entries.new: 你这话到底什么意思！？从最开始你就处处可疑！
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I get it.
entries.new: 我懂了。
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: What do you get? Is your plan to drive us insane? Because you're doing a great job!
entries.new: 你懂什么了？你的打算就是把我们逼疯吗？那你干得可真漂亮！
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Why won't you answer? ...Why did you say that you sympathize with us?
entries.new: 你为什么不肯回答？……你为什么要说同情我们？
