entries.text: However, the gruesome scenery obligated us to think that someone could've done it. Pushing Katei would've achieved the same result.{w} Vast pools of blood would take a long time to dry, so I easily spotted smaller drops on the sides of the desk. Those were much closer to drying up, reminding me of the one in the event room.
entries.new: 然而，眼前的惨状逼得我们不得不考虑，也可能是有人下的手。只要推 Katei 一把，也能造成同样的结果。{w}大片血迹要很久才会干，因此桌边那些细小的血滴格外显眼。它们比大摊血干得快得多，让我想起活动室里的那一滴。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No matter what happened, though... he was dead. Katei, who was an enigma of his own and never stopped claiming his innocence, met his sudden end right after freeing himself from confinement in the attic.
entries.new: 可不管究竟发生了什么……他死了。Katei 本身就充满谜团，又始终声称自己无辜，却刚摆脱阁楼里的囚禁，就突然丢了性命。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Look at the screen. There's a message.
entries.new: ……看屏幕。上面有条消息。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Huh...?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I quickly glanced at it. As she'd said, in the center of the middle screen, I saw a tiny message box, containing one single line of text.
entries.new: 我迅速瞥了一眼。正如她所说，中间那台屏幕的中央有个小小的消息框，里面只有一行字。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "{time=10:04}: Camera(s) disabled and associated footage erased".
entries.new: 「{time=10:04}：摄像头已停用，相关录像已删除」。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, what...? At {time=10:04}?
entries.new: 啊，什么……？是在 {time=10:04}？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That must've been when Katei was here alone. We checked the time at {time=9:41.}.. Twenty minutes later was when we left, and he stayed behind, trying to fix the system.
entries.new: 那应该是 Katei 独自留在这里的时候。我们在 {time=9:41.} 看过时间……二十分钟后我们离开，他留下来想修好系统。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: You're right. And instead, he erased the existing footage and shut down the cameras. That's what this is saying.
entries.new: 你说得对。而他反倒删掉了原有录像，还关掉了摄像头。这条消息就是这个意思。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The most conspicuous hint, a message left on the computer, was potential proof that Katei had been the culprit we were trying to ferret out. I reached for the mouse and dragged the message aside.{w} Behind it, the program Katei had attempted to display the footage with was the only thing seen on the screen. It had a list of all the cameras, but they were useless if they'd actually been disabled.
entries.new: 电脑上留下的那条消息，是最显眼的线索，也可能证明 Katei 就是我们要揪出的犯人。我伸手握住鼠标，把消息拖到一旁。{w}消息后面，屏幕上只剩下 Katei 原本用来播放录像的程序。程序里列着所有摄像头，可如果它们真被停用了，那也毫无用处。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I lowered my eyes. The taskbar contained the single clock we had at our disposal. As soon as I glanced at it, the numbers switched from {time=16:59} to {time=17:00.}
entries.new: 我垂下目光。任务栏上显示着我们唯一能参照的时钟。我刚看过去，数字便从 {time=16:59} 跳到了 {time=17:00.}。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's {time=17.} Only four hours are left.
entries.new: 已经 {time=17.} 了。只剩四个小时。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Let's get out of here. From this room too. The smell is getting unbearable.
entries.new: ……走吧。离开这里，也离开这个房间。气味越来越让人受不了了。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I had no complaints. Even though the hallway's illumination was worse, we left the much darker room and breathed steadily after the minutes we'd spent inside.
entries.new: 我没有异议。走廊的光线虽然更暗，我们还是离开了那间更加昏暗的房间；在里面待了几分钟后，总算能顺畅呼吸了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The message on the screen... Without a doubt, it belonged to the security system program, but was that full proof of its trustworthiness? With such an obvious message being found next to him, I had to ask myself if it was legitimate or a diversion left by his killer. Not only did the room leave the possibility of an accident open, it also displayed an incriminating message next to Katei.
entries.new: 屏幕上的那条消息……它无疑来自安保系统程序，但这足以证明它可信吗？这么显眼的消息就出现在他身旁，我不禁要问，它是真的，还是凶手留下的障眼法。这个房间既留下了意外死亡的可能，又把一条对他不利的消息摆在了 Katei 身边。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Was the message a fabrication by the real culprit to pin the blame on Katei and play it off as an accident while they were the ones to deal with the cameras and the security system? It wasn't easy to tell, and I wasn't sure which idea I was more inclined to lean toward.
entries.new: 这条消息会不会是真凶伪造的，用来把罪责推到 Katei 身上，再把现场伪装成意外，而真正处理摄像头和安保系统的人其实是他们？这并不好判断，我也说不清自己更倾向于哪一种可能。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait, no. It doesn't make any sense. Look.
entries.new: 等等，不对。这说不通。你看。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I followed Shiroya's line of sight again, that time up to the ceiling.
entries.new: 我再次顺着 Shiroya 的视线望去，这一次是抬头看向天花板。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That green light is supposed to indicate that the camera's recording, right? There's no way they were disabled so long ago.
entries.new: 那盏绿灯应该是表示摄像头正在录像，对吧？它们不可能那么早就被关掉了。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I'd forgotten about that... You're right.{w} However... it was Katei who told us what the green light meant. We can't be certain about it.
entries.new: 我都忘了这回事……你说得对。{w}不过……绿灯的含义是 Katei 告诉我们的。我们没法确定他说的是不是真的。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: They haven't stopped flickering, and I'm sure they also were before {time=10}, so if the cameras really aren't recording, the lights must simply indicate that they're powered on.
entries.new: 它们一直在闪，我敢肯定 {time=10} 之前也一样。所以，如果摄像头真的没在录像，这灯就只能表示它们通着电。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: It's strange that Katei would tell a lie like that. If he disabled the cameras, part of the reason would be that he didn't want the police to see him when they entered. Despite that, he incriminated himself by lying to us about what the lights mean.
entries.new: Katei 会撒这种谎，实在奇怪。如果他关掉了摄像头，部分原因应该是他不想让警察进来时看到他。可即便如此，他又在绿灯含义上骗了我们，反而把自己牵连了进去。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah, that's... not consistent. Could someone else have left that message to blame him?
entries.new: 是啊，这……对不上。会不会是别人留下那条消息，为了嫁祸他？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I'm not sure, but thinking about it more, there's no way this was an accident...{w} If Katei fell backward and hit his head against the desk, it means he was exiting the room. Why would he try to leave with that message being shown on the screen? Another person had to be involved somehow.
entries.new: 我不确定，但再仔细想想，这绝不可能是意外……{w}如果 Katei 是向后倒下、头撞上桌沿，那就说明他当时正要离开房间。屏幕上还显示着那条消息，他为什么要在这时候离开？一定有另一个人以某种方式牵涉其中。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Shiroya agreed with me. After a few pensive seconds, being presented once again with the fact that a murderer was nearby, we had to decide on what to do.
entries.new: Shiroya 同意我的看法。沉思几秒后，我们不得不再次面对凶手就在附近的事实，并决定接下来该怎么办。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Do you want to search for the others?
entries.new: 要去找其他人吗？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: W-We should. We don't know what happened to Akaro and Sai, but I'm worried about Erina. Just... We can't split up, Atsuki. We have to stay together no matter what.
entries.new: 我、我们得去。Akaro 和 Sai 不知道怎么样了，但我担心 Erina。只是……Atsuki，我们不能分开。无论发生什么，都得待在一起。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I couldn't say it was unlikely for Erina to become a target for the culprit. Katei was employed by Ashiya, a member of the security staff, but Isla had died despite being a complete outsider and a child. Any one of us could've been next.
entries.new: 我不能说 Erina 不会成为凶手的目标。Katei 受雇于芦屋，是安保人员，可 Isla 明明只是个完全无关的外人，还是个孩子，却同样死了。我们当中的任何一个人，都可能是下一个。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yeah, okay. Let's stick together and find Erina. Let's just be extremely careful. We have nothing to defend ourselves with if we're suddenly attacked.
entries.new: 好，就这么办。我们一起行动，去找 Erina。一定要格外小心。万一突然遭到袭击，我们连能防身的东西都没有。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: She gave me a strained, saddened look. Even though only four hours remained, seeing the outside world felt infinitely far away.
entries.new: 她看了我一眼，神情勉强而哀伤。明明只剩四个小时，外面的世界却遥远得仿佛永远也到不了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Let's see if the Sekimeiya's still here.
entries.new: 去看看 Sekimeiya 还在不在。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We entered the event room.
entries.new: 我们走进了活动室。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The Sekimeiya hadn't been taken while our attention was grabbed by the security room, so it was unlikely that was the intent of the culprit's plan. As a routine effort, I lowered the curtain again.
entries.new: 我们被监控室吸引注意力的那段时间，Sekimeiya 并没有被人拿走，所以那不太可能是凶手计划的真正目的。我照例又把遮布拉了下来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We have to find Erina. It's... not good that we haven't seen her yet.
entries.new: 得找到 Erina。到现在还没见到她……这可不妙。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: All right. There's no need to separate at all. We're only trying to find her, and she wouldn't hide from us. It could be dangerous to try to corner the culprit.
entries.new: 好吧。完全没必要分头行动。我们只是想找到她，而她又不会躲着我们。贸然去逼凶手现身，反而危险。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Right. Let's finish up this floor...
entries.new: 嗯。先把这一层搜完吧……
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: We went to the lobby to access the mechanical room. Down the staircase was the strangely imposing room which could have served purposes beyond our understanding.
entries.new: 我们回到大厅，前往机械室。顺着楼梯下去，那间屋子透着莫名的压迫感，用途或许远非我们所能理解。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There were some spots out of reach from the stairs—under a table or behind some chairs in the back. Stepping farther in revealed the lack of any hidden person.
entries.new: 从楼梯的位置看，有几处角落根本瞧不见——桌子底下，或者靠里的几把椅子背后。再往里走几步，便发现那里并没有藏着人。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I doubt Erina would be in a hallway B room, but let's look before going up.
entries.new: 我不觉得 Erina 会在 B走廊的房间里，不过上楼之前还是先看看吧。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The first room we looked into was empty. Failing to stumble upon anyone made things grow gradually more unsettling... We knew someone had to have traveled with the Sekimeiya shortly before we did...
entries.new: 我们查看的第一间房空空如也。始终没撞见半个人影，气氛反倒一点点变得令人不安……我们很清楚，就在我们之前不久，一定有人用 Sekimeiya 穿越了时间……
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd explored the thought that, perhaps, if the range was huge, Erina had the chance to be caught up in it and escape the tower. However, Katei had gone downstairs before her and should've traveled as well. Since the dryness of his blood indicated that he'd died almost half an hour before we'd found him, I was willing to disregard that theory.
entries.new: 我也想过，也许重叠范围足够大，Erina 有可能被卷入其中，从而逃出了芦屋塔。可 Katei 比她还早下楼，按理也该一同穿越。他的血迹干燥程度说明，他在被发现前将近半小时就已经死了，所以这个推测我愿意暂且搁下。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya and I proceeded to the next room. Of course, if they'd traveled out of the tower after leaving the attic, it was possible Katei had reentered the tower through the storeroom entrance and then died. If the search for Erina yielded no results, that angle would gain some traction.
entries.new: 我和 Shiroya 走向下一间房。当然，如果他们离开阁楼后走出了塔，那 Katei 也有可能从储藏室入口重新回到塔内，然后才死去。要是找 Erina 一无所获，这条思路就值得多想一想。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The next room underwent an identical search. Halfway through, we realized that searching inside the cabinets defeated the point of what we agreed on. They were only a potential hiding spot for a culprit we'd decided was out of our reach.
entries.new: 下一间房也用同样的方式搜了一遍。搜到一半，我们才意识到查看展示柜里面已经偏离了先前的共识。那里只是凶手可能藏身的地方，而我们早已决定不去招惹那个我们对付不了的凶手。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We opened the door to room B4.
entries.new: 我们推开了水晶展室 B4 的门。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Past it, on the floor, Naomi's corpse reminded us that it was the room where we'd found her. The sight stopped us in place, leaving us dumbstruck.
entries.new: 门一开，地板上的 Naomi 的尸体便提醒我们，这里正是当初发现她的地方。那景象让我们僵在原地，说不出话来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Because at her right, Erina lay, her clothes tinted maroon by all the blood on them.{w} Shiroya looked at me with the clear wish to deny reality. It hit us like a truck: Erina was dead too, and the only people remaining with us were dangers who we wanted to avoid.
entries.new: 因为就在她右侧，Erina 躺在那里，衣服被血染成了暗红。{w} Shiroya 望着我，眼神里分明盼着这一切不是真的。这个事实如重锤砸下：Erina 也死了，而还留在我们身边的，尽是些我们避之不及的危险人物。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I gulped before I took short steps forward. She was lying sideways, which let us see all the blood on her chest, though not extensively on the floor. There was some on her stomach and legs too. Unlike Katei's expression, hers looked almost serene despite everything the tower had put her through.
entries.new: 我咽了口唾沫，小步走上前。她侧躺着，胸前的血迹一览无余，地板上倒不算多。腹部和腿上也有。与 Katei 不同，尽管这座塔让她受了那么多折磨，她的神情却近乎安详。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When I turned around, I saw Shiroya kneeling down, burying her face in her hands. Someone around us had killed a mother who'd just lost her daughter, and we would have to continue fearing that looming danger... for four more hours. I had no words for the horrendous view I was forced to accept.
entries.new: 我回过头，只见 Shiroya 跪在地上，双手掩面。我们身边有人杀了一位刚刚失去女儿的母亲，而我们还得继续提防那潜伏的危险……整整四个小时。面对这被迫接受的惨状，我一句话也说不出来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We stared at the scene in silence. Erina's clothes were slightly torn, signaling a physical fight, and the color of the blood indicated that it had been drying long enough to almost be a solid, just like Katei's.
entries.new: 我们默默注视着眼前的景象。Erina 的衣服有轻微的撕裂，说明她曾与人搏斗；血液的颜色则表明，它已经干涸到几乎凝固，和 Katei 的一样。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That's it... I can't look at her. Let's go...
entries.new: 够了……我实在看不下去。走吧……
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I lowered my head even more than it already was, clenching my fists. Seeing Shiroya like that was heartbreaking, but it was ultimately impressive how strong she'd been. On my end, I only found myself rejecting reality, never fully allowing the deaths we'd seen to sink in.
entries.new: 我本就低着的头垂得更低，攥紧了拳头。看到 Shiroya 那个样子，我心里一阵绞痛，可她终究坚强得令人敬佩。至于我，只是一味地拒绝现实，从不肯让亲眼所见的死亡真正落进心里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stepped out of the room, but I couldn't avoid turning around again and witnessing the end of two women we'd met that day.
entries.new: 我走出房间，却还是忍不住回头，看了我们那天才认识的两个女人最后一眼。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Give me a second.
entries.new: 稍等一下。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Naomi's body was covered by an elegant curtain, so I didn't want to leave Erina behind without one. The cameras might not even have been recording, so I went ahead and detached another curtain from a cabinet, laying it over Erina. With that small attempt at dignity, we left the room.
entries.new: Naomi 的遗体盖着一块雅致的遮布，我也不想让 Erina 就这么露着。反正监控未必还在录像，我便从展示柜上又扯下一块遮布，盖在 Erina 身上。算是力所能及的一点体面，随后我们离开了房间。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We walked to the event room, lost. A threatening atmosphere had reared its ugly head with more finality than before; two murders in a row, and perhaps while we were on the same floor as them. Given the state of Erina's blood, it was more than likely that her body had been in that room for a while.
entries.new: 我们茫然地走向活动室。一股比先前更沉重的威胁感笼罩上来，带着几分已成定局的意味；接连两起命案，也许就发生在我们与他们同处一层的这段时间。从 Erina 的血迹来看，她的遗体很可能已经在那间房里躺了许久。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We hadn't reacted strongly to the past two—or three—deaths. It wasn't that we were desensitized, but that our feelings seemed insignificant compared to what was going in that place, as if our defeat had been unavoidable from the start. There had been no time to really stop and consider the true gravity of being sealed away with one or more murderers, at least not for me. Thinking of ways to either avoid or root out danger had taken priority.
entries.new: 先前那两起——也许是三起——死亡，我们并没有太大的反应。倒不是麻木了，只是与这里正在发生的一切相比，我们的感受显得微不足道，仿佛从一开始就注定要败下阵来。至少对我而言，根本没有余裕停下来细想：与一名乃至多名凶手一同被封在这座塔里，究竟意味着什么。如何避开危险、如何揪出危险，才是优先要务。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But things had changed. Shiroya and I being the only ones left hammered in just how deadly the situation was. With all color drained from the world, we simply moved forth, feeling like birds with clipped wings trapped in a cage.
entries.new: 但如今不同了。只剩下我和 Shiroya 两人，这本身就足以说明局势有多致命。世界仿佛褪尽了颜色，我们只是机械地向前走，像被剪去翅膀、困在笼中的鸟。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I made sure the Sekimeiya was inside the cabinet and sat next to the hallway A door. Then, Shiroya leaned against the wall in front of me. More than likely, we were no match for the culprit behind those deaths, so there was no point in trying to do anything else. We had nowhere to possibly hide. Wishing for only stillness, we quietly let time carry us.
entries.new: 我确认 Sekimeiya 收在展示柜里，随后在通往 A走廊的那扇门旁坐下。Shiroya 则靠在我正前方的墙边。凭我们的力量，多半敌不过制造这些命案的凶手，再做别的也是徒劳。这里根本没有可以藏身的地方。我们只求一切静止，就这样安静地任时间流逝。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: With nothing left to do, I meaninglessly ran through the possibility of trusting one of the others.
entries.new: 既然无事可做，我便漫无边际地推想，能否信任其余人中的某一个。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was one detail that felt off. Doubting that Akaro and Sai were the culprits was foolish... but one thing pointed me toward it.
entries.new: 有一个细节不太对劲。怀疑 Akaro 和 Sai 是凶手本显得愚蠢……可偏偏有一处线索把我往这个方向引。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was the drop of blood we'd found in the lobby. It was completely dry, meaning that it was left there while we'd been locked in the attic. However, the blood around Katei's and Erina's bodies had been, naturally, from a time after we unlocked the bedroom.
entries.new: 就是我们在厅里发现的那一滴血。它已经完全干涸，说明它是在我们被关在阁楼期间留下的。而 Katei 和 Erina 尸体周围的血，自然是我们打开卧室之后才流出的。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Therefore, during the time Akaro and Sai should've been the only people outside the attic's bedroom, someone had lost blood. In addition, I thought that a small injury wouldn't have produced a single drop as big as that one.
entries.new: 也就是说，在那段时间里，阁楼卧室外本该只有 Akaro 和 Sai，却有人流过血。而且，我觉得小小的擦伤不可能滴出那么大的一颗血珠。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It had every possibility of being an accident. Akaro and Sai also could've fought, resulting in Akaro's victory, going off the lack of injuries when he'd joined us again. However, the truth had the potential to be slightly more convoluted: perhaps Katei or Erina traveled to the past after leaving the attic. Then, they'd been attacked in the lobby and finished off even later.
entries.new: 那完全可能只是场意外。Akaro 和 Sai 也可能交过手，而从 Akaro 重新与我们汇合时毫无伤痕来看，赢的是他。不过，真相也许还要更曲折一些：或许 Katei 或 Erina 离开阁楼后穿越回了过去，他们在大厅遭到袭击，之后才被彻底了结。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No matter what had happened, it was clear that something went wrong while we were at the top of the tower. And no matter who was left nearby, we didn't want to cross paths with them anymore.
entries.new: 无论真相如何，有一点很明确：我们待在塔顶的那段时间里，出了岔子。而不管留在附近的是谁，我们都不想再与他照面了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Nonetheless, we were guarding the Sekimeiya. We hadn't discussed it again, but it was what we'd intended to do before seeing the last two corpses. If the culprit showed themselves to obtain it, in the instance we had to escape, there were doors on both sides of the room which we'd left open.
entries.new: 尽管如此，我们还是在守着 Sekimeiya。那之后我们没再商量过，可早在看到那两具尸体之前，我们就是这么打算的。万一凶手为了取走它而现身，而我们又不得不逃，房间两侧各有一扇门，我们一直留着没关。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I closed my eyes and left my mind blank. It felt nice after going over so many thoughts. But as soon as I did, different questions came to me.
entries.new: 我闭上眼睛，让脑子放空。在翻来覆去想那么多之后，这样反倒舒服。可刚一放空，别的问题又冒了出来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Instead of how... why? Why had someone killed Erina? What could anyone have gained with that? Had it been out of pure malice, taking advantage of the disabled cameras?
entries.new: 比起怎么做到的……我更想问为什么。为什么会有人杀了 Erina？杀了她又能得到什么？难道只是趁监控失灵，出于纯粹的恶意？
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That didn't feel right; we all would have been killed by that point. With the Sekimeiya around, actions were bound to have more depth than they appeared to, and I had a hard time believing that someone who had actively chosen to remain undiscovered for so long would have no real motive.
entries.new: 这也说不通。真是那样，我们早该全都被杀了。有 Sekimeiya 存在，任何举动背后都必定另有深意，我实在难以相信，一个刻意藏了这么久的人会没有真正的动机。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't be sure with Katei, but Erina hadn't done anything to warrant her death. At most, I could assume she'd found the culprit.
entries.new: Katei 的情况我无法确定，但 Erina 并没有做过任何招致杀身之祸的事。硬要猜，最多也只能猜她发现了凶手。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I went back to the small theory I'd put together. If she had traveled to the past and confronted Akaro and Sai while the rest of us were in the bedroom, that could have given them a motive for her death...{w} Even though they were the only suspects, they hadn't shown back up, so it was appropriate to think that they might never intend to.
entries.new: 我又想起自己拼凑出的那个小推测。如果她穿越回过去，在我们其余人还待在卧室时与 Akaro 和 Sai 撞上，这可能就成了他们杀害她的动机……{w} 虽然他们是仅有的嫌疑人，却始终没有露面，看来他们或许根本不打算再出现。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait... the recording!
entries.new: 等等……那段录音！
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: According to Akaro and Sai, Erina was alive.
entries.new: 按 Akaro 和 Sai 的说法，Erina 当时还活着。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Atsuki, what are you thinking about? Do you have any more ideas...? And hey, Erina, what's with that face?
entries.new: Atsuki，你在想什么？还有什么主意吗……？还有，Erina，你那是什么表情？
entries.speaker: sai2

entries.text: I-Isla, what's gotten into you? ...What are you holding?{w} And Erina, why aren't you doing anything!?
entries.new: Isla，你、你这是怎么了？……你手里拿的是什么？{w} 还有 Erina，你怎么什么都不做！？
entries.speaker: ak2

entries.text: Even though the scenario played out as if Erina and I were present, that isn't possible anymore. Who did that recording actually intend to trick...?
entries.new: 那段录音演得就像我和 Erina 都在场，可这已经不可能了。那段录音究竟是想骗谁……？
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: It couldn't be a coincidence that Akaro and Sai were the only other people still alive and the only ones to have been mentioned in the recording. However, Erina's death nullified its chances of being real.
entries.new: 还活着的人只剩 Akaro 和 Sai，而录音里提到的偏偏也只有他们，这不可能是巧合。可 Erina 一死，录音为真的可能性就被彻底否定了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Or did it? I tried to think about it.
entries.new: ……真的是这样吗？我试着往下想。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even though Isla's already dead, she was the third and last person to appear in the recording. But her death wasn't enough to completely deny it being real.
entries.new: Isla 虽然已经死了，但她却是录音里第三个、也是最后一个出现的人。不过，仅凭她的死，还不足以完全否定录音的真实性。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: And that's solely thanks to the Sekimeiya's existence. It's possible that Isla's still alive, she'll be part of the recording in the future, and will travel to the past to end up in the cabinet where we found her corpse. There might be different arrangements, but the gist would always be the same.
entries.new: 而这一切全靠 Sekimeiya 的存在。Isla 或许现在还活着，将来会出现在那段录音里，然后穿越回过去，最终出现在我们发现她尸体的那个展示柜里。具体的经过也许各有不同，但大致情形总归如此。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Could something similar apply to Erina...? Nothing supports it in her case, but the exact same thing could be going on with her, couldn't it?
entries.new: 同样的情况会不会也发生在 Erina 身上……？她的情况没有任何证据支持这一点，但完全相同的事也可能正在她身上发生，不是吗？
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: So not even her dead body is enough to disregard the recording. Not while the Sekimeiya exists.
entries.new: 所以，即便见到了她的尸体，也不能就此否定那段录音。只要 Sekimeiya 还在，就不能。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Despite my uncomfortable position, my sight began to fade, and I started to feel drowsy.
entries.new: 尽管姿势很不舒服，我的视线还是渐渐模糊，困意涌了上来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Every time I rested a little, my body reminded me of how tired I was and of its strong demand for a full sleep.
entries.new: 每次稍微歇一会儿，身体就提醒我它有多疲惫，又是多么渴望好好睡上一觉。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I saw that Shiroya's eyes were shut. I desperately wanted to resist it, but I couldn't help but close mine too, lay my head on my shoulder, and put my body against the wall.
entries.new: 我看见 Shiroya 闭着眼睛。我拼命想撑住，却还是不由自主地合上眼，脑袋靠向自己肩头，身体抵住墙壁。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I knew that my consciousness was soon to fade, but having to wait for almost another four hours made any attempt at preventing it futile. I let myself go, temporarily abandoning the nightmarish tower engulfed in mystery.
entries.new: 我知道自己的意识很快就要沉下去，可还要再等将近四个小时，再抗拒也是徒劳。于是我放任自己沉入黑暗，暂时将这座笼罩在谜团中的噩梦之塔抛在脑后。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My subconscious was alert at all times, aware that I was surrounded by ever-present danger. For that reason, as soon as the faintest sound met my ears, all my senses came back.
entries.new: 我的潜意识始终警醒，清楚自己身处无时不在的危险之中。因此，耳边刚传来最细微的声响，我的神志便立刻恢复清明。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As if I'd traveled through time, I opened my eyes, unaware of how long I'd been there for. Thanks to the open doors, I discerned the origin of the noise. I stared ahead, where hallway B was.
entries.new: 我睁开眼，仿佛穿越了时间，不知道自己在那边待了多久。门开着，我辨出声音来自哪里，便朝前方望去——那是 B 走廊。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wha—!
entries.new: 什么——！
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I froze. The dry sound of my heart echoed within me and stuttered.
entries.new: 我僵住了。干涩的心跳声在体内回响，忽快忽慢，断断续续。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Just behind the door was Shiroya. As soon as she looked inside the event room, she saw my piercing gaze and returned it with her own.
entries.new: 门后正是 Shiroya。她刚朝活动室里看，就迎上我锐利的目光，也回望过来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After an eternity of a second, she turned around and sped up, her figure rapidly disappearing.
entries.new: 那一秒漫长得如同永恒。她随即转身，加快脚步，身影迅速消失在视野里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Then, without moving, I looked at... Shiroya. She was still sitting down and leaning against the wall before my very eyes, resting her head on her arms.
entries.new: 我还是没动，只把目光投向……Shiroya。她仍坐在我眼前，靠着墙，头枕在自己的手臂上。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: H-Hey... Are you awake?
entries.new: 喂、喂……你醒着吗？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Shiroya...!
entries.new: Shiroya……！
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Huh...?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: She lifted her face and looked at me with nearly closed eyes.
entries.new: 她抬起脸，半睁着眼看我。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Were you sleeping?
entries.new: 你刚才在睡觉？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Sorry... yeah.
entries.new: 抱歉……嗯。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I stood up, clueless, my mind cluttered.
entries.new: 我站起身，满心茫然，脑子里乱作一团。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No... It might sound ridiculous, but I just saw you.
entries.new: 不……说出来可能很荒唐，但我刚才看见你了。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I dashed to hallway B. It was empty.{w} My mind still reeling, I reentered the event room.
entries.new: 我冲去 B走廊。那里空无一人。{w} 我脑子仍乱成一团，又回到了活动室。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wh-What...?
entries.new: 什、什么……？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I'm being serious. Footsteps woke me up, and I saw you in hallway B. You saw me too, but you walked toward hallway C, and there's no one here.
entries.new: 我是认真的。脚步声把我吵醒，我看见你在 B走廊。你也看见我了，却朝 C走廊走去——可这里根本没人。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What? How long have I been asleep?
entries.new: 什么？我睡了多久？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I don't know.
entries.new: 不知道。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What I saw could only have been achieved with the Sekimeiya, so I uncovered the curtain.
entries.new: 我看到的景象，只可能是 Sekimeiya 造成的。于是我揭开了遮布。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The Sekimeiya's still here, and it's locked.
entries.new: Sekimeiya 还在这里，而且锁着。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I don't understand. Are you sure it was me?
entries.new: 我不明白。你确定那是我？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yes, but... there was a big difference. You were wearing different clothes.
entries.new: 确定，不过……有个很大的不同。你穿的衣服不一样。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Different clothes...? Were they mine?
entries.new: 衣服不一样……？是我的衣服吗？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: No, but I think I recognized them. You still had your coat, but you were wearing a different shirt and pants, and I think I saw them earlier in one of the attic wardrobes.
entries.new: 不是，但我好像认得那些衣服。外套还是你那件，可衬衫和裤子换了；那些衣物，我先前似乎在阁楼的某个衣柜里见过。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: She was too lost to respond, and understandably so. It meant that in the future, she was guaranteed to travel to the past and live out what I'd experienced. But it all went far beyond my comprehension, especially her strange behavior and clothing.
entries.new: 她茫然得答不上话，这也不难理解。那意味着，未来的她注定会穿越回过去，经历我方才见到的一切。可这一切远超我的理解，尤其是她那古怪的举止和衣着。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Stay here for a second.
entries.new: 在这里等一下。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I rushed out of the room and ran to hallway C. It was empty as well.{w} Had it been a hallucination? There was no way—I was sure of what I'd seen.
entries.new: 我冲出房间，跑向 C走廊。那里同样空无一人。{w} 难道是我的错觉？不可能——我很确定自己看见了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I circled the floor and entered the event room from hallway A. It appeared the Shiroya I'd seen had deliberately hidden herself, so I wasn't sure if searching in depth was a good idea.
entries.new: 我绕着这一层走了一圈，从 A走廊回到活动室。看来我见到的那个 Shiroya 是故意躲了起来，因此我也不确定该不该仔细搜查。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Let's go to the attic. I need to see if I'm right about this.
entries.new: 去阁楼吧。我得确认自己的猜测对不对。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: She shot me another questioning look and approached with her hand on her forehead. No matter how much we wanted to spend the remainder of our time in the event room, Shiroya's bizarre apparition indicated that something else was happening or just about to.
entries.new: 她又向我投来疑问的目光，手扶着额头走近。无论我们多想在活动室度过余下的时间，Shiroya 那诡异的现身都说明，有别的事情正在发生，或者即将发生。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Should we check the time first?
entries.new: 要不要先看一下时间？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Oh, probably.
entries.new: 哦，也对。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Hallway A was still completely vacant. Shiroya had clearly seen me and chosen to walk away. It made no sense. If that was a future version of her, she already knew that I would see her.
entries.new: A走廊依旧空无一人。Shiroya 明明看见了我，却选择走开。这说不通。如果那是未来的她，她早该知道我会看见她。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was Sai's dilemma all over again. I had just explained what I saw to Shiroya, so if she ever did travel to the past and repeat what I'd told her, she would be completing a loop with no origin. It couldn't be that she purposely let me see her just because I said so.{w} If Shiroya ever traveled again, she'd immediately recognize that the situation I described could come at any time. There was no chance for it to happen without foreknowledge, like when she'd called the elevator in the attic...
entries.new: 这又成了 Sai 当初的困境。我刚把自己看见的告诉了 Shiroya；若她日后真的穿越回过去，并做出我所说的那些事，她就是在补全一个没有源头的因果循环。她不可能仅因我这么说了，就故意让我看见她。{w} 如果 Shiroya 再次时间穿越，她立刻就会明白，我描述的情形随时都可能出现。若没有预知，这一幕根本不可能发生——就像她在阁楼里叫来电梯那次……
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The state of the security room was unchanged. I saw some drops of blood had fully dried up, which was consistent with the time displayed on the computer:{w} {time=17:29.}
entries.new: 监控室仍保持原样。我注意到几滴血已经完全干涸，这与电脑上显示的时间相符：{w} {time=17:29.}
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya! Are you there!?
entries.new: Shiroya！你在吗！？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It was such a nonsensical sight. The person I was calling for was next to me, but she wasn't who my shouts were directed to.
entries.new: 那景象实在荒诞。我呼喊的人就在身旁，可我的喊声并不是冲她去的。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Once again, if I tried to continue reasoning with my assumption that "everything has to have an origin of some kind", the most simple explanation behind things was that Shiroya would eventually lose her memories.
entries.new: 我若再一次以「凡事必有其源头」为前提继续推想，那么一切背后最简单的解释，便是 Shiroya 最终会失去记忆。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was getting a headache. I'd wanted to finally put a stop to all those maddening lines of thought, but I couldn't. Not after the way the Shiroya in the hallway stared right through me.
entries.new: 我的头开始疼了。我本想彻底放下这些折磨人的念头，却办不到——尤其是在走廊里那个 Shiroya 直直地看穿我之后。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The elevator is still here, so if you went up, you probably didn't use it. Let's walk.
entries.new: 电梯还停在这里，所以你要是上去过，大概也没坐它。我们走楼梯吧。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: She simply nodded. I understood that since she hadn't personally seen herself, she was too baffled and sleepy to feel the urgency I did.
entries.new: 她只点了点头。我明白，她毕竟没有亲眼看见另一个自己，又困惑又困倦，自然感受不到我这份紧迫。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As I went up, I reassured myself of what I believed.
entries.new: 上楼时，我不断在心里告诉自己，我的判断没有错。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Something else has to be happening. The way we think the Sekimeiya works does not explain this.
entries.new: 一定还有别的事情在发生。我们对 Sekimeiya 运作方式的理解，解释不了这件事。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Both of us wanted to stay in the event room until {time=21}, but it was a different Shiroya who made us leave. What if whatever's about to happen leads into Shiroya traveling and she experiences her side of what I just saw?
entries.new: 我们俩都想在活动室待到 {time=21}，可把我们叫走的是另一个 Shiroya。假如接下来要发生的事，最终导致 Shiroya 穿越时间，让她经历我刚看见的那一幕中属于她的那一侧呢？
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: That doesn't make a single bit of sense. Again, the reason why we left the room would be because we left the room and then made ourselves leave the room. There's something clearly missing.
entries.new: 这根本说不通。照这样推，我们离开活动室的理由，就成了我们离开过活动室，然后又叫自己离开活动室。显然还有什么缺失。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Not only is this a bootstrap paradox, it contradicts our own interests. We both had every intention of staying there, so what could the meaning behind this actually be?
entries.new: 这不仅是一个自举悖论，还与我们自身的意愿相悖。我们两人当时都打算留在那里，那这件事背后的意义究竟何在？
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I hoped that whatever the attic contained, there would be some kind of hint. The other Shiroya was wearing clothes I thought I'd seen up there, which amplified how outlandish it would be for that bootstrap to occur.
entries.new: 我原本希望，阁楼里不管有什么，总能留下些线索。另一个 Shiroya 身上的衣服，我似乎在上面见过——若真有那样的自举发生，就愈发显得匪夷所思。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Why was she dressed in clothes from the attic? Instead of going over how unlikely causal loops were, I had to shift my approach—the answer had to be something that wouldn't directly come from me seeing her wearing the clothes.
entries.new: 她为什么穿着阁楼里的衣服？与其反复琢磨因果循环何等罕见，我得换个思路——答案不该直接来自「我看见她穿着这身衣服」这件事。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, that had already happened, and I'd told her about it. So what possibilities remained? What could the masked answer have been?{w} ...Reason. That was what I needed to locate.
entries.new: 可那件事已经发生，我也已经告诉了她。那么还剩下哪些可能？那个被遮掩的答案究竟是什么？{w}……是理由。我要找的就是理由。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We arrived at the entrance to the attic. The key was still in the keyhole, so we began to go up the narrow staircase.
entries.new: 我们来到阁楼的入口。钥匙仍插在锁孔里，于是我们踏上了狭窄的楼梯。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A reason behind the Shiroya I just saw, who still has to be somewhere...
entries.new: 刚才那个 Shiroya 背后的理由——她此刻一定还在某处……
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Is it a coincidence that the hardest mysteries to solve have involved double selves? Now that I think about it, almost everyone but me has produced this mystery individually.
entries.new: 最难解的谜团都牵涉到另一个自己，这难道是巧合？现在回想，除我之外，几乎每个人都各自经历过这样的怪事。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Naomi's body appeared dead twice. Sai existed both in the attic and on the crystal floor, and simple time travel couldn't explain it. What about the Akaro who had different memories?{w} Isla and Erina have died despite the fact they're supposed to be alive in the future. Now, a Shiroya that's very hard to explain with pure time travel has suddenly shown herself.
entries.new: Naomi 的尸体两次呈现死亡状态。Sai 同时存在于阁楼和水晶层，单纯的时间穿越解释不通。那个记忆不同的 Akaro 又该如何解释？{w}Isla 和 Erina 已经死去，可在未来她们本该活着。如今，又有一个很难用纯粹的时间穿越解释的 Shiroya 突然露面。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The core mystery is always the origin of the extra person and their reason for existing. Something else might have been happening right under our noses, and we just haven't noticed yet.
entries.new: 谜团的核心始终是多出来的那个人从何而来、又为何存在。或许还有别的事情一直在我们眼皮底下发生，只是我们尚未察觉。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Could it be related to...
entries.new: 会不会和……有关？
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: A second Katei hasn't appeared. Is that related to what Akaro said in the bedroom?
entries.new: 第二个 Katei 始终没有出现。这和 Akaro 在卧室里说的那番话有关吗？
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: He didn't know who Katei was...{w} but he knew me.
entries.new: 他不知道 Katei 是谁……{w}却认得我。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: It doesn't seem like anyone's been here recently, going off the floor.
entries.new: 看这地板的样子，最近似乎没人来过。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We entered, leaving behind the first footprints in a while. If anyone had entered or exited the attic, they used the elevator. However, since the key was still in the door below us, it was unlikely that the elevator could possibly have gone up so far.
entries.new: 我们走进去，留下了许久以来的第一串脚印。若有人进出过阁楼，只可能是乘了电梯。可钥匙还插在楼下的门上，电梯应该不可能一路升到这里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I believe it's in the right bedroom. The wardrobe had a few articles of clothing.
entries.new: 应该在右边的卧室里。衣柜里有几件衣服。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That one, right? I saw them too.
entries.new: 就那个房间吧？那些衣服我也看见了。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I nodded and opened it up. Inside, a few old-looking clothes hung in the empty space.
entries.new: 我点点头，打开了衣柜。里面空荡荡的，只挂着几件显得陈旧的衣服。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I thought so. You were wearing these.
entries.new: 果然如此。你当时穿的就是这些。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I took out a moderately sized white shirt and dark pants, neither of which looked to have been designed for a young girl.
entries.new: 我取出一件尺码中等的白衬衫和一条深色长裤，两件都不像是为年轻女孩做的。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: These? I'm not sure I like them.
entries.new: 这些？我不太喜欢。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Well, there isn't much else to choose from.
entries.new: 可也没有别的可选了。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...I suppose, yeah. I imagine I'd pick these if I wanted to use this wardrobe to get dressed.
entries.new: ……大概吧。要是我真想用这个衣柜换衣服，应该也会挑这几件。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: And you were wearing them even though they're still here.
entries.new: 可它们还在这儿，你却穿着它们。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I'm very lost about this, but does it mean that I'll go back to the past with them?
entries.new: 我完全搞不明白。但这意思是，我会穿着它们回到过去？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I... don't know.
entries.new: 我……不知道。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Could something else have been the answer? I thought about that first.{w} I'd just put together how unlikely it was that anyone had entered the attic recently. That meant the Shiroya I'd seen probably hadn't hurried up to the attic and returned those clothes to the wardrobe.
entries.new: 会不会另有答案？我先想到的是这一点。{w}我刚推断出最近几乎没人进过阁楼，也就是说，我见到的那个 Shiroya 应该没有匆匆跑上阁楼、把这些衣服放回衣柜。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't imagine that had happened, but it wasn't out of the question. If that Shiroya had possessed another key to the attic, she could've come faster than us while we'd gone to the security room.
entries.new: 我并不认为真会这样，但也并非全无可能。若那个 Shiroya 另有一把阁楼钥匙，趁我们去监控室时，她或许能比我们更快赶到这里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I wasn't sure if she had the ability to use the single key we knew existed. The elevator had probably been on the crystal floor, so even if she had the key, she would've had to go up with it, leave the clothes behind, take the elevator down to the sixth floor, send it to the crystal floor, and place the key back in the attic's keyhole.
entries.new: 我们所知只有那一把钥匙，她能不能用得上，我也说不准。电梯多半停在水晶层，所以就算她有钥匙，也得先乘它上去，把衣服留下，再乘电梯下到六楼，把电梯送回水晶层，最后把钥匙插回阁楼门口的锁孔里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}Even though they look the same, I'm willing to assume these clothes aren't the exact same ones I saw you wearing. Meaning that two identical sets exist at the moment, if your other self is still here somewhere.
entries.new: ……{w}虽然看着一样，但我觉得这身不是我见你穿过的那一套。也就是说，如果你的另一个自己此刻还在这栋楼里某处，那眼下就有两套一模一样的衣服。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It feels pointless trying to think about how it happened when I'm completely clueless as to why it did. But if you travel to the past and see me in the event room, something similar to our last travel has to happen.
entries.new: 连原因都毫无头绪，再去想事情是怎么发生的，总觉得白费力气。可如果你穿越回过去，在活动室见到我，那就一定会重演类似上次穿越的情形。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You mean that I'd need to wear the clothes for a while and then travel with the Sekimeiya. After that, I'd have to appear far back enough and the place I show up would have to be from the time I was wearing the clothes.
entries.new: 你是说，我得穿着这身衣服过一阵子，然后带着 Sekimeiya 穿越。之后，我出现的时间要足够早，出现的地点也得是我穿着这身衣服时待过的地方？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I was getting incredibly overwhelmed. The way she described it was one way for it to work. Other arrangements existed, such as traveling far to the past, borrowing the clothes, seeing me in the event room, and eventually going to the past again to return them to the wardrobe.
entries.new: 我越听越觉得头绪纷乱。她说的只是其中一种可能。还有别的安排，比如先穿越到很久以前，借走这身衣服，在活动室见到我，最后再次回到过去，把衣服放回衣柜。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Nonetheless, it didn't make any sense. Why would she do that? It was so bizarre and unlike anything else that had happened, I couldn't think of even a semi-logical explanation.
entries.new: 可这依然说不通。她为什么要那么做？整件事太过离奇，和此前发生的任何事都不同，我连一个勉强合乎逻辑的解释都想不出来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Let me see... It's possible we'll come across that version of you again, even though she didn't look too surprised to see me. Just in case we do...
entries.new: 让我想想……我们也许还会再遇上那个你，虽然她见到我时并不怎么惊讶。以防万一……
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I opened the drawers and took a marker out.
entries.new: 我拉开抽屉，取出一支记号笔。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I hope this hasn't dried yet. If these cameras are actually still working, I might get in trouble for this, but it could tell us something of value.
entries.new: 但愿这支笔还没干透。要是这些摄像头其实还在运转，我这么做可能会惹上麻烦，但也许能让我们弄清一件要紧的事。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Are you gonna leave a mark?
entries.new: 你要做个记号？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yes. Washing it won't get rid of it, so I'll make it tiny.
entries.new: 对。洗也洗不掉，所以我会画得很小。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: On the collar of the shirt, I drew a tiny black cross.
entries.new: 我在衬衫领口上画了一个小小的黑色十字。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The more I think about it, the more unlikely it seems that whatever happened was accomplished by traveling from the future. It'd be a loop without origin, which is not how a consistent timeline would work.
entries.new: 我越想越觉得，这件事不像是从未来穿越回来促成的。那会成为一个没有起点的循环，而自洽的时间线不该如此。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Just like I'd thought when we were locked in the bedrooms, there was a way to place the origin of the loop inside Shiroya's mind.{w} If she'd created a plan downstairs in the event room where a future self of hers would lure us out to accomplish something, and she'd later travel to make that happen, I'd begin to accept it as possible. Since it had happened to Shiroya, though, I wasn't able to reason it out like that.
entries.new: 就像我们被关在卧室里时我想过的，有一种办法能把循环的起点放在 Shiroya 的头脑里。{w}如果她早在楼下的活动室里定下计划——让未来的自己把我们引出去、以此达成某件事——而她后来真的穿越回去促成此事，那我或许还能接受这种可能。可这次事情是 Shiroya 亲身经历的，我就没法这么推想了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If we ever see that version of you again and you're wearing these clothes, I'll check this spot.{w} If the mark is there, it'll mean that you traveled from the future with it somehow. If it's not, that'll tell us the truth is different.
entries.new: 要是我们再见到那个你，而她穿着这身衣服，我就检查这里。{w}如果有记号，就说明她是带着这身衣服从未来穿越来的。如果没有，那就说明真相并非如此。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: If I ran into that Shiroya and saw no mark, there were next to no ways to explain it with her coming from the future, and they all relied on returning the clothes to the wardrobe before we found them. Once again, I couldn't help but experience an impending and threatening pressure when I tried to think about what reason existed behind it all.
entries.new: 如果我遇上那个 Shiroya，却看不到记号，那就几乎没有办法用「她从未来而来」来解释，仅剩的几种可能也都得靠她先在我们找到衣服之前把衣服放回衣柜。一想到这一切背后的原因，我又感到某种迫近的压迫感。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I left the marker inside the drawer and sat on the bed. Shiroya joined me at my side, evidently not fully accepting yet that a mysterious version of her was most likely roaming around downstairs.
entries.new: 我把记号笔放回抽屉，坐到床上。Shiroya 过来坐在我身边，显然还没能完全接受：楼下很可能正有一个神秘的她在走动。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You don't plan to travel to the past or put on those clothes, right? How could that have happened if you'll never make it happen?
entries.new: 你并不打算穿越回过去，也没打算穿这身衣服，对吧？可如果你永远不会去做，那件事又怎么会发生？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I won't, no, and I don't know either. I think it's just as strange as you're making it out to be.
entries.new: 我不会，真的不会，我也搞不懂。我也觉得这事确实像你说的那样古怪。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I replayed the moment in my head. That expressionless person who'd unmistakably been Shiroya... What were her thoughts at the time?
entries.new: 我在脑中回放那一刻。那个面无表情的人分明就是 Shiroya……她当时在想什么？
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I lay back in frustration. That was the first time the bizarre "double body" situation happened to someone I could trust and freely speak with, but she had no idea what the meaning behind it was. Perhaps that also applied to every other case.
entries.new: 我懊恼地仰面躺下。这种诡异的「双重身体」情形，第一次发生在我信任且能畅所欲言的人身上，可她对其中的含义也一无所知。也许其他每一次都是如此。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It could be that the original Naomi wouldn't have been able to explain the existence of her double self either. Could something have been creating replicas of us without our notice?
entries.new: 或许原本的 Naomi 也同样无法解释另一个自己的存在。会不会有什么东西在我们毫无察觉时制造着我们的复制品？
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was no way. Otherwise, the other Shiroya would've run to me as soon as she'd seen me. And even if the answer was that she had a reason to borrow the clothes from the attic, they wouldn't have still been in the wardrobe.
entries.new: 绝无可能。否则，另一个 Shiroya 一见到我就该朝我跑来。再说，就算她真有理由从阁楼借走这身衣服，它们也不该还好端端地留在衣柜里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I clicked my tongue, sighed, and rolled on the bed... I hated everything about it. When I looked at Shiroya, all I got from her face was a despondent expression.
entries.new: 我咂了咂嘴，叹了口气，在床上翻了个身……这一切都让我厌烦透顶。我看向 Shiroya，她脸上只有一片消沉。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That version of you had some goal. If she was lost somehow or suddenly popped into existence, she wouldn't have ignored me.
entries.new: 那个你是有目的的。如果她只是迷了路，或者凭空突然出现，她不会对我置之不理。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What kind of goal...?
entries.new: 什么目的……？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Well, look at what she accomplished. By wearing clothes from the attic, not responding to my shouts, and quickly hiding from view... she brought us here.
entries.new: 看看她做到了什么。穿上阁楼里的衣服，不回应我的喊声，又飞快地躲起来……她把我们引到了这里。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You think I wanted to lead us far away from the event room?
entries.new: 你觉得我是想让我们离活动室越远越好？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Honestly, what else could it be? That's where the Sekimeiya is. I'm not accusing you of anything—I'm sure you would have had a good reason for doing it...
entries.new: 说实话，还能是什么？Sekimeiya 就在那里。我不是在指责你——我相信你那么做一定有充分的理由……
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: No... that can't be it. I'm sure I don't want to touch the Sekimeiya again.
entries.new: 不……不会是这样。我很确定，我不想再碰 Sekimeiya 了。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: But you could've come from the future with further knowledge and a specific plan to achieve.
entries.new: 但你也可能是从未来而来，知道得更多，还有明确的目的要实现。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You just said earlier that doesn't make sense, right? Even if I ever think of a good reason to travel back to this point and use the Sekimeiya, I'd know how to do it just because me doing it already happened. I'd be repeating what you saw thanks to the fact that I repeated what you saw. ...That can't be it.
entries.new: 你刚才不是说过，这说不通吗？就算我将来真想到一个好理由，要穿越回这个时间点使用 Sekimeiya，我也只是因为事情已经发生过，才知道该怎么做。我是在重演你看到的那一幕，而理由仅仅是我已经重演过那一幕。……所以不会是这样。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I couldn't object. I'd used that same argument to deny a multitude of theories, but it wasn't fully reliable, as we didn't know the rules of the universe regarding time travel.
entries.new: 我无从反驳。我用同样的论点否定过许多推测，可这套说法并不完全可靠——关于时间穿越，这个宇宙的规则我们并不清楚。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Let's go back down, I suppose. We'll see if the Sekimeiya's still there, and there's a chance we'll see you again.
entries.new: 那就先下去吧。看看 Sekimeiya 还在不在，说不定还能再见到你。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Okay.
entries.new: 好。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Accompanied by an unsettling, gloomy mood, we entered the hallway. We weren't feeling too energetic, so we called the elevator.
entries.new: 我们怀着不安而沉闷的心情走进走廊。两人都提不起劲，便叫了电梯。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After a few seconds, the button lit up orange. I opened the door and entered after her.
entries.new: 几秒后，按钮亮起橙光。我打开门，跟在她后面走了进去。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After pressing the lowest button, I leaned on the uncomfortable handrail and wished for everything to finally end. We began to descend, surrounded by the unassuming sound of the elevator's motion and my deep sighs.
entries.new: 按下最底层的按钮后，我靠在并不舒适的扶手上，只盼这一切能尽早结束。电梯开始下降，四周只剩下它运行时的轻微声响和我的沉重叹息。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Huh...?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Shiroya also realized that we'd stopped earlier than expected. As the secondary doors opened, we saw the floor 3 button blinking.
entries.new: Shiroya 也察觉到我们停得比预想中早。内门打开时，只见三楼的按钮正在闪烁。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did you hit it accidentally?
entries.new: 是你误按了吗？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: No.
entries.new: 没有。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: We looked at each other, puzzled, before staring at the opaque door that led to the third floor. We were unaware of what awaited us, but we expected something to happen.
entries.new: 我们困惑地对视一眼，随后一同望向通往三楼的那扇不透明的门。我们不知道门外有什么在等着，却都觉得一定会发生些什么。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Someone must've pressed the button while we were inside...
entries.new: 我们还在里面的时候，肯定有人按了按钮……
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: However, the door didn't immediately open. The only explanation was that someone had called it from the third floor, but they weren't getting in.{w} I cautiously reached forward and pushed the door.
entries.new: 可门并没有立刻打开。唯一的解释是有人在三楼叫了电梯，却又不进来。{w}我小心翼翼地伸手推开了门。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A desolate corridor came into view, with zero apparent signs of life.
entries.new: 一条冷清的走廊出现在眼前，看不出半分有人活动的迹象。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't see anyone...
entries.new: 一个人也没有……
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I stepped out with Shiroya right behind. I looked at the button, but nothing indicated whether it had been pressed.
entries.new: 我走了出去，Shiroya 紧跟在后。我看了看按钮，可看不出它是否被人按过。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You're sure you didn't hit it, right?
entries.new: 你确定自己没有按到吧？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yeah, definitely.
entries.new: 嗯，确定。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Oh, the elevator kept moving to the crystal floor.
entries.new: 啊，电梯自己继续往水晶层去了。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Shiroya called it again as I walked a few automatic steps, attempting to comprehend what could've happened.
entries.new: 我下意识地走了几步，试图想明白究竟发生了什么，Shiroya 则再次叫回了电梯。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did someone run away after pressing the button...?
entries.new: 难道是有人按下按钮后就跑掉了……？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I approached the stairs, the most likely route anyone would've chosen to hide in a rush. I couldn't immediately see anyone, so we'd have to choose which way to go.
entries.new: 我走向楼梯——要是有人匆忙躲起来，那里最有可能。一时看不到人影，我们只能自己决定往哪边走了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There's really no one here. Should we keep going down?
entries.new: 这里真的没人。我们要继续往下走吗？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I guess so...
entries.new: 大概吧……
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Maybe we should continue on foot. It could've been the other version of you.
entries.new: 也许我们该走楼梯下去。那说不定就是另一个你。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...{w}Okay.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Our synchronized footsteps began to lightly echo around the wide interior, setting up an uncomfortable atmosphere we'd gotten very familiar with.
entries.new: 我们整齐的脚步声开始在宽敞的空间里轻轻回荡，织出那种早已令我们熟悉的不安气氛。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was barely ahead of Shiroya. After a few steps, I reached the left turn, where the entrance to the offices was.
entries.new: 我走在 Shiroya 前方不远处。几步之后便到了左转的拐角，办公室的入口就在那里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Bloodhound
entries.new: 猎犬

entries.text: Out of nowhere, I saw a hand gripping a knife swing toward me.{w} My heart didn't have time to stop before I began to see the motion slowly. Without being able to give it any thought, I turned my whole body around as fast as possible.
entries.new: 一只握着刀的手不知从何处朝我劈来。{w} 我甚至来不及害怕，眼中的动作已慢了下来。顾不上思考，我用尽全力扭转身子。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I felt a breeze at my side from the swipe whiffing and looked up to witness Shiroya's expression progressively changing to a terrified mask. As fast as my worn-out body let me, I bolted to her and grabbed her hand, running the opposite direction.
entries.new: 刀锋落空，一阵风从我身侧掠过。我抬起头，只见 Shiroya 的神情一点点化作惊恐。我以这具疲惫身躯所能达到的最快速度冲到她身边，抓住她的手，朝反方向狂奔。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We ran as fast as possible and began to hear a third person coming from behind us. We were being chased.
entries.new: 我们拼命奔跑，随即听见身后传来第三个人的声响。有人正在追我们。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The distance between us and the attacker was minimal. While we desperately sprinted, we saw the elevator and the floor 4 staircase in front of us.
entries.new: 我们与袭击者之间的距离近得可怕。我们拼命冲刺，前方出现了电梯和通往四楼的楼梯。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was certain we weren't going to have time to open the elevator and use it before being caught. The staircase was our single option.
entries.new: 我很清楚，在被他追上之前，我们来不及开电梯进去。楼梯是唯一的选择。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I fully focused on running as hard as I could, tightly gripping Shiroya's hand. Without a doubt, the person we heard behind us had tried to kill me.
entries.new: 我把全部心思都放在奔跑上，紧紧握着 Shiroya 的手。毫无疑问，身后那人是真的想杀我。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Before we reached the stairs, I let go of her hand and prayed we could go up fast enough. Halfway up, the crisp steps below us let us know the attacker hadn't given up and would continue to chase us.
entries.new: 还没跑到楼梯，我就松开了她的手，只盼我们能爬得够快。爬到一半时，下方清晰的脚步声告诉我们，袭击者并未放弃，还会继续追来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My heart began to race faster than I'd ever felt it. Despite how unreal it seemed, the idea that someone around us wanted our death had proven correct. As soon as we reached the higher floor, we took off again.
entries.new: 我的心跳快得前所未有。尽管难以置信，但「身边的人想要我们死」这个念头果然应验了。一登上上一层，我们立刻又跑了起来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked to my side, ensuring that Shiroya was still okay. She met my look with terror, not a trace of wooziness remaining in her. What had we done, and why had we been attacked? A myriad of similar questions flooded my mind as we kept running through the straightaway.
entries.new: 我朝身旁看去，确认 Shiroya 安然无恙。她满脸恐惧地回望我，先前那股昏沉已荡然无存。我们究竟做了什么？为什么会遭到袭击？类似的疑问涌进我的脑海，而我们仍在笔直的走廊上不停地跑。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even though the bathrooms could be locked from the inside, Katei said that his key opened all of them. We were most definitely being chased by his killer, who could've picked it up or could go back to the security room to do so.{w} Entering the partitions would only doom us too. Instead, with the distance between us and our attacker beginning to extend, we did our best not to slow down for even a second.
entries.new: 卫生间的门虽然可以从里面上锁，但 Katei 说过，他的钥匙能打开所有卫生间。追我们的十有八九就是杀他的凶手——那把钥匙，对方可能已经捡走，也可能回监控室去取。{w} 躲进隔间只会让我们也送命。眼下我们和对方的距离正渐渐拉开，我们拼尽全力，一秒也不敢放慢。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Let's go to the attic...!
entries.new: 去阁楼……！
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: In a hoarse voice, I let out what I'd intended to be reassurance. I'd realized our only chance relied on the attic: the key should've still been there, so if we could keep the same pace until we arrived at the door, we'd have enough time to lock ourselves inside.
entries.new: 我用沙哑的嗓音喊了一句，本意是想让她安心。我已明白，我们唯一的生路就在阁楼——钥匙应该还在那里，只要保持这个速度撑到门前，就有时间把自己反锁在里面。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Once more, we forced our exhausted bodies up the floor 5 staircase while the adrenaline's effect started to wear off. I desperately needed to slow down, but I pushed myself more than I'd ever thought I could. I wasn't going to die; I rejected that thought more than anything.
entries.new: 肾上腺素的效力开始消退，我们又一次拖着精疲力竭的身体爬上通往五楼的楼梯。我非常想慢下来喘口气，却逼着自己跑得比任何时候都拼命。我不能死——我最抗拒的就是这个念头。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I grabbed Shiroya's hand again and sprinted toward the offices. We hadn't come to the tower to die! It had been the complete opposite!
entries.new: 我再次抓住 Shiroya 的手，朝办公区飞奔。我们来这座塔，可不是为了送命！恰恰相反！
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Almost four hours remained, and the footfalls behind us continually warned us how badly someone wanted us dead. Despite their lower speed, they were still running.
entries.new: 还剩将近四个小时，身后的脚步声不断提醒我们，有人多么迫切地想要我们的命。对方速度虽然不快，却始终没有停下奔跑。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We had to go to the attic—that was our only way to survive. Somehow, the culprit had a knife.
entries.new: 必须去阁楼——那是我们唯一活下去的办法。不知为何，凶手手里有刀。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As soon as I considered how nonsensical that was, a flash of Erina's death came to me. There had been a bloodstain on her chest, and although we hadn't inspected it, the same knife had surely taken her life.
entries.new: 我刚想到这有多荒谬，Erina 死时的景象便闪过脑海。她胸口有一处血迹，虽然我们没细看，但多半就是同一把刀夺走了她的性命。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The last staircase we'd have to power through was in reach. Shiroya's body began to tremble as a sign of how much she'd pushed herself to escape from the danger of death.
entries.new: 最后一段要咬牙冲过去的楼梯已经近在眼前。Shiroya 的身体开始发抖，那是她为了活命拼尽全力的迹象。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Only one more... We'll lock ourselves up in the attic!
entries.new: 只剩一段了……我们进阁楼里把门锁上！
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: My mind started to feel numb as soon as I spat out some words. She nodded almost imperceptibly while the terrifying echo of our persistent attacker refused to fade.
entries.new: 我勉强挤出几个字，脑子就开始发麻。她几乎难以察觉地点了点头，而身后紧追不舍的凶手那可怕的脚步声始终不肯消散。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stepped up the stairs, unable to match our prior pace. Our bodies couldn't withstand much more.{w} As much as I tried to keep up for just a few more seconds, my legs were barely responding. Seeing how the same thing was happening to Shiroya, I feared that our lack of sleep would finally catch up to us.
entries.new: 我迈上楼梯，却已经跟不上先前的速度。我们的身体撑不了多久了。{w} 我拼命想再撑几秒，双腿却几乎不听使唤。看到 Shiroya 也是同样的样子，我担心缺觉的恶果终于要找上门来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I hadn't been able to see the body of the attacker, but there weren't many options. They were chasing us with a knife, so we weren't going to die without knowing our killer's identity.
entries.new: 我没能看清袭击者的身形，但可能的人也就那么几个。对方拿着刀追我们，我们绝不能连凶手是谁都不知道就死在这里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We stepped onto the sixth floor and resumed what could no longer be called running, but a forced stagger. Fortunately, our pursuer seemed to be in similar shape, as they hadn't used our exhaustion to catch up despite their continuous, audible steps.
entries.new: 我们踏上六楼，继续向前，但那已经称不上奔跑，只是勉强的踉跄。所幸追赶者似乎也好不到哪里去——脚步声虽然一直清晰可闻，对方却没能趁我们力竭追上来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's still there!
entries.new: 还在！
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The attic's door was open, and I could see the shining key placed in it. Merely wishing not to faint, we forced a last sprint as we heard the noise behind us growing louder.
entries.new: 阁楼的门开着，我能看见那把闪亮的钥匙插在上面。我们只求别昏过去，拼命做最后的冲刺，身后的声响却越来越大。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My body had already given out, but thankfully too late to spell disaster for me. I took the key and entered the narrow staircase with Shiroya right behind me. As fast as I could, I shut the door and inserted the key in the inner keyhole. With a trembling hand, I turned and locked it. As soon as the tumbler clicked, I stopped trying to control my body and collapsed between the two walls.
entries.new: 我的身体早已到了极限，好在是得救之后才垮掉。我取下钥匙，钻进狭窄的楼梯间，Shiroya 紧跟在后。我尽快关上门，把钥匙插进内侧的锁孔，用发抖的手转动锁上。锁芯咔哒一响，我便再也撑不住，瘫倒在两侧墙壁之间。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Are you okay?
entries.new: ……你没事吧？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We spent a full minute catching our breath, during which no other sound reached our ears. Even though we'd achieved our only available goal, in instance that whoever it was had another key to the attic, there'd be nothing we could do.
entries.new: 我们花了一整分钟才喘匀气，这期间再没有别的声音传进耳朵。虽然我们达成了唯一可行的目标，但万一对方也有一把阁楼的钥匙，我们便无计可施了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I-I'm fine... Let's go up.
entries.new: 我、我没事……上去吧。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I stood up as soon as I felt able to. Still staggering, we began walking up the stairs to distance ourselves as much as possible from the door. The culprit hadn't even tried to open it after chasing us the entire way up, which made it all even more unsettling.
entries.new: 觉得能动了，我便站了起来。我们依旧踉跄着往楼梯上走，尽量离那扇门远一些。凶手一路追到这里，却连试着开门都没有，这反倒更加令人不安。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You didn't see their face, right?
entries.new: 你没看到对方的脸吧？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: No... I only saw a knife coming out of the corridor, and I think their sleeve was black. They must've had it hidden somewhere.
entries.new: 没有……我只看到一把刀从走廊那边伸出来，袖子的颜色好像是黑的。那把刀一定是藏在什么地方带进来的。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I'm not sure... but it could only be Akaro or Sai. I found out earlier that I run faster than Sai, which I very much doubt is the case with Akaro...
entries.new: 我不确定……但只可能是 Akaro 或 Sai。我之前发现自己跑得比 Sai 快，但要是 Akaro，我恐怕就未必跑得过了。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It... has to be him, then.
entries.new: 那……就只能是他了。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I didn't know what to think. Someone had really tried to take my life when I had done nothing. Was I a threat, or were they just a psychopath...? If it was Sai, I couldn't honestly decide.
entries.new: 我不知道该怎么想。我什么都没做，却真的有人想要我的命。是我碍了谁的事，还是对方根本就是个疯子……？如果那人是 Sai，我实在无法判断。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't know, but we might be safe here.
entries.new: 我不知道，不过待在这里也许安全。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I looked by my feet. No new footprints had been left since the last time we'd looked at the floor.
entries.new: 我低头看了看脚边。自从上次查看地面以来，没有新的脚印。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There's supposed to be only one key for this place, but who can really tell... Duplication is a trivial matter at this point.
entries.new: 这里按理说只有一把钥匙，可谁知道呢……到了这一步，复制一把根本不算什么难事。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: At least if they haven't made a duplicate yet, they won't be able to do it now. We could be all right...
entries.new: 至少如果他们还没复制，现在也做不到了。说不定我们真的没事……
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I'm... not sure. If this is the same culprit who's been using the Sekimeiya all this time, I'm certain they'd have a way to replicate the key even if we have it with us.{w} If it's Sai, he could go back to the past and replicate his body during a time he was holding it.
entries.new: 我……没把握。如果对方就是一直使用 Sekimeiya 的那个凶手，那就算钥匙在我们手上，他多半也有办法复制一把。{w} 要是 Sai 的话，他只要回到过去，在自己还拿着钥匙的时候复制身体就行了。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The pale fear projected on her face for a single instant was more than soul-crushing. I'd been with her for so many years and never seen anything like it—not even recently.
entries.new: 她脸上一瞬间闪过的惨白恐惧，几乎要把人的心都碾碎。我和她相识这么多年，从没见过她这样——就连最近这段日子也没有。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That was why I didn't voice the much more frightening way the culprit could make their way in. By traveling from the future, they could deliberately materialize themselves in the attic if their location was simply based on a time they'd been there.
entries.new: 所以我没有说出那个更可怕的潜入方式。如果传送的位置只取决于过去待过的某个时间，凶手就能从未来穿越过来，直接让自己出现在阁楼里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Let's make sure we're alone.
entries.new: 确认一下这里只有我们吧。
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yeah...
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: No matter who the attacker had been, two people would still be unaccounted for between Sai, Akaro, and the other Shiroya. We'd been in the attic just a couple minutes earlier, but it wasn't impossible that someone else had also been present at the time.
entries.new: 不管袭击者是谁，Sai、Akaro 和另一个 Shiroya 三个人里，总还有两个人下落不明。几分钟前我们就在阁楼里，当时还有别人在场也并非不可能。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We quietly walked around while a piercing feeling invaded my chest. Erina and Katei had recently died. I was barely able to accept it, and their killer had shifted to targeting us, the last people remaining.
entries.new: 我们悄声在阁楼里查看，一阵刺痛涌上胸口。Erina 和 Katei 刚刚死去，我几乎还无法接受，而杀害他们的凶手已经把目标转向了我们——最后活着的两个人。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I truly hoped that, at {time=21}, the police would come. I needed to get out with Shiroya at that time. There was no way I could make it even a second longer without breaking down.
entries.new: 我真心盼着{time=21}警察能来。我必须在那时和 Shiroya 一起离开这里。再多撑一秒，我都会崩溃。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...My heart still racing, I went to the hallway through the kitchen and looked at the storeroom while Shiroya stayed in the corner. After I'd seen the empty bathroom, we'd isolated the two bedrooms.
entries.new: ……我心跳还没平复，便穿过厨房走进走廊，查看储藏室，Shiroya 留在角落。确认卫生间没有人之后，我们要查的就只剩两间卧室了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'll go up the ladder. Stay here.
entries.new: 我爬梯子上去看看，你待在这儿。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: She came to the two parallel doors and watched me while I climbed up the ladder in the rightmost bedroom. I was easily able to confirm nobody was hiding.
entries.new: 她来到那两扇并排的门前，看着我爬上最右边卧室的梯子。我很容易就确认了里面没人藏着。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I repeated the process in the opposite one to conclude that we were the only people in the attic.
entries.new: 我在对面那间照做了一遍，最终确定整座阁楼里只有我们两个。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya joined me inside. Our lives were at risk of being cut short, but we couldn't do anything else. She sat on a bed, knowing that we were possibly in the path of an unstoppable force.
entries.new: Shiroya 也进了房间。我们的性命随时可能被截断，却别无他法。她坐在床上，心里明白我们也许正挡在一股无法阻挡的力量面前。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But life took no pity on us. Before we could speak any words, a heart-stopping sound came from the hallway. Through a terrified whisper, Shiroya's raw anguish tore at the foundations of my will. The sound had made it clear: we were dealing with the real culprit, who had been able to enter our makeshift fortress. Trying to escape was futile.
entries.new: 可命运并未怜悯我们。我们还没来得及开口，走廊里就传来一声令人心脏骤停的响动。Shiroya 一声恐惧的低语，那赤裸的绝望几乎撼动了我意志的根基。那声音已经说明了一切：我们面对的是真正的凶手，对方能够闯进我们临时搭起的堡垒。逃跑已经没有意义。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But I couldn't think of anything else. During the few seconds in which the approaching footsteps grew louder, only a single course of action came to me.
entries.new: 可我再也想不出别的办法。在那脚步声越来越近的几秒里，我脑中只浮现出一个选择。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The key...! We need to lock ourselves in again!
entries.new: 钥匙……！得再把自己锁起来！
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: An equally terrified whisper came from within me. I rushed to the drawers, where the key to the bedroom should've been. The bedroom we were in didn't have a chain, and crossing the hallway was too risky.
entries.new: 我内心也涌起同样恐惧的低语。我冲到抽屉前，卧室的钥匙本该放在那里。我们所在的卧室没有门链，穿过走廊又太过冒险。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What!?{w} It's not here!
entries.new: 什么！？{w} 不在这儿！
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The bathroom's door was opened and closed; the culprit was searching for us. Within my panic, I remembered it. Sai had tried to use that bedroom's key to unlock the opposite door, and we hadn't seen where he left it afterward.
entries.new: 卫生间的门被打开又关上，凶手正在逐个搜寻我们。慌乱之中，我想起来了——Sai 曾用那间卧室的钥匙去开对面的门，之后我们没看见他把钥匙放在了哪儿。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Another door was opened. It wasn't ours, but the one in front, leading to the bedroom where we'd spent more than an hour locked inside.
entries.new: 又有一扇门被打开了。不是我们这扇，而是前面那扇——通往卧室的门，我们曾在里面被锁了足足一个多小时。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Fuck! We could shut the culprit inside with the key, but entering to get it might be too dangerous.
entries.new: 该死！我们本可以用钥匙把凶手关在里面，可要进去拿钥匙，未免太冒险了。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: ...We need to leave!
entries.new: ……我们得走了！
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: As I said that, I took my shoes off and gestured at Shiroya to quickly do the same. We'd been able to hear the approaching culprit because of their shoes. Without them, walking on wood would be almost imperceptible.
entries.new: 话音未落，我便脱下鞋，示意 Shiroya 也赶紧照做。我们能听见凶手逼近，是因为他们穿着鞋。赤脚踩在木地板上，几乎听不出声响。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked through the door and heard movements coming from the other bedroom. We didn't have much time. Shiroya and I nodded at each other and left while making the least amount of noise possible, holding our shoes with our hands.
entries.new: 我透过门缝张望，听见另一间卧室里传来动静。时间不多了。我和 Shiroya 对了个眼神，手里拎着鞋，尽可能不出一点声地离开。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We approached the living room and began to increase our speed. The culprit had somehow entered the attic, but we didn't know their method. If they'd taken the elevator, it was likely still there, but we couldn't afford the risk of waiting for it to arrive.
entries.new: 接近客厅时，我们加快了脚步。凶手不知怎么进了阁楼。如果是乘电梯上去的，电梯多半还停在那儿，可我们冒不起等它下来的风险。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Without giving it much thought, we entered the living room. As soon as we did, the dry noise of footsteps on wood froze us in place again.
entries.new: 我们没多想，便踏进了客厅。刚进去，木地板上那干涩的脚步声又让我们僵在了原地。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They were coming to us. Instead of entering the other bedroom, very faint footsteps were approaching the living room, where we were.
entries.new: 他们朝我们来了。那极轻的脚步声没有进另一间卧室，而是直奔我们所在的客厅。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait.
entries.new: 等等。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: No, we can't rush out.{w} We might be going up against Sai, and he wouldn't let us escape like this. If he entered the attic with another key, he could be luring us to the staircase.
entries.new: 不，不能就这么冲出去。{w} 对手也许是 Sai，他不会让我们这样轻易脱身。如果他另有一把钥匙进了阁楼，那多半是在把我们往楼梯口引。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: We'd been so desperate that I'd left our key on the floor, next to the attic door. If Sai had managed to enter and then locked the door... If he'd also picked up our key, we couldn't leave, and we would just corner ourselves by walking down the stairs.
entries.new: 方才情急之下，我把钥匙落在了阁楼门边的地板上。要是 Sai 已经进去了，又把门锁上……要是他顺手捡走了我们的钥匙，我们就出不去了，顺着楼梯往下走，只会把自己逼进死角。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I glanced down and saw footprints that didn't belong to us. Our pursuer had definitely walked across the carpet after our arrival.
entries.new: 我低头一看，地毯上有不属于我们的脚印。追我们的人，确实是在我们到达之后才踩过这块地毯。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The terror locked my muscles in place. While the sound got closer, I began to explore the thought of attacking the culprit as soon as they entered the living room.
entries.new: 恐惧让我的身体动弹不得。脚步声越来越近，我开始盘算：等凶手一进客厅，就扑上去。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Fuck! Why didn't I think about this!? They have a knife, and I can't just tell Shiroya to help me!
entries.new: 该死！我怎么没想到这一点！？对方手里有刀，我又不能直接叫 Shiroya 来帮我！
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: W-We can't go that way.
entries.new: 不、不能往那边走。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: She'd been telling me to hurry up with her eyes, but that could've sealed our fates. I grabbed her available hand and dashed to the kitchen.
entries.new: 她一直用眼神催我快点，可那会要了我们的命。我攥住她空着的那只手，直奔厨房。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What are you doing...!?
entries.new: 你干什么……！？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Trying to leave through the main door didn't sound right, but we might've already been done for. The only other way out, the elevator, was no guarantee either.{w} The person behind us had waited a couple minutes before making their entrance, so if they'd used that time to disable the elevator below us, we were completely trapped.
entries.new: 从大门出去似乎行不通，可我们或许早已无路可走。唯一的另一个出口，电梯，同样未必可行。{w}身后那人等了几分钟才现身，要是他们利用那段时间弄停了我们下面的电梯，我们就彻底被困死了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: From the kitchen, we heard the living room's door being opened. We had to make our move.
entries.new: 厨房里，我们听见客厅的门被推开了。必须行动了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If they look at the footprints, it's possible they could see that we're in the kitchen. We have to get out of here.
entries.new: 要是他们看脚印，说不定能看出我们躲在厨房。得马上离开这里。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: But a different thought came to me. If they recognized the footprints and anticipated our actions, they could wait in the hallway, knowing we'd immediately leave.{w} It was too late, as I'd already grabbed Shiroya's hand, and I wasn't able to stop mine from turning the handle of the door.
entries.new: 可我又想到另一种可能。如果对方认出了脚印，料准了我们的行动，就会守在走廊里，等着我们自投罗网。{w}已经太迟了——我早已抓住 Shiroya 的手，也拦不住自己那只手去转动门把。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The hallway was empty, but we could see the open door to the living room. With very little time to think, I could only come up with two courses of action.
entries.new: 走廊空无一人，但客厅那扇敞开的门看得清清楚楚。留给思考的时间太少，我只想出两条路。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Do we go to the other bedroom where we can lock the door, or do we try to use the elevator!?
entries.new: 是去另一间卧室把门锁上，还是赌一把电梯！？
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I couldn't decide. Once again, I considered that we were potentially up against Sai, who'd taken some time to think up a strategy specifically so that we couldn't run away. He would have thought far enough ahead to disable the elevator below us.
entries.new: 我拿不定主意。我再次想到，对手很可能是 Sai——他特意花时间谋划，就是为了让我们逃不掉。他一定早已想到要弄停我们下面的电梯。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But... he just left the bedroom, and earlier, I put the key inside the drawer where we'd found it. What if he just took it, and going there will trap us as well?
entries.new: 可是……他刚从卧室出来，而先前我把钥匙放回了我们找到它的那个抽屉里。万一他顺手把钥匙拿走了，那我们过去，也一样是自投罗网？
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: We had the chain, but it was unreliable. We'd seen how Akaro burst through it in five seconds. Not only that, but even though we were supposed to possess the single key to the attic, someone had managed to make their way in. The same thing could repeat in the bedroom.{w} Earlier, Akaro and Sai had escaped with its key, and we knew they'd then activated the Sekimeiya in some way. It was possible they'd produced a spare key already.
entries.new: 我们有门链，但那靠不住。我们都见过 Akaro 只用五秒就撞断了它。更何况，阁楼的钥匙本该只有一把、就在我们手里，却仍有人进了去。同样的事，在卧室也可能重演。{w}先前 Akaro 和 Sai 带着卧室的钥匙逃走，而我们知道他们随后以某种方式启动了 Sekimeiya。说不定他们早已造出了一把备用钥匙。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: L-Let's try the elevator. Trying to call it is all we can do. If it doesn't come, we'll have to leave.
entries.new: 还、还是试试电梯吧。能做的也只有试着把它叫上来。要是它不来，我们就只好另想办法出去。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Okay.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: My heartbeat running wild inside my ears almost drowned out our voices. The culprit hadn't entered the kitchen, meaning that they were either in the living room or the staircase. We'd have to pass through the open door to get to the elevator, so we had to hope they'd gone down the stairs and wouldn't see us.
entries.new: 我耳边狂跳的心跳声几乎盖过了我们的说话声。凶手没有进厨房，说明他们要么在客厅，要么在楼梯间。要去电梯，就必须经过那扇敞开的门，只能指望他们已经下了楼，不会看见我们。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In an instant, we were on the other side. I'd been able to glance through the door and seen an empty living room.
entries.new: 转眼之间，我们已到了另一侧。我趁隙往门里瞥了一眼，客厅空无一人。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We sped up toward the elevator, but I stopped myself as soon as I remembered something.
entries.new: 我们加快脚步奔向电梯，可想起某件事的瞬间，我又收住了脚。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Huh?
entries.new: 嗯？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: W-Wait... Th-This could be bad.
entries.new: 等、等等……这、这下不妙了。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Everything carried the threat of a trap, and even though we were in close proximity to a killer, we had to attempt to think rationally. We'd been instinctively running away to gain time, but we knew that was utterly pointless if every place was in reach of them. There was one goal we could strive for.
entries.new: 处处都可能是陷阱。纵使凶手近在咫尺，我们也必须冷静思考。我们一直凭本能逃跑，只为争取时间，可只要任何地方都在对方的掌握之中，这样做就毫无意义。我们还有一个目标可以去争取。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The noise behind us resumed. Again, the culprit was approaching.
entries.new: 身后的声响又起。凶手再次逼近。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We don't have time to run to the elevator and hope it's either here or functioning. This is definitely a trap.
entries.new: 我们没时间跑去电梯，再指望它正好停在这儿还能用。这绝对是个陷阱。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I opened the storeroom and dashed inside.
entries.new: 我拉开储藏室的门，闪身冲了进去。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Through the gap of the door, we could see the hallway. The sound of the culprit's movements still reached our ears, but it had become too hard to discern the way they were going.
entries.new: 透过门缝，能看见走廊。凶手的动静仍传进耳中，却已难以分辨他们朝哪个方向去了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They're not coming here.
entries.new: 他们没往这边来。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I think it's very possible that after we left the event room, the Sekimeiya was taken out. We have to rely on that and try to find it since we don't have the key to open the cabinet.
entries.new: 我觉得很可能在我们离开活动室之后，Sekimeiya 就被人取走了。我们只能靠这一点去找它——毕竟没有展示柜的钥匙。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: If we find it, we can choose a place to stay hidden until we're unavoidably found. Then, we can activate it.{w} If we go far into the past, we won't be able to think of ambushing the culprit knowing where they'll be since it'd contradict them finding us, but we could make it outside the tower if we're lucky enough.{w} If we travel to the recent past, we could find a new place to hide that this person had just looked at. It'd only be buying us more time, but it's better than having to confront someone with a knife or keep exhausting ourselves.
entries.new: 找到它，我们就能选个地方藏起来，一直撑到不得不被发现为止，然后再启动它。{w}若是回到很久以前，我们就不能靠知道凶手的行踪去埋伏——那样会和我们被他们发现这一点相矛盾，不过运气好的话，也许能跑到塔外去。{w}若是回到不久前，我们就能另找一处他刚刚搜过的地方藏身。那也不过是多拖些时间，但总好过跟一个拿着刀的人正面相对，或者把自己累垮。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: This has to work. On the third floor, our attacker was by the offices' corner and not in the staircase next to the elevator. That was either to watch us from afar or prevent us from going down to the crystal floor; they wanted to chase us up instead of down.
entries.new: 这次一定要成。在三楼时，袭击者守在办公室拐角，而不是电梯旁的楼梯间。那要么是为了远远盯着我们，要么是为了阻止我们下到水晶层——他们想逼我们往上跑，而不是往下。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: ...Eventually, every sound faded away, and we could only hear our shaking breaths. In the cramped storeroom, we had to prepare for what our next and most important move would be.
entries.new: ……到最后，所有声响都消失了，只剩下我们颤抖的呼吸。在这狭小的储藏室里，我们必须想好下一步——也是最关键的一步。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Why are they not moving anymore...? Are they waiting for us?
entries.new: 他们怎么不动了……？是在等我们出去吗？
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Should we try to call the elevator?
entries.new: 要不要试着叫电梯？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: N-No. I remembered how this all started when I stopped myself.{w} We were going down with the elevator and stopped on floor 3 because someone called it knowing we were inside. No matter who this is, at this point, they must've thought of disabling the elevator under us so that we can't use it to escape.
entries.new: 不、不行。我刚要动，就想起了这一切是怎么开始的。{w}当时我们乘电梯下行，却在三楼停下，因为有人明知我们在里面，还是按了电梯。不管对方是谁，到了这一步，他们一定想得到要把我们楼下的电梯停住，让我们没法靠它逃跑。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: If we called the elevator anyway and it came, it would definitely be a trap and they intend to do the same thing as before. As soon as we go down, they could call it.{w} The last time, they waited next to the offices, but this time, I'm sure they'd be right outside to make sure we can't continue moving.{w} Think about it, it's also possible we're dealing with both Akaro and Sai. If one of them is on a floor under us, they could be hoping we take the elevator and lose any way out.
entries.new: 就算我们按了，电梯真的上来，那也一定是个陷阱，他们打算故技重施。我们一旦下去，他们就能把电梯叫走。{w}上次他们守在办公室旁边，这一次，我敢肯定他们会直接守在门外，确保我们没法再移动。{w}你想想，对手也可能是 Akaro 和 Sai 两个人。只要其中一人在我们下面的楼层，他们就可能巴不得我们坐电梯，好让我们彻底断了退路。
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: But there's nothing else we can do, is there...?
entries.new: 可我们也没别的办法了吧……？
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Assuming the elevator hasn't been used again... it should still be on floor 3. If the culprit, or one of them, is waiting next to the floor 6 elevator and we call it from here, they'd hear it going up. Then, they'd know we'd be about to board it and use it, so they could call it to intercept us.
entries.new: 假设电梯没再被人用过……应该还停在3楼。要是犯人——或者他们中的某个人——正守在6楼电梯旁，而我们从这里叫梯，他们就会听见电梯升上去的动静。这样一来，他们便知道我们打算乘梯，可以先叫走电梯，截断我们的路。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I was experiencing the most unsettling silence possible. Waiting in the storeroom wasn't an option, so I could only find three:{w} trying to use the elevator to go down, trying to lock ourselves in a bedroom, and trying to leave the attic through the main door.
entries.new: 我从未体会过如此令人不安的寂静。守在储藏室不是办法，我能想到的只有三条路：{w}乘电梯下楼，躲进卧室反锁房门，或者从正门离开阁楼。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The person outside wasn't moving. They could've been close by or far away. Regardless, it was certain they'd thought of a course of action to apprehend us.
entries.new: 外面的人没有动静。他可能近在咫尺，也可能早已退远。但无论远近，他一定已经想好了抓我们的办法。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Why would they have stopped searching for us when it's certain we're in the attic?{w} ...It could mean they're working alone.
