entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I felt a deep unease at the concept of someone watching me from a distance. I couldn't understand why they would, and it put even more pressure on me.
entries.new: 一想到有人可能在远处盯着我，我就深感不安。我不明白对方为何要这样做，这让我更加喘不过气。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was still fairly hungry and far from my apartment, but if I went home in a straight line, I'd have to go through all the deserted streets before getting back to the center.{w} I didn't want to do that if someone was observing me in secret.
entries.new: 我还挺饿的，离家又远，可要是径直回家，就得先穿过那一整片冷清的街巷，才能回到市中心。{w} 若真有人在暗中窥视我，我可不想走那条路。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was close to the outskirts, so instead of going back, I kept on ahead.
entries.new: 我已经靠近城郊，索性没有折返，继续向前走去。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When the curved street came to an end and the short houses stopped, the sight to the tall mountains was wide open. I was at the start of the mountain range, close to the valley that led out of Yushibana.
entries.new: 弯曲的街道走到尽头，低矮的房屋也到了头，高耸的山峦豁然展现在眼前。我已来到山脉的起点，离那条通往丰花之外的山谷不远了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I hadn't seen anyone yet, and there were barely any footprints around. If I'd been followed again, I had surely gone the opposite way.
entries.new: 我始终没见到半个人影，周围也几乎没有脚印。若这次又被人跟踪，那我肯定已经走了相反的路。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I spun in place, confirming again that nobody was there. I doubted anyone was watching me based on where I was. The only place they could be hiding was within some covered windows fairly far away.
entries.new: 我原地转了一圈，再次确认无人。看这地方，我不觉得会有人盯着我。对方若真要藏身，也只能躲进远处那些挂着窗帘的窗户后面。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Noticing the slight weight on my head, I shook off the snow piled on it. Then, I kept walking, my boots sinking deeply into the snow.
entries.new: 感到头顶微微压着分量，我甩掉了积在那里的雪，然后继续前行，靴子深深陷进雪里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The path outlining Yushibana was not well-maintained. Tall weeds dominated it, unfazed by the snow. I'd learned to avoid coming back from Atsuki's house through that route, as it tended to be hard to traverse.
entries.new: 环绕丰花的那条小路疏于打理，高高的杂草占了上风，全然不惧积雪。我早就学会绕开这条路，不从 Atsuki 家那边经它回来，因为它向来难走。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Ahead of me, I saw a thin path going up the mountain. Like the entire hill, it was coated in snow, but the lack of grass peeking up highlighted the way.
entries.new: 前方有一条细窄的小径通向山上。它和整座山坡一样覆着白雪，只因没有杂草冒头，反倒显出了路的轮廓。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I reached the split and instinctively took the path up the large mountain.
entries.new: 来到岔路口，我下意识地走上了通往大山的那条路。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Due to another impulse, I found myself climbing the steep path, leaving behind the straight and plain one. I knew it would level out soon and lead home despite taking longer.
entries.new: 又是一时冲动，我撇下那条笔直平坦的路，沿陡坡向上爬去。我知道这条路很快便会平缓下来，虽然绕远，终究还是通向家里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: All around me, I could only see dried bushes covered in white and tall trees scattered around. I knew the mountains were frequently visited, but I couldn't make out any indications of people having been there.
entries.new: 四下望去，只能看见覆着白雪的枯灌木，还有零星散布的高大树木。我知道这座山常有人来，却看不出任何有人涉足的痕迹。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd turned to that path due to the conversation I'd had with Atsuki in one of the hallway A crystal rooms. It had been so long since both of us had taken that path, but walking up all by myself was still somehow familiar.
entries.new: 我之所以会走上这条路，是因为在 A 走廊的一间水晶展室里和 Atsuki 的那次交谈。我们俩已经很久没走过这条路了，可独自一人爬上来，竟仍有种说不出的熟悉。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Would we ever go up together again? That was also something I had to choose.
entries.new: 我们还有机会一起上去吗？这也是我必须做出的选择。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The wind was noticeably stronger higher up. The terrain there was plain, and the way branched out.{w} Higher still was the entrance to the caves, whereas the path to the right would take me close to home.
entries.new: 越往高处，风明显越强。那里地势平坦，道路分了岔。{w}再往上便是洞穴入口，而右边的路则能通到我家附近。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I turned around to witness the sight I'd earned.
entries.new: 我转过身，去看这份辛苦换来的景色。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The entirety of Yushibana covered by snow... The sight was as pleasant as it had always been, intensified by the moving curtain of falling flakes, which appeared much denser from above.
entries.new: 整个丰花都被雪覆盖……这景象一如往常那样令人心旷神怡，而纷纷扬扬的落雪如帘幕般流动，从高处看去更显密集，又为它添了几分韵味。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked at the way I'd come from, but even from that position, I wasn't able to see anyone. Only when I peered at the center of town was I able to notice the tiny movements of people on the streets.
entries.new: 我望向来时的路，可即便站在这个位置，也看不见半个人影。直到凝神望向镇中心，才辨出街上行人细小的动静。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There wasn't a place I couldn't see. The hospital was close to where I was, most of its windows covered from within. In the distance, the Zubesout Trash Disposal looked like a perfect circle, appearing as elegant as every other place thanks to the snow.
entries.new: 没有哪里是我看不到的。医院就在离我不远的地方，大部分窗户从里面遮了起来。远处，Zubesout 垃圾处理场看上去是个完美的圆形，积雪让它和其他地方一样显得雅致。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And of course, close to it, Ashiya Tower. It was rare to see the top of it, but the snow almost made it blend in completely.
entries.new: 当然，还有近旁的芦屋塔。平时很难看清塔顶，可积雪几乎把它整个融进了白茫茫的一片。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked down to its entrance. I could just barely make it out despite the distance and whirls of snow, but there was no shutter in place.
entries.new: 我俯视它的入口。隔着这段距离和漫天飞雪，我只能勉强辨认，但那里并没有落下卷帘门。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Despite the harsh wind hitting my face, I kept watching with both hands in my pockets, trying not to let the snow fall inside.
entries.new: 寒风扑在脸上，我双手插在口袋里，仍一直望着，生怕雪落进去。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A very important decision still needed to be made, and even ignoring that decision was its own decision. Was there going to be a better time? As soon as I asked myself that, I knew the answer.
entries.new: 还有一个极其重要的决定等着我去做，而即便对它置之不理，本身也是一种决定。还会有更合适的时机吗？这个问题刚在心里浮现，我就知道了答案。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Would I try to alter the fate of the town, trapped in a shrouded sequence of events revolving around a magical gemstone?
entries.new: 我要不要去改变这座小镇的命运？它被一连串围绕着一颗魔法宝石、笼罩在迷雾之中的事件困住了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Would I try to save Miiya and the people I'd met that day at the cost of my own normal life? Even if I succeeded, I would have to keep on living in circumstances I couldn't even fathom.
entries.new: 我要不要豁出自己平静的生活，去救 Miiya 和那天遇见的那些人？就算成功了，我也得在无法想象的处境里继续活下去。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had felt like I'd been living in a mire, and when I was finally pulled out of it, I lost everything. The incident in the tower had only made things worse, and I'd finally been saved from it only to be subsequently forced into destroying my own life as the "right" answer.
entries.new: 我总觉得自己一直陷在泥沼里，而当我终于被拉出来时，却失去了一切。塔里那起事件只是让一切更糟；我好不容易从中脱身，转头却又被迫以毁掉自己的人生作为「正确」的答案。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't know if I could accomplish it, but the choice was about whether to try it. I could be caught by the police or be beaten to the punch by someone else from the future. If the latter happened, I was letting it happen by not acting. It was my own fault.{w} It was all a mess, and there was no way not to make it one. I wanted to talk to Miiya again, but even if I saved her, that wouldn't happen.{w} She hadn't deserved to die, so I could trade positions with her. I wouldn't even be doing it for some twisted form of recognition, as nobody would know what had happened—my other self would exist in my place, and I'd step aside.
entries.new: 我不知道自己能否做到，但这个选择的关键只在于要不要去尝试。我可能被警察抓住，也可能被另一个来自未来的人抢先一步。若是后者，那也等于我袖手旁观、任由它发生，怪不得别人。{w}一切都乱成一团，而且无论如何都注定会乱。我想再和 Miiya 说说话，可就算救了她，这也办不到。{w}她本不该死，那么我可以和她互换位置。我这么做甚至不是为了某种扭曲的认可——没有人会知道发生了什么；另一个我会取代我的位置，而我退到一旁。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked at the tower, knowing the Sekimeiya was inside.{w} Who else in that town knew about what had happened on the 15th? I wished I could know that.
entries.new: 我望着那座塔，知道 Sekimeiya 就在里面。{w}这座镇子上，还有谁知道15号那天发生了什么？我真希望能知道。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I just have to go in, find where the Sekimeiya is, and check if I can open the door in the storeroom. I just have to do that, determine what I can do, and enter again during the night.
entries.new: 我只要进去，找到 Sekimeiya 在哪里，再确认自己能否打开储藏室的门。只要做完这些，弄清自己能做什么，然后夜里再进去一趟就行。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But that wasn't the problem. I would only go back to the tower after knowing whether I truly wanted the past to change.
entries.new: 可问题不在这里。只有在弄清自己是否真的想让过去改变之后，我才会再回那座塔。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So, would I attempt to alter the hellish world I'd experienced at the cost of the life I'd always had, or would I give up on using the Sekimeiya again, accepting the cards we'd been dealt to create the best future we had at hand?
entries.new: 那么，我是要拿自己一直以来的生活作代价，去改变那个我亲身经历过的地狱般的世界；还是放弃再次使用 Sekimeiya，接受已经拿到的牌，用这手牌尽力打出最好的未来？
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Step aside and wait out the days.
entries.new: 退到一旁，等这些日子过去。

entries.text: Try to change the past.
entries.new: 试着改变过去。

entries.text: Mirage
entries.new: 蜃景

entries.text: That was the answer. She wasn't disappointed in herself or sad about what would come. ...Shiroya was relieved to know that she'd made a decision.
entries.new: 那就是答案。她没有对自己失望，也没有为即将到来的一切感到悲伤。……知道自己已经做出了决定，Shiroya 反倒松了口气。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She didn't know what would happen from there. Would Ashiya Tower be locked up for an entire month? If so, then it seemed hard to believe the storeroom door would work to free the remaining people.
entries.new: 她不知道接下来会发生什么。芦屋塔会被封锁整整一个月吗？若真如此，那储藏室的门还能否奏效、把剩下的人放出来，就实在难以指望了。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: What that meant was that she had a few days for herself. Immediately after that, Shiroya didn't know what shape the future would take, but she believed that she and Atsuki would get through it. Her goal was solely to enjoy the remaining time she had.{w} Despite that, seeing a bustling street while she walked down the mountain, she only felt empty.
entries.new: 这意味着，她还有几天属于自己的时间。之后会变成什么样，Shiroya 无从知晓，但她相信自己和 Atsuki 能撑过去。她的目标仅仅是好好享受剩下的时光。{w}然而，下山途中看着街上熙熙攘攘，她心里却只觉得空落落的。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: At least, that was hypothetically what would have happened. However, it simply wasn't to be.
entries.new: 至少，那只是假想中会发生的情形。然而，事情偏偏没有那样发展。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: More precisely, her surroundings at that moment didn't remotely resemble a mountain.
entries.new: 准确说来，她此刻身处的环境与山间没有半点相似之处。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: They were dark and eerie. The person closest to her was someone she'd never spoken with.
entries.new: 四周幽暗而诡异。离她最近的那个人，她从未与之交谈过。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Why...?
entries.new: 为什么……？
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: This world has not been frozen, but modified for convenience and familiarity. Ordinarily, this shape would be unlikely to be constructed, but it is needed to emphasize certain aspects.
entries.new: 这个世界并没有被冻结，而是为了方便和熟悉做了改动。通常来说，不会构造出这样的形态，但为了突出某些方面，它又是必要的。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...Where is Shiroya now, and how did she get there?
entries.new: ……Shiroya 现在在哪里？她又是怎么到那儿的？
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Shiroya had traveled fifteen days through time and found herself underground.
entries.new: Shiroya 穿越了十五天的时间，最后发现自己身处地下。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Her decision would end up being not to attempt to change history, never entering Ashiya Tower again. Naturally, at this point, she didn't know that.
entries.new: 她最终的决定，是不去尝试改变历史，从此再也不踏进芦屋塔。当然，此时的她还不知道这一点。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: After exiting the inclined tunnel, she saw the entirety of Yushibana, the sun long since fallen behind the horizon.
entries.new: 走出那条倾斜的隧道后，整个丰花尽收眼底，太阳早已落到地平线之下。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She wandered through the dim streets, arriving at the shop where the explosion had occurred. Feeling extremely beaten down and ultimately unaware of what had happened, she walked to her apartment.
entries.new: 她在昏暗的街道上漫无目的地走着，来到那家发生爆炸的店铺前。她疲惫到了极点，也始终不知道究竟发生了什么，就这样走回了自己的公寓。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She had been in the tower only minutes ago, where she'd discussed using the Sekimeiya one more time with the hope that the past could really be changed. At home, however, she hurried to her bed, where she lay with the clothes that had been dampened so long ago.
entries.new: 几分钟前她还在塔里，谈论着再一次使用 Sekimeiya，指望过去真的能够改变。可一回到家，她便匆匆扑到床上，穿着那身在许久以前被打湿的衣服躺下。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The next day, she felt the urge to leave her apartment. It was noon, as she'd slept for a very long time. Outside, though, what would happen? Would anyone call her out for having come from the future?
entries.new: 第二天，她很想走出公寓。她睡了很久，醒来已是正午。可到了外面，又会怎样？会不会有人指责她是从未来回来的？
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She wandered mindlessly, witnessing the life that had once disappeared around her.
entries.new: 她漫无目的地游荡，看着周遭曾经消失的生活重新回到眼前。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: And she ended up at the entrance to Ina Café, where she would surely be recognized. However, she suddenly stopped when a note stuck to the shutter caught her notice.
entries.new: 最后，她来到了伊娜咖啡馆门前——在那里她一定会被认出来。然而，贴在卷帘门上的一张纸条忽然吸引了她的注意，她停住了脚步。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It was on top of the drawing of a coffee mug she'd never seen. She got closer and read what it said.
entries.new: 纸条贴在一幅她从未见过的咖啡杯图案上方。她凑近去看上面写了什么。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "We apologize, but due to personal matters, we will be closed most days of the week. We hope this will only last for a short time."
entries.new: 「很抱歉，因个人事务，本店一周的大部分日子暂停营业。希望这只是暂时的。」
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Shiroya could hardly believe what she'd read. In many years, she'd never seen Ina closed, and even though the note was written in plural, she knew the person who'd written it had to be the one who worked there almost every day.
entries.new: Shiroya 几乎不敢相信自己读到的东西。这么多年，她从没见过伊娜咖啡馆关门；尽管纸条上用的是复数措辞，她也知道写这张纸条的，一定是那个几乎每天都在店里工作的人。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Was it the universe's warning, telling her that she wasn't allowed to be seen? Perhaps Darfee seeing her would have created an impossibility that the universe had prevented.
entries.new: 这是不是宇宙给她的警告，告诉她不该被人看见？也许 Darfee 见到她会引发某种不可能，而宇宙已经阻止了它。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: After staring at the note for a long time, she walked away. Hesitant to step into the busy crowd, she went the opposite way, wondering about the cause of Darfee's absence.
entries.new: 盯着那张纸条看了许久，她才转身离开。她不愿走进熙攘的人群，便朝相反的方向走去，心里想着 Darfee 究竟为何不在。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She hadn't visited the café in a long time, so she didn't know how long that note had been there. No matter the reason, she felt a little worried for Darfee, who'd always been kind to her.
entries.new: 她很久没来过这家咖啡馆，所以不知道那张纸条贴了多久。无论原因是什么，她都有些担心 Darfee——那个人一向待她很亲切。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Just what should she do...? She hadn't eaten much, so her head started to feel a little cloudy.
entries.new: 她究竟该怎么办……？没吃多少东西，脑袋渐渐有些发昏。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Distracted, she jumped when a sudden noise came from behind her.
entries.new: 她正心神不宁，身后冷不防传来一声响，惊得她浑身一颤。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She turned around and saw a still car in the middle of the road. Its driver burst out and dashed to the front.{w} "Oh my God! Are you okay!? Hey...!"
entries.new: 她回过头，只见路中央停着一辆一动不动的车。司机冲下车，直奔车头。{w}「天哪！你没事吧！？喂……！」
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: From farther ahead, Shiroya stared, terrified. However, a parked car prevented her from seeing what was on the snowy asphalt.
entries.new: Shiroya 在更前方，惊恐地望着这边，可一辆停着的车挡住了她的视线，她看不见积雪的柏油路面上是什么。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "What the fuck!? I barely tapped him! Don't fucking tell me...!"{w} What had happened wasn't a mystery; Shiroya was stunned into immobility. As a handful of bystanders ran to the car, she desperately wished that no one's life had been lost.
entries.new: 「妈的！？我不过轻轻撞了他一下！别他妈告诉我……！」{w}出了什么事并不难猜；Shiroya 吓得动弹不得。几个路人朝车边跑去，她拼命祈祷没有人因此丧命。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Hey! ...Say something!{w} Come on! Say something!
entries.new: 「喂！……说句话啊！{w}拜托，说句话啊！」
entries.speaker: c5

entries.text: Those anguished cries continued ceaselessly and kept drawing nearby people in, forming a circle.
entries.new: 那凄厉的喊声一刻不停，不断把附近的人引过来，渐渐围成一圈。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: A few of them had phones by their ears, detailing the emergency to the proper officials with the hopeless voice of the driver in the background. Given the way everyone was acting, there was only one conclusion to draw.
entries.new: 有几个人把手机贴在耳边，向有关部门说明情况，背景里混着司机绝望的喊声。看众人的反应，结论只有一个。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: You've gotta be fucking kidding! ...Hey! Wake up!{w} Man! He just ran out in front of me! There was no way I could've stopped in time!{w} Come on, say something! Please!
entries.new: 「你他妈开什么玩笑！……喂！醒醒啊！{w}老天，是他自己冲到车前的！我根本来不及刹车！{w}快啊，说句话！求你了！」
entries.speaker: c5

entries.text: H-He's right, I saw it too. He suddenly crossed the road.{w} It looked like he started running when he saw her.
entries.new: 「他、他说得对，我也看见了。那个人突然横穿马路。{w}好像一看见她就跑了起来。」
entries.speaker: c5

entries.text: Out of nowhere, everyone turned to face the petrified Shiroya.
entries.new: 众人忽然齐齐转向僵立在那里的 Shiroya。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Wh...
entries.speaker: snn

entries.text: She stared back at the onlookers for long seconds, none of them moving.
entries.new: 她与围观的人群对视了好几秒，谁也没有动。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Finally, after she processed what she'd heard, she stepped forward and looked beyond the parked car.
entries.new: 终于，她明白过来，向前迈出几步，朝那辆停着的车后方望去。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Sure enough, she knew the person lying on the snow who was being forcefully shaken by his shoulders.
entries.new: 果然，她认得那个躺在雪地上、正被人抓着肩膀使劲摇晃的人。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Of course she did. On top of all the bright blood soaking into the snow was the person she knew most well. The person she'd gone to the tower with, and her last friend.
entries.new: 她当然认得。鲜红的血浸透了积雪，躺在血泊中的，是她最熟悉的人——曾与她一同前往芦屋塔的人，也是她最后的朋友。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: So when she saw his empty eyes, the sound of her heart thudding echoed inside her own body. Red and white blended into one, the entire world appearing drenched in his blood.
entries.new: 于是，当她看见他空洞的双眼时，自己擂鼓般的心跳声在体内回响。红与白融成一片，仿佛整个世界都被他的血浸透了。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It was absurd to think that scene made any sense. That thought barely managed to cross her mind.
entries.new: 眼前这一幕，怎么可能说得通。这个念头只勉强掠过她的脑海。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She hadn't wished the past to change at all, so why had it changed in the worst way possible?
entries.new: 她从未希望过去发生任何改变，可过去为什么偏偏以最坏的方式改变了？
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Soon, an ambulance came, but everyone was already aware it was futile.{w} The body was quickly placed on a stretcher and injected with a substance. Losing no time, he was brought in through the rear door of the vehicle, and it sped away.
entries.new: 不久，救护车赶到了，但所有人都明白已经无济于事。{w} 遗体很快被抬上担架，注射了某种药剂。救护人员片刻不停，把他从车尾门送进车内，车子随即疾驰而去。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: A swarm of people surrounded the bloodstain left behind, and they started to talk loudly as soon as the ambulance left.
entries.new: 一群人围住了留下的血迹，救护车刚一离开，他们便大声议论起来。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: On the ground, the broken driver stared downward. A few steps back, Shiroya did the same thing, rejecting what she'd witnessed.
entries.new: 司机瘫在地上，低头呆望着。几步之外，Shiroya 也低着头，不愿相信眼前发生的一切。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She had recently been forced to accept the cruelty of reality, but she hadn't been prepared for the same thing to happen again.{w} She denied it. She told herself that she'd mistaken his face or that everyone had failed to notice he'd still been alive. ...If everything was a dream, it would resolve all of her problems at once.
entries.new: 近来她已经被迫接受了现实的残酷，却还没准备好面对同样的事再次发生。{w} 她不愿承认。她告诉自己，是她认错了他的脸，或是所有人都没发现他其实还活着。……如果这一切都是梦，那她的所有问题便能一并解决。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: What's your name?
entries.new: 「你叫什么名字？」
entries.speaker: c5

entries.text: Shiroya heard someone addressing her. It had happened before when they'd noticed she knew the victim, but she hadn't replied. For that reason, she'd been left alone for a while.
entries.new: Shiroya 听见有人在问自己。之前也有人发现她认识死者，问过她同样的话，但她没有回答，所以有一阵子没人再来打扰她。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Answer me. What's your name?
entries.new: 「回答我。你叫什么名字？」
entries.speaker: c5

entries.text: But that voice persisted. When Shiroya moved her head, she saw a police officer staring at her with a serious expression.
entries.new: 可那个声音仍不依不饶。Shiroya 转过头，看见一名警察正神情严肃地盯着她。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...Sh-Shiroya.{w} Mirana.
entries.new: 「……Sh、Shiroya。{w}Mirana。」
entries.speaker: snn

entries.text: You'll have to come with us.
entries.new: 「你得跟我们走一趟。」
entries.speaker: c5

entries.text: ...Wh-Wha—
entries.speaker: snn

entries.text: Grabbed by the wrist, she was dragged to a police car with its door open.
entries.new: 有人抓住她的手腕，把她拽向一辆敞着门的警车。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Sit here.
entries.new: 「坐这儿。」
entries.speaker: c5

entries.text: The officer closed the door from the outside. Immediately, another officer opened the front door and sat in the driver seat.
entries.new: 警察从外面关上车门。紧接着，另一名警察打开前门，坐进驾驶座。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Shiroya had no strength to question anything, so when the engine started up and they began to drive away, she could only gaze at the fading group of people who'd seen the same thing she had.
entries.new: Shiroya 连质问的力气都没有。引擎发动，车子驶离原地，她只能望着那群渐渐远去的人——那些和她看到同一件事的人。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Days passed, and still confined, she remained unable to comprehend a single piece of what had happened.
entries.new: 几天过去，她仍被看管着，对所发生的一切还是完全无法理解。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It was many days later when Shiroya stepped on the snow again.
entries.new: 很多天后，Shiroya 才再次踏上雪地。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She had learned it with certainty: Atsuki had died on that day, instantly.
entries.new: 她已经确知：Atsuki 就在那一天当场身亡。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The incident of the 15th had already occurred, and in the distance, she could see Ashiya Tower.{w} It had been a while ago when she'd touched the Sekimeiya in the bathroom, but she hadn't set foot in that building again.
entries.new: 15日的事件早已发生，远处能望见芦屋塔。{w} 她在洗手间触碰到 Sekimeiya 已是许久之前的事，自那以后，她再没有踏进过那栋楼。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: And she wouldn't. It didn't matter anymore.
entries.new: 她也不会再踏进去了。一切都已经没有意义。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She didn't know where to find the Sekimeiya or what had happened to her life. The day she opened the door to her apartment again... was January 11th of 2012.
entries.new: 她不知道 Sekimeiya 的下落，也不知道自己的生活究竟出了什么变故。她再次推开公寓房门的那天……是2012年1月11日。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: What had happened on the 15th of December? She had heard about it.
entries.new: 12月15日究竟发生了什么？她听说过那件事。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: At {time=21}, the main shutter had unlocked. However, nobody had been found alive inside.
entries.new: {time=21}，主卷帘门打开了。然而，里面没有发现任何生还者。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Two people had been found dead. Their names were Naomi Cabca and Isla Majutsu.{w} Drops of blood that hadn't belonged to them had been found on the floor, but the whereabouts of the remaining people were a mystery. After raiding the building, the police had failed to find them.
entries.new: 有两具尸体被发现，分别是 Naomi Cabca 和 Isla Majutsu。{w} 地板上还找到了不属于她们的血迹，但其余人的下落仍是个谜。警方突入大楼搜查后，始终没能找到他们。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It had been soon confirmed that more people should've been there. Counting everyone who'd scanned their tickets in the entrance, the names of the people who hadn't evacuated were Atsuki Hakutoki, Shiroya Mirana, Sai Yomiya, Akaro Esata, and Erina Majutsu.{w} What had happened to them? It was impossible they had left the building during their twelve hours of imprisonment, as the whole structure had been observed from the outside since that morning.
entries.new: 很快便确认，本该有更多人留在里面。根据入口处所有验票记录，未撤离者分别是 Atsuki Hakutoki、Shiroya Mirana、Sai Yomiya、Akaro Esata 和 Erina Majutsu。{w} 他们究竟遭遇了什么？从那天早晨起，整栋建筑便一直处于外部监视之下，因此他们不可能在被困的十二小时里离开大楼。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The police concluded that Isla Majutsu, the second victim, had died many hours after {time=9.}{w} Yet, they had very few clues as to what had occurred. Almost all the recorded footage had been erased, and what remained was useless. The belongings of the two victims contained nothing of importance, and neither did any place in the building.{w} That only made things more confusing, because despite the belief of many citizens, nothing else had been stolen beyond the gemstones that had been found in the morning.
entries.new: 警方断定，第二名死者 Isla Majutsu 是在 {time=9.} 之后数小时才死去的。{w} 然而，关于究竟发生了什么，他们掌握的线索寥寥无几。几乎所有监控录像都被抹去，剩下的也毫无用处。两名死者的遗物中没有重要物品，大楼各处也同样一无所获。{w} 这反而让事情更加扑朔迷离：许多市民相信失窃的不只是宝石，但除了早上发现的那批宝石之外，并没有其他东西失窃。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But there was another reason why the investigation was majorly hindered.
entries.new: 但调查之所以严重受阻，还有一个原因。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When the entrance opened, the authorities detected a gas present in the interior, especially prominent on the lowest floor. As a safety measure, they quickly locked the main access to the building to analyze what the substance was.
entries.new: 入口打开时，当局检测到建筑内部存在一种气体，尤其在底层最为浓重。出于安全考虑，他们迅速封锁了大楼的主要通道，以分析这种物质。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: After analysis, identifying the substance hadn't been possible. Once that information propagated, the handling of the situation became much more delicate, as neither the gas nor its source had been recognized.
entries.new: 分析之后，仍无法辨明那是什么物质。消息传开后，事态的处理变得更加棘手，因为那种气体及其来源都无人认得。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: This was the first public statement:{w} "Five people who were trapped in Ashiya Tower on the 15th are still to be found. The deaths of Naomi Cabca and Isla Majutsu are being investigated. However, access to Ashiya Tower is strictly prohibited, as a potentially dangerous gas was found within it in high quantities.{w} While investigating the motive behind the attack is not the highest priority, aside from the gemstones found immediately after the authorities secured the situation, no other valuable items were found to be missing, indicating that theft may not have been the goal."
entries.new: 这是首次公开声明：{w}「15日被困在芦屋塔的五人至今下落不明。Naomi Cabca 与 Isla Majutsu 的死亡正在调查中。然而，由于楼内发现了大量可能具有危险性的气体，芦屋塔严禁进入。{w} 虽然查清袭击动机并非当务之急，但除了当局控制现场后立即发现的宝石之外，没有发现其他贵重物品失窃，这表明盗窃或许并非目的。」
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Shiroya couldn't see the walls of her apartment without feeling her heart shrinking. When she finally went back, she wondered what she was supposed to do.
entries.new: 一看见公寓的墙壁，她的心便不由得揪紧。终于回到这里时，她也不知道自己究竟该做些什么。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She had spoken to her parents over the phone, and she'd been forced to speak about Atsuki's death and everything the police had asked her. Even though she'd been released without being considered guilty of anything, she hadn't been able to answer any questions about the attack on the 15th.
entries.new: 她和父母通过电话，不得不提起 Atsuki 的死，也不得不把警方问过她的事说给他们听。虽然她最终获释，也没有被认定犯有任何罪行，但关于15日那场袭击，她连一个问题都回答不了。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Lately, she'd had to talk a lot, but when she found herself at home, she didn't think she had the ability to produce a single sound.
entries.new: 最近她不得不说了很多话，可一回到家里，她觉得自己连一点声音都发不出来。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The pillows were still scattered in her living room. The last time she'd been there, she'd managed to feel hopeful, but that felt so distant that it was hard to believe decades hadn't passed.
entries.new: 客厅里的靠枕仍散落着。上一次待在这里时，她还能生出几分希望，可那份感觉已遥远得让人难以相信，这中间竟然没有过去几十年。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Shiroya didn't know what the point of returning was. She had lost everything.
entries.new: Shiroya 不知道自己回来还有什么意义。她已经失去了一切。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It was the next day. She had slept and eaten, but it couldn't be said she'd done so for any particular reason.{w} The miserable way she felt... it was all too familiar to her, but the difference in potency was immense.
entries.new: 已是第二天。她睡过，也吃过东西，但很难说这么做是出于什么理由。{w} 那种凄惨的心境……她再熟悉不过，可这次的程度之强，却远非往日可比。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That day, she became aware of something she hadn't been told yet.
entries.new: 那天，她得知了一件此前没人告诉过她的事。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: After turning on the television, she learned about the current situation in Yushibana.
entries.new: 打开电视后，她知道了丰花如今的状况。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It wasn't a secret that a large portion of the citizens was opposed to the presence Ashiya had built. Due to Ashiya Tower, Yushibana had undergone a drastic change throughout the recent years.
entries.new: 大部分市民反对芦屋在此建立的势力，这早已不是秘密。因为芦屋塔，丰花这几年经历了剧变。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Perhaps the old activities of what had once been called the Ashiya family weren't as widely known, but what was a commonly shared fact was that when the tower had shifted into a personal exposition center, a new wave of people had taken over the town.
entries.new: 芦屋家族过去的所作所为或许并不广为人知，但众所周知的是，当那座塔变成私人展览中心后，新一批人涌入了这座城镇。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That was the fundamental dispute in Yushibana. The older citizens, aware of the way Ashiya had once been, were becoming outnumbered by the recent influx of people Ashiya had brought, who supported the now-corporation due to financial reasons and were ignorant of its roots.{w} After the 15th of December, the backlash Ashiya had received had been enormous. Through their poor security measures, they'd let two people be killed, and they hadn't publicly responded well to the ordeal, blinded by their battle against Xyn.
entries.new: 这正是丰花最根本的矛盾。熟知芦屋昔日作风的老一辈市民，人数正逐渐被芦屋近来引入的大批外来者超过；这些人出于经济上的理由支持如今这家企业，却对其根源一无所知。{w} 12月15日之后，芦屋遭受的声讨极为猛烈。由于安保措施不力，他们让两人丢了性命，而他们被与 Xyn 的争斗蒙蔽了双眼，面对这场变故也没能在公众面前妥善应对。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Unlike previously, the protests were so strong and visible that the supportive part of Yushibana joined in as well. Everything Ashiya had done to combat Xyn was being revealed, so the older citizens took the chance to expose all they knew about Ashiya's past, and rumors about the missing people and the unknown gas continued to circulate.
entries.new: 与以往不同，这次的抗议声势浩大、触目可见，连丰花那些支持芦屋的人也加入了进来。芦屋为对抗 Xyn 所做的一切正被逐一揭露，老一辈市民便借机抖出他们所知的芦屋往事；有关失踪者与不明气体的传言也愈传愈烈。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: All Ashiya kept saying was that they were still investigating what had happened—that they would find the missing people and expose those working as part of Xyn. Then, the tower would quickly open again.{w} However, everyone knew that nobody had entered that building since the 15th due to the unknown gas, so those statements were seen as a haphazard, lacking defense.
entries.new: 芦屋只是一再声称，他们仍在调查发生了什么，会找到失踪者，也会把为 Xyn 效力的人揪出来。随后，塔很快就会重新开放。{w} 然而人人都知道，自15日以后，由于不明气体，没人进过那栋楼，因此这些说辞被视为仓促拼凑、站不住脚的辩解。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Where were the remaining people? Why had they not been in the tower?{w} One of them had died in a car accident, and another one had been unable to explain anything to the police. It didn't make sense; they should've been in the tower, late on the 15th. ...And what about the other three? They hadn't been found anywhere.
entries.new: 其余的人在哪里？他们为什么不在塔里？{w} 其中一人死于车祸，另一人面对警方的询问什么也解释不清。这说不通；15日深夜，他们本该在塔里。……那另外三人呢？哪里都找不到他们。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Soon, Ashiya went quiet. After days spent repeating themselves, it seemed they'd chosen to drop the subject entirely.
entries.new: 不久，芦屋沉默了。连续几天重复同一套说辞之后，他们似乎决定彻底不再提这件事。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The news had been covered all over the nation and had even reached overseas. When it was noticed that Ashiya had stopped defending themselves from harsh criticism, it was assumed they'd concluded they were done for.
entries.new: 这则新闻传遍全国，甚至传到了海外。人们注意到芦屋不再为自己抵挡猛烈的批评，便猜测他们已经认定自己走投无路了。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: And that was correct. The next time an executive of Ashiya was seen, they were recorded exiting the tower, loading covered boxes onto a truck.
entries.new: 而事实正是如此。下一次有人看见芦屋的高层时，他们正走出塔楼，把蒙着布的箱子搬上卡车，这一幕被拍了下来。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Later that day, from her apartment, Shiroya saw that scene being broadcast.
entries.new: 当天稍晚，Shiroya 在公寓里看到了这一幕的播出。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: So, is it true that you're abandoning the tower? It's been speculated you're selling it. Is that correct? What do you have to say about all the employees you left without a job?
entries.new: 那么，你们放弃这座塔的消息属实吗？外界猜测你们正打算出售它，是这样吗？对于那些被你们丢下、失去工作的员工，你有什么要说的？
entries.speaker: c5

entries.text: There was no reply from the Ashiya member.
entries.new: 那名芦屋成员没有回答。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The police haven't said anything else about the supposed gas that's inside. Is that not a concern anymore?
entries.new: 警方对于里面所传的气体没有再作任何说明。你们已经不再担心这件事了吗？
entries.speaker: c5

entries.text: On the video, the snow was starting to melt in the background. The reporter tried to get the man to answer again, but she couldn't get him to speak.
entries.new: 视频里，背景中的积雪开始融化。记者又试着让那名男子回答，却始终没能让他开口。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Shiroya reached out to pet Maxi. In the corner, Umi's eyes seemed to be fixed on the screen, her dark fur camouflaged in the dim room.
entries.new: Shiroya 伸手去摸 Maxi。角落里，Umi 的眼睛似乎一直盯着屏幕，她深色的毛在昏暗的房间里几乎看不出来。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The screen morphed into static, the audio going with it. As the signal was very poor, it was frequently interrupted.
entries.new: 屏幕化作一片雪花，声音也随之中断。信号极差，画面时常中断。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Staring at the television, Shiroya felt traces of motion sickness. Was it due to the rapidly flashing screen? It almost didn't seem that way.
entries.new: Shiroya 盯着电视，泛起了几分晕眩。是因为屏幕闪得太快吗？似乎又不尽然。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Long ago, evolution had developed motion sickness. When one's sight blurred, as they could've been poisoned, they would react by vomiting to expel the poison. Shiroya was unsure if the static just made her feel that way or if her entire life had been poisoned.
entries.new: 很久以前，进化造就了晕眩反应。当视线变得模糊时，人可能以为自己中了毒，便会用呕吐把毒物排出。Shiroya 说不清，究竟是那片雪花让她有了这种感觉，还是她整个人生都已中了毒。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Alone in her apartment, she didn't look away until the signal resolved.{w} When it did, someone else was speaking about the same topic, but very far from the tower.
entries.new: 她独自待在公寓里，信号恢复前一直没有移开视线。{w} 信号恢复时，另一个人正在谈论同一件事，但那人离塔楼很远。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...ya tower was bought. We don't have the details yet, but it appears the building is not theirs anymore. They just finished taking out anything of worth inside, so Ashiya's quietly leaving their old property behind.
entries.new: ……芦屋塔被买下了。具体情况我们还不清楚，但看样子那栋楼已经不再属于他们。他们刚把里面值钱的东西全部搬走，芦屋就这样悄悄舍弃了旧日的产业。
entries.speaker: c5

entries.text: It became known that someone had offered to buy the tower from Ashiya, and they had accepted due to their awful position. In the blink of an eye, Ashiya, which had been seen as a source of power and wealth within Yushibana, had entirely vanished.{w} Who had been the buyer, however? It didn't seem that information was widely available.
entries.new: 人们得知，有人向芦屋提出买下这座塔，而芦屋由于处境糟糕接受了。转眼之间，曾在丰花被视为权势与财富象征的芦屋便彻底消失了。{w} 可买家究竟是谁？这条信息似乎并未广泛流传。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Despite what many people felt in regards to Ashiya, a large portion of the citizens in Yushibana engaged in business with them, so the group falling to pieces brought hardship. Would the tower's new owner put the building to a similar use?
entries.new: 尽管许多人对芦屋心存不满，丰花仍有很大一部分市民与他们有生意往来，因此这个集团的瓦解也带来了困苦。塔的新主人会把这栋建筑用于类似的用途吗？
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: If not, it was very likely someone else from Yushibana would, as there were a variety of shops and attractions related to the gemstones in the surrounding mountains. As long as those shops could still sell gems, at least a few of them would avoid disaster.
entries.new: 若不会，丰花很可能会有别人接手，因为周边山里有各种与宝石相关的店铺和景点。只要这些店铺还能卖出宝石，至少有一部分能免于灾祸。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But what would happen was soon revealed.
entries.new: 但事情很快便有了答案。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The news finally came out: the building that had been Ashiya's for so many years would disappear.
entries.new: 消息终于公布：那栋多年来属于芦屋的建筑将不复存在。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That began to shine a bit of light on the situation. The demolition of the tower was something one part of Yushibana had always wished for. The structure that clearly didn't belong with the others—the one they'd all seen rapidly increasing in height throughout the years...
entries.new: 这让局势稍微明朗了一些。拆掉这座塔，正是丰花一部分人长久以来的愿望。那座与周围格格不入的建筑——这些年来，所有人都看着它迅速拔高……
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Why had it been purchased just to be demolished? Had it been to follow that old, unattainable demand that Ashiya disappear? Did they hope the rumors still tied with that building would vanish so that something entirely new could be built? There was only speculation on those topics throughout Yushibana, and nothing more.
entries.new: 为什么买下它只是为了拆掉？是为了满足那个陈旧而难以实现的诉求，让芦屋消失吗？还是希望与那栋楼相关的传言就此散去，好建起全然不同的东西？整个丰花对此只有猜测，再无别的。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Weeks had passed, but any answers remained staunchly concealed. However, a date had already been appointed: on October 4th, the building would be destroyed.
entries.new: 数周过去，答案依旧被牢牢掩藏。然而日期已经定下：10月4日，那栋建筑将被拆除。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It was a tall and wide structure, so demolishing it wasn't simple. As no buildings were directly next to it, though, there was little danger to any of the surroundings.
entries.new: 那栋建筑又高又宽，拆除并不简单。不过，由于没有建筑紧挨着它，对周边一带几乎没有危险。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: At some point, the unanswered questions had almost faded. Who had caused the incident on the 15th of December? Who had killed the two victims? Where were the remaining people? Given the blood that had been found, the worst had been assumed by all.
entries.new: 不知从什么时候起，那些未解的疑问几乎淡去了。12月15日的事件是谁造成的？两名死者是谁杀的？其余的人又在哪里？鉴于现场发现了血迹，所有人都已作了最坏的设想。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: After so long, there was a reason why Shiroya and her cat had their heads out their window.{w} It was October 4th, and the sight they were beholding would no longer exist the following day.
entries.new: 过了这么久，Shiroya 和她的猫之所以探出窗外，是有原因的。{w} 今天是10月4日，而他们眼前的景象，到了明天便不复存在。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In the distance, the building stretching past the others was soon to fall. It could've been dangerous to get close to it, so many people were also watching from within their houses. Some of them were about to have a familiar view returned to them. Others, like Shiroya, could hardly imagine what a Yushibana without Ashiya Tower would be like.
entries.new: 远处，那栋高出其他建筑的楼即将倒下。靠近它可能有危险，因此许多人也在自家屋里观望。有些人即将重新见到熟悉的景色。另一些人，比如 Shiroya，则几乎无法想象没有芦屋塔的丰花会是什么样子。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: At {time=12}, the demolition would begin. There'd been no correspondence from Ashiya in months. The facts behind the unknown gas and the deaths within the tower were still shrouded in darkness.{w} The interior of the building had been investigated a few times after the 15th, but nothing useful had been figured out. Ashiya had removed everything of value, so after it was verified by the new owner, the demolition seemed to pose no risk aside from the dust it would scatter across the hill behind the tower.
entries.new: 到了{time=12}，拆除便会开始。芦屋已经几个月没有过任何联络。不明气体与塔内死亡事件背后的真相，仍笼罩在黑暗之中。{w} 15日之后，楼内被调查过几次，却始终没能查出什么有用的东西。芦屋已将值钱之物尽数搬走，经新主人确认后，此次拆除除了会让尘土散落到塔后的山丘上，似乎并无其他风险。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: A minute before the appointed time, many pairs of eyes looked on from behind windows all over town.
entries.new: 约定时间前一分钟，整座城镇的许多双眼睛都在窗后注视着。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: With a faint, deep sound, the building had abruptly fallen. In a second, a huge, brown cloud of dust was all that Shiroya could see on the other side of Yushibana.
entries.new: 伴随一声低沉的闷响，那栋建筑骤然倒下。转眼间，Shiroya 在丰花另一头能看见的，只剩一大团棕色的尘雾。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It didn't seem like it had reached any of the nearest houses. Instead of waiting for it to dissipate, Shiroya shut the window and walked out of her bedroom.
entries.new: 尘土似乎没有蔓延到最近的房屋。Shiroya 没有等它散去，便关上窗，走出了卧室。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Cleaning up the debris would be a long process, and while there was no news about what would happen afterward, the procedure would start a week from that day.
entries.new: 清理废墟将是一个漫长的过程。尽管之后会如何还没有消息，但清理工作将从那天起一周后开始。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Shiroya returned in the afternoon. She'd gotten used to having the television on while she was at home. She'd never done that prior to everything that had happened to her, but it brought her some small form of solace to have any noise at all in her barren set of rooms.
entries.new: Shiroya 在下午回来了。她已经习惯在家时开着电视。在经历这一切之前，她从不会这么做，但如今，空荡荡的房间里哪怕有一点声响，也能给她些许慰藉。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She'd set the volume low because the sporadic static would be hard on her ears otherwise.
entries.new: 她把音量调得很低，否则时不时响起的杂音会刺得她耳朵难受。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The bright screen projected light onto the ceiling. When the color drastically changed, Shiroya lifted her head.
entries.new: 明亮的屏幕将光投在天花板上。屏幕颜色骤然一变时，Shiroya 抬起了头。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She raised her entire body next. On the screen was a man speaking into a microphone.{w} She grabbed the remote and increased the volume, staring at the text beneath him.
entries.new: 她随即直起了身子。屏幕上是一个对着话筒讲话的男人。{w}她抓起遥控器调高音量，目光落在男人下方的文字上。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She had to read it a few times to comprehend it.
entries.new: 她读了好几遍才看明白。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "The last three people who were trapped in Ashiya Tower found dead".
entries.new: 「被困芦屋塔的最后三人已确认死亡」。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In the corner of the screen was an image of the piled debris. Shiroya focused her hearing and began to process the deep voice of the reporter.
entries.new: 屏幕一角是瓦砾堆积的画面。Shiroya 凝神倾听，仔细辨认记者低沉的嗓音。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...en they started to be removed, the first body was found. It was that of Akaro Esata.
entries.new: 「……开始清理之后，第一具遗体被发现了。是 Akaro Esata。」
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: A video began to play in the background. It showed people removing the debris and a pixelated red blob in the middle.
entries.new: 背景开始播放一段视频。画面里有人正在清理瓦砾，中央是一团打了马赛克的红色物体。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Another one was quickly found afterward, belonging to Sai Yomiya. Finally, when almost all the debris had been removed, Erina Majutsu's body was found.{w} The three bodies were heavily crushed, and it's believed some parts of them weren't found.
entries.new: 「紧接着又发现了另一具，属于 Sai Yomiya。最后，当瓦砾几乎清理殆尽时，Erina Majutsu 的遗体也被找到了。{w}三具遗体都严重压毁，据信还有部分残骸未能找到。」
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: Shiroya listened in disbelief. She'd always known that when she'd touched the Sekimeiya, Atsuki, Erina, Sai, and Akaro had been in the lobby. Atsuki had died in a car accident, but the others had all disappeared. A long time ago, Shiroya had concluded that Atsuki must've traveled through time after her.
entries.new: Shiroya 难以置信地听着。她一直清楚，就在她触碰 Sekimeiya 的那一刻，Atsuki、Erina、Sai 和 Akaro 都在大厅里。Atsuki 死于车祸，其余几人却全部下落不明。很久以前，Shiroya 就已断定，Atsuki 一定是在她之后穿越了时间。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But this... What kind of sense did it make? The censoring prevented her from confirming the bodies' faces, but given their descriptions, it didn't seem like that would've been possible regardless.
entries.new: 可这件事……又该怎么解释？马赛克让她无法确认遗体的面容，但单从报道的描述来看，即便没有打码，恐怕也辨认不出。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: As of now, what happened is unknown. While the bodies were severely smashed, they were not fully decomposed. It has been determined that they died the day of the demolition.{w} However, the possibility of the demolition itself causing their deaths has been thoroughly refuted. It was properly verified that nobody was in the building before the impact, and that's not the only reason.{w} The three bodies were below all the rubble. If the building had really fallen on them, their condition would be even worse. Strangely, some of the body parts that were recovered are practically intact, despite the state of most others.{w} There was no dust discovered on the bodies—neither inside their clothes nor in their mouths. For this reason, the situation is being handled very carefully, as the truth behind it might be appalling.{w} It has been considered that the bodies were disposed of within the rubble following the demolition since they couldn't have been directly hit by it. However, given how deep they were and the absence of blood around them, that was immediately discarded as well.{w} Even though the abundance of the unidentified old gas has disappeared, around the three bodies was where the last remaining traces were found.{w} This is an extremely delicate case that has carried unsolved questions with it all year. Now that everyone who was trapped in the building has been found, the authorities will do all they can to figure out what happened on that day.
entries.new: 「截至目前，事情经过仍不清楚。遗体虽然严重损毁，却并未完全腐烂。现已确定他们死于拆除当天。{w}不过，拆除本身导致他们死亡的可能性已被彻底排除。事前已经确认，爆破前建筑物里没有人，而且这还不是唯一的理由。{w}三具遗体位于所有瓦砾之下。若建筑物真的压在他们身上，遗体的状况只会更糟。奇怪的是，尽管大部分残骸损毁严重，找到的部分肢体却几乎完好无损。{w}遗体上没有发现灰尘——衣服里、嘴里都没有。正因为如此，这起案件才被处理得如此谨慎，因为背后的真相可能令人震惊。{w}有人推测，既然遗体不可能是被直接砸中的，那就是在拆除之后被人丢进瓦砾堆里的。然而考虑到遗体埋藏之深、周围又没有血迹，这一推测也立即被排除了。{w}尽管大量不明旧气体已经消散，最后残留的痕迹正是在这三具遗体周围发现的。{w}这桩极其棘手的案件，整整一年都悬而未决。如今被困于建筑物内的人已全部找到，当局将竭尽全力查明那一天究竟发生了什么。」
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: Chapter 3 Credits (Forsaken Relay)
entries.new: 第三章 制作人员名单（Forsaken Relay）

entries.text: Shiroya turned off the television.
entries.new: Shiroya 关掉了电视。

entries.text: After months of dwelling on the incident, the reporter's words released her.
entries.new: 几个月来她一直为那起事件耿耿于怀，而记者的话却让她解脱了。

entries.text: It was over.
entries.new: 一切都结束了。

entries.text: The remaining hope she'd been carrying was gone.
entries.new: 她心中残存的最后一点希望，也终于消散。

entries.text: She wouldn't see the people she'd been with that day again, and she wouldn't learn what had happened to them.
entries.new: 那天与她共处的人们，她再也见不到了，也无从得知他们究竟遭遇了什么。

entries.text: Over time, she'd come to accept that the time when the three had reunited had been but a second farewell.
entries.new: 随着时间流逝，她渐渐接受了：三人重逢的那一刻，不过是一场再度的告别。

entries.text: Shiroya stepped out of her apartment one more time to visit the snowless world.
entries.new: Shiroya 又一次走出公寓，去看那个无雪的世界。

entries.text: The sky above her didn't feel the same as it once had, but it was still there.
entries.new: 头顶的天空已不复昔日的感觉，但它依然在那里。

entries.text: She had somewhere to go.
entries.new: 她有个地方要去。

entries.text: Earlier that day, she'd tried to walk there and stopped halfway.
entries.new: 那天早些时候，她曾试着走过去，却在半路停下了脚步。

entries.text: Surrounded by green, she inhaled a familiar aroma.
entries.new: 置身绿意之间，她嗅到一缕熟悉的气息。

entries.text: She wanted to know if an offer she'd received long ago was still valid.
entries.new: 她想知道，很久以前收到的那份邀请是否仍然算数。

entries.text: Finally hoping for something, she wished it wasn't too late.
entries.new: 她终于又有了期盼，只愿一切都还来得及。

entries.text: And as she saw the last person who remained from her old life, she learned that she hadn't waited too long.
entries.new: 而当她见到旧日生活中仅剩的那一个人时，她才知道自己并没有等太久。

entries.text: It wouldn't make her happy.
entries.new: 这不会让她幸福。

entries.text: And it would probably not make her less lonely.
entries.new: 大概也不会让她少一分孤独。

entries.text: But the fact that she wanted it regardless was enough to know that she had to do it.
entries.new: 但即便如此她仍想要，这便足以说明她非做不可。

entries.text: The next day, she had a reason to get up and fondly remembered the last time she'd awoken in high spirits.
entries.new: 第二天，她有了起身的理由，也怀念地想起上一次怀着好心情醒来的情形。

entries.text: The three gruesome bodies beneath the rubble...
entries.new: 瓦砾下那三具惨不忍睹的遗体……

entries.text: That mystery was nowhere close to being solved.
entries.new: 那桩谜团远未解开。

entries.text: There had been no new information from Ashiya.
entries.new: 芦屋那边再没有传来新的消息。

entries.text: They had vanished completely, and with them the route to any remaining answers.
entries.new: 他们彻底消失了，通往余下答案的线索也随之断绝。

entries.text: The plain terrain where the tower had once been...
entries.new: 高塔曾经矗立的那片空地……

entries.text: After years of the building's increasing height, nothing else would rise there.
entries.new: 那座建筑曾年复一年地越建越高，此后那里再不会有任何东西拔地而起。

entries.text: It didn't take long for that place to become a thing of the past.
entries.new: 没过多久，那个地方就成了过去。

entries.text: And for that inexplicable day to be merely a memory.
entries.new: 那个无从解释的日子，也不过成了一段回忆。

entries.text: Once years had gone by, Shiroya's surroundings were different.
entries.new: 数年过去，Shiroya 身边的一切都已不同。

entries.text: She wasn't far from Yushibana, but she didn't live there anymore.
entries.new: 她离丰花并不远，却已不住在那里。

entries.text: Every time she looked at both animals still at her side, she remembered the person who'd always been with her.
entries.new: 每当她看到仍陪在身边的这两只动物，就会想起那个一直陪伴着她的人。

entries.text: He was someone she'd never forget and someone who didn't exist anymore.
entries.new: 她永远不会忘记那个人，而那个人也已不复存在。

entries.text: Holding a packed, green folder, she laughed along with someone who'd never stepped into her hometown.
entries.new: 她拿着一个塞得鼓鼓的绿色文件夹，和一个从未踏进过她故乡的人一起笑了。

entries.text: She explained the events of one particular December 15th as if they had happened long, long ago.
entries.new: 她讲起某一个 12 月 15 日发生的事，仿佛那已是极其遥远的往事。

entries.text: Leaving out crucial details, she maintained a natural voice as she thought back on that egg-shaped stone.
entries.new: 她略去关键细节，回想那颗蛋形的石头时，语气依旧自然。

entries.text: Was she the last person who remembered its powers?
entries.new: 记得它力量的人，是否只剩她一个了？

entries.text: ...She really was the same person who'd once stepped into that tower, and the only survivor of that day.
entries.new: ……她确实还是当年走进那座塔的那个人，也是那一天唯一的幸存者。

entries.text: Ending: Forsaken Relay
entries.new: 结局：Forsaken Relay

entries.text: Axis Ropeway
entries.new: 轴线索道

entries.text: Tethered
entries.new: 牵系

entries.text: I would... change the past. I had a way to save Miiya, Atsuki, Isla, Katei, Naomi, Erina...
entries.new: 我会……改变过去。我有办法救 Miiya、Atsuki、Isla、Katei、Naomi、Erina……
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had traveled from the 15th to change the past alone, and even though I hadn't been aware of what would happen, I had considered the outcome with my other self.
entries.new: 我是为了改变过去，才独自一人从15日穿越而来的。尽管并不清楚会发生什么，我仍与另一个自己一同推演过结局。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Looking at the small town had finally brought me to lean toward an option. I'd decided to do my best to change the past, as the possible consequences didn't outweigh what good could be achieved.
entries.new: 望着这座小镇，我终于倾向了其中一个选择。我决定尽力去改变过去——可能付出的代价，终究抵不上能换来的东西。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But the tower I could see far in the distance... I still couldn't go there.
entries.new: 然而远处那座塔……我依旧去不了那里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The day I'd enter that building again would likely be the last day of my normal life, and even though I'd decided, the thought could still freeze me in place.
entries.new: 再次踏进那栋大楼的那一天，多半就是我正常生活的最后一天。尽管已经下定决心，光是想到这一点，我仍会僵在原地。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I wanted the days I had to persist, but that couldn't happen. My life in Yushibana was likely soon to end, and I could choose the length of the last stretch.
entries.new: 我希望眼前的日子能一直延续下去，但那不可能。我在丰花的生活大概很快就要结束，而最后这段路能走多长，我可以自己决定。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If I saved Miiya, I wouldn't show myself to her, Atsuki, and the other me, even though I didn't know yet what I would do.
entries.new: 就算救了 Miiya，我也不会在她、Atsuki，还有另一个我自己面前现身——尽管那时还不知道自己究竟要做什么。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So the issue to solve was the possibility of a knowledgeable enemy who could change the past on their own and steal the Sekimeiya before the 15th.
entries.new: 所以，真正要解决的问题是：敌人有可能知晓内情，能自行改变过去，抢在15日之前夺走 Sekimeiya。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't do much to combat that aside from rushing in, which I found far too risky. So I settled on another course of action and accepted that I would take it.
entries.new: 除了贸然闯入，我几乎没有别的手段应对，而那实在太冒险。于是我另定了一条路，并说服自己接受它。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Thursday was two days away.{w} Every Thursday morning, an event would be held in the tower. That was the day I chose to step into the building for the second time and find the Sekimeiya that was surely confined inside.
entries.new: 距离周四还有两天。{w}每逢周四上午，塔里都会举办活动。我选中了那一天，第二次踏进那栋大楼，去找必定被关在里面的 Sekimeiya。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I tried to breathe properly. If I wasn't beaten to it, I only had one more day that I'd chosen to give myself, hopelessly refusing to let them end so soon.{w} And the very next one, I'd go to the tower in the morning and think about the best way to act. Then, I'd put that into effect that very night.
entries.new: 我试着让呼吸平稳下来。如果没人抢先一步，我只剩一天是留给自己的——我还在徒劳地不肯让这些日子这么快结束。{w}再过一天，我便在早晨前往那座塔，思考最合适的行动方式。然后，当晚就付诸实施。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What would the event be? I knew Atsuki had read the upcoming ones and said that only one seemed interesting in late January.
entries.new: 会是什么活动？我记得 Atsuki 看过近期的活动安排，说一月底只有一场还算有意思。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There, people will probably ask about the Sekimeiya. It might even be held in the event room.
entries.new: 那里多半会有人问起 Sekimeiya。活动说不定就在活动室举行。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: We had bought entrance tickets for the 15th many days prior, but when we'd waited in the lobby, I'd heard people trying to buy them at the reception desk. They'd all been sold out, but if you could buy the tickets directly there, it was probably common to do so on the day of less important events.
entries.new: 我们在许多天前就买好了15日的入场券，可在门厅等候时，我听见有人在接待处求购。票早已卖光，不过既然能直接在那里买票，遇上不太重要的活动当天再买，大概也很常见。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And if there are none left, I'll just pay for a normal visit. Joining whatever special event will happen isn't essential.
entries.new: 要是票卖完了，我就按普通参观付钱进去。参不参加那场特别活动，并不重要。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I had to stop staring ahead. The strong wind kept whipping snow into my face, and prickling pains chipped at the corners of my eyes.
entries.new: 我不得不移开直视前方的目光。强风不断把雪刮到脸上，细密的刺痛一下下扎着眼角。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Scanning the ground, I took the path that circled Yushibana.
entries.new: 我扫视着地面，走上了环绕丰花的那条路。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The way wasn't perfectly even, and traversing the dense snow was difficult. I had to take the next path leading down, but I couldn't easily see it in the distance due to its identical color.
entries.new: 路面并不平整，积雪又厚，走起来十分吃力。我得走前面那条向下的岔路，可它和周围的雪一个颜色，隔着这段距离很难看清。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My stomach was demanding food, and the cold was becoming too prominent to bear. Protecting my head with my hood, I advanced steadily, knowing where I was headed for once.
entries.new: 胃里在叫嚣着要吃东西，寒意也渐渐逼人难耐。我用兜帽护住头，稳步前行——这一次，我难得清楚地知道自己要去哪里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was close to home. Even though I was going slow, I knew there wasn't much distance between both trails down.
entries.new: 我已离家不远。尽管走得慢，我也知道两条下山小路之间并没有多长距离。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd been glancing up here and there, but it was hard to recognize the narrow entrance to Yushibana I was going toward.
entries.new: 我时不时抬眼张望，却很难认出前方那处通往丰花的狭窄入口。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: At last, I saw the absence of brown at my right.{w} As I thought, it extended all the way down, leading to a dirt road close to my home.
entries.new: 终于，我看到右侧露出一片没有褐色的空隙。{w}果然，那条路一直延伸向下，通往我家附近的一条土路。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stepped down the steep path, careful not to trip. Slowly, I descended until there was concrete below the snow and composed myself. The wind was noticeably weaker closer to the ground, so I raised my head again.
entries.new: 我踏上陡峭的小路，小心着不绊倒。缓缓下行，直到积雪下面露出混凝土，才稳住心神。贴近地面风明显小了许多，我便重新抬起头。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The narrow path soon became a sidewalk where a couple of cars were parked. Like I'd seen from above, nobody seemed to be on the outskirts.
entries.new: 狭窄的小路很快接上了人行道，那里停着几辆车。正如我在高处所见，城郊似乎一个人也没有。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was less than two minutes away from home. My apartment was one block farther, but I had to walk a bit.
entries.new: 我离家已不到两分钟。公寓就在再往前一个街区，不过还得走上一段。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is someone behind me again?
entries.new: 又有人在我背后？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I could see the metallic staircase far ahead, but I debated whether to stop.
entries.new: 远处已能看见那道金属楼梯，我却在犹豫要不要停下。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No, yesterday that didn't work. They'll just run away.
entries.new: 不行，昨天那样没用。对方只会跑掉。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Should I pass by my apartment? What if they want to know where I live?
entries.new: 要直接走过公寓吗？万一对方就是想知道我住哪儿呢？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I started to feel a little nervous. Had I actually felt someone behind me once more, or was it paranoia...? I just needed to go home.{w} I looked by my feet.
entries.new: 我开始有些不安。究竟是真的又感觉到身后有人，还是我多心了……？我只要回家就好。{w}我低头看了看脚边。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I could circle this block, and if new footsteps are here when I'm back, I'll know I'm not making anything up.
entries.new: 我可以绕这个街区一圈。回来时若多了新的脚印，就说明我没有胡思乱想。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I didn't change my pace, but I avoided even looking at my apartment. I'd just made a very important decision, but I felt indecisive again.
entries.new: 我没有改变步伐，却连看都不愿看一眼公寓。明明刚做了一个十分重要的决定，此刻却又动摇起来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even if I confirm that I'm right, what would I do? ...Ignore it?
entries.new: 就算确认了我是对的，我又能怎样？……装作不知道？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I'd have to go home anyway.
entries.new: 反正我总归要回家的。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Up ahead, the only way to see my back would be from directly behind me. If I suddenly turn around at the end and someone is watching me, I should see them as well.
entries.new: 再往前，想看到我的背影，就只能从我的正后方看。如果我在尽头突然回头，而有人正盯着我，那我也该能看见对方。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I bit my lip and kept walking. I couldn't make any motions that indicated I thought someone was behind me or they'd be able to escape again. If someone was there, I just needed to know who it was.
entries.new: 我咬住嘴唇，继续往前走。任何暗示我察觉身后有人的举动都不能做，否则对方又会逃掉。假如真有人跟着，我只想知道那是谁。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I managed to feel a bit of sweat forming on my palms despite the overwhelming cold. Depending on who it was, I might have had to act sooner than I expected.
entries.new: 天冷得厉害，手心竟还是渗出了一点汗。对方是谁还不清楚，我或许不得不比预想中更早出手。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had passed my apartment. If someone was really looking at me, would the curtain of snow conceal them? If they turned fast enough, identifying them would likely be impossible.
entries.new: 我已经走过了公寓。若真有人在注视着我，雪幕会不会将他们遮住？只要对方转身够快，多半就认不出是谁了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}I was close to the end of the street, where it curved into another one. If someone was watching me from behind at that moment, they had to be in eyeshot.
entries.new: ……{w}我快到街的尽头了，那里街道拐向另一条路。此刻若有人在我身后窥视，就一定在视线范围内。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But I instinctively turned around before I'd planned.
entries.new: 可还没等我按计划行动，身体已经本能地转了过去。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A sudden sound had broken the silence far behind me. And as I'd feared, the falling snow was blurring the image.
entries.new: 一声突兀的响动从身后远处打破了寂静。而正如我担心的那样，纷落的雪让眼前一片模糊。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Frowning, I sprinted back the way I'd come, toward a blue smudge way ahead.
entries.new: 我皱起眉，沿来路奔回去，朝前方远处那一抹蓝色冲去。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is that...?
entries.new: 那是……？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It immediately became visible. It was a police officer.{w} ...But that wasn't all, so I didn't stop.
entries.new: 那一抹蓝色立刻清晰起来。是一名警察。{w}……但还不止如此，所以我没有停下脚步。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Before getting there, I understood what had happened. Next to the officer was a police car, and they'd just closed the back door after making someone else get in.
entries.new: 还没跑到跟前，我就明白发生了什么。警察身旁停着一辆警车，他刚让别人上了车，随后关上了后座车门。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh...! ...What's wrong?
entries.new: 哦……！……怎么了？
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: I panted breathlessly, my hands on my knees. A sudden dizziness invaded me, almost causing me to fall.
entries.new: 我双手撑膝，上气不接下气。一阵眩晕猝然袭来，险些让我栽倒。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Are you okay...?
entries.new: 你没事吧……？
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: I nodded and slowly looked up. Instead of responding, I stared at the window of the car. The glass was tinted, so I couldn't see the interior of the vehicle.
entries.new: 我点点头，慢慢抬起视线。我没有答话，只是盯着那辆车的车窗。玻璃贴了膜，看不见车内。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: S-Sorry, did you just arrest someone?
entries.new: 对、对不起，你刚才是在抓人吗？
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Hm? Yes. What's the matter?
entries.new: 嗯？是啊。有什么问题吗？
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: ...{w}I... was feeling like someone was following me just now. Could it have been this person?
entries.new: ……{w}我……刚才一直觉得有人在跟着我。会不会就是这个人？
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: The man frowned and took out a tiny scrapbook.
entries.new: 男人皱起眉，掏出一本巴掌大的记事本。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What's your name?
entries.new: 你叫什么名字？
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: Mine...?{w} ...It's Shiroya Mirana.
entries.new: 我的……？{w}……我叫 Shiroya Mirana。
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: He looked at me and silently wrote on the paper.{w} Then, he suddenly smiled, completely shifting his expression.
entries.new: 他看了我一眼，默默在纸上写着什么。{w}随后忽然露出笑容，神情为之一变。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I see. You can stop worrying, then. If you think you were being followed, there's nothing to be afraid of.
entries.new: 原来如此。那你可以放心了。就算真觉得被人跟踪，也不必再害怕。
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: Wh-What...? Can you let me see their face?
entries.new: 什、什么……？能让我看看那个人的脸吗？
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: He looked at the black window.
entries.new: 他望向那扇漆黑的窗。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No. I'm not allowed to do that.
entries.new: 不行。我不能这么做。
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: ...What about their name or the reason for arresting them?
entries.new: ……那名字呢？或者抓人的理由？
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: You can stop worrying—believe me. Right now, I'm not allowed to tell you any of that, but just wait for when it's made public.
entries.new: 放心好了，相信我。眼下这些我一样都不能说，等正式公布吧。
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: I tried to produce some way of coercing him into telling me more, but I couldn't come up with anything.
entries.new: 我本想找些话逼他再多说几句，却怎么也想不出来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I have to hurry. Don't hesitate to contact us if you feel you're being followed again, but I don't think you'll be having any more problems.
entries.new: 我得走了。要是再觉得被人跟踪，别犹豫，联系我们。不过我想，你应该不会再遇上麻烦了。
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: ...Okay.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: The man nodded with a sympathetic smile and opened the door to the driver side, quickly shutting it again. Then, the car began to move and soon disappeared toward the direction I'd just run from.
entries.new: 男人点点头，带着几分同情的笑意拉开驾驶座一侧的车门，又迅速关上。车子随即启动，很快朝我刚跑来的方向消失了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked by my feet. The tire marks came from far away, and next to them was a group of footprints.
entries.new: 我看向脚边。轮胎印从远处延伸而来，旁边还有一串脚印。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: These are mine. I looked at the ground earlier specifically for this.{w} ...And these were definitely not here before.
entries.new: 这些是我的。我之前特意看过地面，就是为了这个。{w}……而这些印子，之前绝对没有。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: They're the policeman's, though.
entries.new: 不过，这是那个警察的。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I kept looking down, trying to find a third pair of footprints.
entries.new: 我一直低头查看，想找出第三个人的脚印。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There had to be a third pair right there, but I suddenly remembered the strange smile the officer had. Something felt odd about him.
entries.new: 第三个人的脚印本该就在这里，可我忽然想起那名警官古怪的笑容。他身上有点不对劲。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait, these.
entries.new: 等等，是这些。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: After taking a few steps forward, I noticed the trail of footprints coming from the same direction as the tire tracks.
entries.new: 向前走了几步，我注意到另一道脚印，来向与轮胎印一致。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It must be these since they end where the car was.{w} They also resemble the ones I saw yesterday.
entries.new: 一定是这些——脚印正好停在车子原先停着的地方。{w}而且和我昨天见过的很像。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I kept following them in reverse, hoping they would lead somewhere. However, I immediately realized that wouldn't work.{w} The more I walked, the more the footprints faded due to the falling snow. Soon, I could hardly even make out their shape.
entries.new: 我顺着脚印一路往回追，希望能追到什么地方。可很快就明白这行不通。{w}雪还在下，我越往前走，脚印就越淡，没多久便几乎辨不出形状。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I was right.
entries.new: ……我没猜错。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I stopped myself, stress and relief pulling me from both sides.
entries.new: 我停下脚步，一边是紧张，一边是安心，两相拉扯。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The person who was following me was arrested... Maybe I was right that they were someone else who traveled from the 15th. Depending on what happened, just that alone could've led to their arrest.
entries.new: 跟踪我的人被抓走了……也许我猜得没错，那确实是另一个从15号穿越过来的人。视情况而定，单凭这一点，就足以让他被抓。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What mattered was that someone who potentially wanted to steal the Sekimeiya was out of the picture. Being able to feel a little calmer in that regard was immensely beneficial.
entries.new: 重要的是，一个可能想偷走 Sekimeiya 的人已经出局。光是这一点能让我稍微安心些，就已受益良多。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...And he said that their identity would be made public. When's that gonna be, though? Assuming everything up until the 15th repeats itself, it won't be before that day, right? Otherwise, someone who went to the tower would've known a future self of theirs had been arrested.
entries.new: ……他还说，那人的身份会公开。可什么时候公开呢？假设直到15号为止的一切都会重演，那肯定不会早于那天吧？否则，去过塔的人早该知道未来的自己被逮捕了。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I didn't know what to think, but it seemed someone had really identified me and been following me. Added to their arrest, assuming that they'd traveled from the future seemed the most likely scenario.
entries.new: 我不知道该怎么想，但看来确实有人认出了我，还一路跟着我。再加上那人被抓，推测他是从未来穿越而来，似乎是最合理的解释。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I turned around. My apartment was right there.
entries.new: 我转过身。公寓就在眼前。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I could barely keep myself standing anymore. I approached the staircase while I grabbed the keys and staggered my way to the front door.
entries.new: 我已经快站不住了。我摸出钥匙，走到楼梯口，摇摇晃晃地挪向家门。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I lightly shook off the snow on me and turned the key clockwise.
entries.new: 我轻轻抖落身上的雪，把钥匙顺时针一转。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...How long had the heater been on? The change in temperature was more drastic than it had ever been.
entries.new: ……暖气开了多久？温差比以往任何一次都大。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I hurriedly closed the door and left my coat and boots behind. I wanted to drop to the floor, but I managed to make it to the kitchen.
entries.new: 我赶紧关上门，外套和靴子都扔在原地。我恨不得直接瘫在地上，却还是撑到了厨房。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I knew I still had the instant noodles I'd bought, so I grabbed the bowl I'd used last time, then washed and filled a pot.
entries.new: 我记得买来的泡面还有剩，便拿出上次用过的碗，洗净锅子，接上水。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Once the water began to boil, I dropped the noodles in and watched them slowly spread out.
entries.new: 水一开，我把面下进去，看着它慢慢散开。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It would take three minutes to cook. Meanwhile, I sipped water and tried to compose myself.
entries.new: 要煮三分钟。趁着这段时间，我小口喝水，试着让自己平静下来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I hadn't been able to eat in the tower, and I'd kept going for hours and hours there, but the cold outside in wintertime Yushibana was a real problem for me. I kept underestimating the importance of a reasonable surrounding temperature.
entries.new: 在塔里我一口东西都没吃，还一连奔波了好几个小时，可冬日丰花户外的寒气实在要命。我总是一次次没意识到，周围温度合不合适有多重要。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Someone following me had only thrown me further into disarray. I couldn't put into words why I'd felt again that they'd been watching me, but it was possible their goal had really been to learn where I lived. I was far beyond the point of assuming they only wanted to confirm who I was.
entries.new: 有人跟踪我，只让我更加心乱。我说不清为什么又觉得有人在盯着我，但对方的目的很可能真是摸清我住在哪里。我早就不认为他们只是想确认我的身份了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I removed most of the water from the pot and dropped the noodles in the bowl, garnishing it as I had before. The meal looked pretty ordinary, but I eagerly brought it to the living room.
entries.new: 我倒掉锅里大半的水，把面盛进碗里，照上次那样加了配料。卖相平平无奇，我却迫不及待地端进了客厅。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I ate some. They were hot and a bit stiff, but I kept going.
entries.new: 我吃了几口。面热腾腾的，有点硬，可我还是继续往下吃。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I eventually slowed down. Curiously, I took out the phone from my purse and looked at the time.
entries.new: 后来我放慢了速度。出于好奇，我从包里掏出手机，看了眼时间。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: {time=16} already... I was outside for so many hours.
entries.new: 都已经 {time=16} 了啊……我在外面待了那么多个小时。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The person who was just arrested... Could they have been from Xyn?{w} If so, that's a new occurrence, because we were told that no members had been caught yet.
entries.new: 刚才被捕的那个人……会不会是 Xyn 的人？{w} 要真是，那倒是新情况，因为我们听说还没有成员落网。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Were they someone I'd been with in the tower? ...It was frustrating that I hadn't been able to see their face.
entries.new: 那人会不会是和我一起在塔里待过的人？……没能看清对方的脸，实在叫人不甘心。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I figured there was no point in getting hung up on it, so I kept eating as I thought back on what was most important.
entries.new: 我心想，为这件事纠结也没用，于是继续吃面，一边回想最要紧的事。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It'll be Thursday in just two days... I'm giving myself tomorrow to enjoy, but I'm not sure that's what I want anymore. I'll probably just be nervous all day.
entries.new: 再过两天就是周四了……我原本打算把明天留给自己好好享受，可我已经不确定那还是不是自己想要的了。大概一整天都会心神不宁吧。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: On Thursday morning... finding the Sekimeiya and checking the door in the storeroom shouldn't take too long. After that, there are more important matters.
entries.new: 周四早上……找到 Sekimeiya、确认储藏室的门，应该花不了太久。之后还有更要紧的事。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I'll change the past drastically for the first time by going to Atsuki's house and taking the tickets we bought.{w} Later, I can go to Isla's house and either attempt to talk with whoever her friend really is or try to prevent them from going on the 15th in the same way.
entries.new: 我要第一次大幅改变过去：去 Atsuki 家，把我们买好的票取走。{w} 之后再去 Isla 家，试着和她那位朋友——不管对方究竟是谁——谈谈，或者用同样的办法，阻止她们在 15 号去。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That could be really important, because if I get caught by the police or I'm not able to find the Sekimeiya, at least I'll guarantee that the four of us don't go to the event.
entries.new: 这一步或许至关重要：就算我被警察抓住，或者找不到 Sekimeiya，至少也能保证我们四个人不会去参加那个活动。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I'm not too sure what would happen then. It's pretty likely the two initial groups to get trapped would merely consist of different people, but I can't do anything about that.
entries.new: 那样一来会发生什么，我也说不准。最初被困住的两组人，很可能只是换成另外一批人，可这我也无能为力。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I'd entirely cleaned out the bowl, so I brought it to the kitchen and picked up a pair of cereal bars.
entries.new: 碗里的东西被我吃得一干二净，我便把碗端到厨房，顺手拿了两根谷物棒。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Then, I had a thought I hadn't fully considered before.
entries.new: 就在这时，一个我此前从未认真想过的念头冒了出来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Could this be a bad idea...?
entries.new: 这会不会是个坏主意……？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Assuming I'm not able to find the Sekimeiya in the tower, should I really try to prevent any of us from going there? That might screw it all up.
entries.new: 假设我在塔里找不到 Sekimeiya，那我真的该阻止我们中的任何一个人去那里吗？那样说不定会把一切搞砸。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Right now, the 15th is the failsafe in case I can't find the Sekimeiya beforehand. If I let everything repeat, I'll be able to touch it again on that day.{w} Hell, I could see where the recorder even came from, or even stay there for a month, depending on whether it's real or not.
entries.new: 眼下，如果我事先找不到 Sekimeiya，15 号就是我的保险。只要让一切照旧重演，我那天就能再次碰到它。{w} 说不定还能弄清录音笔究竟从何而来，甚至在那里待上一个月——就看那是不是真的了。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But if Atsuki, Isla, Erina, and I don't go to the event, it will all be considerably different.{w} What if something causes the attack to fail?{w} What if Katei and Ashiya are able to unlock the exit this time?
entries.new: 可要是 Atsuki、Isla、Erina 和我都不去参加活动，一切就会大不相同。{w} 万一某个变故让袭击失败了呢？{w} 万一这次 Katei 和芦屋能打开出口呢？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That would get rid of the only guaranteed time where getting the Sekimeiya again will be possible.{w} So, if I don't find it anywhere on Thursday, maybe waiting until the 15th is the best call.
entries.new: 那样一来，唯一能确定再次拿到 Sekimeiya 的时机就没了。{w} 所以，如果周四我哪儿都找不到它，也许等到 15 号才是上策。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I discarded that idea at the start of all this for a reason. If I let the incident happen like it once did, where really is the proof that the past can change? It would mean that the version of myself Atsuki saw really was just me in the future.
entries.new: 我一开始就否掉这个念头，是有理由的。若我让那起事件照原样重演，又哪里还有证据证明过去能够改变？那岂不是说明 Atsuki 见到的那个我，真的只是未来的我而已。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But that's not the case anymore. This is what I hadn't considered yet.
entries.new: 但如今情况已经不同了。这正是我先前没有考虑到的地方。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: If I don't change anything else until the 15th and everything actually repeats, I won't have to enter the tower again.
entries.new: 如果我在 15 号之前不再改动任何事，而一切真的重演，我就不必再进那座塔了。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Now I know something very important. At close to {time=16}, a very long travel took place, and it reached through the walls of the tower...{w} Could I place myself in that range, or would I be arrested?
entries.new: 现在我知道了一件非常重要的事。接近 {time=16} 时发生过一次极远的穿越，它穿过了塔的墙壁……{w} 我能让自己落进那个范围里吗？还是说我会被抓起来？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Even though everyone close to the building will know that someone with my name is inside, would they recognize my face? All I'd have to do would be spot Vaisude and get very close to him at {time=16.}
entries.new: 虽说靠近大楼的人都会知道有个和我同名的人在里面，可他们认得我的脸吗？我只需找到 Vaisude，在 {time=16.} 时贴近他就行了。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That would make me travel to the 24th of November. This would be the best possible outcome.{w} I'd make it far enough to be the first person to find the Sekimeiya in the mountains, stop all of this at the source, and save everyone.
entries.new: 那样我就会穿越到 11 月 24 日。这将是再好不过的结果。{w} 我能走得更远，成为第一个在山里找到 Sekimeiya 的人，从源头阻止这一切，救下所有人。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Exploring what to do those days seemed like a foolish dream, but I thought about it for a bit. I'd been living in my apartment on the 24th, so if I actually wanted to go that far back, I'd have to seriously plan it out.
entries.new: 去设想那几天该怎么过，宛如一场愚蠢的梦，但我还是想了一会儿。24 号那天我还在自己的公寓里，所以真要回到那么早，就得认真筹划一番。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It sounded great in concept, but I couldn't help but think it was an impossible avenue.
entries.new: 听起来很美，可我不禁觉得这条路根本走不通。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How would I get close to Vaisude without getting arrested? I could call him again to more accurately determine the time he'd traveled, but it was unlikely it would be that precise.
entries.new: 我要怎么靠近 Vaisude 又不被抓？我可以再给他打个电话，更准确地确定他穿越的时间，但恐怕不会那么精确。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I still had no idea why we'd found two Naomis, but I hated the idea of letting that repeat even if I'd be letting it happen again so that I could stop it later. In addition, even though it seemed like a given, I couldn't assume that large travel would still happen.
entries.new: 我仍然不明白为什么会出现两个 Naomi，但一想到让这件事重演，我就满心抗拒——哪怕我是为了日后阻止它才故意让它再发生一次。再说，那场大规模穿越看似理所当然，我也不能就这么断定它仍会发生。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't think Vaisude had lied, but I'd somewhat changed history when I'd called my mom, and I didn't know what extra changes that implied. Furthermore, I had no idea if someone else would change the past differently; the butterfly effect could've easily prevented the {time=16} travel from happening.
entries.new: 我不觉得 Vaisude 撒了谎，可我给妈妈打电话时已经多少改变了历史，不知道这还牵连出哪些变化。更何况，我根本不清楚别人会不会以别的方式改变过去；蝴蝶效应轻而易举就能让 {time=16} 的那次穿越不再发生。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If that was the case, would the Vaisude I'd spoken to exist in the world I was in? While I couldn't answer that, I was inclined to think that he would, and that his travel would merely not repeat due to the change.
entries.new: 若真如此，和我通话的那个 Vaisude 还会存在于我所在的这个世界吗？这我答不上来，但我倾向于认为他仍会存在，只是由于这处改变，他的穿越不会再重演了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I opened my eyes after a while. I saw the familiar ceiling I'd been staring at before, but the illumination had slightly changed.
entries.new: 过了好一阵，我睁开眼。映入眼帘的还是先前一直盯着的那片熟悉的天花板，只是光线稍稍变了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Turning to the window, I noticed the sun was setting.
entries.new: 我转头看向窗外，发现太阳正在西沉。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had been going to sleep very early, so I was pretty tired. However, there was something I had to do that I didn't want to leave for the next day.{w} I'd been yawning and stretching on the floor, but I felt I had a bit of time before going to bed.
entries.new: 最近我睡得很早，所以这会儿已经相当疲倦。可有件事我必须去做，不想拖到第二天。{w} 我躺在地板上打着哈欠、伸着懒腰，不过感觉离上床还有一点时间。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Since doing it on Thursday might have been a bad idea, I stood up and went to the entrance.
entries.new: 拖到周四去做也许不妥，于是我站起身，走向玄关。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The sky had gotten a lot darker, and the icy air almost changed my mind.{w} I quickly put my coat and boots back on, checked that everything was in my purse, and stepped out after turning off the lights.
entries.new: 天色已暗了许多，冰冷的空气差点让我打退堂鼓。{w} 我赶紧重新穿上外套和靴子，确认包里的东西都在，关灯后出了门。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Snow was still falling, but it was much lighter, like in the morning. I wondered whether to turn back to grab an umbrella, but I didn't intend to be out for too long, and it didn't seem like the snow was picking up at all.
entries.new: 雪还在下，但比先前小多了，就像早上那样。我犹豫要不要折回去拿把伞，可我没打算在外面待太久，雪看起来也丝毫没有变大的意思。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I went down the stairs and began to walk. ...I looked at the ground, where neither the tire tracks nor the footprints were visible anymore.
entries.new: 我下了楼梯，迈步向前。……我低头看去，地上的车辙和脚印都已不见了踪影。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was remarkable how different the periphery was compared to the center of the town. After some minutes, I'd only seen a handful of people quietly wandering with an umbrella, but the many lit windows all around gave away the presence of life.
entries.new: 这一带和镇中心真是判若两地。走了几分钟，我只见到零星几个人撑着伞静静走过，可四周亮着的一扇扇窗子却透出鲜活的人气。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I reached the lonely crosswalk leading to Ramon and saw the wide street ahead, illuminated by many faint streetlights. Home to many stores, it looked like an entrance to a different town, its wet stone occupied with passersby.
entries.new: 我来到那条通往拉蒙街的冷清人行横道前，望见前方宽阔的街道，被许多昏黄的路灯照着。那里店铺林立，宛如通往另一座小镇的入口，湿漉漉的石板路上行人往来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's late, but I think it should be open...
entries.new: 虽然晚了，不过我想应该还开着……
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I continued up the path, waiting for my destination to come into sight. While I'd never entered it, I recalled seeing it open at that hour.
entries.new: 我沿着路继续往前走，等着目的地出现在视野里。那地方我从未进去过，但我记得这个点它还开着门。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It should be that.
entries.new: ……应该就是那家。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Ahead and still in Ramon was what looked like a blue storefront with white letters above it. It read "Ishimaru".
entries.new: 前方仍在拉蒙街上，是一家蓝色的店面，上方挂着白字招牌。写着「Ishimaru」。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stood in front of its door. The interior was lit, and a woman was sitting behind a transparent wall. Nonetheless, I felt a bit reluctant to step in.
entries.new: 我站在店门前。里面亮着灯，一位女子坐在透明的隔墙后面。尽管如此，我还是有些踌躇，不想迈进去。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was something about the situation that felt too surreal. I couldn't feel bad about myself, though, because what I was doing was a necessary step.
entries.new: 此情此景总有些过于不真实。不过我也不能因此自怨自艾——我这一步是非走不可的。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I pulled the door open and entered the small space, protected from the cold once more. The woman smiled warmly at me as I approached.
entries.new: 我推开门，走进这方小店，再一次把寒冷挡在门外。我走近时，那位女子朝我温和地笑了笑。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Good afternoon. You'd like to try your luck?
entries.new: 下午好。你是想来碰碰运气吗？
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: ...Yeah.
entries.speaker: c3s
