entries.new: Sai 要是偷偷溜走，他们很快就会察觉。他多半是自己下楼来找，说不定会发现我看见的那块 Sekimeiya。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I wonder what he'll do if he actually does. It wasn't working, so he won't be able to activate it.
entries.new: 真让他找到了，他会怎么做呢。那块已经失效，他也启动不了。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The sound of his movements no longer reached me. Bemused by the fact that I could still be patient, I waited for something to happen.
entries.new: 他的动静再也传不到我这边。我居然还沉得住气，自己都觉得意外，就这样等着事情发生。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't know what Sai's intentions could be. Surely he still has to learn everything about the Sekimeiya, but what is his ultimate goal? ...He was trying to achieve something all day, and I have no idea what.
entries.new: 我不知道 Sai 究竟有什么打算。他必然还要弄清与 Sekimeiya 有关的一切，可他最终想达成什么？……他一整天都在设法做成某件事，我却毫无头绪。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Is that someone above me...?
entries.new: 上面有人……？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: For a second, I could discern footsteps coming from the ceiling.
entries.new: 有一瞬，我隐约听出天花板那边传来脚步声。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is it the others...?
entries.new: 是其他人吗……？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The sound grew clearer: a group of people was coming down.{w} Once they went down the stairs, I slowly opened the door.
entries.new: 声音渐渐清晰：一群人正往下走。{w}等他们下了楼梯，我才慢慢推开门。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't see anyone in hallway A.
entries.new: A走廊里看不见任何人。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They're not in hallway C either?
entries.new: C走廊也没有？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...any of the—{w} Can you he—
entries.new: ……这些里面有没有——{w}你听得见——
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: Akaro's voice came from hallway B. From the stairs, I didn't have a good angle to observe.
entries.new: Akaro 的声音从 B走廊传来。我站在楼梯上，角度不好，看不真切。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I chose not to step down. If I was more patient, I would see them from afar without showing myself.
entries.new: 我决定不下去。再多等一会儿，我就能不露面，从远处看清他们。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: the hell...! ...seriously burning!
entries.new: 搞什么……！……烫得要命！
entries.speaker: k4

entries.text: Wait, did Katei find a Sekimeiya in hallway B?
entries.new: 等等，Katei 在 B走廊找到了一块 Sekimeiya？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...it there?
entries.new: ……它在那边？
entries.speaker: a4

entries.text: And that's me. My past self is with them this time.{w} ...Where the hell is Sai, though?
entries.new: 那是我。这次和他们在一起的是过去的我。{w}……可 Sai 到底跑哪去了？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I have no clue!
entries.new: 我哪知道！
entries.speaker: k4

entries.text: ...either.
entries.new: ……我也一样。
entries.speaker: a4

entries.text: ...eed to leave this—
entries.new: ……得离开这里——
entries.speaker: k4

entries.text: They're walking away.
entries.new: 他们走开了。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The sound of their footsteps was fading, when all of a sudden, a sharp sound split the air.
entries.new: 脚步声渐渐远去，忽然，一声脆响划破了空气。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What was that...? It came from hallway B too.
entries.new: 那是什么声音……？也是从 B走廊传来的。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I couldn't hear the others anymore. After waiting a bit behind the door, I stepped down cautiously.
entries.new: 其他人的声音已经听不见了。我在门后又等了一阵，才小心翼翼地下了楼。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It sounded like something fell to the floor...
entries.new: 听上去像有什么东西掉在了地上……
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It didn't seem like anyone was still there. After that sound, the crystal floor's characteristic silence had arisen.
entries.new: 似乎已经没人在了。那声响过后，水晶层特有的寂静又笼罩下来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Keeping myself hidden, I peeked into hallway B.{w} Nobody was there, but I saw what had hit the floor next to the event room.
entries.new: 我藏起身形，朝 B走廊里张望。{w}那里空无一人，但我看见了掉在活动室旁地上的东西。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Snowmelt
entries.new: 融雪

entries.text: It was a Sekimeiya.
entries.new: 那是一块 Sekimeiya。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...What just happened? Did they touch it, so it fell when they disappeared?
entries.new: ……刚才到底怎么回事？是他们碰了它，消失时它才掉下来？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That doesn't make sense, though...
entries.new: 可这说不通啊……
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...They wouldn't necessarily have come back here. Especially since they could've traveled to the future.
entries.new: ……他们未必会回到这里。何况他们也可能是穿越到了未来。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What was strange was its color. It was white, and if they'd touched it, it would've been gray.
entries.new: 奇怪的是它的颜色。它是白色的；要是他们碰过，就会变成灰色。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even though the Sekimeiya didn't work for me earlier, it could've been working now. It could also be another Sekimeiya.
entries.new: 早先我碰它时它已经失效，此刻却可能正在运作。也可能这根本是另一块 Sekimeiya。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What was strange was its color. It was white, and if they'd touched it, it would've been gray.
entries.new: 奇怪的是它的颜色。它是白色的；要是他们碰过，就会变成灰色。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Its color... It's white.{w} If they had touched it, it would be gray.
entries.new: 颜色……是白的。{w}要是被他们碰过，就该是灰色了。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...Would it have teleported if they'd activated it? Not necessarily; it didn't when Sai and Shiroya traveled from the event room.
entries.new: ……如果他们启动了它，它会传送过去吗？未必；Sai 和 Shiroya 从活动室穿越时，它就没跟过去。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What was strange was its color. It was white, and if they'd touched it, it would've been gray.
entries.new: 奇怪的是它的颜色。它是白色的；要是他们碰过，就会变成灰色。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I approached it while scanning the area around me. Then, I felt it through my sleeve.
entries.new: 我一边留意四周，一边走近，然后隔着衣袖碰了碰它。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Damn, it's super hot, just like Katei said. There's no way they activated it.
entries.new: 可恶，烫得厉害，和 Katei 说的一样。他们绝不可能启动过它。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: They had to have been going to the event room, so I opened its door.
entries.new: 他们一定是往活动室去了，所以我打开了那扇门。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When I did, I hit something on the other side.
entries.new: 门一开，我撞上了对面的什么东西。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was another Sekimeiya. However, it was powered off.
entries.new: 又是一块 Sekimeiya。不过，它已经停用了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, what?
entries.new: 哦？怎么回事？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...What happened? They touched this one instead?{w} Hang on, is this the one I found in the cabinet? If it's not working now, that means it was previously working.
entries.new: ……怎么回事？他们碰的是这一块？{w}等等，这是我在展示柜里找到的那块吗？它现在失效，说明之前是能用的。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The empty cabinet was uncovered...
entries.new: 空荡荡的展示柜露了出来……
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I went to room A1.
entries.new: 我去了A1展室。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Inside the same cabinet from before, a third Sekimeiya rested.
entries.new: 先前那个展示柜里，静静躺着第三枚 Sekimeiya。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the hell...? There are three of them?
entries.new: 怎么回事……？居然有三个？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I felt it through my sleeve as well. As I'd expected, it was cold.
entries.new: 我也隔着衣袖碰了碰。果然，是凉的。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So this one doesn't work?
entries.new: 这么说，这个不能用？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Frowning, I went back to the event room. Two functional Sekimeiya were on the floor, close to each other.
entries.new: 我皱着眉回到活动室。地板上放着两枚还能用的 Sekimeiya，彼此相距不远。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A vague idea had formed in my head during the hours I'd been waiting.
entries.new: 等待的那几个小时里，脑中隐约浮起一个念头。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Was I... right?
entries.new: 我……猜对了吗？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Where was everyone? If they had traveled through time, where were they?
entries.new: 其他人呢？如果他们真的穿越了时间，人又在哪里？
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait, I have to see if I can find them. This is critical.
entries.new: 等等，我得设法找到他们。这是关键。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Focused on my thoughts, I walked through the crystal floor.
entries.new: 我满脑子想着事情，穿行在水晶层中。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki suspected that perhaps...
entries.new: 我猜想，或许……
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Is nobody here? ...What about Sai? Did he disappear with everyone else?
entries.new: 没人吗？……Sai 呢？他也跟其他人一起消失了？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I had to look above too, so I grabbed both functional Sekimeiya and went up the stairs.
entries.new: 楼上也得看看，于是我拿起两枚能用的 Sekimeiya，走上楼梯。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I reached the attic and saw that the door was open. However, the key wasn't in the keyhole.
entries.new: 到了阁楼，我发现门开着。可钥匙并不在锁孔里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Recent footprints were in the living room, but I couldn't hear anyone moving around.
entries.new: 客厅里留着新鲜的脚印，却听不到有人走动的声响。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked in the kitchen, the bathroom, the storeroom, both bedrooms... They were all empty.
entries.new: 我找过厨房、浴室、储藏室，还有两间卧室……全都空无一人。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I... don't think the people who were in hallway B are currently here.
entries.new: 我觉得……之前在B走廊的那些人，现在应该不在这里。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I sat on the sofa. The Sekimeiya I'd seen weren't there anymore, likely because they were the same ones I was holding.
entries.new: 我在沙发上坐下。先前见过的那些 Sekimeiya 已经不见了，多半是因为它们就是我手上这两枚。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This world... it's clearly not the one I started in. Many things are happening differently.
entries.new: 这个世界……显然不是我最初所在的那个。很多事情的走向都不一样。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I thought that maybe the past changed at some point. This would've led into the countless deviations I've noticed.{w} ...But there's something about this world that I recognize.
entries.new: 我原以为，是过去在某个时刻被改变了。我察觉到的那些数不清的偏差，大概就由此而来。{w}……可这个世界里，有一点让我觉得熟悉。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And, if I'm really recognizing something from this world, there's no way it was created after the first time I visited it.
entries.new: 而且，如果那真是我认出的、属于这个世界的东西，那它绝不可能是在我第一次踏入这个世界之后才出现的。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What Atsuki recognized from this world was...
entries.new: Atsuki 在这个世界里认出的，是……
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Not the storeroom handle; he never saw it before his appearance in this world.
entries.new: 不是储藏室的门把手——他来到这个世界之前，从未见过它。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: What I recognized from that world was Miiya's existence.
entries.new: 我从那个世界里认出的，是 Miiya 的存在。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even though I haven't been able to see her, what I heard was her voice. I can't doubt that.{w} When that happened, everyone was there. In other words, Miiya's existence wasn't something anyone found strange—not even my past self.
entries.new: 虽然我没能看见她，但我听到的是她的声音，这一点毋庸置疑。{w}那时所有人都在场。也就是说，Miiya 的存在对谁来说都不奇怪——包括过去的我。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: A while ago, Erina claimed she saw Miiya, but her reaction to that was appropriate. She said she didn't think Miiya had been in the tower before.
entries.new: 刚才 Erina 说看见了 Miiya，但她的反应很自然。她说她以为 Miiya 之前并不在这座塔里。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: However, the same thing didn't occur shortly after that.
entries.new: 可没过多久，同样的情形却不再出现。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Of course, I'm assuming Miiya's in on it as well.
entries.new: 当然，我猜 Miiya 也有份。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Not gonna keep trying to clear your name? I suppose it'd be futile with how obvious it is that this is your doing.
entries.new: 不打算继续证明清白了？事情明摆着是你干的，再挣扎也是白费。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Okay, I'll ask. How do you know about Miiya?
entries.new: ……好吧，我问。你怎么知道 Miiya 的事？
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What? She's been here—
entries.new: 什么？她一直就在这里——
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: That's it, ignore him from now on. He can't get out of the corner he's backed himself into.
entries.new: 行了，从现在起别理他。他已经把自己逼进死角，出不来了。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai and Akaro acted as if Miiya's existence was normal.{w} And that's not all. Akaro disappeared after that point, and when he appeared with different clothes after {time=21}, he said he hadn't been present at the last time I'd seen him.
entries.new: Sai 和 Akaro 的表现，就好像 Miiya 的存在理所当然。{w}不仅如此。那之后 Akaro 就消失了，而 {time=21} 过后，他换了一身衣服出现，还说，我最后一次见到他的时候，他并不在场。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: In addition, Sai's attitude at that time was different from how he behaved afterward.
entries.new: 再者，Sai 当时的态度，和他后来的举止也不一样。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: So, when did that happen? When did Miiya's existence become normal for the world?
entries.new: 那么，那是什么时候的事？从什么时候起，Miiya 的存在在世界上变得理所当然了？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: When that happened, he and Shiroya appeared in the attic. At that point, though, Miiya's existence wasn't yet normal.
entries.new: 那件事发生时，他和 Shiroya 出现在阁楼。不过在那个时候，Miiya 的存在还没有变得寻常。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When that happened, he appeared in the event room. At that point, though, Miiya's existence wasn't yet normal.
entries.new: 那件事发生时，他出现在活动室。但在那个时候，Miiya 的存在仍算不上寻常。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Erina, Sai, Shiroya, and I were in the event room. At that point, everyone was surprised to hear Erina mention Miiya.
entries.new: 活动室里是 Erina、Sai、Shiroya 和我。听到 Erina 提起 Miiya，所有人都吃了一惊。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: When Erina touched the Sekimeiya, that changed. Both Sai and Akaro, who came from outside the room, found Miiya's existence to be an expected thing.
entries.new: Erina 碰到 Sekimeiya 之后，情况就变了。从室外进来的 Sai 和 Akaro，对 Miiya 的存在毫不意外。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Once again, that's not all. There was another major change.
entries.new: 同样不止如此。还有一处更大的变化。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It was Shiroya's existence. Sai and Akaro were shocked when they saw her, and perfectly in line with that, I haven't seen her here.
entries.new: 那就是 Shiroya 的存在。Sai 和 Akaro 见到她时都愣住了，而我在这里也确实没见过她。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...When Erina touched the Sekimeiya, something major occurred. I'm sure of that. The Sekimeiya had some hidden effect all this time.
entries.new: ……Erina 碰到 Sekimeiya 的那一刻，发生了某种重大的事。这一点可以肯定。那枚 Sekimeiya 一直藏着某种效果。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That effect occurred when Erina touched it. That was definitely the strangest travel of them all.
entries.new: 那效果就在 Erina 触碰它时发动了。那无疑是所有穿越中最离奇的一次。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Three major questions arose: why did Erina, Shiroya, and I not travel, but Sai did?{w} Why did the Sekimeiya teleport instantly back to its cabinet?{w} Why was the range bigger than it should've been?
entries.new: 三个疑问随之浮现：为什么 Erina、Shiroya 和我没有穿越，Sai 却穿越了？{w}为什么 Sekimeiya 会瞬间传送回它的展示柜？{w}为什么范围比应有的更大？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Now I'm aware of a factor that I didn't consider at the time, which could be the answer to what happened.
entries.new: 如今我意识到一个当时未曾考虑的因素，或许它正是那件事的答案。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I don't believe Miiya's existence is the answer to those questions.
entries.new: 我不认为 Miiya 的存在能解答那些疑问。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It must be the second Sekimeiya.
entries.new: 一定是第二个 Sekimeiya。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I don't believe traveling to the future is the answer to those questions.
entries.new: 我不认为前往未来能解答那些疑问。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It must be the second Sekimeiya.
entries.new: 一定是第二个 Sekimeiya。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The second Sekimeiya...
entries.new: 第二个 Sekimeiya……
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Before Erina touched the Sekimeiya, when we entered the event room, Shiroya and I were confused to see the Sekimeiya in the cabinet.{w} In my case, it was because I'd recently hidden it.{w} ...Specifically, in a locker in the staff room.
entries.new: Erina 触碰 Sekimeiya 之前，我们走进活动室时，Shiroya 和我看到展示柜里的 Sekimeiya，都感到困惑。{w} 我会困惑，是因为我不久前才把它藏起来。{w}……准确地说，是藏进了员工室的一个储物柜里。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: When I saw it in the cabinet, I thought it must've teleported to its "original place", or where the cold temperature was.{w} The reality was...
entries.new: 看到它出现在展示柜里时，我以为它一定是传送回了“原本的位置”，也就是温度较低的地方。{w} 可事实却是……
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That's not it.
entries.new: 不是这样。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I don't think it was the same Sekimeiya. However, the one I hid in the staff room was working, and the one in the cabinet, which Erina touched, was working as well.
entries.new: ……我觉得那不是同一个 Sekimeiya。可是，我藏在员工室的那个仍在运作，展示柜里 Erina 碰过的那个也同样在运作。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: So, I think that what I believe to be the main key to most of those questions is...
entries.new: 所以我想，那些疑问的关键，多半就在……
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Erina touched the Sekimeiya, but that shouldn't matter.
entries.new: Erina 碰过 Sekimeiya，但这一点应该无关紧要。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The answer might be the location of both Sekimeiya.
entries.new: 答案或许在于两个 Sekimeiya 所在的位置。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I'm not sure the Sekimeiya that was activated was the reason.
entries.new: 我不确定是不是因为被启动的那个 Sekimeiya。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The answer might be the location of both Sekimeiya.
entries.new: 答案或许在于两个 Sekimeiya 所在的位置。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The location of the Sekimeiya... One was near the cabinet, and the other was in a locker.
entries.new: Sekimeiya 的位置……一个在展示柜附近，另一个在储物柜里。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: How many people were in range? ...Actually, I don't think that has any relevance after all.
entries.new: 当时有多少人在范围内？……不，仔细想来，那应该无关紧要。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The answer might be the position of both Sekimeiya.
entries.new: 答案或许在于两个 Sekimeiya 所在的位置。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The one in the event room spent fifteen minutes outside the cabinet. Meanwhile, as I had touched the one in the staff room at around {time=18:30}, it should've gathered power there for almost half an hour.
entries.new: 活动室里的那个在展示柜外待了十五分钟。而我，大约在 {time=18:30} 碰过员工室里的那个，所以它应该已经在那里蓄能将近半小时了。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The range of the Sekimeiya Erina touched probably looked like this.{w} However, the hidden factor that I didn't account for...
entries.new: Erina 碰过的那个 Sekimeiya，范围大概是这样。{w} 然而，还有一个我当时没考虑到的隐藏因素……
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...Was the Sekimeiya in the staff room.{w} It was in the rightmost set of lockers, and given the time it had been there, I imagine its range extended halfway through the event room.
entries.new: ……就是员工室里的那个 Sekimeiya。{w} 它在最右侧的那排储物柜里；按它在那儿待的时间来看，我想它的范围已经延伸到了活动室的一半。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...{w}If this is what was special about that travel, then what happened to us?{w} Sai did travel because he was only within range of Erina's Sekimeiya. However, the rest of us didn't teleport through space or time.
entries.new: ……{w}如果那次穿越的特殊之处就在这，那我们又经历了什么？{w} Sai 确实穿越了，因为他只在 Erina 那个 Sekimeiya 的范围内。可我们其余人并没有在空间或时间上传送。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Instead, what changed was the world around us.{w} The Sekimeiya didn't teleport back to the cabinet—that was a mere illusion.
entries.new: 真正改变的，是我们周围的世界。{w} Sekimeiya 并没有传送回展示柜——那不过是错觉。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Then, I quickly went to check the locker and found out the Sekimeiya I'd hidden there was gone. That only contributed to the same illusion.
entries.new: 随后我急忙去查看储物柜，发现藏在那里的 Sekimeiya 不见了。而这也只是加深了同一个错觉。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I might be mistaken somewhere, but I don't think that was still the same world.{w} However, what happened later? We did reunite with the Sai who'd traveled in the event room, didn't we?{w} Similarly, Akaro and the other Sai weren't found again. It was as if we'd gone back to our world.
entries.new: 也许我在某处弄错了，但我觉得那已经不是同一个世界。{w} 可是后来呢？我们确实和那位在活动室里穿越的 Sai 重逢了，不是吗？{w} 而 Akaro 和另一个 Sai 也再没被找到。就好像我们回到了自己的世界。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I wonder... Does that hypothesis solve every mystery surrounding that travel?{w} What about the range? It was bigger than previous fifteen-minute travels, wasn't it?{w} ...Two functional Sekimeiya existed.{w} If their ranges overlapped, the Sekimeiya's effect wouldn't just be time travel.{w} I think that could be right. It's not an idea that can only be applied in that instance.
entries.new: 我在想……那个假设能解开围绕那次穿越的所有谜团吗？{w} 范围又该怎么解释？它比以往十五分钟的穿越更大，不是吗？{w}……当时有两个能运作的 Sekimeiya。{w} 如果它们的范围发生重叠，Sekimeiya 的效果就不只是时间穿越了。{w} 我觉得这有可能。这个想法不只适用于那一次。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Where is everyone? The Sekimeiya was just activated when both of them were close to each other on the crystal floor, and it doesn't seem like the others are still in this tower.{w} How did I get to this world? Could it really be the same one we briefly visited?{w} This morning, Shiroya and I witnessed the Sekimeiya teleport. But that isn't what's been going on—the Sekimeiya isn't teleporting. It only appears that way because the entire world is changing.
entries.new: 大家都去哪了？两个 Sekimeiya 在水晶层上彼此靠近时，其中一个刚被启动，而其他人似乎已经不在这座塔里了。{w} 我是怎么来到这个世界的？难道这真的是我们短暂造访过的那个世界？{w} 今天早晨，Shiroya 和我亲眼看见 Sekimeiya 传送。可事情并不是这样——Sekimeiya 并没有在传送。它看起来是这样，只是因为整个世界都在改变。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: When it happened, we found the Sekimeiya inside a cabinet in room B4. It's very possible the other one was hidden nearby.{w} That's why Naomi was running to the attic with both Sekimeiya immediately after it disappeared.{w} We chased her up, but in the attic's staircase, Shiroya disappeared.{w} When I looked at the living room, both Sekimeiya were next to each other, and one of them was gray. As a result, neither Naomi nor Shiroya are here.
entries.new: 那件事发生时，我们在 B4 室的展示柜里发现了 Sekimeiya。另一个很可能就藏在附近。{w} 所以它一消失，Naomi 就带着两个 Sekimeiya 跑向阁楼。{w} 我们追了上去，可就在阁楼的楼梯上，Shiroya 消失了。{w} 我看向客厅时，两个 Sekimeiya 并排放在一起，其中一个已经变成灰色。结果，Naomi 和 Shiroya 都不在这里了。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Lastly, though... this would answer the question of how Naomi's corpse appeared two times.{w} If Naomi touched the Sekimeiya and the world around her changed, she would've appeared in the attic. Her keys had been left behind, so she had no way to leave.{w} That's what happened. That's what we saw on the floor of the living room. That's why we found Naomi dead twice.{w} The Naomi that Shiroya disappeared with was one of the two bodies that we found dead. ...Does this mean that version of Shiroya was there since the beginning?
entries.new: 最后……这也能解释 Naomi 的尸体为何会出现两次。{w} 如果 Naomi 触碰了 Sekimeiya，周围的世界随之改变，她就会出现在阁楼里。她的钥匙被留在了原地，所以她没法离开。{w} 事情就是这样。那就是我们在客厅地板上看到的情景。也正因如此，我们才会两次发现 Naomi 死去。{w} 和 Shiroya 一起消失的那个 Naomi，就是我们发现的两具尸体之一。……这是否意味着，那个 Shiroya 从一开始就在那里？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: "The Naomi that Shiroya disappeared with was one of the two bodies that we found dead."
entries.new: “和 Shiroya 一起消失的那个 Naomi，就是我们发现的两具尸体之一。”
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That is...
entries.new: 那就是……
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Unfortunately, it is not correct. While it's understandable for Atsuki to have made that mistake, I thought perhaps you had realized the flaw.
entries.new: 很遗憾，这不对。Atsuki 会犯这个错也情有可原，不过我原以为你已经看出破绽了。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Indeed, it is incorrect. While it's understandable for Atsuki to have made that mistake, I figured you would've realized the flaw.
entries.new: 确实不对。Atsuki 会犯这个错可以理解，但我本以为你已经看出破绽了。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...So, if I activate the Sekimeiya right now, will I go back to the other world?
entries.new: ……那么，如果我现在启动 Sekimeiya，我会回到另一个世界吗？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: When Shiroya disappeared, she wasn't in the living room yet, meaning that she didn't leave any footprints...
entries.new: Shiroya 消失时，她还没有进客厅，也就是说她没有留下任何脚印……
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I wondered earlier how I'd be here for twelve hours without being found when the searches we executed would've found me. Of course, in this world, this doesn't apply. Everyone is gone.
entries.new: 我之前还在想，既然我们展开的搜索应该能找到我，我怎么可能在这里待了十二个小时还没被发现。当然，在这个世界里，这并不适用。所有人都不见了。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Where are they, though? Am I really correct in what I'm thinking?{w} Everyone who was in hallway B is no longer in this world. If that is the case, are they in the world I came from?
entries.new: 可是，他们去哪了？我的想法真的正确吗？{w} 原本在 B走廊 的所有人都不在这个世界了。如果是这样，他们是在我来的那个世界吗？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Is that possible? ...It might be, but it doesn't feel right. After all, if this is the world where I was when Erina touched the Sekimeiya, Sai and Akaro must eventually come back.
entries.new: 有这种可能吗？……也许有，可总觉得不对。毕竟，如果这里就是 Erina 触碰 Sekimeiya 时我所在的世界，那么 Sai 和 Akaro 终究会回来。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It was a speculative mess, especially because I couldn't prove anything. However, the fundamental basis that I was working with seemed correct.
entries.new: 那只是一团乱糟糟的推测，尤其因为我无法证明任何一点。不过，我所依据的基本前提似乎没错。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What exactly were the body double mysteries? I can't understand Shiroya's case at all, and I'm not sure about Sai's.{w} Isla's, though... Could her "friend" have been the Isla from this world?
entries.new: 那些替身之谜究竟是怎么回事？Shiroya 的情况我完全想不通，Sai 的我也说不准。{w} 但 Isla 的……她那位“朋友”会不会就是这个世界的 Isla？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: "From this world"... I don't know what the hell to think, and that's mostly due to the most blatant example: the second Akaro.{w} The Akaro who had different memories and disappeared from the bedroom. Did he come from a different world in the way that I'm thinking?{w} If so, he couldn't have been the Akaro from this world because he didn't know who Katei was, but he did know Shiroya.
entries.new: “来自这个世界”……我根本不知道该怎么想，而这多半是因为最明显的例子：第二个 Akaro。{w} 那个记忆不同、从卧室里消失的 Akaro。他是不是以我所想的那种方式，来自另一个世界？{w} 若是如此，他就不可能是这个世界的 Akaro，因为他不认识 Katei，却认识 Shiroya。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Now, what have you been thinking all this time? Do you have your own answers?
entries.new: 那么，你一直以来都在想些什么？你自己有答案了吗？
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: First off, what is the explanation behind that Akaro?
entries.new: 首先，那个 Akaro 究竟该怎么解释？
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Correct.{w} A world beyond Atsuki's knowledge.
entries.new: 正确。{w} 那是 Atsuki 认知之外的世界。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That's not it.
entries.new: 不是这样。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The explanation is a world beyond Atsuki's knowledge.
entries.new: 答案在于 Atsuki 认知之外的世界。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: So, where did that Akaro come from?{w} Could he have come from a world without Katei?{w} If that's it, though, this is too fucking confusing! Could changing worlds bring me to any kind of world? There could be infinite worlds, and the Sekimeiya could act as random bridges between them!
entries.new: 那么，那个 Akaro 是从哪来的？{w} 他会不会来自一个没有 Katei 的世界？{w} 可要真是这样，这也太他妈让人糊涂了！世界切换会把我带到任何一种世界吗？世界也许有无数个，而 Sekimeiya 可能在它们之间随机架起桥梁！
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Now, tell him. Although he can't hear you, tell him why he's wrong.
entries.new: 现在，告诉他。虽然他听不见你，也要告诉他错在哪里。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Yes. Only three different worlds exist.
entries.new: 没错。不同的世界只有三个。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: How did you know that, though? How could you be sure of such a powerful assertion?
entries.new: 不过，你是怎么知道的？这么笃定的判断，你怎么能保证？
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: No. The answer is three.
entries.new: 不。答案是三。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Now that you know, perhaps you have an idea of how you could've asserted that fact.
entries.new: 既然你已经知道了，或许也想到了自己本可以如何断定这一点。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...Why is it proven that there are not infinite worlds? Why can't a fourth one exist?
entries.new: ……为什么能证明世界不是无限的？为什么不能存在第四个？
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Because the three worlds loop. Congratulations.
entries.new: 因为三个世界构成了循环。恭喜。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That is the essential core of the universe you've witnessed. Through the Sekimeiya, the link between three worlds looped. The three sides of the mountain spun around, leading to a single peak.
entries.new: 这就是你所见证的宇宙的核心本质。借助 Sekimeiya，三个世界之间的联结形成了循环。山的三个侧面旋转交汇，最终归于同一座峰顶。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...Why is it proven that there are not infinite worlds? Why can't a fourth one exist?
entries.new: ……为什么能证明世界不是无限的？为什么不能存在第四个？
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It is because the three worlds loop. That is the essential core of the universe you've witnessed.{w} Through the Sekimeiya, the link between three worlds looped. The three sides of the mountain spun around, leading to a single peak.
entries.new: 因为三个世界构成了循环。这就是你所见证的宇宙的核心本质。{w} 借助 Sekimeiya，三个世界之间的联结形成了循环。山的三个侧面旋转交汇，最终归于同一座峰顶。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But that doesn't answer all the questions, does it? Why only three worlds?
entries.new: 但这并不能解答所有疑问，不是吗？为什么偏偏只有三个世界？
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki correctly figured out the Sekimeiya's core secret.{w} In each world, two Sekimeiya existed. When one was activated, the active range sent anyone encompassed in it through time.{w} However, if both ranges overlapped, whoever found themselves present within both were not transported through time and space, but through worlds.
entries.new: Atsuki 准确解开了 Sekimeiya 的核心秘密。{w} 每个世界里都存在两台 Sekimeiya。激活其中一台时，生效范围会将范围内的人送往另一段时间。{w} 然而，若两个范围发生重叠，同时处在两者之中的人便不会被送往另一个时间，而是会被送往另一个世界。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: This effect is called a world switch, although the full extent of the name might not make a lot of sense to you yet.{w} Like everything about the Sekimeiya, the world switch hid many secrets of its own. Of course, you may have figured some of them out with the tools you were given.
entries.new: 这种现象被称为世界切换，不过这个名称的全部含义，你现在或许还无法完全理解。{w} 如同 Sekimeiya 的一切，世界切换本身也藏着许多秘密。当然，凭借手中的工具，你可能已经解开了其中一些。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: There is one world in which only Atsuki is found alive in the tower. He is suspected of having been behind multiple crimes, but his life is suddenly cut short as he looks through a window.
entries.new: 有一个世界里，塔中只有 Atsuki 一人被找到时还活着。他虽被怀疑是数起案件的主谋，却就在望向窗外时突然丧命。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That world will be called "A".
entries.new: 那个世界就称为“A”。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: If that world is "A", then the world in which everyone survived and left the tower...
entries.new: 如果那个世界是“A”，那么所有人都幸存下来并离开塔的那个世界……
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: No. That world is "C".
entries.new: 不。那个世界是“C”。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "B" is the world in which the recorder was present. At {time=21}, Atsuki, Sai, and Erina weren't able to escape.
entries.new: “B”是录音笔所在的世界。到了 {time=21}，Atsuki、Sai 和 Erina 没能逃出去。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Exactly. It is "C".
entries.new: 没错，就是“C”。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Then, "B" is the world in which the recorder was present. At {time=21}, Atsuki, Sai, and Erina weren't able to escape.
entries.new: 那么，“B”就是录音笔所在的世界。到了 {time=21}，Atsuki、Sai 和 Erina 没能逃出去。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: By world switching from world A, people were brought to...
entries.new: 借助 A 世界的世界切换，众人被带到了……
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Yes. This is the way the worlds looped.
entries.new: 对。世界就是这样循环起来的。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Incorrect. The answer is "B".
entries.new: 不对，答案是“B”。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: You've seen a few instances of full loops. Miiya's group went from their own world, C, to world A. From world A they went to world B, and then from world B they went back to world C.{w} Shiroya, after traveling from January 5th to December 15th, went from world B to world C with Atsuki. In the attic, she went from world C to world A with Naomi, and she finally returned alone to world B. The order is A - B - C - A.
entries.new: 你已经见过几次完整的循环。Miiya 一行人从她们所在的 C世界 前往 A世界。接着从 A世界 到 B世界，再从 B世界 回到 C世界。{w} Shiroya 从1月5日穿越到12月15日后，与 Atsuki 一同从 B世界 来到 C世界。在阁楼里，她又和 Naomi 从 C世界 到了 A世界，最后独自返回 B世界。顺序是 A - B - C - A。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Worlds A and C were drastically different, as the worlds followed an intrinsic progression with each other. However, as strange as it might seem, there was only a single degree of separation between C and A.
entries.new: A世界与 C世界截然不同，因为各个世界之间遵循着一种内在的递进关系。然而，说来奇怪，C 与 A 之间却只隔了一层。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: There is, isn't there? I'm sure you can find instances that didn't follow that order—all of which had something in common.
entries.new: 确实有，不是吗？我相信你能找到一些不按这个顺序发生的例子——它们都有共同点。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: You don't think so? Can you not find any instances that didn't follow that order?{w} They do exist. If you find them, perhaps you'll notice what they had in common.
entries.new: 你不这么认为？难道找不到不按这个顺序发生的例子吗？{w} 那样的例子确实存在。只要找出来，或许你就会注意到它们的共同点。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The incident at the tower happened in all three worlds, but the outcome was vastly different.{w} Why?
entries.new: 塔中的事件在三个世界里都发生过，结果却大相径庭。{w} 为什么？
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The major difference in world A...
entries.new: A世界的主要差异在于……
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In world A, many people died. The major difference from the beginning was Katei's absence.
entries.new: 在 A世界，许多人丧命。最大的差异从一开始就是 Katei 不在。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The major difference from the beginning was Katei's absence.
entries.new: 最大的差异从一开始就是 Katei 不在。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In world A, only one Naomi was found. The major difference from the beginning was Katei's absence.
entries.new: 在 A世界，只找到了一个 Naomi。最大的差异从一开始就是 Katei 不在。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Katei put his plan into action: he put both real Sekimeiya in the suitcase he had prepared and moved to the secret door in the storeroom.
entries.new: Katei 开始执行他的计划：他把两台真正的 Sekimeiya 装进准备好的手提箱，然后来到储藏室的暗门前。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He felt the handle, but he quickly realized he had dropped the key in the hallway.
entries.new: 他摸到门把手，却很快意识到钥匙掉在了走廊里。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: While he was searching for it, Naomi found the suitcase and took it.
entries.new: 就在他寻找钥匙时，Naomi 发现了手提箱，把它拿走了。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Then, when Katei found the key, he attempted to unlock the secret door.
entries.new: 随后，Katei 找到钥匙，试图打开暗门。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: And he did. He was able to leave.
entries.new: 他成功了，本可以就此离开。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But he didn't step out. He saw the Sekimeiya had been taken before hearing Naomi's movements. His plan had been very close to succeeding, so he panicked.
entries.new: 但他没有迈出去。还没听到 Naomi 的动静，他就发现 Sekimeiya 已被拿走。计划本来只差一点就能成功，他因此慌了神。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He ran behind her desperately, but Naomi had a safe place: the attic.
entries.new: 他拼命追在她身后，但 Naomi 有一个安全的去处：阁楼。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He chased her up, but he recognized that going all the way was a mistake. He could never enter the final floor.
entries.new: 他一路追上去，却意识到一直追到顶是个错误。他根本进不了最顶层。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He tripped in the staircase leading to the fourth floor and distractedly walked back without realizing he'd dropped yet another key.
entries.new: 他在通往四楼的楼梯上绊了一跤，心神恍惚地往回走，浑然不觉自己又掉了一把钥匙。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The security room's.
entries.new: 监控室的钥匙。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That isn't right. Katei didn't have that key.{w} He dropped the security room's.
entries.new: 不对。Katei 没有那把钥匙。{w} 他掉的是监控室的钥匙。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That isn't right. He dropped the security room's.
entries.new: 不对。他掉的是监控室的钥匙。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: You remember that Atsuki found it there, but that didn't happen in world A, did it? That was in world C.{w} You might know who found the key in world A. It was Akaro. Although many things were different, Atsuki only came across it in world C because Katei had been staring at the floor, and he wasn't there in world A.
entries.new: 你记得是 Atsuki 在那里发现了钥匙，但这件事并没有发生在 A 世界，对吧？那是在 C 世界。{w} 你也许知道 A 世界里是谁发现了钥匙：Akaro。虽然许多事情都不一样，但 Atsuki 之所以会在 C 世界偶然发现钥匙，是因为 Katei 当时一直盯着地板看，而 A 世界里没有 Katei。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: His mind threatening to collapse in on itself, Katei realized his only option was to escape from the building as quickly as possible.
entries.new: Katei 脑中乱得几乎要崩裂，他明白自己只有一条路：尽快逃出这栋建筑。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He left through the storeroom before the others woke up. Outside, he was fast enough to meet up with everyone else who'd evacuated. He knew the floor 2 cameras had recorded him, but he was confident he could take care of that at {time=21.}
entries.new: 其他人醒来之前，他从储藏室离开了。到了外面，他脚程够快，追上了其他已经疏散出来的人。他知道二楼的监控拍到了自己，但有把握在 {time=21.} 处理好。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Meanwhile, in world C, everything happened similarly. However, when Katei attempted to unlock the storeroom door, he couldn't. Something prevented him from doing so.{w} Like in world A, he heard Naomi's movements and chased her up, dropping the key in the same staircase.
entries.new: 与此同时，C 世界里的一切也大致相同。然而，Katei 试图打开储藏室的门时却没能成功。有什么东西阻碍了他。{w} 就像在 A 世界一样，他听见 Naomi 的动静后追了上去，又在那段楼梯上掉了钥匙。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...So, what about world B? What happened to the security room key in that world?
entries.new: ……那么 B 世界呢？监控室的钥匙在那个世界怎么样了？
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The truth is that Katei didn't drop it.
entries.new: 其实，Katei 并没有弄掉那把钥匙。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: How is that possible? Why did that differ between worlds?
entries.new: 怎么可能？为什么不同世界会有这种差异？
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The answer is tied to something else that only occurred in B.
entries.new: 答案与另一件只在 B 世界发生的事有关。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...It was the handle's removal.{w} In world B, Katei went to the secret door, ready to leave. However, he immediately felt it with his hand: the handle wasn't there.
entries.new: ……问题出在门把手上。{w} 在 B 世界，Katei 来到暗门前，准备离开。然而他伸手一摸，立刻察觉：门把手不见了。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He couldn't believe it—he had been outsmarted. Speechless, he froze in place.
entries.new: 他不敢相信——自己竟被人抢先一步。他一句话也说不出，僵在原地。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Of course, as the keyhole had been in the handle, he couldn't even attempt to unlock the door. That is why he didn't notice that he'd dropped the rusty key in hallway A, and it's why Naomi didn't have the chance to take his suitcase.
entries.new: 钥匙孔本就开在把手上，他连试着开锁都做不到。也正因如此，他没察觉自己把生锈的钥匙掉在了 A 走廊；也正因如此，Naomi 才没机会拿走他的手提箱。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He understood that he would have to stay in the tower, but he didn't immediately give up. Xyn's Sekimeiya was still in the event room, and perhaps he could make use of it.{w} Katei sighed deeply, trying to figure out who could've known about the storeroom's secret.
entries.new: 他明白自己只能留在塔里，却没有就此放弃。Xyn 的 Sekimeiya 还在活动室，或许还能派上用场。{w}Katei 深深叹了口气，思索着究竟有谁会知道储藏室的秘密。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Before anyone could see him, he went to a crystal room in hallway B; he had been told that refrigeration was essential to keep the Sekimeiya stable.
entries.new: 趁没人看见，他去了 B 走廊的一间水晶展室；他听说过，要让 Sekimeiya 保持稳定，冷藏必不可少。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He had independently learned that Ashiya had two identical Sekimeiya, but it wasn't public knowledge. Hence, abusing Xyn's plan still seemed feasible: he could keep a Sekimeiya for himself as long as Ashiya found Xyn's fake in the cabinet. That was why he left each Sekimeiya inside different cabinets in room B4.
entries.new: 他私下打听到，芦屋手上有两个一模一样的 Sekimeiya，但这件事并未公开。因此，他觉得仍可把 Xyn 的计划反过来利用：只要芦屋在展示柜里找到 Xyn 的赝品，他就能私吞一个 Sekimeiya。正因如此，他把两个 Sekimeiya 分别放进了水晶展室 B4 的两个展示柜。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He came to the conclusion that it was a good idea to let the suitcase be found. As he disposed of it, he heard a sound coming from the crystal room he'd just been in.
entries.new: 他断定，让人发现那只手提箱反倒有利。就在他处理手提箱时，听见自己刚离开的水晶展室传来声响。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He ran there and saw one of the Sekimeiya on the floor: Atsuki and Shiroya had just world switched to world C.
entries.new: 他跑回去，看见其中一个 Sekimeiya 落在地上：Atsuki 和 Shiroya 刚刚切换到了 C 世界。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He couldn't comprehend it. The Sekimeiya was gray, but nobody was there. Nobody could've escaped after he'd heard the sound.
entries.new: 他无法理解。那是个灰色 Sekimeiya，可现场空无一人。他听到声音之后，不可能有人已经逃掉。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Yet, one of the cabinets was open...{w} It was impossible anyone had been there, and the cabinet's temperature hadn't even cooled off yet. He hurriedly put the Sekimeiya back in, still trying to process what could've happened.
entries.new: 然而，有一个展示柜敞开着……{w}刚才不可能有人在那里，柜里的温度甚至还没降下来。他匆匆把 Sekimeiya 放回去，脑中仍在琢磨究竟发生了什么。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When he left the room, he saw Erina's group on the floor of the hallway. She was moving slightly, so Katei felt trapped. He didn't want her to wake up and see him leaving.{w} Slowly, he walked over and crouched beside the three incapacitated people.
entries.new: 他走出展室，看见 Erina 一行人倒在走廊的地上。她微微动着，Katei 顿时觉得自己被困住了。他不愿她醒来时撞见自己离开。{w}他缓缓走过去，在那三个失去意识的人身旁蹲下。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: So, doesn't this beg the same question? Why was the handle taken off in B?
entries.new: 那么，这不就引出同一个问题了吗？B世界的门把手为什么会被卸下来？
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: To begin with, who do you think was responsible for that?
entries.new: 那么首先，你觉得是谁干的？
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Yes. It was Akaro A.
entries.new: 没错。是 Akaro A。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That's not right.{w} The person who removed the secret door's handle in world B was Akaro A.
entries.new: 不对。{w}在B世界卸下暗门把手的人，是 Akaro A。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He was the main person behind the attack. In his world, however, Xyn were outsmarted.{w} The alarm Xyn didn't know about went off, and the Sekimeiya Akaro had hidden in the cleaning cart was taken.
entries.new: 他是这次袭击的主谋。然而在他的世界里，Xyn 反被人算计了。{w}Xyn 不知道的警报响了，Akaro 藏在清洁车里的 Sekimeiya 被人拿走。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Who had been responsible? For a while, Akaro had no idea.
entries.new: 那究竟是谁干的？有一阵子，Akaro 毫无头绪。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: However, eventually, he world switched to B with Isla.
entries.new: 不过，他最终还是和 Isla 一起切换到了B世界。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In that world, he was surprised to find out the attic was unlocked, and even more so to see that everyone was taking shelter inside a bedroom.{w} There, he learned about two things: Katei's presence in the tower and the existence of the storeroom's secret.{w} Naturally, he knew who Katei Kuiji was, but he shouldn't have been there. Akaro had suspected someone from Ashiya had hindered their plan, so he was internally taken aback when he heard details about that world's events.
entries.new: 在那个世界，他惊讶地发现阁楼没有上锁，更惊讶的是所有人都躲在某间卧室里避难。{w}在那里，他得知了两件事：Katei 就在塔里，以及储藏室藏有暗门。{w}他自然知道 Katei Kuiji 是什么人，但那人本不该出现在这里。Akaro 一直怀疑是芦屋的人妨碍了他们的计划，所以听到那个世界事件的细节时，他心里暗自震惊。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Soon, that Akaro traveled to the past and appeared on the 24th of November. You remember what Shiroya thought, don't you?
entries.new: 不久之后，那个 Akaro 穿越到过去，出现在了11月24日。你还记得 Shiroya 当时是怎么想的吧？
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Out of nowhere, he appeared in a detention cell, but he was able to leave it. Then, he realized he was in the far past.{w} He recalled the times Katei had chosen to speak to Ido: he must've been who had interfered with Xyn's plan.
entries.new: 他毫无征兆地出现在一间拘留室里，却顺利离开了。随后他意识到，自己身处遥远的过去。{w}他回想起 Katei 几次主动找 Ido 说话的情形：干扰 Xyn 计划的，一定就是此人。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Katei hadn't been in the tower, yet everyone had eventually claimed he'd been there since the start. It wasn't hard to suspect the truth.{w} However, Akaro still couldn't believe what he'd done. In the tower, desperate to fulfill Xyn's plan...
entries.new: Katei 本不在塔里，可到头来所有人都说他从一开始就在。要猜到真相并不难。{w}然而，Akaro 仍不敢相信自己做了什么。在塔里，他为了完成 Xyn 的计划不惜一切……
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: How had Shiroya come back to life? ...And she had clearly been aware of what he'd done.{w} Why had she not said anything, then? Akaro had no idea why she had come back, but he had been next to her and Atsuki for hours; he'd seen how they'd turned out after he'd caused the death of their friend.
entries.new: Shiroya 是怎么死而复生的？……而且她显然知道他做过什么。{w}那她为什么一句都没说？Akaro 完全不明白她为何会回来，但他曾在 Shiroya 和 Atsuki 身边待了好几个小时；他亲眼看到，在自己害死他们的朋友之后，两人变成了什么样子。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: At first, when he appeared in November, Akaro thought of what to do. He could take advantage of it—he knew what would happen.{w} Yet his remorse soon overcame him. His greatest wish was to walk away, and he had the opportunity to do so. The plan was going to be a failure, but he was no longer in his world. Perhaps he could let his other self take the blame while he tried to atone for his actions...
entries.new: 刚出现在11月时，Akaro 还在盘算该怎么办。他本可以利用这一切——他知道接下来会发生什么。{w}可愧疚很快压过了这个念头。他最大的心愿就是一走了之，而现在他正好有这样的机会。计划注定要失败，但他已不在自己的世界里。或许他可以让另一个自己去背这个罪责，而自己设法赎罪……
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Of course, due to a certain perspective you've viewed, you know that's not what happened.
entries.new: 当然，从你先前看到的某个视角来看，事情并没有那样发展。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In any case, Akaro's actions significantly changed the start of world B's incident. Katei didn't know he'd dropped the rusty key, and Naomi didn't run to the attic with the suitcase.
entries.new: 总之，Akaro 的举动大大改变了B世界事件的开端。Katei 不知道自己弄丢了生锈的钥匙，Naomi 也没有拎着手提箱跑向阁楼。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In worlds A and C, however, the same thing occurred. In the attic, Naomi touched the Sekimeiya and world switched.{w} When Naomi A touched it, she appeared in world B. Her keys remained in world A, and the elevator was disabled. Until that changed, she was trapped up there.{w} From her point of view, both Sekimeiya disappeared, as she brought the suitcase along as one of her possessions.
entries.new: 然而在A世界和C世界，发生的是同一件事。Naomi 在阁楼触碰到 Sekimeiya，世界切换了。{w}Naomi A 触碰它时，出现在B世界。她的钥匙留在了A世界，电梯也无法使用。在情况改变之前，她一直被困在上面。{w}在她看来，两个 Sekimeiya 都消失了，因为手提箱作为她的随身物品也被一并带了过来。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: However, Naomi C's outcome was different.{w} She world switched to world A, and the range encompassed Shiroya as well.{w} Even though the attic was locked, they weren't trapped. Not only did Shiroya have the key, but so did Naomi: although she'd changed worlds, she grabbed the keys Naomi A had left behind, unaware they were no longer hers.
entries.new: 但 Naomi C 的结果不同。{w}她切换到了A世界，重叠范围也把 Shiroya 包含了进去。{w}尽管阁楼上了锁，她们却没有被困住。Shiroya 有钥匙，Naomi 也有：她虽已换了世界，却顺手拿上了 Naomi A 留下的钥匙，并不知道那已不属于她。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In addition, she brought the suitcase along too, but the Sekimeiya Naomi A had used were both still there. As both Naomis world switched at exactly the same time, for Naomi C, it only seemed as though the Sekimeiya she'd touched turned gray, even though it was the one Naomi A had activated.{w} Instinctively, what she did was touch the other Sekimeiya, unable to believe her finger had changed a gem's color. When she did, she traveled through time: since one of the Sekimeiya was powered off, there was no world switch.
entries.new: 此外，她也把手提箱带了过来，但 Naomi A 用过的两个 Sekimeiya 都还在原处。由于两个 Naomi 是在同一瞬间切换世界的，在 Naomi C 看来，就只是自己碰过的那个 Sekimeiya 变成了灰色，尽管那其实是 Naomi A 激活的那一个。{w}她无法相信自己的手指能让宝石变色，便本能地去碰了另一个 Sekimeiya。这一碰，她穿越了时间：因为其中一个 Sekimeiya 已经断电，所以没有发生世界切换。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Although these beginning sequences evolved into drastically different days, some of the differences between worlds came from before the 15th.
entries.new: 这些开端虽然发展成了截然不同的几天，但世界之间的某些差异，早在15日之前就已经存在。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Isla's friend only existed in world B. In the other worlds, Isla hadn't been assured everything would go smoothly; nobody had told her she'd be able to touch the Sekimeiya. Hence, her mood was more dampened, and Erina's was lighter.
entries.new: Isla 的朋友只存在于B世界。在其他世界，没人向 Isla 保证一切都会顺利，也没人告诉她她可以触碰 Sekimeiya。因此她情绪更低落，Erina 反倒轻松些。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Sai sniffed out that something would occur on the day of the event. However, only in world B was he certain—he had read a forum thread that foretold what would unfold in the tower. In that world, he was much more active from the start.
entries.new: Sai 察觉到活动当天会出事。但只有在B世界，他才确信无疑——他读过一篇论坛帖子，预告了塔中将会发生什么。在那个世界，他从一开始就活跃得多。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In world A, Akaro couldn't see Katei as his enemy, so his attitude toward the others was rougher and sterner.{w} In addition, the article detailing his escape from prison only existed in world B.
entries.new: 在A世界，Akaro 无法把 Katei 视为敌人，所以他对待其他人的态度更加粗暴严厉。{w}此外，详细报道他越狱的那篇文章只存在于B世界。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In world C, Katei's Sekimeiya were taken by Naomi, so his priorities were very different. In world B, Katei had to step up to Erina's group, while in world C, he saw room A5 by himself before everyone else regained consciousness.
entries.new: 在C世界，Katei 的 Sekimeiya 被 Naomi 拿走了，所以他的侧重点就截然不同了。在B世界，Katei 不得不挺身面对 Erina 一行人；而在C世界，他趁其他人还没恢复意识，独自去查看了水晶展室 A5。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Do you think there's a relation between all these changes?
entries.new: 你觉得这些变化之间有关联吗？
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: There certainly is one: they were all caused by someone from another world.
entries.new: 当然有关联：它们全都出自另一个世界来的人之手。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That's it. They were caused by someone from another world.
entries.new: 正是如此。这些变化都是另一个世界来的人造成的。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: No, they had an origin. The actual relation is that they were all caused by someone from another world.
entries.new: 不，它们是有源头的。真正的关联在于，它们全都是另一个世界的人造成的。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Up to the 24th of November, all the worlds were identical.{w} You might be familiar with the many-worlds interpretation. According to it, every choice splits the world, leading into infinite worlds which are infinitely different.
entries.new: 在11月24日之前，所有世界都完全相同。{w}你或许听说过多重世界诠释。照这种说法，每一个选择都会分裂世界，衍生出无穷多个彼此千差万别的世界。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In these three worlds, the initial difference came in November of 2011, and it was caused due to someone who had world switched from another world.{w} In other words, there was no change that wasn't influenced by another world—if zero world switches had occurred, each of the three worlds would've remained identical.
entries.new: 在这三个世界中，最初的差异出现在2011年11月，起因是有人从另一个世界切换而来。{w}换句话说，没有任何变化不是受另一个世界影响——假如一次世界切换都不曾发生，这三个世界至今仍会完全相同。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Only they caused reality to differ. It was the world switches that shaped this maze—a maze whose walls could be broken.
entries.new: 正因为他们，现实才产生了分歧。是这些世界切换造就了这座迷宫——一座墙壁可以被打破的迷宫。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: There are numerous enigmas around the world switch. Perhaps you have some lingering questions.{w} When Akaro A appeared in world B, the storeroom had been sealed by his future self. However, in part, that helped him go back in time and seal it. Doesn't that seem contradictory? If he had appeared in a world without a sealed storeroom, he wouldn't have been able to go back and seal it... You might find a number of similar cases.{w} For that, you can look at the people who world switched and the way they shaped their new world. If the answer escapes you, that's where you will find it, alongside the real form of the world switch.
entries.new: 围绕世界切换，还有许多谜团。你或许仍有疑问。{w}当 Akaro A 出现在B世界时，储藏室已经被他未来的自己封上了。然而在某种程度上，正是这一点促使他回到过去将其封上。这看上去岂不自相矛盾？如果他出现的那个世界里储藏室并没有被封锁，他就无法回去把它封上……类似的情形你或许还能找出不少。{w}要看清楚，你可以去看看那些世界切换的人，以及他们如何塑造自己的新世界。若你想不出答案，那里便藏着答案，也藏着世界切换的真实面貌。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Hm...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I couldn't just think that infinite worlds existed. After all, it was possible I was going back and forth between two.{w} The first time, Erina had brought us to a different world, but we had eventually returned. When we'd later traveled back to that morning, Shiroya and I had changed worlds, but I suspected that we'd appeared in the same one again. That was why thinking that infinite worlds existed was a bit of a leap.
entries.new: 我不能就此认定存在无穷多个世界。毕竟，我也可能只是在两个世界之间来回。{w}第一次，Erina 把我们带到了另一个世界，但最后我们还是回去了。后来我们穿越回那天早晨时，Shiroya 和我切换了世界，可我怀疑我们又一次落在了同一个世界。所以说，断言存在无穷多个世界，还是有些操之过急。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked at both Sekimeiya. If I touched one, would the world around me really change?
entries.new: 我看着那两个 Sekimeiya。如果碰其中一个，身边的世界真的会改变吗？
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What about the range, the replicated location, the time traveled, and all that nonsense?
entries.new: 那重叠范围、复制的位置、穿越的时间，还有那一堆乱七八糟的东西呢？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I stepped into the kitchen.
entries.new: 我走进了厨房。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Can the refrigerator act like the cold cabinet?
entries.new: ……冰箱能当那种冷藏展示柜用吗？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I opened it and put my hand inside. While it was cold, the temperature didn't seem as low as the Sekimeiya cabinet's.
entries.new: 我打开冰箱，把手伸了进去。里面确实冷，但温度似乎不如放 Sekimeiya 的展示柜那么低。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was a regulation mechanism inside, so I changed it to the coldest setting.
entries.new: 里面有调节装置，我就把它调到了最冷的一档。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I shut a Sekimeiya inside the refrigerator for a few seconds.{w} When I took it out, I felt it through my shirt.
entries.new: 我把一块 Sekimeiya 关进冰箱里，放了几秒。{w}取出来时，我隔着衬衫感受它的温度。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It did work. It was pretty hot before, and now it's not.
entries.new: 确实有效。刚才还烫得很，现在已经不热了。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: So, as long as I keep a Sekimeiya in here, I might not be encompassed within two ranges.
entries.new: 也就是说，只要我把一块 Sekimeiya 一直放在里面，也许就不会同时落入两个范围。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I wasn't confident the concept of range I was working with was correct, though.
entries.new: 不过，我自己所设想的「范围」这一概念是否正确，我并没有把握。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I put both Sekimeiya inside to hopefully reset them. A few seconds later, I took one out and set it on the countertop.
entries.new: 我把两块 Sekimeiya 都放了进去，指望它们能借此重置。几秒后，我取出一块，放在流理台上。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Theoretically, it should begin to gather energy now, so I'll travel a short distance if I touch it soon.
entries.new: 按理论，它现在应该开始蓄能了。如果我马上碰它，大概只会移动一小段距离。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I counted up to a minute in my head. Then, I touched the Sekimeiya on the marble.
entries.new: 我在心里数满一分钟，然后碰了碰放在大理石台面上的那块 Sekimeiya。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}Hm? What just happened?
entries.new: ……{w}嗯？刚才怎么回事？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I was still in the kitchen, but I had teleported less than a step backward.
entries.new: 我仍在厨房里，只是传送到了身后不到一步的地方。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Huh? The Sekimeiya is powered off just where I touched it.
entries.new: 咦？Sekimeiya 就在我碰它的地方停止运作了。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Does that mean I traveled to the future? I think I only went a few seconds through time, and there's no past self of mine here.
entries.new: 难道说，我穿越到了未来？我记得只往前跳了几秒，而且这里也没有过去的我。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The Sekimeiya was gray, indicating that I was at a point after my travel. Surprised, I realized I really had traveled forward in time.
entries.new: 那块 Sekimeiya 是灰色的，说明我此刻身处穿越之后的时间点。我这才惊觉，自己真的穿越到了未来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What was the difference? Why didn't I travel to the past?
entries.new: 差别在哪里？为什么我没有穿越到过去？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And the location where I appeared... Why was it right next to where I touched the Sekimeiya?{w} It's as if I only moved a tiny bit because I only went a few seconds to the future.
entries.new: 还有我出现的位置……为什么恰好就在我碰 Sekimeiya 的地方旁边？{w}就好像因为我只往未来走了几秒，所以也只移动了一点点。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Hm...{w} I have an idea, but I don't think I can test it.
entries.new: 嗯……{w}我有个想法，不过恐怕没法验证。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Wait, no, maybe I can.
entries.new: 等等，不对——也许能验证。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: As soon as I put the Sekimeiya in the refrigerator, it regained its white color. However, I ignored that and ran to the staircase.
entries.new: 我刚把 Sekimeiya 放进冰箱，它就恢复了白色。但我没有理会，径直朝楼梯跑去。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It appeared the crystal floor was still empty, but I couldn't know for certain.
entries.new: 水晶层看上去还是空的，可我没法确认。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Quietly, I walked to the security room.
entries.new: 我放轻脚步，走向监控室。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: All the screens were still black, but they weren't my focus. I began to look everywhere I could.
entries.new: 所有屏幕仍是黑的，但那不是我要找的东西。我开始四处翻找。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai said he found the voice recorder here, but perhaps he hasn't yet. I might be able to get it in this world.
entries.new: Sai 说过他是在这里找到录音笔的，不过也许现在还没找到。在这个世界里，我也许能先拿到手。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And I did. Behind one of the monitors on the wall, I found the device that had been in Isla's purse.
entries.new: 我果然找到了。在墙上某台显示器背后，我摸到了那支原本在 Isla 包里的录音笔。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When I pressed the "record" button, a line appeared on the screen. Above it, numbers began to count the recorded seconds.
entries.new: 我按下「录音」键，屏幕上出现了一条线。线的上方，数字开始累计已录的秒数。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was no saved recording this time...
entries.new: 这一次里面没有已保存的录音……
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That wasn't strange. After all, the recorder in Isla's purse had to have traveled from the future, while the one in the security room was the original one.{w} However, my intention wasn't to record anything. I wanted to use the device as a timer that I could hold.
entries.new: 这并不奇怪。毕竟 Isla 包里的那支是从未来穿越而来的，监控室里的这一支才是原本的那支。{w}可我要的并不是录音。我只想把它当作可以随身带着的计时器。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Back in the attic, I entered the kitchen again. Both Sekimeiya were still in the refrigerator, but I didn't want to take one out yet.
entries.new: 回到阁楼，我又走进厨房。两块 Sekimeiya 都还在冰箱里，但我还不想取出来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Instead, I powered on the oven and set it to finish after ten minutes.
entries.new: 我转而打开烤箱，设定为十分钟后结束。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Then, at the same time that the oven began to count down, I pressed the record button. Immediately, the seconds began to count up on the device's screen.
entries.new: 接着，在烤箱开始倒计时的同时，我按下录音键。录音笔屏幕上的秒数随即开始递增。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: With this setup, I can know the amount of time I'm traveling.
entries.new: 这样一来，我就能知道自己穿越了多久。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I held the recorder in my hand so that it would always be in my possession. When the oven's timer showed nine minutes, the device had hit one minute.
entries.new: 我把录音笔握在手里，确保它始终跟着我。烤箱的计时显示九分钟时，录音笔刚好走到一分钟。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Meanwhile, I thought back on the many travels I'd experienced, wondering if there was any idea I could apply to every single one.
entries.new: 与此同时，我回想自己经历过的那些穿越，琢磨有没有哪条规律能适用于每一次。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When three minutes had been recorded, I took the Sekimeiya I'd last used out of the refrigerator and left it on the countertop.
entries.new: 录音笔走到三分钟时，我把上次用过的那块 Sekimeiya 从冰箱里取出，放在流理台上。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So, it's started gaining energy after three minutes have gone by.
entries.new: 也就是说，过了三分钟，它才开始蓄能。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I didn't stop staring at the ticking timer. A few seconds later, I brought my hand close to the Sekimeiya. I didn't touch it yet, though. I had to make sure I did so at the appropriate time.
entries.new: 我目不转睛地盯着跳动的计时。几秒后，我把手凑近那块 Sekimeiya，却没有碰它。我必须等到合适的时机再动手。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Above the Sekimeiya, my hand patiently hovered. As soon as the recorder and the oven hit five minutes, I touched it.
entries.new: 我的手悬在 Sekimeiya 上方，耐心地等着。录音笔和烤箱同时走到五分钟的那一刻，我碰了上去。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Once again, I'd hardly moved through space: I was still in the kitchen, staring at the Sekimeiya. However, it was gray, meaning that I was in the future.
entries.new: 这一次我几乎还是待在原地：人还在厨房，仍盯着那块 Sekimeiya。可它是灰色的，说明我身处未来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Immediately, I looked at the oven. Its timer indicated that four minutes and fifteen seconds still remained.{w} Right after that, I glanced at my own hand, eager to look at my timer.{w} The device was there.
entries.new: 我立刻去看烤箱，计时显示还剩四分十五秒。{w}紧接着，我低头看向自己的手，急着看自己的计时器。{w}录音笔还在手里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: 4:15... It's the same time!
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But while the device's screen changed to 4:16, the oven's timer went to 4:14.{w} Like before, the recorder kept counting up, whereas the oven counted down.
entries.new: 可录音笔的屏幕跳到 4:16 时，烤箱的计时却变成了 4:14。{w}和刚才一样，录音笔在递增，烤箱在倒数。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Huh...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I touched the Sekimeiya at the five-minute mark and went 45 seconds into the future. That's a little odd—the Sekimeiya gathered energy for two minutes. The times it gathered energy for fifteen minutes, we went twenty minutes through time.
entries.new: 我在计时器显示五分钟时碰了 Sekimeiya，往未来跳了四十五秒。这有点奇怪——它只蓄了两分钟的能量。而之前它蓄了十五分钟能量的时候，我们穿越了二十分钟。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The most important thing, though... is that although I went 45 seconds to the future, the recorder seems to have gone 45 seconds backward in time.
entries.new: 不过最关键的是……我虽然往未来走了四十五秒，录音笔却似乎往过去退回了四十五秒。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That must mean... that the replicated location was from 45 seconds before I touched the Sekimeiya.
entries.new: 也就是说……被复制的位置，是我碰 Sekimeiya 之前四十五秒时的位置。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That left me thinking, but the train of thought was interrupted by the Sekimeiya. It turned white a few seconds after my reappearance.
entries.new: 我正想得出神，思绪却被 Sekimeiya 打断了。我重新出现几秒后，它就变回了白色。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is strange too. It took almost two minutes to power back on, but it spent about five minutes powered off when Sai and Shiroya disappeared from the event room.
entries.new: 这一点也很奇怪。它花了将近两分钟才重新启动，可 Sai 和 Shiroya 在活动室消失那次，它停止运作了大约五分钟。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I had to do it again.{w} I turned off the oven and erased the recording. Next, I set the oven to five minutes and pressed the device's record button at the same time.{w} I left the Sekimeiya in the refrigerator until two minutes had elapsed. Then, thirty seconds later, when the recorder displayed 2:30, I touched the gem again.
entries.new: 我得再来一次。{w}我关掉烤箱，删除了录音。接着，我把烤箱设成五分钟，同时按下录音笔的录音键。{w}我让 Sekimeiya 在冰箱里放了两分钟。三十秒后，录音笔显示 2:30 时，我再次碰了那块晶体。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The immediate result was the same: I appeared in the kitchen, pretty much where I'd already been standing. I looked at both timers at once.{w} The two of them showed "2:21", yet the device's timer kept ticking up while the oven's counted down.
entries.new: 眼前的结果还是一样：我出现在厨房，差不多就在原先站立的地方。我同时看了两个计时。{w}两边都显示「2:21」，可录音笔的计时仍在递增，烤箱的却在倒数。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the fuck? Again, I went nine seconds to the future, but the location I appeared in was from nine seconds before touching the Sekimeiya.{w} Is this it? Does traveling to the future X amount of time replicate the location in space you were at X amount of time in the past?{w} What about traveling back, though? I've gone to the future three times in a row!
entries.new: 这他妈是怎么回事？又是这样——我向未来跳了九秒，落点却是我触碰 Sekimeiya 之前九秒所在的位置。{w}难道说，向未来穿越 X 秒，复制出来的就是你 X 秒前所在的空间位置？{w}可要是向过去穿越呢？我都已经连着三次跳往未来了！
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The only idea I had was to use the other Sekimeiya, so I put the one I'd been using in the refrigerator.
entries.new: 我能想到的唯一办法，就是换另一枚 Sekimeiya 试试。于是我把一直用的那枚放进了冰箱。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I set up the same conditions with the oven's timer at five minutes as I began a new recording.
entries.new: 我按同样的条件把烤箱定时器设为五分钟，同时开始新的录音。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That time, when two minutes had elapsed, I took the other Sekimeiya out. Thirty seconds later, I activated it.
entries.new: 那一次，等过了两分钟，我取出另一枚 Sekimeiya。三十秒后，我启动了它。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The result was almost identical. I appeared in the kitchen, very close to where I'd been.
entries.new: 结果几乎一模一样。我出现在厨房里，离原先的位置很近。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, someone was in front of me. It was my past self.
entries.new: 可有人站在我面前。是过去的我。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I remained completely still, just like a deer caught in headlights. The back of my own head was in front of my eyes.
entries.new: 我僵在原地，动也不动，活像被车灯照住的鹿。眼前正是我自己的后脑勺。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But it didn't remain there for long. Quickly, my figure disappeared, revealing the powered-off Sekimeiya.
entries.new: 可那身影没有停留多久。转眼间，我的人影消失了，露出已经关掉的 Sekimeiya。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I see... I just traveled through time, and the Sekimeiya's range was so small that it didn't pick me up again. It does seem like I went nine seconds to the past.{w} It's probably due to the Sekimeiya I used: this one makes you travel to the past, while the other sends you to the future.
entries.new: 原来如此……我刚刚完成了时间穿越，而 Sekimeiya 的作用范围太小，没能把我再次收进去。看来我确实是回到了九秒前。{w}原因大概出在我用的这枚 Sekimeiya 上：这一枚让人穿越到过去，另一枚则把人送往未来。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The oven's timer was at 2:25, so I hurried to look at the voice recorder as I thought about it.{w} I had gone nine seconds to the past, so upon appearing, the oven's timer would've been at 2:39. Then, I had waited out the nine seconds needed for my past self to disappear, and five extra seconds had elapsed since. Before the oven's timer counted down to 2:24, I looked at the device between my hands.
entries.new: 烤箱定时器显示 2:25，我一边琢磨，一边急忙去看录音笔。{w}我是回到了九秒前，所以刚出现时，烤箱定时器应该停在 2:39。之后我等到过去的自己消失，用掉九秒，又过了五秒。趁烤箱定时器还没跳到 2:24，我看向手中的录音笔。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The screen is blank! What the hell!?{w} Why? I can't know where this location is from!
entries.new: 屏幕一片空白！这算什么！？{w}为什么？这样一来，我根本没法知道这个位置是从哪儿来的！
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Traveling nine seconds to the future put me where I'd been nine seconds in the past!{w} Wouldn't traveling to the past put me—{w} ...{w}where I'd be nine seconds in the future.{w} And I'm still here, exactly where I appeared.
entries.new: 向未来跳九秒，会把我送到九秒前所在的地方！{w}那向过去跳，不就会把我送到——{w}……{w}九秒后我将会在的地方吗。{w}而我现在还待在这里，就是我出现的位置，一动没动。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But then why is the screen...
entries.new: 可既然如此，屏幕为什么……
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Wait,{w} no.{w} It might make sense.
entries.new: 等等，{w}不，{w}也许说得通。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Let's say the Sekimeiya is touched at time {b}t{/b}. In this case, {b}t{/b} is 2:30.{w} {b}X{/b} will refer to the travel time, which is nine seconds.
entries.new: 假设在时刻 {b}t{/b} 触碰 Sekimeiya。这里 {b}t{/b} 是 2:30。{w}再设 {b}X{/b} 为穿越时间，也就是九秒。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Let's assume that traveling {b}X{/b} seconds to the past copies your state {b}X{/b} seconds after touching the Sekimeiya. What would the time on the device be upon appearing?
entries.new: 假设向过去穿越 {b}X{/b} 秒，复制的是你触碰 Sekimeiya 后 {b}X{/b} 秒时的状态。那么出现时，设备上的时间是多少？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: {b}t+X{/b}, or 2:39.{w} Then {b}2X{/b} seconds would pass to reach the future state.
entries.new: 应是 {b}t+X{/b}，也就是 2:39。{w}可要抵达那个未来状态，还得再经过 {b}2X{/b} 秒。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The timer would read {b}t+3X{/b}, or 2:57, but that contradicts the past position.{w}  The timer at arrival would have to be {b}t+3X{/b}.
entries.new: 定时器会读到 {b}t+3X{/b}，即 2:57，但这与过去的位置不符。{w}照此推算，抵达时的定时器读数只能是 {b}t+3X{/b}。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But nothing stops this from continuing. Another {b}2X{/b} seconds would be added...
entries.new: 但没有什么能让它停下。还会再叠加 {b}2X{/b} 秒……
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The recorder's time would add up infinitely, and eventually its battery would run out.
entries.new: 录音笔上的时间会无限累加，电池迟早耗尽。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: This can't make sense, though.{w} If the replicated location is one that occurs after touching the Sekimeiya, we would die.
entries.new: 可这样根本说不通。{w}如果复制出的位置是触碰 Sekimeiya 之后才会出现的，那我们不就死定了。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Just like with the recorder's timer, my age would've increased by a few seconds repeatedly, making me die instantly upon traveling to the past.
entries.new: 就像录音笔的计时一样，我的年龄也会一次又一次地叠加几秒，向过去穿越的瞬间就会死掉。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: If the device aged in a loop until it ran out of batteries, its appearance would've changed too. It would've degraded, probably even disintegrated into nothing.
entries.new: 如果设备在循环中不断老化，直到电池耗尽，它的外观也会一起改变。它会老化，甚至可能崩散到什么都不剩。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: However, isn't this what happened... to Sai's watch?{w} Not only to Sai, but to a Sai who I have to assume traveled to the past. When I saw him, he should've been in the attic, so he'd come from the future. Later, I learned his watch had stopped working again.
entries.new: 然而……Sai 的手表，不正是这样吗？{w}不只是 Sai，而是一个我不得不假设穿越到了过去的 Sai。我见到他时，他本该待在阁楼，可见他是从未来回来的。后来我得知，他的手表又停了。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: If he appeared five minutes in the past where he would be ten minutes after his appearance... the time on his watch would've increased by ten minutes infinitely, and the battery would've eventually stopped working.{w} There's no way it would've lasted thousands of years, though, so what the hell?{w} And why would the watch's inner mechanism add up the looped time while its outer appearance wasn't affected?
entries.new: 如果他出现在五分钟前，而那个位置正是他出现十分钟后会在的地方……那手表上的时间就会以十分钟为单位无限累加，电池迟早撑不住。{w}可它绝不可能撑上几千年，这到底是怎么回事？{w}况且，为什么只有手表的内部机件在累加循环的时间，外表却毫无变化？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...The recorder isn't working anymore, so I can't keep testing.
entries.new: ……录音笔已经坏了，我没法再继续测试。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Wait, no. I can make it work again if what I've concluded is correct.{w} After all, just minutes ago, I was holding it when it worked. I just have to replicate that location, which should be easy. I only have to travel a couple minutes to the future.
entries.new: 等等，不对。只要我的推论没错，我就能让它重新工作。{w}毕竟就在几分钟前，我拿着它的时候它还是好的。我只要复制出那个位置就行，这应该不难。我只需要向未来跳几分钟。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That was what I did. I put the broken recorder in a drawer and traveled to the future. When I appeared, I was holding the device. The timer on its screen said 1:35, as it was still working.
entries.new: 我就这么做了。我把坏掉的录音笔放进抽屉，然后穿越到了未来。出现时，我手里正拿着那支录音笔。屏幕上的计时显示 1:35，它还在正常工作。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is definitely how traveling to the future works, then...
entries.new: 看来穿越到未来的原理，确实就是这样……
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But what about traveling to the past? Did all those travels work like this as well?
entries.new: 可穿越到过去呢？之前那几次也都是这样吗？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The first time I went to the past, I appeared in the lobby, right in front of the hallway A door. I later determined I'd gone about twenty minutes to the past.
entries.new: 第一次回到过去时，我出现在大厅，正对着 A走廊的门。后来我推算出，我大约回到了二十分钟前。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: So, twenty minutes after the point I touched the Sekimeiya...{w} I was in the lobby, right in front of the hallway A door. I was watching the hallway while the others looked through every room.
entries.new: 也就是说，在我触碰 Sekimeiya 之后二十分钟……{w}我就在大厅里，正对着 A走廊的门。当时其他人逐个房间搜查，我则守着走廊。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Seriously...? Is this what's been happening?
entries.new: 真的假的……？难道一直都是这样？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Later, Shiroya and I traveled about forty minutes to the past. I appeared in the security room, sitting down. However, the chair wasn't there to support me, so I fell to the floor.
entries.new: 后来，我和 Shiroya 一起回到了大约四十分钟前。我出现在监控室里，坐着。可那把椅子并不在那里，我一下子摔到了地上。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Forty minutes after the time we touched the Sekimeiya... I really was in the security room, looking at the computer. Sai had just run away from me, and I even looked at the time. I was there from {time=12:18} to {time=12:31.}
entries.new: 在我们触碰 Sekimeiya 之后四十分钟……我确实待在监控室里，盯着电脑。那时 Sai 刚从我这逃走，我还看过时间。从 {time=12:18} 到 {time=12:31.}，我一直都在那里。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Even Shiroya... She said she'd appeared in the second floor offices, and when we reunited outside the security room, she'd just been searching for me through every floor starting from the top. Both of us had just been in the locations we'd appeared.
entries.new: 就连 Shiroya 也是……她说她出现在二楼的办公室，我们在监控室外会合时，她才刚从顶层开始一层层找我。我们两个当时都正好待在自己出现的位置。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I could hardly believe it, but I finally knew the logic behind what had agonizingly eluded me: the replicated location.
entries.new: 我几乎不敢相信，可我终于弄明白了那个一直让我百思不得其解的东西——复制的位置。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But hang on... Does this mean that every time we touched the Sekimeiya and appeared in a location we recognized, we'd gone to the future? ...It's only traveling to the future that replicates a past coordinate you've been at.
entries.new: 可等等……难道说，每次我们触碰 Sekimeiya 后出现在一个我们认得出的地方，其实都是去了未来？……只有穿越到未来，才会复制你曾经待过的过去坐标。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: This is absurd, though! It doesn't even make sense!
entries.new: 这也太荒唐了！根本说不通！
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Why the hell did I appear in the security room in the past!? Because I was later in the security room? That's nonsense!
entries.new: 我到底为什么会出现在过去的监控室！？就因为后来我会待在监控室？胡说八道！
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Why the security room? If I had appeared in the attic, for example, I would've been somewhere else eighty minutes later! I was only in the security room in the future because it's where I appeared in the past!
entries.new: 为什么偏偏是监控室？比如，如果我出现在阁楼，那八十分钟后我就在别的地方了！我在未来之所以会待在监控室，只因为那是我在过去出现的位置！
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Why couldn't I have appeared on another continent? Then I would've been there in the future and made it come true!
entries.new: 为什么我不能出现在另一块大陆？那样未来的我就会到那儿去，把它变成事实！
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It's nonsense! What's actually determining where we appear?{w} Something must be. We appeared inside the tower every single time.
entries.new: 荒唐！到底是什么决定了我们出现的位置？{w}一定有什么在决定。每一次，我们都出现在塔内。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Shiroya and Atsuki had spent a long time in the elevator. Thanks to the stop button, they had managed to escape from Sai.
entries.new: Shiroya 和 Atsuki 在电梯里耗了很久。多亏了停止按钮，两人才得以从 Sai 手中逃脱。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But Shiroya soon noticed something was happening to Atsuki. He looked pale, and his breathing had sped up.
entries.new: 可 Shiroya 很快发觉 Atsuki 有些不对劲。他脸色苍白，呼吸也急促起来。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...Are you okay?
entries.new: ……你还好吗？
entries.speaker: snn

entries.text: Yes, don't worry.
entries.new: 嗯，别担心。
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: Shiroya stared at her lap, worried about Atsuki's thoughts. Did he, perhaps, think they wouldn't be able to leave?
entries.new: Shiroya低头望着自己的膝头，心里揣度着Atsuki在想什么。他会不会以为他们根本出不去？
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The silence went on for a long time.
entries.new: 沉默持续了很久。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Eventually, Shiroya experienced some relief. Atsuki had closed his eyes, and he didn't appear to be as stressed. Mirroring him, Shiroya closed her eyes too.
entries.new: 到后来，Shiroya稍稍松了口气。Atsuki已经闭上眼，看上去不像先前那样紧绷。她跟着他，也合上了眼睛。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Minutes later, both pairs of eyes shot open at the same time, and Shiroya couldn't believe what she saw.
entries.new: 几分钟后，两人同时睁开了眼，而Shiroya不敢相信眼前的景象。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: A knife was buried in Atsuki's chest.{w} She looked directly into his eyes, but only silence filled the elevator—neither of them could bring themselves to utter a word.
entries.new: 一把刀插在Atsuki的胸口。{w}她直直望进他的眼睛，电梯里却只有沉默——两人谁都说不出一句话来。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Then, Shiroya looked at the hand gripping the knife. She followed it up to an arm and then a shoulder.{w} Finally, she traced it to Sai's face.
entries.new: 随后，Shiroya看向握着刀的那只手。视线顺着手臂上移，越过肩膀，{w}最后落在Sai的脸上。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But that sight didn't last long. Immediately after killing his first victim, Sai felt the urge to have a second. With a frantic motion, the knife sliced Shiroya's chest.
entries.new: 然而那一幕没有持续多久。Sai刚杀掉第一个人，立刻又涌起再杀一个的冲动。他疯狂挥刀，划开了Shiroya的胸口。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Before she could process the scene, Shiroya's body fell beside Atsuki, their blood pooling together in the elevator.
entries.new: 还没等她看清这一幕，Shiroya的身体已倒在Atsuki身旁，两人的血在电梯里汇成一摊。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Of course, you know this never occurred.
entries.new: 当然，你知道这一切从未发生。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: If it had, though... how would it have come to happen?
entries.new: 可若真发生过……那又是怎么发生的呢？
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Sai stared at both bodies momentarily. However, he didn't immediately understand that he was trapped.
entries.new: Sai怔怔地看了两具尸体片刻，却没有立刻意识到自己已被困住。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki had pressed the stop button, so Sai couldn't leave the elevator.
entries.new: Atsuki按下了停止按钮，Sai无法离开电梯。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He couldn't move either—two bodies were on the floor. Eventually, when the replicated location took place, Sai was exactly where he'd appeared.
entries.new: 他也动不了——两具尸体就躺在地上。最终，复现地点生效时，Sai仍待在他出现时的位置。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But... why? He was able to be there in the future because he had appeared there in the past. {tip=saielevator}Why had that been the location where he'd appeared?{/tip} Why not somewhere else?
entries.new: 可是……为什么？他之所以能在未来待在那里，是因为他过去曾在那里出现。{tip=saielevator}可为什么偏偏是那个地方？{/tip}为什么不是别处？
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Maybe you have a good idea.
entries.new: 或许你已经有了答案。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: I had no idea. It seemed to make no sense at all.
entries.new: 我毫无头绪。这怎么看都说不通。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But what the hell would happen now if I travel to the past?{w} Let's say I travel two minutes back and appear in the kitchen. Will it be guaranteed that I'll be in the kitchen four minutes later?
entries.new: 可如果我穿越回过去，现在到底会怎样？{w}假设我回到两分钟前，出现在厨房。那么四分钟后，我是否就一定会待在厨房？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What if I don't want to? What if I decide to leave?{w} Does the location where I appear force me to be somewhere in the future? That makes even less sense!
entries.new: 要是我不愿意呢？要是我决定离开呢？{w}难道我出现的地点，还能逼我未来必须待在某个地方？这更说不通！
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I frowned, curious. What would actually happen? I had never traveled with knowledge of how the replicated location worked, but it seemed like having that knowledge alone would break the rule—I would no longer replicate the location in the future through some weird, unconscious fate.
entries.new: 我皱起眉，心生好奇。实际会发生什么？我从未在了解复现地点运作方式的情况下穿越过，但光是知道这一点，似乎就足以打破规律——我不会再因为某种诡异而无意识的命运，在未来复现那个地点。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I mean, if I do appear in the kitchen, can I refuse to be there in the future? Can I risk doing that just out of curiosity?{w} What if it's the universe's rule? Would I end up not trying to go against it out of fear of what might happen, which would confirm the impossibility of being in a paradoxical location?
entries.new: 我是说，假如我真出现在厨房，难道能拒绝在未来回到那里？仅仅出于好奇，我就敢冒这个险吗？{w}万一这是宇宙定下的规律呢？我会不会因为害怕后果而不敢违逆，结果反倒坐实了「不可能待在悖论地点」这件事？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That's pretty similar to not attempting to change the past just in case it's not possible, but it can't be fought, can it?
entries.new: 这和「以防万一改变不了，就干脆不去尝试改变过去」差不多，可这种事根本无从对抗，不是吗？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...And yet it doesn't make sense. Why would I purposely be somewhere just because it's where I appeared in the past?
entries.new: ……可还是说不通。凭什么只因为我过去曾出现在某处，就要刻意待在那里？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...I wonder. Can I maybe take advantage of it?
entries.new: ……不过，说不准。我能不能反过来利用这一点？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It doesn't seem fair that figuring out how it works would be a detriment if I intend to travel back. Until now, the rule has been consistent through mere fate, but it wouldn't be the same if I was aware of it as it happened.
entries.new: 如果我打算回到过去，弄懂它的运作方式反倒成了阻碍，这未免太不公平。至今为止，那条规律只是靠命运维持着一贯性；可要是我在事情发生时就清楚这一点，结果就不会一样了。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: A way to put the knowledge into practice... Maybe, as long as I have accurate knowledge...
entries.new: 一个能把这份知识用于实践的办法……或许，只要我的认知足够准确……
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I put the Sekimeiya that had sent me to the past in the refrigerator. After I waited a bit, I took it back out.
entries.new: 我把送我回到过去的那个Sekimeiya放进冰箱，等了一会儿，再取出来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I set the timer and waited half a minute. Then, I brought my hand toward its glow.
entries.new: 我设好计时，等了半分钟，然后把手伸向它的光芒。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: All right. Will you send me to the living room?
entries.new: 好。你会把我送到客厅去吗？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That was where I appeared: in the middle of the room.
entries.new: 我出现的地方正是那里：房间正中央。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And so I waited. I had traveled nine seconds to the past, so the only mandatory rule was that I had to be there after eighteen seconds.{w} ...But I didn't wait there because the universe had forced me to—I did it so that my request could be fulfilled.
entries.new: 于是我就在那里等着。我回到了九秒之前，唯一必须满足的规则，就是十八秒后我得待在那里。{w}……不过我留在那里，并非宇宙强迫，而是为了让自己的请求得以成立。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Eighteen seconds later, I was still there.
entries.new: 十八秒后，我仍在那里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Before touching the Sekimeiya, I had thought of what would happen. I had thought that eighteen seconds after appearing in the past, I would be in the living room.{w} Of course, if that was the case, it implied I would appear in the living room, so it was what had happened. Then, to make it possible, I'd remained there, exactly where I'd imagined myself appearing.
