entries.new: 在碰Sekimeiya之前，我已经想过会发生什么。我心想，回到过去后过十八秒，我会待在客厅。{w}当然，若真是这样，那就意味着我会出现在客厅，所以事情确实就是这样发生的。而为了让这一切成立，我就一直待在那里——正是我想象中自己出现的地方。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I see. So this is the opposite of useless.
entries.new: 原来如此。那这可不是没用，恰恰相反。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It's like the thought-up loops that I came up with. As long as the loop is in my head before touching the Sekimeiya, and as long as it can be executed, it will work.{w} "As long as it can be executed". Didn't I just travel from the 5th of January to the 15th of December?
entries.new: 这就像我自己设想出来的那些循环。只要在碰Sekimeiya之前，循环已经在我脑中成形，而且它能够被执行，就会成立。{w}「只要能够被执行」——我不就刚从1月5日穿越到了12月15日吗？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I went 21 days into the past, and my knowledge of the replicated location came after the travel but before the location is replicated in the future. What the hell happens now?{w} I appeared in the lobby; does that confirm that I'll be alive in the future?
entries.new: 我回到了二十一天前，而我对复现地点的认知，是在穿越之后、未来那个地点复现之前才有的。现在到底会怎样？{w}我出现在了大堂；这是否就能确认，未来我还活着？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Doesn't this travel genuinely force me to be in the lobby on the day—
entries.new: 这次穿越不就真的强迫我那天必须待在大堂——
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...{w}I went 21 days to the past.{w} 21 days after January 5th is a Thursday, January 26th...
entries.new: ……{w}我回到了二十一天前。{w}1月5日往后二十一天，是1月26日，星期四……
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: There was something there. That wasn't some random day.{w} Shiroya and I had talked with Miiya about it. We had said that we would go back to the tower on the 26th if we liked it the first time.
entries.new: 那天确实有点名堂。那并不是随便哪一天。{w}我和Shiroya曾和Miiya聊起过。我们说过，如果第一次玩得尽兴，26号就再去一次塔里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Miiya had died because of the Sekimeiya—without the Sekimeiya's existence, the explosion wouldn't have occurred, and Miiya would've kept on living. Ashiya held an event in the tower every Thursday, and on January 26th, a Thursday, an event that had grabbed our attention would take place.{w} If the Sekimeiya hadn't existed, we would've been in the tower on January 26th. Even after Miiya's death, if no travels had taken place, it was feasible that Shiroya and I would've returned to continue healing and moving forward. But from what I understood, our reason for returning would be different—to satisfy a travel that had already happened.
entries.new: Miiya是因Sekimeiya而死的——若Sekimeiya不曾存在，那场爆炸就不会发生，Miiya也会继续活下去。芦屋每周四都会在塔里举办活动，而1月26日正是星期四，那天会有一场吸引我们注意的活动。{w}若Sekimeiya不存在，1月26日我们本就会在塔里。即便Miiya死后、没有任何穿越发生，我和Shiroya也很有可能回到那里，继续疗伤、继续向前走。但据我所知，我们回去的理由会不一样——为了满足一次已经发生过的穿越。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What was the exact truth hidden behind that? I didn't know, but it confirmed again that the locations where we appeared were in no way random.
entries.new: 那背后究竟藏着怎样的真相？我不知道，但这再次证实了：我们出现的地点绝非随机。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This means that I can pretty much teleport anywhere I want, doesn't it?{w} I just have to think about where I'll be in the future. The limit is that the location has to be possible to reach in a set time. Is that it?
entries.new: 也就是说，我几乎能传送到任何想去的地方，对吧？{w}我只要想好自己未来会在哪里就行。限制只在于，那个地点必须能在规定时间内抵达。是这样吗？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I went to the kitchen and briefly put the Past Sekimeiya in the refrigerator. Once it had stored energy for thirty seconds, I touched it.
entries.new: 我去了厨房，把Past Sekimeiya放进冰箱里待了一会儿。等它蓄能三十秒后，我碰了它。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Once more, I appeared in the living room, where I'd wanted to appear.{w} I looked at my hands, but they were empty.
entries.new: 我再一次出现在客厅——我想出现的地方。{w}我看了看自己的手，手上空无一物。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I see. I guess that was too nonsensical to work.
entries.new: 原来如此。看来那太荒唐了，自然不会成立。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Before touching the Sekimeiya, I had thought that I'd be in the living room with a chocolate bar in my hands. By appearing there with the chocolate, I would be able to have it in the future so that it could appear in the past.{w} Presumably, that hadn't worked because I could never have obtained that chocolate in the span of those seconds, so I went back to the kitchen after I waited the proper amount of time.
entries.new: 在碰Sekimeiya之前，我想的是：我会出现在客厅，手里拿着一块巧克力。只要我带着巧克力出现在那里，未来我就能拥有它，好让它出现在过去。{w}大概正因为在那几秒之内我根本不可能拿到那块巧克力，这招才没有奏效。于是等够时间后，我又回到厨房。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Once again, I touched the Past Sekimeiya after it had gathered energy for thirty seconds.
entries.new: 等Past Sekimeiya完成三十秒蓄能，我再一次碰了它。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After I appeared in the living room, I looked at my hands.{w} I was holding a pen.
entries.new: 出现在客厅后，我看了看自己的手。{w}手里握着一支笔。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked next to the television and saw the same pen.
entries.new: 我看向电视机旁，那里放着同一支笔。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I see... This does work.
entries.new: 原来如此……这样确实可行。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Before touching the Sekimeiya, I'd thought that I would appear in the living room, and that during those eighteen seconds, I would go grab the pen. That was why I had appeared with it.{w} However, I already had the pen. I didn't have to go get it; I could simply stay where I'd appeared so that I could appear with it.
entries.new: 在触碰 Sekimeiya 之前，我以为自己会出现在客厅，然后在那十八秒里过去拿笔——正因为这样，我才会带着笔出现。{w} 可笔本来就已经在我手上了。我根本不必去拿，只要一直待在自己出现的位置不动，就能带着它出现。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Eighteen seconds went by, and I didn't step away from where I'd appeared.
entries.new: 十八秒过去，我一步也没有离开自己出现的位置。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So, even though I never obtained the pen myself, I was able to appear with it solely because I could have obtained it. I effectively duplicated the pen, but I can't spawn objects that don't exist or I can't feasibly obtain before the future coordinate, like the chocolate. And this only happened because I thought of my actions before touching the Sekimeiya.
entries.new: 也就是说，我本人压根没拿到过那支笔，只因为「本可以拿到」，就能带着它一起出现。我等于把那支笔复制了一份；但不存在的东西，或者在未来坐标之前根本不可能到手的东西——比如那块巧克力——就没法凭空弄出来。而这一切之所以成立，只因为我在触碰 Sekimeiya 之前就已经想好了自己要做的事。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It was a fascinating concept, and an incredibly strong one. Simply by having awareness of a single rule, the Sekimeiya had grown drastically more useful.
entries.new: 这个概念很有意思，也强得惊人。仅仅是意识到这样一条规则，Sekimeiya 的用处就一下子大了许多。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If I touch the Past Sekimeiya while I'm holding the pen now, I'll appear with it in the past. However, that's possible only as long as I have it in the proportional future.
entries.new: 如果我现在拿着笔去触碰 Past Sekimeiya，我就会带着它出现在过去。但前提是：在与之对应的未来，我仍然持有它。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: So when I touch the Sekimeiya, if I either think that I'll let go of the pen before the time expires or otherwise wouldn't have it, I won't appear with it. I would be instantly annihilating the pen without having to actually get rid of it. Even though I should appear with it, I wouldn't.
entries.new: 所以，触碰 Sekimeiya 时，只要我认定自己会在时间结束前松手，或者认定自己届时不会持有它，我就不会带着它出现。这样一来，我不必真的把笔丢掉，就能让它当场湮灭。明明本该带着它出现，结果却没有。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Exactly. On January 5th, Shiroya traveled to December 15th and noticed that out of the things she'd been holding, only her phone had disappeared.
entries.new: 正是如此。1月5日，Shiroya 穿越到12月15日，随后发现：自己原本拿着的东西里，只有手机不见了。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Why?{w} She appeared in the lobby of the tower, and the future coordinate was January 26th. I'm sure you haven't forgotten that phones are strictly prohibited in the tower: she couldn't have been there with it in the future, so she appeared without it in the past.
entries.new: 为什么？{w} 她出现在塔的大厅，而未来坐标是1月26日。想必你还记得，塔内严禁携带手机：在未来，她不可能带着手机待在那里，所以她在过去出现时，手机也就不在了。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: You might have realized that the same thing happened to the "XYN" card, which she didn't think about, and her clothes. Unlike Atsuki, she didn't appear with the ones she'd been wearing. ...That's still strange, isn't it?
entries.new: 你可能已经想到了，那张她根本没放在心上的「XYN」卡，还有她身上的衣服，也是同样的情况。和 Atsuki 不同，她出现时穿的不是原先那一套。……这仍然很奇怪，不是吗？
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The knife disappeared from Shiroya's purse when she traveled to the future because she didn't have it in the past, so it would've been impossible for her to appear with it.
entries.new: Shiroya 穿越到未来时，小刀从她的手包里消失了，因为她在过去并没有带着它，所以她不可能带着它出现。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But on January 5th, when she traveled to December 15th, she noticed that out of the things she'd been holding, only her phone had disappeared. She didn't think about it, but the "XYN" card did as well, and her clothes had changed.
entries.new: 可是1月5日她穿越到12月15日时，发现手里拿着的东西中，只有手机不见了。她并未留意，但那张「XYN」卡同样消失了，她的衣服也变了。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Why?{w} She appeared in the lobby of the tower, and the future coordinate was January 26th. I'm sure you haven't forgotten that phones are strictly prohibited in the tower: she couldn't have been there with it in the future, so she appeared without it in the past.
entries.new: 为什么？{w} 她出现在塔的大厅，而未来坐标是1月26日。想必你还记得，塔内严禁携带手机：在未来，她不可能带着手机待在那里，所以她在过去出现时，手机也就不在了。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The cleaning cart disappeared when Shiroya traveled to the future because she didn't have it in the past, so it would've been impossible for her to appear with it.
entries.new: Shiroya 穿越到未来时，清洁推车消失了，因为她在过去并没有推着它，所以她不可能带着它出现。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But on January 5th, when she traveled to December 15th, she noticed that out of the things she'd been holding, only her phone had disappeared. She didn't think about it, but the "XYN" card did as well, and her clothes had changed.
entries.new: 可是1月5日她穿越到12月15日时，发现手里拿着的东西中，只有手机不见了。她并未留意，但那张「XYN」卡同样消失了，她的衣服也变了。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Why?{w} She appeared in the lobby of the tower, and the future coordinate was January 26th. I'm sure you haven't forgotten that phones are strictly prohibited in the tower: she couldn't have been there with it in the future, so she appeared without it in the past.
entries.new: 为什么？{w} 她出现在塔的大厅，而未来坐标是1月26日。想必你还记得，塔内严禁携带手机：在未来，她不可能带着手机待在那里，所以她在过去出现时，手机也就不在了。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: This is pretty insane. I can't believe the mechanics actually followed some rules.
entries.new: 这简直离谱。没想到这套机制居然真的遵循着某种规则。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I was overwhelmed by the number of things I was learning, but I didn't want to focus on a single detail. I didn't know if anyone else would come back at some point, and there were plenty of aspects I was wondering about.
entries.new: 一下子学到这么多东西，我有些应接不暇，但我不想只盯着某一点。我不知道别人会不会在什么时候回来，而且还有不少地方让我挂心。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How much can I figure out with what I know? Was Sai aware of all this? He had a wristwatch, so I bet it would've been a lot easier for him to learn some of it.{w} There were two Sekimeiya since this morning, but what about the third one? Does that one never work...?
entries.new: 凭我现在知道的东西，能推出多少？Sai 清楚这些吗？他有一只手表，要弄明白其中几件事，想必比我容易得多。{w} 从今天早上起就有两台 Sekimeiya，那第三台呢？那一台难道永远不会启动……？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And one made us travel back in time, while the other sent us forward.{w} If I know the time someone appeared in the future, I can know that's where they were in the past—there are many ways to apply all of this.{w} I wonder... When someone travels to the past, if I think that I'll bring them somewhere in the future, would I make them appear there in the past? Could the origin be in my mind even though I'm not the one traveling?
entries.new: 而且，一台让我们回到过去，另一台把我们送往未来。{w} 只要知道某人出现在未来的时刻，就能知道他在过去身处何处——这些信息能派上很多用场。{w} 我在想……如果有人要穿越到过去，而我认定自己会在未来把他带到某个地方，那他在过去是不是就会出现在那里？即便穿越的人不是我，原点也可能出在我的意识里？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I tried to calm down a bit and went to the kitchen. It was better to answer the larger questions first.
entries.new: 我让自己稍微冷静下来，走进厨房。还是先弄清更重要的问题为好。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait a second. I can duplicate anything obtainable, can't I?
entries.new: 等等。只要东西能到手，我就能把它复制出来，对吧？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: We wondered whether duplicating the Sekimeiya was possible, but it doesn't appear to be the case. When it's activated, it doesn't count as something you possess, and it stays behind.
entries.new: 我们曾怀疑 Sekimeiya 能否被复制，看来答案是否定的。它启动时不算你持有的东西，会留在原地。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Now I'm certain that the Sai with the broken wristwatch came from the future, and he had a Sekimeiya in his hip pack. He acted as if he didn't know it was there, so perhaps that was the truth.
entries.new: 现在我确定了：那个手表坏掉的 Sai 来自未来，他的腰包里有一台 Sekimeiya。他表现得好像并不知道那东西在里面，说不定那确实是实话。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Maybe he appeared with it. An important detail is that it was inactive.{w} If he hid a powered-off Sekimeiya in his hip pack in the future, it's possible he appeared with it in the past.
entries.new: 也许他是带着它一起出现的。关键的一点是，它当时处于关闭状态。{w} 如果他在未来把一台关掉的 Sekimeiya 藏进腰包，那他穿越回过去时就有可能带着它出现。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Trying it was simple. First, I used the Past Sekimeiya to travel nine seconds to the past.
entries.new: 验证起来很简单。我先用 Past Sekimeiya 穿越到九秒之前。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In the living room, I waited eighteen seconds before I reentered the kitchen.
entries.new: 我在客厅里等了十八秒，才重新走进厨房。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The Sekimeiya will now spend a little while powered off.
entries.new: 这样一来，Sekimeiya 会有好一阵子处于关闭状态。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I took the Future Sekimeiya out of the refrigerator and grabbed the disabled Past Sekimeiya.{w} Half a minute later, I left it on the countertop and touched the Future Sekimeiya.
entries.new: 我从冰箱里取出 Future Sekimeiya，再拿起那台已经无法使用的 Past Sekimeiya。{w} 半分钟后，我把它放在台面上，触碰了 Future Sekimeiya。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I appeared in the kitchen nine seconds in the future. Then, I glanced at my hands.
entries.new: 我出现在了九秒后的厨房。然后，我低头看了看自己的双手。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was there. Still gray, I had it in my hands.
entries.new: 它就在那里。依然是灰色的，正握在我手中。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did I really duplicate it...?
entries.new: 我真的把它复制出来了吗……？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I looked at the marble, where I'd left the Past Sekimeiya before traveling.
entries.new: 我望向那张大理石台面——穿越之前，我把 Past Sekimeiya 放在了那里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What!? It's not there!
entries.new: 什么！？它不在那儿！
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The Future Sekimeiya was where I'd touched it, and it was gray. That proved I'd traveled to the future. However, the original Past Sekimeiya was gone: I hadn't duplicated it.
entries.new: Future Sekimeiya 仍在我触碰它的地方，颜色是灰的。这证明我确实穿越到了未来。可是，原本那台 Past Sekimeiya 却不见了——我并没有复制成功。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the hell? Can the Sekimeiya not be duplicated?{w} It seems like the original one disappeared when I appeared with it in the future and disallowed the duplication. There's no way anyone came and took it during the nine seconds I wasn't here, right?
entries.new: 搞什么？难道 Sekimeiya 无法被复制？{w} 看来，当我在未来带着它出现、否定了这次复制时，原本那一台就消失了。总不可能有人趁我不在的那九秒里把它拿走吧？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It was bizarre, but the fact that I'd appeared with it was notable. It had counted as one of my past possessions.
entries.new: 这很离奇，但我能带着它出现这一点值得注意。它确实被算作了我过去持有的物品。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: While I was thinking, the Past Sekimeiya powered on.
entries.new: 就在我思考的时候，Past Sekimeiya 启动了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's still working.{w} I wonder if the fact that it was powered off mattered at all.
entries.new: 它还能用。{w} 不知道「处于关闭状态」这一点到底有没有影响。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I repeated the same process but held the powered Past Sekimeiya with my sleeves for half a minute.{w} Then, I left it in the refrigerator to avoid overlapping ranges and went nine seconds to the future.
entries.new: 我把同样的流程重做了一遍，只是这次隔着袖子，握了那台启动中的 Past Sekimeiya 半分钟。{w} 随后，为避开重叠范围，我把它放进冰箱，再穿越到九秒之后。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}I didn't appear with the Sekimeiya. My hands looked to be holding something that wasn't there.
entries.new: ……{w}我没有带着 Sekimeiya 出现。我的双手维持着握着什么东西的姿势，可手里空无一物。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I opened the refrigerator and saw the Past Sekimeiya where I'd just left it.
entries.new: 我打开冰箱，看见 Past Sekimeiya 就放在我刚放下的位置。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So it did matter that it wasn't active. When it isn't, its powers fade temporarily, and it acts as a normal object.
entries.new: 看来它未启动这点确实有影响。未启动时，它的力量会暂时消退，只被当作普通物品。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What would happen if I did the reverse of this? Wouldn't the past change?{w} If I go to the past holding the powered-off Future Sekimeiya, I would appear with it in the past, so the "original" one would disappear. That means that I couldn't hold it anymore when I'm traveling to the past, thereby changing it.
entries.new: 如果把顺序反过来，会怎么样？过去不就会被改变吗？{w} 如果我拿着关闭状态的 Future Sekimeiya 回到过去，我就会带着它在过去出现，那么「原本」那一台就会消失。也就是说，我穿越回过去之后，就再也拿不到原本那一台了——过去便由此被改写。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I tried it out of curiosity. Holding the Future Sekimeiya that I'd powered off, I went nine seconds to the past.
entries.new: 出于好奇，我试了一次。我拿着那台被我关掉的 Future Sekimeiya，穿越到九秒之前。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In the living room, however, I didn't have the Future Sekimeiya between my hands.
entries.new: 然而，我人在客厅，两手之间却没有 Future Sekimeiya。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It didn't work? I thought that I would stay here for eighteen seconds with the Sekimeiya, so that's strange.
entries.new: 没成功？我明明想着要带着 Sekimeiya 在这里待上十八秒，这就奇怪了。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Suddenly, I heard a sound coming from the kitchen. It scared me at first, but I immediately understood what it was.{w} Nine seconds later, I entered through the door.
entries.new: 忽然，厨房里传来一阵声响。我起初被吓了一跳，但马上就明白那是什么了。{w} 九秒后，我从门口走了进来。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The disabled Sekimeiya was on the floor. It hadn't disappeared alongside my past self.
entries.new: 那台已经失效的 Sekimeiya 躺在地板上。它并没有随过去的我一同消失。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Why, though? I don't get it.{w} ...Wait, no, I might have an idea.
entries.new: 可是为什么？我想不通。{w}……等等，不对，我或许有点头绪。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I think it's due to the infinite loop concept I thought of.{w} If I had appeared with the powered-off Future Sekimeiya in the past, eighteen seconds later, it would've been closer to powering on. Once the infinite loop is applied, the Sekimeiya could've never appeared powered off, and when it's powered on, it doesn't count as a normal object. I believe that's why it didn't travel.
entries.new: 我想，这跟先前设想的无限循环有关。{w}如果断电的 Future Sekimeiya 随我一同出现在过去，那么十八秒之后，它就更接近通电了。一旦套用无限循环，Sekimeiya 就绝不可能以断电状态出现；而通电状态下，它又不算普通物体。我认为这就是它没有穿越的原因。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...What exactly would happen if I wait in the middle of the living room for a few seconds, move the sofa to where I'd been standing, and then travel to the future?
entries.new: ……如果我站在客厅中央等上几秒，把沙发挪到我刚才站的位置，再穿越到未来，究竟会发生什么？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: My appearance would collide with the sofa, but what would that do? Would I overwrite part of the sofa? Would it cut off my legs and kill me?
entries.new: 我出现时会与沙发相撞，可那会造成什么后果？我会覆盖掉沙发的一部分吗？还是沙发会截断我的双腿，要了我的命？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It's too risky to test that, but I have no idea what the result would be. After all, I've been appearing where there is air, and it seems I'm overwriting it, or else it would also kill me.
entries.new: 拿这个做实验太危险了，可我完全猜不到结果。毕竟我每次出现的位置都有空气，看样子是我把空气覆盖掉了，否则空气同样会要了我的命。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The case might be different if I appear on top of a solid object, though.
entries.new: 不过，如果我出现在某个固体物体上面，情况也许就不一样了。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Indeed. That is the fate Sai A met.
entries.new: 正是。那便是 Sai A 所遭遇的命运。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Incorrect. That is the fate Sai A met.
entries.new: 不对。那才是 Sai A 遭遇的命运。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In his world, he was the first person to leave room B4, in which everyone waited.
entries.new: 在他的世界里，所有人都在 B4 室等待，而他是第一个离开那里的人。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: After his departure, he never came back. He was never again seen alive.
entries.new: 他离开之后，再没有回来。从此没人见过活着的他。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Unaware of what awaited him, he touched the Future Sekimeiya that had been hidden in the attic.
entries.new: 他并不知道等待自己的是什么，伸手碰了那台藏在阁楼里的 Future Sekimeiya。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: For a prolonged period of time, he had been sitting against a door in a crystal room. However, when he appeared there in the future, that door had been opened...
entries.new: 他曾在水晶展室里靠着一扇门坐了很久。然而当他于未来出现在那里时，那扇门已经被人打开了……
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: I've been figuring all of this out, but I still don't fully understand the most important aspect: the amount of time traveled.{w} I've been repeatedly traveling nine seconds through time, so it has to be consistent as well.
entries.new: 这些我已经一点点理清了，可最关键的一点仍没弄明白：穿越的时间长度。{w}我反复穿越的都是九秒，那它也应该是一致的才对。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Thirty seconds stored equals nine seconds traveled. Two minutes stored equals 45 seconds traveled.{w} There's already an indication here: each stored second turns into more amount of time traveled than the previous. In the first case, each second stored added 0.3 seconds traveled. In the second case, each second stored added 0.37 seconds traveled.
entries.new: 蓄能三十秒，穿越九秒；蓄能两分钟，穿越 45 秒。{w}这里已经有迹象了：每多蓄一秒，换算出的穿越时间都比前一秒更多。第一种情况，每蓄一秒增加 0.3 秒；第二种情况，每蓄一秒增加 0.37 秒。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And it's evident this keeps going—fifteen minutes stored led into twenty minutes traveled. In that case, each second stored added 1.3 seconds.{w} Earlier, keeping the Sekimeiya out of the cabinet for 25 minutes made me travel about 45 minutes to the past. That's a pretty noticeable increase. Each stored second would've counted for 1.8 seconds traveled.
entries.new: 而且很明显，这个趋势还在延续——蓄能十五分钟，穿越二十分钟。这样算下来，每蓄一秒等于 1.3 秒。{w}之前我把 Sekimeiya 放在展示柜外二十五分钟，结果穿越到了约四十五分钟前。增幅相当明显，每蓄一秒已经相当于 1.8 秒的穿越时间。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: So the more time it's gathered, the larger the increase is. It's exponential.{w} The difference between five and ten minutes is very little compared to the difference between twenty and 25. For a while, the numbers will be low, but there'll be a point where they suddenly become immense.{w} Once the Sekimeiya has been out of the cabinet for 35 minutes, how much will one stored second equal to?{w} ...What about after an hour?
entries.new: 也就是说，蓄能越久，增幅越大。这是指数级的。{w}五分钟到十分钟的差距，跟二十分钟到二十五分钟的差距相比微不足道。起初数值会很低，但总有一刻会突然变得极其庞大。{w}Sekimeiya 离开展示柜三十五分钟后，蓄一秒会等于多少？{w}……那一小时之后呢？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: There's an indication that I'm correct about this: Akaro and Shiroya.{w} They traveled days through time, and so did I. Akaro said he touched the Sekimeiya while we were in the attic's bedroom, so it's very possible it stored energy for a long time.
entries.new: 有件事可以证明我猜得没错：Akaro 和 Shiroya。{w}他们穿越了数日之久，我也是。Akaro 说，我们还在阁楼卧室时他碰过 Sekimeiya，所以它很可能已经蓄能了很长时间。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: In any case, the increase of the time traveled is not gradual. However, I think something might be.
entries.new: 无论如何，穿越时间的增长不是渐进的。不过我认为，有另一样东西或许是渐进的。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The range. That's what all the travels indicate.
entries.new: 重叠范围。所有的穿越都指向这一点。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Although I still don't fully comprehend it, I believe it must work under a gradual increase. Otherwise, when Akaro and Shiroya traveled days through time, we would've traveled as well.
entries.new: 虽然我还没完全弄懂它，但我认为它的变化一定是渐进的。否则 Akaro 和 Shiroya 穿越数日的时候，我们也该一并被传送过去。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: There is something else that could follow a similar progression, which is the time it spends recovering.{w} No matter the amount of time traveled, the Sekimeiya always spends a while gray. However, the amount of time stored seems to gradually add to the guaranteed amount.
entries.new: 还有另一样东西也许是类似的渐进变化，那就是它的恢复时间。{w}无论穿越多久，Sekimeiya 总会维持一段灰色状态。不过，蓄能的时长似乎会一点点累加到那段保底时间上。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: There's gotta be a formula behind the amount of time traveled that always applies.
entries.new: 穿越的时长背后一定有一个始终成立的公式。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What could it be? A formula that increases the amount each second adds as more seconds have passed...{w} If I could figure it out, I could use the Sekimeiya to appear at any point in time.
entries.new: 会是什么公式？蓄能秒数越多，每秒换算出的时长也跟着增加的公式……{w}如果能解出来，我就能用 Sekimeiya 出现在任何时间点。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Thankfully, if it doesn't change over time, I could do small-scale tests to figure out what exactly would occur at a larger scale; observing the difference between 30, 31, 32, 33, 34, and 35 stored seconds might be all I need to understand what one hour of stored time would cause.
entries.new: 好在只要公式不随时间改变，我就能用小规模实验推知大规模的结果；只要比较蓄能 30、31、32、33、34、35 秒之间的差异，或许就足以弄清蓄能一小时会带来什么。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But my way to measure time isn't precise, and I can't measure decimals. I might need a calculator too, and I don't know if there'd be one here in the attic.
entries.new: 可我计时的方式并不精确，也量不出小数。也许还需要计算器，而我不知道这阁楼里有没有。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Why was I so preoccupied with the idea? Was it due to mere curiosity?{w} No. That wasn't all. At some point, I had realized it.
entries.new: 我为什么对这件事如此执着？只是出于好奇吗？{w}不，不只是这样。不知从何时起，我已经意识到了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: While locked in the tower for twelve hours, I'd spent a long time trying to figure out if saving Miiya was possible. And I knew, at that moment, that it was.{w} However, those thoughts had all faded from my mind some time previously. Shiroya had caused me to abandon the idea of saving her.{w} But I'd learned that wasn't the real Shiroya, and it made a lot of sense—she would never have said that. She had wanted to save Miiya just like me and had been prepared to do it once I'd told her it was possible.
entries.new: 被困在塔里的那十二个小时，我花了很长时间思考救下 Miiya 是否可行。而在那一刻，我已经知道答案是可行的。{w}然而那些念头，早在之前某个时候就从我脑中消散了。是 Shiroya 让我放弃了救她的想法。{w}可我已经知道那不是真正的 Shiroya——这样一切都说得通了，她绝不会说出那种话。她和我一样想救 Miiya，只要我告诉她可行，她早就做好了准备。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Had I truly heard Miiya earlier? ...That voice continually replayed in my head, but I couldn't understand the circumstances around it.
entries.new: 我先前真的听到了 Miiya 的声音吗？……那个声音在我脑中反复回响，可我理不清它究竟是怎么来的。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't know how reasonable this is. After a while of storing time, being off by even a single decimal would result in a substantial difference...
entries.new: 我不知道这法子有多靠谱。蓄能时间一长，哪怕只差一个小数位，结果也会天差地别……
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Even if I analyze repeated short travels to the future, it might take me a really long time to come up with an accurate equation with just these two timers.
entries.new: 就算反复分析短时间穿越到未来的情况，光靠这两个计时器要推出准确的公式，恐怕也得花上很久。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I had no idea how long I'd be alone in the tower, but I couldn't afford to spend hours perfecting a formula. I didn't even know if it was consistent in the first place.
entries.new: 我不知道自己还要在塔里独自待多久，但耗上几个小时去打磨一个公式，我耗不起。何况我连它是否始终一致都还不知道。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My mind went back to a thought I'd had long in the past. When I'd originally conceived of thought-up loops, I'd also considered a particular scenario.
entries.new: 我的思绪回到了很久以前有过的某个念头。最初构思假想循环的时候，我也曾设想过一种特定的情形。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "Depending on how it works, the possibilities could be limitless. There's even a higher step to reach."
entries.new: 看它如何运作，可能性也许无穷无尽，甚至还有更高的一层可以抵达。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: "It's considerably different, but it follows along with a few things I thought about earlier, regarding the date displayed on Sai's watch."
entries.new: 「这跟之前大不一样，却和我早先关于 Sai 手表上那个日期的几点想法一脉相承。」
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: "Out of the countless examples, could you go back in time, trade information with someone, write it all down, and leave it all on a note that you'd see before traveling through time?"
entries.new: 在无数例子中，有没有这样一种：你回到过去，和某人交换信息，把一切写下来，全部留在一张便条上，让自己在时间穿越前看到？
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: "You'd read the note and go back to the past. However, since you would already know the contents of it, you'd have no reason to exchange the information—all you'd have to do is leave behind the note you'd read so that you could read it before traveling."
entries.new: 你读到那张便条，然后回到过去。可既然你已经知道上面的内容，就没有理由再去交换信息——你只需把读过的那张便条留下，让自己在穿越前读到它。
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: "The note itself would be a paradox that you caused, but was the past truly changed? Was a past in which you exchanged information truly overwritten? ...Or did it never exist in the first place?"
entries.new: 那张便条本身会是你造成的悖论，但过去真的被改变了吗？那个你曾交换信息的过去，真的被覆盖了吗？……还是说，它从一开始就不存在？
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: "...If Sai's watch got to "9999-12-31" by spending infinite time in a loop, did the pasts in which the time counted up to that date really exist in any capacity?"
entries.new: ……如果 Sai 的手表是在循环中度过了无限时间才走到「9999-12-31」，那么那些时间一路累积到那一天的过去，到底有没有以任何形式存在过？
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: ...Would something like that actually be possible?
entries.new: ……这种事真的可能发生吗？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I don't have the time needed to find an equation that lets me calculate time values for the Sekimeiya, but as long as it's possible to find, could I use something like this to obtain it?
entries.new: 我没有时间去推导一条能算出 Sekimeiya 时间数值的公式，但只要它确实可以被找到，我能不能用这种办法把它弄到手？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: How long would it take me to find it? Maybe two hours of monitoring innumerable travels?
entries.new: 找到它需要多久？也许要花两个小时，盯着无数次穿越？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: If I extrapolate my old scenario to this, it would look something like... going two hours back in time, spending them working to find the formula, and noting it down on a piece of paper that I would hide inside a drawer. Before traveling two hours back, I would find the note, and in the past, as I would already know the formula, I would just have to write it down and leave it in the drawer.
entries.new: 把旧设想套用到这件事上，大概会是这样……回到两小时前，用这两个小时推导公式，再把它记在纸上，藏进抽屉。而在穿越回两小时之前，我会先找到那张纸条；回到过去后，既然我已经知道公式，只需把它写下来放进抽屉即可。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But this isn't applicable, because if I go two hours back, I won't have access to the Sekimeiya. I've been testing with them, so if I go back and use them, I'll be changing the past, and the note will not be written in my current reality.
entries.new: 但这行不通。因为回到两小时前，我就拿不到 Sekimeiya 了。我一直在用它们做实验，如果回去之后继续使用，就等于改变了过去，那张纸条也就不会出现在我当前的现实里。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But what if I change it up a little?
entries.new: 不过，如果我稍作改动呢？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Let's say I take the Past Sekimeiya out of the refrigerator. Two minutes later, I touch it and go 45 seconds back. I'm not even sure if this first travel would be needed, but it might be.
entries.new: 假设我把 Past Sekimeiya 从冰箱里拿出来。两分钟后，我碰它一下，回到 45 秒前。我还不确定这第一次穿越有没有必要，但也许有。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Then, 45 seconds later, my original self will disappear, and I'll spend two hours testing with both Sekimeiya to come up with the right formula. Once I have it, I'll go back in time to a point before I traveled the 45 seconds and write down the formula.
entries.new: 接着，45 秒之后，原本的我会消失，而我将用两个小时，拿两台 Sekimeiya 反复试验，推出正确的公式。一旦得到公式，我就回到进行那 45 秒穿越之前的某个时刻，把公式写下来。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Before traveling the 45 seconds, I'll read the note with the formula. Then, 45 seconds in the past, I'll write it down so that my original self can see it.{w} Would this allow me to spend two hours finding the formula without actually having to waste that time?
entries.new: 在穿越那 45 秒之前，我会先读那张写着公式的纸条。然后回到 45 秒前，把它写下来，好让原本的我能看到。{w}这样一来，我岂不是能花两个小时找出公式，却又不必真的耗掉那两个小时？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: There was no point in assuming an answer because it was easy to test. I readied myself to perform the loop and started to store time with the Past Sekimeiya.{w} However, when I looked at the drawer where I wanted the note to be hidden, it was empty.
entries.new: 空想答案没有意义，因为这件事一试便知。我做好准备，要执行这个循环，便用 Past Sekimeiya 开始蓄能。{w}然而，当我看向那个打算藏纸条的抽屉时，里面空无一物。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Huh, okay. ...Why did it not work?
entries.new: 咦，好吧。……可为什么没成功呢？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The success of the loop required the existence of hypothetical events. In reality, if I had seen the note, I would never have spent two hours working to find the formula—those events would only have existed in a hypothetical history. Once their result was known, their existence would've become unneeded.
entries.new: 循环要成立，假想事件就必须存在。可在现实中，如果我已经看到了那张纸条，就绝不会再花两个小时去推公式——那些事只会存在于一段假想的历史里。一旦结果已知，它们也就没有存在的必要了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Am I mistaken, then? Is this concept just unworkable?{w} That can't be. It's the same thing as the recorder powering off when I go to the past: the hypothetical realities in which it progressively loses battery need to exist in order for it to appear without power in the real one.
entries.new: 那么是我想错了？这套思路根本行不通？{w}不可能。这跟我回到过去时录音笔会断电是一个道理：它必须在那些假想现实里一点点耗尽电量，才能在真正的现实中以没电的状态出现。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Although I didn't fully understand that, as the recorder not degrading physically still didn't make sense to me.
entries.new: 只是我并未完全想通——录音笔本身没有任何损耗，这一点我始终无法理解。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What if it didn't work because two hours wouldn't have been enough to determine the formula? Or what if, during those two hours, people would've shown up and I would've been unable to continue and go to the past to leave the note behind?
entries.new: 会不会是因为两个小时根本不够推出公式？又或者，那两个小时里有人来了，我无法继续，也没法回到过去把纸条留下？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: If two hours wouldn't have been enough, what about ten? What if it would've taken me more than twenty hours to refine the formula until it was consistent with every travel?
entries.new: 两个小时不够，那十个小时呢？要把公式修正到与每一次穿越都吻合，说不定得花上二十多个小时。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The tower will open at {time=21}, so assuming no one else comes, even in a hypothetical world, I would only have until {time=21} to experiment... Actually, probably way less than that, because to travel to the past and appear in the tower, I'd have to be inside it hours after {time=21.}
entries.new: 塔要到 {time=21} 才会开放，所以假设没有别人来，即便在假想世界里，我也只能在 {time=21} 之前做实验……不，实际时间恐怕还要短得多，因为要回到过去并出现在塔内，我得在 {time=21.} 之后好几个小时还待在塔里。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...But assuming I had all the time I needed, would I be able to use a hypothetical world to my advantage? Could I make use of countless hours without actually spending any?{w} ...I considered that there might've been a way to test it.
entries.new: ……不过，假如时间充裕，我能不能把假想世界利用起来？能不能用掉无数个小时，而现实中一个小时都不必花？{w}……我想，或许有办法验证这一点。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I took the Past Sekimeiya out and pressed "play" on the recorder. Following that, I went to the living room with the Past Sekimeiya and the recorder and closed the door to the kitchen.
entries.new: 我取出 Past Sekimeiya，按下录音笔的播放键。随后，我带着 Past Sekimeiya 和录音笔去了客厅，关上了通往厨房的门。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had to think very thoroughly about it. Instead of using a single hypothetical world, what if I used multiple at once by making it recursive?
entries.new: 这件事得想得非常透彻。与其只用一个假想世界，不如让它层层嵌套，同时动用许多个？
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}If I touch the Sekimeiya when fifteen minutes have passed, I'll go twenty minutes to the past.{w} But before I touch it, I'll open the door to the hallway and find a notepad from the bedrooms on the floor. Depending on what it says, I'll do one of three things.
entries.new: ……{w}等过了十五分钟，我再去碰 Sekimeiya，就会回到二十分钟前。{w}不过在碰它之前，我要先打开通往走廊的门，看看地上有没有从卧室拿来的笔记本。看上面写着什么，我再决定做三件事中的哪一件。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: 1: If it has a formula written down, I'll go twenty minutes to the past, obtain the notepad, write the formula down, and leave it in the hallway.
entries.new: 一：如果上面写着公式，我就回到二十分钟前，拿到那本笔记本，把公式抄下来，再放回走廊。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: 2: If I don't find a notepad, I'll go twenty minutes to the past, and using the Future Sekimeiya in the kitchen, I'll start to work toward finding the formula. Before twenty minutes pass, I'll obtain a notepad from the bedrooms, and in the top left corner of the first page, I'll write a "1" along with the progress I made in those twenty minutes. Then, I'll leave it in the hallway.
entries.new: 二：如果没找到笔记本，我就回到二十分钟前，用厨房里的 Future Sekimeiya 开始推算公式。二十分钟结束前，我从卧室取来一本笔记本，在第一页左上角写上一个“1”，再写下这二十分钟里取得的进展，然后把笔记本留在走廊。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: 3: If I find a notepad that doesn't contain the formula, it will have my current progress along with a number in the top left corner of the first page, which will indicate the amount of iterations that have occurred so far.{w} I'll go back to the past, and using the information I read in the notepad, I'll start working to find the formula. Before the twenty minutes pass, I'll write down the updated progress in a notepad from the bedrooms, increase the number I saw in the top left corner by one, and then leave the notepad in the hallway.
entries.new: 三：如果找到的笔记本上没有公式，那上面会写着我当前的进展，第一页左上角还有一个数字，代表到目前为止已经重复了多少轮。{w}我就回到过去，依据笔记本上读到的内容继续推算公式。二十分钟结束前，我把更新后的进展写进一本从卧室拿来的笔记本，再把左上角的数字加一，然后把笔记本留在走廊。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: This makes use of infinite time. By repeatedly using these twenty minutes across multiple hypothetical worlds, I can carry my progress over until the formula is found. I'm able to compress years' worth of calculations into a single twenty-minute loop.
entries.new: 这样就能动用无限的时间。让这二十分钟在多个假想世界里反复重来，我就能把进展一路带到公式被推出来为止。数年的计算，可以压缩进一个二十分钟的循环里。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Since all the worlds will collapse into a final result, I'll always find the real formula behind the hallway door if this is viable; actions 2 and 3 are only for the hypothetical worlds.
entries.new: 既然所有世界最终都会收敛成一个结果，那么只要这套办法可行，我打开走廊那扇门时，看到的就一定是真正的公式；第二、第三种做法只发生在假想世界里。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: As another final point, if the number in the top left corner exceeds, say, a billion, then I can be confident no answer exists.
entries.new: 最后还有一点：如果左上角的数字超过了，比如十亿，那我就基本可以确定，这道公式根本无解。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...{w}I realized the plan had a small flaw.
entries.new: ……{w}我意识到，这个计划有一个小小的漏洞。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But if in the real world, I open the hallway door and find no notepad, I'll think that the plan hasn't worked and won't go through with the first loop. In the same way, the first hypothetical version of me, instead of assuming that he's about to start the first iteration, would assume that the plan is flawed and wouldn't start the sequence. If I want this to work, I'll have to execute the first loop in the instance that I don't find a notepad in the hallway right now.{w} This is okay, because even though the plan wouldn't work for me, I'd have to resort to trying to find the formula manually in the real world. Executing the first loop would work toward that, and it would make the plan succeed if the concept is valid.
entries.new: 可如果我在现实世界里打开走廊的门，什么笔记本都没找到，我就会认定计划失败，也不会去走第一轮。同样，第一个假想中的我也不会认为自己正要开始第一轮，而会断定计划有破绽，从而不肯启动这一连串循环。要让计划成立，我必须在此时此刻——在走廊里没有找到笔记本的这一刻——照样执行第一轮。{w}这没关系，因为即便这套计划对我无效，我在现实中也只能靠手工去推公式。执行第一轮正是在为此铺路；而只要那个构想成立，计划就会因此成功。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Thirteen minutes had passed.
entries.new: 十三分钟过去了。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I hadn't heard anything in the attic; if another version of me had been ready to pass the formula on to me, he'd been very quiet.
entries.new: 阁楼里一点动静也没有。就算有另一个我正等着把公式交给我，他也安静得很。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Still completely clueless as to whether it would work, I approached the hallway.
entries.new: 我仍然完全不知道这办法行不行，就这样朝走廊走去。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wh—
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: My mouth dropped to the floor. Flashes of a certain bedroom popped in my mind, a normal occurrence after seeing my own messy handwriting.
entries.new: 我目瞪口呆。某个卧室的画面在脑海里一闪而过——每次看见自己潦草的字迹，都会这样。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A notepad was beside my feet, containing a large string of numbers on the first page. Upon closer inspection, it was definitely a formula—far from a clean one.
entries.new: 脚边放着一本笔记本，第一页写着一长串数字。凑近一看，那无疑是一条公式——只是远谈不上工整。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is really it. It actually worked...!
entries.new: 就是这个。居然真的成了……！
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: All the pages after the first one were completely empty. There was no number on the top left, so I didn't know how many iterations had been needed to reach it, but its complexity was evident.
entries.new: 第一页之后全是空白。左上角没有数字，所以我不知道一共重复了多少轮才得到它，但它的复杂程度一目了然。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So Shiroya and Akaro weren't lying... Touching the Sekimeiya after an hour of stored time will really send you weeks through time, and I can calculate the exact amount.
entries.new: 看来 Shiroya 和 Akaro 没有说谎……蓄能一个小时之后再碰 Sekimeiya，真的会把人送到几个星期之外，而且我还能算出具体的数值。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Before that, though, I had to travel to the past. Less than twenty seconds remained until the fifteen-minute mark. When the timer hit it, I touched the Past Sekimeiya.
entries.new: 不过在那之前，我得先回到过去。距离十五分钟还差不到二十秒。计时一到，我便碰了 Past Sekimeiya。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As expected, I appeared in the hallway, right next to the kitchen, which was closed. I had gone twenty minutes back, but the Past Sekimeiya had only stored energy for fifteen. During the first five minutes, I had no access to the kitchen because my past self was there. In the hypothetical loops, that time would've been used to check the progress made until the previous iteration.
entries.new: 不出所料，我出现在走廊上，就在关着门的厨房旁边。我回到了二十分钟前，可 Past Sekimeiya 只蓄了十五分钟的能量。最初五分钟里我进不了厨房，因为过去的我还在里面。在假想的循环中，这段时间本该用来查看截至上一轮取得的进展。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I went to the right bedroom and took a notepad from a drawer. I recalled all the numbers that had comprised the formula and wrote them down.
entries.new: 我走进右边的卧室，从抽屉里取出一本笔记本，把构成公式的那些数字一一回忆出来，写在了上面。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Then, I silently approached the hallway and left the notepad next to the living room.
entries.new: 然后，我悄无声息地走到走廊，把笔记本放在客厅旁边。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is crazy. I wonder how much time was spent to reach this equation. It feels like an instant result for my real self, so I could even use something like this to brute force the computer passwords downstairs.
entries.new: 简直是疯了。不知道为这条公式花了多少时间。对现实中的我来说，结果却像凭空得来的一样——用这种办法，我甚至可以硬破楼下电脑的密码。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I stood in silence until I heard my past self leaving the kitchen.
entries.new: 我一声不响地站着，直到听见过去的我离开厨房。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The Future Sekimeiya's in the refrigerator...
entries.new: Future Sekimeiya 在冰箱里……
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I had a slight doubt. I understood the formula, but a certain factor wasn't part of it.
entries.new: 我心里还有一点疑问。公式我看懂了，但其中少了一个因素。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is that really it? Is there no other influential factor?
entries.new: 真的就这些？没有别的变量会影响结果？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I stepped over to the sink and set the plug for the drain. Then, I filled it with water very slowly so that I didn't make noise. Once it reached the top, I took the Future Sekimeiya out and put it in the water.
entries.new: 我走到水槽边，堵好排水口，然后极慢地放水，以免发出声响。等水满到边缘，我取出 Future Sekimeiya，把它放进水里。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I set the oven to count for ten minutes. When only five had passed, I put my hand in the water and touched the Sekimeiya.
entries.new: 我把烤箱定时十分钟。只过了五分钟，我就把手伸进水里，碰了 Sekimeiya。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I appeared in the kitchen and immediately saw the disabled Future Sekimeiya under the water. Then I looked at the oven and saw the amount of time I'd gone to the future.{w} The timer was at 4:31, immediately ticking down to 4:30.
entries.new: 我出现在厨房，立刻看见水里那台已经停摆的 Future Sekimeiya。接着我看向烤箱，确认自己去了多久的未来。{w}计时器显示 4:31，转眼就跳成了 4:30。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: 29 seconds. I have gone 29 seconds forward.{w} So I was right. There's another factor:{w} the temperature.
entries.new: 29 秒。我向前跳了 29 秒。{w}果然，我没猜错。还有一个因素：{w}温度。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The water is at room temperature, and the Sekimeiya spent five minutes in it. I should've definitely gone more than 29 seconds forward.
entries.new: 水是常温的，而 Sekimeiya 在里面泡了五分钟。按理说，我向前跳的时间绝不止 29 秒。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But the heat capacity of water is four times the air's, meaning that it heats up four times slower.{w} It appears a temperature higher than the cabinet lets the Sekimeiya store energy and become hot. Of course, that heats up the air around it.{w} Then, that same air makes the Sekimeiya even hotter, leading into the infinite increase of energy.
entries.new: 可水的比热是空气的四倍，升温速度也就慢四倍。{w}看来，只要温度高于展示柜，Sekimeiya 就能蓄能并升温。它当然会把周围的空气也烘热。{w}而这些空气又让它更热，如此循环，能量便无止境地增长。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: This is why the water's different heat capacity changes things. Because water heats up four times slower, five minutes submerged in it is the same as 75 seconds outside it. So I only traveled 29 seconds. I'm sure the hypothetical versions of me thought about this too when they were coming up with the equation, but it's not really part of it, it just modifies the result.
entries.new: 水的比热不同，结果也就变了。水升温慢四倍，泡上五分钟，只相当于在外面放了 75 秒。所以我只跳了 29 秒。假想中的我在推公式时想必也考虑过这一点，但它并不算公式的一部分，只是对结果作修正。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Finally, this answers the last question regarding that time Erina touched the Sekimeiya.
entries.new: 最后，这也解开了 Erina 那次碰 Sekimeiya 留下的最后一个疑问。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Why were we encompassed within Erina's range? The Sekimeiya had spent fifteen minutes outside the cabinet, and based on the previous identical travel, we should've been outside of it.
entries.new: 为什么我们会落在 Erina 的范围内？Sekimeiya 离开展示柜已经有十五分钟，按照先前那次相同的穿越来看，我们本应处在范围之外。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: "Erina opened the glass and rolled the Sekimeiya into her purse, avoiding direct contact with it."
entries.new: 「Erina 打开玻璃，把 Sekimeiya 拨进她的手提包，避免直接碰到它。」
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That's why. For those fifteen minutes, the Sekimeiya was in her purse.{w} That led to the opposite situation as the water. The air inside the purse couldn't easily escape, so it heated up faster than outside it. That is the reason why the range was bigger.{w} And Sai, the only person who actually traveled through time, would have been sent more than twenty minutes.
entries.new: 原来如此。那十五分钟里，Sekimeiya 一直在她的手提包里。{w}这就和水里的情形正好相反。包里的空气不易散出，升温比包外更快。范围之所以更大，原因就在这里。{w}而真正穿越了时间的只有 Sai，他被送往的时间应该超过二十分钟。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I wonder how much of an effect this had on the travels. When the Sekimeiya was in the other cabinets, for example, did it heat up faster? Their interiors are wide, but I'm sure there was an imperceptible difference.
entries.new: 不知道这对那些穿越有多大的影响。比如说，Sekimeiya 放在别的展示柜里时，升温是否也会更快？那些柜子内部空间宽敞，但肯定存在着难以察觉的差异。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Maybe you noticed the instances where this property was a factor in play.
entries.new: 或许你已经注意到，有几处情形正是这个特性在起作用。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Earlier, did you wonder why Shiroya world switched alongside Naomi? She was in the staircase while the Sekimeiya were on the sofa, and they had recently been taken out of the cabinet.
entries.new: 先前你是否想过，Shiroya 为什么会和 Naomi 一同发生世界切换？她当时在楼梯间，而 Sekimeiya 正放在沙发上，而且不久前才从展示柜里取出来。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: As you might guess, it was Katei's tight suitcase that let the Sekimeiya gain power faster than normal.
entries.new: 你应该也猜到了，正是 Katei 那只塞得严严实实的行李箱，让 Sekimeiya 蓄能的速度比平时更快。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That... might be everything. Although I could be wrong on details that I can't verify, I can apply the time formula as long as I touch the Sekimeiya outside the water and in this room. The temperature in the attic doesn't feel different from everywhere else, but I should stay here.
entries.new: 大概……就是这些了。有些细节我无从验证，或许会有出入，但只要在这间房里、不隔着水触碰 Sekimeiya，我就能套用时间公式。阁楼的温度和别处感觉不到差别，不过我还是应该留在这里。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I heard myself in the living room stepping to the hallway. Soon after, that me touched the Sekimeiya and went back in time.
entries.new: 我听见客厅里的自己走向走廊。紧接着，那个我便触碰了 Sekimeiya，回到了过去。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I retrieved the Past Sekimeiya and the recorder, then stepped back into the kitchen.
entries.new: 我取回 Past Sekimeiya 和录音笔，随后走回厨房。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I put both Sekimeiya in the refrigerator and took out the Past Sekimeiya as I began a new recording.
entries.new: 我把两块 Sekimeiya 都放进冰箱，又取出 Past Sekimeiya，开始新一轮录音。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I moved to the hallway; I had appeared right outside the kitchen, so I had to be there in twenty minutes. By leaving the door open, I could make sure the Future Sekimeiya was safe in the refrigerator.
entries.new: 我走向走廊。我出现的位置就在厨房门外，所以二十分钟后我必须待在那里。只要把门敞着，我就能确认 Future Sekimeiya 在冰箱里安然无恙。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Is there anything else? Is there any mystery that I can't explain?
entries.new: ……还有别的吗？还有什么我解释不了的谜团吗？
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: In the storeroom, I'd sporadically thought about the long series of events that had gone on during the twelve-hour span of time. A few ideas had come to me, but I had to seriously think about everything with what I'd learned.
entries.new: 在储藏室里，我断断续续地回想过那十二个小时里接连发生的种种。心里也冒出过几个念头，但我必须结合已经掌握的一切，认真把事情从头想一遍。
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: At {time=9}, the smoke was released in the tower, beginning the attack that trapped us inside. What triggered the alarm? Was anyone aware of the Sekimeiya's powers? I'm still not sure about the details behind it, but it's a lot clearer now.
entries.new: {time=9}，塔内释放了烟雾，那场把我们困在里面的袭击就此开始。警报是谁触发的？有人知道 Sekimeiya 的力量吗？背后的细节我仍不清楚，但现在已经明朗了许多。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: While we were asleep, someone hid the Sekimeiya in room B4 and turned on the temperature regulation.{w} Was it Naomi? In this world, she ran up to the attic with them.
entries.new: 我们睡着的时候，有人把 Sekimeiya 藏进了 B4 室，还打开了温度调节。{w}是 Naomi 吗？在这个世界里，是她带着它们跑上了阁楼。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: There's also Katei. He wasn't in the security room, and he has to be who dropped the rusty key in hallway A.{w} Beyond the truth of the attack, the third Sekimeiya, the one that doesn't work, was the only one inside the cabinet when we woke up. When Isla touched it, nothing happened to her.
entries.new: 还有 Katei。他不在监控室，A 走廊里那把生锈的钥匙一定是他掉的。{w}除了袭击的真相之外，还有一点：我们醒来时，展示柜里只剩下第三块 Sekimeiya，也就是那块失效的。Isla 碰了它，却什么也没有发生。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: We went to the security room and contacted the outside. That's when we had the call with Suripo, who told us about the story behind Ashiya and Xyn.
entries.new: 我们去了监控室，与外界取得联系。就是那时和 Suripo 通了话，他告诉了我们芦屋与 Xyn 之间的往事。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Before it ended, Sai turned off the monitor next to him. However, the whole computer immediately powered off too.
entries.new: 通话结束前，Sai 关掉了他身旁的显示器。可整台电脑也随之立刻断电了。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Who did that, and why? At this point, I believe there's an answer far more likely than the others.
entries.new: 是谁做的，又为了什么？事到如今，我认为有一个答案的可能性比其他的都大得多。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I think it was Katei. The person who was sitting in front of the computer.{w} When it happened, we were about to look at the recorded footage. That would've revealed that he hadn't been in the security room and who knows what else.
entries.new: 我想是 Katei。就是坐在电脑前的那个人。{w}当时我们正要查看录下的画面。那会揭穿他根本不在监控室，天知道还会带出什么别的东西。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: He probably wanted to use Sai's trick to his advantage. We were all focused on the screen that went black, so nobody saw him pressing the power button below the desk. Due to his timing, he tried to make it seem as if both things had the same cause.
entries.new: 他大概是想借 Sai 那一手为自己所用。我们全都盯着黑掉的屏幕，没人看见他在桌下按电源键。他挑准了时机，想让两件事看起来出自同一个原因。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The first thing he did was crouch under the desk and check the wires. He said nothing was wrong behind the computer, but I think that what he did was disconnect a cable. Then, when he repeatedly pressed the power button, the computer didn't turn on.
entries.new: 他做的第一件事是蹲到桌下检查线路。他说电脑后面没有问题，但我认为他其实是拔掉了一根线。接着，他反复按电源键，电脑自然开不了机。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: However, he couldn't leave it like that. If we explained what had happened to the police, they would immediately notice the disconnected cable, and no one would believe a word Katei said. So, after he acted like he'd been trying to figure out the issue for a long time, he reconnected the cable and the computer was able to power back on.
entries.new: 可他不能就这么放着不管。要是我们向警察说明经过，他们一眼就会发现那根被拔掉的线，就没人会信 Katei 说的话了。于是，他装模作样地查了很久，才把线接回去，电脑也得以重新开机。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I don't think that's all he did, though. During all the time he was below the desk, he unplugged the camera system from the computer. Later into the day, I realized the drive that stored the recorded footage wasn't being detected.
entries.new: 不过，我觉得他做的还不止这些。他待在桌下的那段时间里，把监控系统从电脑上拔了下来。那天稍晚，我才意识到存着录像的硬盘根本没有被识别。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And even that wasn't all. We tried to communicate with the outside a second time, but upon inputting his credentials, an "Access Denied" message appeared.{w} Why? I'm not completely sure why he would've done that, but he could've purposely entered an incorrect password to prompt that message. Perhaps there was a reason why he couldn't allow a second call, but he must've done that. After all, there's no way Ashiya would've been the ones to cut our single method of communication.
entries.new: 而且事情还不止这些。我们第二次尝试与外界联络，输入他的账号信息后，却弹出了「拒绝访问」的提示。{w}为什么？我并不能完全确定他这样做的理由，但他很可能故意输错密码，好让那行提示出现。也许出于某种原因，他不能让第二次通话打通，而这事一定是他做的。毕竟，芦屋那边绝不可能自己切断我们唯一的联络方式。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...He wasn't in the security room when the smoke went off, but one of the things he said was that he'd tried to do his part of removing the shutter and that the system hadn't let him.{w} That didn't actually happen, but Suripo told us that a similar error was affecting Ashiya. Since Katei knew or lied about it without experiencing it, it follows he was probably the cause behind it. He didn't want the exit to open before the time limit.{w} Therefore, there was something he had to do before the time expired, and deleting the saved footage was likely part of that.{w} When we were done, we left him alone in the security room. That was the time we later learned footage had been erased; he used it to briefly reconnect the system and delete what he didn't want us to see.
entries.new: ……烟雾弥漫的时候，他并不在监控室，但他说过一句话：他试过拆下自己负责的那部分卷帘门，系统却没让他操作。{w}这件事其实并没有发生，可 Suripo 告诉过我们，芦屋那边也出现了类似的故障。既然 Katei 没亲身经历却能知道这件事，或者干脆是在撒谎，那么他很可能就是造成这起故障的人。他不想让出口在时限之前打开。{w}也就是说，在时限结束前，他有非做不可的事，而删除已存的录像多半就是其中一环。{w}我们办完事之后，把他一个人留在了监控室。后来我们才知道，录像正是在那段时间被抹掉的——他利用那段时间短暂地接回系统，删掉了他不想让我们看到的东西。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: We looked through the crystal floor, but we didn't find Naomi. Then, we separated into two groups to look through the other floors. Erina, Isla, Shiroya, and I took the elevator up to the sixth floor.
entries.new: 我们找遍了水晶层，却没有找到 Naomi。随后我们分成两组，去其他楼层搜寻。Erina、Isla、Shiroya 和我乘电梯上了六楼。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: On the fifth floor, before Isla told us about her friend, we heard the elevator. Since we had left it on the sixth, and the other group only heard it once, it had to have been going down.
entries.new: 在五楼，Isla 讲起她那位朋友之前，我们听见了电梯的动静。我们把电梯留在了六楼，而另一组只听到一次声响，那么它只能是在往下走。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It was the Naomi who'd ended up trapped in the attic. When she appeared there, the elevator wasn't working, but she must have eventually tried it again after Katei reenabled it.
entries.new: 那就是最终被困在阁楼里的 Naomi。她出现在那里时，电梯还无法使用，但等 Katei 重新启用电梯后，她一定又试着搭过电梯。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: From the sixth floor, the elevator went to the attic. Of course, we didn't hear that.{w} Then, that Naomi used it to go all the way down.
entries.new: 电梯从六楼一路上了阁楼。当然，那一下我们没有听见。{w}随后，那个 Naomi 又乘着它一路下到了底层。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It was soon after when we found Naomi's first corpse in the hallway B crystal room.
entries.new: 没过多久，我们就在 B 走廊的水晶展室里发现了 Naomi 的第一具尸体。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I don't think that was the Naomi who'd taken the elevator, though. The elevator moved after one Naomi had already appeared, and her set of keys was on the first dead body.
entries.new: 不过，我觉得那并不是乘坐电梯的 Naomi。电梯启动时，已经有一个 Naomi 现身了，而她的那串钥匙就在第一具尸体身上。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That was likely the Naomi from our world. She appeared in front of the others and asked to talk to Katei privately. Later, the Naomi in the attic went down.
entries.new: 那多半是来自我们世界的 Naomi。她出现在众人面前，要求和 Katei 单独谈谈。之后，阁楼里的那个 Naomi 下了楼。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But after we waited, Katei came back alone, saying Naomi hadn't wanted to come back.
entries.new: 可我们等了许久，Katei 独自回来了，说 Naomi 不愿意回来。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: If she was still down there, we couldn't let her keep escaping. Shiroya and I waited in front of the elevator while the others went down to make sure we'd find her.{w} Suddenly, we heard the elevator going up.
entries.new: 如果她还在下面，我们就不能再让她这样一次次脱身。Shiroya 和我守在电梯前，其他人则下楼去，确保能找到她。{w}忽然，我们听见电梯升了上来。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: We thought that was Naomi, but we didn't find anyone where the elevator would've stopped. The reason was that my past self was the person who used it.
entries.new: 我们以为是 Naomi，可电梯该停下的地方却没有半个人影。原因在于，使用电梯的是过去的我。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And while we were discussing what could've happened, Akaro came running. The Sekimeiya had vanished from the cabinet for the first time.
entries.new: 就在我们讨论究竟出了什么事的时候，Akaro 跑了过来。Sekimeiya 第一次从展示柜里消失了。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Everyone was waiting near the stairs when we arrived. Shiroya and I saw the empty cabinet in the event room, but the priority was still Naomi—she had to be there.
entries.new: 我们赶到时，大家都等在楼梯附近。Shiroya 和我看到了活动室里空掉的展示柜，但当务之急仍是 Naomi——她一定就在那里。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Making sure nobody could leave, room B4 was eventually looked into. That's where we found her corpse.
entries.new: 为了确保没人能离开，我们最终查看了 B4 室，发现她的尸体就在那里。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Someone coming from the future could've killed her, but I'm inclined to think it was actually Katei.{w} It happened in the room where the Sekimeiya were hidden, and in this world, Naomi didn't bring them there. That makes me think it was Katei who did.
entries.new: 从未来赶来的人也可能杀了她，但我更倾向于认为动手的就是 Katei。{w}事情发生在藏匿 Sekimeiya 的那间房里，而在这一世界，把 Sekimeiya 带过去的人并不是 Naomi。所以我才会觉得下手的是 Katei。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Naomi appeared from the second floor. She had been watching the group from a distance just in case she could gather information such as Katei's potential accomplices. Finally, she mustered the courage to confront them.
entries.new: Naomi 从二楼现身。她一直在远处观察众人，以便尽可能收集情报，比如 Katei 是否可能有同伙。最后，她鼓起勇气，走到了他们面前。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She requested to talk to Katei privately; she represented Ashiya, so she couldn't let the others hear such a bold accusation against one of their workers if it was possible an explanation existed. However, she knew Katei had taken the Sekimeiya out of the cabinet.
entries.new: 她要求和 Katei 单独谈谈。她代表的是芦屋，只要事情还有解释的余地，就不能让旁人听见她对公司员工做出这样大胆的指控。然而，她清楚 Katei 把 Sekimeiya 从展示柜里取了出来。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Without speaking a word, they walked to the crystal floor. There, Naomi brought Katei to the room she'd seen him leave.
entries.new: 两人一言不发地走向水晶层。到了那里，Naomi 把 Katei 带进了她曾看见他走出来的那间房。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The Sekimeiya had to be there. Naomi asked him to unlock all the cabinets and saw two of them lying inside.
entries.new: Sekimeiya 一定就在那里。Naomi 让他把展示柜全部打开，只见里面躺着两块 Sekimeiya。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Raising her voice, she demanded an explanation while Katei kept quiet. He knew how bad the situation was: Naomi would bring about his doom. She would ruin everything.
entries.new: 她提高声音，要他给出解释，Katei 却一言不发。他清楚处境有多糟：Naomi 会让他万劫不复，会把一切毁于一旦。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He didn't bother making flimsy excuses. He explained everything he'd done, hoping she would sympathize with him. He had worked in Ashiya Tower all his life; he couldn't take it anymore. He'd only wanted to free himself from the life he'd lived.
entries.new: 他懒得编那些站不住脚的借口，索性把自己做过的事一一说了出来，希望她能体谅。他一辈子都在芦屋塔里工作，实在熬不下去了。他只是想从这样的日子里脱身。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When she discarded Katei's justification, it was his voice that rose. There was no way he would let his life end like that.
entries.new: 她驳回了 Katei 的理由，这回轮到他提高了嗓门。他绝不可能让自己的生命就这样结束。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The truth was out, so Katei attempted a bribe. If they obtained the Sekimeiya, both of them could work together to trade it off.{w} Immediately, Naomi refused—she was Ashiya's most trusted employee.{w} The third step was a threat. With a calm voice, Katei let her pick between Ashiya or her own safety. He needed her to stay quiet, and starting immediately; she knew two real Sekimeiya existed.{w} However, as Katei's words were dismissed again, he finally wavered. He had been acting stern, but that was far from reality. Inwardly, Katei burned with rage toward Naomi.
entries.new: 真相已经败露，Katei 便试着收买她。只要拿到 Sekimeiya，两人就能联手把它转手卖掉。{w}Naomi 当即拒绝——她可是芦屋最受信任的员工。{w}第三步，他改用威胁。Katei 用平静的语气让她在芦屋和自己的安危之间做选择。他必须让她立刻保持沉默；她已经知道有两块真正的 Sekimeiya。{w}然而，她再次拒绝，他终于动摇了。他一直摆出强硬的样子，可那与事实相去甚远。内心深处，Katei 对 Naomi 已是怒火中烧。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: After a sudden step forward, Katei dashed at her.{w} She had enough time to react and defend herself, but she was no match for him. After an abrupt scuffle, Katei dragged her to the wall and knocked her out. Before her death, Naomi let out a yell that only reached a single pair of ears outside the room: her own.
entries.new: Katei 猛然踏前一步，朝她扑了过去。{w}她来得及反应，也做出了反抗，但根本不是他的对手。一阵短促的扭打之后，Katei 把她拖到墙边，击昏了她。临死之前，Naomi 发出了一声喊叫，而门外听见这声音的只有一双耳朵——她自己的。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: From above, Katei stared at Naomi's body, unaware that a cabinet's temperature wheel had been damaged. Seconds later, he finally checked her breathing. ...There was none.{w} But all wasn't lost. Earlier, he had turned off that room's camera. He had known that he would have to take one of the Sekimeiya away eventually, so he had preemptively disabled the video.{w} But although he hadn't been recorded, he knew he was the only possible suspect.
entries.new: Katei 居高临下地望着 Naomi 的尸体，没有察觉展示柜的温度转盘已被撞坏。几秒之后，他才去探她的呼吸。……已经没有了。{w}但事情还没有到山穷水尽的地步。早些时候，他已经关掉了那间房的摄像头。他早就知道自己迟早要带走一块 Sekimeiya，因此提前让监控失效了。{w}可是，尽管没有被拍下来，他也清楚自己是唯一可能的嫌疑人。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...That was until he heard a sudden sound that forced him out of the room. Outside, he saw Atsuki's lone figure.{w} Katei rapidly stepped aside; he couldn't afford to be seen. However, Atsuki had just been recorded by the cameras, so there was another potential culprit to build a narrative against.{w} Before he walked back up, Katei thought about what he had to say. He had killed someone else after all those years, and he could find another way out.
entries.new: ……直到一阵突如其来的声响把他逼出了房间。到了外面，他看见了 Atsuki 孤零零的身影。{w}Katei 迅速闪到一旁，绝不能让人看见自己。不过，Atsuki 刚刚被摄像头拍了下来，也就是说，还有一个可以拿来做文章的可疑对象。{w}在往回走之前，Katei 盘算着该说些什么。时隔这么多年，他又杀了人，而他还能另寻出路。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When Naomi's body was found, Atsuki's eyes landed on the damaged wheel. It had stopped the temperature regulation, so the Sekimeiya made him travel to the past. However, the Sekimeiya lying in the neighboring cabinet was still kept cold, so no world switch occurred.
entries.new: Naomi 的尸体被发现时，Atsuki 的目光落在了那个损坏的转盘上。温度调节因此停止，Sekimeiya 便把他送回了过去。不过，躺在隔壁展示柜里的那块 Sekimeiya 仍然保持着低温，所以没有发生世界切换。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: There, I traveled to the past for the first time, and twenty minutes later, I walked right back to where everyone had seen me disappear.
entries.new: 就在那里，我第一次穿越到了过去，二十分钟后，我又走回了众人看见我消失的那个地方。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The Sekimeiya turned gray, so we brought it to its cabinet in the event room, where it became white again.{w} We heard a sound coming from outside. After all, someone else was still lurking within the tower—the Naomi who took the elevator down. The corpse had stopped our search, and we'd never looked into every room.
entries.new: 那块 Sekimeiya 变成了灰色，我们便把它送回活动室里它原本的展示柜，它在那里又变回了白色。{w}我们听见外面传来声响。毕竟，塔里还藏着另一个人——乘电梯下楼的 Naomi。那具尸体让我们中断了搜索，我们始终没有把每一间房都查遍。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But we couldn't let her escape, so we separated into two groups to look at both hallways. Katei, Erina, Isla, and I looked at hallway A, while Shiroya, Akaro, and Sai looked at hallway B. Despite that, we didn't find her.
entries.new: 可我们不能让她逃掉，于是分成两组，分别查看两条走廊。我和 Katei、Erina、Isla 查看 A走廊，Shiroya、Akaro 和 Sai 则去 B走廊。即便如此，我们还是没找到她。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: When we finished, Sai reiterated his distrust for Katei and refused to believe that Naomi hadn't been found in the rooms he'd investigated.
entries.new: 搜查结束后，Sai 再次表示不信任 Katei，也不肯相信 Naomi 不在 Katei 查过的房间里。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Sai wanted to confirm it for himself, which led him to enter the storeroom. There, he found a Sekimeiya.
entries.new: Sai 想亲自确认，便走进了储藏室。在那里，他发现了一块 Sekimeiya。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Had it been taken already? We went to the event room, and it was in fact gone from the cabinet.{w} Who hid it in the storeroom? That question ate at me.
entries.new: 难道它已经被人拿走了？我们赶到活动室，展示柜里果然空了。{w} 是谁把它藏进了储藏室？这个问题始终缠着我不放。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I believe I now understand what happened.{w} To get the Sekimeiya out of the event room's cabinet, the key was necessary, and it was with Naomi's corpse in room B4. That means someone who investigated hallway B must have taken it to unlock the cabinet.{w} However, none of them had the chance to hide it in the storeroom without being seen by the people who'd investigated hallway A. That's why it didn't make sense.
entries.new: 我想，我现在明白发生了什么。{w} 要把 Sekimeiya 从活动室的展示柜里取出来，必须用到钥匙；而钥匙就在 B4 房间里 Naomi 的尸体旁。也就是说，搜查 B走廊的人当中，必定有人取走钥匙打开了展示柜。{w} 可搜查 A走廊的人一直盯着，他们之中没人有机会把 Sekimeiya 藏进储藏室而不被发现。所以这件事才说不通。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The answer is that...
entries.new: 答案就是……
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I don't believe two people worked together. The issue was caused by a misconception.
entries.new: 我不认为有两个人合谋。问题出在一个误解上。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I entertained the thought that Sai had it in his hip pack, but I saw clearly when he entered the room that he didn't have the Sekimeiya yet.
entries.new: 我曾设想，Sai 会不会把它放在腰包里；可他进房间时我看得清清楚楚，他那时还没有 Sekimeiya。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It wasn't the same Sekimeiya. The first mystery regarding its whereabouts already pointed at the truth that more than one Sekimeiya existed.{w} ...After all, when Sai left the storeroom, he made me touch it, and nothing happened.{w} It was definitely the third Sekimeiya—the one that had disappeared from the event room the first time. The Past Sekimeiya was in room B4 since we'd regained consciousness, so we never actually found the one that disappeared first.
entries.new: 那不是同一块 Sekimeiya。最初关于它下落的谜团，其实早已指向一个事实：Sekimeiya 不止一块。{w} ……毕竟，Sai 离开储藏室时让我碰过它，却什么也没发生。{w} 那肯定就是第三块 Sekimeiya——最初从活动室消失的那一块。自我们醒来后，Past Sekimeiya 就一直在 B4 房间里；也就是说，我们从未真正找到最初消失的那一块。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Who hid the third Sekimeiya in the storeroom? That happened before Shiroya, Akaro, and I walked down from the sixth floor.{w} I don't believe it was Katei because he's likely the one who hid the two working Sekimeiya. If he wanted to also hide the third, which was originally in the event room, he would have done so while we were asleep.{w} I don't believe the other Naomi would have wanted to leave it there either.
entries.new: 是谁把第三块 Sekimeiya 藏进了储藏室？那是发生在我、Shiroya 和 Akaro 从六楼下来之前的事。{w} 我不认为是 Katei。藏起那两块还能用的 Sekimeiya 的人，多半就是他。若他还想连原本放在活动室的第三块也一并藏起来，趁我们睡着时动手就行了。{w} 我也不认为另一个 Naomi 会愿意把它留在那里。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: There's one last likely candidate: Sai.
entries.new: 最后还有一个可能的人选：Sai。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: After Katei said that Naomi didn't want to return, the others investigated the crystal floor while Shiroya and I waited next to the elevator on the fourth floor. We were told exactly what happened.
entries.new: Katei 说 Naomi 不愿意回来后，其他人去搜查水晶层，而我和 Shiroya 留在四楼的电梯旁等候。有人把事情的经过原原本本告诉了我们。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Sai guarded hallway A from the stairs while Katei guarded hallway B and the lobby.{w} As the hallway B rooms were inspected, Sai could've gone to the event room to take the gemstone and hide it in the storeroom.
entries.new: Sai 守住楼梯口，负责盯 A走廊；Katei 则守着 B走廊和大厅。{w} 在 B走廊的房间被逐一检查时，Sai 本有机会去活动室取走宝石，再把它藏进储藏室。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Then, he let the others discover that it had disappeared and asked Akaro to go find us.
entries.new: 随后，他让其他人发现东西不见了，又让 Akaro 来找我们。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: When they came and told me what had happened, I thought you two had to get down here. Since we're dealing with this situation, I found it appropriate to join up and make sure nothing slipped away.
entries.new: 他们过来告诉我出了什么事时，我就觉得你们俩该下来了。既然事情已经变成这样，我觉得还是汇合起来比较妥当，免得再有什么从眼皮底下溜走。
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Why would he have done that?{w} ...At that point, we hadn't learned about the Sekimeiya's powers yet.{w} During the morning, Sai's attitude was different from how it was later. He often talked with me about what he thought and was visibly enjoying what was happening around him. When did that change, exactly?{w} I believe it was when we found out about time travel. He became a lot more reserved and hard to read. If he hid the Sekimeiya so early, his motive likely aligned to his original attitude.
entries.new: 他为什么要那么做？{w} ……那时我们还没弄清 Sekimeiya 的力量。{w} 那天早上，Sai 的态度和后来截然不同。他常跟我谈起自己的想法，也看得出他很享受身边发生的事。他究竟是什么时候变的？{w} 我想，是在我们得知时间穿越之后。他变得沉默许多，让人看不透。若他在那么早的时候就藏起了 Sekimeiya，动机多半与他最初的态度有关。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The event room and hallway A weren't being recorded. He chose the storeroom, another place without cameras. Later on, he acted as if he'd found it there, so I don't think his intention was to keep it.{w} Did he do it for fun, or did he have a better reason? In any case, it's likely he already knew that he would point the finger at Katei, who he immediately accused.
entries.new: 活动室和 A走廊都没有监控。他选了同样没有摄像头的储藏室。后来他又装出是在那里发现它的样子，所以我觉得，他并不打算把它留在手里。{w} 是出于好玩，还是另有更充分的理由？无论如何，他恐怕早就知道自己会把矛头指向 Katei——毕竟他一开口便指控了 Katei。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: So, going back a little, when we found the Past Sekimeiya in room B4, we thought it was the one that disappeared from the event room. After putting it in the cabinet, we split up and searched both hallways for the person who'd made a sound. During that time, the Past Sekimeiya was hidden somewhere else while the third Sekimeiya was in the storeroom.
entries.new: 那么，稍微往前回溯一下：我们在 B4 房间发现 Past Sekimeiya 时，还以为它就是活动室里消失的那一块。把它放回展示柜后，我们分头去两条走廊寻找发出声响的人。就在那段时间里，Past Sekimeiya 被藏到了别处，而第三块 Sekimeiya 则躺在储藏室里。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It must've been Sai again. The only choices were the people in hallway B.
entries.new: 那一定又是 Sai。可选的人只有当时在 B走廊的那几个。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I was told Shiroya and Akaro looked through the rooms while Sai watched the hallway like I did. We had to make sure the person we were searching for was found, so the search took a while. During the time Shiroya and Akaro were inside the crystal rooms, Sai had the chance to pick up the key in room B4, take the Sekimeiya from the event room, and then hide it somewhere in hallway B.{w} After that, he slipped the cabinet key into Shiroya's purse as soon as possible.
entries.new: 我听说，Shiroya 和 Akaro 逐个查看房间时，Sai 像我一样守在走廊里。为了确保能找到那个人，搜查花了不少时间。在 Shiroya 和 Akaro 进入水晶展室期间，Sai 有机会去 B4 房间取走钥匙，从活动室拿走 Sekimeiya，再把它藏到 B走廊的某处。{w} 之后，他又尽快把展示柜的钥匙塞进了 Shiroya 的手袋。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: By acting like he'd found the Sekimeiya in the storeroom, he removed any potential blame from himself.{w} I didn't really think about it, but he said we couldn't trust Katei's search and never ended up looking at all the other rooms Katei went through.
entries.new: 他装出在储藏室里发现 Sekimeiya 的样子，把自己可能受到的怀疑摘了个干净。{w} 我当时没怎么细想，但他说过不能相信 Katei 的搜查，最后也没有把 Katei 查过的其余房间逐一查看。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And still, I'm sure there's another reason Sai did that.{w} I don't know why, but everyone thought only one Sekimeiya existed. By finding the one that didn't work, he made sure we wouldn't search for the one he had hidden.
entries.new: 不过，我确信 Sai 那么做还有另一个理由。{w} 不知为何，所有人都以为只存在一块 Sekimeiya。他找出那块无法使用的，正是为了让我们不去寻找他藏起来的那一块。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I see... That must be the answer to that question.{w} "Why is the Sekimeiya being hidden when it can easily be found?"{w} I wonder who knew the truth. I wonder who knew that three Sekimeiya existed.{w} The people who did kept hiding them because leaving the third one in the event room cabinet meant no one would look for others. The quality of their hiding spots hardly mattered—we just found one Sekimeiya and thought that was it. Maybe they were often poorly hidden precisely so that we'd find one and stop the search before coming across another.
entries.new: 原来如此……那个问题的答案一定就是这个。{w} 「为什么 Sekimeiya 明明很容易就能找到，却总被人藏起来？」{w} 我想知道，究竟是谁知道真相。是谁知道存在三块 Sekimeiya。{w} 知情者之所以一再把它们藏起来，是因为只要把第三块留在活动室展示柜里，我们便不会再去寻找其他 Sekimeiya。藏得是否妥当并不重要——我们只要找到一块 Sekimeiya，就会以为只有这一块。说不定它们之所以常常被藏得很草率，正是为了让我们找到一块后就此收手，不会撞见另一块。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Akaro knew it from the beginning, and Sai learned it shortly after. They knew two real Sekimeiya existed alongside Xyn's fake. For twelve hours, they had a plan in mind: to keep one of the real Sekimeiya hidden.
entries.new: Akaro 从一开始就知道，Sai 也在不久后得知。他们知道，除了 Xyn 造的赝品之外，还有两块真正的 Sekimeiya。整整十二个小时里，他们心里盘算着一个计划：把其中一块真正的 Sekimeiya 藏起来。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: If that was achieved, Ashiya would find two Sekimeiya, and they wouldn't search for the second real one. That was how they intended to pull it off and why they didn't want anyone else to know the truth. The Sekimeiya were hidden countless times, but the intent was rarely to keep them from being found.
entries.new: 只要成功，芦屋方面就只会找到两块 Sekimeiya，不会再去寻找第二块真品。他们正是想借此成事，也正因如此，才不愿让旁人知道真相。Sekimeiya 曾被藏起过无数次，但藏起来的目的很少是为了不让人找到。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: We still hadn't found the Naomi who'd made the sound, which meant that she had successfully escaped upstairs. That's why we searched through the higher floors.{w} Shiroya and I stayed on the fifth, and although we didn't hear anything, something strange happened with the elevator.
entries.new: 我们始终没找到那个发出声响的 Naomi，这说明她已经成功逃到楼上。所以我们才去搜查更高的楼层。{w} 我和 Shiroya 留在五楼，虽然我们什么声音都没听见，电梯却出了怪事。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Sai heard it three times. Based on that, it started from the crystal floor, which was not where we'd last left it...
entries.new: Sai 听见了三次。照此推断，电梯是从水晶层开始动的，可我们最后并没有把电梯停在那里……
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I don't believe Sai lied. Something happened during that time.
entries.new: 我不认为 Sai 说了谎。那段时间里，一定发生了什么。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That's because in the event room, we heard another sound. It was the bathroom's door closing.
entries.new: 因为我们在活动室里又听到了一声响。那是洗手间的门关上的声音。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Then, inside it, we found Naomi's second body.{w} However, I later traveled forty minutes to the past and appeared on the crystal floor before we'd all come back down.
entries.new: 随后，我们在里面发现了 Naomi 的第二具尸体。{w} 可后来，我却穿越回四十分钟前，出现在我们所有人下楼之前的水晶层。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I kept a close eye on the bathroom, but nothing happened until Naomi entered it...
entries.new: 我一直紧盯着洗手间，可直到 Naomi 走进去，什么也没发生……
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: First of all, why was Naomi not found? We inspected every floor but the attic. As I now understand the attic's footprints, I don't believe that Naomi went back there. Especially because she didn't have the key to unlock it.
entries.new: 首先，为什么没找到 Naomi？除了阁楼，我们把每一层都搜过了。我现在已经看懂阁楼里的那些脚印了，所以不认为 Naomi 回去过。何况她也没有阁楼的钥匙。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Somehow, the search failed to find her.{w} A different person stayed on each floor, so it's possible one wasn't investigated—the floor the person who used the elevator was supposed to guard.{w} ...Erina and Isla were on the second floor. Sai was on the third floor. Akaro was on the fourth floor. Shiroya and I were on the fifth floor. Katei was on the sixth floor.
entries.new: 不知为何，搜查没能找到她。{w} 每一层都安排了不同的人留守，所以也许有一层根本没被搜查——就是本该由乘电梯的人守着的那一层。{w} ……Erina 和 Isla 在二楼。Sai 在三楼。Akaro 在四楼。我和 Shiroya 在五楼。Katei 在六楼。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The strongest candidate to consider is Akaro.
entries.new: 最可疑的人是 Akaro。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: We told him we'd left the elevator on the fifth floor, but for some reason, it was originally below Sai. If he called it from the fourth, Sai would've heard it.
entries.new: 我们告诉过他，电梯停在五楼；可不知为何，它最初却停在 Sai 所在楼层的下方。若他从四楼叫电梯，Sai 应该会听见。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Then, he used it to go to the crystal floor... Why, though?{w} I can't help but remember that it was him who proposed this arrangement. He wanted us to stay separated between different floors, leaving the crystal floor vacant.
entries.new: 然后，他乘电梯去了水晶层……可他为什么要这么做？{w} 我不由得想起，提出这种安排的人正是他。他希望我们分散在不同楼层，好让水晶层空着。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Later, he would've gone back to the fourth floor, and finally, he would've sent it to the fifth, where it was supposed to be. Shiroya and I wouldn't have noticed that.{w} It definitely ended up there: Sai confirmed it when he called it from the crystal floor.
entries.new: 之后，他再返回四楼，最后把电梯送回它本该停在的五楼。我和 Shiroya 不会察觉。{w} 电梯确实回到了那里：Sai 从水晶层叫电梯时，就确认了这一点。
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I don't get it, though. Why would Akaro do that? He knew his trips up and down could be heard, didn't he?{w} And Erina and Isla didn't hear the elevator even once. I suppose it's possible Akaro stopped on floor 2 and then used the elevator to the crystal floor if he knew that wouldn't be heard, but if that happened, surely he would've done the same on floor 3 so that Sai wouldn't hear him either...
entries.new: 可我还是不明白。Akaro 为什么要那么做？他明知道自己乘电梯上下会被人听见，不是吗？{w} 而且 Erina 和 Isla 一次也没听见电梯声。我也想过，如果 Akaro 知道在二楼乘电梯不会被听见，他或许会先停在二楼，再乘电梯去水晶层；可如果真是这样，他经过三楼时也应该这么做，免得被 Sai 听见才对……
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Akaro had seen that one of the real Sekimeiya had been hidden in a cabinet with a damaged temperature wheel. It had changed colors, so he knew it wasn't the one Xyn had created.
entries.new: Akaro 曾看到，其中一块真正的 Sekimeiya 被藏在温度转盘损坏的展示柜里。它已经变了颜色，所以他明白那不是 Xyn 造的那一块。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Naomi A was going up the floors ahead of them, but she stopped on the fourth when she realized that was where Akaro would remain. She wanted to collect herself enough to talk to him; her shock at what Katei had done hadn't faded at all. ...However, before she did, he was gone.
entries.new: Naomi A 先他们一步往楼上走，却在四楼停下——她意识到 Akaro 会留在那里。她想让自己镇定下来，好去跟他谈谈；Katei 做的事仍让她震惊不已。……然而，还没等她开口，他已经不在了。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Akaro had a bad feeling. Something very strange was happening with the Sekimeiya, so he needed to see the cleaning cart for himself. When he did, he saw that the one he'd hidden was actually gone.
entries.new: Akaro 有种不祥的预感。Sekimeiya 的情况十分古怪，他必须亲眼看看清洁推车。等他去看时，才发现自己藏起来的那一块竟然不见了。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Who had taken it? Not only the one in the cart, but also one of the two Akaro had left in the event room before lying on the floor. Silently, Akaro continued watching Katei, but it could've been Naomi as well.{w} Katei was acting like only one Sekimeiya existed, and Akaro didn't know the reason. It was rational to conclude that one of them being in a cold cabinet indicated the other was as well.
entries.new: 是谁拿走的？不只是推车里的那一块，就连 Akaro 躺到地上之前留在活动室的两块中也少了一块。Akaro 默不作声地继续观察 Katei，但拿走它的也可能是 Naomi。{w} Katei 的举动仿佛只存在一块 Sekimeiya，而 Akaro 不知道其中缘由。既然有一块被放进了低温展示柜，那另一块很可能也在同样的地方，这么想才说得通。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: During the previous search, he had looked through that room. He knew there was another cabinet that had been set to 0 °C.{w} The other real Sekimeiya was there, and it was all he needed. He only had to keep one hidden, but there weren't many places he could think of.
entries.new: 在先前那次搜查中，他查看过那个房间。他知道那里还有另一个设定为 0 °C 的展示柜。{w} 另一块真正的 Sekimeiya 就在里面，而这正是他需要的。他只要藏起一块就够了，可一时也想不出多少合适的地方。
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He took the Future Sekimeiya out of the cabinet. When he did, it turned gray immediately, but nothing happened to him. Did it really have time travel powers? He had a hard time believing that, but it had just changed colors before him.
entries.new: 他把 Future Sekimeiya 从展示柜里取了出来。刚一拿出，它就立刻变成了灰色，可他身上什么也没发生。它真的拥有时间穿越的力量吗？他实在难以相信，可它刚刚就在他眼前变了颜色。
entries.speaker: c
